Unlike generic AI models, GaIA is grounded in a personalised "Collection of Votes," allowing the AI to replicate the specific writing style, argumentative structure, and technical vocabulary of each judge. To enhance legal certainty and uniformity, the system features an advanced similarity search tool that locates the judge's previous rulings on identical legal issues, ensuring that new judgments remain harmonised with the chamber’s jurisprudential history. Ethical security and data governance are fundamental pillars; processing occurs within a secure local VPN infrastructure, with strict anonymisation guidelines and a contractual guarantee that judicial data is never used to train external models. 
GaIA also introduces the concept of "Specialists"—optimised and approved prompts shared within an institutional library. This ecosystem is strengthened by an integrated Peer Forum, where law clerks collaborate to refine AI interactions and share best practices. Institutionalised via Act 1629/2025, the system is evolving toward intelligent data reprocessing and detailed audit logs to ensure total accountability. GaIA solves the "robotic AI" dilemma by maintaining human critical analysis as the sovereign validator of every final judicial decision, serving as a worldwide benchmark for human-centric and ethical AI governance.

items.title: AssessorIA: A Multi-Agent Ecosystem for Judicial Intelligence (Subnational: Porto Velho)
items.original_name: AssessorIA: Ecossistema de Agentes de IA para o Poder Judiciário
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: AssessorIA: Ecossistema de Agentes de IA para o Poder Judiciário
items.body:
AssessorIA is a pioneering multi-agent ecosystem for the Rondônia Court of Justice, designed to transform legal workflows for judges and staff. By utilising "Specialists" for routine tasks and autonomous agents for complex case analysis, it integrates with judicial systems to solve high caseload challenges. This tool holds immense potential to centralise institutional knowledge and ensure unprecedented speed and precision, delivering a more efficient and ethical justice system.

AssessorIA addresses the critical challenge of high caseloads at the Court of Justice of Rondônia (TJRO) by transforming legal document management through an advanced AI agent platform. Unlike conventional chatbots, the system acts as an intelligent digital assistant capable of understanding complex commands and using specific tools to analyse processes, search jurisprudence databases, and generate document drafts. The central objective is to optimise administrative and judicial activities, allowing judges and staff to focus on high-complexity analysis while the AI automates repetitive tasks and identifies predatory litigation patterns.

The technical architecture, based on multiple Large Language Models (LLMs) and LangGraph technology, enables the execution of high-level directives in a structured and logical manner. The system stands out for its deep personalisation, where the AI learns user profiles and preferences through a proactive memory system, ensuring that interactions become exponentially more useful over time. With "Specialists" — profiles configured for tasks like summarising texts or generating headnotes — the court encapsulates and distributes institutional knowledge scalably.

Innovations in the last version elevated the tool's standard with the implementation of personalised libraries, allowing each chamber to create its own knowledge base from PDF and TXT files. Additionally, the new browser extension enables direct interaction with any text selected on the PJe or Cabinet Module screen, eliminating the need to copy and paste content. These features ensure that users remain focused on their primary task, with AI support contextualised in real-time.

The future of AssessorIA is grounded in the 2026/2027 Management Plan and Resolution No. 615/2025, which establishes guidelines for ethical and secure AI governance in the Judiciary. The initiative foresees an evolution toward a technology infrastructure based on cybersecurity and the expansion of an internal "knowledge market," where user-created specialists can be shared and collectively improved. Thus, TJRO does not just adopt technology but institutionalizes a digital innovation culture aimed at delivering better judicial services.

items.title: Ulysses – Smart analysis on e-Polls
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
“Ulysses – Smart analysis on e-Polls” is an AI algorithm that analyses citizens' comments on e-polls about legislative bills available. The algorithm identifies the main arguments for and against each legislative bill in progress, grouping them. As all legislative bills are available for e-polls, there is a huge number of citizens contributing opinions. In addition, quantitative indicators are not sufficient to effectively identify exactly the items of articles accepted or rejection by citizens.

The Brazilian Chamber of Deputies defined that all bills presented by parliamentarians are systematically made available to receive citizens' contributions through e-polls. There are about 16,000 proposals per year, and some of them receive more than 1,000,000 suggestions/comments from citizens during the weeks of greatest discussion on the topic. 
It was observed that merely knowing the percentage of citizens who were for/against a legislative bill is not sufficient to improve the legislative text. Therefore, it was necessary to add an analysis of a free field in the e-poll through which citizens are invited to leave their comments and opinions. A human full analysis on these opinions is practically impossible, due to the large number and the timeliness with which parliamentarians need to position themselves in debates regarding those bills. 
The "Ulysses – Smart analysis on e-Polls" algorithm identifies the main arguments for and against each legislative bill in progress, grouping them and showing how distant the opinion groups are from each other. The analysis is semantic, which enables deep analysis of opinions, identifying situations of irony included in the texts. In addition to results presented in text format, the algorithm also presents a graphical view of citizens' opinion groups.
Results, outcomes and impacts
More accurate and timely analysis of the arguments for and against a legislative bill, which makes it possible to identify: 
Which part of the legislative text is most accepted or rejected by citizens; Whether there is any problem with society's interpretation of the legislative proposal, which may have resulted from disinformation.Challenges and lessons learned
Qualitative analyses of large volumes of data need to be incorporated into analyses on content received from citizens;This type of analysis is an important mechanism for identifying the impact that disinformation has on citizens' opinions

items.title: Ulysses - Legislative Demand Router
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Ulysses - Legislative Demand Router is an AI solution designed to automatically distribute legislative demands from Members of Parliament (MPs) to appropriate expert groups within the Legislative Consultancy Department. It analyses the demand text and suggests up to three specialist groups based on thematic relevance. The system aims to increase distribution efficiency, reduce bias, and lower staff workload, with demands automatically routed when the AI's confidence exceeds 90%.

An AI system developed by the Brazilian Chamber of Deputies to automate the distribution of legislative demands from parliamentarians to specialized consultancy groups. When Members of Parliament (MPs) submit requests for bill drafting or research support, the system employs semantic analysis to interpret the content and thematic complexity of each demand, subsequently recommending up to three expert groups best suited to fulfill the request. A legislative consultancy staff member reviews these AI-generated suggestions before authorizing distribution, though demands with confidence scores exceeding 90% are routed automatically. 
The solution pursues three main objectives:
Enhance operational efficiency by accelerating the demand distribution process and reducing processing timeMinimize allocation bias by applying consistent, data-driven criteria rather than subjective human judgmentReduce administrative burden on legislative consultancy staff, allowing them to focus on higher-value supervisory tasks rather than manual classification work.The system leverages historical demand distribution data for model training and integrates with existing digital platforms used by MPs and legislative consultants. Success is measured primarily through Top-1 accuracy rates, assessing the percentage of demands correctly classified by the AI model. Key implementation challenges include maintaining model accuracy over time, adapting to evolving distribution rules, and monitoring organizational changes within lawmaking expert groups
Results, outcomes and impacts
Decrease the staff work for reading and interpretating the demand textsDecrease the likehood of biases for interpeting and choosing the group of experts to be in charge of the new bill draftingImproved the incorporation of new subjects in the bills, especially when there is a blend of many subjects that would encompass many groups of lawmaking expertsChallenges and lessons learned
To substantially enhance the performance of the AI model, it was necessary to join many legislative experts (from differrent groups of experts) to analyse historical data, which required a deep legislative knowledge, before the AI training.As demand distribution rules change over time, it was required to discard obsolete training data

items.title: Ulysses - Consolidated summaries of legislative bills
items.original_name: Ulysses - Consolidação de sumaríos de proposições legislativas
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Ulysses - Consolidação de sumaríos de proposições legislativas
items.body:
Legislative consultants assist parliamentarians by producing consolidated executive summaries of bills, including justifications, amendments, attached bills, and approved substitutes. This process can take hours or days depending on the volume of related documents. The solution employs generative AI tools to help consultants create these summaries, which are then reviewed and supplemented as needed.

Legislative consultants, staff in charge of support the laymaking drafting, assist parliamentarians in reporting on legislative bills by producing consolidated executive summaries for each bill, including its justification and other related documents: amendments, attached bills, and approved substitutes. 

The production of these summaries can take hours or days, depending on the number of amendments and bills attached to the main bill being reported. This challenge is amplified along with the bills' lifecycle, once the set of documents increases eveyday and the updated version can assume a different meaning along with the time. In some cases, the bill intends to change other bills, resulting in a complex chain of documents.

The AI system uses generative AI tools to assist consultants in producing these summaries, which must be reviewed and supplemented by the consultants themselves according to thematic or contextual needs. These are the main objectives for this AI application: (i) decrease the time required to produce consolidated executive summaries from hours or days to minutes, enabling legislative consultants to work more efficiently; (ii) automatically identify and synthesize key information from all related documents to prevent oversight of critical content; and (iii) provide standardized, well-structured summaries that serve as a robust foundation for consultants to review and refine, ensuring uniformity across legislative reports. This initiative necessitates ongoing investment in ensuring the quality of both metadata and complete textual content of the legislative proposals under analysis and their respective cited legislation.

Results, outcomes and impacts:
A first positive impact achieved was the standardization of AI-generated summaries based on consensus obtained among the consultants who participated in the solution validation. For example, there are rules for initiating summary text, for limiting the number of words generated, for incorporating cited legislation into the summarization context, etc. We have begun collecting feedback-based measurements for ongoing investigation and continuous improvement of the deployed solution

Challenges and lessons learned:
Along the implementation of the AI system, it was necessary to perform extraction of textual and tabular content from documents produced in various different formats (e.g., .doc, .docx, .pdf, .tiff, among others). Some bills and regulations may contain both text and tables simultaneously. Moreover, varying context window constraints and behavioral differences were observed across different generative AI models, which required specific testing and targeted interventions to handle each encountered issue.

items.title: Ulysses - Bill Procedural Routing Analysis
items.original_name: Ulysses - Análise de Roteamento Procedimental de Propostas Legislativas
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Ulysses - Análise de Roteamento Procedimental de Propostas Legislativas
items.body:
Ulysses - Bill Procedural Routing Analysis is an AI system incoming legislative bills to identify procedural requirements and committee assignments, then produces a dispatch draft suggesting the bill's processing regime, committee routing order, and consideration procedures. It supports the Clerk’s staff before sending the bill to be discussed in the legislative committees. The Clerk staff are required to make many deep analyses of each incoming bill, which requires a lot of time.

The process of distributing legislative bills to the thematic committees – Initial Dispatch – requires manual and technical analysis by the Clerk staff. This activity, although critical for the proper progress of legislative processing, is susceptible to inconsistencies, delays, and work overload. Additionally, the growing volume of bills makes the process increasingly challenging in terms of time and accuracy. 
That process is composed of five modules and implemented by AI agents that evaluate the legislative document from different perspectives:
Assessment of the bill's procedural and constitutional requirementsSearch for similar legislative documents already being processed in the Brazilian Chamber of Deputies, so that, instead of having independent processing, they can be attached to a similar billDefinition of the form of analysis of the legislative matter, that is, whether by characteristic or rule it will first be evaluated by thematic committees before being voted on in plenary, or whether it is possible for the legislative proposal to become law as long as it has a conclusive opinion in the thematic committees through which it must pass. Below are the alternatives for form of bill analysis procedure:
Bill subject to conclusive discussion by committeesBill subject to plenary discussion,Bill subject to internal discussions in committees.Definition of the processing regime: under Brazilian legislation, legislative matters can be processed under the following regimes: Ordinary, Priority, Urgency, Special.Distribution to thematic committees for evaluation of merit, financial adequacy, and constitutionality. In the Chamber of Deputies of Brazil there are 30 permanent committees. All these analyses approaches are supported by AI agents to choose the best option, complying with the procedural and constitutional rights and rules involved.

items.title: Prompting Guide for Public Administration
items.original_name: Guía de prompting para la gestión pública
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.document_name: Guía de prompting para la gestión pública
items.body:
The Prompting Guide for Public Administration is a national guidance for professionals working at National Public Administration. It supports the responsible use of generative AI by providing practical instructions, legal safeguards, and human oversight criteria for interacting with large language models. It was developed to strengthen institutional digital capabilities while ensuring data protection, transparency, and accountability in the use of AI tools.

The Prompting Guide for Public Administration was developed to support professionals across Argentina’s National Public Administration as the use of generative AI tools rapidly expanded within government. As public servants increasingly rely on large language models for drafting, analysis and information processing, the guide provides a shared institutional framework to ensure that prompting practices are safe, effective and legally compliant.

The guide addresses both skills development and governance. It introduces a practical, structured methodology for prompt design—most notably the ROCLET framework (Role, Objective, Context, Limitations, Style and Output type)—to improve the quality, clarity and reproducibility of AI‑assisted work. At the same time, it establishes clear safeguards covering data protection, confidentiality, intellectual property, transparency and bias mitigation. AI‑generated outputs are explicitly defined as preliminary inputs that support, but do not replace, human judgment or legal, technical and administrative responsibility.

Although the guide has not yet been formally published, its expected impact is clear. It is designed to strengthen institutional AI literacy, standardise prompting practices across agencies and reduce risks such as data exposure, hallucinations and overreliance on automated outputs. By embedding mandatory human supervision and traceability into AI‑assisted workflows, the initiative aims to increase confidence, accountability and compliance with Argentina’s legal and administrative framework.

Key challenges emerged during the design phase. Balancing innovation with strict legal and security requirements—particularly around data protection and institutional responsibility—required careful framing. Another challenge was ensuring that the guide discourages dependency on AI outputs while promoting their responsible use. The main lesson learned is that practical, operational methodologies are more effective than abstract principles alone. Clear boundaries, institutional endorsement, targeted training and regular updates are essential for sustainable adoption.

The central purpose of the guide is to professionalise how public servants interact with AI systems, enabling consistent, transparent and responsible use across government. Following formal publication, it is expected to be institutionalised through internal dissemination, training programmes and integration into broader digital transformation and AI‑governance initiatives. Over time, the guide may be updated to reflect technological advances, regulatory changes and feedback from practical implementation.

items.title: NugepIA: AI-Powered Judicial Precedent Management System (Subnational: Porto Velho)
items.original_name: NugepIA: Sistema de Gestão de Precedentes Judiciais Potencializado por IA
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: NugepIA: Sistema de Gestão de Precedentes Judiciais Potencializado por IA
items.body:
NugepIA is an AI tool that organizes repetitive lawsuits to ensure faster and more consistent decisions for citizens. It was developed to replace slow manual processes and spreadsheets that were prone to human error in identifying similar cases. The system now automatically identifies identical cases and extracts dates from documents, making the court’s work more efficient.

NugepIA was developed by the Court of Justice of Rondônia (TJRO) to resolve critical bottlenecks in the management of binding precedents, such as IRDR and IAC, within the court’s NUGEPNAC unit. Prior to its introduction, monitoring of precedents relied on manual spreadsheets and institutional memory, creating fragmented communication, high risk of error and delays in reporting information to the National Council of Justice (CNJ). Judges’ chambers also lacked automatic visibility into suspended cases, negatively affecting productivity and legal certainty.

The initiative’s core objective is to automate the NUGEPNAC workflow using the Collectivus AI tool. The system automatically extracts key procedural dates—such as suspension, judgment and finality—directly from case documents, ensuring accurate and up‑to‑date records. It applies textual‑similarity analysis to group identical or highly similar cases, alerting judges in their workspaces to repetitive litigation and suggesting links to existing or potential binding precedents. In addition, the system performs daily monitoring of the Supreme Federal Court (STF) website to track updates in constitutional‑control actions relevant to ongoing cases.

Development progressed from initial mapping in February 2025 to full implementation by December 2025. Integration was completed across the PJe system, the Nugep System and the Chamber Module, eliminating manual reconciliation between platforms. This milestone institutionalised AI as a support tool for judicial decision‑making and laid the technological foundation for the broader AssessorIA platform, which now scales similarity‑analysis capabilities across the entire court.

Operationally, NugepIA eliminated manual data verification and enabled automated, accurate reporting to the CNJ’s National Precedent Bank (BNP). The AI achieves over 95% precision in grouping similar lawsuits and provides direct, actionable suggestions to judges’ chambers. Impact is measured through reduced screening and verification time, continuous validation cycles parallel to development and improved visibility of first‑ and second‑instance caseloads that were previously unmonitored by the central system.

Implementation addressed several challenges. Manual grouping of cases and spreadsheet‑based communication were error‑prone, and inconsistencies in procedural dates previously prevented automatic validation. These issues were resolved through full system integration and AI‑based date extraction, replacing manual review. Experience showed that successful AI use in the judiciary depends on coordinated planning between technical and legal teams, realistic timelines and continuous testing to mature similarity‑analysis functions.

items.title: Data EF AI Agent
items.original_name: ភ្នាក់ងារបញ្ញាសិប្បនិម្មិតនៃថ្នាលវិភាគទិន្នន័យសេដ្ឋកិច្ចនិងហិរញ្ញវត្ថុ
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: ភ្នាក់ងារបញ្ញាសិប្បនិម្មិតនៃថ្នាលវិភាគទិន្នន័យសេដ្ឋកិច្ចនិងហិរញ្ញវត្ថុ
items.body:
GDDE's Data EF AI Agent is a digital assistant that helps Ministry of Economy and Finance staff quickly find and understand open government data. It was designed for making searching, downloading, and analyzing datasets from the Data EF Portal less time-consuming. It enables quicker and more effective decision-making by letting users ask straightforward questions and providing statistics, charts, and summaries.

The Data EF Open Data Portal serves as Cambodia’s central platform for sharing economic and financial datasets across areas such as public finance, macroeconomics, revenue collection and industry. While the portal provides extensive data access, staff and decision‑makers often struggled to translate these datasets into timely insights. Manual search, review and download processes were slow and resource‑intensive, and inconsistent metadata and complex schemas made it difficult for users to locate relevant information. These limitations reduced the portal’s effectiveness as a decision-support tool.

To address this gap, the General Department of Digital Economy developed the Data EF AI Agent and integrated it into Data EF Insight, the analytics portal. The AI agent connects natural-language queries to underlying datasets through a semantic metadata layer, automatically identifying relevant data, retrieving it from the Data EF lakehouse and delivering results as tables, visualizations or concise summaries. This allows users to move directly from a question to an insight within seconds, while keeping human oversight at the center of validation and decision‑making.

The Data EF AI Agent aligns closely with Cambodia’s digital transformation agenda. It supports the Digital Government Policy 2022–2035 and the Digital Economy and Society Policy Framework 2021–2035, both of which emphasize evidence-based policymaking, data interoperability and digital government. Cambodia’s low scores on the OECD OURdata Index (0.04) and the Digital Government Index (0.2) highlight the importance of initiatives that make government data easier to access and analyze. The AI agent reduces barriers to data use, strengthens analytical capacity and advances responsible, human-centered AI consistent with OECD AI Principles.

The purpose of the AI agent is to remove technical barriers and improve administrative efficiency across the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF). Internal testing shows that data retrieval and summarization can now be completed in 10–15 seconds—compared to lengthy manual processes involving multiple dataset searches and downloads. Staff can explore more than 600 datasets through a single, easy‑to‑use interface, strengthening evidence-based reporting and analysis. Improvements are evaluated through workflow comparisons, usage observations and user feedback on usability and efficiency. Early results show reduced reliance on technical expertise, faster reporting cycles and stronger internal data-use capability. The initiative is expected to encourage broader adoption of data-driven governance within MEF and expand to additional use cases as confidence grows.

items.title: Ulysses chat
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Ulysses chat is an AI assistant developed for the Brazilian Chamber of Deputies. It considers official data and documents as well as the Chamber’s rules before answering questions.

The Brazilian Chamber of Deputies provides a wide range of internal services that support roughly 10,000 people, including 513 deputies, parliamentary staff, public servants and outsourced workers. Its operations span broadcasting (radio and TV), news services, medical care, engineering, architecture, finance, procurement, IT, legal services, training, a legislative university, dozens of legislative committees and extensive research and library functions. This diversity generates a constant demand for rapid access to accurate institutional information.

The Chamber’s traditional intranet model could no longer meet the speed and analytical depth required by employees in their daily work. As generative AI became widely used, staff increasingly turned to external platforms; however, using these tools without institutional context would require uploading large volumes of internal documents, creating risks around data privacy, rule misapplication and high duplication‑related costs. To address this, the Chamber developed Ulysses Chat—a generative AI‑based virtual assistant designed specifically for internal use and grounded in the institution’s own knowledge base. 
Ulysses Chat draws on a network of interconnected AI agents and operates within a governance layer designed to ensure privacy, security and responsible AI behaviour. It incorporates mechanisms for auditing, token accountability, minimising bias and hallucinations, and managing out‑of‑context queries. In its first implementation stage, the system answers questions using official institutional data, including internal standards, legislation, manuals, administrative rules, planning and budget information, logistics and human‑resources procedures, and legislative data such as bills, speeches and voting records. It also uses the Chamber’s organizational chart to contextualize information. In the current second phase, Ulysses Chat is beginning to automate selected internal processes through direct interaction with institutional systems. Across all information domains, data managers, data stewards and the Data Protection Officer oversee ongoing data‑quality monitoring.

items.title: Transform Paraná Program – Integrated Ecosystem of AI, Automation, and Data Governance (Subnational: Paraná)
items.original_name: Programa TRANSFORMA PARANÁ – Ecossistema Integrado de IA, Automação e Governança de Dados.
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Programa TRANSFORMA PARANÁ – Ecossistema Integrado de IA, Automação e Governança de Dados.
items.body:
The Transform Paraná Program uses AI to modernize state management and deliver faster, more efficient digital services. It creates a unified data foundation to overcome fragmentation and automate slow manual processes across government agencies. Citizens, rural producers, and safety officials benefit from diverse projects like smart food donation, environmental monitoring, and traffic safety analysis.

The Transforma Paraná Program establishes a statewide infrastructure for territorial and environmental intelligence designed to modernize public governance in Paraná. It responds to long‑standing structural challenges in public administration, including fragmented data across multiple systems, limited automation and heavy reliance on manual, time‑consuming processes. By combining artificial intelligence with cloud‑native architecture, the program aims to eliminate data silos and support faster, evidence‑based decision‑making across government.

At the heart of the initiative is the creation of a unified Data Foundation, implemented through a Macro State Data Lake that consolidates large volumes of information under a single governance framework. This foundation standardizes metadata, ensures interoperability and embeds compliance with Brazil’s General Data Protection Law (LGPD). It enables a range of high‑impact projects, including the Paraná Mais Sustentável platform for rural digital addressing and environmental monitoring; SISTRANSITO, which uses AI to analyze more than 82,000 traffic accident reports to improve road safety; and the J.A.C.A. project, which digitizes food donations at CEASA‑PR using conversational agents to reduce hunger and food waste.

The program is institutionalized through a strategic partnership between the Secretariat of Innovation and Artificial Intelligence (SEIA) and CELEPAR, ensuring that the technology is embedded in official state services and remains sustainable over time. Implementation follows a phased approach, starting with core infrastructure and pilot modules before scaling to full production. Continuous improvement is supported through automated pipelines and the introduction of an Agent Development Kit, enabling the deployment of intelligent, proactive digital services in areas such as health, education and public security. Concrete results are already visible. The Data Foundation has centralized petabytes of information, automated the analysis of 82,000 traffic accident reports and enabled the creation of unique digital addresses for 300,000 rural properties. Impact is measured through reductions in manual processing time, high levels of data structuring (exceeding 90% completeness) and the successful deployment of AI‑based conversational services for social programs.

Beyond these core initiatives, Transforma Paraná supports a broader innovation ecosystem. Complementary actions include the Conecta IA program to identify operational bottlenecks, Hub GovTech Paraná to promote open innovation, the Paraná Artificial Intelligence Cup for civil servants and AI solutions applied to public security and housing programs such as COHAPAR. Together, these efforts reduce bureaucracy, increase efficiency and modernize service delivery across multiple policy domains.

items.title: GOV.BR Chatbot
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Chat GOV.BR is an interface tool that aims to provide and maintain a complete and integrated communication and relationship service with citizens regarding the provision of public services, encompassing multiple channels, digital service, automation, and the use of AI resources, including LLMs, proprietary to the generative IA platform or integrated from third parties, the construction of proactive communication journeys, and integration with government systems.

The Chat Gov.BR was built as a secure platform to manage government AI chatbots using LLMs and RAG technology. This ensures millions of Brazilians get accurate and safe answers to public policies. It is essential because 144 agencies are preparing their own assistants. Our central infrastructure saves costs, protects data, and improves services. 

In the pilot, the GOV.BR Chat helped high school students to enroll in graduation, clarifying doubts about the ENEM (the national exam, similar to "SATs") and SISU (the University selection system after ENEM results). The primary goal of this pilot project was to support high school students throughout their academic journey by providing clear guidance on the SISU system and other public policies. This initiative aimed to increase citizen confidence in official government communications while testing the ability of AI tools to handle massive peaks of demand when millions of people use the system simultaneously. Furthermore, the chatbot collected performance metrics and interaction data, which allowed leaders to make better, evidence-based decisions to continuously improve digital public services.

The initiative then evolved from a simple idea into a functional tool with a dedicated knowledge base. In January 2026, the government sent a proactive message to students to announce the ENEM results. This was a significant evolution because the chatbot moved from a passive tool to a proactive one. Instead of waiting for the student, the government started the conversation to clarify the next steps for SISU. This test showed that the government can share accurate information on a massive scale.

Looking ahead, this pilot is the foundation for a more modern and inclusive digital governance model. After the team assesses the final performance of this project, the goal is to institutionalize the use of AI in government communication.  By using the lessons learned from this education case, the government aims to create "transactional chats." In the future, citizens will not only receive information but will also be able to request benefits and complete government tasks directly through the chatbot.

The initiative has yielded measurable results. In the Education case, we reached 6 million students, with a 3.5% interaction rate and an average of 5 messages per user. With Gov.br support, the chatbot independently resolved 65% of queries, significantly reducing human escalation. We measure these impacts using real-time platform analytics and resolution metrics.

Developing the GOV.BR chatbot brought several challenges. The main risk was the possibility of incorrect or confusing answers due to flaws in the knowledge base. To address this, we implemented a phased testing strategy: we started with internal checks and followed with a pilot group of students. These tests were essential to build the confidence needed for a large-scale launch.

items.title: CiudadanIA: AI-Powered Citizen Correspondence Processing for the Spanish Prime Minister’s Office
items.original_name: CiudadanIA: Procesamiento con IA de Correspondencia Ciudadana para el Gabinete de Presidencia del Gobierno de España
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: CiudadanIA: Procesamiento con IA de Correspondencia Ciudadana para el Gabinete de Presidencia del Gobierno de España
items.body:
CiudadanIA uses AI to accelerate the processing of citizen letters addressed to the Spanish President through the “Write to the President” service. Small language models generate summaries of citizen correspondence, enabling faster routing and response. The project also produced open-source tools for testing AI prompts and models at scale, including an LLM-as-a-judge evaluation framework, contributing to trustworthy AI in government.

CiudadanIA is an AI initiative within the PresidencIA programme that applies generative AI to improve the processing of citizen correspondence addressed to the President of Spain through the official “Escribe al Presidente” (Write to the President) service. This channel receives thousands of letters from citizens raising concerns, making requests, and sharing opinions on policy matters. Each letter requires reading, summarising, categorising, and routing to the appropriate government department, a labour-intensive process that directly affects how quickly and effectively citizens receive responses.  

CiudadanIA automates the summarisation step using small language models. Rather than relying exclusively on large cloud-based AI systems, the project combined cloud with fine-tuned compact models (specifically Gemma-3-4B, quantised for efficiency) to run on local government infrastructure. This design decision was driven by two requirements: citizen letters contain personal and sensitive information, and the government’s AI sovereignty objectives call for reduced dependency on third-party systems.  The fine-tuning and evaluation process was rigorous. Government staff who process citizen correspondence daily provided expert feedback on model outputs, identifying systematic errors such as hallucinated information (inventing details not present in letters), tone distortion (characterising respectful requests as demands), and omission of relevant content. This feedback was used to iteratively refine prompts and model behaviour.  To support this evaluation at scale, the programme developed an open-source LLM evaluation workbench that enables systematic testing of different prompts, models, and configurations. 

The tool supports both cloud APIs and local models, includes batch processing for evaluating large sets of correspondence, and implements an LLM-as-a-judge methodology where one language model evaluates the quality of another’s outputs against configurable criteria (accuracy, conciseness, tone preservation). The tool also supports English and Spanish and is available for other government teams.

items.title: BizData
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
BizData is a free, 24/7 digital advisory service developed by Israel’s Ministry of Economy to support businesses and entrepreneurs. The AI‑powered system provides business guidance alongside relevant government and public information, enabling users to access planning, regulatory and market insights through a single, easy‑to‑use interface. Its purpose is to help businesses make informed decisions about establishment, growth and operations without needing to consult multiple sources.

Each year, the Ministry of Economy provides in‑person or assisted consulting to around 30,000 businesses, covering only about 5% of Israel’s entrepreneurial population. BizData was created to extend this support to the remaining majority of small and medium‑sized enterprises by delivering scalable, digital business guidance. Using conversational interaction, the system identifies the type of business, its activities, geographic context and customer base, and then provides tailored information such as comparable business characteristics, recommendations for business planning, guidance on licensing and employment, and market‑related insights.

The system is built on an AI agent combined with custom databases developed specifically for the initiative and is being progressively connected to additional governmental and public data sources. This allows businesses to receive context‑specific information from a unified platform rather than navigating fragmented systems. A key technical capability enables the AI to interpret a simple verbal description of a business and match it across datasets that use different classification systems, resolving inconsistencies that previously prevented effective data integration. 
Less than one year after launch, BizData is used by approximately 5,500 businesses and entrepreneurs, with 60% returning for repeated use. Among survey respondents, 86% report receiving significant value from the system. Interest from other government ministries has led to discussions on expanding shared knowledge contributions, and partnerships are being explored with organisations that employ business consultants and mentors. These collaborations would allow the development of a “consultant assistant” function to support professional advisors in delivering higher‑quality guidance.

Implementation presented several challenges. Business‑related datasets varied in structure and classification, requiring the development of an AI‑based matching component to align user input with reliable data sources. Additional effort was required to secure approvals from data owners to enable lawful reuse of information for public benefit. A current strategic challenge is positioning BizData as the primary digital gateway for businesses across Israel.

The long‑term objective is to strengthen business resilience, support the creation of new enterprises and enable growth among small and medium‑sized firms, contributing to broader economic development. BizData is designed to evolve into the central channel through which businesses in Israel access trusted business and government information, combining scalability, accessibility and informed decision‑making in a single platform.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Governance Policy of the Chamber of Deputies
items.original_name: Política de Governança de Inteligência Artificial na Câmara dos Deputados
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.document_name: Política de Governança de Inteligência Artificial na Câmara dos Deputados
items.body:
AI Governance Policy, which is a mandatory standard that covers: a) AI ethical principles; b) rules related to privacy, transparency, accountability, human autonomy, robustness, security, and intellectual property; c) an AI risk management process; d) an AI governance process which that adds an AI Ethics Committee to the IT governance process, with new roles and responsibilities. It is intended to maximise AI benefits and minimise risks in legislative and administrative and legislative dimension

Beyond an AI policy, this Artificial intelligence governance is integrated into the corporate governance, the IT governance, the data governance with a view to ensuring that the use, development, contracting, and implementation of AI systems occur in an ethical, secure, transparent, responsible manner, and aligned with institutional purposes. The AI Governance Policy aims to: 
a) ensure that the use of AI is guided by ethical principles, including good faith, legitimate purpose, transparency, data protection, non-discrimination, fairness, security, robustness, human oversight, and respect for the integrity of results; b) guarantee that AI systems are not developed, contracted, or used without observing formal mechanisms for risk assessment, continuous supervision, and traceability; c) ensure that any AI system strictly observes applicable legislation, especially the Brazilian Data Protection Law, internal data protection, information security, and IT governance standards; d) establish formal processes for authorisation, supervision, documentation, monitoring, and decommissioning of AI systems, considering the entire lifecycle; e) regulate the use of generative AI, including requirements for prompts, instructions, autonomous or semi-autonomous agents, usage standards, and human review mechanisms; f) ensure that personal data and data with restricted access are only processed by AI systems as authorised by the competent managers, prohibiting misuse, unnecessary use, or use in computing environments that compromise the security, privacy, or sovereignty of the data; g) prohibit the use of AI systems that produce discriminatory, harmful, biased, illegitimate results, or results incompatible with the institutional purposes of the Chamber of Deputies; h) ensure that users are informed when interacting with AI agents; i) establish mechanisms for continuous supervision of AI systems, including monitoring of failures, security incidents, biases, hallucinations, inconsistencies, and unexpected behaviours; j) ensure that business managers, data managers, technical areas, and competent collegiate bodies act in accordance with defined roles and responsibilities.

items.title: AI Chatbot for Statistical Analyses of Fiscal Data
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The initiative consists in the development of an AI-based chatbot capable of analysing aggregated statistical data. The first chatbot prototype was based on a monolithic assistant, but a multimodal agent is being designed with the support of our technical partner, Società Generale d’Informatica (SOGEI).  The initiative develops an AI-based chatbot designed to analyse aggregates fiscal data and statistical data and support advanced analytical tasks. It addresses the growing volume and complexity

The initiative addresses the growing volume and complexity of fiscal and statistical data, which increasingly challenge traditional analytical tools and constrain the capacity of public administrations to fully leverage available information for decision-making. At the same time, it capitalises on the opportunity offered by high-quality, structured public data and advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI) to modernise analytical processes, strengthen evidence-based policymaking, and improve transparency in the management of public information. 
The initiative pursues three main objectives: 
to enhance the accuracy, speed, and efficiency of fiscal data analysis through AI-based tools;to support data-driven decision-making within public administration;to promote the responsible and trustworthy use of AI, in line with principles of data protection, accountability, and human oversight. To achieve these objectives, a prototype AI-based chatbot was developed using aggregated statistical data published by the Department of Finance. The tool supports statistical analysis and facilitates interaction with complex datasets. The initial prototype was based on monolithic architecture and limited data domain. 
The initiative is now evolving towards a more advanced multimodal AI agent with enhanced reasoning capabilities and dynamic data-loading functions. In the medium term, the project aims to transition from a single-assistant model to an integrated ecosystem of specialised AI agents embedded within existing analytical workflows. Institutionalization will involve the adoption of governance frameworks ensuring compliance with ethical, legal, and security standards, as well as capacity-building for public officials. The model is designed to be scalable and transferable to other policy domains and public administrations, enabling broader adoption of AI solutions to strengthen public sector performance and trust.

items.title: Taina (Public Service Agent)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Taína is a public service agent developed by the Government Office of ICT (OGTIC) to help citizens access information about public services and procedures in clear and accessible language. It provides guided assistance through a web interface. The initiative explores how public AI can improve citizen service while remaining ethical, inclusive, and open source.

Taína is a public artificial intelligence initiative developed by the Government Office of Information and Communication Technologies (OGTIC) of the Dominican Republic, in collaboration with Universidad del Caribe (UNICARIBE) and the Center for Public Intelligence (CPI), an applied research lab focused on public AI systems. The initiative was launched as a research and development (R&D) project to explore how artificial intelligence could be applied to citizen assistance in an ethical, inclusive, and context-aware manner. CPI contributed to the conceptual and technical design of the public AI infrastructure, while UNICARIBE supported academic validation and testing environments. Taína provides guided assistance covering all services available in the official public service catalogue of the Dominican State. Through natural language interaction, citizens can consult requirements, procedures, documentation, timelines, and institutional responsibilities in clear and accessible language. The system structures and interprets catalogue information to make it easier for people to navigate government services. In its current version, Taína operates through a web interface and has been validated in academic and citizen environments to test usability, clarity, and accessibility. The next phase of the initiative includes integration with the Government Call Center, enabling citizens to interact with Taína via telephone as well as digital channels. The objective is to embed the AI agent across the State’s omnichannel service system, ensuring consistent responses through web, phone, and future service touchpoints. Taína is designed as public AI infrastructure rather than as a proprietary product. Built under open-source principles, it enables collaborative development and oversight by public institutions, developers, and universities. Guided by principles of ethics, inclusion, accountability, and public value, the project seeks to position artificial intelligence as a shared digital public good that strengthens access to information and public services across the Dominican Republic.

items.title: ServetIA: AI Research Platform for the Spanish Prime Minister’s Office
items.original_name: ServetIA: Plataforma de Investigación con IA para el Gabinete de Presidencia del Gobierno de España
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: ServetIA: Plataforma de Investigación con IA para el Gabinete de Presidencia del Gobierno de España
items.body:
ServetIA is an AI-powered research platform developed for the Spanish Prime Minister’s Office to help government staff conduct faster, more thorough policy research. The tool uses large language models with source verification to provide reliable, evidence-based outputs. It was developed to reduce the time public servants spend on information gathering and improve the quality of briefing materials supporting government decision-making. ServetIA is in Beta.

ServetIA is a custom-built AI research platform developed within the PresidencIA programme to support analysis and information retrieval in the Spanish Prime Minister’s Office. Named after Miguel Servet, the Spanish polymath and pioneer of scientific inquiry, ServetIA embodies the same spirit of rigorous, evidence-based investigation applied to modern governance. Government advisors in the Prime Minister’s Office routinely research complex policy topics, prepare briefing documents, and synthesise information from multiple sources under tight deadlines. Traditional methods are slow and resource intensive. Off-the-shelf AI tools raise concerns about data privacy, accuracy, and suitability for sensitive government contexts. ServetIA bridges this gap. Built on large language model technology, it provides a complete suite of tools for research powered with AI, where staff can pose policy questions and receive structured, source-referenced responses, conduct literature review, reach consensus and generate drafts with verified citation. The platform prioritises “grounding”, ensuring outputs are anchored in verifiable sources rather than generating unsupported claims. This responds directly to the government’s need for reliable, citable information. A deep research module handles comprehensive, multi-source investigations that go beyond simple question-answering. The platform is in Beta, deployed and accessible at servetia.eu, with iterative refinements based on government user feedback. Development follows human-centred design: features are prioritised through user interviews and observation during structured Discovery phases within the Prime Minister’s Office. Technical implementation leverages both cloud-based and on-premises models. For sensitive use cases, the platform enables the use of local LLMs instead of Cloud, using open-weight models that can run on local infrastructure, supporting AI sovereignty objectives. This hybrid approach balances performance with data security requirements of a head-of-government institution. ServetIA complements a broader ecosystem within the PresidencIA programme, demonstrating how purpose-built AI tools, developed with government-specific requirements for security, accuracy, and usability, can enhance core government functions. Its architecture is modular and transferable, can be adapted to other departments and ministries, and its methodology, combining user research, iterative prototyping, and security-first design, provides a replicable model for AI tool development in government settings across countries. The tool augments rather than replaces human judgment, positioning AI as a support layer for public servants.

items.title: Khmer eKYC OCR API — AI-Powered Identity Document Recognition for Cambodian Citizens
items.original_name: ប្រព័ន្ធ Khmer eKYC OCR API
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: ប្រព័ន្ធ Khmer eKYC OCR API
items.body:
Khmer eKYC OCR API uses AI to instantly extract data from Cambodian identity documents in Khmer and English, and already powers CamDigiKey, Cambodia's official government single sign-on application. Available completely free via CamDX to all 45+ registered public and private members, including banks, insurance companies, and government agencies, it requires no integration cost and is open to both public and private CamDX members. It has processed more than Khmer ID card images, as of now.

Background and problem
Reliable Optical Character Recognition (OCR) for Khmer-script documents has historically been unavailable, creating a significant bottleneck in Cambodia's digital transformation. Financial institutions, public agencies, and businesses were forced to rely on manual data entry for identity verification, a slow, error-prone, and costly process. TSC's response to this gap, the Khmer eKYC OCR API, earned the Best R&D Award 2023 from the Ministry of Post and Telecommunication (MPTC) of Cambodia, recognising it as the country's most impactful research and development achievement of the year. 
What the initiative does 
TSC's AI team built the eKYC OCR API from the ground up using deep learning models, extracting structured data from Cambodian National IDs (Khmer and English), Passports (MRZ and biographical), and Driving Licences. The API is available entirely free of charge via CamDX, Cambodia's national data exchange platform, to all 45+ registered members, including banks, insurance companies, microfinance institutions, and government bodies. Both public- and private-sector CamDX members can access it freely. Notably, it powers CamDigiKey, Cambodia's official government single sign-on (SSO) app, enabling citizens to authenticate and access public digital services such as online business registration using their national identity documents. 
Objectives
Eliminate manual identity data entry;accelerate eKYC compliance for NBC-regulated institutions;deliver inclusive digital services in Khmer;provide a sovereign, locally-hosted alternative to foreign OCR; and democratise access by offering the API free of charge through CamDX, removing cost as a barrier to digital transformation for all member organisations. Future evolution
Having surpassed 8 million processed requests (Khmer ID card images or passport images) with zero cost to integrators, TSC will continue expanding document coverage, growing the CamDX member base, and deepening integration with Cambodia's national digital identity infrastructure. Provincial government adoption and ASEAN-level replication are key targets for 2026 and beyond.

items.title: Khmer Intelligent Document AI Agent (KIDAI-A)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
KIDAI-A is Cambodia’s first sovereign AI agent purpose-built for the Khmer language. It processes Khmer and English text, speech, and image documents, enabling government agencies, businesses, and citizens to query, summarise, and extract information from official documents in their native language. KIDAI-A closes the critical gap left by global AI tools that perform poorly on Khmer, a low-resource language, advancing digital sovereignty and public service efficiency.

Documents are the backbone of governance, commerce, and social life. Yet virtually all leading Document AI systems, designed for high-resource languages like English, perform poorly on Khmer, Cambodia’s official script used by over 17 million people. This creates a compounding digital divide: government officials cannot efficiently query Khmer-language policy archives; businesses struggle to automate Khmer invoice processing; and citizens face barriers accessing public information in their own language. No commercially available AI solution adequately addresses this gap.

Government Use Cases in Action:
1. Admin Assistant: Summarises official letters, retrieves staff records, and answers queries about internal reports in real time.
2. Policy Assistant: Enables officials to query national AI strategies (e.g., NAIS), MEF IT frameworks, and regulatory documents conversationally.
3. Data Entry Automation: Extracts structured data from invoices, sale reports, and forms, dramatically reducing manual processing time.

KIDAI-A locally hosts open-source LLMs (Qwen, Gemma, GPT-OSS variants) to ensure data sovereignty, no sensitive government data leaves Cambodia’s infrastructure. The platform is offered through Subscription (PaaS), API services (OCR, STT, MT, RAG), Knowledge Hub digitisation services, and vertical solutions. Target customers include government agencies, education and research institutes, the financial sector, enterprises, SMEs, and legal services. The team is pursuing co-development partnerships with government ministries and plans to expand KIDAI-A into a national-grade AI infrastructure for Cambodia’s digital government ecosystem. KIDAI-A represents more than a product, it is a national movement. Cambodia, like many lower-middle-income nations, faces a structural risk: dependence on foreign AI tools that neither understand Khmer culture, nor protect Cambodian data. KIDAI-A is Cambodia’s answer to this challenge, a fully sovereign AI stack designed, trained, and deployed by Cambodians, for Cambodians.
Results, outcomes and impacts: KIDAI-A is actively under development with the following milestones achieved and projected:
1. Proprietary Khmer speech recognition model trained on 500+ hours of audio data, achieving high transcription accuracy for Cambodian speech.
2. In-house OCR and document layout analysis models functional for Khmer/English document extraction.
3. Working prototype deployed locally — vector store loaded with 406+ government documents, demonstrating real-time multilingual Q&A.
4. Projected impact: reduce document processing time for government staff by 60-80%; enable digital access to Khmer-language policy archives; support Cambodia’s national digitisation agenda.

items.title: Aurora – Institutional AI Cognitive Infrastructure (Subnational: State of Rio Grande do Sul)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Aurora (“Dawn”) is an AI ecosystem developed by the Public Prosecution Service of Rio Grande do Sul (Brazil) to transform justice administration. Active in judicial and extrajudicial domains, it supports prosecutors protect vulnerable groups and collective rights by analyzing large volumes of documents and audiovisual records and integrating AI into legal workflows. With a human-in-the-loop approach, it enhances institutional capacity while preserving accountability and professional judgment.

Aurora emerged as an institutional effort to mark a "new Dawn" in legal work, treating technology as a strategic teammate rather than a standalone tool. It was developed to address increasing procedural complexity, data fragmentation, and cognitive overload within the justice system of Rio Grande do Sul. Prosecutors must analyse large volumes of documents, reports, and recorded hearings across multiple systems, which limits timely action in areas such as criminal prosecution, child protection, environmental enforcement, and public integrity. The initiative seeks to strengthen institutional capacity by embedding AI as a structured and accountable capability within core justice functions. 

Rather than focusing solely on document automation, Aurora operates as a cognitive support infrastructure. It enables natural language interaction with procedural records, automated transcription and summarisation of audiovisual evidence, cross-referencing of testimonies across different hearings, and identification of potential inconsistencies. Integration with existing judicial back-office systems (including eProc and SAJ) reduces workflow disruption and eliminates mechanical bottlenecks from case intake to judicial submission.  Aurora evolved through an internal prototyping phase in which prosecutors tested and refined prompts and transcription workflows before full deployment. This ensured alignment with operational needs and encouraged voluntary adoption. Governance is anchored in institutional policy and ICT oversight, including human-in-the-loop review, audit trails, and structured prompt curation. A collaborative prompt library enables users to share and evaluate analytical instructions, which are subsequently curated by a central body that may assign an official “Approved” designation. This transforms individual expertise into institutional knowledge while preserving intellectual autonomy. 

As of February 2026, Aurora has processed 13,012 hours of audio and video and supported the production of 37,028 legal documents. On February 11, 2026, it reached a historic milestone of 1,000 documents produced in a single day. System analytics indicate 1,432 unique users, reflecting strong voluntary uptake. Results are monitored through usage data and workflow indicators. In time-sensitive cases, such as sexual abuse testimonies, faster evidence analysis reduces delays and strengthens safeguards. Future impacts include expanded integration and analytical capacity to improve access to justice.

items.title: ANAC Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2025–2026
items.original_name: Estratégia de Inteligência Artificial da ANAC 2025-2026
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Estratégia de Inteligência Artificial da ANAC 2025-2026
items.body:
ANAC’s AI Strategy 2025–2026 is the Brazilian Civil Aviation Agency’s roadmap for adopting AI across the organisation in a broad, safe and responsible way. It links governance, capacity-building, risk management and implementation. It was created to improve public services, strengthen decision support and protect data, rights and trust.

ANAC’s AI Strategy 2025–2026 is the formal roadmap that operationalizes the agency’s AI Policy and translates AI adoption into concrete goals, governance arrangements, actions and monitoring routines. The strategy responds to a clear opportunity and challenge: to use AI to improve internal work, digital services and regulatory performance while ensuring safety, ethics, transparency, data protection and institutional accountability. The initiative is closely aligned with ANAC’s broader institutional planning. It connects to the agency’s Strategic Plan 2020–2026, its Digital Strategy 2024–2026 and the federal digital government agenda. Its strategic vision is to achieve excellence in the broad, safe and responsible adoption of AI to advance ANAC’s mission. To support this, the strategy defines key results for staff adoption and service transformation, and organizes implementation around five objectives: integrating AI into staff activities, increasing the capacity to develop AI-enabled solutions, improving data governance, ensuring security and ethics, and optimizing AI costs. The strategy is also a governance mechanism in practice, because it assigns roles and responsibilities across the institution. ANAC’s normative framework establishes an AI governance structure involving the IT Committee, the Superintendence of Technology and Digital Transformation, the data protection officer, technical advisory units, director-linked units and AI focal points. It also created an AI core with representatives from nearly all units, who met weekly, received training and helped design the policy and strategy. This creates a cross-functional model for prioritization, oversight, risk handling, implementation support and organizational learning. Looking ahead, the initiative is designed to become more institutionalized and scalable. ANAC established a roadmap, an operational model, periodic monitoring and evaluation routines, and requirements for existing AI systems to adapt to the new rules. The strategy foresees broader uptake across internal and external services, additional specific procurements if needed, and stronger reuse of models, standards and knowledge across the agency. In this sense, the initiative is not only a strategy document, but an institutional framework for trustworthy AI adoption in a federal regulator.

items.title: Santo Domingo Declaration — Third Ministerial Summit and High Authorities on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence in Latin America and the Caribbean
items.category: AI Policy Frameworks and Initiatives (intergovernmental or supranational)
items.body:
The Santo Domingo Declaration is the outcome document of the Third Ministerial Summit and High Authorities on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence in Latin America and the Caribbean, held on 25–26 June 2026 in Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic. Supported by UNESCO and CAF, it approves a Roadmap f2026–2027 focused on governance and regulation, talent and the future of work, protection of vulnerable groups, environment and sustainability, and infrastructure, building on prior summits in Santiago.

The Santo Domingo Declaration was adopted on 25–26 June 2026 during the Third Ministerial Summit and High Authorities on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence in Latin America and the Caribbean, hosted by the Government of the Dominican Republic. It was approved with the strategic backing of UNESCO and development bank of Latin America and the Caribbean (CAF), and builds directly on two earlier summits, Santiago, Chile (2023) and Montevideo (2024), which established a regional AI governance process, including a dedicated Working Group and a first Roadmap covering 2024–2025.
The declaration values the outcomes of that first Roadmap, noting it enabled progress in developing regional instruments to strengthen AI governance. It highlights that the new Roadmap 2026–2027 represents a transition from planning towards active implementation, with an emphasis on building sustainable capacities and practical mechanisms to consistently address, in line with international human rights norms, specific challenges including AI-driven disinformation, equitable access to technology, and AI's associated environmental impact. The declaration underscores that regional leadership on ethical AI requires coordinated governance mechanisms, prepared human talent, protection of groups in vulnerable situations, responsible environmental policies, and robust, accessible, sustainable technological infrastructure.
Under the Roadmap 2026–2027, countries commit to a 12-month implementation horizon structured around five strategic lines: governance and regulation; talent and the future of work; protection of vulnerable groups; environment, sustainability and climate change; and infrastructure. Concrete outputs to be promoted include a Regional Group of Disinformation and AI Specialists, a rapid-response intervention Playbook, an open online course on gender-mainstreaming competencies in AI, a regional data infrastructure standard, and studies and workshops on technological infrastructure and data sandboxes.
On governance and oversight, the declaration consolidates the Working Group on the Ethics of AI as a permanent coordination body responsible for monitoring the Roadmap's implementation, periodically updating its outputs, and coordinating with other regional and international networks. It also establishes the Ministerial and High Authorities Summits on AI Ethics as an annual recurring space to review progress, approve new initiatives, and ensure continuity of the regional process.

items.title: Cartagena de Indias Declaration for Governance, the construction of AI ecosystems and the promotion of AI education in an Ethical and Responsible manner in Latin America and the Caribbean
items.original_name: Declaración de Cartagena de Indias para la Gobernanza, la Construcción de Ecosistemas de Inteligencia Artificial (IA) y el Fomento de la Educación en IA de manera Ética y Responsable en América Latina y el Caribe
items.category: AI Policy Frameworks and Initiatives (intergovernmental or supranational)
items.document_name: Declaración de Cartagena de Indias para la Gobernanza, la Construcción de Ecosistemas de Inteligencia Artificial (IA) y el Fomento de la Educación en IA de manera Ética y Responsable en América Latina y el Caribe
items.body:
The Cartagena de Indias Declaration is a regional agreement signed by ministers and high authorities from seventeen Latin American and Caribbean countries in August 2024. Building on the 2023 Santiago Ministerial Summit on AI Ethics, it sets out commitments to strengthen cooperation on building AI ecosystems, promoting ethical AI education, and developing AI governance frameworks that respect human rights, sustainability and gender equity.

The Cartagena de Indias Declaration was adopted in August 2024 by ministers and high authorities from Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Cuba, Curaçao, Ecuador, Guatemala, Guyana, Honduras, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, the Dominican Republic, Suriname and Uruguay. It forms part of a regional process initiated by the 2023 Ministerial Summit on the Ethics of AI in Santiago, Chile, and its associated regional AI Working Group, and is positioned ahead of a further summit in Montevideo, Uruguay, on 3-4 October 2024. 
The declaration addresses the challenge of guiding AI development in the region "with full respect for human rights and dignity, sustainability and gender equity, avoiding any form of bias and discrimination," while harnessing AI's potential to strengthen democratic systems. It acknowledges support from the UN system, particularly UNESCO, as well as other multilateral organisations including the Development Bank of Latin America and the Caribbean (CAF), the European Union, the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB), the Organization of American States (OAS), and the Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean (ECLAC). It also references existing regional processes such as the Digital Agenda for Latin America and the Caribbean (eLAC), aiming to generate synergies rather than duplicate efforts.
Signatory countries commit to three main areas of action. On ecosystem-building, they agree to exchange knowledge, information and good practices on infrastructure, computing capacity, and AI development and deployment, and to use standardised diagnostic tools. They also commit to promoting AI development in Spanish and Portuguese that reflects the region's cultural, social and linguistic characteristics, and to sharing practices on AI use in the public sector. On education, countries commit to fostering digital skills training, AI certification programmes for professionals and students, and adaptive digital literacy that includes media and information literacy and critical, humanistic perspectives.
On governance, signatories reaffirm their commitment to promoting AI governance frameworks that respect human rights, including the right to personal data protection, while fostering innovation and sustainability. They commit to coordinating regional positions in international AI forums and to ensuring that international AI governance frameworks account for the region's specific characteristics, particularly regarding gaps in access, talent, data, infrastructure and regulatory capacity. 
NB: Included under UNESCO because it forms part of the broader Latin American and Caribbean AI governance process developed in alignment with UNESCO's Recommendation on the Ethics of AI, although it was not itself a formal UNESCO summit declaration.

items.title: UK National AI Infrastructure Roadmap
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The UK Compute Roadmap is a long-term national strategy for expanding the United Kingdom’s computing capacity to support AI research, innovation, and industrial development.

The UK Compute Roadmap outlines the government’s plan to significantly expand national high-performance computing and AI-optimised infrastructure over the coming decade. The roadmap includes major investments in supercomputers, AI-specific compute clusters, and the scaling of the UK AI Research Resource (AIRR). The strategy aims to address growing demand for computational power from universities, startups, and industry by increasing national compute capacity and improving access mechanisms. It also focuses on strengthening collaboration between public research institutions, technology companies, and innovation clusters. The roadmap supports frontier AI research, advanced model training, and large-scale experimentation. It also ensures that SMEs and startups can access advanced computing resources through national programmes and compute allocation mechanisms.

items.title: R&D Tax Credit System
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Japan's core corporate R&D tax credit system providing a 6–14% tax credit on total R&D expenses, with enhanced rates of 12–17% for SMEs, an open innovation add-on of up to 10%, and a new 40% credit for strategic technologies including AI from FY2026.

The Japanese R&D Tax Credit System (試験研究費の税額控除) is a long-standing element of Japan's innovation policy, administered by METI and the NTA. The system operates through blue-form corporate tax returns. Core credit (general category): 6–14% of total qualifying R&D expenses, with the rate sliding upward as R&D intensity increases (R&D expenses as a percentage of total expenses); the credit ceiling is 25% of annual corporate tax liability, extendable to 20–30% depending on changes in R&D spending. SME special rate: 12–17%, with a higher base rate to compensate for limited access to other innovation incentives. Open innovation add-on: an additional up to 10% credit for R&D expenses related to joint or commissioned research with universities and certified research institutions; credit ceiling of 10% of corporate tax. From FY2026, a new strategic technologies track was introduced under the FY2026 Tax Reform: 40% credit for R&D expenses related to six 'national strategic technologies' designated by the Cabinet Office (including AI and robotics; semiconductors and communications; quantum technology; space; bio and healthcare; fusion energy); 50% for joint/commissioned research in these areas with certified institutions; ceiling of 10% of corporate tax. In FY2023, approximately JPY 950B in deductions were claimed under the R&D credit system across all categories. Target audience: all Japanese companies conducting qualifying R&D, from SMEs to large enterprises.

items.title: Japan AI Safety Institute (AISI Japan)
items.original_name: AIセーフティ・インスティテュート（J-AISI）
items.category: National – AI governance bodies or mechanisms
items.document_name: AIセーフティ・インスティテュート（J-AISI）
items.body:
A national institute dedicated to evaluating, testing and improving the safety and reliability of artificial intelligence systems.

The AI Safety Institute (AISI) was established by the Japanese government to advance research, standards and evaluation methodologies for safe and trustworthy artificial intelligence. Hosted within Japan’s Information-technology Promotion Agency (IPA), the institute operates as a national hub for technical assessment of advanced AI systems and for coordination with international AI safety efforts. AISI develops evaluation frameworks and testing protocols that enable governments, companies and researchers to assess the reliability, security and societal impacts of AI models. Its activities include building safety benchmarks, conducting model evaluation studies, developing safety guidelines and organising working groups that bring together industry experts, researchers and regulators. The institute also plays an important role in international cooperation on AI governance, particularly through engagement with initiatives such as the Hiroshima AI Process and other G7-related activities.

items.title: Backing your business: our plan for SMEs
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Government support initiative helping SMEs improve productivity and adopt digital technologies.

The programme forms part of the UK government’s broader small business support framework. It provides SMEs with access to advisory services, training, and financial support designed to help businesses develop and implement growth strategies. Through the initiative, companies can access guidance on digital transformation, productivity improvements, and the adoption of emerging technologies such as AI. The programme also connects SMEs to funding opportunities, innovation support schemes, and government-supported business advisory networks. The initiative aims to improve SME competitiveness, encourage technology adoption, and support business growth across sectors.

items.title: AI Opportunities Action Plan
items.org: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT)
items.category: National – Strategy
items.body:
The UK Government's central AI strategy document, published in January 2025, setting out a comprehensive national agenda to secure the UK's position as a world-leading AI nation.

Published in January 2025, the AI Opportunities Action Plan represents the most comprehensive articulation of UK AI ambitions since the 2021 National AI Strategy and was received with a formal Government Response that committed to acting on all 50 of Clifford's recommendations. The Plan is structured around three strategic pillars. First, foundations for AI: securing the physical and data infrastructure necessary for AI development, including a UK Compute Roadmap targeting GBP 1.5 billion in public compute investment, the National Data Library, the Sovereign AI Unit, and AI Growth Zones.
