The initiative represents the Concept for the State Scientific and Technical Program for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in Ukraine, adopted by the Cabinet of Ministers in 2024. It addresses the growing need to strengthen Ukraine’s scientific and technological capacity in the field of artificial intelligence (AI), focusing on leveraging AI to modernize priority sectors of the national economy.
Objectives:
To define strategic directions and specific tasks for the development of AI technologies, while introducing mechanisms of state support for innovation. Creating favorable conditions for research, development, and deployment of AI solutions, particularly in priority economic sectors such as mechanical engineering, chemical and petrochemical industries, coal mining, defense industry, nuclear industry, scientific and scientific-technical activities, healthcare, and agriculture. Promoting the integration of AI technologies into these sectors, the initiative seeks to improve efficiency, productivity, and decision-making processes, ultimately contributing to the strengthening of Ukraine’s economic potential and its position in the international market.Impact:
As a newly adopted policy instrument (2024), the initiative is at an early stage of implementation. However, it builds upon earlier efforts to develop a national AI strategy, including the 2020 Concept for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in Ukraine. The current Concept represents a more targeted and applied approach, focusing not only on general principles but also on mobilizing national resources for scientific and industrial AI development. 
Future outlook:
In the long term, the initiative is expected to evolve into a comprehensive program that will guide Ukraine’s AI ecosystem, attract investment, and promote responsible and human-centered AI development.

items.title: Concept for the Development of Artificial Intelligence
items.original_name: Концепція розвитку штучного інтелекту в Україні
items.org: Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.document_name: Концепція розвитку штучного інтелекту в Україні
items.body:
Concept for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in Ukraine was adopted in 2020 as one of the country’s key strategic documents in the AI sector. It focuses on promoting the development and integration of artificial intelligence across multiple areas of public life. The Concept was designed to foster innovation, improve public services, and strengthen economic growth.

Concept for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in Ukraine was approved in 2020 and sets out the national vision and strategic priorities for the development, deployment, and regulation of AI technologies across all sectors. The initiative addresses the lack of coordinated state policy in the AI field, the absence of a legal and ethical framework, and the growing need to ensure Ukraine’s global competitiveness in digital technologies.
Objectives:
To foster research and innovation in AI, promote the responsible and safe implementation of AI technologies, and support their integration into both the public and private sectors. To raise awareness of AI opportunities among citizens, develop educational programmes, and establish a governance system that ensures ethical, transparent, and human-centred use of AI. The Concept is expected to be updated with the forthcoming National AI Strategy 2030.

items.title: CheckEye – AI-based Digital Screening
items.original_name: CheckEye – цифровий скринінг на основі ШІ
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: CheckEye – цифровий скринінг на основі ШІ
items.body:
Digital screening using artificial intelligence helps to detect diabetic retinopathy early and direct ophthalmological care to those who need it. Such programmes, carried out by nurses without the involvement of doctors, have already proved effective: they reduce costs, ease the burden on specialised facilities, and make examinations more accessible.

Background:
In healthcare facilities in Odesa and Chernihiv regions, more than 800 patients have already undergone screening to detect the early risk of vision loss. Conducted as part of a pilot digital screening project for diabetic retinopathy, the initiative enables nurses to take fundus photographs and analyse them with AI, ensuring early intervention and reducing the workload of specialists. Diabetic retinopathy is a complication of diabetes that damages the blood vessels of the retina and can lead to vision loss.
Impact: 
As part of the pilot, family doctors referred patients with type I or II diabetes, or suspected undiagnosed type II diabetes, for screening.Nurses used special cameras to take non-dilated eye images and uploaded them into the AI system, CheckEye, which returned results within 30 seconds. Of 873 screened patients, 651 showed no signs of diabetic retinopathy, while 222 were referred to ophthalmologists. The pilot confirms that digital screening improves early detection and helps to preserve vision. The project is supported by the Ministry of Health using the CheckEye digital platform.

items.title: Action Plan for the Implementation of the Concept for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in Ukraine for 2025–2026
items.original_name: План заходів з реалізації Концепції розвитку штучного інтелекту в Україні на 2025–2026 роки
items.org: Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.document_name: План заходів з реалізації Концепції розвитку штучного інтелекту в Україні на 2025–2026 роки
items.body:
Action Plan for the Implementation of the Concept for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in Ukraine for 2025–2026 is an action plan of the Government of Ukraine that aims to implement Ukraine’s Concept for the Development of Artificial Intelligence by 2030. It includes actions related to the use of AI in higher education, cybersecurity, public administration, regulation, and national defence.

The initiative is aimed at implementing the national Concept for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in Ukraine by 2030. It addresses the issue of insufficient coordination of policies and the absence of a comprehensive approach to AI implementation in key sectors such as education, cybersecurity, public administration, and defence. The use of AI in these areas creates opportunities to improve the efficiency, security, and quality of public services.
Objectives:
Supporting research and development in AI, drafting national AI legislation, promoting the application of AI technologies in higher education, combating cyber threats, and using AI for analysis, forecasting, and modelling of public administration systems. Ensuring the safe use of AI in the defence sector, which is an essential aspect of national security.Impact:
The initiative is implemented through a set of measures including the development of regulatory legal acts, methodological recommendations, adoption of international standards, and the creation of educational programmes. Further institutionalised implementation is envisaged through coordination between government bodies and expanded international cooperation. This will facilitate scaling results and deeper integration of AI into various sectors.

items.title: Action Plan for the Implementation of the Concept for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in Ukraine for 2021–2024
items.org: Secretariat of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
The initiative supports the development and responsible use of artificial intelligence (AI) in Ukraine. It focuses on advancing AI research, education, and applications in key sectors such as healthcare, public administration, and the economy. The overall aim is to foster innovation while ensuring legal compliance, safeguarding safety, and promoting respect for human rights.

The initiative aimed to implement a national strategy for the responsible and effective use of artificial intelligence (AI) in Ukraine. It sought to harness AI technologies to improve key sectors such as science, healthcare, and the economy, while also addressing challenges in cybersecurity and information security.
Impact:
Through a coordinated set of actions, the initiative worked to enhance Ukraine’s capacity to integrate AI safely into public administration. 
Objectives 
Advancing AI research and innovation, fostering applications of AI in medicine to improve diagnostics and treatment, and supporting economic growth by enabling new AI-driven solutions.Strengthening cybersecurity measures and regularly assessing information security to mitigate emerging digital threats. Evaluating and modelling the performance of public administration systems with AI tools to increase transparency, efficiency, and accountability. Impact:
The initiative supported AI research to protect the rights of persons who had served sentences, promoting their reintegration and social protection."

items.title: AI-based Computer-Aided Detection Software Product
items.original_name: Програмний продукт автоматизованого виявлення на основі штучного інтелекту
items.org: Public Health Centre of the Ministry of Health of Ukraine
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Програмний продукт автоматизованого виявлення на основі штучного інтелекту
items.body:
AI-powered CAD software helps doctors detect tuberculosis by analysing chest X-rays. It was developed to make screening faster, cheaper, and more reliable, especially where there are not enough specialists. The tool improves early diagnosis and protects people at risk, supporting global health efforts recommended by WHO.

Chest radiography (CXR) is an important tool for screening and triage of pulmonary tuberculosis (TB). It helps to identify people who may have TB and guides further testing, improving case detection and cost-efficiency. Computer-aided detection (CAD) products powered by artificial intelligence (AI) can automatically analyse CXR images for signs of TB. They provide an abnormality score that indicates the likelihood of TB and signals the need for further diagnostic evaluation. This makes screening faster, more consistent, and less dependent on the availability of trained specialists.
Impact:
According to the World Health Organization (WHO) consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis, CAD software can replace human readers in interpreting digital chest X-rays for TB screening and triage among people aged 15 years and older in populations where screening is recommended. This recommendation highlights CAD as a reliable and scalable solution that supports early TB detection and better use of health resources. By improving accuracy and accessibility, AI-powered CAD systems strengthen national TB control programmes and help protect at-risk communities."

items.title: White Paper on AI Regulation in Ukraine
items.original_name: Біла книга з регулювання ШІ в Україні
items.org: Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Біла книга з регулювання ШІ в Україні
items.body:
This initiative aims to create a clear and ethical framework for the development and use of artificial intelligence (AI) in Ukraine. It laid the foundation for a bottom-up and gradual approach to AI regulation and alignment with the EU AI Act, starting from the self-regulation environment in Ukraine. The initiative addresses the need to regulate AI to protect rights and boost innovation responsibly and it serves as a key AI policy framework.

The AI initiative outlined in the White Paper aims to establish a comprehensive and ethical framework for the development, deployment, and governance of artificial intelligence technologies in Ukraine. The White Paper on AI Regulation (White Paper) was developed in 2024 based on the AI Regulation Roadmap. It laid the foundation for the bottom-up and gradual approach to AI regulation and alignment with the EU AI Act. 
 
The essence of the approach is to divide the path to mandatory regulation into two stages: 
1. The preparatory stage (2-3 years, before the adoption of a law that is analogous to the EU AI Act) includes facilitation of self- and co-regulation among stakeholders and providing them tools for compliance.
2. The implementation stage of law that is analogous to the EU AI Act. By that moment, Ukraine is ensuring the state’s and the industry's capacity to regulate and comply accordingly.
According to the White Paper, Ukraine is currently implementing the first stage of approach, which includes such policy instruments and soft law tools as:
Sandbox;adaptation of the Council of Europe HUDERIA methodology;support of signment of the Voluntary Code of Conduct between AI companies and further establishment of self-regulatory organisations (currently 14 companies have signed it);publication of guidelines on AI for various sectors (guidelines for developers, higher educational institutions, civil servants, schools, intellectual property field, media, advertisement sector were already released. Guidelines for lawyers, courts, HR and some others are being developed)Also, the Glossary of Terms on AI was developed as part of the implementation of the AI Regulation Roadmap and White Paper.
These measures introduce self-regulatory measures to ensure safe, secure AI deployment, respect human rights, and prepare stakeholders for future regulation.  

Looking ahead, the initiative is expected to evolve through phased implementation and institutionalization within government structures, including the creation of dedicated bodies or commissions to oversee AI governance. It envisions continuous monitoring, evaluation, and updating of AI policies to keep pace with technological advancements. The initiative may also expand to cover cross-sectoral applications and international cooperation, aligning Ukraine’s AI policies with global best practices and standards."

items.title: The Guidelines on the Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence in Advertising and Marketing
items.original_name: Рекомендації з відповідального використання штучного інтелекту у сфері реклами та маркетингових рекомендацій
items.org: Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine, National Council of Ukraine for Television and Radio Broadcasting, State Service of Ukraine on Food Safety and Consumer Protection
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.document_name: Рекомендації з відповідального використання штучного інтелекту у сфері реклами та маркетингових рекомендацій
items.body:
The initiative “Recommendations for the Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence in Advertising and Marketing Communications” helps advertisers and marketers in Ukraine use artificial intelligence (AI) responsibly. It explains how to avoid risks such as discrimination or misleading consumers. The goal is to promote the safe, fair, and transparent use of AI in advertising and marketing.

The initiative “Recommendations for the Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence in Advertising and Marketing Communications” was developed by the Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine to address emerging ethical and practical challenges posed by the rapid adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in these sectors. With AI becoming increasingly integrated into advertising strategies and marketing communications, risks such as discrimination, manipulation, misleading consumers, and lack of transparency have grown. 
Objectives:
This initiative aims to mitigate such risks by providing clear, actionable guidelines that promote the safe, fair, and transparent use of AI tools by advertisers and marketers in Ukraine.
The primary objectives of the initiative are to raise awareness among industry professionals about responsible AI practices, establish a baseline for ethical AI deployment in advertising, guide the implementation of AI in professional and organisational practice, and protect consumer rights by preventing harmful AI-driven practices. It seeks to empower businesses to harness AI technologies effectively while ensuring compliance with ethical standards and regulatory frameworks. The recommendations cover key aspects such as avoiding bias, ensuring transparency, safeguarding personal data, respecting intellectual property and copyright, and fostering accountability in AI-driven marketing activities.

items.title: Recommendations on the Responsible Use of AI: Issues of Intellectual Property Law
items.original_name: Рекомендації щодо відповідального використання ШІ: питання права інтелектуальної власності
items.org: Ministry of Economy of Ukraine with Ministry of Digital Transformation and Ukrainian National Office for Intellectual Property and Innovations (UANIPIO)
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.document_name: Рекомендації щодо відповідального використання ШІ: питання права інтелектуальної власності
items.body:
This initiative provides practical guidance for developers, rights holders, and users on the responsible use of artificial intelligence (AI) in the field of intellectual property. It addresses key issues such as protecting copyright, managing AI-generated outputs, and establishing clear procedures for challenging unauthorised use. The recommendations aim to ensure ethical AI deployment while safeguarding creators’ rights and promoting innovation.

The initiative provides comprehensive guidance on the responsible use of artificial intelligence (AI) in the field of intellectual property (IP). It addresses key issues such as protecting copyright, managing AI-generated outputs, and establishing clear procedures for challenging unauthorised use. The recommendations aim to ensure ethical AI deployment while safeguarding creators’ rights and promoting innovation.
Objectives:
These guidelines offer practical advice for developers, rights holders, users, as well as all entities involved in the development, training, implementation, and use of AI systems.They cover aspects such as determining ownership of AI-generated content, utilising technological protection measures, and navigating legal avenues for enforcement. The initiative also emphasises the importance of labelling AI-generated content and provides strategies for preventing and addressing infringements.Future outlook:
Looking ahead, the initiative is expected to evolve alongside Ukraine’s broader AI regulatory framework. As part of a phased approach to AI regulation, the recommendations serve as preparatory tools for businesses and stakeholders, aligning with future legislation modelled after the European Union’s AI Act. This progression aims to balance innovation with the protection of rights, ensuring that Ukraine’s AI landscape develops responsibly and in harmony with international standards.

items.title: Recommendations for the Responsible Implementation and Use of Artificial Intelligence Technologies in Higher Education Institutions
items.original_name: Рекомендації щодо відповідального впровадження та використання технологій штучного інтелекту в закладах вищої освіти
items.org: Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine, Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.document_name: Рекомендації щодо відповідального впровадження та використання технологій штучного інтелекту в закладах вищої освіти
items.body:
These recommendations provide clear guidance for higher education institutions on how to responsibly use artificial intelligence (AI). They help educators and students safely integrate AI tools to improve learning, research, and administration. The initiative was developed to address the challenges of ethics, data privacy, and transparency in AI, ensuring trustworthy and effective use in higher education institutions.

The recommendations on the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in higher education institutions in Ukraine address the growing need to integrate AI technologies responsibly within the academic environment. As AI tools become increasingly accessible and powerful, universities face challenges related to ethics, data privacy, transparency, and potential biases in AI applications. 
Objectives:
This initiative seeks to provide practical guidance to educators, administrators, and students on how to leverage AI benefits while minimising risks, ensuring that AI enhances rather than undermines educational quality and fairness.
to create a methodological basis for the implementation and rational use of artificial intelligence technologies in higher education institutions; to promote the ethical and transparent use of AI technologies in teaching, learning, research, and administration; to protect personal data and privacy rights of all users; to support human oversight of AI systems; and to build digital literacy and trust within the higher education community. Looking ahead, the initiative is expected to evolve by being integrated into formal university policies and curricula, supporting the development of specialised AI-related courses and training programmes. Institutionalisation will involve cooperation among government bodies, educational institutions, and the private sector to continuously update guidelines in line with technological progress and emerging legal frameworks, such as the EU AI Act. Scaling the initiative nationally and potentially regionally can contribute to modernising higher education and improving its global competitiveness through trustworthy AI adoption.

items.title: Instructional and Methodological Recommendations Regarding the Introduction and Use of Artificial Intelligence Technologies in General Secondary Education Institutions
items.original_name: Інструктивно-методичні рекомендації щодо запровадження та використання технологій штучного інтелекту в закладах загальної середньої освіти
items.org: Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine, Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.document_name: Інструктивно-методичні рекомендації щодо запровадження та використання технологій штучного інтелекту в закладах загальної середньої освіти
items.body:
This initiative provides practical recommendations for teachers and school leaders on the responsible use of artificial intelligence (AI) in general secondary education. It helps schools understand how to use AI tools safely, ethically, and in line with educational values. The guidance was developed to support digital transformation while protecting students’ rights and ensuring human oversight.

The Recommendations were developed by the Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine and the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine. This initiative provides practical advice for educators and school leaders on the responsible use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools in the teaching and learning process.
Impact:
The document outlines the main principles for integrating AI technologies in schools, including respect for human dignity and rights, preservation of human-centric learning, and compliance with legal, ethical, and pedagogical standards. It identifies both potential benefits and risks of AI use in education, such as biased content, data privacy violations, and overreliance on AI tools. The recommendations emphasise the need for human oversight and informed decision-making by educators.
Objectives:
The guidance also includes practical use cases and scenarios where AI may assist teachers and students, as well as specific risks that should be avoided. It encourages the development of digital competence among teachers and outlines basic rules for safe and ethical AI use in schools. The recommendations aim to support digital transformation in education while maintaining trust, safety, and transparency.

items.title: Human Rights in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
items.original_name: Права людини в епоху штучного інтелекту
items.org: Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine, Ombudsman of Ukraine
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.document_name: Права людини в епоху штучного інтелекту
items.body:
Human Rights in the Age of Artificial Intelligence are methodological materials designed to explore how artificial intelligence (AI) affects human rights and to outline legal ways to regulate it. They offer recommendations for safely managing AI systems under Ukrainian laws and global standards, benefiting policymakers, businesses, and citizens. Developed to balance technological innovation with privacy and fairness, the materials address risks such as data misuse and bias in everyday AI uses.

Human Rights in the Age of Artificial Intelligence are methodological materials designed to address the growing challenges posed by artificial intelligence (AI) to human rights, particularly in areas such as privacy, discrimination, and fairness. As AI permeates sectors including healthcare, law enforcement, finance, education, and daily life, it offers immense opportunities for societal progress, such as efficient data analysis and personalised services. However, it also carries risks of rights violations through biased algorithms, unauthorised data processing, and opaque decision-making, as evidenced by global cases like faulty facial recognition systems or discriminatory hiring tools. 
Objectives:
The primary objectives are to educate stakeholders on AI’s human rights implications, provide practical recommendations for legal compliance, and promote balanced regulation. By drawing on Ukrainian and European laws, the materials aim to equip policymakers, businesses, and developers with tools to ensure AI systems respect privacy, minimise bias, and enable human oversight, ultimately supporting Ukraine’s AI development goals as set out in its 2020 AI Concept.Future outlook:
Looking ahead, the materials are expected to be implemented more broadly through integration into Ukraine’s digital policies, potentially via regulatory sandboxes and expert committees established by the Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine. They could also scale regionally by influencing EU-aligned reforms and through periodic updates reflecting evolving technologies such as generative AI."

items.title: Guidelines on the Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence in the News Media
items.original_name: Рекомендації з відповідального використання штучного інтелекту в медіа
items.org: Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine, Ministry of Culture and Strategic Communications of Ukraine, National Council of Television and Radio Broadcasting of Ukraine
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.document_name: Рекомендації з відповідального використання штучного інтелекту в медіа
items.body:
Guidelines on the Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence in the News Media help media organisations and journalists use artificial intelligence (AI) tools responsibly. The document explains how to maintain clarity by labelling AI-generated content, ensure human editorial oversight, and protect audiences from misinformation and privacy risks. Developed to support ethical innovation and transparency, it benefits both media professionals and the public.

Guidelines on the Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence in the News Media aim to support media professionals in integrating artificial intelligence (AI) tools in a way that upholds ethical journalism and safeguards public trust. As AI becomes more prevalent in news production, content personalisation, moderation, and audience targeting, media organisations face risks such as bias amplification, misinformation, erosion of editorial accountability, and opacity of AI-generated outputs. These guidelines address such challenges by providing practical principles for responsible AI use in the media context.
Objectives: 
The initiative outlines core values such as transparency, human oversight, editorial responsibility, data protection, and the need to distinguish AI-generated content from human journalism. It also encourages media actors to disclose the use of AI, regularly assess its impact, and ensure public awareness. Recommendations are structured to support both media producers and technology providers, fostering responsible design and deployment of AI systems.Impact:
The guidelines are part of Ukraine’s broader effort to shape a trustworthy AI ecosystem. While currently presented as a non-binding tool, they serve as a foundation for future standard-setting and capacity-building initiatives. They reflect international best practices while taking into account the specifics of Ukraine’s media environment.
Future outlook:
Over time, these recommendations could be integrated into editorial policies, journalistic training, and digital media regulation frameworks. They represent a step towards aligning AI practices in media with democratic values, media independence, and the right to access reliable information.

items.title: Guidelines on the Responsible Use of AI: for Developers
items.original_name: Pекомендації з відповідальної розробки систем із використанням технологій штучного інтелекту
items.org: Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.document_name: Pекомендації з відповідальної розробки систем із використанням технологій штучного інтелекту
items.body:
This initiative provides practical guidance on the responsible development and use of artificial intelligence in Ukraine. It covers key topics such as data, human rights, copyright, privacy, and competition risks. The goal is to help developers, policymakers, and users ensure that AI systems are safe, fair, and legally compliant.

The Guidelines on the Responsible Use of AI: For Developers initiative is aimed at providing clear, practical guidance to developers, legal professionals, and other stakeholders involved in the creation of artificial intelligence (AI) products in Ukraine. It addresses the growing need to integrate ethical, legal, and human rights considerations into the design and development of AI tools, with a focus on ensuring compliance with existing legislation, mitigating discrimination, protecting privacy, and managing intellectual property risks.
Objectives:
Key objectives include increasing legal awareness among developers, promoting responsible data use, embedding human rights assessments into model design, and clarifying copyright protections for AI-generated outputs and datasets. The initiative emphasises the importance of human oversight and offers specific guidance on privacy-by-design, data minimisation, and transparency.Impact: 
The initiative responds to the rapid growth of AI technologies and their integration into public and private sector systems. Developers often lack accessible legal frameworks or human rights guidelines when training or deploying models. This document fills that gap by offering structured recommendations on data governance, model training, choice of large language models, human oversight, consumer protection, copyright, and privacy. It also includes a dedicated section on antitrust risks, making it one of the most comprehensive local tools for ethical AI development in Eastern Europe.

items.title: Guidelines on the Responsible Use of AI: For Lawyers
items.original_name: Рекомендації з відповідального використання штучного інтелекту для правників
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.document_name: Рекомендації з відповідального використання штучного інтелекту для правників
items.body:
Guidelines on the Responsible Use of AI for Lawyers offer practical guidance on using artificial intelligence (AI) safely in legal work in Ukraine. They help lawyers, judges, prosecutors, and advocates understand how to verify sources, protect client data, and comply with ethical standards. The purpose is to support legal professionals in using AI responsibly and reducing risks in their daily practice.

The initiative provides guidance for the responsible use of artificial intelligence (AI) in the legal sector in Ukraine. As AI tools become more accessible and widely used in legal work, there is a growing need to help professionals such as judges, lawyers, prosecutors, and advocates understand how to apply these tools ethically and safely. 
The rapid development of generative AI creates both opportunities for efficiency and risks of misinformation, privacy violations, and erosion of trust in legal systems. This initiative responds to these challenges by promoting transparency, critical thinking, and ethical standards in the use of AI in law.
Objectives:
The key objective of the initiative is to ensure that AI technologies support, rather than undermine, the quality and integrity of legal services. The recommendations help legal professionals assess the reliability of AI-generated content, avoid over-reliance on such tools, and take full responsibility for decisions made in legal proceedings. The document also highlights the importance of data protection, confidentiality, and fairness when using AI in interactions with clients, courts, and institutions. By raising awareness of both benefits and risks, the initiative promotes informed, cautious, and human-centred use of digital tools in the justice sector.
Impact:
The document may serve as a foundation for professional standards or internal guidelines in courts, law firms, and public institutions. As Ukraine continues to align with international standards and digital governance practices, the approach outlined in this initiative could also contribute to broader discussions on trustworthy AI use across the justice system and beyond."

items.title: Guidelines for the Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence by Civil Servants
items.original_name: Поради з відповідального використання штучного інтелекту публічними службовцями
items.org: Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine, National Agency of Ukraine on Civil Service, Higher School of Public Administration
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.document_name: Поради з відповідального використання штучного інтелекту публічними службовцями
items.body:
This initiative provides clear and practical advice for Ukrainian civil servants on how to use generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools in their work responsibly. It helps them understand the risks and benefits of AI, and how to apply it ethically and safely in daily tasks. The guidelines were developed to support informed decision-making and build trust in the public sector’s use of AI.

The “Recommendations for the Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence by Civil Servants” is an initiative aimed at helping civil servants in Ukraine navigate the growing presence of generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools in the public sector. As AI technologies become more widely accessible, public institutions face new challenges, including ethical risks, data protection concerns, lack of human oversight, and the potential for misuse or over-reliance on AI-generated content. While these risks cannot be entirely eliminated, the recommendations help public servants avoid or mitigate them by providing clear, practical guidance tailored to the specific needs and responsibilities of the public sector.
Objectives:
to ensure the safe, ethical, and effective use of AI tools by public servants; to support informed and critical use of generative AI; and to encourage responsible innovation without undermining human accountability. Impact:
The recommendations emphasise transparency, proper documentation, data privacy, and the importance of human oversight in AI-assisted decision-making. By providing this guidance, the initiative aims to build trust in the use of AI within government, protect the rights of citizens, and contribute to a more informed and digitally competent public service.
The guidance can serve as a basis for internal policies at various levels of public administration, and may also be adapted for use in other sectors of the public sphere, such as education, healthcare, or local governance. As national and EU-level regulations on AI evolve, these recommendations will support public institutions in aligning their practices with legally binding requirements, including the forthcoming EU AI Act.

items.title: Glossary of Terms on AI
items.original_name: Словник термінів у сфері Штучного Інтелекту
items.org: Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.document_name: Словник термінів у сфері Штучного Інтелекту
items.body:
The Glossary of Terms on AI was developed to ensure consistent understanding of artificial intelligence (AI) concepts across government, industry, and education. It helps policymakers, developers, and educators communicate clearly and prepare for future regulation. The glossary also supports the implementation of Ukraine’s AI Regulation Roadmap and White Paper.

"The Glossary of Terms on AI was developed by the Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine in cooperation with national and international experts as part of the implementation of the AI Regulation Roadmap and the White Paper on AI Regulation in Ukraine. It provides a consolidated set of definitions for key terms used in the context of artificial intelligence (AI), aiming to harmonise terminology and ensure a shared understanding among various stakeholders.
Objectives:
The main objective of this initiative is to support the development of coherent, transparent, and effective communication in the AI field by offering clear definitions for commonly used concepts. This is particularly relevant for policymakers, developers, educators, researchers, and other actors involved in the development and use of AI systems. By promoting consistency in the use of terminology, the glossary contributes to improving legal clarity, regulatory drafting, education, and public understanding.Impact
The glossary includes over 100 terms structured alphabetically in both Ukrainian and English. Each entry provides a term and its definition, with references to sources such as the OECD, EU legislation, UNESCO recommendations, ISO standards, and documents of the Council of Europe. Where appropriate, Ukrainian context and legal interpretations are taken into account, ensuring alignment with international standards while respecting local specifics.Future outlook:
This initiative is expected to evolve through updates as AI-related terminology develops. The glossary will serve as a reference point for future legislation, policy documents, educational materials, and sector-specific guidelines. It strengthens Ukraine’s capacity to adopt and implement harmonised AI regulation in line with the EU AI Act and other international frameworks."

items.title: Web Portal “Centre for Responsible Artificial Intelligence”
items.org: Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Centre for Responsible AI is a one-stop-shop web portal created by the Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine. It provides access to AI regulatory tools, guidelines, and educational materials, keeping stakeholders informed about Ukraine’s progress towards AI regulation. The portal also offers awareness resources for citizens on safe and responsible AI use.

The Centre for Responsible AI is a national initiative developed by the Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine to provide a central access point for regulatory, educational, and practical tools supporting the safe and responsible use of artificial intelligence (AI). 
Methodology:
The portal is designed on a one-stop-shop principle, ensuring maximum integration of available instruments such as human rights impact assessments, AI labelling procedures, participation in a regulatory sandbox, joining codes of conduct, and training courses on safe AI interaction.
Objectives:
Beyond regulatory tools, the portal will serve as an information and awareness hub. It will provide citizens, businesses, and policymakers with guidance documents, white papers, and roadmaps, along with news and updates on AI governance and regulation in Ukraine. An important element is the educational component for society at large, aimed at improving digital and AI literacy while raising awareness of risks and safeguards against malicious use of AI.
Impact:
The initiative seeks to increase transparency, trust, and accountability in AI development and application. It provides stakeholders with a unified space to access recommendations, consult best practices, and take part in experimentation initiatives."

items.title: Unified State Web Portal of Digital Education “Diia.Education”
items.original_name: Єдиний державний веб-портал цифрової освіти “Дія. Освіта”
items.org: Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine, State Enterprise “Diia”
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Єдиний державний веб-портал цифрової освіти “Дія. Освіта”
items.body:
In 2020, the Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine launched the Unified State Web Portal of Digital Education “Diia.Education” to improve citizens’ digital literacy. The portal now has over 2.7 million users and offers more than 600 educational products, including over 220 free edutainment series, guides, podcasts, webinars, tests, simulators, and skill bytes.

By the Resolution of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine dated 10 March 2021, No. 184, the Regulation on the Unified State Web Portal of Digital Education “Diia.Education” was approved. According to this Regulation, the free portal is available 24 hours a day, seven days a week.
The main tasks of the Digital Education Web Portal include:
providing access to educational materials in formal and non-formal education;ensuring digital literacy for people of all age categories;forming individual lists of materials;enabling personalised educational trajectories.Upon completing the courses, registered users receive certificates in their personal accounts.
The Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine continues to develop educational materials on artificial intelligence (AI) within the Diia.Education portal, which already has a dedicated section. With an audience of over 2.7 million users, the portal offers more than ten resources in various formats, including educational series, guides, and short “byte learning” modules.
Over 121,000 users have started learning from the AI section. Available courses include “Artificial Intelligence,” “ChatGPT: Your Personal Assistant for Work, Study, and Life,” “Future AI Leaders,” “ChatGPT for Personal Effectiveness,” and “Artificial Intelligence for Schoolchildren.” In addition, there are guides and byte learning modules on topics such as AI in education, its current and future capabilities, and AI as a teacher’s tool for lesson planning and task creation.

items.title: The First Regional Forum on the Implementation of Artificial Intelligence
items.original_name: Перший регіональний форум про впровадження штучного інтелекту
items.org: Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine, Odesa State Administration
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Перший регіональний форум про впровадження штучного інтелекту
items.body:
The First Regional AI Forum in Odesa gathered educators, civil servants, and digital experts to explore the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in education and public administration. The initiative aims to promote responsible and ethical AI implementation at the local level. More than 150 participants from the region discussed practical tools, human rights safeguards, and developed skills for effective AI use.

The First Regional AI Forum, held in Odesa, was launched to address the growing need for responsible and effective adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) at the local level in Ukraine. The initiative responds to the increasing relevance of AI in public administration and education, and the necessity to ensure that AI technologies are introduced in a way that respects human rights, promotes trust, and supports inclusive digital transformation.
Organised by the Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine and the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine, the forum brought together over 150 educators, public servants, digital transformation officers, and community leaders.
Objectives:
It served as a regional platform to present national and international frameworks on ethical AI use and offered practical tools for implementing AI in schools and public institutions. A key feature was the presentation of recommendations on AI use in education and civil service, including the Council of Europe’s HUDERIA methodology for assessing AI’s impact on human rights and democracy.
Impact:
This forum marked the beginning of a broader effort to institutionalise AI education and awareness at the regional level in Ukraine. Future plans include expanding the CDTO Campus AI programmes, scaling the HUDERIA methodology to more regions, and replicating the forum format in other parts of the country. The initiative helps build a foundation for informed and ethical AI transformation, with direct benefits for public administration, education, and local communities."

items.title: Partnership with WIN2EDIH
items.org: Ukrainian Startup Fund (state institution under the Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Win-Win EDIH (WIN2EDIH) is a digital transformation hub providing high value-added services for testing, training, ecosystem networking, and funding support to SMEs, start-ups, and the public sector in Ukraine. It operates through a dynamic and interconnected ecosystem with access to leading European practices and technological players. The hub is strongly committed to becoming a relevant participant in the EDIH network and expanding its collaboration with other European regions.

The Win-Win EDIH (WIN2EDIH) is a digital transformation hub providing high value-added services for testing, training, ecosystem networking, and funding support to SMEs, start-ups, and the public sector in Ukraine.
It operates through a dynamic and interconnected ecosystem with access to leading European practices and technological players. The hub is strongly committed to becoming a relevant participant in the EDIH network and expanding its collaboration with other European regions.
Objectives:
The main objective of WIN2EDIH is to enhance the level of digital and green transformation of its target audience by introducing deep tech solutions and integrating coherently into the EU network of EDIHs.WIN2EDIH was established by a consortium representing the Quadruple Helix Model: KNEU, ZPSU, and CPNU as the most digitalised educational establishments in Northern Ukraine. Alongside them, the public, industry, and community sectors are represented by the Ukrainian Startup Fund, a public authority with a proven track record of supporting start-ups through collaborations with ongoing European projects; Vacuum Deep Tech Acceleration, the sole deep tech supporter in Ukraine; and YEP Accelerator, which serves as the centre of the Ukrainian innovation ecosystem.
Impact:
The WIN2EDIH covers the Chernihiv, Zhytomyr, and Kyiv regions. It focuses on selected deep tech smart specialisations, including Smart Mobility, Manufacturing and Processing, Smart Factories, Food Tech, Education, Public Administration, Energy, and Healthcare. The technologies applied include HPC, AI, Cybersecurity, Advanced Digital Skills, Automation and Robotics, IoT, Advanced and Additive Manufacturing, VR, Cloud Services, Software Architectures, Internet Services, Applications, and Communication Networks.

items.title: Parliamentary Committee on Digital Transformation of the Verkhovna Rada
items.original_name: Комітет з питань цифрової трансформації Верховної Ради
items.org: Parliamentary Committee on Digital Transformation of the Verkhovna Rada
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Комітет з питань цифрової трансформації Верховної Ради
items.body:
Parliamentary Committee on Digital Transformation of the Verkhovna Rada was established to develop legislation and oversee policies related to digital technologies in Ukraine. Its mission is to promote digital innovation, ensure data protection, and support the responsible use of emerging technologies such as AI. Through its efforts, citizens, businesses, and public institutions benefit from more transparent, efficient, and modern digital governance.

The Parliamentary Committee on Digital Transformation of the Verkhovna Rada was established by Resolution No. 19-IX of 29 August 2019 as a standing parliamentary committee. The Committee was created in response to the growing need for effective legislative and policy frameworks in the fields of digital innovation, electronic governance, cybersecurity, data protection, and emerging technologies, including AI. It plays an important role in shaping Ukraine’s digital transformation.
Objectives:
Develop and oversee legislation that supports Ukraine’s digital development and the responsible integration of technologies such as AI into the public and private sectors.Provide a platform for parliamentary debate on digital issues and exercises parliamentary oversight over relevant ministries and agencies. Engage with civil society, the private sector, and international partners to ensure inclusive and forward-looking digital policies. Supports trustworthy AI development, promotes democratic digital governance, and strengthens digital rights, transparency, and accountabilityFuture outlook:
The Parliamentary Committee on Digital Transformation of the Verkhovna Rada is expected to continue playing a central role in legislative efforts related to digital transformation, especially in the context of Ukraine’s EU accession process. This includes harmonisation of Ukrainian law with the EU acquis in areas such as digital services, privacy and data protection, digital markets, and AI regulation. The Committee will also facilitate parliamentary dialogue on digital security, online safety, digital inclusion, and innovation-friendly regulatory approaches.

items.title: National Stage of the International Teens in AI Hackathon
items.original_name: Національний етап міжнародного хакатону Teens in AI
items.org: Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine, Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Національний етап міжнародного хакатону Teens in AI
items.body:
The Teens in AI hackathon is a global initiative that empowers teenagers to use artificial intelligence to solve real-world problems. In 2024, Ukraine held its national stage, where young participants developed AI-based projects addressing education, mental health, and accessibility. The initiative aims to promote youth innovation, digital skills, and ethical AI use across more than 40 countries.

The Teens in AI initiative is an international hackathon programme aimed at engaging young people in the development of ethical and socially beneficial applications of artificial intelligence (AI). Launched globally in over 40 countries, it provides a platform for teenagers to gain practical experience in AI and develop projects that address real-world challenges.

In 2024, Ukraine hosted its first national stage of the hackathon, supported by the Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine and the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine. Ten teams of teenagers from across the country presented AI-based solutions on issues such as sign language translation, PTSD support for veterans, and combating cyberbullying. The initiative also included workshops and lectures that helped participants strengthen their technical and problem-solving skills.
Impact:
Three winning teams were selected for their innovative and socially impactful projects. One of them, ConnectAbility, developed an AI-powered application to teach sign language and act as a gesture-based voice translator. This project will participate in the international selection round alongside teams from other countries.
Objectives:
The Teens in AI initiative contributes to fostering digital literacy, ethical awareness, and innovation among youth. It supports the development of inclusive, socially conscious AI applications while equipping young people with the skills needed for the future digital economy."

items.title: Expert Committee on the Development of Artificial Intelligence in Ukraine under the Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine
items.original_name: Експертно-консультаційний комітет з розвитку сфери штучного інтелекту в Україні при Міністерстві цифрової трансформації України
items.org: Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine
items.category: National – AI governance bodies or mechanisms
items.document_name: Експертно-консультаційний комітет з розвитку сфери штучного інтелекту в Україні при Міністерстві цифрової трансформації України
items.body:
Expert Committee on the Development of Artificial Intelligence was created by the Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine to support the safe and ethical development of artificial intelligence. It brings together experts to provide input on national AI policy and strategy. The initiative helps ensure that AI in Ukraine is developed in a responsible and trustworthy way.

The Expert Committee on the Development of Artificial Intelligence in Ukraine was established in December 2019 by the Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine. It serves as a multi-stakeholder platform for shaping AI-related policy and regulatory approaches in Ukraine. The Committee includes experts from academia, civil society, the private sector, government bodies, and international organisations.
Objectives: 
To support the development of AI that is ethical, safe, human-centric, and aligned with democratic values and international best practices. Developme Ukraine’s AI policy by initiating broad discussions on regulatory approaches, including a roadmap for AI regulation. This roadmap was developed using a bottom-up model that emphasises the role of businesses and civil society in self-regulation and ethical implementation of AI technologies. Through open dialogue and collaboration, the Committee works to ensure that Ukrainian AI solutions are competitive globally and aligned with European standards, especially in light of the upcoming EU AI Regulation.
 Engage in educational initiatives. It supported the creation of teaching materials on artificial intelligence (AI) for upper secondary school students, hosted on the UNICEF Learning Passport platform. Facilitate international cooperation, public discussions on AI ethics, technological sovereignty, human rights, and innovation, and it has organised events on AI governance in partnership with international experts. It also cooperates with the Ombudsman’s Office and other institutions on the development of legal frameworks that respect fundamental rights."The Committee operates through thematic working groups: 
AI and Public GovernanceAI and EducationAI and SecurityAI Regulation

items.title: CDTO Campus AI Faculty
items.original_name: Факультет зі штучного інтелекту CDTO Campus
items.org: Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Факультет зі штучного інтелекту CDTO Campus
items.body:
The AI Faculty of CDTO Campus provides public sector leaders and digital transformation specialists with practical knowledge and skills in artificial intelligence (AI). It was created to help government officials understand and use AI effectively, improving public services and decision-making. The programme offers training developed with international partners to ensure modern and relevant learning.

The AI Faculty of CDTO Campus develops key competencies in artificial intelligence (AI) for digital transformation specialists, guiding them in the effective use of AI technologies to modernise state processes, optimise public services, and advance Ukraine’s digital transformation. Its programmes help shape a new governance model where decisions rely on data analysis, and AI acts as a driver of innovation and sustainable development. 
Since its launch, the AI Faculty has expanded to include educational programmes with global partners such as Microsoft, Cisco, EU4DigitalUA, and Apolitical, and its curriculum continues to evolve in line with Ukraine’s needs and international best practices in AI governance.
The following programmes are included in the AI Faculty:
Introduction to Artificial Intelligence in Plain LanguageImplementation of Artificial Intelligence in E-GovernanceCloud Platforms and AI for Enhancing Productivity and SecurityFundamentals of Artificial Intelligence

items.title: Big Course on Artificial Intelligence in Education
items.original_name: Великий курс про штучний інтелект в освіті
items.org: Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine, Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Великий курс про штучний інтелект в освіті
items.body:
The “Big Course on Artificial Intelligence in Education” is a professional development programme for educators, educational institution staff, lecturers, scientists, researchers, and students in Ukraine. It provides training on responsible AI use in teaching, assessment, academic integrity, and legal aspects, and builds upon the Recommendations on Responsible AI Use in Higher Education, developed by the Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine and the Ministry of Education and Science

The “Big Course on Artificial Intelligence in Education” is a professional training programme designed for university lecturers in Ukraine. Organised by the NGO Progresylni with the support of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine and the Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine, the course builds upon the Recommendations on Responsible AI Use in Higher Education developed by the Expert Advisory Committee on AI at the Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine.
Objectives:
The programme addresses key topics related to integrating AI into teaching and learning processes. These include new pedagogical approaches, academic integrity, assessment practices, personalisation of learning, and the legal and ethical dimensions of AI use in education. Methodology:
The course is delivered online and combines lectures, public discussions, and practical workshops, with participation from leading Ukrainian and international experts.Upon successful completion and passing of the final test, participants receive a certificate of professional development. The course aims to foster responsible AI use in higher education and to enhance educators’ capacity to adapt to the digital transformation of learning environments.
This initiative contributes to the professional growth of Ukrainian educators, strengthens the culture of responsible AI integration in higher education, and aligns national practices with international standards of AI use in education.

items.title: AI Centre of Excellence under the Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine
items.original_name: Центр передового досвіду з питань штучного інтелекту при Міністерстві цифрової трансформації України
items.org: Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine
items.category: National – AI governance bodies or mechanisms
items.document_name: Центр передового досвіду з питань штучного інтелекту при Міністерстві цифрової трансформації України
items.body:
WINWIN AI Centre of Excellence is a cutting-edge hub for AI development and integration. It will drive the transformation of government, business, and society while strengthening Ukraine’s global competitiveness. The Centre will implement AI in public administration and key sectors such as defence, healthcare, education, and business.

The AI Centre of Excellence was launched in 2025 by the Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine as the first national institution dedicated to accelerating the development and integration of AI across public governance, defence, education, business, and healthcare. The Centre was created as part of Ukraine’s WINWIN innovation strategy 2030 and aims to enhance the country’s global competitiveness by transforming the state, economy, and society through responsible AI adoption.
Key objectives:
Brings together experts, infrastructure, and innovation capacity to address national priorities through applied AI solutions. Its primary focus is the development of national LLM and AI tools for the government and defence sectors. It also supports the implementation of AI in education, scientific research, and healthcare, while fostering the growth of start-ups and small and medium enterprises.Results:
In its first year, the Centre launched an AI incubator and initiated the development of a pipeline for piloting AI products in the public sector. Work began on 16 AI prototypes, with several expected to advance to MVP stage and transition into full-scale products. These efforts aim to test practical applications of AI and build implementation capacity across public services.
Impact:
A strategic goal of the Centre is to lay the technological foundation for Ukraine’s AI sovereignty. It has begun developing national infrastructure for AI deployment and is working on the development of a national large language model (LLM) tailored for public service use. The Centre is also shaping a technological strategy focused on scaling and integrating AI into major digital platforms, such as Diia (Ukraine’s mobile app for e-governance services), Mriia (a national digital education platform), and AI Legal (a planned tool for automating legal support in the public sector), as well as AI for EU integration and acquis alignment. While specific defence applications remain confidential, the Centre is expected to contribute to the development of AI-enabled solutions in the security sector."

items.title: “Science + Digital" Program
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This initiative aims to accelerate the digital transformation and digitalisation of science and the services that support the National Scientific and Technological System. The programme includes the completion of 94 projects funded under the AI and Data Science R&D Projects Programme in Public Administration, as well as the availability of 50 new courses offered through the national platform for massive open online courses (MOOCs).

The Science+Digital programme is part of Portugal's broader strategy to integrate digital technologies into scientific research and public administration. Managed by the Foundation for Science and Technology (FCT), the programme aims to:
Accelerate Digital Transformation: Implementing advanced digital solutions to modernize scientific research and public administration services.Enhance AI and Data Science Capabilities: Funding R&D projects that utilize artificial intelligence and data science to improve public sector operations.Expand Digital Education: Offering new online courses to build digital competencies among researchers, public servants, and citizens.The programme's initiatives include:
AI and Data Science R&D Projects: Supporting 94 projects that focus on the application of AI and data science in public administration.MOOCs: Launching 50 new online courses to enhance digital literacy and skills across various sectors.These initiatives are expected to:
Improve Public Sector Efficiency: By integrating AI and data science into public administration, leading to more effective governance.Foster Innovation: Encouraging the development of new technologies and solutions to address societal challenges.Promote Lifelong Learning: Providing accessible educational opportunities to continuously update skills in a rapidly changing digital landscape.

items.title: gIAp Intelligent Solution for Face-to-Face Service
items.org: gIAp Solução Inteligente para Atendimento Presencial
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
gIAp is a digital platform under development that aims to help public sector organisations optimise the delivery of in-person services using advanced data analysis. It is intended to match service supply with demand, evaluate efficiency, and offer suggestions for improvement based on data. The platform plans to integrate multiple sources of input, including citizen feedback, and expand its coverage over time.

The gIAp platform initiative seeks to address inefficiencies in how public services are delivered on site. Its goal is to evaluate patterns of demand and supply, identify bottlenecks, and propose data-driven scenarios to improve efficiency and user satisfaction. Through performance analytics, the tool would allow public administrators to make more informed decisions about staffing, opening hours, and resource allocation.
Key intended features include:
Integration of various data sources (e.g. administrative data, service usage statistics, citizen feedback)Scenario modelling to test changes (for instance, adjusting service hours or staff levels)Dashboards and visualisations for public officials to monitor performance over time

items.title: Ubbu Project
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The ubbu project primarily focuses on teaching computer science and programming to students in the 1st and 2nd cycles of basic education in Portugal.

This project aims to address digital exclusion, school failure, dropout rates, and youth unemployment by training teachers and promoting digital literacy among students. The curriculum includes programming concepts such as algorithms, events, variables, and functions, taught through animated videos, games, exercises and quizzes.

items.title: The Strategy for the Development of Artificial Intelligence Technologies until 2030
items.original_name: Sun’iy intellekt texnologiyalarini 2030-yilga qadar rivojlantirish strategiyasi
items.category: National – Strategy
items.document_name: Sun’iy intellekt texnologiyalarini 2030-yilga qadar rivojlantirish strategiyasi
items.body:
Uzbekistan is developing artificial intelligence in key sectors: healthcare, education, agriculture, fintech and banking, energy, as well as tax and customs. The national AI strategy aims to solve practical problems, increase efficiency, and benefit citizens, businesses, and the economy.

Uzbekistan’s national artificial intelligence (AI) initiative aims to accelerate the digital transformation of the country by introducing AI solutions into key economic and social sectors. The initiative addresses the need to modernise industries, improve decision‑making, and increase efficiency in sectors such as healthcare, education, agriculture, fintech and banking, energy, as well as tax and customs administration. By leveraging AI, the country seeks to reduce manual work, improve service quality, and foster innovation across both public and private sectors.
The initiative is guided by the National AI Strategy and Cabinet of Ministers Resolution No. 425 (2025), which outlines priority AI projects for 2025–2026. Its primary objectives are to:
Implement AI solutions that enhance the quality of services and operational efficiency in priority sectors;Develop local expertise and foster research and innovation through public‑private partnerships and startup support;Build the necessary digital and data infrastructure for sustainable AI deployment;Ensure that AI applications contribute to economic growth and social well‑being.Over time, the initiative is expected to evolve into a sustainable, institutionalized program. Key steps include developing ethical and legal frameworks for AI, integrating AI projects into sectoral digital strategies, and expanding pilot projects to nationwide implementations. Capacity‑building programs, training of AI specialists, and the creation of open data and research platforms will ensure long‑term scalability. Future phases will involve active collaboration with international partners to bring global best practices and advanced technologies to Uzbekistan.
Since its inception, the initiative has progressed from strategic planning to practical implementation. Initial efforts focused on defining priority sectors, adopting regulatory frameworks, and launching pilot projects. The current stage emphasizes execution, monitoring outcomes, and adjusting the approach based on measurable results. These efforts have been recognized by international platforms: in 2024, Uzbekistan rose by 17 positions in the Oxford Insights Government AI Readiness Index, reflecting significant progress in AI development and readiness.

items.title: The CroRIS Project: A National CRIS in Croatia
items.original_name: Projekt CroRIS: Nacionalni CRIS u Hrvatskoj
items.org: The Ministry of Science and Education
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Projekt CroRIS: Nacionalni CRIS u Hrvatskoj
items.body:
The Ministry of Science and Education in Croatia has developed a comprehensive database mapping the research competencies and innovation capacities of scientific institutions and private sector entities in the fields of artificial intelligence (AI) and space technologies. This initiative is part of the strategic project Science and Technology Foresight, co-financed by the European Union.

As part of the Science and Technology Foresight project (Contract reference number: KK.01.1.1.03.0001), the Ministry of Science and Education has established a comprehensive database that maps the research competencies and innovation capacities of scientific institutions and private sector entities operating in the areas of artificial intelligence (AI) and space technologies. This project aims to inform the development of the Croatian National Plan for the Development of AI.
Key aspects of the initiative include:
Database Development: The creation of a detailed database encompassing research competencies and innovation capacities in AI and space technologies.Strategic Planning: Utilising the database to inform the development of the Croatian National Plan for the Development of AI.EU Co-Funding: The project is co-financed by the European Union from the European Regional Development Fund.Implementation and Future Outlook:
Project Duration: The project is set to run from 1 December 2017 to 1 August 2023.Total Project Value: HRK 16,573,042.00, with HRK 15,494,132.14 provided by EU co-funding.Institutional Collaboration: The project is being implemented by the Ministry of Science and Education in cooperation with the University Computing Centre of the University of Zagreb (SRCE).

items.title: Technovation Girls
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
A global programme designed to empower girls aged 8–18 to identify and address social issues by creating technology-based solutions. The programme has been running in Portugal since 2018 and was relaunched in 2022 to reach even more participants. In 2023, around 400 students and 100 mentors participated across 14 districts and 60 localities. Students from more than 110 educational establishments participated, marking a 30% increase from the previous year.

This initiative is a global programme designed to empower girls aged 8–18 to identify and address social issues by creating technology-based solutions. 
The programme has been running in Portugal since 2018 and was relaunched in 2022 to reach even more participants. In 2023, around 400 students and 100 mentors participated across 14 districts and 60 localities. Students from more than 110 educational establishments participated, marking a 30% increase from the previous year. 
Out of the participating teams, 59 delivered complete technological and entrepreneurial projects, and 7 Portuguese teams advanced to the world semi-finalist stage.

items.title: Strategic framework of National Cloud Computing
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This strategic framework outlines the roadmap for the adoption and optimisation of cloud computing services in Czechia’s public sector.

The eGovernment Cloud framework is designed to promote efficient and secure information systems and ICT services, preventing wasteful spending and maximising the use of shared services in public administration.

items.title: Shared Data Pool
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Scheduled for launch in 2025, this initiative under the European Digital Programme aims to create a shared data pool to facilitate smoother and more efficient data sharing across public administrations.

By providing centralised access to key data resources, the initiative will allow various institutions to collaborate more effectively, streamline processes, and improve the delivery of public services.

items.title: Programme “Our second language”
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Programme aimed to teach computer programming in the school curriculum, combined with artificial intelligence.

This programme of the Research and Academic Computer Network (Naukowa i Akademicka Sieć Komputerowa – NASK) to teach computer programming in the school curriculum utilises an approach of solving tasks during class time on an online platform, combined with artificial intelligence. After a pilot programme with three municipalities, it is envisioned to scale this project nationwide, in conjunction with the Ministries of Digitalisation, Education and Finance (NASK, 2023[46]). This programme is not AI-specific.

items.title: Programme for the development of digital competencies
items.org: Center for the Development of Digital Competencies
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This horizontal multi-stakeholder programme, coordinated by the Center for the Development of Digital Competencies (Centrum Rozwoju Kompetencji Cyfrowych - CRKC), situated in the office of the Minister of Informatisation, aims to significantly increase the digital competencies of Poland’s population, both with regard to the general population, ICT specialists and particularly women.

The implementation of activities is taken place under the following five priorities: i) Development of digital education; ii) Providing everyone with opportunities to develop digital competencies; iii) Supporting digital competence of employees in various sectors; iv) Development of advanced digital competencies; v) Strengthening the management of digital competence development.
While this programme is not AI-specific, a specific component on AI is the “Activity to prepare teachers to develop students' skills in artificial intelligence in the educational process and to expand young people's skills in artificial intelligence” (2023-2025), led by the Ministry of Education.

items.title: Polish Development Fund (PFR) workshops
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
"The Polish Development Fund (PFR) launched (commercial) workshops on “Artificial Intelligence for Leaders” for businesses to understand the potential of AI and how to use it effectively in business processes (PFR, 2024[47]).

This initiative has been used by other national economic development institutions (e.g. the national economic development bank BGK). PFR also launched a free course on AI to familiarise the wider population with AI.

items.title: Policy on the use of Generative AI
items.original_name: Politika dwar l-użu tal-Intelliġenza Artifiċjali Ġenerattiva
items.org: Ministry for Education, Sport, Youth, Research, and Innovation
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Politika dwar l-użu tal-Intelliġenza Artifiċjali Ġenerattiva
items.body:
The Ministry for Education, Sport, Youth, Research, and Innovation is working to draft a framework for responsible generative AI in public administration. The goal is to set rules for accountability, transparency, security, and recourse in AI-supported decision making. The Directorate for Digital Literacy & Transversal Skills (DDLTS) aligns its work with both EU and UNESCO guidance on AI in education.

The ministry is preparing a policy framework for the responsible use of generative AI across public administration. The framework is intended to establish clear principles around accountability, transparency, security, and effective recourse for citizens when AI systems influence administrative decisions. This is part of a broader effort to ensure that AI systems used by government remain trustworthy, fair, and aligned with public values.
At the same time, the Directorate for Digital Literacy & Transversal Skills (DDLTS) is actively adopting and referencing European Union AI frameworks and UNESCO guidance in its work on AI in education. This shows a commitment to aligning national educational initiatives with international standards for ethical and responsible AI in learning contexts

items.title: Pilots for the Impact Assessment Human Rights and Algorithms
items.original_name: Proefprojecten voor de impactbeoordeling van mensenrechten en algoritmes
items.org: Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Proefprojecten voor de impactbeoordeling van mensenrechten en algoritmes
items.body:
The Dutch government has implemented pilot projects to promote the use of the Impact Assessment on Human Rights and Algorithms (IAMA) within public sector organizations. These pilots aim to ensure that the deployment of algorithms aligns with human rights principles and helps prevent unintended negative consequences.

In 2023, the Dutch Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations commissioned Rijks ICT Gilde (RIG) and Utrecht University (UU) to supervise a series of Fundamental Rights and Algorithms Impact Assessment (FRAIA) processes with government organizations. A total of 16 pilot projects were conducted, involving various public sector entities, to assess the human rights implications of algorithmic systems. These pilots aimed to build knowledge and expertise on issues regarding algorithms and human rights and to promote the use of the FRAIA tool among government organizations, particularly municipalities.
The FRAIA is a discussion and decision-making tool designed to facilitate interdisciplinary dialogue among those responsible for the development and use of algorithmic systems. It comprises a series of questions that need to be addressed when considering the development, procurement, adjustment, or use of an algorithm, ensuring that fundamental rights are safeguarded throughout the process.

items.title: National Semiconductor Strategy
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
The National Semiconductor Strategy aims to bolster Czechia’s semiconductor sector, aligning with EU-wide goals outlined in the Chip Act. The strategy targets a threefold growth in the semiconductor sector by 2029, with a focus on research, export, and highly skilled talent migration.

The National Semiconductor Strategy proposes five strategic objectives to enhance the Czech Republic's competitiveness in this critical area.
