The total estimated maximum cost associated with the implementation of the National Semiconductor Strategy is EUR 967 million. Approximately EUR 830 million (20 billion CZK) of this is earmarked for investment incentives for strategic investment actions in the semiconductor sector. These investment incentives will, in accordance with the current legislation, be subject to government approval and therefore the entire amount may not be allocated. The total direct support from the strategy to the semiconductor industry and its suppliers is approximately EUR 192 million.

items.title: NOLAI
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
NOLAI is a 10-year government-funded initiative that brings together academics, businesses, and schools to explore the potential of AI in education.

This initiative focuses on integrating smart technologies in primary, secondary, and special education to improve learning outcomes and develop AI-based educational tools.
Budget: 
EUR 91 million from the national growth fund, of which
EUR 36 million are refinancied by the EU’s RRF
EUR 53 million are reserved from the national growth fund

items.title: Introduction to machine learning
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
In the 2022–2023 school year, Romania introduced the optional subject “Introduction to Machine Learning” in upper secondary education (grades 11 and 12). This initiative, approved by the Ministry of Education through Order no. 4049/2022, aims to equip students with foundational digital skills essential for future careers. The curriculum was developed by a team of experts, including Dr. Viorica Păliucean, Dr. Răzvan Pașcanu, and others.

Romania's Ministry of Education launched the “Introduction to Machine Learning” course as part of a broader effort to integrate artificial intelligence (AI) concepts into the national curriculum. This move aligns with the country's commitment to enhancing digital literacy among students and preparing them for the evolving job market.
Key Objectives:
Curriculum Development: The course was developed by a team of experts, including Dr. Viorica Păliucean, Dr. Răzvan Pașcanu, and professors Antonia Haller, Dr. Miana Arișanu, and Emil Onea.Implementation: Starting from the 2022–2023 school year, the subject was introduced as an optional course in grades 11 and 12, allowing students to choose it based on their interests and career aspirations.Curricular Integration: The subject is part of the Technologies curricular area, reflecting the growing importance of digital competencies in education.

items.title: Important Project of Common European Interest in Microelectronics and Communication Technologies
items.org: Ministry of Industry and Trade, European Commission
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
As part of a Europe-wide initiative, this project supports the development of next-generation microelectronics and communication technologies in Czechia. It provides direct financial support to select companies involved in advancing semiconductors and microprocessor technologies, contributing to the EU's goals of technological autonomy (European Commission).

Czechia is actively involved in four projects with total funding of EUR 60 million. As part of its National Recovery Plan, the country is currently implementing the R&D phase, with an allocated budget of EUR 46 million running until 2026.

items.title: IT4Innovations Supercomputing Centre
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The IT4Innovations Supercomputing Centre plays a critical role in developing Czechia’s HPC capabilities. Hosting supercomputers like Barbora and Karolina, and being part of e-INFRA CZ, the centre actively supports research in AI and other advanced fields.

The centre also participates in international HPC projects through EuroHPC and the LUMI consortium, while preparing for quantum computing with LUMI-Q

items.title: INA Training Programs
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The National Institute of Administrative Management (INA) offers specialized training programs for public sector employees in areas such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), blockchain, quantum technologies, Internet of Things (IoT), and data science. These programs aim to enhance digital competencies, enabling civil servants to effectively manage digital transformation and procurement processes within government institutions.

The INA Training Programs are designed to address the evolving technological landscape and its impact on public administration. Key aspects include:
Curriculum Focus: Courses cover foundational and advanced topics in AI, blockchain, quantum computing, IoT, and data science, tailored to the needs of public sector professionals.Target Audience: Public sector employees seeking to develop skills that support digital governance, innovation, and the management of emerging technologies.Program Objectives:
Equip civil servants with the knowledge to implement and oversee digital projects.Enhance the ability to make informed decisions regarding digital procurement and integration of new technologies.Promote a culture of innovation and adaptability within government institutions.Delivery Format: Courses are offered through various modalities, including online platforms and in-person workshops, to accommodate diverse learning preferences and schedules.
Collaborations and Partnerships: The programs are developed in collaboration with academic institutions, industry experts, and international organizations to ensure relevance and quality.

items.title: Happy Code
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Happy Code Portugal is a technology and programming school that offers STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, and Mathematics) education to children and young people aged 5 to 17. Through a variety of programs—including extracurricular courses, holiday bootcamps, workshops, and professional training—it aims to develop future thinkers, creators, and entrepreneurs. The school has already trained over 50,000 students nationwide.

Happy Code Portugal is a national initiative dedicated to providing comprehensive digital education to children and young people. The school offers a range of programs designed to foster creativity, problem-solving, and entrepreneurship skills. Key aspects include:
Curriculum and Programs: Happy Code provides a complete and continuous curriculum in technology and programming. Programs are available in various formats, including extracurricular courses, holiday bootcamps, workshops, hackathons, and professional training. Age Range: The programs are designed for children and young people aged 5 to 17, ensuring age-appropriate content and teaching methods.Pedagogical Approach: The teaching methodology is based on the STEAM concept, integrating Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, and Mathematics to provide a holistic learning experience.Impact and Reach: Since its inception, Happy Code has trained over 50,000 students across Portugal, demonstrating its significant impact on digital education.Partnerships and Collaborations: Happy Code collaborates with schools, municipalities, companies, and social organizations to expand its reach and enhance the quality of its programs.

items.title: Engineers for 1 Day
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
A programme targeting elementary and secondary school students to challenge gender stereotypes in engineering and ICT through hands-on activities, mentoring, and professional experiences in collaboration with schools and municipalities.

The “Engineers for 1 Day” programme is a Portuguese initiative under INCoDe.2030 that seeks to challenge gender stereotypes in engineering and ICT by giving basic and secondary school students hands-on exposure to these fields. Through laboratory activities, mentoring, role-model sessions and professional experiences — delivered in partnership with schools, higher education institutions, industry and municipalities — it aims to inspire everyone to see engineering and tech careers as accessible.

items.title: DiGiNN Cyprus (European Digital Innovation Hub)
items.org: the European Union’s Digital Europe Programme (DIGITAL) under grant agreement 101083772 and the Deputy Ministry of Research, Innovation and Digital Policy of the Republic of Cyprus
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
DiGiNN (Cyprus Digital Innovation Hub) is a national one-stop-shop supporting companies and public sector organisations in their digital transformation journey. It offers services such as coaching, access to advanced infrastructure, investment support, and networking opportunities. The hub focuses on technologies like Artificial Intelligence, High-Performance Computing, and Cybersecurity.

DiGiNN is Cyprus’s European Digital Innovation Hub, co-funded by the EU Digital Europe Programme and the Deputy Ministry of Research, Innovation and Digital Policy. It serves as an end-to-end digital transformation partner for businesses and public institutions across the country.
Key Services Include:
Coaching & Mentoring: Personalised guidance from industry experts to support digital strategy and implementation.Advanced Infrastructure Access: Utilisation of state-of-the-art facilities for testing and development in areas like AI, HPC, and Cybersecurity.Investment Support: Assistance in identifying and securing funding opportunities for digital projects.Networking & Ecosystem Access: Facilitation of connections within the innovation ecosystem, including startups, SMEs, and research institutions.Strategic Objectives:
Enhance the digital maturity of SMEs.Foster innovations with high market potential.Mobilise investments for digital transformation projects.Increase the uptake of advanced digital technologies.Position public administration as a catalyst for productivity and competitiveness.

items.title: Czech Institute of Informatics, Robotics and Cybernetics
items.original_name: Český institut informatiky, robotiky a kybernetiky
items.org: Czech Institute of Informatics, Robotics and Cybernetics
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Český institut informatiky, robotiky a kybernetiky
items.body:
The Czech Institute of Informatics, Robotics and Cybernetics (CIIRC) is a leading research institute at the Czech Technical University in Prague. It focuses on advancing artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, and cybernetics, bridging academic research with industrial applications to foster innovation.

Established in 2013, CIIRC is dedicated to cutting-edge research in areas such as:
Artificial Intelligence (AI)Robotics and Machine PerceptionCyber-Physical SystemsIndustrial InformaticsCognitive Systems and NeurosciencesBiomedical Engineering and Assistive TechnologiesThe institute comprises several specialized departments, including:
INTSYS: Intelligent SystemsRMP: Robotics and Machine PerceptionIPA: Industrial Production and AutomationCOGSYS: Cognitive Systems and NeurosciencesBEAT: Biomedical Engineering and Assistive TechnologiesCIIRC's mission is to become a leading European center for AI, contributing to advancements in Industry 4.0 and smart city technologies. It actively collaborates with industrial partners, government agencies, and academic institutions to translate research into practical solutions. Notably, CIIRC is a founding partner and coordinator of the RICAIP project, a significant EU initiative in AI and Industry 4.0 research.

items.title: Competencies in Advanced Technologies for SMEs
items.original_name: Competențe în Tehnologii Avansate pentru IMM-uri
items.org: Authority for the Digitalisation of Romania (ADR)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Competențe în Tehnologii Avansate pentru IMM-uri
items.body:
The Competencies in Advanced Technologies for SMEs project, initiated by the Authority for the Digitalization of Romania (ADR) in 2022, aims to enhance the digital skills of employees in Romanian SMEs. Funded through the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (NRRP), Component 7, Investment 19, the project will support the digital transformation of a minimum of 2,000 SMEs by providing fully financed training programs. The project is set to conclude on December 16, 2025

The Competencies in Advanced Technologies for SMEs initiative addresses the need for upskilling employees in small and medium-sized enterprises to facilitate their digital transformation. The project is structured as follows:
Target Beneficiaries: The project aims to support the digital transformation of a minimum of 2,000 SMEs by enhancing the digital competencies of their employees.Training Programs: Employees of participating SMEs will have access to fully financed training programs designed to improve their skills in advanced technologies, thereby increasing the companies' competitiveness and innovation capacity.Implementation Timeline: The project commenced in 2022 and is scheduled for completion by December 16, 2025Digital4All Platform: In 2024, ADR launched the Digital4All platform in collaboration with Zitec to provide a seamless digital platform and tech training, aiming to boost SME digital skills across Romania

items.title: Academy of Innovative Applications of Digital Technologies (AI Tech)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
AI Tech is cooperation project between five universities to develop a model of systemic education of specialists in the field of artificial intelligence, machine learning and cybersecurity.

The developed solution, consisting of second-cycle university study programme, tutoring, IT projects, internship/study visits, summer schools, conferences and other cooperation projects, will be implemented on a large scale in 2021-27 by the involved universities.
Budget: EUR 12 million (PLN 52 million), of which EUR 10 million (PLN 44 million) co-financed by the EU under “Digital Poland” and European Regional Development Fund (ERDF)

items.title: AP Digital
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The AP Digital programme in Portugal is designed to enhance the digital skills of public sector employees, thereby accelerating the digital transformation within public administration. Key aspects include: i) Digital productivity tools: training employees to use digital tools effectively to improve productivity, ii) technical specialised training: for IT professionals and those in related roles within the public sector and iii) educating employees about new and emerging technologies.

The AP Digital 4.0 Programme is designed to address the digital skills gap within Portugal's public sector, aiming to:
Enhance Digital Literacy: Provide foundational training in digital tools and technologies to all public administration employees.Specialised IT Training: Offer advanced courses for IT professionals and those in related roles to deepen their technical expertise.Focus on Emerging Technologies: Educate employees on cutting-edge areas such as data science, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, and natural language processing.The programme is structured to eliminate information exclusion, improve the ability to use essential tools, and develop skills in emerging digital areas.
In 2022, the programme aimed to qualify and retrain approximately 9,800 public administration workers, with a goal to train 65,000 workers and managers by 2023.

items.title: AMA Academy
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Digital Academy for Citizens offers free, fully online courses aimed at enhancing digital literacy and competencies among the Portuguese population. This initiative is managed by the Agency for State Technological Reform (ARTE), a public institute under the Ministry of State Reform.

The Digital Academy for Citizens is a national initiative designed to improve digital literacy across Portugal. It provides citizens with access to free, certified online courses covering a wide range of topics, including artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, digital citizenship, and cloud computing. The academy aims to empower individuals to navigate and thrive in an increasingly digital world.
Key objectives of the academy include:
Enhancing digital skills among citizens to foster inclusion and participation in the digital economy.Supporting lifelong learning by offering accessible and flexible learning opportunities.Promoting digital transformation within communities and small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).The academy offers a variety of courses, such as:
Artificial Intelligence: Industry, Business, and Services – An intermediate-level course exploring the impact of AI across sectors.Digital Innovation Based on Statistical Data – A course focusing on leveraging data for digital innovation.Introduction to Cloud Computing – A beginner-level course covering the fundamentals of cloud technologies.Digital Communication Tools – A course aimed at improving communication skills in digital environments.

items.title: AI4Youth
items.org: Ministry of Economic Development and Technology
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This programme, piloted in 2019 under the auspices of the Ministry of Economic Development and Technology, aimed to teach secondary school students and help them develop competences related to the use of artificial intelligence.

The programme included a competition in which prizes are awarded to student teams for the development of solutions to societal problem through the application of AI.

items.title: AI training courses
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Institute for the Public Service of Malta is implementing training programmes for public officers in Artificial Intelligence under a three-year agreement with educational institutions and government bodies. The training aims to build knowledge in AI fundamentals, applications, and responsible use. It is designed to improve how public servants use AI to enhance service delivery.

In 2022, the Maltese government signed a Memorandum of Understanding involving the Institute for the Public Service, University of Malta, MCAST, eSkills Malta Foundation, and the Office of the Prime Minister. This agreement covers three years of AI training for public officers.
The aim of the training is to raise the capacity of public servants to apply Artificial Intelligence in government operations and internal processes. The training is expected to include courses at various levels, scholarships for those wishing to specialise, and collaboration with international institutions (e.g. drawing on material from Helsinki University).
While there is public documentation of these plans, the precise structure of an “Introduction to AI” module—covering machine learning, applications, and fundamentals—has not been fully detailed in the sources reviewed. Some content is clearly about foundational AI knowledge, but without full breakdowns in all cases.

items.title: AI for justice
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Polish Ministry of Justice has launched a dedicated website to provide current and verified information on the applications of artificial intelligence (AI) in the Polish judiciary. The site serves as a resource for a broad audience interested in understanding AI's impact on the administration of justice.

The Ministry of Justice's initiative aims to enhance transparency and accessibility regarding the integration of AI technologies within the Polish judicial system. The dedicated website offers:
Scientific Articles and Analyses: Access to scholarly articles, including translations of foreign publications, providing insights into AI applications in justice.Expert Meetings and Conferences: Information on events such as the "Ius ex silico" conference held in April 2023, focusing on AI's role in the judiciary.Collaborations and Partnerships: Updates on international cooperation, including discussions with the Ministry of Justice of South Korea and joint initiatives with Germany on digital transformation in justice.These efforts are part of Poland's broader strategy to modernize the judiciary through digitalization and AI, aiming to improve efficiency, accessibility, and fairness in legal proceedings.

items.title: AI chatbot
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Servizz.gov Chatbot provides 24/7 online assistance for people seeking information about Maltese government services. Users can ask questions in Maltese or English, and the chatbot handles many inquiries without needing a live agent. It helps reduce wait times and improve access to public services across the country.

The Servizz.gov Chatbot is part of the Maltese government’s Servizz.gov portal, a unified hub that brings together many public services, forms, and government interactions. It was developed to make government services more accessible and efficient by providing immediate, AI-powered support for citizens. 
Key features and functioning:
The chatbot is available 24/7 and supports both Maltese and English.It helps with a broad range of public service queries, including those about services, forms, online applications, and general information.It is integrated with Servizz.gov’s interface together with options for live agent interaction when the chatbot cannot address a queryUsage and impact:
Over the first eight months, the chatbot handled about 40,000 user interactions for specific types of information.It has helped reduce the load on customer care agents, especially for routine or frequently asked questions.

items.title: AI Centre Lipik
items.org: Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The AI Centre Lipik offers a six-month training programme in artificial intelligence and programming, combining theoretical and practical instruction. It supports emerging AI startups through an incubator that provides mentoring, business development, and infrastructure. It aims to strengthen skills, innovation, and AI-based entrepreneurship in the Lipik region and beyond.

The AI Centre Lipik, founded by the Lipik Development and Touristic Agency (LIRA d.o.o.) in 2020, consists of an Education Centre and a Startup Incubator. The Education Centre runs a six-month AI programmer training programme involving both theory and hands-on practice, offering over 1,000 hours of teaching, with stipends and living support for participants. After completion, successful graduates are offered employment or support in starting their own business.
The Startup Incubator is designed to help new and emerging companies working in AI and programming. It offers mentoring, business training, consulting, and access to infrastructure. As of the latest data, about 15 startups have been incubated in Lipik, employing several dozen people. The centre is also expanding its entrepreneurial modules, accelerator, and lab facilities.
AI Centre Lipik is part of the AI & Gaming EDIH network (European Digital Innovation Hub) focused on helping SMEs, the public sector, and startups adopt digital technologies like AI, gamification, blockchain, and IoT. It offers services like “test-before-invest,” training, consulting, networking, and business support.

items.title: AI Business School for Public Administration
items.original_name: Escola de Negócios de IA para a Administração Pública
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Escola de Negócios de IA para a Administração Pública
items.body:
The AI Business School for Public Administration, launched by the National Institute of Administration (INA) in partnership with six higher education institutions and Microsoft Portugal, provides online training to senior public sector leaders. The programme focuses on ethical AI use, project management, and leveraging AI to modernise public services and enhance efficiency.

The AI Business School for Public Administration is a strategic initiative designed to address the digital skills gap in Portugal's public administration. By offering targeted training to senior leaders, the programme aims to foster the adoption of AI technologies in public sector organisations, ensuring that they can effectively manage and implement AI-driven projects.
Key Features:
Target Audience: Senior public sector leaders, including directors and managers, with a focus on those in positions of responsibility within public institutions.Curriculum: The training covers a range of topics, including:Ethical considerations in AI deploymentProject management methodologies for AI initiativesData analysis and interpretationImplementation of intelligent bots and automation toolsStrategic planning for AI integration in public servicesDelivery Mode: The programme is delivered online, allowing participants to engage with the content flexibly and at their own pace.Partnerships: In addition to the INA and Microsoft Portugal, the programme collaborates with six esteemed higher education institutionsObjectives:
Enhance AI Literacy: Equip public sector leaders with the knowledge and skills necessary to understand and apply AI technologies in their organisations.Promote Ethical AI Use: Ensure that AI applications in the public sector are developed and implemented in an ethical and responsible manner.Improve Public Service Delivery: Leverage AI to streamline processes, improve decision-making, and enhance the efficiency of public services.Foster Innovation: Encourage a culture of innovation within public institutions by integrating AI solutions that address contemporary challenges.

items.title: "Science+Training" Program
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Science+Training Programme is a national initiative in Portugal aimed at enhancing the innovation and entrepreneurship ecosystem within higher education institutions. It provides funding to support basic research, promote knowledge transfer, reduce researcher precariousness, and strengthen the link between companies and society. Key components include the ERC-Portugal and FCT-Tenure programmes, which focus on talent attraction, retention, and the stabilization of scientific careers.

The Science+Training Programme is part of Portugal's broader strategy to bolster its research and innovation landscape. Implemented by the Foundation for Science and Technology (FCT), this programme is designed to:
Support basic research by providing funding to higher education institutions.Promote knowledge transfer between academia and industry to foster innovation.Reduce researcher precariousness by offering stable career opportunities.Strengthen the link between companies and society, ensuring that research outcomes contribute to societal development.A significant component of the programme is the FCT-Tenure Programme, which aims to stabilize scientific careers by offering permanent positions to PhD researchers. In its first edition (2024), the programme co-financed the hiring of up to 1,000 PhD researchers for permanent positions, with an additional 400 positions expected in the second edition (2026) dp.tecnico.ulisboa.pt+1.
Another key initiative is the ERC-Portugal Programme, which supports Portuguese researchers in participating in the European Research Council (ERC) funding schemes.

items.title: Wallonian Digital Agency
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Wallonian Digital Agency, under the DigitalWallonia4.AI programme, has supported over 500 AI projects across Walloon companies and public organisations. These projects span various levels of technological maturity and aim to drive innovation and adoption of AI technologies. The agency's efforts extend beyond start-ups to encompass broader public and private sector engagement.

The Walloon Digital Agency (Agence du Numérique) leads the DigitalWallonia4.AI programme, a cornerstone initiative advancing artificial intelligence (AI) adoption across Wallonia. The programme aims to strengthen the region’s digital ecosystem by supporting the development and integration of AI solutions in both public and private sectors.
Since its launch, DigitalWallonia4.AI has supported more than 500 AI projects across Walloon companies and public organisations. These initiatives cover a wide spectrum of technological maturity — from early-stage experimentation to large-scale deployment — and address diverse domains such as manufacturing, healthcare, logistics, and public administration. By doing so, the programme accelerates innovation and enhances the competitiveness of Walloon enterprises.
The initiative takes a comprehensive and inclusive approach, engaging not only start-ups but also established firms and public institutions. Through funding support, awareness-raising activities, and access to expertise, the Walloon Digital Agency ensures that AI technologies are accessible to organisations of all sizes. The programme also fosters collaboration between academia, industry, and government to promote knowledge exchange and the responsible use of AI.

items.title: Use case pilots
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
AI is being adopted across Government Departments and public service bodies. The Department of Public Expenditure, NDP Delivery and Reform, is conducting use case pilot projects. A related objective is implementing a vendor-neutral approach to AI development to develop a generic “building block” approach for reusable services.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is being increasingly integrated across Irish Government Departments and public service bodies to improve service delivery, decision-making, and operational efficiency. The initiative addresses the challenge of leveraging AI in a coordinated and scalable manner, ensuring that innovations provide tangible benefits to citizens while maintaining transparency and accountability.
The Department of Public Expenditure, NDP Delivery and Reform (DPENDR) is leading several pilot projects to test practical use cases of AI within government operations. These pilots explore how AI can streamline processes, enhance public services, and support evidence-based policymaking. The projects provide valuable insights into the potential and limitations of AI, helping to inform broader adoption strategies.
A key objective of the initiative is to implement a vendor-neutral approach to AI development. This strategy promotes the creation of generic “building blocks”, reusable AI services that can be adapted across multiple departments and functions. By standardising approaches and tools, the initiative aims to reduce duplication, improve interoperability, and accelerate the deployment of AI solutions throughout the public sector.

items.title: Teton.ai
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Founded in 2020, Teton.ai provides an AI nurse companion to support patient care and improve nursing staff efficiency. Teton.ai uses sensors to monitor patient movements and predict when there could be urgent needs or potential falls. The technology is in use at the North Denmark Regional Hospital as of 2024.

Teton.ai has created a sensor and AIpowered system that gives nurses more time to care for patients by removing unnecessary routine tasks. The solution consists of an AI-driven nurse companion that revolutionises patient safety and staff efficiency through the use of advanced AI and camera technology. More specifically, the solution monitors patient movements, analysing patterns to pre-emptively alert staff to potential falls and urgent care needs, reducing fall incidents by 83%. The system not only facilitates quicker staff intervention, enhancing patient safety, but also serves as a preventive tool by measuring patient activity and sleep rhythms. These insights enable targeted care strategies, preventing incidents before they occur. Moreover, the system automates routine checks and documentation, cutting workload by 25% during evening and night time. This significantly eases staff burden, minimises burnout, and frees up more time for direct patient care. The solution is already in use at North Denmark Regional Hospital, where it not only enhances patient and resident safety but also incorporates privacy into its design.

items.title: Start-up Ecosystem Support
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This initiative aims to enhance the start-up environment by providing support to entrepreneurs, particularly in the fields of innovation and technology, with a strong emphasis on AI. It focuses on improving access to venture capital and fostering a more effective policy framework for entrepreneurship. The initiative seeks to position Bulgaria as a competitive hub for startups, encouraging growth and development in various high-value industries.

The Startup Ecosystem Support initiative in Bulgaria is designed to strengthen the country’s entrepreneurial environment, with a particular focus on innovation, technology, and artificial intelligence (AI). It addresses key challenges faced by start-ups, including limited access to funding, mentorship, and supportive policy frameworks, which can hinder the growth and scaling of early-stage companies.
The initiative provides targeted support for entrepreneurs, including guidance on business development, access to venture capital, and facilitation of connections with investors and industry partners. By improving the availability of resources and knowledge, it helps start-ups implement innovative technologies and develop AI-based products and services.
A central goal of the programme is to foster a robust and sustainable start-up ecosystem in Bulgaria. This involves not only supporting individual ventures but also shaping policies that encourage entrepreneurship, reduce barriers to market entry, and stimulate collaboration between start-ups, research institutions, and established companies.
By enhancing access to capital, expertise, and supportive frameworks, the initiative seeks to position Bulgaria as a competitive hub for high-value start-ups. It promotes growth and development across multiple industries, strengthening the country’s capacity for innovation and contributing to broader economic and technological advancement.

items.title: Smart Specialisation Strategy 2023-2029
items.org: Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
A research and innovation strategy that provides a framework to foster innovation through developing research and innovation infrastructure and collaboration between business and research institutions. It supports applied research and development activities in smart and green solutions, providing grant funding for AI-related research projects and focusing investments in areas where Croatia has competitive advantages and research strengths.

The Smart Specialisation Strategy 2023–2029 is Croatia’s national research and innovation framework, designed to strengthen the country’s innovation ecosystem by fostering collaboration between business, academia, and research institutions. The strategy addresses the need to focus resources on areas where Croatia has competitive advantages, supporting the development and application of advanced technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI).
A core objective of the strategy is to support applied research and development activities that generate practical solutions for economic and societal challenges. This includes promoting smart and green technologies, accelerating the translation of research into commercial applications, and encouraging innovation-driven growth across key sectors. By concentrating efforts on areas of research strength, the strategy ensures that investments are impactful and aligned with Croatia’s long-term development priorities.
The strategy also provides grant funding for AI-related research projects, enabling businesses and research institutions to explore and implement innovative AI applications. These investments aim to enhance Croatia’s technological capabilities, improve competitiveness, and support evidence-based policymaking.

items.title: Shared Government Data Centre
items.org: Department of Public Expenditure, NDP Delivery and Reform (DPENDR)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The strategy aims at supporting digitalisation of Government services through delivery of high-quality Data Centre facilities.

Ireland’s Shared Government Data Centre was created to support the digitalisation of public services by providing a modern, secure, and energy-efficient facility for storing and managing government data. As more services move online, the government needed reliable infrastructure to replace outdated and scattered data centres across departments.
The centre’s main goal is to offer a shared, high-quality facility that reduces duplication, lowers costs, and improves data security. Managed by the Office of Public Works (OPW), it serves multiple public bodies, helping ensure consistent standards in how data is stored and protected.
By centralising services, the initiative supports broader goals like sustainability, cybersecurity, and efficient use of public resources. It also lays the groundwork for future developments, such as AI and advanced data tools, by offering scalable and modern infrastructure.
As digital demands grow, the Shared Government Data Centre will continue to play a central role in delivering secure, high-quality public services.

items.title: Research Ireland Centre for Future Networks and Communications (CONNECT)
items.org: Research Ireland Centre for Future Networks and Communications (CONNECT)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
CONNECT’s research notably focuses on edge computing, e.g. under its Sustainable IoT research area, which addresses challenges such as: 
Energy harvesting and storage, with power-management algorithms to allow the device to be completely energy autonomous for its entire lifetime
Efficient protocols and networking principles for connecting devices at the edge to the network
Highly reconfigurable software-defined devices based on low-power platforms.

CONNECT, a leading research centre, focuses on addressing key challenges in edge computing, especially within its Sustainable Internet of Things (IoT) research area. As IoT devices become increasingly common in everyday life—used in homes, cities, industries, and agriculture—they often operate in environments where energy supply is limited and connectivity can be unreliable. This creates a pressing need for smarter, more energy-efficient, and adaptable technologies that can work independently at the edge of the network without constant human intervention or connection to centralized data centres.
One of the main objectives of CONNECT’s research is to develop devices that are completely energy autonomous, meaning they can harvest and store energy from their surroundings and manage power intelligently to last for their entire operational lifetime. This involves creating advanced power-management algorithms that help devices use energy efficiently and avoid wasting power. Additionally, CONNECT works on building efficient communication protocols and networking methods to connect these edge devices reliably to broader networks, even in challenging conditions where bandwidth or connectivity may be limited.
The research also focuses on designing highly flexible and reconfigurable devices. These devices use low-power hardware platforms combined with software that can be easily updated or changed, allowing them to adapt to different tasks or environments over time without requiring physical changes. This flexibility is critical to support the wide variety of IoT applications and to extend the usefulness and sustainability of the devices.

items.title: Research Infrastructure Development Roadmap of the Republic of Croatia 2023-2027
items.org: Government of Croatia and European Commission
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
A national roadmap that prioritises investments in research infrastructures focused on AI development and application. The roadmap recognises AI as a key solution to addressing social challenges, acknowledging its impact on the labour market and its role in transforming business and social processes. The strategy emphasises international cooperation through knowledge exchange and expert collaboration in AI development.

The Research Infrastructure Development Roadmap of the Republic of Croatia 2023–2027 is a national strategy that identifies priority investments in research infrastructures, with a strong emphasis on artificial intelligence (AI) development and applications. The roadmap addresses the growing need to equip Croatia’s research ecosystem with advanced facilities and capabilities to explore AI solutions that can tackle complex societal challenges.
The initiative recognises AI as a key driver of innovation across multiple domains, from transforming business processes and social services to reshaping the labour market. By investing in AI-focused research infrastructure, Croatia aims to create environments where researchers, public institutions, and private sector actors can collaborate on the development and deployment of AI technologies.
A significant aspect of the roadmap is its emphasis on international collaboration and knowledge exchange. The strategy promotes partnerships with global AI research centres, participation in European initiatives, and engagement with experts to ensure that Croatian AI research remains aligned with international standards and best practices.

items.title: Radiobotics - RBfracture
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Radiobotics product RBfracture, which detects fractures, effusions, and lipohemarthrosis with high accuracy has been introduced in Denmark to support the diagnostic process.

Radiobotics’ flagship product, RBfracture, detects fractures, effusions, and lipohemarthrosis with unparalleled accuracy, trained on a dataset of over 300,000 images from the US and Europe. This technology expedites diagnosis, ensures comprehensive evaluations, and adapts to diverse clinical settings. RBfracture addresses traditional radiology challenges by providing clinicians a sophisticated tool for precise radiographic interpretation. Powered by advanced algorithms, the project accelerates the diagnostic process and enhances treatment outcomes. Its cross-cultural training dataset reflects a global healthcare commitment. By fostering collaboration, constantly refining technology based on clinician feedback, Radiobotics aims to revolutionise radiological diagnostics, ushering in a new era of precision medicine.

items.title: RAIT - Radiological AI test center
items.original_name: Innovation Unit of the Radiology Departments at Herlev and Gentofte Hospital and Bispebjerg and Frederiksberg Hospital
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Innovation Unit of the Radiology Departments at Herlev and Gentofte Hospital and Bispebjerg and Frederiksberg Hospital
items.body:
The Radiological AI test center aims to accelerate the development and use of AI technology in radiology practice.

The Radiological Artificial Intelligence Test center (RAIT) combines the experience of the Innovation unit at the radiology department at Herlev and Gentofte Hospital with the radiological Research group at Frederiksberg and Bispebjerg Hospital. With the unique combination of skills and data across the hospitals, RAIT aspires to establish a collective knowledge and competence center for developing, validating, and implementing AI applications in medical radiological imaging in the Capital Region of Denmark. With the joint forces, we seek to move barriers, standardize processes, and generate excellent best practices for validating and implementing AI in Radiology to generate equal health for all.
RAIT consists of several AI-projects and a joint project office across Bispebjerg and Herlev Hospital. We ensure that good practice is shared and obstacles common to AI projects are identified and handled, fostering the future way for AI projects. Furthermore, we work in close collaboration with our partners, clinicians, national and international companies, universities, ministries etc. and support a non-competitive environment.

items.title: Quantum 2030
items.org: Department of Further and Higher Education, Research, Innovation and Science
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
Ireland’s National Quantum Technology Strategy (Department of Further and Higher Education, Research, Innovation and Science, 2023[8]). It consists of five pillars:

Excellent fundamental and applied quantum research 
Top science and engineering talent
National and international collaboration
Innovation, entrepreneurship and economic competitiveness
Build stakeholder awareness of quantum technologies and their benefits

Ireland’s National Quantum Technology Strategy (2023) outlines a plan to build the country’s strength in quantum science and its applications. Quantum technologies—like ultra-fast computing, secure communications, and advanced sensors—are expected to impact many sectors. The strategy aims to prepare Ireland to take part in this global shift and benefit from future breakthroughs.
The strategy is built on five main pillars: supporting strong fundamental and applied research, developing top science and engineering talent, promoting national and international collaboration, boosting innovation and entrepreneurship, and raising awareness of quantum’s potential. Together, these actions aim to create a strong, connected ecosystem for quantum in Ireland.
It involves universities, public research bodies, industry, and international partners. The goal is to ensure Ireland can compete globally, support new businesses, and use quantum technologies responsibly and effectively.
As the field grows, this strategy provides a foundation for future investment, skills development, and global partnerships—positioning Ireland as an active player in the emerging quantum economy.

items.title: PRODIGIT project
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The PRODIGIT project, a collaboration between the Presidential Council of Tax Justice (CPGT) and the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF), aims to modernise judicial tax proceedings through AI-powered tools. The initiative focuses on enhancing efficiency and accuracy in tax-related legal processes while reducing administrative burdens. PRODIGIT leverages AI techniques such as legal summarisation and information extraction to support tax judges.

The PRODIGIT project is a collaborative initiative between the Presidential Council of Tax Justice (Consiglio di Presidenza della Giustizia Tributaria, CPGT) and the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF), aimed at modernising judicial tax proceedings through the use of artificial intelligence (AI). The project addresses key challenges in tax-related legal processes, including lengthy case handling, administrative complexity, and the need for more accurate decision-making.
PRODIGIT focuses on enhancing efficiency and accuracy in judicial procedures by integrating AI-powered tools into the workflow of tax judges. The initiative employs techniques such as legal summarisation, information extraction, and data-driven analysis to assist judges in processing cases, identifying relevant information, and making informed decisions more quickly. This approach reduces the administrative burden on judicial staff while maintaining the quality and reliability of legal outcomes.
The project involves close collaboration between judicial authorities, public administration, and AI experts, ensuring that technological solutions are tailored to the legal context and practical needs of the tax justice system. By embedding AI into judicial processes, PRODIGIT demonstrates the potential of AI to support public sector transformation in specialised legal domains.

items.title: National-Level Deliberations on Draft Legislation as part of the EU AI4Deliberation project
items.category: National – AI governance bodies or mechanisms
items.body:
In Greece, every draft law is published by the relevant Ministry on opengov.gr, typically for a two-week period, during which citizens can express their opinions – within the AI4Deliberation project, several AI features will be tested during specific deliberations hosted on open-gov.gr. For instance, the project will explore the AI Summarisation functionality for processing deliberation comments.

Greece is participating in the EU AI4Deliberation project, which explores how artificial intelligence (AI) can enhance citizen engagement and improve public consultations on draft legislation. The initiative addresses the challenge of efficiently processing and analysing public feedback during law-making processes, where governments must consider large volumes of citizen comments to inform policy decisions.
In Greece, every draft law is published by the relevant ministry on opengov.gr for a typical two-week consultation period, during which citizens can provide feedback. Within the AI4Deliberation project, several AI-powered features are being tested to support these consultations, aiming to make the deliberation process more efficient, transparent, and inclusive. One key feature under evaluation is AI summarisation, which processes and synthesises public comments to highlight trends, common concerns, and suggestions.
The project involves collaboration between Greek ministries, the National Centre for Public Administration & Local Government, and European research partners, ensuring that AI tools are adapted to the legal, social, and linguistic context of Greece. By leveraging AI, the initiative seeks to reduce the administrative burden on public officials while ensuring that citizen input is accurately considered in legislative processes.

items.title: InvestEU Guarantee Programme
items.org: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The InvestEU Guarantee Programme is a financial initiative aimed at supporting SMEs in Europe. The programme offers loans of up to EUR 2 million to businesses focusing on innovation and digital transformation. It specifically covers projects that incorporate AI technologies, facilitating access to funding for companies looking to enhance their technological capabilities.

The InvestEU Guarantee Programme is a major financial initiative designed to support small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) across Europe, including Bulgaria, in pursuing innovation and digital transformation. The programme addresses a critical challenge faced by many Bulgarian companies — limited access to financing for high-risk, technology-driven projects, including those involving artificial intelligence (AI).
Under the InvestEU framework, Bulgarian businesses can access loans of up to EUR 2 million to develop and implement projects that integrate innovative and digital technologies. By providing a financial guarantee, the programme helps reduce investment risks for lenders, making it easier for companies to secure funding for activities that advance technological capacity and competitiveness.
A key focus of the initiative is to promote the adoption of AI technologies in business operations, from process automation and data analytics to the creation of AI-based products and services. The InvestEU Guarantee Programme thus supports Bulgaria’s broader goals of digitalisation and innovation, contributing to the development of a resilient and future-ready business ecosystem.

items.title: Institute of Information and Communication Technologies (IICT-BAS)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Institute of Information and Communication Technologies, established by the Bulgarian Academy of Sciences in 2010, advances research and innovation in information and communication technologies. The institute maintains state-of-the-art computing facilities and conducts research in advanced computing infrastructure, big data processing and AI. IICT-BAS provides specialised AI training and high-performance computing resources, with an emphasis on supporting doctoral research programmes.

The Institute of Information and Communication Technologies (IICT), established in 2010 by the Bulgarian Academy of Sciences (BAS), is a leading centre for research and innovation in information and communication technologies. The institute addresses the growing need for advanced computing infrastructure, big data analysis, and artificial intelligence (AI) research in Bulgaria and the broader region.
IICT-BAS maintains state-of-the-art computing facilities and high-performance computing resources that enable researchers to develop and test AI models, process large datasets, and explore complex computational problems. The institute plays a central role in advancing AI applications in areas such as scientific computing, data analytics, and digital services.
In addition to research, IICT-BAS provides specialised AI training and support for doctoral programmes, fostering the development of highly skilled professionals in the field. By combining advanced infrastructure, academic expertise, and hands-on training, the institute contributes to building Bulgaria’s human and technological capacity in AI and related disciplines

items.title: Institute for Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence and Technology (INSAIT)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Research institute established in partnership with ETH Zurich and EPFL, representing Eastern Europe's major initiative in AI and computer science research. The institute has achieved significant milestones including the development of BgGPT and establishment of deep-tech AI ventures. As a member of the ELLIS network, it focuses on advanced research in GPT models, computer vision, robotics, and quantum computing.

The Institute for Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence and Technology (INSAIT) is a leading research institute in Bulgaria, established through a partnership with ETH Zurich and EPFL. Representing one of Eastern Europe’s most ambitious AI and computer science initiatives, INSAIT addresses the growing need for advanced research, technological innovation, and talent development in AI across the region.
INSAIT has achieved several notable milestones, including the development of BgGPT, a state-of-the-art language model, and the establishment of deep-tech AI ventures that translate research breakthroughs into practical applications. The institute conducts cutting-edge research in areas such as GPT models, computer vision, robotics, and quantum computing, positioning Bulgaria at the forefront of AI innovation in Eastern Europe.
As a member of the European Laboratory for Learning and Intelligent Systems (ELLIS) network, INSAIT fosters collaboration with leading AI research centres across Europe, ensuring knowledge exchange, high-quality research outputs, and access to advanced computational resources. The institute also emphasises interdisciplinary approaches and partnerships with industry, supporting technology transfer and the practical deployment of AI solutions.

items.title: INPS’s experimentation on generative AI
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The National Social Security Institute (Istituto nazionale della previdenza sociale, INPS) pioneered AI adoption in Italian public administration by implementing machine learning algorithms in 2023. The system includes a generative AI-powered virtual assistant for portal users and automated communication processing. The implementation has doubled processing capacity from 3 million to 6 million official communications annually.

In 2023, the Italian National Social Security Institute (INPS) advanced its digital transformation by deploying artificial intelligence across key administrative functions. Central to this effort was the introduction of a generative AI virtual assistant on its user portal, designed to streamline access to services and improve user interaction. Alongside this, INPS implemented machine learning systems to automate the processing of official communications, significantly boosting operational efficiency.

items.title: GovTech AI sandbox
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
The GovTech AI Sandbox pilot aims to tackle critical barriers to innovation in user-centric public services. Public sector organisations face significant challenges in effectively deploying and scaling AI solutions, which can limit the impact of technological advancements meant to enhance services for citizens. The sandbox is expected to significantly improve of Greek public sector organisations in effectively deploying and testing AI solutions.

The GovTech AI Sandbox pilot represents Greece’s commitment to modernising public service delivery through responsible and effective use of artificial intelligence. The initiative was launched to address long-standing barriers that hinder innovation within the public sector — particularly the difficulty of safely testing, deploying, and scaling AI-driven solutions designed to improve citizen services.
Greek public authorities often face challenges in navigating regulatory uncertainty, limited technical expertise, and fragmented infrastructure, all of which can slow the adoption of AI technologies. The GovTech AI Sandbox seeks to overcome these constraints by providing a controlled environment where public sector organisations can experiment with AI applications in a secure, transparent, and compliant way.
The sandbox enables collaboration between government bodies, academia, and technology providers, helping to test real-world AI use cases — such as process automation, data analysis for policy design, and enhanced citizen engagement tools. It also fosters an exchange of best practices and supports the development of common standards for ethical and user-centric AI in the public sector.

items.title: European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Four European Digital Innovation Hubs operate in Bulgaria under the Digital Europe Programme, providing AI implementation support and technical expertise to SMEs and public organisations. The initiative is expanding with eight additional hubs. The four existing hubs include InnovationAmp, the European Digital Innovation Hub in the Construction Sector (EDIHCS); EDIH Thrace, and AgroHub.BG.

Bulgaria hosts a network of European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs) under the Digital Europe Programme, designed to support the adoption and implementation of artificial intelligence (AI) and other advanced digital technologies. These hubs address a key challenge for Bulgarian small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and public organisations: accessing the expertise, infrastructure, and technical guidance required to deploy AI effectively and responsibly.
The current network comprises four operational hubs: InnovationAmp, the European Digital Innovation Hub in the Construction Sector (EDIHCS), EDIH Thrace, and AgroHub.BG. Each hub offers specialised services tailored to its sector or region, including support for AI integration, digital transformation strategies, and access to testing and experimentation environments. By providing hands-on guidance and resources, the hubs enable organisations to explore innovative solutions, improve operational efficiency, and accelerate the development of AI-driven products and services.
The initiative is expanding with eight additional hubs, aiming to broaden regional coverage and increase the accessibility of AI and digital innovation services throughout Bulgaria. This expansion will further strengthen the country’s innovation ecosystem, promote cross-sector collaboration, and enhance the competitiveness of Bulgarian enterprises in European and global markets.

items.title: European Digital Innovation Hub (EDIH) Crobohub++
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
A specialised digital innovation centre that serves as part of the European Digital Innovation Hubs network. The hub focuses on three strategic areas: AI applications for business processes, cybersecurity solutions and high-performance computing (HPC) infrastructure. The centre provides crucial data storage and HPC computing capacity necessary for AI development, making advanced technological capabilities accessible to businesses and organisations.

Crobohub++ is a specialised digital innovation centre in Croatia, forming part of the European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIH) network. The hub addresses the critical need for businesses and organisations to access advanced technologies and infrastructure to support innovation, particularly in artificial intelligence (AI).
The hub focuses on three strategic areas: AI applications for business processes, cybersecurity solutions, and high-performance computing (HPC) infrastructure. By providing access to HPC resources and secure data storage, Crobohub++ enables organisations to develop, test, and implement AI solutions that enhance operational efficiency, security, and competitiveness.
Crobohub++ collaborates closely with research institutions, technology providers, and industry partners, ensuring that its services are tailored to the practical needs of businesses. The hub also offers technical guidance, training, and support to facilitate the adoption of AI and other digital technologies across diverse sectors.

items.title: EDIH Adria
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
A member of the European Digital Innovation Hubs Network, focusing on addressing Croatia's specific technological needs in AI and HPC. The hub specifically targets key sectors including health, tourism, transport (with maritime sector emphasis), energy, and sustainable development. The hub’s aims is to accelerate the digital economic transition in Croatia through sector-specific technological solutions and support.

Funded jointly by the EU’s Digital Europe Programme and Croatia’s National Recovery and Resilience Plan, the initiative supports small businesses and local governments in adopting advanced technologies. Its core areas of expertise are Artificial Intelligence and High-Performance Computing, applied across sectors such as health and quality of life, transport and mobility (especially maritime), and energy and sustainable development. EDIH Adria offers services like testing digital solutions before investment, training programs, and access to innovation financing, aiming to strengthen regional competitiveness and foster a transition toward a digital economy.

items.title: Danish Centre for Clinical Artificial Intelligence (CAI-X)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Danish Centre for Clinical Artificial Intelligence (CAI-X) is partnership between the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute at the University of Southern Denmark and Odense University Hospital to connect clinicians with technical staff and researchers within the universities, along with private enterprises to benefit patients and hospital staff through the use of AI.

CAI-X explores the use of AI to improve quality in healthcare.
CAI-X is the Danish Centre for Clinical Artificial Intelligence – established by the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) and Odense University Hospital (OUH). It is a knowledge and competence centre that helps connect clinicians from the hospital with the engineers and researchers at the university, as well as private companies.
At CAI-X, you can get help with the scoping process and assistance when applying for funding. CAI-X can also help drive the projects and draw attention to results, publications, researchers etc.
CAI-X is a joint centre between OUH and the Faculty of Engineering and the Faculty of Health Sciences at SDU. CAI-X covers all clinical specialities of OUH and cooperates with the additional faculties, private organisations (both Danish and international), research centres, councils and other hospitals to ensure a close connection between patients, health care staff, researchers and engineering experts.
Odense University Hospital and the University of Southern Denmark have a long history of strategic collaboration with respect to health technology and to bridging clinical challenges with technical expertise to provide new treatment solutions. OUH has the clinical setting and the data, and The Faculty of Engineering at SDU has the technical knowledge and experience with algorithms.

items.title: Competitiveness and Innovation in Enterprises Programme
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Priority 1 of PCIE is to implement the priorities set in the ISSS that support innovation capacity and digital transformation of enterprises. It includes a specific objective to provide grants and financial instruments to develop AI and other Industry 4.0 technologies.

The Competitiveness and Innovation in Enterprises Programme (PCIE) is a key initiative supporting the digital transformation and innovation capacity of Bulgarian enterprises. The programme addresses the challenges faced by companies in adopting advanced technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI) and other Industry 4.0 solutions, which are critical for maintaining competitiveness in an increasingly digital and global market.
Priority 1 of PCIE focuses on implementing the strategic objectives set out in the Innovation Strategy for Smart Specialisation (ISSS), particularly those that strengthen innovation ecosystems and support enterprise digitalisation. Within this framework, the programme provides grants and financial instruments to enterprises seeking to develop and deploy AI technologies, advanced automation, and other digital innovations.
The initiative targets a broad range of organisations, from start-ups to established companies, helping them access funding, technical expertise, and guidance needed to successfully implement AI and Industry 4.0 solutions. By doing so, it encourages technological modernisation, process optimisation, and enhanced productivity across Bulgarian industries.

items.title: Cloud Strategy
items.org: Department for Digital Transformation of the Presidency of the Council of Ministers and the National Cybersecurity Agency (ACN)
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
Published by the Department for Digital Transformation and Agency for National Cybersecurity, the strategy provides guidelines for migrating public administration data to qualified cloud services. It outlines data classification criteria and establishes the National Strategic Hub (Polo Strategico Nazionale – PSN) to host critical public sector services.

The key objectives include: 
i) migrating 75% of Italian public administration data and IT applications to qualified cloud environments by 2026, 
ii) enhancing technological autonomy, data control, and digital service resilience and, 
iii) implementing regulations developed by the Agency for Digital Italy which define adoption criteria (Governo Italiano.

items.title: Centre for Artificial Intelligence (CAI)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
A leading research institution with three primary objectives: advancing theoretical AI foundations across multiple domains, facilitating industry collaboration through AI technology transfer to develop innovative products and services; and providing comprehensive AI education at undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral levels, along with specialised industry training programmes.

The Centre for Artificial Intelligence (CAI) at the University of Zagreb, established in October 2019, is Croatia’s largest AI research hub. It brings together around 200 researchers from 19 laboratories at the Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Computing. CAI focuses on advancing AI theory and applications across domains such as machine learning, natural language processing, robotics, bioinformatics, and cybersecurity. It also fosters industry collaboration through technology transfer and offers comprehensive AI education at all academic levels, including continuing education for professionals.

items.title: Centre for AI and Cybersecurity
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
An interdisciplinary research centre at the University of Rijeka that brings together scientists from various faculties to create innovative AI-based solutions. The centre serves as a collaborative hub for continuous idea exchange and development, emphasising both AI advancement and robust cybersecurity measures. The centre’s work focuses on creating practical applications while ensuring high-level security standards through interdisciplinary collaboration.

The Center for Artificial Intelligence and Cybersecurity (AIRI) at the University of Rijeka serves as a multidisciplinary hub for research, innovation, and collaboration in AI and cybersecurity. It unites scientists from diverse fields to work on interdisciplinary projects, emphasizing strong ties between academia and industry. AIRI supports the development and testing of high-potential digital solutions, fosters international partnerships, and promotes knowledge exchange across sectors.

items.title: Capital Investment Fund (CIF)
items.org: Capital Investment Fund (CIF), part of BDB
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Capital Investment Fund (CIF) is a Bulgarian fund that supports SMEs with strong growth potential through equity investments. It aims to co-invest with private equity funds and foster the development of Bulgaria's private equity ecosystem. The fund is sector-agnostic but actively supports innovation, including AI. A notable example is its 2022 investment of BGN 4 million (approximately EUR 2 million) in Barin Sports, a company developing AI systems to monitor athletes' performance.

The Capital Investment Fund (CIF) is a Bulgarian investment fund designed to support small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) with strong growth potential through equity investments. The fund addresses a key challenge in the Bulgarian business ecosystem: limited access to private capital for high-potential companies, particularly those engaged in innovative and technology-driven activities, including artificial intelligence (AI).
CIF operates by co-investing alongside private equity funds, thereby fostering the development of Bulgaria’s private equity market and helping innovative enterprises scale their operations. While the fund is sector-agnostic, it actively supports projects that drive technological innovation and strengthen Bulgaria’s competitiveness in emerging industries.
A notable example of CIF’s impact is its 2022 investment of BGN 4 million (approximately EUR 2 million) in Barin Sports, a company that develops AI systems to monitor athletes’ performance. This investment illustrates how CIF not only provides financial backing but also facilitates the practical deployment of AI solutions with real-world applications.

items.title: Capacity building for Civil and Public Servants
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
In line with the public service transformation strategy, series of one-day courses administered by the Department of Public Expenditure, NDP Delivery and Reform (DPENDR) and the Institute of Public Administration to civil and public servants on how AI can help transform public service delivery.

Certificate in Foundations of AI (part-time over 12 weeks). Approximately 120 public service employees have completed this course.

items.title: Cadastre
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Hellenic Cadastre developed a system to automate the reading and categorisation of property contracts, apply the relevant legal rules, and then generate assessments for approval using AI. The Hellenic Cadastre is set to become the first Greek state service to use AI. Innovative AI applications for land registry cases will significantly facilitate pertinent public administration operations by offering enhanced processing speed and reducing related costs and errors.

The Hellenic Cadastre is pioneering the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in Greece’s public administration by developing an advanced system to automate the processing of property contracts. This initiative marks a significant step in the digital transformation of the Greek public sector, as the Cadastre is set to become the first Greek state service to deploy AI.
The system is designed to automatically read and categorise property contracts, apply the relevant legal rules, and generate assessments for approval. By integrating AI into these workflows, the Hellenic Cadastre aims to streamline complex administrative processes that traditionally require extensive manual effort and legal oversight.
This innovation addresses longstanding challenges related to processing delays, administrative costs, and human error in property registration and land management. Through the automation of document analysis and rule application, the system enables faster and more reliable case handling, supporting both efficiency and legal accuracy.

items.title: AI virtual assistant/chatbot network
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This initiative aims to create a unified and centralised platform for managing government institutions' websites, improving public access to information and ensuring compliance with accessibility requirements under Directive 2016/2102. The platform enhances resource efficiency through a unified content management system and integrates 55 public authorities into a single system`.

The AI Virtual Assistant/Chatbot Network is a Latvian government initiative designed to centralise and streamline public access to information across multiple government websites. The platform addresses the challenge of fragmented digital services by providing a unified interface through which citizens and businesses can interact with public authorities, improving the efficiency and accessibility of online government services.
A core objective of the initiative is to ensure compliance with accessibility requirements under Directive 2016/2102, enabling equal access to information for all users, including those with disabilities. By integrating AI-powered virtual assistants and chatbots, the platform can respond to queries efficiently, provide consistent information, and support user navigation across government websites.
The initiative unites 55 public authorities into a single content management system, allowing for centralised administration and maintenance of web resources. This approach not only reduces operational costs and redundancies but also promotes standardisation of content and improves the overall quality and reliability of online public information.

items.title: AI in the evaluation of EU projects
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This study assesses the applicability of generative AI for analysing procurement documentation related to EU-funded projects. It evaluates AI solutions’ technological readiness, quality, and accuracy in text analysis and response generation in Latvian, aiming to develop recommendations and test AI prototypes for public sector applications.

The AI in the Evaluation of EU Projects initiative in Latvia explores the potential of generative artificial intelligence (AI) to support the assessment of procurement documentation for EU-funded projects. The study addresses a key challenge in public administration: the need to analyse large volumes of complex textual information efficiently while maintaining accuracy and consistency in evaluations.
A primary objective of the initiative is to assess the technological readiness and performance of AI solutions in processing and understanding text in the Latvian language. This includes evaluating the quality, reliability, and accuracy of AI-generated analyses and responses, ensuring that any implemented tools can meet the rigorous standards required for public sector decision-making.
The initiative involves the testing and development of AI prototypes, aimed at providing practical insights into how generative AI can assist in document review, summarisation, and evaluation tasks. By piloting these solutions, public authorities can identify opportunities to streamline workflows, reduce administrative burden, and enhance the quality and consistency of project assessments.

items.title: AI in tax administration
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Inland Revenue Authority (Agenzia delle Entrate) leverages advanced analytics software to prevent tax avoidance by analysing data from the Tax Registry and Archive of Financial Relations. This system enables more effective identification of potential tax compliance issues while optimising resource allocation.

The Agenzia delle Entrate (Italian Inland Revenue Authority) has implemented advanced AI and analytics software to strengthen tax administration and improve compliance monitoring. This initiative addresses the challenge of detecting tax avoidance and fraud within a large and complex national tax system, where manual monitoring is time-consuming and prone to gaps.
The system integrates data from the Tax Registry and the Archive of Financial Relations, enabling sophisticated analysis to identify potential irregularities, anomalies, and high-risk cases. By leveraging AI algorithms, the authority can prioritise investigations, allocate resources more efficiently, and focus on cases with the highest potential impact on revenue protection.

items.title: AI Ecosystem in Social and Health Services (SOTE)
items.org: Ministry of Social Affairs and Health
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Established in 2024, this national AI ecosystem for social and health services fosters collaboration among public authorities, businesses, and researchers to promote AI integration in healthcare.

The Finnish national AI ecosystem for social and health services (SOTE) is an informal network of stakeholders in the social and healthcare sector, including authorities, businesses and researchers.
The SOTE AI ecosystem network is led by the Ministry of Social Affairs and Health. The coordinating group also includes the Finnish Institute for Health and Welfare (THL), the Hospital District of Helsinki and Uusimaa (HUS), Una Oy, and DigiFinland Oy. DigiFinland acts as the practical operations coordinator for the ecosystem. The innovation network was established by the Ministry of Social Affairs and Health in the summer of 2024. We have more than 200 member organizations.
