The AI ecosystem facilitates, enables and funds the utilisation of AI in the social and health sector:
Brings together stakeholders to implement development projects and grants subsidies
Collects and shares AI use cases and the experiences of pioneers
Conducts and facilitates national surveys and studies, and promotes international cooperation
Identifies legislative needs and makes proposals for enabling legislation.
The utilisation of AI has vast potential in the social and health sector. The ecosystem aims to ensure that the effective use of AI:
Secures high-quality services for clients and assists professionals in their work, freeing up time for the most important tasks, such as personal interaction with clients
Improves the productivity of the service system
Creates business opportunities and exports, thereby generating new jobs

items.title: AI Cluster Bulgaria
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
An industry association that strengthens Bulgaria's AI ecosystem by providing targeted support to AI companies and fostering collaboration across sectors. The cluster offers specialised programmes including professional development training, financing facilitation, technical guidance for AI implementation, and access to testing infrastructure. It creates partnerships between AI companies, research institutions, and government agencies to accelerate AI adoption in Bulgaria's business sector.

AI Cluster Bulgaria is an industry association dedicated to strengthening Bulgaria’s artificial intelligence (AI) ecosystem and accelerating the adoption of AI technologies across the economy. It responds to the growing need for collaboration, knowledge sharing, and capacity building among businesses, research organisations, and public institutions working with AI.
The cluster provides targeted support to AI companies through a range of specialised programmes and initiatives. These include professional development and training opportunities, facilitation of access to financing, and technical guidance for AI implementation. By connecting businesses with resources, expertise, and partners, AI Cluster Bulgaria helps organisations of all sizes integrate AI solutions into their operations effectively and responsibly.
A core focus of the cluster is on fostering cross-sector collaboration between AI companies, research institutions, and government agencies. Through partnerships and joint initiatives, it supports the creation of new AI products and services while ensuring that innovation aligns with national and European priorities for digital transformation. The cluster also offers access to testing environments and infrastructure, helping companies pilot and scale their AI technologies.

items.title: AI & gaming (JURK) EDIH
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Operates as a comprehensive digitisation and digital transformation centre serving small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and public sector entities in central Croatia and the northern Adriatic region. The hub functions as a one-stop shop for digital technology integration, with particular expertise in AI, gamification, and blockchain technologies.

The AI & Gaming (JURK) European Digital Innovation Hub (EDIH) operates as a central resource for digitalisation and digital transformation in Croatia, targeting small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) as well as public sector entities in central Croatia and the northern Adriatic region. The hub addresses a key challenge faced by organisations in these areas: accessing specialised expertise and infrastructure to implement advanced digital technologies effectively.
JURK functions as a one-stop shop for digital technology integration, providing support for AI adoption, gamification, and blockchain solutions. The hub helps organisations explore innovative applications, improve operational efficiency, and implement technologies that can transform business processes and public services. Its services include technical guidance, access to testing environments, and training programs tailored to organisational needs.
By fostering collaboration between industry, research institutions, and public organisations, JURK ensures that technological solutions are practical, scalable, and aligned with local economic and societal priorities. This collaborative approach enhances the capacity of SMEs and public bodies to adopt advanced digital solutions responsibly and effectively.

items.title: UGENT.AI Institute
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
UGENT.AI promotes AI research at Ghent University, focusing on innovative AI applications, ethics, and cross-disciplinary approaches. It collaborates with academia, industry, and policymakers to address societal challenges and drive AI innovation.

UGENT.AI is the artificial intelligence research initiative at Ghent University dedicated to advancing AI across multiple disciplines and societal domains. The initiative addresses the need for innovative AI applications that are both technically advanced and ethically responsible, while fostering cross-disciplinary collaboration between computer science, social sciences, healthcare, and other fields.
The primary objective of UGENT.AI is to promote high-quality research that combines innovation, ethics, and societal impact. The initiative explores diverse AI applications, from healthcare solutions and smart cities to data-driven policy insights, ensuring that AI development contributes meaningfully to solving real-world challenges.
UGENT.AI operates through collaboration with academic partners, industry stakeholders, and policymakers. These partnerships facilitate knowledge exchange, practical implementation of AI solutions, and the co-creation of projects that integrate technical expertise with societal needs. By connecting research with policy and industry, UGENT.AI helps ensure that AI technologies are both innovative and socially relevant.

items.title: Tremplin IA
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Tremplin IA focuses on developing Proofs of Concept for AI projects over six months. It enables organisations to assess the feasibility of innovative AI solutions, with calls for projects made available periodically.

Tremplin IA is a Belgian initiative designed to support organisations in exploring and validating innovative artificial intelligence (AI) solutions. The programme focuses on developing Proofs of Concept (PoCs) for AI projects over a period of six months, allowing participants to test the feasibility and potential impact of their ideas in a structured and practical way.
The primary objective of Tremplin IA is to help organisations—from start-ups and SMEs to larger enterprises—identify the viability of AI solutions before committing significant resources. By providing dedicated support, technical expertise, and guidance, the programme reduces risk and accelerates the early stages of AI project development.
Calls for participation are made available periodically, enabling companies and research institutions to submit project proposals aligned with their strategic goals. Throughout the six-month period, participants receive mentorship, access to data and technology resources, and opportunities to collaborate with AI experts to refine their concepts.

items.title: TRAIL (Trusted AI Labs)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
TRAIL fosters ethical AI development through collaborative research, industry partnerships, and the ARIAC project, advancing innovation in sectors such as healthcare and energy while prioritising transparency and societal impact.

TRAIL is a Belgian initiative dedicated to advancing ethical artificial intelligence (AI) development through a combination of collaborative research, industry partnerships, and targeted projects, including the ARIAC project. The initiative addresses the growing need to ensure that AI technologies are developed and deployed in ways that are transparent, accountable, and socially responsible.
The primary objective of TRAIL is to foster innovation while maintaining a strong focus on ethics and societal impact. By promoting collaboration between academic researchers, industry actors, and public institutions, the initiative encourages the development of AI solutions that are both technologically advanced and aligned with human-centred principles.
Projects within TRAIL span multiple sectors, including healthcare, energy, and environmental technology, exploring applications such as predictive analytics, decision support systems, and sustainable solutions. The initiative integrates rigorous ethical standards, data governance practices, and transparency measures to ensure that AI outputs are trustworthy and beneficial for society.

items.title: Start IA
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Start IA provides 40 hours of support to companies by an AI expert. The goal of Start IA is to identify, based on the company’s activity and data, potential projects where AI technologies can add value.

Start IA is a support programme in Belgium designed to help companies explore the potential of artificial intelligence in their operations. Through this initiative, each participating company receives 40 hours of guidance from an AI expert, who works closely with the business to assess how AI can generate concrete value. The programme’s goal is to identify potential projects tailored to the company’s specific activities, data assets, and strategic priorities.
Start IA primarily targets small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) seeking to better understand how AI can enhance efficiency, innovation, and decision-making. During the support process, experts help participants analyse their existing data infrastructure, determine suitable AI use cases, and outline practical steps for implementation. This hands-on approach ensures that companies can move beyond theoretical knowledge and toward actionable, business-relevant AI adoption.
The initiative also contributes to the broader objective of strengthening Belgium’s AI readiness by building awareness, fostering digital skills, and promoting collaboration between industry and AI specialists. By lowering the barriers to entry, Start IA enables companies without extensive technical resources to begin their AI journey in a structured and low-risk way.

items.title: Second Joint Action Towards the European Health Data Space
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The TEHDAS2 initiative, coordinated by the Finnish Innovation Fund (Sitra), is a collaborative project involving 29 European countries. It aims to facilitate the secondary use of health data across Europe by developing harmonised guidelines and technical specifications, thereby supporting the implementation of the European Health Data Space (EHDS).

The primary goal of TEHDAS2 is to prepare for the coordinated implementation of the EHDS, focusing on the secondary use of health data. This includes developing concrete guidelines and technical definitions to streamline the use of health data across different countries, ensuring secure and efficient access for research, innovation, and policymaking.
Key Activities:
Development of 11 draft guidelines and technical specifications covering areas such as data access procedures, data minimisation, secure processing environments, and citizens' rightsOrganisation of public consultations to gather stakeholder feedback on these drafts, ensuring broad applicability and acceptanceEstablishment of collaboration models and cooperation frameworks to facilitate cross-border data sharing and accessAs of October 2025, TEHDAS2 has initiated a 60-day public consultation on the draft documents, inviting feedback from stakeholders including citizens, health professionals, authorities, and regulators. This consultation is a critical step in refining the guidelines and ensuring they meet the needs of all relevant parties.

items.title: Research Foundation Flanders
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Research Foundation Flanders funded approximately EUR 22 million annually for fundamental and basic AI research in 2024. These funds support bottom-up initiatives in academia.

The Research Foundation Flanders (FWO) plays a central role in advancing artificial intelligence (AI) research in Belgium by providing consistent and substantial funding for academic initiatives. In 2024, the FWO allocated approximately EUR 22 million annually to support fundamental and basic research in AI. This investment underlines Flanders’ commitment to fostering scientific excellence and building the knowledge base necessary for innovation in AI and related fields.
The programme primarily supports bottom-up research, enabling universities and research institutions to propose projects driven by scientific curiosity rather than predefined policy priorities. This approach allows researchers to explore diverse AI topics—from machine learning and data science to robotics and cognitive systems—encouraging innovation that emerges organically from academic inquiry.
By sustaining a strong foundation for basic research, the FWO helps ensure that AI development in Flanders remains anchored in scientific rigor, openness, and interdisciplinarity. The funding not only strengthens the region’s research ecosystem but also supports the training of early-career scientists, promoting the long-term growth of AI expertise.

items.title: Regional Centre of Excellence for Robotics (CRTA)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
A specialised centre focused on establishing a regional hub of excellence for robotics and AI research, development, and education. The centre concentrates on developing advanced robot applications, particularly in industrial and medical sectors, working to replace traditional automation and human work with adaptive and intelligent systems. Their work extends to various human activity areas requiring intelligent automation solutions.

CRTA, based at the University of Zagreb, is a robotics and AI centre focused on developing intelligent systems for industrial and medical use. It combines cutting-edge labs, EU-funded projects, and academic-industry collaboration to drive innovation beyond traditional automation. CRTA’s work supports Croatia’s tech competitiveness by translating research into real-world applications.

items.title: Quantum Computing Research and Development Programme
items.original_name: Programma di Ricerca e Sviluppo sul Calcolo Quantistico
items.org: Ministry of University and Research; National Recovery and Resilience Plan (NRRP)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Programma di Ricerca e Sviluppo sul Calcolo Quantistico
items.body:
The Italian quantum computing initiative is a key component of the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (NRRP). This programme is designed to bolster Italy’s quantum computing capabilities by supporting the entire research and development spectrum—from fundamental research to technological applications and market deployment.

The NQSTI is a three-year programme with a total funding of €115.9 million under the NRRP, specifically aligned with the European Union’s NextGenerationEU framework. The initiative encompasses three main action lines:
Enhancing Research Infrastructure
Developing state-of-the-art facilities and platforms for quantum research, including integration with high-performance computing infrastructures and the European Quantum Communication Infrastructure (EuroQCI).Fostering Collaboration Between Academia and Industry
Establishing a network of national quantum institutes to optimize resources, bridge research with industry, and stimulate industrial innovation through joint laboratories and prototyping.Developing Innovative Research Models
Implementing new standards, training programs, and fostering the creation of spin-offs and start-ups, particularly focusing on the southern regions of Italy to promote balanced regional development.The NQSTI is a consortium that includes over 20 institutions, comprising research centres, universities, and enterprises across Italy. It aims to translate quantum research into industrial applications, addressing the entire innovation chain—from fundamental research to market deployment.
A significant aspect of the programme is its emphasis on education and outreach, aiming to make quantum science and technology pervasive in society. This includes initiatives in secondary and higher education, public engagement, and the development of a skilled workforce to support the growing quantum industry.

items.title: National Strategic Hub
items.org: Department for Digital Transformation; Agency for National Cybersecurity; National Strategic Hub S.p.A
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Polo Strategico Nazionale (PSN) is Italy’s high-reliability cloud infrastructure for public administrations. It hosts critical and strategic data and services, aiming to improve security, resilience, and efficiency in government IT. The project forms a central part of Italy’s cloud-first strategy to have 75% of public administrations using cloud services by 2026.

The PSN was officially activated on 21 December 2022 under Italy’s National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR), as part of Mission 1, Component 1, Investment 1.1 (“Cloud PA / Polo Strategico Nazionale”). Its aim is to provide public administrations—including central administrations, Local Health Units (ASLs), and the main regional/local administrations—with cloud infrastructure meeting high standards of security, sovereignty, operational continuity, and environmental sustainability.
Key features include:
Ownership and governance via Polo Strategico Nazionale S.p.A., a special purpose company jointly owned by TIM, Leonardo, Cassa Depositi e Prestiti (CDP via CDP Equity), and SOGEI. Four data centres located in Acilia and Pomezia (Lazio), and Rozzano and Santo Stefano Ticino (Lombardy), designed with high availability, fault tolerance, and elevated environmental standards.Strong emphasis on digital sovereignty, meaning the infrastructure is intended to be independent of non-EU entities for critical services, with certified high security, resilience, and compliance with cloud-first principles.The initiative also encompasses migration support: administrations whose infrastructures are considered insecure or critical are prioritised for migration to the PSN. By 2026, the goal is for 75% of Italian public administrations to be using cloud services, including via PSN.
Recent developments include AgID (the Agency for Digital Italy) formally joining or migrating some of its services to the PSN cloud under an agreement signed in May 2024. This migration follows the “cloud-native” and “cloud-first” architectural model, ensuring equivalence in functionality and architecture

items.title: National Quantum Science and Technology Institute (NQSTI)
items.original_name: Istituto Nazionale di Scienza e Tecnologia Quantistica (NQSTI)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Istituto Nazionale di Scienza e Tecnologia Quantistica (NQSTI)
items.body:
​The NQSTI is a consortium established to advance Italy's research and innovation in quantum science and technology. The institute brings together 20 Italian institutions, including research centres, universities, and enterprises, to conduct competitive and innovative research in this field. NQSTI aims to stimulate industrial innovation by providing a forum for transferring ideas and opportunities to companies.

The National Quantum Science and Technology Institute (NQSTI) is a strategic initiative aimed at positioning Italy as a leader in the field of quantum science and technology. Officially launched in January 2023, the institute operates under the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR), funded by the European Union's NextGenerationEU programme. The project is scheduled to run until November 2025, with a total funding allocation of €115.9 million.
Key Objectives:
Research and Development: NQSTI focuses on advancing research in quantum technologies, including quantum computing, sensing, and secure communication, particularly at the experimental "proof of concept" level.Technology Transfer: The institute aims to bridge the gap between research and industry by facilitating the translation of quantum research into practical applications, fostering innovation and economic growth.Education and Outreach: NQSTI is committed to enhancing public understanding of quantum technologies through educational programs and outreach activities, aiming to build a well-informed society and workforce.Support for Start-ups: The institute supports the creation and incubation of spin-offs and start-ups, with a special focus on southern Italy, to move research outcomes up in the Technology Readiness Level (TRL) scale.NQSTI brings together a diverse group of over 20 Italian entities, including:
Research Centres: Such as the National Research Council (CNR) and the Institute for Complex Systems (ISC).Universities: Including the University of Pisa and the University of Milan-Bicocca.Enterprises: Collaborating to translate research into commercial applications.

items.title: Leuven.AI
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Leuven.AI promotes AI research at Leuven University, focusing on innovative AI applications, ethics, and cross-disciplinary approaches. It collaborates with academia, industry, and policymakers to address societal challenges and drive AI innovation.

The Leuven.AI initiative started up in 2018.  Its purpose is to bring together the wealth of expertise on AI that exists at KU Leuven, spread over multiple faculties and departments, and provide a single access point to it.
Leuven.AI became recognized as the KU Leuven Institute for Artificial Intelligence in January 2020 and now involves 15+ AI research topics, 100+ professors, 100s of researchers and 500 master students.

items.title: Innoviris
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Innoviris, the Brussels research and innovation agency, plays a key role in funding and supporting AI research and innovation.

Innoviris' programmes encompass applied R&D, strategic initiatives, and proof of concept, fostering collaboration between academic institutions and businesses to drive impactful AI advancements. Among its notable initiatives is the “Innovative Starters Award”, which supports high-potential enterprises with up to EUR 500k over three years to finance strategic innovation plans.

items.title: Innovation and Enterprise Flanders
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Innovation and Enterprise Flanders allocated approximately EUR 97 million in 2024 to fund AI innovation projects, fostering research excellence and strengthening innovation capacity across industries. This funding supports bottom-up initiatives, enabling businesses to develop and implement cutting-edge AI solutions that drive economic growth and technological advancement.

Innovation and Enterprise Flanders (VLAIO) has made significant investments to strengthen the region’s AI innovation ecosystem. In 2024, VLAIO allocated approximately EUR 97 million to support AI innovation projects, promoting research excellence and boosting the innovation capacity of Flemish industries. This initiative reflects Flanders’ strategic commitment to embedding artificial intelligence across sectors as a driver of sustainable economic growth and technological leadership.
The funding primarily supports bottom-up innovation, allowing businesses—ranging from start-ups and SMEs to large enterprises—to develop and apply AI-driven solutions tailored to their needs. These projects span diverse domains such as manufacturing, healthcare, logistics, and environmental technology. By encouraging experimentation and co-creation, VLAIO helps companies turn emerging AI capabilities into practical tools that enhance productivity, competitiveness, and digital maturity.
Beyond financial support, VLAIO provides access to a broader innovation ecosystem that connects businesses with research institutions, technology centres, and public partners. This collaborative approach ensures that AI solutions are developed responsibly and effectively, with a strong emphasis on applicability and societal value.

items.title: Innovation Centre Nikola Tesla
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
A technology centre dedicated to supporting Croatian economic growth through high-technology development and implementation. The centre specialises in multiple sectors including energetics, transport, automation and robotics, advanced components, biomedical engineering, and information and communication technology. Their work aims to bridge the gap between research and practical industrial applications in these high-tech domains.

ICENT is a Croatian technology centre focused on accelerating high-tech development to support national economic growth. It bridges the gap between research and industry by fostering innovation across sectors such as energy, transport, robotics, biomedical engineering, and ICT. Through collaborative projects and partnerships, ICENT seeks to promote the commercialization of research, strengthen Croatia’s innovation ecosystem, and contribute to the country’s digital and industrial transformation.

items.title: IPCEI Cloud
items.org: Ministry of Enterprises and Made in Italy; Italian participating companies (e.g. TIM, Fincantieri)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Italy is actively participating in the EU’s Important Project of Common European Interest (IPCEI) on Cloud Infrastructure and Services (CIS). This initiative aims to develop an interoperable, open-source cloud-to-edge ecosystem to support sectors like energy, health, and maritime. Italian companies such as TIM, Fincantieri, Engineering Ingegneria Informatica, Tiscali, and Reply are key contributors to this project.

The IPCEI-CIS is a strategic EU initiative designed to establish a European value chain for Cloud Infrastructure and Services (CIS). Approved by the European Commission in December 2023, the project involves seven EU member states and 19 companies, with Italy receiving approximately €409 million in state aid, part of a total of €1.2 billion allocated across Europe.
Key objectives of the initiative include:
Developing a federated cloud-to-edge continuum: Creating an interoperable, multi-provider infrastructure to support real-time, low-latency data processing across various sectors.Enhancing sector-specific applications: Focusing on areas such as smart manufacturing, energy efficiency, maritime operations, and healthcare.Promoting open-source and open-access platforms: Ensuring that the developed technologies are accessible and adaptable for various users and industries.Italian contributions to the project encompass:
TIM: Leading the development of the TIM Edge & Cloud Continuum, aiming to provide high-performance, low-latency cloud services with guaranteed bandwidth and compliance with EU data regulations.Fincantieri: Focusing on creating an efficient suite of processing services to organize and orchestrate information flows in an Edge-Cloud/Multicloud Continuum, with applications in smart shipyards and smart ships.Engineering Ingegneria Informatica: Contributing to the development of advanced processing tools and services within the cloud infrastructure.Tiscali: Participating in the development of cloud capabilities and services.Reply: Engaging in the integration and interoperability aspects of the cloud infrastructure.

items.title: HealthHub
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
As part of the EDIH Network, a pan-European partnership of over 150 European Digital Innovation Hubs, the EDIHs function as service points that boost digital investment and, in particular, the digitalisation of SMEs. HealthHub aims to promote AI applications in the health sector and partner organisations to enable the use of Finnish health data for digital innovation.

The European Digital Hubs (EDIH) Network is the driving force behind Europe’s digitalisation. With the support of the European Commission, it brings together EDIHs, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), and public sector organisations (PSOs) to make the EU’s Digital Decade 2030 targets a reality.
The EDIH Network is a community of tech experts dedicated to guiding Europe’s businesses on their path to digital transformation. EDIHs serve as one-stop shops throughout all EU regions, equipping companies with the essential digital tools to improve their competitiveness, upgrade their infrastructure, and boost their overall success.

items.title: Government Council for Information Society ­– Working Group for Cloud Computing
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Government Council for Information Society has established a working group focused on cloud computing as part of the broader Digital Czechia initiative.

This group is responsible for steering the development of eGovernment cloud strategies, ensuring that public sector entities adopt cloud-based services in a secure, efficient, and cost-effective manner.

items.title: Genomic Medicine Plan
items.org: Ministry of Health and Access to Care
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Plan aims to provide patients with timely access to the latest genomic innovations and integrate genomics into routine healthcare to improve diagnosis and treatment, reduce diagnostic errors, and personalise therapeutic strategies.

The Ministry of Health officially launched in December 2016 a national call for projects, marking the start of funding for the first two genomic platforms dedicated to diagnostics and therapeutic monitoring, out of a total of 12 platforms expected within five years. These centers of excellence illustrate the ongoing support of public authorities for medical innovation, particularly for high-throughput human genome sequencing, which underpins genomic medicine, also referred to as “personalized” medicine.
Key focus areas include:
Cancer: Enables more effective therapeutic adaptation, particularly through immunotherapyRare diseases: Improves diagnosis for ~7,000 identified rare diseases, ending the “diagnostic wandering” patients often experienceCommon diseases: Addresses major metabolic disorders (e.g., diabetes, obesity), cardiovascular diseases, and neurodegenerative diseases (e.g., Alzheimer’s)

items.title: France 2030: digital health acceleration strategy
items.original_name: France 2030 : stratégie d’accélération de la santé numérique
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: France 2030 : stratégie d’accélération de la santé numérique
items.body:
The strategy aims to position France as a leader in digital health by fostering innovation and supporting the development of advanced e-health solutions, with a specific focus on integrating AI-based technologies, e.g. by funding medical imaging advancements, developing AI-based diagnostic and treatment tools, and ensuring secure and ethical use of health data.

In a process of mobilizing all stakeholders in the digital health sector, this proactive acceleration strategy aims in particular to:
Encourage the transition from curative, siloed medicine to a more preventive, predictive and personalized approachPromote the emergence of a major e-health ecosystem in France, capable of establishing itself in a competitive global marketTreat health data securely and ethically, without relying entirely on a few players subject to less protective regulations for personal data.

items.title: FARI Institute
items.org: Vrije Universiteit Brussel (VUB), Université libre de Bruxelles (ULB)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
FARI, a joint initiative of VUB and ULB, coordinates 300 researchers to develop AI, data, and robotics solutions. Projects range from AI for public safety to sustainable urban innovations. The institute bridges interdisciplinary research with practical applications, advancing AI for societal benefit.

FARI is a Brussels-based institute jointly founded by the Vrije Universiteit Brussel (VUB) and the Université libre de Bruxelles (ULB) to advance artificial intelligence (AI), data, and robotics for the public good. The initiative brings together around 300 researchers from diverse disciplines to develop solutions that address social challenges and promote responsible, human-centred innovation.
The institute’s work responds to the growing need for trustworthy and transparent AI systems that can be applied to real-world issues, from sustainable urban development to public safety and digital inclusion. By fostering collaboration between academia, public authorities, and industry, FARI serves as a bridge between cutting-edge research and practical applications that deliver tangible societal impact.
Projects undertaken within FARI span multiple domains, including AI-assisted public decision-making, ethical data governance, and the use of robotics in environmental and social contexts. Its interdisciplinary structure enables cross-sectoral innovation while maintaining a strong focus on ethics, fairness, and accountability in AI use.

items.title: Datalabs
items.org: Federal Ministry of the Interior and Community
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Since 2021, the German government's data labs have recruited experts in data science and AI from academia, civil society, and the private sector to support the federal administration. These experts help develop and implement AI-driven solutions within government agencies, making data and AI more useful in decision-making and public services. Through exploring and testing new AI applications, the data labs help to modernise administrative processes and promote AI technologies in the public sector

Since 2021, the German government has established Data Labs (Datenlabore) to enhance the use of artificial intelligence (AI) and data-driven decision-making within federal administration. The initiative addresses the need for specialised expertise in data science and AI to modernise administrative processes and improve the quality and efficiency of public services.
The primary objective of the Data Labs is to recruit experts from academia, civil society, and the private sector who collaborate with government agencies to develop and implement AI-driven solutions. These experts support the federal administration in exploring innovative approaches to data analysis, predictive modelling, and AI application, ensuring that new technologies are effectively integrated into everyday public sector operations.
The Data Labs provide a structured environment to test and prototype AI solutions, allowing ministries to assess feasibility, impact, and scalability before wider deployment. By fostering experimentation, knowledge exchange, and interdisciplinary collaboration, the labs help ensure that AI adoption is both responsible and results-oriented.

items.title: Data centres
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Polo Strategico Nazionale (PSN) is Italy’s sovereign cloud infrastructure for public administrations. It uses four national data centres to host critical public sector data and services securely and reliably. The PSN enables digital transformation of government services while promoting technological autonomy, sustainability, and resilience.

The PSN was established by the Department for Digital Transformation under the Presidency of the Council of Ministers to consolidate and modernise Italy’s public administration infrastructure. It is operated by Polo Strategico Nazionale S.p.A., a public-private company owned by TIM, Leonardo, CDP (through CDP Equity), and Sogei.
Its mission is to host the critical and strategic data and services of central and local government bodies, including health services (ASL) and major municipalities, in a secure and resilient environment.
The PSN currently operates four data centres:
Acilia and Pomezia (Lazio)Rozzano and Santo Stefano Ticino (Lombardy)These centres are built to high standards of reliability, security, and energy efficiency (green design, certifications, redundancy) to support continuity, disaster recovery, and sovereignty of public data.
Under the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR), one of the PSN’s goals is to have 75% of Italian public administrations migrate to cloud services by 2026. 
As of December 2022, the PSN infrastructure was declared operational at the four sites, and migrations of public administrations are underway.

items.title: Centre for Excellence in Language Technology
items.org: Latvian Ministry of Education and Science; Tilde
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Centre for Excellence in Language Technology is a Latvian initiative focused on training specialists in language computing technologies, developing advanced digital skills modules, and creating innovative solutions in this field. It also supports the production of scientific publications and contributes to impactful projects, such as Tilde’s award-winning AI tools.

The Centre for Excellence in Language Technology is a collaborative effort involving Latvian universities and research institutions, aimed at advancing the field of language technology. Key components of the initiative include:
Specialist Training: Providing education and training to specialists in language computing technologies, ensuring a skilled workforce capable of driving innovation in this sector.Development of Digital Skills Modules: Creating advanced modules to enhance digital competencies among individuals, facilitating their participation in the digital economy.Innovative Solution Development: Fostering the creation of cutting-edge solutions in language technology, contributing to the global advancement of the field.Support for Scientific Publications: Encouraging and supporting the production of scientific research, thereby contributing to the academic community and the advancement of knowledge in language technology.Contribution to Impactful Projects: Participating in significant projects, such as Tilde’s award-winning AI tools, which enhance the accessibility and efficiency of language technologies.

items.title: AI in updating cadastral data
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
AI is used to improve the accuracy of cadastral data by updating national records on buildings. The system reduces administrative burden and reliance on property owners for data updates, ensuring more efficient and resource-effective land and property management.

Latvia’s State Land Service has implemented an upgrade to its cadastral information system, supported by the European Regional Development Fund. The project uses AI to improve the accuracy of building data, reduce administrative burden, and streamline property registration. The system enhances efficiency in land and real estate management by automating updates and minimizing reliance on property owners. New datasets and improved e-services also contribute to better public access and data-driven decision-making.

items.title: AI Plattform "KIPITZ”
items.org: Federal Ministry of the Interior and Community
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Jointly managed by BeKI, BMF and the Federal Chancellery's Data Lab, KIPITZ is an overarching AI infrastructure supporting LLMs for the federal administration. The platform, built by ITZBund with open-source components, allows cross-departmental testing and deployment of generative AI tools, fostering innovation and digital sovereignty in the public sector.

KIPiTZ is a German AI platform designed to support public administration in identifying, testing, and implementing artificial intelligence (AI) solutions. The initiative focuses on creating a structured environment where federal institutions can experiment with AI technologies, evaluate their potential, and share knowledge and experiences across ministries and agencies.
The primary objective of KIPiTZ is to foster efficient and responsible AI adoption in government operations. By providing a platform for collaboration, the initiative enables public sector organisations to explore AI applications that improve service delivery, streamline administrative processes, and enhance decision-making while adhering to ethical, legal, and societal standards.
KIPiTZ is coordinated in close collaboration with multiple federal ministries, technical experts, and the AI Advisory Centre (BeKI). The platform provides access to tools, pilot projects, and best practices, ensuring that AI implementations are both practical and aligned with Germany’s value-based approach to AI.

items.title: AI Marketplace for Opportunities
items.org: Federal Ministry of the Interior and Community
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
As a pilot project under BeKI, this marketplace will connect ministries and agencies with AI solutions that meet their needs. It will improve transparency and collaboration by cataloguing AI applications and experiences within government departments. The project is currently being developed with the BMI’s Data Lab, ITZBund, and other ministries, with plans to launch publicly by late 2024.

Germany is developing an AI Marketplace for Opportunities as a pilot project coordinated under the AI Advisory Centre (BeKI). The initiative aims to connect federal ministries and agencies with AI solutions tailored to their operational needs, enhancing both transparency and collaboration in the public sector. By cataloguing available AI applications and sharing departmental experiences, the marketplace seeks to streamline the identification and adoption of AI technologies across government institutions.
The primary objective of the marketplace is to make it easier for public administrations to access suitable AI solutions while encouraging knowledge exchange and best practices. Ministries and agencies will be able to discover, evaluate, and implement AI applications more efficiently, reducing duplication of effort and fostering innovative approaches to administrative challenges.
The project is being developed in collaboration with the BMI’s Data Lab, ITZBund, and other federal ministries, ensuring that technical, operational, and policy requirements are all considered. The pilot phase focuses on testing functionality, usability, and governance mechanisms, with the goal of launching the platform publicly by late 2024.

items.title: AI Guidelines
items.org: Federal Ministry of the Interior and Community
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
Coordinated by the AI Advisory Centre (BeKI), AI Guidelines are being developed to ensure a harmonised inter-ministerial approach to the use of AI in public administration. These guidelines promote a value-based approach to AI deployment and offer practical guidance for both employees utilising AI systems and the respective administrative units responsible for providing these systems.

Germany has developed the KI-Leitlinien (AI Guidelines) to ensure a harmonised and responsible approach to the use of artificial intelligence (AI) across federal public administration. This initiative addresses the need for a consistent framework that guides government institutions in deploying AI systems ethically, transparently, and effectively, while maintaining public trust and accountability.
The primary objective of the KI-Leitlinien is to promote a value-based approach to AI adoption. The guidelines provide practical guidance for both employees using AI systems and the administrative units responsible for implementing and managing these technologies. By outlining principles such as fairness, transparency, human-centred design, and legal compliance, the guidelines help ensure AI applications align with societal and administrative objectives.
The development of these guidelines is coordinated across multiple federal ministries, combining expertise from policy makers, AI experts, and public administration specialists. This inter-ministerial collaboration ensures that the framework reflects operational realities and can be applied consistently across departments, providing clear instructions for AI deployment, risk management, and accountability.

items.title: Working Group on AI of the Future Committee of Lithuanian Parliament
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The main tasks of the Working Group is to advise on future AI policies in the public sector and to foster an innovative culture in the public administration.

AI Resolution by the Seimas of Lithuania establishes a principled framework for the use of artificial intelligence in the public sector. Recognizing both the potential and risks of AI, the Resolution outlines 11 guiding principles—including transparency, traceability, responsibility, and safeguarding human interests—to ensure ethical, accountable, and effective integration of AI technologies in public administration.

items.title: VELES Excellence Hub
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Cyprus aims to advance dementia care and regional collaboration in the VELES initiative by integrating Big Data, AI, and IoT to enhance personalised medicine, informed decision-making, and disease prediction through secure, data-driven healthcare solutions.

VELES Excellence Hub, a dynamic consortium aimed at accelerating innovation excellence in smart healthcare, proudly announces its official launch starting on June 1st, 2023. With a focus on the widening countries of Bulgaria, Greece, Romania, and Cyprus, VELES develops novel methodologies and pilots to enable new collaboration opportunities and smart health innovations within a sustainable, excellent place-based ecosystem driven by Regional Health Data Space. This ambitious EU-funded project, valued at 4,750,000 euros, will conclude on May 31, 2027, leaving a lasting legacy of transformative impact.
The overarching objective of VELES is to foster an environment where smart health innovations thrive, creating excellent innovation ecosystems within the participating countries. Aligned with the Regional Research and Innovation Strategies for Smart Specialisation (RIS3) in healthcare, VELES aims to leverage cutting-edge technologies such as Big Data, Artificial Intelligence (AI), and the Internet of Things (IoT) to enable personalized medicine, informed decision-making, and enhanced disease prediction.
VELES was established as a consortium composed of 15 partners, representing both the four widening countries (Bulgaria, Romania, Greece, and Cyprus) and three developed countries (Sweden, Spain, and Germany).
The consortium includes prominent organisations such as
National eHealth Authority, Cyprus
3AE HEALTH LTD, Cyprus
STEGI EVGIRIAS ARCHAGGELOS MICHAEL KAIMAKLIOY, Cyprus

items.title: Testing and Experimentation Facility for Health AI and Robotics (TEF-Health) – Czechia Node at Masaryk University
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
As part of the European Commission’s Digital Europe Initiative, the Czechia node of the TEF-Health project leverages cross-sectoral collaboration to facilitate the testing of innovative health solutions, including AI initiatives. In doing so, they accelerate the development of these initiatives while ensuring compliance with legal, ethical, quality and interoperability standards.

European Testing and Experimentation Facilities (TEFs) help providers of AI technologies for the healthcare sector to bring their solutions to market faster by providing testing and validation services.
AI-Act – the worldwide first regional regulation enforcing trustworthy AI foresees Testing and Experimentation Facilities (TEFs) as an implementation instrument.
The purpose of TEFs is to “contribute to the implementation of this Regulation. Within their respective mission and fields of competence, they may provide in particular technical and scientific support to providers and notified bodies.” (AI-Act, Article 74) Additionally, access to TEFs shall be facilitated “to bodies, groups or laboratories established or accredited pursuant to any relevant Union harmonization legislation and which fulfil tasks in the context of conformity assessment of products or devices covered by that Union harmonization legislation.” (AI-Act, Article 75)
Four sectorial TEFs have been established under the Digital Europe program – one of which is TEF-Health.
To date, four TEFs have been founded in the sectors Healthcare (TEF-Health), Smart Cities (Citcom.ai), Agriculture (Agrifood-TEF) and Manufacturing (AI-Matters). The four TEFs work closely together under the label xTEF and use synergies. Formally this collaboration is supported by a Coordinate Support Action (CSA). TEF-Health comprises nine participating member states (Germany/lead, Belgium, Czech Republic, Finland, France, Italy, Portugal, Slowakia, Sweden) and 52 participating public and private entities including notified certifiers, standardization authorities, University Hospitals, and Research Organizations.

TEFs are funded by the European Commission (EC) and members states and will provide continuous access to testing infrastructure.
TEF-Health is funded with € 60 Million from January 2023 to December 2027 – where €30 Million are provided by the EC and €30 Million by member states and participating organizations. TEFs are part of the implementation instruments outlined in the AI-Act and as such will continue to exist beyond the 5 years of initial funding.

items.title: Public Service Data Strategy
items.org: Department of Public Expenditure, Infrastructure, Public Service Reform and Digitalisation
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
The Public Service Data Strategy for the period 2019-2023 sets out goals and actions to deliver a more joined-up approach to how data is used and managed in the public service. A new strategy is expected to be published in 2025.

The Public Service Data Strategy 2019–2023 was designed to improve how data is used and managed across Ireland’s public service. Many government departments and agencies collect large amounts of data, but often in disconnected systems. This strategy aimed to fix that by encouraging a more coordinated and consistent approach, helping public bodies share and use data more effectively to improve services.
Key goals included improving data quality, strengthening data governance, and making sure data could be shared securely and responsibly. It also focused on training staff, building better systems, and encouraging evidence-based decision-making. The strategy supported wider government goals like digital transformation and open data, while also respecting privacy and legal standards.
The work involved a range of public bodies and policy makers, with clear actions and guidance to support implementation. It marked an important step toward treating data as a shared resource for the public good.
A new strategy is expected in 2025. It will likely build on the progress made so far, while responding to new challenges such as artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, and growing demands for more transparent and efficient public services.

items.title: Public Sector Innovation Hub
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Luxembourg’s Public Sector Innovation Hub, launched through the GovTech Lab, supports innovation within the public sector by fostering the adoption of new technologies and digital solutions. The hub serves as a platform for collaboration between government entities and tech innovators, aiming to enhance public service delivery through cutting-edge digital solutions.

GovTech Lab Luxembourg is a dynamic initiative driving digital transformation in the public sector. By connecting government bodies with tech innovators, it acts as a catalyst for co-creating forward-thinking solutions that improve public services. The lab emphasizes experimentation, collaboration, and the practical application of emerging technologies to meet societal needs more effectively.

items.title: OTP-Emese
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
OTP-Emese, a specialized HPC system, is tailored specifically for developing and training deep learning language models with a computational capacity estimated at 27 PetaFlops on GPT data. Positioned as a resource for advancing natural language processing (NLP) capabilities, OTP-Emese serves both commercial and research needs, driving innovation in AI language models.

OTP-Emese is a specialized high-performance computing (HPC) system built to meet the increasing demands of training deep learning language models. As natural language processing (NLP) technologies grow more complex, traditional computing systems often lack the capacity to handle the massive data and processing needs. OTP-Emese addresses this by offering an estimated 27 PetaFlops of computational power, making it suitable for training large-scale models like GPT.
Its main purpose is to support both commercial and research efforts in AI language model development. By providing a powerful and stable infrastructure, it helps developers and researchers train models faster, more efficiently, and with better results. Users include AI engineers, data scientists, and academic institutions working on NLP tasks such as machine translation, text generation, and chatbots.
The system is actively maintained and optimized for deep learning workloads. Although its current focus is language models, the platform’s capacity makes it adaptable for other advanced AI tasks.

items.title: Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Microsoft
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
A strategic partnership has been established between Microsoft and the Ministry of Economics, the Ministry of Smart Administration and Regional Development, the Investment and Development Agency of Latvia (LIAA), and the State Digital Development Agency. The MoU focuses on establishing a National Centre for AI and accelerating digital transformation in public administration to enhance service delivery and efficiency.

In December 2024, Latvia signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Microsoft to advance artificial intelligence and digital innovation in the public sector. The collaboration includes the creation of a National Center for Artificial Intelligence, pilot projects for process digitization, and the use of Microsoft’s AI tools like Azure AI Services. The initiative aims to modernize public administration and improve service delivery.

items.title: Levente HPC
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Levente project, Hungary’s initiative to develop a 20 PetaFlops mid-range supercomputer, is a EuroHPC JU-supported endeavor aimed at bolstering Hungary’s compute infrastructure. Current delays in implementation are due to economic challenges related to the pandemic and other geopolitical factors. Once operational, Levente is expected to significantly enhance Hungary’s capacity for computationally intensive R&D and support large-scale AI projects across industries.

The Levente project is Hungary’s plan to build a powerful supercomputer with a capacity of 20 PetaFlops to boost its computing power for research and AI projects. This is important because many scientific and industrial tasks now require large amounts of computing resources, which Hungary’s current systems cannot fully support.
The main goal of Levente is to provide advanced computing to universities, research centers, and industries, helping them run complex simulations and AI models more efficiently. This will support innovation in areas like healthcare, manufacturing, and technology development.
Supported by the European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC JU), the project involves government bodies, academic institutions, and industry partners working together to build and operate the supercomputer. However, the project has faced delays due to economic challenges linked to the COVID-19 pandemic and geopolitical issues.
Once operational, Levente will significantly improve Hungary’s ability to handle demanding research and industrial tasks. In the future, it could expand and connect with Europe’s wider supercomputing network, strengthening Hungary’s role in international research and innovation.

items.title: KURSUOK / one stop shop
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
KURSUOK is a national adult education platform that operates on a one-stop-shop principle, where individuals can choose the training they need and that align with state priorities, and receive funding of up to 500 Euros. The KURSUOK platform aims to encourage adults to develop their general and professional competencies, contribute to fostering a lifelong learning culture in society, and provide opportunities for individuals who want to learn to apply for state funding.

KURSUOK is Lithuania’s national adult learning platform designed to promote lifelong learning. Operating as a one-stop-shop, it allows individuals to select training aligned with national priorities and apply for funding of up to €500. The platform empowers adults to enhance both general and professional skills, supporting personal growth and workforce development.

items.title: GovTech Sandbox
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
This pilot programme is being implemented to responsibly test AI solutions and gather information on the potential opportunities and risks of using this technology in the public sector. The pilot iteration of the programme involves 14 public sector organisations and the development of six concepts exploring possible future interactions between the public sector and artificial intelligence.

GovTech Sandbox Lithuania is a pilot programme designed to explore the responsible use of AI in the public sector. Involving 14 public institutions, it supports the development of six experimental concepts to assess both the opportunities and risks of AI, fostering informed innovation and future-ready governance.

items.title: GovTech Lab
items.org: Agency for Science, Innovation and Technology
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The GovTech Laboratory is Lithuania’s main initiative to help bring innovative digital solutions into the public sector. Established in 2018, it helps public sector institutions identify challenges that can be solved by AI or other emerging technologies and invites innovative startups and academia to co-create solutions.

GovTech Lab helps the public sector identify challenges that can be solved by emerging technologies.

items.title: GovTech Challenge Series
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The GovTech Challenge Series is a structured open innovation process that connects public sector challenges and teams with ideas or solutions. The programme is designed to solve complex public sector challenges that do not have a clear answer but a potential to foster the creation of innovative digital solutions. The GovTech Challenge Series is supported by a co-creation acceleration programme, designed to foster user centricity, collaboration between public sector institutions and startups.

GovTech Challenge Series is an innovation programme that bridges the gap between public sector needs and tech-driven solutions. By inviting startups and innovators to co-create with government institutions, it transforms complex challenges into opportunities for digital experimentation. The programme fosters user-centric design and agile development whilst also  strengthening the innovation ecosystem by embedding collaboration and adaptability into public service delivery.

items.title: European Health Data Space for Secondary Use @CY CY-EHDS-2ND
items.org: Ministry of Research, Innovation and Digital Policy
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Cyprus aims to strengthen its role in the EHDS by establishing a National Health Data Access Body (HDAB) through the National eHealth Authority (NeHA), enhancing cross-border health services to improve health policymaking and innovation.

Cyprus is working to improve how health data is shared and used within the country and across Europe by joining the European Health Data Space (EHDS). Health data, like medical records and test results, can help improve patient care and support medical research, but sharing it safely and securely has been a challenge.
To tackle this, Cyprus is setting up a National Health Data Access Body (HDAB) under the National eHealth Authority (NeHA). This body will manage access to health data, making sure it is shared responsibly between healthcare providers, researchers, and across borders. The goal is to enhance health services, speed up medical innovation, and improve health policy decisions.
The HDAB will work with hospitals, government agencies, and other partners to ensure privacy and consent rules are respected. It will also support cross-border healthcare, helping patients get care abroad with their data shared safely. Over time, Cyprus plans to expand this system, making health data more useful and accessible, while strengthening its role in Europe’s health data network.

items.title: Etalon of National Interpreted Genome Map in Czech Republic (ENIGMA)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Conduct comprehensive whole-genome sequencing of Czech individuals to map the central European genome. This effort involves sequencing and analysing the genomes of approximately 1 200 healthy citizens from the Olomouc district, contributing to a digital genome map and providing a publicly accessible tool, Gen Seeker, for exploring genetic variants in the Czech population.

A project of high technological level and high degree of innovation focusing on the development of new diagnostic products and software bioinformatics solutions, including a DNA database. The mentioned solution is unique in its scope in the Czech Republic and Central Europe. The combination of advanced diagnostics and bioinformatics products completely pushes the boundaries of personalized medicine, speeds up and makes not only the process of developing new drugs, but also therapy more efficient.

items.title: EHDSxShare
items.org: Deputy Ministry of Research, Innovation and Digital Policy
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The xShare initiative aims to enable seamless health data sharing across Europe through the European EHRxF, with Cyprus integrating the xShare Button into national health portals to support data exchange, research, and innovation in the EHDS.

xShare envisions everyone sharing their health data in EEHRxF with a click-of-abutton. The xShare button to be featured across health portals and patient apps and allow people to exercise their data portability rights under GDPR. Hence, the European EHRxF will be the driver for research and innovation in EHDS. xShare will establish the European EHRxF Standards and Policy Hub, the “Hub” partnership of six standards developing organizations (CEN/TC251, HL7 Europe, IHE Europe, SNOMED, CDISC, IEEE) market actors (DIGITAL Europe, MedTech-Europe and EUCROF), supported by competence centers, nationals and regional authorities and European SMEs. xShare will develop: • Harmonized common specifications, create and maintain xBundles i.e., collection of common data specifications including FHIR implementation guides, tools and data sets, and educational support for key EHRxF health information domains as noted in the EHDS draft regulation Annex 1. 2) A set of common elements across EHRxF health information domains applicable across EHDS-1 (JA-9), public/population health (EHDS-2), and clinical research. • Extended harmonized IPS specification to include care plans and making it fit for the purpose of clinical research use cases i.e. clinical trial eligibility, real world data, patient reported outcomes, and returning clinical research data to patients. • xShare feature the xShare Button in 8 adoption settings in Hospital network (Italy), National portal (Greece, Ireland, Cyprus), regional network with emphasis in medical tourism and the connection of the public to the private sector (Catalunya and Madeira), entry of digital health applications to the myHealthSpace ecosystem in France. Care plans will be demonstrated in Denmark. xShare investigate the feasibility and value of the EU xShare Industry label as a vehicle towards implementing the draft EHDS regulation. Lastly open calls at the last year of the project aim to onboard with EHRxF almost 100 settings across Europe.

items.title: E-prescriptions
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
E-prescriptions are the second action within the National eHealth Strategy for the period 2016–2020.  Within this action, Phase I (a gradual move to full-scale electronic prescriptions) was introduced and then the legal obligation to create medical prescriptions only in electronic form, the so-called electronic prescription, was introduced on 1 January 2018.

Electronic prescription and the implementation of the ePrescription information system are based in legislation – Act No 378/2007 Coll., on Pharmaceuticals, as amended. The doctor issues an electronic prescription (ePrescription) for the patient and on the basis of the ePrescription, the pharmacy dispenses the medicinal product. The Central Repository of Electronic Prescriptions (“CÚER”), as one of the components of the ePrescription system, collects and stores all ePrescriptions under conditions stipulated by effective legislation. The implemented ePrescription system is one of the provided eHealth services and its operation in the Czech Republic has been mandatory since 1 January 2018. Section 81f of Act No 378/2007 Coll., on Pharmaceuticals, permits certain exceptional situations in which it is still possible to issue paper prescriptions.

items.title: E-course for Basic Competence level in AI for Public Administration Employees
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This foundational AI training programme for 1,000 public administration employees is structured into four modules: i) Introduction to AI, ii) AI Concepts and Applications, iii) AI Issues and Ethics, and iv) Future and Practical Use of AI. It aims to improve AI literacy in public administration and encourage AI adoption in government services.

VAS – Latvia’s School of Public Administration plays a key role in advancing digital transformation across the public sector. Through initiatives like the Digital Academy for Public Administration, VAS supports the development of digital skills, promotes data-driven governance, and fosters innovation. Its programmes focus on upskilling civil servants, implementing AI responsibly, and enhancing service delivery through modern technologies.

items.title: Biobank.cy
items.org: Center of Excellence in Biobanking and Biomedical Research of the University of Cyprus
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Center of Excellence in Biobanking and Biomedical Research of the University of Cyprus contributes to the European Genomic Data Infrastructure (GDI) which aims to implement the 1+MG initiative to advance genomic medicine across Europe. Biobank.cy operates as the first biobank approved by the Cyprus National Bioethics Committee housed within the University of Cyprus and it was built based on funding from the European Regional Development Fund and the Republic of Cyprus.

Biobank.cy holds samples from more than 1% of Cyprus population with a national bioethics approval and citizens’ consent ready to be used for research in the context of the 1+MG initiative. Finally, biobnak.cy will soon be part of the Genome of Europe (GoE) network.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Preparing Responses to Taxpayer Inquiries
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This pilot project explores AI applications in tax administration by using AI tools to generate responses on labour taxes and related topics, such as income tax, payroll deductions, and state social insurance contributions. The goal is to improve response efficiency and accuracy in handling taxpayer inquiries.

As part of its broader strategy to promote AI innovation, Latvia has launched a pilot project under the National Artificial Intelligence Center to explore AI applications in tax administration. The initiative uses AI tools to generate responses to inquiries on labour taxes, income tax, payroll deductions, and social insurance contributions.

items.title: AI4Citizens
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This project focuses on AI adoption in local and regional governments, addressing both opportunities and challenges. It aims to improve public services, enhance governance efficiency, and mitigate risks related to AI in municipal administration, such as security, ethics, and trust. The initiative supports responsible AI governance in cities and regions.

AI4Citizens is a European initiative aimed at supporting ethical and effective AI governance in cities and regions. It focuses on helping local and regional governments navigate the opportunities and risks of AI adoption by promoting knowledge exchange, co-creation, and policy development. The goal is to ensure AI integration enhances public services while safeguarding ethics, trust, and legal compliance.

items.title: AI and Data Governance Workshops
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Luxembourg's Ministry for Digitalization has organized a series of workshops on AI and data governance for public decision-makers. These workshops aim to raise awareness and prepare for the upcoming review of the National AI2030 Strategy, ensuring that key stakeholders are informed and engaged in shaping the future of AI and data governance in the country.

Daprolab Reloaded, led by Luxembourg’s Ministry for Digitalization, is a strategic workshop series focused on AI and data governance. Designed for public decision-makers, it fosters informed dialogue and capacity-building ahead of the National AI2030 Strategy review. The initiative supports responsible innovation and ensures that key stakeholders are equipped to shape Luxembourg’s digital future.

items.title: AI Charter
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
In response to the growing role of AI in parliamentary activities, Luxembourg's Chamber of Deputies has established an AI Charter that outlines 10 key guidelines for the responsible use of AI. These guidelines ensure that AI is used ethically and transparently in parliamentary procedures, promoting accountability and respect for human rights.

AI Charter by the Chamber of Deputies sets a framework for the ethical and transparent use of artificial intelligence in parliamentary work. Comprising 10 guiding principles, the charter promotes responsible innovation, safeguards democratic values, and ensures respect for human rights in the digital age.

items.title: embrAIsme
items.org: Federal Chancellery Austria and Interreg Europe
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
embrAIsme is an Interreg Europe project co-financed by the Federal Chancellery Austria which endeavours to encourage AI takeup at SMEs, in particular by raising awareness of AI and the importance of AI skills, facilitating access to funding and building tools to ease the compliance burden of SMEs.

embrAIsme is an Interreg Europe project co-financed by the Austrian Federal Chancellery that aims to support small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in adopting artificial intelligence (AI). The initiative addresses the challenge that many SMEs face in understanding, accessing, and implementing AI technologies, which can limit their competitiveness and ability to innovate.
The primary objectives of embrAIsme are to raise awareness of AI and its benefits, promote the development of AI skills among SME employees, facilitate access to funding opportunities, and provide practical tools to reduce regulatory and compliance burdens. By addressing these barriers, the project seeks to make AI more accessible and actionable for smaller businesses that often lack internal expertise or resources.
The project works through a combination of training programs, workshops, informational campaigns, and the creation of practical support tools. It engages a wide range of stakeholders, including regional and national innovation agencies, industry partners, research institutions, and SMEs themselves. These collaborations ensure that the support provided is both practical and aligned with the real needs of businesses.

items.title: Working Group on Artificial Intelligence
items.original_name: Grupa Robocza ds. Sztucznej Inteligencji – GRAI
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Grupa Robocza ds. Sztucznej Inteligencji – GRAI
items.body:
Working Group on Artificial Intelligence brings together 350 experts across 14 subgroups industry, legal, research across many sectors including health. The GRAI followed the Policy for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in Poland from 2020 to build capacity and knowledge within Polish businesses on AI while also considering regulatory compliance and protection of human dignity.

GRAI was established to support the implementation of the Policy for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in Poland (2020), aiming to foster AI adoption in both public and private sectors. The group focuses on building capacity within Polish businesses, ensuring regulatory alignment (including with the EU AI Act), and promoting ethical AI use that respects human dignity and democratic values.

items.title: Training on AI for healthcare professionals
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
AI training is available for all healthcare professionals through the Institute of Public Services. The curriculum includes the "Artificial Intelligence Introduction" module, which covers fundamental AI concepts and their applications in healthcare. Additionally, healthcare professionals have the opportunity to attend various AI and healthcare courses and receive refunds of up to EUR 1 165 per year.

Malta’s AI Training Programme for Healthcare Professionals offers a structured learning pathway designed to strengthen digital literacy in clinical settings. Beyond basic concepts, the curriculum includes modules on AI-driven diagnostics, predictive analytics, and ethical deployment in medicine, helping practitioners understand how machine learning, natural language processing, and cloud-based models integrate into patient care pathways. Funded through the Institute of Public Services, the initiative aims to enhance workforce preparedness and ensure clinicians can confidently apply AI tools in decision-making and workflow optimisation across hospitals and primary care.

items.title: Smart labs
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
All high schools in Romania are being equipped with intelligent laboratories (smart labs), with the Ministry of Education ensuring the funding of 1120 projects through the NRRP. Smart labs offer students the opportunity to personalise learning based on topics of interest and to reflect on their own learning process through the use of AI.

The initiative to equip high schools with smart labs is part of Romania's broader educational transformation under the NRRP. The Ministry of Education is funding 1,120 projects to establish these advanced digital learning environments. Each lab is designed to foster personalized learning, allowing students to explore subjects of interest and reflect on their learning processes. AI integration within these labs enables adaptive learning experiences and supports the development of digital competencies among students.
Key Objectives:
Enhance Digital Literacy: Equip students with the necessary skills to navigate and utilize digital technologies effectively.Personalized Learning: Provide tools that allow students to tailor their learning experiences to individual interests and needs.AI Integration: Incorporate artificial intelligence to facilitate adaptive learning and support educational outcomes.Support SMEs: By improving digital competencies, the initiative indirectly aids small and medium-sized enterprises in their digital transformation efforts.

items.title: SNOMED CT and Semantic Interoperability
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
In 2023, Poland committed to the implementation and use of SNOMED CT classification standard for its health data to enable semantic interoperability and establish the foundations for AI solutions in its health services.

In 2023, Poland officially committed to implementing SNOMED CT, a global clinical terminology standard, to enhance semantic interoperability across its healthcare system. This move supports the structured and consistent exchange of health data, laying the groundwork for AI-driven solutions in clinical decision-making and patient care. By adopting SNOMED CT, Poland aims to improve the quality, safety, and efficiency of its digital health services, aligning with international best practices for health data management.

items.title: Robotics and Life
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
At ISCED level 2, the integrated optional subject “Robotics and Life” aims to train skills in transdisciplinary and multidisciplinary use of concepts acquired in Physics, Mathematics, Informatics and ICT, to develop research and technical creative skills. It includes designing and assembling models of robots and developing driving algorithms and programmes in simulated working environments.

The subject “Robotica și viața (Robotics and Life)” is an optional subject in Romanian gymnasium (grades 6–7) offered one hour per week. It is designed as an interdisciplinary course, integrating content and skills from Mathematics, Physics, Informatics and ICT to build a broader STEM foundation.
Its objectives include:
Forming transdisciplinary / multidisciplinary skills in students so they can link concepts across subject areas.Encouraging technical creativity, for example by designing and building robot models and developing control algorithms.Developing algorithmic thinking, modelling, and an understanding of virtual simulations, where physical robotics kits are not available.The curriculum is competency-centered, referencing the gymnasium graduate profile, Romania’s Digital Agenda strategy, and uses existing school resources where possible (ICT labs, internet, simulators).
