If kits are available, physical robot-building is included, but simulations ensure the subject can be delivered in schools without extra costly resources.

items.title: Robotics Project at Mater Dei Hospital
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Mater Dei Hospital uses advanced robotic systems to assist surgeons during operations. These systems improve surgical precision, reduce recovery times, and enhance patient outcomes, aiming to ensure safer and more efficient procedures.

In 2024, the hospital performed 104 robotic surgeries, primarily utilizing the Da Vinci Surgical System. These procedures addressed cancers affecting the esophagus, stomach, pancreas, intestines, and prostate. The Da Vinci system allows surgeons to operate through small incisions, offering 3D visualization and enhanced dexterity.

items.title: RapidAI solution
items.org: Medical Imaging departments of Mater Dei and Gozo General Hospital
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
An AI-powered imaging solution that generates advanced and perfusion scans to support faster and more accurate diagnoses. RapidAI is used in the Medical Imaging departments of Mater Dei and Gozo General Hospital, particularly for stroke and aneurysm treatment.

RapidAI is an AI-powered medical imaging platform used in Maltese hospitals to support rapid stroke and aneurysm diagnosis. It analyses CT and angiography scans to detect vessel occlusions and assess brain perfusion, improving clinical decision-making. Recently, its AngioFlow tool gained FDA clearance for real-time perfusion imaging during interventions, further enhancing treatment precision.

items.title: Promote AI use for better policymaking and/or public service delivery
items.org: Ministry of Transformation and Public Services
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Several relevant initiatives developed as part of public service modernisation efforts (and with an explicit commitment to using open-source components and follow open data practice).

• In May 2023, the Minister of Transformation and Public Services and the Prime Minister, decided to commit and invest in AI in order to improve the quality of public services through Services Publics+, implemented by all public services and based in particular on the “Je Donne Mon avis” feature, i.e. a platform that enables all French citizens to give and share their opinions on how to improve public services.  
• Albert, an LLM designed on the basis of “free and open” technological bricks, pre-trained and available in open source, is being tested in various administrations.
• The Alliance Numérique incubator supports projects relating to AI models/AI-based solutions for the public sector.

items.title: Portuguese Quantum Institute
items.org: Instituto Superior Técnico and University of Lisbon’s School of Science and Engineering
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Portuguese Quantum Institute (PQI), a new research institution founded by Instituto Superior Técnico and the University of Lisbon’s School of Science and Engineering. PQI conducts theoretical research in quantum networks, quantum computation, and quantum sensing. It engages both private and public stakeholders in quantum technology initiatives, offers training programs, and participates in international quantum science and technology projects.

The Portuguese Quantum Institute (PQI) is a newly established national institute focused on research, innovation, education, and outreach in Quantum Information Science and Technologies.

items.title: Portuguese Quantum Communications Infrastructure (PTQCI)
items.org: National Security Office (Gabinete Nacional de Segurança)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Led by the National Security Office (Gabinete Nacional de Segurança), the PTQCI establishes a national consortium that includes public entities, academic institutions, R&D entities, and businesses to advance quantum communication technologies in Portugal.

The Portuguese Quantum Communication Infrastructure aims to establish Portugal’s first quantum communication network. It forms the country’s terrestrial segment of the broader European Quantum Communication Infrastructure (EuroQCI).

items.title: Plan for new technology and automation of the public sector
items.org: Ministry of Digital Government and Gender Equality
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Plan for new technology and automation of the public sector. The joint public digitalisation strategy 2022-2025 contains an initiative to use new technologies such as AI to free up labour for other tasks in the public sector. New technological solutions, such as automation, AI, and robotics, are increasingly being implemented in the public sector. The state, municipalities, and regions have therefore agreed to launch a 10-year plan for new technology and automation of the public sector.

The initiative aims to help address the expected labor shortage, particularly in areas related to citizen-centric welfare.
A sandbox for testing of AI solutions has been established (see also previous section) that is open to public and private organisations.

items.title: National and European Digital Innovation Hubs
items.org: Federal Ministry of Labor and Economic Affairs, European Commission
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Austria has three national Digital Innovation Hubs and four European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs), which provide SMEs with support in digital transformation and the use of AI through access to expertise and infrastructure. One of these European Hubs, the AI5Production Hub, focuses specifically on AI. Comprising 16 partner institutions in Vienna and Upper Austria, it offers manufacturing companies comprehensive support with digitalisation.

Austria hosts three national Digital Innovation Hubs (DIHs) and four European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs), providing small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) with support in digital transformation and the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI). These hubs address the challenge of enabling companies, particularly SMEs, to access the expertise, technology, and infrastructure required to innovate and remain competitive in a rapidly evolving digital economy.
The primary objective of these hubs is to help businesses integrate AI and other digital technologies into their operations. They provide consulting, training, access to testbeds, and practical support for implementing AI applications in areas such as production, logistics, and service delivery. By connecting companies with research institutions, technology providers, and industry experts, the hubs create an environment that fosters innovation and practical experimentation.
Among Austria’s European Digital Innovation Hubs, the AI5Production Hub focuses specifically on AI for manufacturing. Comprising 16 partner institutions in Vienna and Upper Austria, it offers manufacturing companies comprehensive support in digitalisation, including the development of AI-driven production processes, predictive maintenance, and optimization of operational workflows. The hub combines expertise from universities, research centers, and industry partners to provide hands-on guidance and infrastructure for AI adoption.

items.title: National Strategy for e-Health and Digitalization of the Health System 2030
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Sub-goal 7.2 focuses on using big data in healthcare, specifically enabling the secondary use of health data for research and innovation. The necessary regulations to ensure this, aligned with European Commission recommendations, are currently under consideration and still being discussed.

Sub-goal 7.2 focuses on making better use of health data by enabling its “secondary use”—that is, using patient data not just for care, but also for research and innovation. Today, much of this valuable data is underused, even though it could help improve treatments, public health strategies, and medical research.
The goal is to allow researchers and developers to access this data safely and legally, while protecting patient privacy. To do this, new rules are being developed, in line with recommendations from the European Commission. These regulations are still under discussion and aim to support responsible data sharing across the EU.
This initiative involves healthcare providers, researchers, policymakers, and data protection experts. In the future, it could allow for secure cross-border collaboration, helping to turn Europe’s health data into a powerful resource for innovat

items.title: National Strategy for Semiconductors
items.org: Foundation for Science and Technology (FCT) and the National Innovation Agency (ANI)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This strategy aims to enhance Portugal's semiconductor sector, contributing to EU resilience and strategic autonomy. It is managed by the Foundation for Science and Technology (FCT) and the National Innovation Agency (ANI). It also sets strategic actions to increase industrial involvement and promote national scientific and technological advancements in innovative fields.

The National Strategy for Semiconductors in Portugal, approved in December 2023, outlines the country’s roadmap to strengthen its role in the global semiconductor ecosystem. Coordinated by the Ministry of Science, Technology and Higher Education, alongside the Ministry of Economy and the Sea, FCT, and ANI, the strategy aligns with the European Chips Act and aims to boost national participation in EU-funded initiatives. Key priorities include developing pilot production lines, establishing a design platform, and creating a network of semiconductor competence centers.

items.title: National Platform of Technologies and Semiconductors
items.org: Ministry of Research, Innovation and Digitalisation (MCID); National Institute for Research and Development in Microtechnologies (IMT Bucharest)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
A National Platform of Technologies and Semiconductors has been launched in December 2024 as a priority project aiming to bring together and consolidate the R&D capacities in the area of semiconductors.

The National Platform for Semiconductor Technologies (PNTS), launched in December 2024, is a strategic initiative led by IMT Bucharest and supported by Romania’s Ministry of Research, Innovation, and Digitalization. Funded under the Smart Growth, Digitalization, and Financial Instruments Program (2021–2027), the platform aims to consolidate national R&D capabilities in semiconductors.

items.title: National Framework for Supporting Strategic Semiconductor Investments
items.original_name: Krajowe Ramy Wspierania Strategicznych Inwestycji Półprzewodnikowych
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Krajowe Ramy Wspierania Strategicznych Inwestycji Półprzewodnikowych
items.body:
This programme (Krajowe Ramy Wspierania Strategicznych Inwestycji Półprzewodnikowych) is dedicated to supporting strategic semiconductor investment in Poland, aiming to cover the entire value chain from chip design to production.

Poland’s Krajowe Ramy Wspierania Strategicznych Inwestycji Półprzewodnikowych is a government programme designed to boost strategic semiconductor development across the value chain—from chip design and research to manufacturing and packaging. It offers incentives and support measures aimed at strengthening domestic capacity and making Poland a more competitive player in semiconductor technologies. The framework is intended to align public funding, regulatory support, and industry development to promote sustainable growth in this sector.

items.title: Komondor HPC
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
As part of Hungary’s strategic engagement with the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking, the Komondor HPC system was installed in 2023 through the Governmental IT Development Agency KIFÜ at Debrecen University. With a computing power of 6 PetaFlops, Komondor serves as a critical resource for Hungarian universities, research institutions, and SMEs, providing computational support to drive advancements in research, innovation, and AI-driven projects across various sectors.

In 2023, Hungary installed the Komondor HPC system at Debrecen University as part of its involvement with the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking, a European effort to boost supercomputing capabilities. This system addresses the growing need for powerful computing resources to support research and innovation, especially in areas like AI, data analysis, and complex simulations.
Komondor offers a peak performance of 6 PetaFlops, providing Hungarian universities, research centers, and small and medium-sized businesses with access to advanced computing power. This helps accelerate scientific discoveries, improve industrial innovation, and enhance competitiveness by enabling faster and more complex data processing.
Managed by the Governmental IT Development Agency (KIFÜ), Komondor brings together government, academia, and industry to share a valuable resource that benefits a wide user base. Looking forward, the system will expand alongside EuroHPC’s network of supercomputers, strengthening Hungary’s digital infrastructure and supporting larger, more collaborative research projects across Europe.

items.title: Knowledge centre for municipalities
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Local Government Denmark (KL), which represents municipalities, has established this centre to collect and help share knowledge about digitalisation and help explore how new technologies, including AI, can be applied and create value in municipalities, and identify emerging challenges. It also provides action-oriented guidance and tools on topics ranging from security to IT procurement and framework architecture. KL has also launched an AI school for managers, executives, and politicians.

Local Government Denmark (KL), the association representing Danish municipalities, has established a Digitalisation Centre to strengthen local governments’ capacity to use digital technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI). The centre addresses the growing need for municipalities to adapt to rapid technological change while ensuring that digital transformation creates tangible value for citizens, improves public services, and supports sustainable local development.
The centre’s main objectives are to collect and share knowledge on digitalisation, support municipalities in experimenting with and adopting new technologies, and identify emerging challenges related to digital governance and innovation. It provides municipalities with practical, action-oriented guidance on key areas such as data security, IT procurement, framework architecture, and ethical AI use. By acting as a central hub of expertise, the centre helps ensure that digital solutions are implemented effectively and responsibly across Denmark’s municipalities.
In addition to its advisory and coordination role, KL has launched an AI School designed for managers, executives, and elected officials. This programme aims to build understanding and leadership capacity around AI, enabling decision-makers to recognise opportunities, manage risks, and strategically integrate AI into municipal operations and services.

items.title: Juvoly, AI Speech Recognition for Medical Consultations
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Juvoly is a speech model that transcribes the conversation between patient and General Practitioner (GP) reducing administrative tasks and freeing up time to focus on the patient. The product, QuickConsult, is integrated into the Sanday electronic health record, and planned inegrations with Medicom and MicroHIS.

Juvoly is a Dutch AI startup revolutionizing healthcare through advanced speech recognition and generative AI. Founded in 2023, Juvoly developed QuickConsult, a tool that listens to doctor-patient conversations and automatically generates structured summaries, reducing administrative burden and allowing clinicians to focus more on patient care. Their proprietary Medical Dutch speech model is tailored for healthcare settings and runs entirely on Dutch infrastructure.

items.title: Integrating AI into the Electronic Health Records
items.org: Universitair Medisch Centrum Groningen (UMCG) and the Elisabeth-TweeSteden Hospital (ETZ)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
At Universitair Medisch Centrum Groningen (UMCG) and the Elisabeth-TweeSteden Hospital (ETZ), work is underway to integrate generative AI into the electronic health record, dragging answers to patient’s questions.  The aim is to save healthcare provider time.

UMCG (University Medical Center Groningen) has launched an innovative initiative using artificial intelligence to help healthcare providers respond to patients' written questions more efficiently. Integrated into the hospital’s electronic patient record (EPR) system, the AI reads patient queries and drafts suggested responses, which are then reviewed and personalized by medical staff. This approach aims to reduce administrative workload, freeing up more time for direct patient care. UMCG is the first hospital in Europe to implement this AI chatbot in actual patient communication, ensuring responses remain safe, empathetic, and informative without compromising data privacy.

items.title: Innovative reception of the Emergency Call Center
items.org: General Directorate of Fire Rescue Service
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Czech Republic is modernising its Emergency Call Center system by integrating AI tools to enhance its efficiency and functionality. The upgrade will create a unified, modernised environment, including a dispatcher interface, application, and database, ensuring seamless integration across all components of the integrated rescue system. Additionally, advanced AI-powered analytics will be employed to optimise processes and set capacity parameters, improving overall system performance.

The Czech Republic is undertaking a comprehensive modernisation of its Emergency Call Center system by integrating artificial intelligence (AI) tools to improve its efficiency, functionality, and responsiveness. This initiative addresses the growing need for faster, more coordinated emergency responses in an era of increasing data complexity and demand for real-time decision-making.
The project’s primary goal is to establish a unified, modern environment that seamlessly connects all components of the country’s integrated rescue system. This includes the development of an updated dispatcher interface, application layer, and central database—all designed to work together in a cohesive, interoperable framework. By ensuring full integration, the new system will enhance communication between emergency operators, police, fire, and medical services, enabling faster and more accurate responses to emergencies.
AI plays a central role in this transformation. Advanced analytics and machine learning tools will be employed to optimise workflows, forecast resource needs, and set capacity parameters across the emergency network. These capabilities will not only improve operational performance but also help identify patterns and areas for efficiency gains, contributing to better public safety outcomes.

items.title: Health Data Lake
items.org: Serviços Partilhados do Ministério da Saúde
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
SPMS (Serviços Partilhados do Ministério da Saúde) is developing a health data lake and access portal to support value-based healthcare, enhance data accessibility, and enable interoperability. This initiative aims to facilitate the secondary use of health data for innovation, epidemiological analysis, and research, driving advancements in healthcare services and products.

SPMS is developing a national health data lake and access portal as part of Portugal’s digital health transformation. This initiative supports value-based healthcare by improving data accessibility, interoperability, and secondary use of health data. It aims to enable innovation, epidemiological analysis, and research, ultimately enhancing healthcare services and product development. The project is aligned with broader efforts under Digital Health Portugal, which promotes sustainable and efficient healthcare through strategic use of digital technologies and AI.

items.title: Guidelines for the responsible use of generative AI
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
The Prime Minister’s Office (VNK) has developed common guidelines for the responsible use of generative AI for the Government. There is a government wide network within which experiences and best practices regarding AI use are shared. Furthermore, AI-related coordination will be developed within the government under the auspices of the Digital Office cooperation and coordination structure. This work builds on experience such as the AuroraAI programme.

The Prime Minister’s Office (VNK) in Finland has developed common guidelines to ensure the responsible use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) across government operations. This initiative addresses the need for safe, ethical, and effective AI adoption within public administration, ensuring that emerging AI technologies are used transparently, responsibly, and in ways that maintain public trust.
The primary objective of the initiative is to provide a unified framework for government authorities to implement generative AI while mitigating risks and promoting best practices. This includes guidance on ethical considerations, data protection, transparency, and accountability in AI deployment. By establishing clear principles, the guidelines support consistent and responsible AI use across multiple government agencies.
Implementation relies on a government-wide network where experiences, lessons learned, and best practices regarding AI use are actively shared. Coordination efforts are further supported through the Digital Office cooperation and coordination structure, which oversees AI-related initiatives, facilitates inter-agency collaboration, and ensures alignment with national digital strategies. This work builds on prior experiences, including the AuroraAI programme, which explored AI-driven digital services and citizen-centric solutions.

items.title: Flanders AI-EDIH
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Flanders AI European Digital Innovation Hub (EDIH) aims to accelerate AI adoption among SMEs by offering a neutral, integrated, and accessible service ecosystem.

The Flanders AI European Digital Innovation Hub (EDIH) is designed to accelerate the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) among small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in the region. The initiative addresses the challenge that many SMEs face in integrating AI into their operations due to limited expertise, infrastructure, and access to practical support.
The primary objective of the hub is to provide a neutral, integrated, and accessible service ecosystem where SMEs can explore, experiment with, and implement AI solutions. By offering technical guidance, training, access to AI tools, and collaborative support, the hub helps companies understand how AI can improve efficiency, innovation, and competitiveness across sectors.
 Backed by a consortium of 13 partners, the hub provides targeted support across four key areas: 
i) test before invest, 
ii) skills and training, 
iii) access to funding, and 
iv) innovation ecosystem and networking. By leveraging existing initiatives such as the Flemish Industry Partnership (Industriepartnerschap), the Flanders AI Academy (VAIA), and the Knowledge Centre Data & Society (Kenniscentrum Data & Maatschappij), the hub strengthens AI expertise, fosters collaboration, and enhances digital transformation across Flemish industries

items.title: FedEU.ai
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Supported by Hungary’s participation in the Important Project of Common European Interest (IPCEI) on Cloud, the FedEU.ai project led by Hungarian E-Group aims to foster cloud and AI capabilities within Hungary. FedEU.ai enhances cloud-based infrastructure and services, contributing to secure, scalable AI solutions for businesses and government entities in Hungary.

FedEU.ai is a Hungarian-led project aiming to strengthen national capabilities in cloud computing and artificial intelligence. Led by E‑Group ICT and supported through Hungary’s participation in the Important Project of Common European Interest (IPCEI) on Cloud, the project focuses on building secure, scalable digital infrastructure for both businesses and government use.
The goal is to reduce reliance on foreign cloud providers by developing trusted, local solutions that protect sensitive data while supporting AI innovation. FedEU.ai places strong emphasis on secure data processing, including federated and privacy-preserving methods, so that AI tools can work across multiple systems without compromising confidentiality.
The project is part of a wider European initiative, involving several countries and dozens of partners, to boost Europe’s digital sovereignty. As the technology develops, FedEU.ai will help more Hungarian organisations access safe, advanced AI and cloud services—while keeping control over their data and systems.
References:

items.title: Experimentation with generative AI to support legislative work
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
The Ministry of Transport and Communications has also experimented with the use of generative artificial intelligence based on Finnish language models to support legislative preparation.

The Ministry of Transport and Communications in Finland has conducted experiments using generative artificial intelligence (AI) based on Finnish language models to support legislative preparation. This initiative addresses the challenge of efficiently processing large volumes of legislative texts and drafting proposals while maintaining high standards of accuracy, coherence, and legal compliance.
The primary objective of the project is to explore how AI can assist public officials in drafting, reviewing, and refining legislative documents. By leveraging AI, the Ministry aims to reduce repetitive tasks, streamline workflows, and provide preliminary analyses or drafts that can inform decision-making and enhance the quality of legislative outputs.
The experimentation relies on Finnish-language AI models that are trained to understand and generate text in the context of national legislation. Government experts work alongside AI systems to ensure outputs are legally sound and contextually appropriate, combining human oversight with AI capabilities for efficient and informed legislative work.

items.title: European Digital Innovation Hub (EDIH) Brussels
items.org: Agoria, Sirris, BeCentral, Université libre de Bruxelles (ULB), Vrije Universiteit Brussel (VUB)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The EDIH in Brussels supports SMEs in sustainable digital innovation using AI and emerging technologies. It aims to strengthen the digital capabilities of Brussels' industrial landscape, comprising predominantly SMEs. Strategic goals include economic, social, and environmental transitions and post-COVID recovery. The hub is implemented by Agoria, Sirris, BeCentral, Université libre de Bruxelles (ULB), and VUB, providing services to over 1,500 companies.

The European Digital Innovation Hub (EDIH) Brussels supports small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in adopting sustainable digital innovation, including artificial intelligence (AI) and other emerging technologies. The initiative addresses the challenge that many SMEs face in developing digital capabilities necessary to drive competitiveness, sustainability, and resilience in a rapidly changing industrial and societal landscape.
The primary objective of the hub is to strengthen the digital skills and technological adoption of Brussels’ industrial sector, which is predominantly composed of SMEs. Strategic goals include fostering economic growth, facilitating social and environmental transitions, and supporting post-COVID recovery by enhancing the capacity of companies to implement innovative, digital solutions.
EDIH Brussels is implemented through a partnership of Agoria, Sirris, BeCentral, Université libre de Bruxelles (ULB), and Vrije Universiteit Brussel (VUB). Together, these partners provide SMEs with a comprehensive service ecosystem that includes training, experimentation, technology demonstrations, and access to expertise. The hub currently serves over 1,500 companies, helping them explore AI applications, optimize processes, and develop innovative products and services.

items.title: EuroQCS-Poland
items.org: EuroHPC Joint Undertaking; Poznan Supercomputing and Networking Center (PSNC)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The EuroQCS-Poland project is a joint initiative of Polish and European institutions, owned by the EuroHPC JU and located at the Poznan Supercomputing and Networking Center (PSNC).  EuroQCS-Poland will be a digital, gate-based quantum computer, based on trapped-ions offering 20-plus physical qubits, with the infrastructure allowing for remote access. PSNC leads the EuroQCS-Poland consortium, handling the integration and development of hardware and software.

EuroQCS-Poland is a European initiative to install a quantum computer in Poland, hosted at the Poznan Supercomputing and Networking Center. The system, called PIAST-Q, is based on trapped-ion technology and offers over 20 physical qubits. It is designed to support research and innovation across science, industry, and public sectors, and will be integrated with classical supercomputing infrastructure to enable hybrid computing approaches. The project is part of a broader European effort to advance quantum technologies and is co-funded by the EU and Poland’s Ministry of Digital Affairs.

items.title: EuroHPC JU
items.org: National Institute for Research and Development in Informatics – ICI Bucharest
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Romania participates in the European High-Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC JU). The Romanian partner is the National Institute for Research and Development in Informatics – ICI Bucharest. Such capacity is primarily used for scientific and research purposes, and the demand for AI-specific uses has grown particularly in recent years and this infrastructure could be further leveraged to support AI start-ups and SMEs.

Romania, through ICI Bucharest, contributes to the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking, accessing high-performance computing resources for scientific and research applications. With growing interest in AI, this infrastructure presents an opportunity to support emerging AI start-ups and SMEs, expanding its use beyond academia to foster innovation and competitiveness in Romania’s tech ecosystem.

items.title: Education and Employment Programme
items.org: Ministry of Investments and European Projects
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This programme helps people gain digital and green skills needed for today’s jobs. It supports new or updated vocational training standards and trains teachers to keep up with technology. The aim is to prepare workers for careers in areas like AI, robotics, and sustainable development.

Romania's Education and Employment Programme aims to align the country's vocational education and training (VET) system with the evolving needs of the labour market, particularly in the digital and green sectors. Key components of the programme include:
Curriculum Development: Updating vocational training standards and curricula to reflect technological advancements in fields such as AI, 3D printing, and sustainable technologies.Teacher Training: Providing professional development opportunities for educators to equip them with the knowledge and skills necessary to teach the updated curricula effectively.Industry Collaboration: Engaging with industry partners to ensure that the training provided aligns with current and future labour market needs.Digital and Green Skills Focus: Emphasizing the development of digital and green competencies to prepare the workforce for the green and digital transition.The programme is supported by Romania's Recovery and Resilience Plan, which allocates significant funding for investments and reforms in education and employment. This includes investments in digital and green skills development, as well as initiatives to modernize vocational education and training institutions.

items.title: Development of AI solutions for patient triage
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This initiative focuses on developing AI tools to help hospitals in Croatia better triage patients. It benefits medical staff and patients by improving decision-making and speeding up care. The goal is to make healthcare more efficient and responsive using advanced technology.

This Croatian initiative aims to create and implement artificial intelligence solutions to support patient triage in healthcare settings. By using AI to assess and prioritise patient needs, the system helps healthcare professionals make faster, more accurate decisions. The project addresses the need for more efficient hospital workflows and improved patient outcomes through the integration of innovative digital tools.

items.title: Deucalion
items.org: Government of Portugal / University of Minho
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
In September 2023, Portugal’s most powerful supercomputer, Deucalion, was installed at the University of Minho. Capable of ten petaflops, Deucalion has expanded Portugal's HPC capacity tenfold. It enables advanced simulations and modelling across a wide range of scientific fields, including personalised medicine, drug and material design, environmental monitoring, climate change mitigation, and the development of of smart cities and autonomous vehicles.

Deucalion is Portugal’s most powerful supercomputer, inaugurated in September 2023 as part of the European High-Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC JU). Located at the University of Minho, it is designed to support advanced research in fields such as climate modeling, artificial intelligence, and biomedical sciences. Deucalion combines cutting-edge CPU and GPU technologies to deliver high computational performance while maintaining energy efficiency, contributing to Europe's strategic autonomy in digital and scientific innovation.

items.title: Deployment of the Government Cloud Infrastructure
items.org: Authority for the Digitalisation of Romania (ADR)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The main objective of this investment is to deploy government cloud infrastructure, using secure and energy efficient technologies to ensure the safe, interoperable and standardised public date, in order to provide higher quality public services. By centralising and modernising IT systems, the project seeks to improve data protection, enable seamless communication between government agencies, and reduce operational expenses.

Romania’s Government Cloud legislation, adopted in June 2022, establishes a national hybrid cloud infrastructure to modernize and centralize public sector IT systems. The platform includes both private and certified public cloud components and follows a “cloud first” policy, prioritizing cloud solutions for new and upgraded government IT projects. Managed by multiple national agencies, the initiative aims to enhance data security, interoperability, and service quality while reducing costs.

items.title: DIGITALIS
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
DIGITALIS is designed to support Flemish manufacturing SMEs in their digital and green transition, equipping them with the necessary tools to stay competitive in an evolving industrial landscape.

Its key objectives include: 
i) accelerating the adoption of digital technologies on the shop floor, 
ii) enhancing the digital skills of SME workforces, 
iii) strengthening collaboration within the European Digital Innovation Hub (DIH) network, and iv) contributing to the European Green Deal goals. The initiative provides targeted support for AI, cybersecurity, and other digital technologies, ensuring SMEs can harness innovation for sustainable growth.

items.title: Cross-sectoral Care Agreement
items.org: Ministry of Health, Welfare and Sport
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The objective of the funding is to support the implementation of the novel bundled funding model of healthcare in the Netherlands – the Integrated Care Agreement (IZA) – by accelerating the processes in which healthcare providers, healthcare professionals, patient organisations, health insurers, and municipalities together develop and realise plans for impactful healthcare transformation.

The Integrated Care Agreement (IZA) in the Netherlands is a major healthcare reform initiative aimed at improving collaboration across the healthcare system. Backed by €2.395 billion in funding from 2023 to 2027, its goal is to accelerate the development and implementation of regional transformation plans. These plans are co-created by healthcare providers, professionals, insurers, municipalities, and patient organizations, focusing on delivering more appropriate, efficient, and patient-centered care through a bundled funding model.

items.title: Cross-border and multi-country projects — Low Power Processors, incl. support for Romanian companies involved in IPCEI ME/CT
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects

items.title: Creating an AI Model of the Navigation Framework within the Service Catalogue
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This project aims to enhance citizens' access to digital public administration services using AI.

The initiative focuses on developing a tool based on large language model technology, designed to streamline navigation through digital services. By processing queries in natural language, the tool will offer quick, relevant, and personalised responses, making it easier for users to access the information and services they need.

items.title: Competitive call for projects for digitalisation of higher education
items.original_name: Apel competitiv pentru proiecte privind digitalizarea învățământului superior
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Apel competitiv pentru proiecte privind digitalizarea învățământului superior
items.body:
This initiative supports the digital transformation of higher education in Romania. It helps students, teachers, researchers, and IT professionals by improving digital infrastructure and offering digital skills training. The goal is to modernize education and boost Romania’s competitiveness in emerging technologies.

Launched in December 2022, Romania's competitive call for digitalisation projects in higher education focuses on three main areas:
Digital Infrastructure Modernisation. Universities are investing in:Modernising laboratories and computing centresEstablishing innovation hubs and start-up incubation centresDeveloping digital librariesDesigning and adapting resources for online learning and assessmentDigital Skills Training. The initiative supports:Training programmes for students, teaching, and research staff to enhance digital competenciesDevelopment of learning modules and study programmes for emerging professionsAdvanced Digital Skills Development. Focused on IT specialists, the programme aims to:Develop advanced skills in emerging technologies such as AI, Blockchain, and IoTIncrease the added value of services and products developed by Romanian IT&C companiesEnhance the competitiveness of the Romanian IT sectorThe projects selected under this call are currently in the implementation phase, with an extended deadline for completion set to December 31, 2025.

items.title: C2.3. R3-I4 Consolidation of THE CEZIH health information infrastructure system (Central Health information system of the Republic of Croatia)
items.org: Ministry of Justice, Public Administration and Digital Transformation
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
source_urls: A team member has requested headphone replacements. Could you please confirm the cost so I can obtain the necessary approvals from our Head of Department and verify the budget availability?
items.body:
This initiative focuses on improving Croatia’s Central Health Information System (CEZIH) by implementing a TIER 3 data centre to guarantee continuous, dependable, and secure operations. The project aims to migrate the system to a state cloud environment, establish disaster recovery solutions, and enhance overall data management.

Croatia’s Central Health Information System (CEZIH) is essential for managing health data and services. However, its current setup lacks the reliability and security needed for a modern healthcare system. The system is vulnerable to outages and data loss, and it doesn’t meet high availability standards. To address this, the Croatian government launched a project to upgrade CEZIH’s infrastructure, ensuring stable, secure, and round-the-clock operations.
The main goal is to move CEZIH into a state-managed cloud environment and build two data centres—primary and backup—that meet TIER 3 standards. This ensures high system availability and protection against failures. The project also includes disaster recovery planning, improved monitoring, and data backup to prevent service disruptions and data breaches.
Led by the Central State Office for the Development of Digital Society and supported by Croatia’s National Recovery and Resilience Plan, the project runs from 2021 to 2025. Once completed, it will offer a stronger foundation for digital health services, with better reliability, data protection, and room to grow as technology and healthcare demands evolve.

items.title: Analytical AI platform to support draft legislation
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
A Proof of Concept was developed to identify discrepancies with Act No. 12/2020 Coll. on the Right to Digital Services. The project aimed to pinpoint regulations that conflict with this legal framework, highlight these inconsistencies, and propose necessary amendments to ensure alignment with the law.

The Czech Republic has developed a Proof of Concept (PoC) project to support the implementation of Act No. 12/2020 Coll. on the Right to Digital Services, a key piece of legislation ensuring citizens’ ability to interact digitally with public administration. The initiative addresses the challenge of aligning existing regulations with this modern legal framework, which seeks to guarantee accessible, user-friendly, and fully digital public services.
The PoC was designed to systematically identify legal provisions that conflict with or hinder the goals of the Right to Digital Services Act. Using a structured analytical approach, the project examined selected areas of legislation to locate inconsistencies, redundancies, and outdated requirements that could obstruct digital service delivery. By mapping these regulatory barriers, the project created a clear foundation for legal reform aimed at enabling smoother and more coherent digital governance.
In addition to identifying discrepancies, the PoC proposed specific legislative amendments to bring existing laws into conformity with the Act. These recommendations are intended to streamline administrative procedures, remove unnecessary paperwork, and ensure that all public services can be delivered digitally when appropriate.
The initiative represents a forward-looking step in the Czech Republic’s digital transformation journey. By proactively addressing legal obstacles to digitalisation, it supports the creation of a more efficient, transparent, and citizen-oriented public administration. The lessons learned from this pilot are expected to guide future regulatory reviews and reforms across other sectors.

items.title: Academic Computer Centre CYFRONET AGH
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
In the context of its National Digitalisation Strategy, a new “AI Factory” facility will be built at the Academic Computer Centre CYFRONET AGH in Kraków to boost computing power in Poland. The facility is expected to be operational by the end of 2025.

The AI Factories initiative by the European Commission aims to establish a network of advanced AI development hubs across Europe. These facilities leverage high-performance computing resources from the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking to support the creation of large-scale, trustworthy AI models. The project is designed to foster collaboration among researchers, startups, SMEs, and industry by providing access to computing power, data, and expertise. AI Factories will serve various sectors including health, climate, manufacturing, and finance, and are part of a broader strategy to strengthen Europe’s position in global AI innovation.

items.title: AI4Health.Cro
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
A non-profit public-private consortium of experts in the field of AI, healthcare and startups that sees AI as the key to advancing healthcare and medicine. The consortium brings together 15 partners coordinated by the Ruđer Bošković Institute (RBI) and is funded equally under the Digital Europe Programme and the Next Generation EU with a funding period of three years.

A new non-profit consortium is working to bring the benefits of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into healthcare. Coordinated by the Ruđer Bošković Institute in Croatia, the group includes 15 partners from research, healthcare, and the startup world. Their shared goal is to use AI to improve medical care—by supporting faster diagnosis, better treatment decisions, and more efficient healthcare systems.
The project is funded equally by the EU’s Digital Europe Programme and the Next Generation EU fund, with a three-year funding period. By combining expertise from public and private sectors, the consortium aims to develop practical AI tools, help startups scale health innovations, and make sure new technologies meet ethical and safety standards.
Looking ahead, the group plans to expand its work across Europe—by building new partnerships, sharing results, and supporting training and pilot projects. The initiative offers a promising model for how AI can be used responsibly to support better healthcare for all.

items.title: AI-related training for civil servants
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Public Digital Campus brings together and promotes the interministerial digital training offering. The goal is to equip public sector employees—both within and beyond the digital field—with transformative knowledge and skills that are essential for energising public action and delivering high-quality digital services.

The Public Digital Campus in France is an interministerial initiative that brings together and promotes the government’s digital training offerings for public sector employees. The initiative addresses the growing need for civil servants to acquire the knowledge and skills required to implement digital transformation effectively across all areas of public administration.
The primary objective of the Public Digital Campus is to equip public sector professionals—with or without a digital background—with the competencies necessary to drive innovation, improve service delivery, and support data- and technology-driven public action. Training programs cover a broad range of topics, including digital tools, data management, cybersecurity, and emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence.
The campus operates as a central platform, coordinating training content across ministries, providing access to online and in-person courses, and fostering knowledge sharing. By centralizing resources and expertise, the initiative ensures that public employees receive consistent, high-quality training tailored to their roles and responsibilities.

items.title: AI-Triage for General Practitioners
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Huisartsencoöperatie West-Brabant (HCWB) began rolling out an general practitioner AI triage tool to reduce administrative workload and improve the job satisfaction of general practitioners.

The AI triage project by Huisartsencoöperatie West-Brabant (HCWB) aims to support general practitioners by automating parts of the patient intake and assessment process. The tool is designed to reduce administrative workload, improve workflow efficiency, and enhance job satisfaction among GPs. By using AI to assist in initial triage, the system helps prioritize cases, streamline communication, and ensure patients are directed to appropriate care pathways more quickly. The broader goal is to improve access to care while maintaining quality and reducing pressure on primary care services.

items.title: AI in Protontherapy
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
A collaboration between Maastricht UMC+, UMCG and Raysearch have developed an AI proton therapy treatment plan, where the AI developed the plan rather than a radiotherapy planning technician. This treatment is specifically for patients with health and neck cancer. The new technology is able to develop the treatment plan within 2.5 hours with clinical review, rather than two days.

The AI-driven proton therapy planning project, developed through collaboration between University Medical Center Groningen (UMCG) and RaySearch, aims to automate the creation of robust treatment plans for head and neck cancer patients. The system uses a machine learning model trained on historical data from 80 patients to infer dose distributions and generate intensity-modulated proton therapy (IMPT) plans. The primary goals of the project are to reduce manual workload, improve planning efficiency, and maintain clinical quality and robustness. The framework supports rapid plan generation—under 20 minutes—and is designed to facilitate adaptive therapy and modality comparisons between photon and proton treatments.

items.title: AI for Healthcare pilot project: Forecasting application
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
An AI-driven tool for budgeting, procurement, and inventory management in healthcare. The system predicts future outcomes using data analysis and management insights, helping optimize costs, ensure resource supply, and prepare for fluctuations in demand.

The AI for healthcare pilot project under Malta’s Ultimate AI Launchpad 2030 focuses on using artificial intelligence to improve financial and resource management in the health sector. It aims to support hospitals and clinics by predicting future needs, optimizing procurement and inventory, and helping manage budgets more effectively. The goal is to ensure consistent supply of medical resources while reducing costs and preparing for changes in demand.

items.title: AI Fund
items.org: Federal Public Service Policy and Support (FPS BOSA)
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
Established under FPS BOSA, the AI Fund supports applied AI research in domains prioritised by the National Convergence Plan, including health, cybersecurity, and AI development.

Belgium’s Federal Public Service for Policy and Support (FPS BOSA) has established the AI Fund to support applied research in artificial intelligence. The initiative addresses the need to accelerate AI development in strategic domains that are critical for public services, economic growth, and societal well-being, ensuring that research efforts align with national priorities.
The primary objective of the AI Fund is to finance applied AI research projects in areas identified by the National Convergence Plan, including health, cybersecurity, and broader AI development. By providing targeted funding, the initiative encourages collaboration between academic institutions, research centers, and industry, fostering the creation of innovative AI solutions that can be deployed in real-world contexts.
The fund operates through a competitive application process, inviting researchers and institutions to submit proposals aligned with priority domains. Selected projects receive financial support, technical guidance, and opportunities for knowledge exchange, ensuring that outcomes contribute effectively to Belgium’s AI ecosystem and public sector modernization.

items.title: AI Framework Guiding Statements
items.org: Federal Ministry of the Interior and Community
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
Launched by the BMI, this framework focuses on an opportunity-oriented and responsible approach to AI within the Ministry and its affiliates. It outlines guiding principles, such as human-centred design, transparency, and fairness, and identifies critical factors along the AI value chain that contribute to successful AI use in public administration. Similarly, the Foreign Office (AA) has adopted an AI-Charter.

Germany has developed AI frameworks within its federal administration to promote responsible, opportunity-oriented adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) across public institutions. Launched by the Federal Ministry of the Interior and Community (BMI), the framework addresses the challenge of integrating AI technologies into government operations while ensuring that ethical, legal, and social considerations are fully respected.
The primary objective of the BMI framework is to guide AI implementation within the Ministry and its affiliated bodies, fostering human-centred, transparent, and fair AI applications. It outlines key principles for AI use and identifies critical factors along the AI value chain that contribute to successful, responsible deployment in public administration. These principles aim to ensure that AI systems enhance service quality, support decision-making, and maintain public trust.
Similarly, the Federal Foreign Office (AA) has adopted an AI Charter, establishing standards and recommendations for responsible AI use in its operations. Both initiatives encourage structured governance, risk assessment, and accountability in AI applications, ensuring that public sector AI projects are aligned with national ethical guidelines and policy objectives.

items.title: AI Education Council
items.original_name: Consiliul pentru Educație în Domeniul Inteligenței Artificiale
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Consiliul pentru Educație în Domeniul Inteligenței Artificiale
items.body:
The newly formed Romanian Committee for AI includes the establishment of the AI Education Council, facilitating input and guidance on issues related to Romanian AI skills development, education and training.

The Romanian Committee for Artificial Intelligence is a government-level body created to coordinate AI strategy across different domains such as ethics, education, research, and innovation. Within this structure, the AI Education Council is charged with overseeing educational policy related to AI: ensuring that training, curricula, and skill-building align with national priorities.
Key functions and intended outcomes include:
Shaping AI education policy in Romania, especially how AI is introduced into school and university curricula.Advising on how to train teachers and researchers in AI-related skills, to ensure a supply of qualified professionals.Integrating ethical, societal, and inclusive dimensions into AI education, so that not just skill but responsibility is embedded in learning.

items.title: A National Health Systems Strategy for Malta 2023 - 2030
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Digital Health Strategic Roadmap aims to meet the needs of citizens, patients, and health professionals, focusing on enabling patient-centered care. It’s a foundation for system integration and continuity of care across the healthcare ecosystem.

Malta’s National Health Systems Strategy 2023–2030 outlines long-term investments and reforms to strengthen healthcare delivery and system resilience. It places strong emphasis on digital transformation and data governance, aiming to improve interoperability, enhance electronic health records, and enable more efficient health data use across institutions. The strategy also supports the development of secure digital and computing infrastructure to facilitate advanced analytics and the gradual integration of AI-driven tools into healthcare planning and service delivery.

items.title: National Strategy for SMEs 2021-2027
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Bulgaria's National Strategy for SMEs 2021–2027, adopted by the Council of Ministers on April 1, 2021, outlines a comprehensive policy framework to support the development and competitiveness of small and medium-sized enterprises. The strategy focuses on enhancing digital transformation, fostering innovation, improving access to finance, and strengthening the overall business environment for SMEs.

The National Strategy for SMEs 2021–2027 serves as a key strategic document for Bulgaria, aligning with European Union policies to promote sustainable and digital growth of small and medium-sized enterprises. Developed under a project funded by the European Commission's Directorate-General for Structural Reform Support, the strategy was informed by an analysis of the state of SMEs in Bulgaria conducted by PricewaterhouseCoopers Bulgaria.
Key Objectives:
Digital Transformation: Promote the adoption of digital technologies among SMEs to enhance efficiency and competitiveness.Innovation and Research: Encourage innovation and research activities within SMEs to foster growth and adaptation to market changes.Access to Finance: Improve access to financial resources for SMEs to support their development and expansion.Business Environment: Enhance the regulatory and institutional framework to facilitate the growth of SMEs.Implementation and Monitoring:
The strategy is to be implemented through an Action Plan and annual programmes adopted by the Minister of Economy and Industry. An interim evaluation and analysis of the state of SMEs will be conducted to assess the effectiveness of the strategy and make necessary adjustments.

items.title: National Semiconductor Strategy
items.org: Department of Enterprise, Trade and Employment
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Ireland’s National Semiconductor Strategy is being developed to guide research and innovation in semiconductor technologies. Research in this area is conducted at several Research Ireland Centres. A public consultation in 2023 helped shape the strategy, which was published in early 2025.

The National Semiconductor Strategy aims to strengthen Ireland’s position in semiconductor research, development, and innovation. It builds on the work of multiple Research Ireland Centres, which conduct studies in semiconductor-based technologies and related fields.
Key objectives of the strategy include:
Supporting research and innovation in semiconductors and related technologiesGuiding investment and resource allocation for research infrastructureEnhancing collaboration between research centres, industry, and governmentThe strategy’s development included a public consultation process in 2023 to gather input from stakeholders, ensuring alignment with national and international priorities

items.title: National Research and Innovation Strategy
items.original_name: National Strategie fir Fuerschung an Innovatioun
items.org: Ministry of Higher Education and Research (MESR)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: National Strategie fir Fuerschung an Innovatioun
items.body:
Luxembourg's National Research and Innovation Strategy positions artificial intelligence (AI) as a key enabling technology across its research priorities. The strategy aims to scale AI for specific use cases, such as personalized healthcare and education, and to establish Luxembourg as a "living laboratory" demonstrating the societal benefits of AI at the national level.

Luxembourg's National Research and Innovation Strategy, approved in December 2019, outlines the country's vision for its scientific ecosystem over the next decade. AI is identified as a transversal and interdisciplinary priority, integrated into the four main research areas:
Personalized Healthcare: Leveraging AI to enhance medical treatments tailored to individual patients.Personalized Education: Utilizing AI to adapt educational experiences to the needs of each learner.Autonomous Mobility: Developing AI-driven transportation solutions.Financial Technology: Applying AI to innovate financial services.The strategy envisions Luxembourg as a "living laboratory," where AI applications are tested and scaled in real-world settings, benefiting societal development. The country's small size is seen as an advantage, allowing for rapid implementation and international visibility as a frontrunner in AI deployment.
To support this vision, Luxembourg focuses on:
AI Research and Innovation: Fostering cutting-edge AI research and facilitating innovation.Data Infrastructure: Building and managing large data lakes to support AI applications.Ethical and Legal Frameworks: Developing regulations that ensure responsible AI use.

items.title: National Health Strategy 2030
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Priority 4, "Electronic Healthcare," aims to create a digital transformation strategy for the healthcare sector, focusing on building a unified digital platform for improved diagnostics and treatment of key diseases. It will enhance communication among stakeholders while addressing concerns such as data privacy, cybersecurity, and workforce capacity.

Priority 4, called “Electronic Healthcare,” aims to improve how health care uses digital technology to better diagnose and treat major diseases. Right now, health systems often struggle to share important medical information quickly and safely, which can slow down care and create risks for patient privacy.
The initiative’s main goal is to create one digital platform that connects doctors, hospitals, labs, and patients, making communication smoother and health data easier to access and use. It also focuses on protecting sensitive data and ensuring health workers have the skills to use these new tools effectively.
This platform will allow different health care providers to share information securely, helping doctors make faster, more accurate decisions. It involves health authorities, medical professionals, IT experts, and patients working together. The plan is to start with key diseases and regions, then gradually expand the system and train more staff.
Over time, this digital health network will grow to cover more services and improve care quality, making the healthcare system stronger and more responsive to patient needs.

items.title: National Data Strategy
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Portugal’s National Data Strategy aims to create a collaborative data ecosystem that promotes data altruism and drives innovation. It focuses on ethical data management, stakeholder collaboration, and continuous monitoring of data initiatives to assess their societal and economic impact.

The National Data Strategy is a key component of Portugal’s digital transformation agenda. It envisions a governance model designed to foster a collaborative and dynamic ecosystem that promotes data altruism and creates synergies among stakeholders. The strategy focuses on three main pillars:
Ethical and efficient data management: Establishing robust guidelines for the ethical and efficient management of data, ensuring reliability and security throughout its lifecycle.Stakeholder collaboration: Fostering effective collaboration between stakeholders to facilitate data and resource sharing in ways that drive innovation and value creation.Continuous monitoring and impact assessment: Implementing continuous monitoring of data initiatives, using models to assess the impact of these actions on society and the economy.The strategy aims to create a data-driven economy, enhancing public sector efficiency, fostering innovation, and improving citizens' quality of life. By promoting data altruism, it encourages the sharing of data for public good, ensuring that data is used responsibly and ethically.

items.title: National Data Strategy
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Germany’s National Data Strategy sets out a comprehensive plan to maximize the potential of data across public, private, and research sectors. It promotes responsible, effective, and sustainable data use while ensuring alignment with EU and national laws. The strategy strengthens data availability, quality, and accessibility to foster a culture of data-driven decision-making throughout society.

The National Data Strategy represents Germany’s overarching framework for building a data-driven economy and society. It aims to unlock the full potential of data in public administration, research, industry, and civil society while upholding the principles of transparency, privacy, and security.
The strategy is guided by three main objectives:
Expand data availability by creating new datasets and improving access to government data.Enhance data quality through standardized descriptions, quality assurance mechanisms, and interoperability.Foster a data culture that encourages evidence-based policy, research, and business innovation.Implementation is supported by several concrete measures:
Development of the National Research Data Infrastructure (NFDI) to enable better data sharing across scientific disciplines.Establishment of interconnected data laboratories and appointment of Chief Data Officers and Open Data Coordinators within each Federal Ministry to promote innovation and coordination.A detailed implementation roadmap running through Q4 2024, ensuring alignment with EU legislation and federal data regulations.

items.title: National Data Governance Strategy
items.org: Ministry of Smart Administration and Regional Development
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Latvia is in the process of developing its first National Data Governance Strategy, aiming to establish a comprehensive framework for data management across the public and private sectors. The strategy will address key aspects such as technical, semantic, legal, and organizational interoperability to enhance data sharing and utilization. Approval of the strategy is anticipated by the end of 2025.

Latvia's National Data Governance Strategy is being crafted to create a unified approach to data management and governance. The strategy seeks to:
Establish a coherent framework: Develop a national policy that aligns data governance practices across various sectors.Enhance interoperability: Address technical, semantic, legal, and organizational challenges to facilitate seamless data sharing and integration.Promote data-driven innovation: Encourage the use of data to drive innovation in public services, business, and research.Ensure data privacy and security: Implement measures to protect personal data and uphold citizens' rights.The strategy is expected to be approved by the end of 2025, with implementation to follow in subsequent years.

items.title: National Action Plan on the Digital Decade for Romania
items.original_name: Planul Național de Acțiune pentru Decada Digitală a României
items.org: Ministry of Research, Innovation and Digitalisation (MCID)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Planul Național de Acțiune pentru Decada Digitală a României
items.body:
Romania's National Action Plan on the Digital Decade for Romania (2024–2030) aims to enhance the country's digital infrastructure and services. A key objective is to increase the number of edge nodes from 11 in 2024 to 113 by 2030, aligning with the EU's target of 10,000 climate-neutral, highly secure edge nodes. This expansion is part of Romania's broader strategy to improve digital connectivity and services nationwide.

Romania's National Action Plan on the Digital Decade for Romania (2024–2030), officially approved in October 2024, outlines the country's commitment to achieving the EU's Digital Decade targets. The plan focuses on four main areas: digital public services, digital skills, digital transformation of businesses, and secure and sustainable digital infrastructures.
Key Objectives:
Edge Nodes Expansion: Increase the number of edge nodes from 11 in 2024 to 113 by 2030, supporting high-performance connectivity and data processing closer to end-users.Digital Infrastructure Development: Enhance the availability and quality of digital infrastructure, including high-speed internet and cloud services, to support digital transformation across sectors.Digital Skills Enhancement: Improve digital literacy and skills among the population to ensure broad participation in the digital economy.Digitalisation of Public Services: Expand and improve digital public services to increase efficiency and accessibility for citizens.

items.title: Italian Strategy on Data
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Italian Strategy on Data aims to improve how Italy manages and uses public data. It seeks to enhance information assets and make public services more efficient. The ultimate goal is to benefit citizens through better data management and accessibility.

The Italian Strategy on Data (Cloud Strategy) is a national initiative focused on enhancing the country’s information assets and improving public data management. It provides a framework for organising, sharing, and using data across government agencies and public institutions. By doing so, it aims to make public services more efficient, transparent, and citizen-focused.
Key objectives of the strategy include:
Optimising the use of public data to improve decision-making and service deliveryPromoting interoperability between government systems and databasesIncreasing transparency and accessibility of public information for citizens and businesses

items.title: Greek participation in the Chips Joint Undertaking
items.org: GSRI (General Secretariat for Research and Innovation)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Greece participates in the Chips JU through the call for applications “Key Digital Technologies Joint Undertaking".

Greece is participating in the Chips Joint Undertaking (Chips JU), a European programme that supports the development of semiconductor technologies—essential components in electronics like computers, cars, and medical devices. The aim is to reduce Europe’s reliance on imported chips and build stronger local capabilities in research, design, and production.
Through the Key Digital Technologies call, Greece has committed €6 million to support Greek organisations—such as universities, research centres, and companies—that want to take part in EU-funded projects. These projects cover everything from early research to testing and innovation in chip-related technologies. Applications are reviewed both by the EU and Greece’s national funding agency, GSRI.
To boost its role in this sector, Greece has also launched the Hellenic Chips Competence Centre (HCCC). This new hub will provide training, technical support, and access to tools for designing and testing chips. It’s part of a larger EU effort to grow a skilled workforce and support innovation across Europe’s chip industry.

items.title: Greek National Data Strategy
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Greek National Data Strategy (2020–2025) is part of Greece’s Digital Transformation Bible and aims to create a balanced, privacy-respecting data ecosystem. It promotes open government, data-driven innovation, and compliance with EU standards. The strategy supports productivity, research, business growth, and better public services.

The Greek National Data Strategy (2020–2025) forms a central pillar of Greece’s Digital Transformation Bible, setting the vision for how data should be governed, shared, and used responsibly. The strategy seeks to build a balanced data ecosystem that both respects individual privacy and unlocks the value of data for innovation, research, and public benefit.
Its main objectives are to:
Boost productivity and trade through effective use of dataSupport new businesses and job creation, especially in data-driven sectorsIncrease the speed, efficiency, and scope of scientific researchEnhance policy-making and public service delivery through data insightsPromote fairness and inclusion, ensuring that data benefits all citizensImplementation of the strategy involves aligning national data governance frameworks with EU obligations and international best practices, ensuring interoperability, transparency, and trust in the use of data. The strategy also encourages open government and cross-sector collaboration to drive digital transformation across society.

items.title: Digital Academy for Citizens
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Digital Academy for Citizens offers free online courses to improve people’s digital literacy and skills. By strengthening citizens’ digital competencies, it also supports SMEs in their digital transformation.

The Digital Academy for Citizens is a national initiative designed to make digital learning accessible to everyone. It provides free online courses aimed at improving digital literacy and competencies among citizens of all ages and backgrounds. By raising the general level of digital skills, the programme also helps small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) benefit from a more digitally capable workforce and customer base.
The initiative’s objectives include:
Expanding access to digital education and training nationwideEnabling citizens to participate fully in the digital economy and societySupporting SMEs’ digital transformation by improving the digital skills of employees and customers

items.title: SFI Discover Programme
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The SFI Discover Programme in Ireland funds projects that increase participation in STEM, develop key skills, and raise awareness of diverse STEM careers. In 2023, 40 projects were supported, including the STEM Passport for Inclusion and OurKidsCode.

The SFI Discover Programme is an annual funding initiative designed to broaden participation in STEM education and enhance science, technology, engineering, and mathematics skills across Ireland. It provides support to projects that engage learners, educators, and communities in hands-on, inclusive STEM activities.
Key objectives of the programme include:
Increasing participation in STEM education, particularly among underrepresented groupsSupporting skills development relevant to future careers in STEMRaising awareness of the wide range of STEM career pathways availableIn 2023, the programme funded 40 diverse projects, including initiatives such as:
STEM Passport for Inclusion – promoting access to STEM learning for all studentsOurKidsCode – engaging young people in coding and digital skills developmentThe programme is expected to continue evolving, funding new projects each year that encourage innovation, inclusivity, and STEM literacy, and further strengthen Ireland’s STEM talent pipeline.

items.title: Research Ireland Centres for Research Training (CRT)
items.org: Irish Research Centres for Research Training (CRT)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Research Centres for Research Training (CRT) in Ireland provide postgraduate training in AI, data science, and related technologies. Students gain skills in areas such as machine learning, genomics, and digitally enhanced reality. The programme supports AI research and applications across sectors like smart buildings, transportation, manufacturing, and climate change.

The Research Centres for Research Training (CRT) were established to provide high-quality postgraduate training in emerging technology fields, including Artificial Intelligence (AI), data science, and digitally enhanced reality. The centres offer structured programmes that equip PhD students with both theoretical knowledge and practical skills for research and innovation.
Key objectives include:
Training postgraduate students in cutting-edge AI and data science methodsSupporting the development of AI solutions in multiple sectors, such as:Smart buildings, mobility, and transportationAutonomous vehicles and manufacturingCybersecurity and climate changeAgriculture and natural resourcesStrengthening Ireland’s research capacity and innovation ecosystemFor example, the CRT for AI has trained 78 PhD students so far, with a focus on developing AI solutions that address real-world challenges. The programme encourages collaboration between academia and industry, ensuring that research is applied and transferable to practical applications.

items.title: Research Ireland Centres
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Research Ireland Centres conduct AI-related research across multiple institutions. Key centres include Insight, Lero, CONNECT, ADAPT, and I-Form. These centres support innovation, technology development, and collaboration between academia and industry in Ireland.

Research Ireland Centres are a network of research institutions focused on advancing AI and related technologies. They play a key role in driving innovation, knowledge creation, and technology transfer across academic and industrial sectors in Ireland.
The initiative aims to:
Conduct cutting-edge AI research in areas such as data analytics, machine learning, and digital technologiesFoster collaboration between universities, research institutes, and industry partnersSupport the development of new technologies and applications that can benefit Irish businesses and societySome of the main centres include:
Insight: Specialises in data analytics and AI for business and societal applicationsLero: Focuses on software engineering and AI-enabled systemsCONNECT: Develops AI and communications technologiesADAPT: Works on AI, natural language processing, and digital mediaI-Form: Concentrates on materials research with AI applications

items.title: Public Administration Pillar in the Italian Strategy for AI (2024-2026)
items.original_name: Pilastro della Pubblica Amministrazione nella Strategia Italiana per l’Intelligenza Artificiale (2024–2026)
