items.category: National – Strategy
items.document_name: Pilastro della Pubblica Amministrazione nella Strategia Italiana per l’Intelligenza Artificiale (2024–2026)
items.body:
The Public Administration Pillar of Italy’s National Strategy for AI (2024–2026) focuses on using AI to modernise public services. It aims to make administrative processes more efficient and improve the accessibility and quality of services for citizens and businesses. The strategy also promotes AI training and education for public sector employees.

The Public Administration Pillar represents one of the core components of Italy’s National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence (2024–2026). Developed under the guidance of the Agency for Digital Italy (Agenzia per l’Italia Digitale – AgID), this strategic pillar seeks to transform public sector operations through the responsible and effective adoption of AI.
The initiative’s main objectives include:
Promoting AI adoption in public administration through comprehensive national guidelinesEstablishing clear procurement protocols to ensure transparent and ethical AI deploymentDeveloping frameworks for the design and implementation of AI applications in government processesIntegrating AI education and training into professional development programmes for public officialsThrough these measures, the strategy aims to simplify AI-enabled services for both citizens and businesses, while streamlining administrative workflows and reducing bureaucratic barriers.

items.title: Participation in the LUMI-Q project
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Finland is participating in the LUMI-Q project under the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking to develop a quantum computer located in the Czech Republic. The project is linked to the LUMI supercomputer network. Procurement for Finland’s participation was launched in 2024.

The LUMI-Q project is a European initiative aimed at advancing quantum computing infrastructure. Finland’s participation contributes to the development of a quantum computer hosted in the Czech Republic and connected to the LUMI high-performance computing network, one of the largest supercomputers in Europe.
Key objectives of Finland’s participation include:
Supporting research and innovation in quantum computingIntegrating Finland into European quantum computing networksEnabling Finnish researchers and companies to access cutting-edge quantum computing resourcesThe project started procurement in 2024, marking the beginning of Finland’s active involvement in this cross-border collaboration. Over time, participation is expected to allow Finnish stakeholders to conduct experiments, develop applications, and build expertise in quantum computing, contributing to both academic research and industry innovation.

items.title: National Roadmap for Research Infrastructure (2021-2027)
items.original_name: Национална пътна карта за изследователска инфраструктура на България (2021–2027)
items.org: Bulgarian Ministry of Education and Science
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Национална пътна карта за изследователска инфраструктура на България (2021–2027)
items.body:
The National Roadmap for Research Infrastructure (2021–2027) is a strategic initiative to strengthen Bulgaria’s research capabilities. It supports the development of 51 research infrastructures, including the Avitohol supercomputer and INSAIT, to boost AI and high-performance computing (HPC) capacities. The initiative aligns with EU research frameworks to enhance innovation and competitiveness.

The National Roadmap for Research Infrastructure (2021–2027) aims to modernise and expand Bulgaria’s research ecosystem. By prioritising the development of 51 key research infrastructures, the initiative strengthens the country’s capacity in science, technology, and innovation, with a particular focus on AI and high-performance computing (HPC).
Key objectives of the roadmap include:
Supporting the construction and upgrading of research facilities, including laboratories, supercomputers, and data centresAligning Bulgaria’s research infrastructure with European Union frameworks and standardsEnhancing the country’s competitiveness in AI, HPC, and related advanced technologiesFacilitating collaboration among universities, research centres, and industryHighlighted projects include:
Avitohol supercomputer, one of the most powerful computing systems in the regionINSAIT, the Institute for Advanced Studies in Artificial Intelligence, promoting AI research and innovation

items.title: Guidance on the use of AI by the public sector
items.org: Department of Public Expenditure, NDP Delivery and Reform
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
Ireland has developed Interim Guidelines for the Use of AI in the Public Service to promote responsible and transparent use of AI technologies. These guidelines support ethical, secure, and trustworthy AI adoption across public sector organisations. Additional guidance on AI-related cybersecurity risks has also been published to help safeguard government systems.

The Guidance on the Use of AI by the Public Sector in Ireland provides a framework to ensure that AI technologies are used responsibly and effectively within government operations. Published by the Department of Public Expenditure, NDP Delivery and Reform (DPENDR) in 2024, the Interim Guidelines for the Use of AI in the Public Service establish principles and best practices for deploying AI tools in a transparent, fair, and accountable manner.
Key objectives of the initiative include:
Promoting ethical and human-centred AI use in public administrationEnsuring transparency, accountability, and fairness in AI-supported decision-makingProviding practical guidance for public bodies experimenting with or implementing AI systemsSupporting capacity-building and awareness across the civil serviceComplementing this effort, the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) has issued guidance on cybersecurity risks associated with generative AI. This document aims to:
Raise awareness of potential vulnerabilities in AI useSupport public bodies in managing data security and privacy risksEncourage safe experimentation with AI tools while maintaining system integrityFurther Guidelines on the Responsible Use of AI in the Public Sector are scheduled for publication in 2025, building upon the interim framework and integrating lessons learned from early AI use cases across government.

items.title: Flemish participation in EuroHPC infrastructure projects
items.org: Flanders Department of Economy and Innovation
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Flanders participates in the EuroHPC LUMI supercomputing consortium to provide researchers with access to world-class Tier 0 supercomputing. This enables advanced AI, data science, and simulation-based research. Participation also allows Belgium to benefit from expertise sharing and cost-efficient access to Europe’s most powerful supercomputers.

Flemish participation in the EuroHPC LUMI pre-exascale supercomputing consortium (2020–2026) gives researchers access to high-performance computing resources at the forefront of European infrastructure. By joining this large-scale international initiative, Flemish institutions can conduct cutting-edge AI, data science, and simulation-based research that would otherwise be difficult or impossible to achieve locally.
Key objectives and benefits include:
Access to Tier 0 supercomputing infrastructure, supporting complex computations and large-scale simulationsKnowledge sharing and collaboration with international experts in high-performance computing (HPC)Cost-efficient utilisation of Europe’s most powerful supercomputersEnsuring high performance and affordability for Flemish researchers and institutionsThe strategic location and scale of the LUMI infrastructure are designed to maximise performance while keeping access efficient and sustainable. This participation also strengthens Belgium’s position in European HPC research and supports innovation in AI, scientific computing, and related fields.

items.title: Flemish AI Academy
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Flemish AI Academy (VAIA) provides education and training in AI for researchers, professionals, and entrepreneurs. It coordinates AI learning opportunities across Flemish universities and research institutions. VAIA also identifies gaps in AI training and develops new courses to address them.

The Flemish AI Academy (VAIA) was established in 2020 to strengthen AI education and training in Flanders, Belgium. Its main goal is to ensure that researchers, professionals, and entrepreneurs have access to high-quality AI learning opportunities.
Key objectives of VAIA include:
Coordinating AI education across Flemish universities and research institutionsMapping existing AI courses and identifying gaps in trainingDeveloping new AI learning offerings to meet the needs of the workforce and research communityVAIA acts as a central hub for AI education, promoting collaboration between academia and industry. By improving access to AI knowledge and training, the initiative contributes to skills development, innovation, and the competitiveness of the Flemish economy.

items.title: Flanders AI Research Programme
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Flanders AI Research Programme (FAIR) funds AI research to support both industry innovation and societal progress. It promotes collaborative projects in advanced technologies, sustainable practices, and interdisciplinary research. The programme helps strengthen Flanders’ AI capabilities in both academia and industry.

The Flanders AI Research Programme (FAIR) was launched in 2019 to drive foundational and applied AI research across Flanders. It aims to position the region as a leader in AI innovation by supporting projects that combine academic excellence with practical applications in industry.
Key objectives include:
Promoting collaboration between universities, research centres, and industryAdvancing cutting-edge AI technologies and their applicationsSupporting sustainable practices and interdisciplinary research that address societal challengesFAIR implements its goals through:
Collaborative research projects across different sectorsFunding initiatives that encourage knowledge transfer and innovationStrengthening the AI research ecosystem in Flanders

items.title: Centre for Artificial Intelligence in Public Health Research" (ZKI-PH)
items.original_name: Zentrum für Künstliche Intelligenz in der Forschung im Bereich Öffentliche Gesundheit (ZKI-PH)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Zentrum für Künstliche Intelligenz in der Forschung im Bereich Öffentliche Gesundheit (ZKI-PH)
items.body:
The Centre for Artificial Intelligence in Public Health Research (ZKI-PH) at Germany’s Robert Koch Institute supports the use of AI and advanced data methods in public health research. It combines bioinformatics, computational epidemiology, and big data analysis with AI to improve health research outcomes. The centre develops realistic simulations and decision-making tools to address public health challenges.

The ZKI-PH initiative is dedicated to advancing public health research through AI-based technologies. Located within the Robert Koch Institute, it integrates multiple disciplines including:
Bioinformatics and computational epidemiologyModern data visualisation and systems analysisBig data and machine learning applicationsThe centre focuses on combining these disciplines with core methodological approaches such as AI, machine learning, decision-making research, and the development of realistic computer simulations. Its work supports evidence-based strategies for public health and improves understanding of complex health data.

items.title: AI demonstrators: DIAC and DIAT
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
France’s AI Demonstrators initiatives (DIAC and DIAT) support the development and testing of trusted and applied AI technologies. They fund projects that demonstrate AI in real-world settings across healthcare, mobility, industry, energy, and critical infrastructure. The programmes aim to strengthen the position of French AI companies and accelerate the adoption of AI in society and the economy.

In March 2023, the French government announced the extension of two existing AI demonstration schemes and the launch of a new one focused on trusted AI, as part of the France 2030 national strategy. These initiatives aim to support the technological maturation and demonstration of AI in practical, real-world contexts.
Key initiatives include:
Trusted Artificial Intelligence Demonstrators (DIAC):Supports development of hardware, software, and system innovations to ensure AI is safe, secure, robust, explainable, and ethicalProjects focus on demonstrating a functional need, strengthening market position or opening new marketsCovers sectors such as medical devices, mobility, Industry 4.0, energy, and critical infrastructureArtificial Intelligence Demonstrators in the Territories (DIAT):Launched April 2023 as a second wave of fundingSupports territory-specific AI and data science demonstratorsProjects must use energy- or data-efficient AI and demonstrate results in real-world environmentsTechnological Maturation and Demonstration of Embedded AI:Supports AI functionalities implemented close to sensors in embedded systemsApplications include IIoT, consumer IoT, medical devices, energy networks, urban infrastructure, telecommunications, and agricultureAlso funds advanced hardware architectures, especially for AI-dedicated semiconductors

items.title: AI Usage in the Flemish Public Employment Service (VDAB)
items.original_name: Gebruik van AI bij de Vlaamse Dienst voor Arbeidsbemiddeling en Beroepsopleiding (VDAB)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Gebruik van AI bij de Vlaamse Dienst voor Arbeidsbemiddeling en Beroepsopleiding (VDAB)
items.body:
The Adoption and Exploitation of AI in Agriculture programme supports the use of AI-driven automation in agriculture and industry. It funds R&D projects, including EU-supported initiatives, to promote digitalisation in agriculture and food sectors. The initiative aims to increase efficiency and innovation in farming and agri-food operations.

The Adoption and Exploitation of AI in Agriculture programme is designed to accelerate AI and automation uptake in the agricultural and industrial sectors. It focuses on providing practical support for AI applications, such as robotics and smart farming technologies, to improve productivity and sustainability.
Key objectives include:
Stimulating development and application of AI-driven automation solutions in agriculture and industrySupporting R&D projects, including those funded under Horizon Europe, to advance digitalisation in agriculture and food systemsPromoting innovation and competitiveness in the agri-food sectorThe programme encourages collaboration between research institutions, companies, and technology providers to ensure AI solutions meet real-world needs. By combining public and EU funding, it enables projects that might otherwise be too risky or resource-intensive for individual organisations.

items.title: myEESZT
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
EgészségAblak (myEESZT) is Hungary’s national mobile health app, launched in Q2 2024 as part of the Recovery and Resilience Plan. Managed by the Ministry of the Interior, it offers secure access to personal health records, prescriptions, appointments, and vaccination data. By mid-2025, it surpassed 170,000 active users. The app aims to enhance patient engagement and healthcare efficiency, with full rollout expected by June 2026.

EgészségAblak (myEESZT) is Hungary’s national mobile front end to the EESZT e-health infrastructure. Beyond viewing prescriptions and records, the app provides access—after electronic identification and TAJ verification—to EESZT-stored medical documents (e.g., lab results, discharge summaries), vaccination credentials, appointment details (Calendar/“Időpontok”), and COVID certificates. Users can also check social insurance status, and manage proxy access so a parent/guardian or authorised person can view a dependent’s records where legal representation is registered.

items.title: fTEHDAS2 - Second Joint Action Towards the European Health Data Space
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This project aims to develop 20 guidelines and technical specifications to support the implementation of the European Health Data Space (EHDS2) regulation. It focuses on standardising metadata through the adoption of health DCAT-AP, harmonising de-identification procedures, and ensuring interoperability for seamless data sharing among health data access bodies, data holders, and users within the HealthData@EU ecosystem.

The TEHDAS (Towards the European Health Data Space) joint action supports the rollout of the European Health Data Space (EHDS2) by developing 20 guidelines and technical specifications. Its work covers standardising metadata through the adoption of health DCAT-AP, harmonising de-identification methods, and enabling interoperability between health data access bodies, data holders, and users. The project underpins the HealthData@EU ecosystem, aiming to ensure that secondary use of health data is secure, consistent, and usable across borders.

items.title: VELES - The Smart Excellence Hub for Southeastern Europe - Regional Smart Data Space
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Established in South-East Europe, spanning 4 widening countries: Bulgaria, Greece, Romania, and Cyprus. Supported by Sweden, Spain, and Germany. The primary aim is to establish a robust regional data space in healthcare as an initial step to creating a comprehensive EU data health space.

The RIS3 strategies of Bulgaria, Romania, Greece, and Cyprus, defined as Widening countries, underscore the urgency of digitalizing society and enhancing crucial services offered by public and private stakeholders. The healthcare sector takes center stage, highlighting the need for advancement.
Tailored innovation and joint strategies are vital, as in the EU, various policy initiatives prioritize innovation’s role in societal and economic progress. Amid political transformations, innovation, especially at the local level, plays a pivotal role in strengthening continental integration. A coordinated cross-country approach is essential to align the efforts of participating Widening countries.
Furthermore, one of European Commission’s priorities is to establish a European Health Data Space by 2025, facilitating the exchange and access to diverse health data. This initiative aims to address the challenge EU citizens face when seeking healthcare abroad due to a lack of health data interoperability.
On June 1st, 2023, under the HORIZON-WIDERA-2022-ACCESS-04 (Excellence Hubs) initiative, VELES Excellence Hub was kicked off. Our mission is to elevate innovation excellence in South-East Europe by establishing a sustainable place-based innovation ecosystem, powered by the Regional Smart Health Data Space.
VELES merges the RIS3 healthcare priority with the Smart Health Strategic EU Value Chain, driving systematic impact and continual enhancement of smart specialization paths across multiple countries.
With a dedicated focus on the Widening countries of Bulgaria, Greece, Romania, and Cyprus, VELES aspires to solidify the region’s standing as a thriving center for groundbreaking healthcare innovations. We are proud to have the support of three developed countries: Sweden, Spain, and Germany. VELES comprises a consortium of 15 partners, representing all seven countries.

items.title: Upgrading of the National Network of Infrastructures for Research and Technology (GRNET)
items.original_name: Αναβάθμιση λογισμικού και υπηρεσίας υπολογιστικού νέφους στα μέλη της ερευνητικής και ακαδημαϊκής κοινότητας
items.org: GRNET (National Infrastructures for Research and Technology)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Αναβάθμιση λογισμικού και υπηρεσίας υπολογιστικού νέφους στα μέλη της ερευνητικής και ακαδημαϊκής κοινότητας
items.body:
The aim of the project is to expand GRNET's existing cloud computing infrastructure in order to offer advanced services to its users, members of the research and academic community of the country.

This project aims to expand GRNET’s cloud computing infrastructure to better support the country’s research and academic community. As researchers and educators need more powerful and flexible computing tools, the existing system needs to grow to meet these increasing demands.
The goal is to improve the cloud platform by adding more capacity and advanced services tailored to scientific and academic work. This will allow users to access resources like high-performance computing and data storage through a centralized system.
GRNET leads the project, working closely with universities and research centers to upgrade hardware and software, ensuring the platform is secure and easy to use. Training and support will help users benefit from the new capabilities.

items.title: To Be Seen and To Be Heard
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Societal Impact of Pain (SIP) Malta Platform launched the ‘To Be Seen and To Be Heard Patient Empowerment project. This initiative, supported by the Malta Health Network, aims to empower patients by promoting self-management, enhancing patient-professional communication, and ensuring that patients are actively involved in their healthcare decisions.

The To Be Seen and To Be Heard patient empowerment project promotes patient self-management, strengthens communication between patients and healthcare providers, and seeks to ensure that individuals play a central role in shaping their own care.

items.title: Swestore
items.org: National Academic Infra-structure for Supercomputing Sweden (NAISS)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Swestore is a Research Data Storage infrastructure intended for active research data, operated by the National Academic Infra-structure for Supercomputing Sweden (NAISS).

Swestore is a national research data storage infrastructure operated by the National Academic Infrastructure for Supercomputing Sweden (NAISS). The service addresses the need for reliable, high-performance storage for active research data, enabling Swedish researchers to efficiently store, access, and manage large datasets used in ongoing scientific projects. 
The primary objective of Swestore is to provide a secure, scalable, and high-capacity storage environment for active datasets across disciplines, ranging from bioinformatics and climate modeling to AI research and physics simulations. By offering robust storage capabilities, the infrastructure supports researchers in handling data-intensive workflows while maintaining data integrity and accessibility.
Swestore is integrated with NAISS’s broader high-performance computing (HPC) and network services, providing seamless access for computational tasks and enabling researchers to work collaboratively across institutions. The infrastructure supports features such as version control, backup, and controlled access, ensuring that sensitive and critical data remain secure while facilitating efficient data sharing among project partners.

items.title: Swedish participation in the Chips Joint Undertaking
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Vinnova supports Swedish projects in the Chips JU.

Sweden participates in the European Chips Joint Undertaking (Chips JU), a key European initiative aimed at strengthening semiconductor research, development, and production. The initiative addresses the strategic need for Europe to secure a competitive position in the global semiconductor market, which is critical for digital technologies, AI hardware, and advanced computing applications.
Vinnova, Sweden’s innovation agency, supports Swedish research and industrial projects participating in the Chips JU. The primary objective is to enable Swedish actors—universities, research institutes, and companies—to contribute to joint European efforts in microelectronics, semiconductors, and chip technologies, while benefiting from access to cutting-edge research, funding, and collaborative networks.
Projects supported by Vinnova focus on R&D activities that drive innovation in semiconductor materials, chip design, manufacturing processes, and applications for AI, computing, and industrial technologies. Swedish teams work in collaboration with European partners, combining expertise and infrastructure to accelerate development and ensure that European semiconductor capabilities remain competitive.

items.title: Swedish participation in LUMI hosted by CSC in Finland
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
LUMI is the fastest supercomputer in Europe and part of the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking.

Sweden participates in the LUMI supercomputing infrastructure, hosted by CSC in Finland, to provide researchers with access to one of Europe’s most powerful high-performance computing (HPC) systems. LUMI, the fastest supercomputer in Europe, is part of the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking, which aims to strengthen European HPC capabilities and advance research and innovation across the continent. 
The initiative addresses the growing demand for computational resources for data-intensive scientific research, including artificial intelligence, climate modeling, genomics, and materials science. By leveraging LUMI, Swedish researchers gain access to cutting-edge computational power, enabling complex simulations, AI model training, and advanced analytics that would not be feasible on national infrastructure alone.
Sweden’s participation is coordinated through the National Academic Infrastructure for Supercomputing Sweden (NAISS), which facilitates access for universities, research institutes, and other partners. Researchers can submit proposals to use LUMI for collaborative projects, ensuring that the system supports a wide range of scientific and technological applications.

items.title: Supporting the digital transformation of healthcare (COFOG code: 07.4) – Recovery and Resilience Fund Plan
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The initiative aims to enhance healthcare by using ICT to improve prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and monitoring, while increasing efficiency, accessibility, and quality, ensuring sustainability, securing health data, reducing administrative burdens, and fostering digital skills through coordinated implementation across healthcare institutions.

Hungary’s Recovery and Resilience Plan includes a health-sector digitalization component that seeks to modernize prevention, diagnosis, treatment and follow-up through ICT. The measures are framed to improve efficiency and access while strengthening data security, reducing administrative load, and building digital skills across institutions. Planned actions include upgrading core e-health infrastructure, expanding interoperable services for clinicians and patients, and coordinating implementation so that hospitals and primary care adopt common standards and tools. The intent is to create a more connected system where health data can be used safely for care, management, and quality improvement.

items.title: Sunet Drive – collaborative data space for research data
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Sunet Drive is a storage and file sharing service, making it possible for researchers to be able to work and collaborate with large amounts of data.

Sunet Drive is a national storage and file-sharing service provided by Sunet, Sweden’s research and education network. The service addresses the growing need for secure, reliable, and high-capacity data storage for researchers, enabling them to work with large datasets and collaborate efficiently across institutions and geographic locations. 
The primary objective of Sunet Drive is to provide a user-friendly platform that supports both individual and collaborative research workflows. Researchers can upload, store, and share large datasets, ensuring data integrity and compliance with relevant security and privacy requirements. The service is designed to handle high volumes of data, which is critical for fields such as bioinformatics, environmental research, AI model training, and other data-intensive scientific activities.
Sunet Drive is integrated into Sunet’s broader digital infrastructure, which includes high-speed networking, identity management (EduID), and other cloud-based services. The service is accessible to universities, research institutes, and other partner organizations, providing a seamless environment for secure collaboration and data exchange. Users benefit from features such as access control, versioning, and synchronization across devices, facilitating both local and cross-institutional projects.

items.title: Senate Act No. 1146 – Law on Artificial Intelligence
items.org: Senate of the Republic of Italy
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
The AI Bill (Senate Act 1146/2024) is a national framework to implement EU AI Act 2024/1689. It enshrines principles—transparency, human oversight, data protection, non-discrimination—and delegates rulemaking to the government. It sets sectorial rules for healthcare, research, public administration and justice; establishes AgID and ACN as overseeing authorities; and introduces provisions on copyright, data localisation, cybersecurity, and research exemptions.

This project represents the country’s legislative response to the EU AI Act, setting out how European rules will be applied nationally. The framework provides the legal basis for tailoring implementation across different sectors, with oversight assigned to national agencies. It also introduces complementary measures in areas such as intellectual property, cybersecurity, and data governance, reflecting both compliance with EU standards and attention to domestic priorities in managing AI deployment.

items.title: SURF
items.org: SURF – Cooperative of Dutch Education & Research Institutions
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
SURF is a cooperative for Dutch education and research institutions, offering ICT services and solutions to improve digital infrastructure, research, and education. The organisation plays a key role in driving innovation in education and research through ICT, and its current strategy (2022-2027) focuses on enhancing service transparency, fostering ICT-related innovation, and testing new technologies in its Innovation Lab.

SURF is a national cooperative for digital services in Dutch education and research, bringing together universities, universities of applied sciences, research institutes, and vocational institutions. It provides shared ICT infrastructure, advanced networking, cloud services, and cybersecurity solutions to support collaboration and innovation. Through its 2022–2027 strategy, SURF also explores emerging technologies such as AI and quantum computing in its Innovation Lab, while promoting secure data exchange and digital sovereignty in line with European initiatives.

items.title: SMASH – Machine learning in climate
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The SMASH – Machine Learning in Climate Research project in Slovenia develops AI solutions to better understand and predict climate and atmospheric processes. Research areas include extreme weather events, aerosols, air pollution sources, and long-term climate prediction. The project runs from 2023 to 2028 and applies machine learning to support climate science and policy.

The SMASH – Machine Learning in Climate Research initiative is a major Slovenian project running from 2023 to 2028, focusing on the use of AI and machine learning to advance climate science. It forms part of the broader SMASH programme, which supports interdisciplinary research at the intersection of artificial intelligence and environmental challenges.
The initiative addresses several key research fields:
Extreme weather events – improving forecasting and risk analysisAerosols and their impact on climate – studying anthropogenic and natural aerosols and their mixturesAir pollution source identification – using machine learning to trace pollutantsLong-term atmospheric prediction – enhancing climate models with AI methodsThe project supports both scientific research and policy development, aiming to provide better tools for understanding environmental risks, mitigating climate change, and supporting sustainable decision-making.

items.title: Romanian National HPC Competence Center (RoNCC)
items.org: National Institute for Research & Development in Informatics - ICI Bucharest
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Romanian National HPC Competence Center (RoNCC) creates a network of skills in High Performance Computing (HPC) and functions as an interface to facilitate access to resources and capabilities in this field, both in Romania and in Europe, through the EuroCC network, as the national contact point for providing support in training activities, technical expertise, access to HPC resources, consulting services and coordination of HPC activities at national level.

Romania’s National HPC Competence Center (RoNCC) serves as the country’s one-stop interface to high-performance computing. It coordinates national HPC activities and, through the EuroCC network, connects researchers, public bodies, and SMEs to training, technical expertise, consultancy, and access to computing resources in Romania and across Europe. The centre’s role is to build skills, lower entry barriers for advanced computing, and channel users to appropriate infrastructure and support.

items.title: R&D Funds for Data Science and AI
items.original_name: Fundos de I&D para Ciência de Dados e IA
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Fundos de I&D para Ciência de Dados e IA
items.body:
The R&D Funds for Data Science and AI in Portugal provide national funding for research and development in AI and data science. The programme supports collaborative projects, including partnerships with companies like Google, to improve public administration efficiency and foster innovation in AI technologies.

The R&D Funds for Data Science and AI initiative, managed through the Foundation for Science and Technology (FCT), aims to stimulate research, innovation, and collaboration in AI and data science across Portugal. Key objectives include:
Supporting collaborative projects that integrate AI and data science into public administration, enhancing efficiency and service deliveryFunding joint initiatives with private partners, such as Google, to promote innovation and technology developmentEncouraging the adoption of AI technologies across sectors, strengthening Portugal’s research and innovation ecosystemThe funding is designed to bridge research and practical application, allowing both academic and industry partners to test, develop, and implement AI solutions in real-world contexts. By supporting collaboration between universities, research centres, and private companies, the programme aims to accelerate the adoption of AI technologies and strengthen national innovation capacity.

items.title: Programme for AI Literacy and Skills
items.org: Ministry for Digital and Economic Affairs
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Austria’s Programme for AI Literacy and Skills is being developed to improve AI knowledge and digital skills across the population. It focuses on groups with lower digital literacy, such as the elderly and rural residents, and promotes gender diversity in AI skills. The programme aims to broaden Austria’s pool of IT and AI experts.

The Programme for AI Literacy and Skills in Austria is a national initiative aimed at improving AI understanding and digital competence among citizens. The programme has officially kicked off in July 2024 with an expert event and is aligned with Austria’s broader national digital literacy and skills strategy and the national AI strategy.
Key objectives include:
Promoting AI literacy among population groups with lower digital skills, including the elderly and people in rural areasEnhancing gender diversity in AI and technology-related skillsBroadening the national pool of IT and AI experts to meet future labour market needsThe programme will adopt inclusive approaches and targeted educational measures to reach underrepresented groups and ensure equitable access to AI education. It also aims to strengthen Austria’s overall digital competence, supporting the country’s innovation and competitiveness in AI-related fields.

items.title: Polish Cloud Support Fund
items.original_name: Polski Fundusz Wsparcia Przetwarzania w Chmurze
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Polski Fundusz Wsparcia Przetwarzania w Chmurze
items.body:
This action aims to encourage private investments and improve access to financing for the digital transformation of Polish enterprises. Loan support may only be granted for digital transformation projects where at least 30% of the total eligible costs are related to cloud infrastructure and cloud computing services. The remaining costs are also directly related to the digital transformation of the business, e.g. increasing the use of other smart solutions.

This project is a loan-based instrument to support the digital transformation of enterprises, with a cloud-first orientation. Financing is available only for projects in which at least 30% of eligible costs concern cloud infrastructure or cloud services (e.g., migration, IaaS/PaaS/SaaS), while remaining costs must also directly advance the firm’s digitalisation (such as integrating smart solutions or related software/services). The scheme is framed to stimulate private investment, ease access to capital for technology upgrades, and align company IT with modern, scalable architectures.

items.title: Poland's Public Data Opening Programme, part of the Programme of Integrated Informatisation of the State (PZIP)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Poland’s Public Data Opening Programme (PZIP) is an initiative aimed at enhancing the accessibility and usability of public sector information. This programme is part of Poland's broader strategy to foster an open data culture, aligning with the EU's directives on open data and the reuse of public sector information.

Poland’s Public Data Opening Programme (PZIP), developed under the Integrated State Digitalisation Programme, seeks to improve the accessibility and reuse of public sector information. It focuses on standardising datasets, expanding access to high-value data, and encouraging innovation by making public information more usable for research, business, and civic purposes. The initiative also supports compliance with EU open data directives and promotes the development of digital services built on transparent and reliable information.

items.title: Pilot projects to enhance energy efficiency and the enhancement of the use of renewables in the economy
items.original_name: Pilotni projekti za izboljšanje energetske učinkovitosti in povečanje uporabe obnovljivih virov v gospodarstvu
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Pilotni projekti za izboljšanje energetske učinkovitosti in povečanje uporabe obnovljivih virov v gospodarstvu
items.body:
Slovenia has launched pilot projects to improve energy efficiency and increase the use of renewable energy in the economy. These projects use advanced digital technologies, including AI, to make business processes more sustainable. Key initiatives include a peer-to-peer renewables marketplace, emissions monitoring, and digital solutions for circular construction.

As part of its strategic plan for energy efficiency and renewable energy, Slovenia introduced three pilot projects in 2022 that integrate AI and advanced digital technologies to promote environmentally friendly and sustainable development. The initiatives are designed to test innovative approaches and demonstrate their potential for wider adoption.
Key measures include:
Peer-to-peer marketplace for renewables: enabling businesses and individuals to trade renewable energy efficientlyRMV (Recording, Measurement, and Verification of Emissions): improving the Emissions Trading System (ETS) through more accurate monitoringDigital solution for BIM (Building Information Modelling) - circular construction: supporting sustainable construction practices and resource efficiencyA green corporate e-identity tool was also proposed as a web service on the Energy Agency’s website, allowing companies to track and showcase their sustainability efforts digitally.

items.title: Pilot project “Implementation of a solution to reduce the number of Was Not Brought (WNB) and no-show patients in the hospital”
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This AI solution aims to optimise outpatient scheduling by predicting and reducing patient no-shows. The system will enable better appointment management for chronic patients and improve access to healthcare services. The project is part of Latvia’s national healthcare digitalisation efforts.

The Children’s Clinical University Hospital of Riga has introduced an AI-driven scheduling system designed to address inefficiencies in outpatient care. By analysing patient data to anticipate missed appointments, the tool seeks to improve planning for chronic care patients and reduce waiting times. The project forms part of Latvia’s wider healthcare digitalisation strategy, which links hospitals into European Reference Networks to enhance cross-border cooperation in specialised medicine.

items.title: New Energy
items.org: National Fund for Environmental Protection and Water Management
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The New Energy (Nowa Energia) programme in Poland supports entrepreneurs and local governments in adopting innovative energy technologies. It promotes solutions such as Smart Cities for Growth and Self-Sufficient Energy Clusters. The programme strengthens sustainable development in the energy sector and public services.

Launched in 2022, the New Energy (Nowa Energia) programme is a national initiative to drive innovation and sustainability in Poland’s energy sector. It provides financial and strategic support to both entrepreneurs and local government bodies, helping them test and implement modern energy solutions.
The programme has two main thematic areas:
Smart Cities for Growth – developing technologies that enhance urban sustainability and efficiency through smart energy systems.Self-Sufficient Energy Clusters – supporting local communities and municipalities in building decentralised, renewable-based energy systems to increase resilience and reduce reliance on external supply.Key objectives include:
Encouraging entrepreneurship and innovation in the energy sectorSupporting local governments and public service providers in sustainable transformationStrengthening energy self-sufficiency and resilience across regionsPromoting the development of green technologies aligned with EU sustainability goals

items.title: National Rescue Service
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The national ambulance service in Hungary is leveraging AI to enhance capacity allocation and logistics, utilising smart algorithms to analyse data from over 3,000 daily patient cases and 40 million kilometres of coverage annually, making predictive decisions and improving service efficiency.

Hungary’s National Ambulance Service has integrated AI-driven tools to improve logistics and resource management. By applying predictive algorithms to data from thousands of daily patient cases and extensive annual coverage, the system supports more efficient allocation of ambulances and staff. The initiative seeks to optimise emergency response times, reduce operational strain, and strengthen overall service reliability.

items.title: National Data Center of Excellence
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
A National Data Center of Excellence, which is to coordinate the activities of local centres providing secure and fast access to data, is currently under preparation.

Poland’s Ministry of Digital Affairs has outlined the beginnings of a National Data Centre of Excellence—a proposed coordination hub for a network of local centres that would provide secure, high-speed access to public data.

items.title: National Center for Data Processing
items.org: Ministry of Digital Affairs and the Digital Poland Project Centre
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This joint project between the Digital Poland Project Centre and the Ministry of Digital Affairs, carried out jointly with the Research and Academic Computer Network, the National Research Institute and the Central Information Technology Centre, aims at building modern processing centres ensuring the continuity and security of public administration resources.

The National Data Processing Centre (KCPD) is a joint initiative led by the Digital Poland Project Centre and the Ministry of Digital Affairs, in cooperation with NASK (Research and Academic Computer Network – National Research Institute) and the Central Information Technology Centre. The project focuses on building secure and modern processing facilities to guarantee the continuity and resilience of Poland’s public administration resources. It is part of a broader effort to modernise digital infrastructure, improve cybersecurity, and provide reliable support for the country’s expanding e-government services.

items.title: National Artificial Intelligence PhD Programme
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Italian National PhD Program in Artificial Intelligence is a joint initiative of 5 federated PhD courses that bring together 60+ universities and research institutions.

The 5 PhD courses share a common basis in the foundations and developments of AI, and each one has an area of specialisation in a strategic sector of AI applications. Each PhD course is organized by a lead university, in collaboration with the National Research Council (CNR).

The National PhD Program in in AI will train researchers, innovators and professionals, both with specialisations in the cutting-edge topics of Artificial Intelligence and in important application sectors, also ensuring an integrated and “complex” vision of the ecosystem of AI technologies and solutions, able to address problems with a systemic and multi-disciplinary approach.
PhD students in AI will participate in common training experiences and activities, both foundational and specialised, offered by the 5 PhD courses. The program covers costs for PhD student’s mobility at national and international level.

items.title: National Academic Infrastructure for Supercomputing Sweden (NAISS)
items.org: National Academic Infrastructure for Supercomputing Sweden (NAISS); Linköping University
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
NAISS, the National Academic Infrastructure for Supercomputing in Sweden, is providing researchers with high-performance computing (HPC) resources, storage capacity, and data services. Through a new supercomputer projected to be operational in 2025, NAISS will be a full member of the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking.

The National Academic Infrastructure for Supercomputing (NAISS) in Sweden provides researchers with high-performance computing (HPC) resources, advanced storage solutions, and data services to support data-intensive scientific work. NAISS addresses the growing demand for computational power and storage capacity needed for modern research, including AI, climate modeling, bioinformatics, and physics simulations. 
NAISS’s primary objectives are to deliver scalable and reliable HPC resources, facilitate secure and efficient data management, and enable collaborative research across Swedish universities and research institutions. The infrastructure supports both large-scale simulations and the processing of massive datasets, ensuring that researchers have the tools necessary to accelerate scientific discovery.
The organization operates a range of services, including computing clusters, storage systems such as Swestore, and support for data-intensive workflows. By integrating HPC resources with national research networks, NAISS allows seamless collaboration and access for researchers across disciplines and institutions.
NAISS plans to deploy a new supercomputer projected to be operational in 2025. This development will enable Sweden to become a full member of the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking, providing access to European HPC infrastructure and strengthening Sweden’s capacity for AI-driven research and high-performance scientific computing.

items.title: MyFab
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Swedish Research Council supports clean room facilities at Swedish universities through Myfab, the Swedish national research infrastructure for micro and nano fabrication.

MyFab is Sweden’s national research infrastructure for micro- and nano-fabrication, supported by the Swedish Research Council. The initiative addresses the need for advanced clean room facilities to enable research and development in areas such as microelectronics, nanotechnology, photonics, and material science. By providing access to state-of-the-art fabrication equipment, MyFab supports innovation across academic and industrial research projects. 
The primary objective of MyFab is to provide Swedish universities, research institutes, and industrial partners with access to clean room environments and specialized fabrication tools that would otherwise be difficult to maintain individually. Researchers can design, prototype, and test micro- and nanoscale devices, facilitating high-quality experimental work and accelerating scientific discoveries.
MyFab operates through a network of participating universities, including Chalmers University of Technology, KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Linköping University, and Lund University. These sites host clean rooms and equipment, while MyFab coordinates access, training, and standardization to ensure efficient use of resources and high-quality outcomes.

items.title: Master in Artificial Intelligence for Industry 4.0
items.org: Malta College of Arts, Science and Technology (MCAST)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Malta offers advanced Master’s programmes in Artificial Intelligence through MCAST and the University of Malta. These programmes equip students with AI skills for business, industry, and specialised research areas. Students gain practical experience and theoretical knowledge to solve real-world challenges and enhance competitiveness using AI.

Malta provides targeted Master-level education in Artificial Intelligence through two main programmes:
Master in Artificial Intelligence for Industry 4.0 at the Malta College of Arts, Science and Technology (MCAST)A 90-credit EQF Level 7 programme focusing on AI applications in business contextsEquips students with skills to solve business challenges and gain a competitive advantage through AI technologiesDesigned for those aiming to integrate AI into industrial and commercial practicesMaster of Science in Artificial Intelligence at the University of MaltaAvailable as a taught and research programme, primarily research-basedCovers AI fundamentals and allows specialisation in thematic areas such as:AstronomyBig DataComputer VisionFintechGeosciencesRoboticsStatisticsOffers potential industry internships, applied projects, or dissertation-integrated experienceDesigned for both working professionals and recent graduatesIn the 2024–2025 academic year, 89 students were enrolledObjectives of these programmes include:
Developing a comprehensive understanding of AI principlesProviding practical and applied skills for business and industryStrengthening Malta’s AI talent pipeline to support innovation and digital transformation

items.title: Law as Code
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body: The project aims to establish the foundations for technically implementing laws and legally binding documents using symbolic AI and logical programming paradigms. It also focuses on integrating these technologies into e-government, particularly within Austrian administrative processes and European interoperability initiatives.

items.title: Latvian population genome reference project
items.org: Latvian Biomedical Research and Study Centre
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Latvian portion of the project aims to create a reference genome using 3,500 samples from Latvian residents. This will contribute to a broader European initiative to build a reference genome database representing genetic variation across at least 500,000 citizens.

The Latvian Genome Database, managed by the Latvian Biomedical Research and Study Centre, collects and analyses biological material and health data to support genomics and precision medicine research. As part of a wider European effort, Latvia is sequencing thousands of local samples to contribute to a reference genome resource, which will enable more accurate research into genetic variation and disease predisposition. The initiative also supports international collaboration by ensuring compatibility with other biobanks and research infrastructures.

items.title: Latvian Digital health centre
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The management of digital development in the health sector will be transferred to the new Latvian Digital Health Centre in September 2024. The establishment of the Digital Competence Centre for the health sector, backed by government support, will propel the evolution of digital health.

The establishment of the Digital competence center for the health sector, backed by government support, will propel the evolution of digital health and guarantee the strategic management of the digital health ecosystem.

Currently, there are 19 state information systems and seven registers overseen by subordinate institutions of the Ministry of Health. Following these adjustments, one institution will gradually assume responsibility for the maintenance and coordinated development of information and communication (ICT) systems. The center is envisioned to be established as a state-owned enterprise, with 100% of its capital shares owned by the state, and the Ministry of Health acting as the shareholder. This institutional model is poised to streamline the integration of innovations into the industry.

items.title: International Patient Summary (IPS) and ePrescription/eDispensation services through MyHealth@EU
items.original_name: Resumo Internacional do Paciente (IPS) e serviços de ePrescrição/eDispensação através do MyHealth@EU
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Resumo Internacional do Paciente (IPS) e serviços de ePrescrição/eDispensação através do MyHealth@EU
items.body:
Portugal has developed International Patient Summary (IPS) and ePrescription/eDispensation services through MyHealth@EU. These services enable the secure sharing of health information across countries. They ensure that medical data is consistently understood and interoperable between different health systems.

The International Patient Summary (IPS) and ePrescription/eDispensation services aim to facilitate cross-border health information exchange. Built on Portugal’s Serviço Nacional de Saúde (SNS) portal, these services leverage existing digital infrastructure and interoperability standards to ensure reliable and secure data sharing.
Key objectives include:
Enhancing cross-border access to patients’ health informationEnsuring semantic interoperability using standards such as HL7 FHIR and SNOMED CTImproving continuity of care for patients traveling or receiving treatment abroadThe implementation relies on modern digital infrastructure that allows healthcare providers in different countries to access and interpret clinical data consistently. By aligning with EU-wide interoperability standards, these services support safe and effective care delivery across borders.

items.title: Institute of Public Administration (IPA) Initiatives
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Institute of Public Administration conducts conferences, forums, and trainings on AI technologies, including AI’s use in governance and HR management.

The Institute of Public Administration in Bulgaria organizes conferences, forums, and training programs focused on artificial intelligence technologies, with a particular emphasis on their applications in governance and human resource management. The initiative addresses the need to equip public sector professionals with knowledge and skills to effectively leverage AI in administrative and organizational processes.
The primary objective of the program is to increase awareness and competence in AI among government officials, managers, and public administrators. By providing targeted training and practical demonstrations, the initiative ensures that AI tools can be used responsibly and effectively to enhance decision-making, optimize workflows, and improve public services.
The program is implemented through a combination of workshops, seminars, and interactive sessions, bringing together experts, academics, and practitioners in the field of AI. Participants explore applications such as AI-assisted recruitment, performance evaluation, predictive analytics for resource allocation, and other use cases relevant to public administration.

items.title: IPCEI-CIS
items.org: Ministry of Digital Affairs and the National Centre for Research and Development
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Poland is participating in the IPCEI Next Generation Cloud Infrastructure and Services (CIS), with four projects, some of which include AI-specific components.

Poland is actively participating in the IPCEI Next Generation Cloud Infrastructure and Services (CIS) programme under its national recovery plan. Four projects have received funding—some of which explicitly incorporate AI modules, such as cloud-based AI model training or smart services applications. The initiative forms part of Poland’s strategy to enhance sovereign cloud capabilities and to support advanced digital transformations in business and government.

items.title: IPCEI Cloud Infrastructure and Services (CIS)
items.org: Netherlands Enterprise Agency - Ministry of Economics and Climate
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The IPCEI CIS initiative supports projects in cloud infrastructure, services, and software development through national subsidies. Its main goal is to enhance European cooperation in cloud technologies, encouraging innovation and the adoption of secure cloud infrastructures. The programme provides funding to Dutch businesses working on projects that align with the broader European cloud strategy, helping to build a robust and competitive digital economy.

The Important Project of Common European Interest on Cloud Infrastructure and Services (IPCEI CIS) is part of the EU’s strategy to strengthen technological sovereignty in cloud and data services. In the Netherlands, the programme is coordinated by RVO and channels subsidies to companies developing innovative and secure cloud solutions. The initiative emphasises cross-border collaboration, linking Dutch businesses with European partners to advance cloud infrastructure, software development, and data-sharing frameworks that support competitiveness and digital resilience.

items.title: IPA AI Training Programmes
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
A comprehensive training initiative offering civil servants' practical education in AI applications through multiple formats including self-learning e-modules, face-to-face training, and interactive workshops. The program focuses on practical applications of AI in public administration and HR management.

The Institute of Public Administration (IPA) in Bulgaria runs a comprehensive AI training initiative designed for civil servants. The program addresses the growing need for practical knowledge and skills in artificial intelligence applications within public administration and human resource management, helping to modernize governmental operations and decision-making.
The primary objective of the IPA AI Training Programmes is to equip public sector professionals with practical expertise in applying AI tools to real-world administrative tasks. The program emphasizes hands-on learning, enabling participants to understand, implement, and manage AI-based solutions that improve efficiency, enhance service delivery, and support data-driven decision-making.
The initiative is delivered through multiple learning formats, including self-paced e-learning modules, face-to-face training sessions, and interactive workshops. Participants explore AI use cases relevant to their work, such as automating routine administrative processes, enhancing HR management, and supporting policy analysis. The program combines theoretical foundations with practical exercises, fostering applied skills that can be directly utilized in government operations.

items.title: Hybrid Cloud
items.original_name: Παροχή Κεντρικών Νεφο-Υπολογιστικών Υποδομών και Υπηρεσιών
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Παροχή Κεντρικών Νεφο-Υπολογιστικών Υποδομών και Υπηρεσιών
items.body:
The aim of the project Hybrid Cloud (“Provision of Central Cloud Computing Infrastructures and Services”) is the general upgrade and optimization of the central Cloud infrastructure (Hybrid Cloud), by providing central Cloud Computing Infrastructures and Services, in order for the Organization to be able to exploit the qualitative and economic benefits of the technologies and the operating model by utilising Cloud computing technologies.

The Hybrid Cloud project aims to improve and modernize the organization’s central cloud infrastructure. Many organizations struggle to balance the need for flexible computing power with managing costs and security. This project addresses those challenges by upgrading to a hybrid cloud system that combines private and public cloud resources, offering better performance, flexibility, and cost efficiency.
The main goal is to provide reliable cloud computing services that meet the organization’s needs. By centralizing cloud resources, users can access the right computing power and storage quickly and efficiently, helping the organization benefit fully from cloud technology while controlling expenses.
The project works by integrating private cloud systems (run internally) with public cloud services from external providers. This allows sensitive data to stay secure, while less critical tasks use scalable public clouds. IT teams, cloud providers, and users collaborate to build and maintain this improved system.
In the future, the Hybrid Cloud infrastructure will grow and adapt as new technologies emerge. It will scale to support more users and applications, helping the organization stay flexible and efficient over time.

items.title: High-Performance Computer
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The European Digital Innovation Hub (DiHubMT) in Malta will host a High-Performance Computer (HPC), designed for AI and data-intensive workloads. It will provide essential resources to support the local start-up and innovation ecosystem.

Malta’s European Digital Innovation Hub (DiHubMT) is being equipped with a high-performance computing (HPC) facility to support data- and AI-intensive workloads for startups, SMEs, and public bodies. Government statements specify that the HPC will be hosted at DiHubMT and used for areas such as AI, computational physics, and data analysis, complementing the hub’s “test-before-invest,” skills, and advisory services. The move follows Malta’s accession to the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking in 2021, and aligns with the EDIH network’s remit to provide access to advanced technologies including HPC and AI.

items.title: Healthcare Professionals' Competency Platform
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The project aims to develop a system for analysing and evaluating quality indicators in personal healthcare and to implement technological solutions that connect health professional licenses with mandatory professional development to enhance the monitoring and supervision of competency renewal for healthcare specialists.

Lithuania is developing a competence platform for healthcare professionals to improve oversight of skills and qualifications. The project introduces a system for analysing and evaluating healthcare quality indicators, while integrating professional licences with mandatory continuous training requirements. By linking licensing and competency renewal, the platform seeks to strengthen supervision mechanisms and ensure that healthcare specialists maintain up-to-date knowledge and skills.

items.title: HIDRA
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The HIDRA system in Slovenia uses deep neural networks to forecast sea levels and coastal floods. It helps improve early warning systems and supports climate resilience.

The HIDRA system applies artificial intelligence techniques to enhance environmental monitoring and disaster preparedness. Specifically, it uses deep neural networks to forecast sea levels and coastal flooding, providing more accurate and timely data for decision-makers and communities.
The system contributes to:
Improved flood forecasting and prevention, particularly in vulnerable coastal areasStrengthening national resilience against climate-related risksEnhancing data-driven decision-making for environmental and civil protection authorities

items.title: Genomic Data Infrastructure (GDI) Ireland
items.org: European Commission – Directorate-General for Communications Networks, Content and Technology (DG CONNECT)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Genomic Data Infrastructure (GDI) Ireland is the Irish arm of a collaborative European research project that aims to allow safe and secure access to genetic data.

Genomic Data Infrastructure (GDI) Ireland is the Irish arm of the European GDI project which aims to create federated genetic data infrastructures across Europe to allow for safe and secure sharing of genomic data.

A federated genetic data infrastructure will allow countries taking part in the project to collaboratively share data while storing the data in their own country. This ensures data privacy and protection. Access to analyse the data will only be granted to individuals after a review process.

Ireland has committed to the onboarding stage of the overall European GDI project, which means that over the next 4 years we will develop a proof-of-concept infrastructure that will be tested using artificial genetic data first. This is to ensure that the infrastructure works correctly and is safe and secure.

items.title: GAIA-X Hub Netherlands
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The GAIA-X Hub Netherlands focuses on creating a federated and secure data infrastructure for Europe, in line with the broader GAIA-X initiative. This Dutch hub acts as a facilitator for businesses, governments, and organizations to develop cloud and data services that meet European standards. It contributes to the development of trusted data spaces across sectors, including energy, healthcare, and industry, fostering cross-border data collaboration.

The GAIA-X Hub Netherlands is part of the European GAIA-X initiative, which promotes a federated approach to cloud and data infrastructure. The Dutch hub brings together stakeholders from government, academia, and industry to define use cases and technical frameworks for secure, interoperable data sharing. It plays a coordinating role in shaping Dutch contributions to European data spaces, with an emphasis on ensuring compliance with EU values such as transparency, sovereignty, and security.

items.title: Dutch Vision on Data Sharing Between Companies
items.original_name: De Nederlandse visie op datadeling tussen bedrijven
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.document_name: De Nederlandse visie op datadeling tussen bedrijven
items.body:
This framework for responsible data sharing between businesses aims to create economic and societal value while safeguarding security and privacy. The vision focuses on voluntary data sharing to boost innovation and avoid risks like fragmentation and vendor lock-in, while still allowing for potential mandatory data sharing in the future. The government encourages an ecosystem that maximises the use of data, ensuring that businesses can securely exchange information across sectors.

The Netherlands’ vision on business-to-business data sharing sets three guiding principles: prefer voluntary sharing arranged by market actors; allow mandatory sharing where a clear public interest exists and voluntary arrangements fall short; and ensure people and firms retain control over their data. In practice, the government adopts a facilitative role (e.g., supporting agreements frameworks such as iSHARE in logistics) and points to sector schemes like MedMij (health) and JoinData (agriculture) as models for technical/organisational governance. The document also links the approach to EU developments (e.g., PSD2) and tasks ministries with applying these principles in their domains, with attention to interoperability, privacy (AVG), and protection of confidential business information.

items.title: Digital Wallonia Strategy on Digital Administration
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This strategy aims to transform Wallonia into a digital platform by innovating public services, fostering collaboration through open data, and serving as a testing ground for scalable digital solutions. It integrates AI to improve mobility-related services, such as traffic management and urban planning.

The Digital Wallonia Strategy on Digital Administration is a comprehensive initiative aimed at transforming Wallonia into a fully digital region by 2024. This strategy focuses on innovating public services, fostering collaboration through open data, and serving as a testing ground for scalable digital solutions. It is structured around five key themes: Digital Uses, Smart Territory, Digital Economy, Digital Innovation, and Digital Administration. 
A central component of this strategy is the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) to enhance mobility-related services. AI technologies are being applied to improve traffic management and urban planning, aiming to create more efficient, sustainable, and citizen-centric urban environments. For instance, the Smart Region project, launched in 2019 with a budget of EUR 4 million, seeks to propose a new model of governance for Walloon cities to transform them into Smart Cities. This initiative rethinks the experience of public administration offered to citizens. 
The DigitalWallonia4.ai programme plays a pivotal role in supporting AI adoption across public organizations. It provides resources and support mechanisms to assist in the digital transformation, enabling the development of AI-driven solutions that address regional challenges.

items.title: Digital Transition Fund
items.org: Ministry for Enterprise and Made in Italy
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Digital Transition Fund in Italy supports start-ups and SMEs in adopting innovative technologies, including AI, cloud computing, and Industry 4.0 solutions. It provides venture capital investments to stimulate the national innovation ecosystem. The initiative aims to drive digital transformation across sectors and supply chains.

The Digital Transition Fund, launched in 2023 by the Ministry for Enterprise and Made in Italy, strengthens the National Innovation Fund (Fondo Nazionale Innovazione – FNI) to accelerate digital innovation across Italy. Its primary goal is to support start-ups and SMEs that implement cutting-edge technologies, fostering competitiveness and growth.
Key objectives include:
Providing direct and indirect venture capital investments to innovative start-upsSupporting projects across sectors such as AI, cloud computing, healthcare, Industry 4.0, cybersecurity, fintech, and blockchainPromoting digital transformation within supply chains and small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs)The fund encourages collaboration between entrepreneurs, investors, and industry stakeholders to ensure that innovative projects scale successfully. By leveraging venture capital, the initiative reduces financial barriers for start-ups and facilitates the deployment of next-generation digital solutions.

items.title: Digital Transformation of Robotic Factories of the Future DIGITOP
items.original_name: Digitalna preobrazba robotskih tovarn prihodnosti DIGITOP
items.org: Ministry of Higher Education, Science and Innovation
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Digitalna preobrazba robotskih tovarn prihodnosti DIGITOP
items.body:
The DIGITOP programme helps manufacturing companies adopt advanced digital technologies, including AI, robotics, and Industry 4.0/5.0 solutions. It supports automation and optimisation of production processes through research and innovation projects. The initiative aims to strengthen digital transformation and strategic autonomy in Slovenia’s manufacturing sector.

The DIGITOP programme is designed to accelerate the digital transformation of manufacturing companies in Slovenia. Its main focus is the adoption of advanced technologies such as robotics, artificial intelligence (AI), information and communication technologies (ICT), and Industry 4.0/5.0 practices to improve automation, efficiency, and production optimisation.
Key objectives include:
Introducing advanced digital technologies into manufacturing operationsAutomating and optimising production processes using AI and roboticsSupporting strategic autonomy and technological independence in Slovenian industryThe programme consists of nine R&D projects at various stages of technological readiness. It is implemented through a public call for co-funding of longer-term, large-scale collaborative research and innovation programmes, targeting projects at Technical Readiness Levels 3–6.

items.title: Digital AI Assistant
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The "Digital Assistant", the Cypriot public sector's first Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) application, is now operational on the government portal gov.cy.

The purpose of the "Digital Assistant" is to facilitate more direct and faster communication between citizens and the state by providing information on issues of concern 24/7. Citizens can submit their queries in both Greek and English, and questions can also be typed using "Greeklish" characters.

items.title: Data Opening Programme
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The programme, jointly with the Act on Open Data and the Re-use of Public Sector Information covers key issues in the field of data sharing and management. It is addressed to government administration bodies and aims at: increasing the availability of data in the portal Dane.gov.pl, including data made available via API; improving interoperability and data quality; increase in the use and exchange of data; stimulating the market for the re-use of cultural resources and scientific data.

Poland’s Open Data Programme 2021–2027, implemented alongside the Act on Open Data and the Re-use of Public Sector Information, outlines measures to expand access to public sector information and improve data governance. It focuses on increasing the availability of datasets through the national portal Dane.gov.pl, including greater use of APIs, while also enhancing interoperability and data quality. The programme aims to support wider data use and exchange across public institutions and stimulate markets for cultural and scientific data re-use, contributing to both transparency and innovation.

items.title: Common State IT Infrastructure Programme
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
Common State IT Infrastructure Programme (WIIP) includes the handbook on Cloud in Government Services: Guide for Public Authorities, which aims to introduce uniform, high standards of IT systems protection and support for public administration in maintaining these systems. As part of the program, a tool for searching, comparing, and acquiring cloud services, the Cloud Service Provision System (Zapewniania Usług Chmurowych - ZUCH) was made available to the public administration.

Poland’s Common State IT Infrastructure Programme (WIIP) includes practical tools and guidance for cloud adoption in public administration. A core element is ZUCH—a cloud services marketplace for verified providers—used by authorities to search, compare and procure services from the Government and Public Cloud catalogues under WIIP rules. The programme is accompanied by implementation aids such as the Cloud in Government Services guide and a Model Cloud SLA, which set out procurement, security and interoperability expectations and align agencies on common standards. Together, these components are intended to simplify compliant cloud purchasing and raise protection levels across state IT systems.

items.title: Cloud development and migration
items.org: Authority for the Digitalisation of Romania (ADR)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The main objective of this investment is to upgrade the technologies used in public institutions so that they become cloud ready, while also developing new cloud native applications for cloud migration.

Romania has launched a €170m+ tender to build a Government Private Cloud, with the investment focused on bringing public-sector systems to a cloud-ready state and developing cloud-native applications for migration. The programme is framed to modernise core IT across institutions, improve scalability and continuity of services, and provide a common environment for future digital public services, while aligning with security and governance requirements.

items.title: Chips Competence Centre
