items.org: Malta Enterprise in collaboration with the University of Malta, MCAST, MDIA and Silicon Catalyst
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Malta Chips Competence Centre is a strategic initiative to strengthen Malta's semiconductor ecosystem. Spearheaded by Malta Enterprise in collaboration with the University of Malta, MCAST, MDIA and Silicon Catalyst. The Centre will have the objective to spur innovation and develop new talent. The Centre will also provide access to technical expertise and experimentation in the area of semiconductors targeted primarily for SMEs and startups.

Malta Enterprise, together with the University of Malta, MCAST and MDIA, is setting up the Malta Chips Competence Centre to strengthen the local semiconductor ecosystem with a focus on SME and start-up needs. In May 2024 Malta Enterprise signed an MoU with imec - a semiconductor and nanotechnology research centre - signalling plans to connect Maltese firms and researchers to European design platforms, pilot lines and imec’s venturing activity. The arrangement also foresees better access for UM/MCAST students to imec facilities during MSc/PhD work. The centre is framed to nurture talent, provide hands-on expertise and experimentation—especially in chip design—and to position Malta’s companies to tap EU instruments while building on a sector that already accounts for a notable share of exports and manufacturing employment.

items.title: Charter for the Responsible Use of AI in Public Services
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
This project by AI4Belgium’ Ethics & Law Working Group aims to draft a Charter defining ethical principles for AI use in public services.

The Charter developed by AI4Belgium’ Ethics & Law Working Group seeks to ensure trust and accountability in AI implementations, clarify government AI usage for citizens, and uphold democratic and legal principles. The Charter is currently being finalised by integrating comments from stakeholders and public consultations.

items.title: Automated Transport – Innovation Labs
items.org: Ministry of Climate Action, Environment, Energy, Mobility, Innovation, and Technology (BMK)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Automated Transport – Innovation Labs in Austria provide physical and digital testing infrastructures for automated road transport. They use AI technologies in multiple transport applications. The labs support innovation and testing, funded by the Ministry of Climate Action, Environment, Energy, Mobility, Innovation, and Technology (BMK).

The Automated Transport – Innovation Labs initiative encompasses Alp.Lab and DigiTrans, two Austrian innovation labs that offer environments for testing and developing automated road transport solutions. These labs provide both physical infrastructure (test tracks, vehicles) and digital platforms for simulation and experimentation.
Key objectives include:
Enabling research and experimentation in automated and AI-driven transport systemsSupporting development and testing of innovative mobility solutions under real and simulated conditionsPromoting collaboration between companies, research institutes, and universitiesThe labs integrate AI technologies in various applications, including autonomous driving, traffic management, and mobility optimisation. By offering access to state-of-the-art infrastructure, the initiative reduces barriers for companies and researchers to prototype, validate, and scale automated transport solutions.

items.title: Algorithm & AI Register
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Algorithm & AI Register in the Netherlands promotes transparency in public sector AI use. It ensures that algorithms are applied responsibly across government institutions. The register was developed with stakeholder feedback to meet societal expectations.

The Algorithm & AI Register is a national initiative aimed at enhancing transparency and accountability in the use of AI and algorithmic systems by government bodies. It responds to public and societal concerns about the ethical and responsible deployment of AI in public services.
Key objectives include:
Providing insight into how algorithms and AI are used across public sector institutionsEnsuring responsible and ethical use of AI in government decision-makingEngaging stakeholders to gather feedback and inform implementationA survey of various stakeholder groups was conducted to understand societal expectations and improve the design and functionality of the register. By documenting AI applications, the initiative helps governments remain accountable and allows citizens to understand and trust public sector use of technology.

items.title: Agreement Implementation Act 2024
items.org: Ministry of Social Affairs, Health, Care and Consumer Protection
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
The Agreement Implementation Act 2024 provides a legal framework for applying international and European agreements in health and social care. It ensures that Austria meets required standards and obligations. The act supports better integration and cooperation in the health sector.

The Agreement Implementation Act 2024 (Vereinbarungsumsetzungsgesetz) sets out the rules and procedures for implementing agreements in Austria related to health and social care. It ensures that the country complies with both international and European regulations, facilitating consistent application across different levels of government and healthcare institutions.
Key objectives include:
Ensuring compliance with international and European health and social care agreementsPromoting integration of health policies across federal, regional, and local levelsEnhancing cooperation between Austrian authorities and international partners in health-related mattersThe act provides clarity on legal responsibilities, reporting obligations, and procedural steps for adapting national legislation to international standards. By doing so, it helps Austria maintain a high-quality health and social care system while participating effectively in international collaborations.

items.title: Advancement of paediatric cancer care
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
In collaboration with Switzerland, Latvia is working on improving the approach to diagnosis and personalised treatment by creating a monitoring system for long-term support of children with cancer. In the future, this system will also be developed for adult oncological and rare disease. This project uses advanced genetic diagnostics and artificial intelligence (AI) to analyse patient data and create personalised treatment plans for patients.

The project combines advanced genetic diagnostics with AI-based analysis to inform personalised treatment. Alongside building the monitoring infrastructure, the programme emphasises clinical pathway development and knowledge exchange between Latvian and Swiss institutions to strengthen precision oncology capacity.

items.title: ARIS (Advanced Research Information System)
items.org: GRNET (National Infrastructures for Research and Technology)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
GRNET's Advanced Research Information System (ARIS) - GRNET has developed and maintains the ARIS infrastructure, which is the Greek High-Performance Computing System. This initiative supports research and development by providing high-performance computing resources.

GRNET’s Advanced Research Information System (ARIS) is Greece’s national high-performance computing system, managed by GRNET. It was created to support researchers and academics who need advanced computing power for complex tasks like simulations, data analysis, and artificial intelligence.
ARIS provides access to shared computing resources, along with training and support. Researchers from universities and public institutions can apply to use it based on the quality of their projects.
The system helps speed up scientific discovery across many fields, including climate science, biology, and engineering. GRNET regularly upgrades ARIS to keep it current and effective.
Looking ahead, ARIS is expected to grow and connect more closely with European HPC networks, giving Greek researchers broader access to international computing resources.

items.title: AIDA – Artificial Intelligence-Based Diagnostic Assistant for Detecting Stomach Inflammation
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This AI-powered diagnostic tool supports doctors in identifying precancerous stomach inflammation and developing personalised treatment strategies. The system enhances early detection of gastric cancer and provides tailored recommendations for patient health monitoring. Researchers from the University of Latvia are training AI models to recognize cancer cells with an accuracy of 92%.

The project involves 15 partners from eight European countries, AIDA is a multidisciplinary AI-powered assistive tool that helps doctors diagnose precancerous lesions, offers personalised therapeutic strategies for medical treatment, and provides personalised recommendations for monitoring patients' health status, promoting gastric cancer prevention.

Most cases of stomach cancer are detected at a late stage - when the patient's survival is predicted only for a year. The potential risk of developing stomach cancer can be detected at an early stage of its development, which is usually indicated by a chronic infection with the bacterium H. pylori residing in the stomach. This can greatly improve the patient's chances.

The AIDA project supports doctors and researchers by providing accurate and automated data analyses. It combines data from various sources to create a vast virtual data set to obtain a "risk score" for stomach cancer and discover the mechanisms of its development.

items.title: AIDA
items.org: UL Institute of Clinical and Preventive Medicine
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Lithuania is one of the partners of this project. The project aims to develop an AI-driven platform that assists healthcare professionals in creating personalised testing, tracing, and treatment plans for patients with precancerous stomach conditions, ultimately helping to prevent the progression to stomach cancer.

AIDA is a four-year Horizon Europe project (Grant 101095359; ~€7 million incl. UKRI support) coordinated by INCLIVA (Spain) to develop and validate an AI assistant for gastric-cancer prevention. The consortium brings together 12 centres of excellence from 8 countries, including the University of Latvia and the Hospital of Lithuanian University of Health Sciences Kaunas Clinics. The workplan targets a deployable solution—with certification as a medical device—covering diagnosis of precancerous gastric inflammation, personalised therapy selection and follow-up monitoring.

items.title: AI-powered medical chatbot
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This first AI-driven virtual assistant for a medical institution in the Baltics provides real-time responses to patient inquiries, offering information on doctor schedules, appointment availability, medical procedures, pricing, and hospital navigation. The chatbot processes 70–100 inquiries daily and is designed to improve patient communication and accessibility.

Latvia’s introduction of an AI-based virtual assistant in the healthcare sector marked a regional first in the Baltics. Beyond handling patient inquiries, the project was framed as part of a broader government agenda to integrate conversational AI into public services. By piloting the technology in a medical institution, the initiative aimed to demonstrate how AI could reduce administrative bottlenecks, improve service delivery, and set a precedent for scaling digital assistants across other sectors of public governance.

items.title: AI for Intelligent Image Analysis
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
In Flemish policymaking, AI is used for intelligent image recognition to support mobility and environmental efforts. Applications include traffic analysis, congestion prediction, and salting actions on highways. Other uses comprise flood mapping, agricultural monitoring, and soil sealing detection.

In Flanders, artificial intelligence is being applied to support policymaking through intelligent image recognition. The initiative addresses the need for improved data-driven insights in areas such as mobility, environmental management, and public safety. By leveraging AI technologies, policymakers and authorities can monitor, analyze, and respond more efficiently to evolving conditions.
The primary objective of the initiative is to enable automated analysis of visual data to support decision-making. In the mobility sector, AI is used for traffic analysis, congestion prediction, and planning salting actions on highways to improve safety and efficiency. In the environmental domain, AI applications include flood mapping, agricultural monitoring, and detection of soil sealing, providing valuable information for sustainable land management and climate resilience strategies.
The initiative combines AI algorithms with high-resolution imaging data from traffic cameras, satellites, drones, and other sources. It is implemented in collaboration with Flemish government agencies, research institutions, and technology partners who provide technical expertise, computational resources, and domain knowledge.

items.title: AI Usage in Flemish Government Agency for Innovation and Entrepreneurship (VLAIO)
items.org: Flemish Government Agency for Innovation and Entrepreneurship
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
VLAIO utilises generative AI to power a chatbot that provides accurate, reliable answers to entrepreneurs’ queries. The chatbot supports start-ups and established businesses by addressing challenges related to enterprise creation and innovation.

The Flemish Government Agency for Innovation and Entrepreneurship (VLAIO) has implemented artificial intelligence to enhance its support for entrepreneurs and businesses. The initiative addresses the challenge of providing timely, accurate, and consistent guidance to start-ups and established companies navigating complex procedures related to enterprise creation, funding, and innovation.
At the core of this initiative is a generative AI-powered chatbot. The chatbot is designed to respond to entrepreneurs’ queries in a reliable and efficient manner, covering a wide range of topics such as business registration, innovation grants, regulatory requirements, and support programs. By automating responses to common questions, the system helps reduce administrative workload and ensures that users receive prompt guidance.
The AI solution is integrated within VLAIO’s existing digital services and is continually updated to reflect policy changes and emerging business needs. It draws on a knowledge base maintained by VLAIO experts, allowing it to deliver accurate answers while also learning from new interactions. The chatbot supports entrepreneurs in real time, enabling them to focus on strategic planning and business development rather than navigating administrative complexity.

items.title: AI Map
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The aim of the project is to create a central catalogue/ register for all ministries on productive and planned AI initiatives.

The AI Map catalogue is to be updated on an ongoing basis. The aim is to provide a clear source of information on internal AI initiatives or AI systems and to avoid duplication.

items.title: AGENAS National Platform
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects

items.title: A campaign promoting the use of health data
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
A campaign aimed at raising awareness about the responsible collection and use of healthcare data, facilitated through applications linked to the health data wallet app.

In 2021, Hungary launched the Electronic Health Service Space as part of a campaign to modernise the country’s healthcare system. The initiative introduced a cloud-based communication platform that linked general practitioners, outpatient services, and other providers, with the aim of improving coordination and efficiency in the public healthcare sector.

items.title: A Land for Tomorrow
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This Federal Government initiative collects proposals from citizens and experts on government reform and democracy development. AI processes and analyses these ideas to generate insights for policymaking, culminating in a public report.

The Belgian Federal Government’s initiative “A Land for Tomorrow” (Un Pays pour Demain) engages citizens and experts in shaping government reform and the development of democratic processes. The project addresses the challenge of processing large volumes of public input to generate actionable insights for policymakers. By leveraging artificial intelligence, the initiative ensures that diverse perspectives are systematically analysed and synthesized.
The primary objective of the project is to collect proposals from the public and experts, process them using AI-driven text analysis, and identify patterns, priorities, and emerging themes. This approach helps policymakers gain a clear understanding of societal expectations, innovative ideas, and areas where governmental practices can be improved.
AI techniques applied in this initiative include natural language processing, clustering, and semantic analysis, which enable the extraction of key insights from thousands of submissions. The process culminates in a comprehensive public report that presents findings, recommendations, and actionable insights for government reform and democratic development. The initiative is implemented by the Federal Government in collaboration with research partners and technology providers who provide expertise in AI and data analysis.

items.title: 1 million genomes - Vilnius University Hospital (VUL) Santaros Klinikos
items.org: Vilnius University Hospital Santaros Klinikos Biobank
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Lithuania has announced funding for this project, covering the period from 2023 to 2026 (EUR 7.6M). Lithuanian institutions will participate in the EU’s Genomic Data Infrastructure (GDI) initiative, utilising the national genomic medicine infrastructure to support personalised healthcare. This will create new opportunities for delivering high-quality, effective health services.

Lithuania committed €7.6 million (2023–2026) to its participation in the EU Genomic Data Infrastructure (GDI) initiative. The funding supports the use of national genomic medicine infrastructure to advance personalised healthcare, while contributing to the broader European effort to link genomic data resources across countries. This initiative is expected to strengthen research, enable cross-border data use, and open opportunities for more precise health services.

items.title: eHealth Strategy for a Healthier Society
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This project will elaborate a way to implement a unified electronic health record, as well as design a national telemedicine framework and revise the legislation to enable better oversight of the eHealth system and to streamline data flows for better patient care and informed policy making.

Slovenia's "eHealth Strategy for a Healthier Society" is a comprehensive initiative aimed at transforming the national healthcare system through digitalization. Developed with support from the European Commission's Structural Reform Support Programme, the strategy outlines objectives for the period 2022–2027.
Key Components:
Unified Electronic Health Record (EHR): The strategy emphasizes the implementation of a nationwide EHR system to centralize patient data, enhancing accessibility and continuity of care.National Telemedicine Framework: A national framework for telemedicine services is being designed to facilitate remote consultations and healthcare delivery, improving access to services across the country.Legislative Reforms: The strategy includes revising existing legislation to enable better oversight of the eHealth system, streamline data flows, and ensure secure data exchange.Implementation and Expected Outcomes:
The strategy aims to optimize and integrate existing health information systems, improve data security, and enhance the efficiency of healthcare management processes. By 2027, Slovenia seeks to establish a patient-centered, secure, and interoperable digital health ecosystem that aligns with EU frameworks such as the European Health Data Space and the Digital Decade 2030 objectives.
Governance and Stakeholder Involvement:
A hybrid governance model will be established, balancing national standardization with local autonomy. A Central National Unit (CNU) will coordinate efforts, supported by advisory and executive boards that include key stakeholders from healthcare providers, policymakers, and payers.

items.title: eHealth Strategy
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The project aims to develop an eHealth Strategy and Investment Plan that will outline the objectives and priorities for the development of eHealth in Slovenia for the period 2022-2027. It details the introduction of a single electronic health record (eHealth Record) and the creation of a national telehealth framework and the amendment of related legislation to enable better oversight of the eHealth system and to streamline the flow of data for better patient care and informed policymaking.

Slovenia's eHealth Strategy for 2022–2027, titled “eHealth for a Healthier Society”, is a comprehensive initiative developed with support from the European Commission’s Structural Reform Support Programme. The strategy outlines the objectives and priorities for the development of eHealth in Slovenia, focusing on enhancing patient care, improving system efficiency, and facilitating data-driven decision-making.
Key Objectives:
Unified Electronic Health Record (eHealth Record): The strategy emphasizes the introduction of a single electronic health record system, aiming to centralize patient data, enhance accessibility, and improve the continuity of care across the healthcare system.National Telehealth Framework: A national telehealth framework is being designed to facilitate the provision of remote healthcare services, ensuring broader access to medical consultations and reducing geographical barriers to healthcare delivery.Legislative Reforms: The strategy includes the amendment of related legislation to enable better oversight of the eHealth system, streamline data flows, and ensure compliance with data protection regulations.System Integration and Interoperability: Efforts are underway to optimize, integrate, and connect existing information systems and databases, enhancing the efficiency of management and control processes within the healthcare sector.Data Security and Governance: The strategy prioritizes the enhancement of data security measures and the establishment of robust governance frameworks to safeguard patient information and ensure the responsible use of health data.Strategic Vision:By 2027, Slovenia aims to have a patient-centered, secure, interoperable, and efficient digital health ecosystem. The strategy seeks to empower citizens and health professionals through digital tools, improve population health, and promote trust in digital services. It aligns with broader EU frameworks such as the European Health Data Space and the Digital Decade 2030 objectives, contributing to the modernization and digitalization of the healthcare system in Slovenia.
Implementation and Oversight:
The Government Office for Digital Transformation, soon to become the Ministry of Digital Transformation, plays a pivotal role in coordinating the digitalization efforts. The strategy emphasizes the importance of a dedicated management structure, specialized workforce, and active involvement of all relevant stakeholders to ensure the successful implementation and sustainability of the eHealth initiatives.

items.title: Translate-AD
items.original_name: VUB, UZ Brussel, ULB, Hôpital Erasme, Université Catholique de Louvain (UCL), and Cliniques Universitaires St. Luc
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: VUB, UZ Brussel, ULB, Hôpital Erasme, Université Catholique de Louvain (UCL), and Cliniques Universitaires St. Luc
items.body:
The Translate-AD project unites six universities and university hospitals (VUB, UZ Brussel, ULB, Hôpital Erasme, Université Catholique de Louvain (UCL), and Cliniques Universitaires St. Luc) in developing digital platform designed to streamline the exchange patient data among these institutions. Initially tailored to Alzheimer’s patients in Brussels, the platform is envisioned to expand in the long term to other Belgian and international centers.

In Belgium, an estimated 200,000 people suffer from dementia, with around 6% of them being under 65 years of age. The most common cause is Alzheimer’s disease, responsible for 70% of dementia cases in the region. Alzheimer’s is also the leading cause of death in Belgium. The disease causes the loss of brain cells and the breakdown of connections between them, leading to memory loss and cognitive decline. However, many questions about the origins of Alzheimer’s remain unanswered, partly because privacy laws have made the sharing of patient data for collaborative research challenging.
To address this need, researchers in the Translate-AD project will develop a digital platform to facilitate the exchange of expertise and patient data between university hospitals. This will enable the identification of biomarkers – the ‘fingerprints’ of diseases that predict whether someone has or will develop a condition. The project will improve diagnosis and prognosis, a milestone in treating a disease whose progression is difficult to predict. Additionally, a better understanding of the disease will likely lead to new therapeutic possibilities.
The platform will allow researchers to tackle even the most complex research questions together, without the need to exchange patient data. A research question will be translated into a script, which is then sent from a central research computer to local hospital servers. All data analyses will be conducted on these local servers, where anonymised patient data is stored. Once complete, the results of the data analysis are sent from the local servers back to the central research computer. This approach makes research collaboration far easier while fully respecting privacy regulations.

items.title: The new Section 393 SGB V (Social Security Code – Book V) has been enacted with the recent “Digital Act”
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Germany established uniform and transparent standards for the use of cloud-computing services for processing health data, protecting sensitive health information from unauthorized access, manipulation, or loss. This regulation can positively impact AI use and research by providing a secure and standardised framework for handling sensitive health data, fostering trust and enabling more robust, compliant AI-driven innovations in healthcare.

Germany’s Digital Act introduced Section 393 of the Social Security Code (SGB V), establishing binding IT-security standards for the use of cloud services in the healthcare sector. The provision ensures that health data may only be processed in certified environments meeting strict criteria, such as the BSI’s C5 standard, and that data remain subject to EU jurisdiction. This framework aims to provide legal certainty for healthcare providers, safeguard sensitive patient information, and create clearer conditions for the deployment of digital and AI solutions in medical research and care.

items.title: The Hellenic Digital Health Cluster (HDHC) - VELES Excellence Hub
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Founded in 2021, the Hellenic Digital Health Cluster strengthens Greece's digital health sector by supporting innovation and connecting academia with industry. It is part of the VELES Excellence Hub, launched in 2023 driving healthcare innovation in Greece, Bulgaria, Romania, and Cyprus using data and AI to enhance personalised medicine and healthcare decision-making.

The VELES Excellence Hub, launched in 2023, is a cross-border initiative that promotes innovation in healthcare across Greece, Bulgaria, Romania, and Cyprus. It builds on existing national clusters—such as the Hellenic Digital Health Cluster—to foster collaboration between research institutions, businesses, and healthcare providers. The hub focuses on applying data and AI technologies to strengthen personalised medicine, improve clinical decision-making, and support sustainable healthcare systems. By linking academic expertise with industry needs, VELES aims to accelerate the adoption of advanced digital health solutions and position the region as a centre for data-driven healthcare innovation.

items.title: Sunet Data Center DC Orion in Kalix + EOSC data storage
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This project aims to establish a redundant data centre in Northern Sweden for Sunet's services.

Sunet, Sweden’s national research and education network, is responsible for providing secure and reliable digital infrastructure to universities, research institutions, and public bodies. To strengthen the resilience of its services, Sunet is establishing a new data centre in northern Sweden under the project known as DC Orion. This development responds to the need for greater redundancy in national digital infrastructure, reducing the risk of disruption from regional outages or other incidents in the Stockholm area where many of Sunet’s existing systems are currently located.
The main objective of the initiative is to ensure continuity of Sunet’s critical services—such as identity management (EduID), storage and archiving, virtual computing environments, media services, and DNS—by hosting them in a geographically distinct location with secure and scalable infrastructure. Locating the facility in the north offers additional benefits, including access to a stable power supply, robust fibre connectivity, and the natural advantages of a cooler climate for sustainable operations.
The project is led by Sunet and has been developed through a detailed planning process, building on earlier feasibility studies. The facility is designed to meet high standards of security and reliability, including redundant power and network connections. Services are being progressively migrated to the new site, with Sunet’s Virtual Datacenter (VDC) now available from DC Orion. This supports both Sunet’s own redundancy needs and the growing demands of Sweden’s research and education communities for high-performance, secure, and flexible digital services.

items.title: Strategy of the e-Health Centre – summary 2023-2027
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Strategy for Poland’s e-Health Centre, focused on continuing the development of e-Health services and maximise the potential of digitalisation.

The vision was centered around innovation and the satisfaction – of patients and other participants in the health care system – with the products provided by CeZ. It also stems from the need to reinforce the brand. Although the e-Health Centre has been on the market for more than 20 years, it is not as recognizable as other units in the health sector. This has only begun to change in recent years, with the increase in the level of IT implementation in the health care system in Poland. Appropriate communication and information activities were planned to further reinforce CeZ’s brand and to popularize its e-services. Innovation appears in the vision due to the dynamic development of the IT area. CeZ also wants to be synonymous with reliability, providing solutions using the latest technology stack, quality e-services and elements of artificial intelligence.

items.title: Secure and cost-effective IT operations
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body: These proposals for lasting forms of coordinated state IT operations are designed to increase security and cost-effectiveness of authorities' IT operational solutions.

items.title: SMEs Innovative: Medical Technology
items.org: Federal Ministry of Education and Research
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
To strengthen the innovative capacity of "Made in Germany" medical technology, the Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF) supports SMEs in their research on innovative medical products, in-vitro diagnostics, and digital medical technology solutions. This funding aims to initiate additional research and development activities, boost medical technology research in Germany, enhance networking between SMEs and partners in science and healthcare.

Medical technology plays an indispensable role in healthcare. The German medical technology sector is primarily made up of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), which account for over 90% of the companies in the field. These SMEs are the innovative backbone of the industry, operating in a highly dynamic environment and under stringent regulatory requirements for medical products, which significantly increase the investment risks in research and development. The BMBF supports SMEs to strengthen the competitive position of the German medical technology sector.

items.title: Roadmap for a national digital infrastructure for healthcare
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body: Through common standards and specifications, a national infrastructure is made possible. The purpose of the infrastructure is to create better conditions for residents to gain access to and have control over their own health data. The infrastructure will also make healthcare work more efficient; conditions are created for using data to develop healthcare, conduct research and create better opportunities for decision-making.

items.title: Public Administration Cloud Strategy
items.org: Presidency of the Council of Ministers
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The cloud is a network of remote computers connected by the Internet that allows you to store and manage data, run applications, and provide services. The Cloud Strategy for the Public Administration aims to promote the use of the cloud by public entities.

The Cloud Strategy for Public Administration outlines a set of tools to promote sustainable cloud adoption: i) a governance model to align objectives across agencies and coordinate implementation, ii) an adoption framework to guide decisions on system migration to the cloud, iii) an HR qualification plan to ensure skilled personnel are prepared for cloud-related challenges, iv) updated procurement and accounting processes, including legislative changes to simplify cloud service acquisition, v) standardised tender documents and framework agreements for contracting cloud services, vi) monitoring tools to evaluate, manage, and control cloud contracts with visibility into costs and usage, and vii) an awareness model to reduce hesitation around cloud adoption. to support these objectives, working groups with representatives from various government sectors have been established.

items.title: PariSanté Campus
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Designed as a digital health development center in Paris, PariSanté Campus brings together public institutions, research institutes, and startups to foster innovation in digital health, emphasising AI applications in healthcare.

It aims to:
Stimulate the production and use of health data for research and innovation;Support excellence in training in the field of e-health and foster the creation of talent pools and expertise;Develop high-impact applications that drive economic growth, create businesses, and generate employment;Improve medical care strategies and enhance the efficiency of the healthcare system, always in the best interest of the patient.The originality of the project lies in the broad range of disciplines mobilized to achieve this goal: biology, physics, mathematics, computer science, engineering, and the humanities and social sciences.

items.title: Optimal therapies through data-driven decision and support systems
items.original_name: Optimale Therapien durch datengetriebene Entscheidungs- und Unterstützungssysteme
items.org: Federal Ministry of Education and Research
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Optimale Therapien durch datengetriebene Entscheidungs- und Unterstützungssysteme
items.body:
In many diseases, choosing the appropriate therapy forms the basis for the subsequent course and success of the treatment. The goal of the funding is to optimize patient care through medical technology solutions in the form of innovative decision and support systems. Data-driven approaches should support healthcare providers at all stages of the care process to achieve better healing or a reduction in side effects.

Projects should primarily use data-driven approaches, such as those typically found in Artificial Intelligence (AI) or machine learning techniques beside rule-based methods.

items.title: Open Data Action Plan
items.org: Latvian Ministry of Environmental Protection and Regional Development (VARAM); State Chancellery Riga 2024
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Building on the Digital Transformation Guidelines 2021–2027, this initiative is aimed at updating Latvia’s approach to open data management in order to enhance data access and usage for societal and economic benefits.

Based on the Digital Transformation Guidelines 2021–2027, Latvia has set out measures to update its approach to open data management. The initiative is framed around improving access to and use of public data with the intention of generating broader societal and economic value.
Planned activities include adjustments to standards for formats, metadata, and interoperability, alongside efforts to encourage reuse of datasets by different stakeholders. These steps are expected to support the gradual development of a more coordinated national data ecosystem.

items.title: NeIC Heilsa
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Eilsa Tryggvedottir is the name of the Nordic collaboration on sensitive data funded by NeIC and partner nodes. Access to sensitive data, such as genomics and phenomics data, is critical for driving ground-breaking discoveries and advance human health. The project aims to build on the technology developed in the previous NeIC Tryggve projects to increase interoperability and strengthen Nordic cross-border e-infrastructure.

Heilsa Tryggvedottir is a Nordic project, funded through the Nordic e-Infrastructure Collaboration (NeIC) with participation by partner nodes, which builds on prior work under the NeIC Tryggve and Tryggve2 projects. Its purpose is to enable secure cross-border sharing and analysis of sensitive human data—such as combined genomic and phenotypic (phenomics) datasets—in order to drive discovery, strengthen public health, and improve healthcare outcomes.
The project has several core objectives:
To transform the prototype or experimental tools developed in earlier Tryggve phases into production-ready, interoperable services.
To support federated data services across Nordic countries so that researchers with appropriate authorization can access or combine data hosted in different countries without moving sensitive raw data in insecure ways.
To incorporate key infrastructure pieces such as sensitive data archives, synthetic data generation, and imputation services, along with federated authentication/authorization (e.g. using ELIXIR AAI) to ensure data is managed responsibly.
Heilsa Tryggvedottir is carried out by ELIXIR node partners in Norway, Denmark, Sweden, Finland, and Estonia, under the larger umbrella of NeIC. The project works closely with existing national sensitive data services and archives, and with European infrastructure efforts such as the Federated European Genome-phenome Archive (FEGA), combining legal, ethical, technical, and operational expertise.

items.title: National Strategy for Advanced Computing
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Portugal was one of the six pioneering countries to sign the EuroHPC Declaration in March 2017. Through its National Strategy for Advanced Computing, the country aims to establish itself as a European reference point in three areas: an advanced computing services economy, a cutting-edge laboratory environment, and the education and training of specialists in this field.

Portugal's National Strategy for Advanced Computing aims to create a robust HPC infrastructure, drive research and innovation, and foster international collaboration. The strategy highlights the importance of developing appropriate infrastructure, building a skilled workforce, and cultivating a culture that recognises advanced computing as essential to research and industry. Key areas of focus include: 
i) establishing a supercomputing network with data centres to support research and innovation, 
ii) developing and retaining talent with advanced computing skills, and 
iii) creating a policy "info-structure" to bridge infrastructure and users, enabling high-value services and software. The Strategy plays a critical role in promoting advanced scientific computing and data processing across various domains, including industry, academia, health, climate, energy, mobility, and social sciences.

items.title: National Reference Centre for semantic resources of the Ministry of Health
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Provides information on national reference terminology resources for semantic interoperability in the information systems of the National Health System and in the exchange of clinical documentation in national and international projects.

Spain’s National Reference Centre for Semantic Resources (SNOMED CT), managed by the Ministry of Health, is designed to ensure semantic interoperability across the National Health System (SNS). The centre manages and distributes SNOMED CT clinical terminology, promoting its adoption and use within health information systems nationwide.
Main Functions:
License Management: Administers SNOMED CT licenses for users in Spain.Content Distribution: Publishes and distributes both the official SNOMED International content and Spain-specific extensions, including reference sets and a Spanish-language lexicon.Support and Training: Provides official training on SNOMED CT and offers technical support and consultancy for SNS users.International Collaboration: Serves as Spain’s point of contact with SNOMED International and participates in working groups to develop and improve clinical terminology.

items.title: National Health Data Lake
items.org: Ministry for Digital Transformation and Public Service
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Repository of anonymous raw data storage in a virtual format, which can be used to improve healthcare.

Spain is advancing the creation of a National Health Data Lake as part of its broader strategy to establish a National Health Data Space. This initiative aims to centralize anonymized health data from various sources into a virtual repository, facilitating enhanced research, innovation, and evidence-based policymaking.
Key Features:
Anonymized Data Collection: The repository will aggregate de-identified health data from multiple health databases, ensuring privacy and compliance with data protection regulations.Integration of Regional Databases: By connecting regional health databases, the data lake will provide a comprehensive view of health trends and outcomes across the country.Support for Research and Innovation: The centralized data will enable researchers and policymakers to conduct studies on various health topics, including vaccine effectiveness and healthcare accessibility.Alignment with European Health Data Space (EHDS): Spain's efforts are in line with the EU's vision for a decentralized infrastructure that connects health data access bodies across member states, promoting the secondary use of health data for research and innovation.Strategic Importance:
The National Health Data Lake is a pivotal component of Spain's digital health transformation. It not only supports national health objectives but also contributes to the European Health Data Space, enhancing cross-border data sharing and collaboration within the EU.

items.title: National Electronic Health File (NEHF)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This initiative aims to interconnect Greek hospitals, enabling doctors to access national electronic health records, streamline healthcare, and reduce bureaucracy by providing mobile access to medical data. An AI-powered NEHF (AI applications' integrated processing of large volumes of diverse data) is expected to improve interconnectivity and interoperability of national healthcare networks and national healthcare databases and provide faster and better justified management decisions.

Greece has introduced the National Electronic Health File (Ατομικός Ηλεκτρονικός Φάκελος Υγείας – ΑΗΦΥ) as part of a broader digital health reform. The system provides every citizen with a unified electronic record that can be securely updated and accessed across different points of care. Managed through gov.gr, it integrates data from hospitals, primary care units, and pharmacies into a single platform under the oversight of the Ministry of Health. Beyond improving coordination, it also sets the groundwork for advanced data use, including AI-assisted analysis, while ensuring compliance with strict security and privacy rules.

items.title: Memorandum of Understanding
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Signed by 12 partners during the 5G Techritory event, the MoU aims to establish a partnership for developing Latvia’s semiconductor ecosystem. Coordinated by Riga Technical University and open to international collaborators. Since December 2024, 5 additional partners have signed the MoU. the MoU of a total of 17 partners aims to establish a partnership for developing Latvia’s semiconductor ecosystem. Coordinated by Riga Technical University and open to international collaborators.

The initiative is coordinated by Riga Technical University and remains open to international participation. By the end of 2024, the number of signatories had grown to seventeen partners, reflecting expanding interest in strengthening Latvia’s role in the digital sector.

items.title: Member of IPCEI Microelectronics, IPCEI Cloud data, and IPCEI Health
items.org: Latvian Ministry of Economics; Latvian Investment and Development Agency (LIAA)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Latvia participates in IPCEI working groups on Microelectronics, Cloud Data, and Health to advance innovative technologies and meet digital and green goals. RRF funding supports these projects.

Latvia is involved in several IPCEI initiatives that pool European expertise and funding to accelerate strategic technologies. With support from the Recovery and Resilience Facility, these projects are framed to link national priorities with EU-wide goals for digitalisation and sustainability.

items.title: Making repositories and AI systems usable in everyday nursing care
items.original_name: Repositorien und KI-Systeme im Pflegealltag nutzbar machen
items.org: Federal Ministry of Education and Research
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Repositorien und KI-Systeme im Pflegealltag nutzbar machen
items.body:
This funding measure aims to support caregivers as well as caregiving relatives and to improve the self-determination and quality of life of people in need of care through innovative AI applications. Funded projects develop long-term usable data and software repositories as well as AI systems for use in everyday care.

This measure funds projects that (1) build long-term usable data and software repositories for care, (2) develop AI systems for everyday care, and (3) run a scientific accompanying/coordination project—all to support caregivers and relatives and improve autonomy and quality of life for people in need of care.

items.title: Luxembourg National Data Service (LNDS)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
LNDS aims to accelerate economic, ecological, and societal transitions through the efficient and responsible use of data, with a focus on improving the secondary use of data. A key emphasis is placed on sharing public sector data to enable value creation for data partners, which include public and private organizations interested in using or providing data, or both.

The Luxembourg National Data Service (LNDS) is a state-owned initiative created to strengthen the country’s data ecosystem and promote the secondary use of data for research, innovation, and policy. Its mandate is to act as a trusted intermediary that facilitates secure data sharing between public institutions, private organisations, and research actors. By setting governance frameworks, providing technical infrastructure, and ensuring compliance with ethical and legal standards, LNDS seeks to unlock value from public sector data while maintaining strong safeguards on privacy and security. The service also supports Luxembourg’s ambition to position itself as a hub for responsible data-driven innovation.

items.title: Joining Chips Joint Undertaking (JU)
items.org: Latvian Ministry of Education and Science Republic of Latvia
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Latvia plans to join the Chips JU and establish a national semiconductor competence centre. The initiative aims to strengthen the national semiconductor ecosystem and is supported by multi-year co-funding.

In October 2024, Latvia amended its regulations to enable full participation in the EU Chips Joint Undertaking (Chips JU), allowing national research institutions and companies to access Horizon Europe co-financing. The initiative is framed as part of a tripartite European partnership on advanced nanoelectronics and microchips, aimed at strengthening Latvia’s semiconductor competence. Implementation will be coordinated by the Ministry of Education and Science together with line ministries and national research bodies.

items.title: Invest-NL
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Invest-NL provides financing to promising Dutch companies that contribute to societal transitions, including in deep tech sectors like AI. It focuses on providing equity and debt financing, particularly for SMEs that struggle to secure funding.

Invest-NL is the Netherlands’ national financing institution, created to support companies and projects driving key transitions in areas like energy, circular economy, life sciences, agrifood, and deep tech, including AI. It focuses on filling financing gaps for SMEs and scale-ups that struggle to attract private investment for high-risk, capital-intensive innovations.
It provides equity and debt financing, typically €5–50 million, often through co-investments, and also invests in venture and private equity funds. With initiatives like the Dutch Future Fund II, Invest-NL mobilizes public and private capital to help Dutch innovations scale and compete internationally.

items.title: Integration of state information resources into the state data lake
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The goal of this project is to consolidate public sector data and transfer it to a common “data lake” - the State Data Management Information System common space, where it could help make data-based decisions, conduct scientific research and promote digital innovations.

The initiative consolidates data from hundreds of public IT systems into a shared State Data Management Information System, often referred to as the data lake. This centralised environment is designed to make state-held data more usable for decision-making, research, and digital innovation. By standardising how data is stored and accessed, it aims to improve interoperability across institutions and strengthen Lithuania’s overall data maturity.

items.title: Important Project of Common European Interest – Next Generation Cloud Infrastructure and Services (IPCEI-CIS)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
IPCEI-CIS is a significant European initiative involving over 100 companies and research organizations across 12 Member States, with Germany playing a coordinating role. This project aims to establish a decentralized cloud-edge ecosystem that will reduce technological dependencies and foster new data-driven business models. The primary goal of IPCEI-CIS is to create a “Multi-Provider Cloud-Edge Continuum,” which allows for advanced use of data processing resources from cloud-edge environments.

The IPCEI-CIS (Important Project of Common European Interest – Cloud Infrastructure and Services) is a large European initiative designed to strengthen Europe’s digital independence. Today, many cloud services used in Europe are operated by non-European providers. This creates risks around data security, privacy, and long-term control. At the same time, emerging technologies—like autonomous vehicles or smart factories—need to process data quickly and close to where it is generated. Existing systems aren’t always fit for these needs.
To address this, IPCEI-CIS aims to build a decentralised, secure, and efficient “cloud-edge continuum.” This means creating a system where different cloud and edge service providers across Europe can work together seamlessly. It will allow users to process and move data across different locations and providers, without being locked into one company’s platform. The goal is not just technical independence, but also the development of new, data-driven services and business models across industries.
The project involves over 100 companies and research organisations from 12 EU countries, with Germany coordinating. Work is split into areas like building energy-efficient data centres, developing management software, and testing real-world applications. With around €2.6 billion in combined public and private funding, the project is now moving from research to deployment.
Over time, IPCEI-CIS aims to create a lasting digital infrastructure for Europe—one that is secure, sustainable, and open to future innovation.

items.title: IMPaCT
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
IMPaCT's mission is to establish and transfer the necessary knowledge to support and facilitate the effective deployment of Personalized Precision Medicine, which will represent a paradigm shift and a new reality for the healthcare system, enabling a preventive, diagnostic, and therapeutic approach that is personalized, more effective, and safer for each patient.

Spain’s IMPaCT initiative is a national programme, coordinated by the Carlos III Health Institute (Instituto de Salud Carlos III, ISCIII), designed to accelerate the deployment of Personalized Precision Medicine across the Spanish National Health System.  It is intended to shift healthcare toward more preventive, diagnostic, and therapeutic approaches that are tailored to each patient, making them safer and more effective. 
The structure of IMPaCT is arranged around three major axes or pillars:
Predictive Medicine (the Cohort Axis): This involves building a large-scale, population-based cohort. The cohort is meant to include 200,000 people from 50 “nodes” spread across all 17 autonomous communities plus Ceuta and Melilla. Participants will provide data via clinical records, lifestyle/environmental inputs, biological sampling and periodic follow-ups. Data Science (the DATA Axis): This axis deals with integrating and analysing clinical, molecular and genetic data. It aims to ensure good practices around data collection, interoperability, secondary data use, and building models for research and healthcare decision making. Genomic Medicine (the GENOMICS Axis): This pillar supports the genomic-side of things: developing infrastructure to carry out high-complexity genomic analyses, sequencing, and making those resources available across the country.Two cross-cutting themes run through all of IMPaCT: ethics and scientific integrity, and internationalization.

items.title: Health IT Interoperability Governance Ordinance (GIGV) Competence Centre
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Germany has advanced healthcare interoperability through the Digital Act, which expanded the Coordination Office for Interoperability into a Competence Centre. Supported by the Interop Council and expert working groups, it promotes technical, syntactic, and semantic interoperability, with the Health IT Interoperability Governance Ordinance (GIGV) ensuring a holistic, coordinated approach to developing binding guidelines and standards.

Germany’s Digital Act expanded the Coordination Office for Interoperability into a Competence Centre intended to guide healthcare data integration. Supported by the Interop Council and expert working groups, the centre is tasked with developing approaches to technical, syntactic, and semantic interoperability in health IT.
The Health IT Interoperability Governance Ordinance (GIGV) provides the framework for this work and seeks to ensure that standards and guidelines are developed in a coordinated and binding manner, promoting consistency across the digital health system.

items.title: Health Data Lab
items.org: Federal Institute for Drugs and Medical Devices
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Health Data Lab (HDL) at the Federal Institute for Drugs and Medical Devices makes pseudonymised claims data from people insured in the statutory health system available for research purposes and other legally defined public interest purposes, including AI development, the HDL makes an important contribution towards better and safer healthcare.
With the Act on Health Data Use the Social Security Code – Book V (SGB V) has been amended to explicitly enable the development of AI systems.

The Health Data Lab (HDL), hosted at Germany’s Federal Institute for Drugs and Medical Devices (BfArM), is structured to provide pseudonymized claims data from citizens insured under the statutory health system for research and public interest uses—explicitly including development of AI applications. It emerged from the reorganisation of the former DIMDI unit and is grounded in legal reforms such as the Data Transparency Regulation (DaTraV) and the Health Data Use Act.

items.title: G-Cloud
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The strategy of investing in the Government Cloud “G-Cloud" is part of the government's strategy to centralise all the Information Systems of the individual Public Administration Bodies into a single structure under the management of the infrastructure by the GSIS of the Ministry of Digital Governance. G-Cloud aims at the common use of computing infrastructures by public administration bodies, thus reducing their maintenance and support costs and increasing their flexibility and security.

The Government Cloud, or “G-Cloud,” is an initiative to centralize the IT systems of all public administration bodies into one shared cloud platform. This approach helps reduce costs by avoiding the need for each agency to maintain its own separate infrastructure. It also improves flexibility, allowing agencies to scale and adapt their digital services more easily, while strengthening security by managing everything under a single, well-governed system.
G-Cloud is managed by the General Secretariat for Information Systems (GSIS) within the Ministry of Digital Governance. Through this shared infrastructure, public bodies can access computing resources as needed, making government operations more efficient and connected.
As the project grows, more public agencies will join, and the platform will support new digital services, helping create a modern, cost-effective, and secure digital government.

items.title: EUCAIM project
items.org: European Institute for Biomedical Imaging Research
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Sweden is part of the EUCAIM-project which focuses on leveraging AI-based technologies for cancer diagnosis and treatment to improve patient outcomes and transform cancer care across the European Union.

Sweden is actively participating in the EUCAIM (European Federation for Cancer Images) project, a pivotal initiative under the European Cancer Imaging Initiative, which is a cornerstone of Europe's Beating Cancer Plan. This project aims to establish a pan-European digital infrastructure that facilitates the secure sharing and analysis of cancer-related imaging data, thereby enhancing the development and deployment of artificial intelligence (AI) tools in oncology.
The primary objective of EUCAIM is to create a federated platform that integrates anonymized cancer images and associated clinical data from diverse sources across Europe. This infrastructure will support the development, benchmarking, and validation of AI models for precision medicine, ultimately leading to improved diagnostic accuracy and personalized treatment strategies for cancer patients. 
In Sweden, the initiative is coordinated by Umeå University, with significant contributions from Region Västerbotten, Uppsala University (SciLifeLab), Linköping University, and Karolinska Institutet.  These institutions are instrumental in providing access to high-quality imaging data and clinical expertise, ensuring that the platform is both clinically relevant and scientifically robust. Vinnova, Sweden's innovation agency, is co-funding the Swedish participation, with a total investment of SEK 12.4 million allocated to the project.

items.title: Development of the state cloud ICT infrastructure
items.org: Lithuanian Ministry of the Economy and Innovation
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This project is aimed at the creation of the main infrastructure for cloud ICT for the provision of cloud services.

Lithuania is developing a State Cloud Services Infrastructure as part of its broader digital transformation strategy. The initiative is designed to provide a centrally managed and secure cloud platform for public sector institutions, enabling the migration of state IT systems to a unified environment. This is expected to enhance service reliability, improve cost-efficiency, and ensure consistent standards for data security and management across government systems.

items.title: Development of a data management model
items.org: Lithuanian Ministry of the Economy and Innovation
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The reform of public sector data management is set to yield a national data model describing the data stored in every public IT system, help increase the overall data maturity level, allow institutions to exchange data more efficiently and accelerate the implementation of digitisation solutions and the development of digital services in the public sector.

Lithuania is reforming public-sector data management by creating a unified national data model and catalogue covering all state IT systems. Led by the Ministry of the Economy and Innovation and the State Data Agency, the reform aims to improve data maturity, streamline exchange between institutions, and accelerate digital service delivery. Key steps include developing a central data catalogue, setting quality standards for open datasets, and building a shared “data lake” for public institutions.

items.title: Development and implementation of the National Digital Platform for Medical Diagnostics
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This platform is designed to improve of diagnostics and treatment of socially important diseases. It is also expected to facilitate communication between healthcare professionals and other relevant stakeholders.

This platform aims to improve the diagnosis and treatment of diseases that have a major impact on society. Many such diseases require fast, accurate care, but communication between healthcare professionals and other stakeholders can be slow or fragmented. By providing a digital space for easier and faster sharing of information, the platform supports better coordination of care and more informed decision-making.
It connects doctors, nurses, researchers, public health officials, and patient groups, allowing them to exchange data, discuss cases, and share best practices securely. This helps speed up diagnosis, improve treatment quality, and develop new approaches to managing important diseases.
The platform is designed to grow over time by adding more users, covering more conditions, and integrating new technologies like AI and telemedicine. Ultimately, it aims to become a key tool for improving healthcare outcomes across regions.

items.title: Dataspace4Health
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Dataspace4Health project aims to transform Luxembourg’s healthcare by creating a secure platform for health data sharing, enhancing patient care through improved diagnosis, treatment, and prevention while respecting GDPR and patient rights.

The Dataspace4Health project presents several key strengths. First, it is a flagship Gaia-X candidate in the healthcare domain for Europe, setting the standard for secure and compliant health data exchange across the continent. It fully supports the goals of the international precision health initiative Clinnova, coordinated by the Luxembourg Institute of Health (LIH).

Secondly, the platform is a collaborative effort led by a consortium of industry and domain leaders and remains open to new members. Third, it aims to explore and unlock new medical treatments through data and AI. Finally, the ecosystem is use-case-driven and has been validated through initial use cases in the fields of diabetes and oncology, paving the way for future applications in other healthcare areas.

Diabetes affects more than half a billion people worldwide, and this number is projected to reach 783 million by 2045. Diabetes is not a uniform disease (e.g., type 1, type 2), and it leads to various complications that require personalized care. AI is considered a promising technology to help prevent these complications. In one use case, a reliable AI-based decision support system—fed by thousands of anonymized patient records and digital twins from LIH—delivers personalized treatment to help prevent complications.

Cancer is the second leading cause of death in many countries, following cardiovascular diseases. Each year, cancer affects tens of millions of people globally, with more than half dying from the disease. While hospitals are responsible for diagnosis and therapy, researchers contribute with new solutions, treatments, and insights into disease mechanisms in the oncology field. The primary goal of this use case is to implement a precision oncology program and a federated data architecture, enabling better interoperability and data exchange between healthcare providers and research institutions.

items.title: Data-Driven Innovation Strategy for the Development of a Trusted and Sustainable Economy in Luxembourg
items.org: The Government of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg - Ministry of the Economy
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Luxembourg’s strategy to boost a trusted and sustainable data economy through infrastructure, advanced digital technologies, and supportive regulation.

Led by the Ministry of Economy, Luxembourg's data-driven innovation strategy is built on three key pillars: 
i) enhancing digital infrastructure capacity, 
ii) promoting the experimentation and integration of advanced digital technologies into industry, and 
iii) ensuring a robust regulatory, intellectual property, investment, and financing framework.

There has been a request to renew the national data strategy, recognizing that AI and data are deeply interconnected. On the Ministry for Digitalization’s side, significant progress is being made on a public data strategy, which is set to be published in 2025. The key question remains whether this will be a standalone strategy or part of a broader national data framework.

items.title: Data – an underutilized resource for Sweden
items.original_name: Data – en underutnyttjad resurs för Sverige
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Data – en underutnyttjad resurs för Sverige
items.body:
This strategy, created as part of the governments innovation program in collaboration with industry, aimed at increased access to data for e.g. artificial intelligence and digital innovation. There were seven directly related government commissions to a number of government agencies, financed by the National Innovation Council. All commissions/tasks are completed as of 2024, and the Agency for Digital government has a long-term task to coordinate data-driven innovation.

Sweden's national data strategy, titled Data – an underutilized resource for Sweden, was introduced in 2021 as part of the government's innovation program. Developed in collaboration with industry stakeholders, the strategy aims to enhance access to data, particularly to support advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) and digital innovation. Recognizing data as a critical asset, the strategy seeks to unlock its potential to drive economic growth, improve public services, and foster innovation across various sectors.
To implement this strategy, the Swedish government issued seven specific commissions to various government agencies, coordinated by the National Innovation Council. These commissions focused on developing the necessary infrastructure and frameworks to facilitate secure and efficient data sharing and utilization. As of 2024, all assigned tasks have been completed, marking a significant milestone in Sweden's data-driven transformation.
A key component of this initiative is the role of the Agency for Digital Government (DIGG), which has been tasked with coordinating data-driven innovation efforts across the public sector. DIGG's responsibilities include overseeing the implementation of shared data platforms, establishing data governance standards, and promoting the use of open data to stimulate innovation and improve public services. The agency's work ensures that data is utilized responsibly and effectively, aligning with Sweden's digitalization goals.

items.title: Data dissemination and management platform (DAGR)
items.org: Society Integration Foundation Republic of Latvia
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
​DAGR is a next-generation data exchange and governance platform enabling secure data sharing across government, business, and citizen interactions. It will consolidate all government data sources into a single access point by 2030, streamlining public sector operations and reducing administrative burdens. The platform will also support emerging digital initiatives such as the European Digital Identity Wallet and AI training.

DAGR (Data Dissemination and Management Platform) is Latvia’s planned next-generation data governance infrastructure. The platform is designed to enable secure data sharing among government bodies, businesses, and citizens, consolidating multiple government data sources into a single access point by 2030.
By streamlining public sector data access and reducing administrative overhead, DAGR seeks to make government services more efficient and integrated. It also intends to support emerging programmes like the European Digital Identity Wallet and AI training initiatives, giving them a foundational data environment to build on.

items.title: Coordinated and secure government IT operations
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
A number of public authorities are collaborating on IT services through the Swedish Social Insurance Agency's IT department to the conditions for the digitalisation of operation.

Sweden's Coordinated and Secure Government IT Operations initiative, known as Samordnad och säker statlig it-drift, is a collaborative effort led by the Swedish Social Insurance Agency (Försäkringskassan) to enhance the digital infrastructure of public authorities. This initiative aims to provide secure, sovereign, and resilient IT services tailored for the public sector.
Key Components:
Digital Collaboration Platform (SAFOS): Developed as part of the initiative, SAFOS is a collaboration platform designed for Swedish government agencies. It delivers digital sovereign and resilient IT services, built on top of open-source technologies to ensure accessibility and security. Nextcloud Service: Försäkringskassan offers Nextcloud as a service to public authorities, facilitating secure file sharing and collaboration. This service is delivered within the framework of the agency's assignment to ensure coordinated and secure state IT systems. esamverka.sePrivate Cloud Solutions: The agency utilizes a private cloud infrastructure to manage its IT operations, ensuring that data remains within Swedish borders and complies with national security standards. Strategic Objectives:
Digital Sovereignty: By developing and managing its own IT services, Sweden aims to maintain control over its digital infrastructure, reducing dependency on external providers.Interagency Collaboration: The initiative fosters collaboration among various public authorities, enabling them to share resources and best practices, thereby enhancing overall efficiency.Security and Compliance: Ensuring that all IT services meet stringent security requirements and comply with national regulations is a fundamental aspect of the initiative.

items.title: Clinnova
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Clinnova’s mission is to advance precision medicine by using AI-driven solutions to provide tailored treatments for patients, focusing initially on inflammatory bowel disease, rheumatoid disease, and multiple sclerosis. The initiative aims to bridge biomedical research and healthcare by creating an interoperable infrastructure for federated health data across Europe, driving innovation and supporting Luxembourg's personalised healthcare goals.

Covering the Greater Region with core partners including Grand Est in France, Baden-Württemberg in Germany, Basel in Switzerland, and Luxembourg, Clinnova stands as a beacon of opportunity for digital and translational medicine at the heart of Europe. The program is set to pioneer integrated digital AI-driven health solutions that transcend borders, promising a shift towards personalised, sustainable and preventative healthcare systems.
The mission of Clinnova is to support the digitalisation of healthcare and precision medicine by creating a data-enabling environment for accessing, sharing and analysing interoperable, high-quality health data. We want to improve patient care and accelerate biomedical research through an increase in patient-oriented application.

items.title: Clarence
items.org: Joint venture between Proximus Luxembourg, LuxConnect and the Ministry of Digitalisation
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Clarence, a joint venture between Proximus Luxembourg, a leader in convergent ICT and telecom services, and LuxConnect, offers a sovereign, fully disconnected cloud solution tailored for governments, regulated industries, international organizations, and enterprises handling sensitive data in Europe. Its core mission is to deliver an innovative cloud solution that ensures the highest levels of confidentiality, security, and operational autonomy.

Clarence is a Luxembourg sovereign cloud operated by a joint venture between LuxConnect and Proximus Luxembourg. It offers an air-gapped (“disconnected”) cloud—installed in LuxConnect Tier IV data centres in Luxembourg—that is locally managed and kept isolated from the internet and third parties, with the goal of ensuring EU-only jurisdiction, data residency, and operational sovereignty. The platform is built on Google’s Distributed Cloud Hosted technology (sovereign controls without external operator access) and targets government and regulated sectors needing confidential workloads, including AI.

items.title: Centre of Excellence for Data Sharing and Cloud (CoE-DSC)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The CoE-DSC was established to overcome challenges in data sharing, such as building trust, ensuring regulatory compliance, and defining governance structures. It supports the development of "data spaces," which allow organizations to securely exchange data across sectors. These data spaces, such as the Smart Connected Supplier Network and HDN, have the potential to drive innovation and economic growth.

The mission is to unlock the true value of data sharing by supporting organisations in realising scalable data spaces, the next evolutionary concept in data sharing. Through the development of generic building blocks and collaborative efforts, we enable easier and cost-effective implementation of data spaces across sectors and geographies.

items.title: Bled Institute for Leadership in Digital Transformation and Artificial Intelligence (BILDAI)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Bled Institute for Leadership in Digital Transformation and AI (BILDAI), established by the IEDC-Bled School of Management in collaboration with Roche Slovenia, is dedicated to unlocking the transformative potential of artificial intelligence and digitalisation. BILDAI's primary mission is to cultivate leaders who are not only prepared to navigate the challenges of this new era but also empowered to shape its future.

The Bled Institute for Leadership in Digital Transformation and AI (BILDAI) was established in 2023 through a strategic partnership between the IEDC-Bled School of Management and Roche Slovenia. This initiative aims to harness the transformative potential of artificial intelligence (AI) and digitalization to cultivate leadership capable of navigating and shaping the evolving digital landscape.
Mission and Objectives:
BILDAI's core mission is to develop leaders equipped to lead in the digital era. The institute focuses on:
