Assessing AI's Impact: Evaluating the effects of AI across various sectors and capturing emerging trends.Research and Integration: Conducting research on AI integration within commercial, academic, and government organizations.Ethical and Regulatory Guidance: Providing guidance on ethical considerations and regulatory compliance for AI utilization.Strategy Development: Crafting effective strategies for AI deployment in management and decision-making processes.International Collaboration: Partnering with global research groups focusing on key AI studies.

items.title: BIFAP
items.org: Spanish Agency of Medicines and Medical Devices
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Electronic database made up of medical records from Primary Care destined for pharmacoepidemiologic studies and belonging to the Spanish Agency of Medicines and Medical Devices (AEMPS).

Spain's BIFAP (Base de Datos para la Investigación Farmacoepidemiológica en Atención Primaria) is an electronic database comprising anonymised medical records from primary care settings. Managed by the Spanish Agency of Medicines and Medical Devices (AEMPS), BIFAP serves as a critical resource for pharmacoepidemiological studies, enabling the evaluation of medication safety and effectiveness within the Spanish population.
Key Features:
Data Source: BIFAP aggregates anonymised clinical data from primary care physicians across Spain, focusing on medication prescriptions, patient demographics, and health outcomes.Research Applications: The database supports a wide range of pharmacoepidemiological research, including post-authorisation safety studies, risk-benefit analyses, and the identification of adverse drug reactions.Collaboration and Oversight: Developed and funded by AEMPS, BIFAP operates with the support of professional medical societies such as the Spanish Society of Family and Community Medicine (SEMFYC), the Spanish Society of Rural and General Medicine (SEMERGEN), and the Spanish Association of Primary Care Paediatrics (AEPAP). Scientific Advisory: A scientific committee oversees the project, ensuring methodological rigor and ethical compliance in research activities.International Collaboration: BIFAP collaborates with international pharmacoepidemiological research initiatives, contributing to global efforts in medication safety surveillance.

items.title: Advanced digitalisation – future solutions in Swedish industry
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This programme administered by Vinnova, Sweden’s innovation agency, supports approx. 100 innovation projects, including on secure data flows for applied AI edge technologies.

Sweden's Advanced Digitalisation Programme, administered by Vinnova, the Swedish innovation agency, is a strategic initiative aimed at fostering industrial innovation through digital transformation. The programme supports approximately 100 innovation projects, including those focused on secure data flows for applied AI edge technologies.
Key Aspects of the Programme:
Objective: To strengthen Swedish industry's competitiveness and technological leadership by mobilising and facilitating collaboration across various sectors.Focus Areas: The programme targets system-changing innovations in electrification, data flows, AI, and digital infrastructure to accelerate the industry's digital transformation.Funding Structure: The programme operates in three stages, with funding available for pre-studies and subsequent project phases, potentially up to SEK 50 million per year for six years. Collaboration: Projects are expected to be carried out in collaboration between at least two actors, including companies, universities, research institutes, and other relevant organizations. .Strategic Goals:
Digital Sovereignty: Developing secure and sovereign digital solutions tailored for Swedish industry.Intersectoral Collaboration: Fostering cooperation between public and private sectors to drive innovation.Sustainability: Aligning digital transformation efforts with environmental and societal sustainability goals.

items.title: Act on Health Data Use (GDNG)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The GDNG is a key enabler to facilitate the access to healthcare data for secondary use. Its measures include procedural simplifications on re-using health data across multiple states (Länder). It further provides a legal basis for healthcare institutions to re-use their patients‘ data for research, patient safety and quality assurance, and enables statutory health insurance funds to utilize data to improve the quality of care and to support AI applications.

Germany’s Health Data Use Act (GDNG) is intended to make secondary use of health data easier and more consistent. It introduces procedural simplifications for re-using data across federal states and sets out rules to streamline access for approved purposes.
The law provides a legal basis for healthcare institutions to re-use patient data for research, patient safety, and quality assurance, and it enables statutory health insurers to analyse data to improve care quality and to develop or support AI applications. Overall, it seeks to balance greater data availability with clear governance for compliant use.

items.title: AI-based assistance systems for in-process healthcare applications
items.org: Federal Ministry of Education and Research
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
In addition to the much-discussed potential in diagnostics, AI-based interactive systems can very effectively support processes in hospitals and comparable healthcare facilities and thus contribute to the improvement of medical, organizational and administrative processes. The aim of the projects in this funding measure is to research and develop AI-based assistance systems that lead to quantifiable and measurable improvements in clinical processes.

This funding measure seeks to advance the integration of AI into hospital operations by focusing on the development of assistance systems that can deliver measurable efficiency gains. Beyond clinical outcomes, the initiative emphasises improving workflows, reducing administrative burdens, and enhancing resource management in healthcare facilities. By targeting these systemic aspects, the programme aims to support more sustainable and effective healthcare delivery.

items.title: AI-assisted precision surgery in oncology
items.org: Federal Ministry of Education and Research
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Surgical interventions are a core element of multimodal treatment strategies for solid cancers and continue to play a central role in modern oncology. Artificial intelligence is expected to contribute to more personalised and precise approaches to cancer care, supporting clinical decisions before, during, and after surgery. The funding measure seeks to advance the precision of oncological surgery through the development and application of interactive AI technologies.

Germany’s Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF) has launched a funding measure that seeks to improve the precision of surgical treatment in oncology using interactive AI technologies. The call frames AI as a contributor to personalised, precision oncology before, during, and after surgery, reflecting surgery’s central role in multimodal cancer care.
The programme is designed to support R&D that advances AI-assisted planning, intra-operative support, and post-operative decision-making, with attention to clinical relevance, data quality, and patient safety. It encourages collaboration across medicine, research and industry so that validated solutions can progress toward use in practice.

items.title: AI-Supported Administrative Notification
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Within the AI-supported administration notification project, the possibilities for the automation of administrative processes using AI-supported solutions were examined as part of a feasibility survey. Three different use cases (handwriting recognition, translation, and knowledge management) were analysed on the basis of two Proof of Concepts and one Rapid Prototype.

Austria is exploring the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) to streamline public administration through the AI-Supported Administration Notification project. This initiative aims to enhance the efficiency and accessibility of government services by automating key administrative processes.
The project's primary objectives are to assess the feasibility of implementing AI-driven solutions in public administration and to identify areas where automation can lead to significant improvements. By focusing on specific use cases, the project seeks to demonstrate the practical benefits of AI in reducing manual workloads and accelerating service delivery.
Three distinct use cases were analysed: handwriting recognition, translation, and knowledge management. Each use case was evaluated through the development of two Proof of Concepts and one Rapid Prototype, allowing for a comprehensive assessment of AI's capabilities in these areas.
The outcomes of this project are expected to inform future AI applications in public administration, guiding the development of scalable solutions that can be integrated across various government departments.

items.title: AI Priority Research Program and Equipment (PEPR)
items.org: French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission (CEA), National Centre for Scientific Research (CNRS), and National Institute for Research in Digital Science and Technology (INRIA)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Within France’s 2030 strategy, this programme accelerates innovation in key fields, including AI in healthcare. By supporting foundational AI research, it drives advancements in medical imaging, predictive analytics, and therapeutic development. The programme also fosters digital health innovation through AI-powered personalised medicine and diagnostics, while encouraging collaboration between research institutions, healthcare providers, and industry.

This program is a powerful tool supporting the national AI strategy, already encompassing nine ambitious projects. It aims to tackle key and fundamental challenges in machine learning across three complementary pillars:
 
Trustworthy and Distributed AI
Through a multifaceted approach to trust, this axis integrates:
The development of robustness foundations using statistical approaches.The incorporation of formal methods for the specification, learning, and safety validation of AI modelsThe development of decentralized learning mechanisms that ensure security.The integration of causal models with machine learning to provide explainable, evidence-based capabilities.Frugal and Embedded AI
This involves deepening the theoretical and algorithmic foundations of machine learning to ensure data and computation frugality by design. It includes:
Advanced model optimization and training guided by hardware constraints.The design of dedicated AI hardware architectures that are modular, flexible, and adaptive.The exploration of physics-informed computational models.
New Mathematical Foundations of AI, particularly in the field of mathematical analysis, this pillar includes:
The integration of tools and advances from partial differential equations, optimal control, and optimal transport.To develop novel architectures with stable optimization schemes, efficient solvers and approximations.The analytical treatment of generative and diffusion methods.

items.title: WinGo Deposit
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The WinGo Deposit facility in Latvia uses machine vision and neural networks to sort recyclable materials, including PET and glass bottles, metal cans, tetra packs, and batteries. It helps improve recycling efficiency and reduce waste contamination. Future plans aim to expand its processing capabilities to additional waste types, such as shampoo bottles.

The WinGo Deposit initiative is a state-of-the-art waste sorting facility that leverages AI technologies, including machine vision and neural networks, to improve the accuracy and efficiency of recycling operations. By automatically identifying and sorting different types of recyclable materials, the facility reduces human error and increases the volume of correctly processed waste.
Key features and objectives include:
Sorting of multiple recyclable materials, including PET and glass bottles, metal cans, tetra packs, and batteriesIntegration of AI and machine learning to improve processing speed and accuracySupporting environmental sustainability by enhancing recycling and reducing landfill wasteFuture developments aim to:
Expand processing capabilities to additional waste types, such as shampoo bottles and other plasticsFurther optimise AI algorithms for higher accuracy and efficiencyServe as a model for smart waste management in Latvia and the broader region

items.title: Virtual civil servants
items.org: Ministry of Research, Innovation and Digitisation of Romania
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Two local communities have introduced 'virtual civil servants'. The creation of this 'civil servant,' based on artificial intelligence, is part of the digitisation process of procedures in the local public administration in Cluj. Galați City Hall also launched a virtual civil servant based on artificial intelligence. The virtual assistant is currently being trained and tested but will soon be able to provide information to citizens on town planning, taxes, fees, and other local revenues.

In Romania, several municipalities are experimenting with AI-based “virtual civil servants” as part of efforts to modernise local public administration. The initiative began in Cluj, where the system was introduced to support the digitisation of procedures and citizen services. Soon after, Galați City Hall launched its own version of the tool.

items.title: Various projects on decryption of logging sites
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Lithuanian State Forest Service (2021-2022) and the Environmental Protection Agency have conducted multiple successive projects using AI solutions to identify clear-cut forest areas as a result of logging.

Lithuania’s State Forest Service and the Environmental Protection Agency have run successive projects (2021–2022) that apply AI to detect clear-cut areas from logging. Using satellite and other remote-sensing imagery, models flag recent canopy loss so authorities can verify felling, monitor compliance, and update forest inventories faster.
These projects improve timeliness and consistency compared with manual mapping alone, and create a repeatable workflow the agencies can rerun after each logging season. The outputs feed into national monitoring and enforcement, with the aim to support more transparent, data-driven forest governance.

items.title: Use of AI in Business Intelligence System - Skrinja
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Ministry of Digital Transformation is planning to introduce AI-based predictive analytics into the Business intelligence system Skrinja (‘box’), which is used by different public authorities to analyse data about their policy area, like public sector salaries, public tenders and administrative procedures, supporting data-driven decisions in real time in public administration.

Slovenia’s Ministry of Digital Transformation is preparing to expand the country’s central business intelligence system, Skrinja, by integrating AI-driven predictive analytics. Skrinja already serves as a platform for public authorities to analyse data on areas such as public sector salaries, tenders, and administrative processes, helping improve oversight and efficiency. The planned upgrade seeks to move beyond descriptive analysis and enable real-time, forward-looking insights to support more effective, data-driven decision-making across public administration.

items.title: Transition 5.0 Plan
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Transition 5.0 Plan supports Italy’s move toward energy and environmental sustainability. It offers tax incentives for investments in energy-efficient digital infrastructure, smart manufacturing, and AI-driven resource optimisation. The initiative aims to reduce energy consumption while promoting renewable energy adoption.

The Transition 5.0 Plan is a national programme designed to accelerate Italy’s transition to sustainable and energy-efficient industrial and digital practices. It integrates environmental goals with technological innovation to support the green transformation of businesses.
Key objectives include:
Reducing energy consumption in industrial and digital operationsPromoting renewable energy adoption across sectorsSupporting investments in energy-efficient digital infrastructureEncouraging smart manufacturing and AI-driven optimisation of resourcesThe plan provides financial incentives, primarily in the form of tax breaks, to stimulate investments that align with environmental and sustainability targets. It fosters collaboration between companies, research institutions, and technology providers to ensure that AI and digital solutions are applied effectively in sustainable practices.

items.title: Technology Voucher Programme for Enterprises
items.org: National Research, Development and Innovation Office
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Scheduled for launch in 2024, this programme provides financial grants covering 60-80% of costs to Hungarian SMEs seeking to implement AI solutions. It aims to support up to 200 SMEs, facilitating the integration of AI technologies into business operations.

Hungary’s Innovation Voucher Programme, managed by the National Research, Development and Innovation Office (NRDI), is designed to help SMEs adopt new technologies, including AI. Launched in 2024, it offers financial grants covering 60–80% of project costs, lowering the barrier for smaller firms to test and integrate digital solutions.
The scheme is expected to support up to 200 SMEs, with funding directed at practical business applications such as process optimisation, data use, and automation. By backing concrete use cases, the programme aims to accelerate digital transformation across Hungary’s SME sector and strengthen competitiveness.

items.title: TEF-Health
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
TEF-Health is a European Testing and Experimentation Facility supporting AI validation and certification in the healthcare sector. It provides technical and scientific assistance to AI providers and notified bodies, aiming to accelerate AI solution development and market access while ensuring compliance with legal, ethical, quality, and interoperability standards. This initiative involves multidisciplinary teams focused on enhancing healthcare system efficiency, resilience, and sustainability.

Technological advances in the field of artificial intelligence (AI) offer new opportunities to support decision making in healthcare. Yet, new medical devices must first prove their safety and usefulness before they can be adopted in clinical practice. Concerningly, there is a lack of standardized procedures and testing infrastructure for developing, testing and certifying new medical AI products.
The EU project TEF-Health addresses this gap by establishing a European reference testing and experimentation facility (TEF) to ensure that the digital transformation of our healthcare system occurs safely and for the benefit of all. In this project, 50+ interdisciplinary partners from Europe work together to develop new regulatory testing procedures for this technology. These activities include for instance developing standardized testing protocols and certifications and a testing facility to test new tools in real or realistic environments. The newly created evaluation resources and infrastructure will be made available to industry in the future in the form of fee-based services.
In the project team Responsible Algorithms at the BIH QUEST Center, we contribute to the TEF-Health project by developing services to implement ethical requirements for developing trustworthy medical AI tools. In particular, we aim to develop standardized procedures to fulfil the ethical requirements of transparency and robustness, which will be offered as services to companies.

items.title: TAKEOFF Seed Fund Award
items.org: University of Malta & Ministry for the Economy, Enterprise & Strategic Projects (with MDIA)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The TAKEOFF Seed Fund Award (TOSFA) is a seed funding initiative established in 2014, aimed at fostering innovation by providing financial support to researchers and entrepreneurs. This joint initiative between the University of Malta and the Ministry for the Economy, Enterprise and Strategic Projects (MEEP) supports early-stage technology and start-up development by offering grants ranging from EUR 2 500 to EUR 25 000 per project, with a total allocation of EUR150,000 in 2023.

Malta’s TAKEOFF Seed Fund Awards (TOSFA)—a joint scheme of the University of Malta and the Ministry for the Economy, Enterprise and Strategic Projects (MEEP)—seeks to support early-stage tech and start-up development with small grants that help teams validate ideas and build first prototypes.
Since 2014, the programme has offered awards of €2,500–€25,000 per project (total pot €150,000 in 2023), aiming to bridge the gap between research and market by funding proof-of-concept, customer discovery, and initial go-to-market work.

items.title: Swiss Latvian Cooperation Programme – Pre-defined Programme Component in ICT and Smart Energy
items.original_name: Šveices–Latvijas sadarbības programma – iepriekš definēta programmas sastāvdaļa IKT un viedajā enerģētikā
items.org: Institute of Solid-State Physics, University of Latvia
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Šveices–Latvijas sadarbības programma – iepriekš definēta programmas sastāvdaļa IKT un viedajā enerģētikā
items.body:
The Swiss–Latvian Cooperation Programme supports research and innovation in smart grids and energy storage. AI-enabled tools will be developed for real-time stability assessment of the Baltic electricity grid, alongside improved materials for energy storage and hydrogen production. The initiative involves national research institutions, led by the Institute of Solid-State Physics at the University of Latvia.

The Swiss–Latvian Cooperation Programme – Pre-defined Programme Component in ICT and Smart Energy (2025–2029) aims to advance research and innovation in sustainable energy technologies. The programme focuses on improving the efficiency and stability of the Baltic electricity grid while supporting the development of advanced energy storage and hydrogen production materials.
Key objectives include:
Developing AI-enabled tools and models for real-time dynamic stability assessment of the electricity gridAdvancing energy storage technologies to support renewable integration and grid reliabilityPromoting innovative materials for hydrogen production to accelerate clean energy solutionsThe initiative is implemented by the Institute of Solid-State Physics at the University of Latvia, in collaboration with other national research institutions. By combining expertise from academia and research organisations, the programme seeks to create practical, deployable solutions for the region’s energy sector.

items.title: SustAInLivWork – Centre of Excellence (CoE) for Sustainable Living and Working
items.org: Kaunas University of Technology (coordinator) and partner universities
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The CoE will be specialised in the development and application of R&I solutions based on AI in the manufacturing, energy, health and transport sectors and to create an internationally connected Lithuanian AI cluster.

The Centre of Excellence (CoE) in Lithuania seeks to promote research and innovation with AI in strategic sectors: manufacturing, energy, health and transport. It is intended to act as a national hub, fostering collaboration among public, private and academic actors, while serving as a bridge to international partners.
A key aim is to build an internationally connected Lithuanian AI cluster, ensuring that local solutions can integrate with European and global networks, attract investment, and scale beyond national boundaries.

items.title: Supporting Health Data Access Bodies in Slovenia (SI-SUD)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The National Institute for Public Health started this project with the objective of enabling secondary use of data by developing four digital capabilities: Data Access Management System, National Metadata Catalogue, Secure Processing Environment and Quality labelling.

Slovenia is advancing its digital health infrastructure through the "Supporting Health Data Access Bodies in Slovenia" (SI-SUD) project, led by the National Institute of Public Health (NIJZ). This initiative aims to enhance the secondary use of health data for research, innovation, and policy-making, aligning with the European Health Data Space (EHDS) framework.

items.title: Support for Slovenian companies involved in the Chips JU
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Slovenia supports research and innovation projects within the tenders of the joint European Chips JU, as part of its measures to promote entrepreneurship from Ministry of Digital Transformation.

Slovenia is actively supporting research and innovation projects within the European Chips Joint Undertaking (Chips JU) as part of its broader strategy to promote entrepreneurship and technological advancement. The Ministry of Digital Transformation plays a pivotal role in facilitating these initiatives, ensuring alignment with national priorities and European objectives.

items.title: Support for Slovenian companies involved in IPCEI ME/CT
items.org: Ministry of the Economy, Tourism and Sport
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This measure of the Ministry of the Economy, Tourism and Sport aims at supporting companies involved in the important project of common European interest in microelectronics and communication technologies (IPCEI ME/CT) in carrying out R&D activities, including the first industrial deployment of pilot solutions, in the framework of R&D projects in the field of microelectronics, semiconductors, microchips and communication technologies.

Slovenia is actively supporting companies engaged in the Important Project of Common European Interest in Microelectronics and Communication Technologies (IPCEI ME/CT). The Ministry of the Economy, Tourism and Sport is facilitating this support through the STEP Slovenia platform, which provides financial incentives and advisory services to Slovenian companies participating in cross-border, multi-country projects. These projects involve collaboration with partners from various EU Member States and focus on areas such as microelectronics, semiconductors, microchips, and communication technologies. The aim is to strengthen Slovenia's position in the European semiconductor ecosystem and foster innovation-driven growth.

items.title: Start-up Finance Scheme
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The scheme provides financial support to innovative start-ups that demonstrate viable business concepts and a commitment to expanding their economic activities. In 2024, it allocated dedicated funding through various grants to support small start-ups undertakings and academic research in AI. The financial support is provided as a repayable advance.

The Startup Finance scheme, managed by Malta Enterprise, is designed to assist early-stage companies with innovative business ideas by providing repayable financial support. In 2024, the scheme dedicated resources specifically for start-ups and academic research working with AI, offering targeted grants to strengthen this sector.
By encouraging both entrepreneurial ventures and research-driven initiatives, the programme seeks to accelerate the growth of Malta’s start-up ecosystem and promote the application of AI and other emerging technologies in business.

items.title: Smart Cities Projects in Kozani, Trikala, Ioannina, Kalamata, Thessaloniki and Athens
items.original_name: Έργα Έξυπνων Πόλεων σε Κοζάνη, Τρίκαλα, Ιωάννινα, Καλαμάτα, Θεσσαλονίκη και Αθήνα
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Έργα Έξυπνων Πόλεων σε Κοζάνη, Τρίκαλα, Ιωάννινα, Καλαμάτα, Θεσσαλονίκη και Αθήνα
items.body:
The Smart Cities Projects in Kozani, Trikala, Ioannina, Kalamata, Thessaloniki, and Athens use AI technologies to improve urban planning and reduce emissions. They help cities optimize energy use, manage traffic, and monitor environmental quality. The projects involve collaboration between municipalities, technology providers, and research institutions.

The Smart Cities Projects are part of the broader initiative “100 Climate Neutral Cities by 2030”, which aims to make Greek cities more sustainable and resilient. The projects focus on integrating AI-driven solutions into urban management to reduce emissions, improve environmental quality, and enhance overall city livability.
Key objectives include:
Optimizing energy use across public buildings and infrastructureImproving waste management and reducing urban heat islandsMonitoring air quality and other environmental indicators in real-timeManaging traffic flow and public transportation more efficientlyThe projects are implemented through collaboration between municipalities, technology providers, and research institutions, ensuring that AI solutions are practical, scalable, and aligned with local needs. By leveraging advanced technologies, these initiatives aim to improve urban sustainability, citizen wellbeing, and climate resilience.

items.title: Smart Attica EDIH
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Smart Attica Digital Innovation Hub (EDIH) helps organisations develop and implement AI solutions for environmental challenges. It provides services such as training, testing technologies before investment, and building innovation networks. The initiative focuses on promoting sustainable and green technologies in Greece.

The Smart Attica Digital Innovation Hub (EDIH) is part of Greece’s network of Digital Innovation Hubs, designed to support businesses and public organisations in adopting AI and digital technologies. Its primary goal is to address environmental and sustainability challenges by providing practical support for AI solutions.
Key objectives include:
Offering training programmes to improve AI and digital skillsProviding testing facilities to trial technologies before investmentBuilding a regional innovation ecosystem that connects companies, research centres, and startupsThe hub focuses on sustainable and green technologies, encouraging innovations that can improve environmental outcomes while enhancing competitiveness. Through collaboration and guidance, it helps organisations reduce risks associated with AI adoption and accelerates the deployment of environmentally focused AI solutions.

items.title: Smart & Sustainable Investment Grant
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Smart & Sustainable Investment Grant provides business funding to support investments that lead to more sustainable processes, enhancing the competitiveness of enterprises through the optimisation of resource use in their activities. This includes initiatives such as sustainable digitisation. The service is offered by the DiHubMT.

The Smart & Sustainable Investment Grant, managed by Malta Enterprise, supports businesses in adopting greener and more efficient practices. It funds projects that improve competitiveness through better use of resources, while also promoting sustainability in business operations.
The scheme extends to areas like sustainable digitisation, enabling enterprises to modernise their processes in line with environmental and digital goals. Advisory and support are provided through DiHubMT, Malta’s Digital Innovation Hub.

items.title: Slovenian national strategy in semiconductor technologies and chips until 2030
items.org: The Ministry of Digital Transformation, the Ministry of Economy, Tourism and Sport, and the Ministry of Higher Education, Science and Innovation
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The strategy is being conducted under the auspices of the Ministry of Digital Transformation in association with two other ministries – the Ministry of Economy, Tourism and Sport, and the Ministry of Higher Education, Science and Innovation.

Slovenia has developed a national strategy for semiconductor technologies and chips, aiming to position the country as a significant player in this critical sector by 2030. This initiative is led by the Ministry of Digital Transformation in collaboration with the Ministry of Economy, Tourism and Sport, and the Ministry of Higher Education, Science and Innovation. 
The primary goal of Slovenia's semiconductor strategy is to strengthen its capabilities in semiconductor research, development, and manufacturing.

items.title: Slovenian national Competence centre for chips and semiconductors, and other support as part of the Chips Joint Undertaking (Chips JU)
items.org: Ministry of Digital Transformation and the Permanent Representation to the European Union Brussels
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
As part of the European Chips Joint Undertaking, Slovenia envisages the establishment of a consortium of public RTOs, which will manage the role of the Competence Centre for chips and semiconductors, to be located at the University of Maribor’s Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (FERI UM).

Slovenia is planning to create a consortium of public research and technology organizations (RTOs) as part of the European Chips Joint Undertaking. This consortium will serve as the Competence Centre for chips and semiconductors, providing expertise and support for research, development, and innovation in the sector. The centre will be based at the Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science at the University of Maribor (FERI UM), leveraging existing academic and research capacities. Its main goal is to strengthen Slovenia’s capabilities in semiconductor technologies and foster collaboration with European partners. The consortium will coordinate research projects, training programs, and industry engagement to support both national and EU-wide initiatives.

items.title: Signature Projects
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Signature Projects in Denmark test AI applications in the public sector to improve sustainability and reduce CO2 emissions. AI is applied in areas such as energy management, fleet optimisation, and flood forecasting. The projects aim to make public services more efficient and environmentally friendly.

The Signature Projects initiative was launched in 2020 to explore how AI technologies can improve public sector operations while contributing to climate and sustainability goals. The initiative supports testing and implementation of AI-driven solutions across multiple areas of municipal and public services.
Key focus areas include:
Energy optimisation of municipal buildings to reduce energy consumption and emissionsFleetOptimiser, which uses AI to manage municipal vehicle fleets efficiently and promote climate-smart drivingForecasting tools to support planning, mapping, and flood warnings in rural and urban areasOptimised building usage through AI to manage heating and resource allocationBy using AI to make operations more data-driven and efficient, the initiative aims to:
Reduce CO2 emissions across public sector activitiesSave resources and costs for municipalitiesProvide decision support tools for sustainable planning and service delivery

items.title: ROBUST
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The ROBUST consortium, initiated in 2022, is a 10-year research project focusing on reliable and trustworthy AI. Comprising 54 partners in AI labs, including knowledge institutions, private companies, and civil society organisations, ROBUST aims to enhance AI systems across five dimensions: accuracy, reliability, repeatability, resilience, and safety. It seeks to formalize AI reliability through contracts and develop methods to foster trust in AI systems.

The ROBUST consortium, which began in 2022, is a major European research effort spanning ten years that is designed to strengthen the reliability and trustworthiness of AI systems. With 54 partners drawn from universities, research institutions, industry, and civil-society organizations, the initiative brings together a wide spectrum of expertise. Its goal is to improve AI across five core dimensions: accuracy, reliability, repeatability, resilience, and safety. One important strand of work is to formalize notions of reliability in AI using flexible contracts or guarantees, so that users and developers can trust behaviour in changing environments. The consortium also develops methods, tools, and frameworks aimed at building trust—for instance by making AI decisions more interpretable, robust to faults, and verifiable.

items.title: Programme to support edge technologies (as part of UNICO IPCEI subsidy programme)
items.org: Ministry for Digital Transformation and the Civil Service
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Subsidies granted to actions aimed at supporting Spain's contribution to Important Projects of Common European Interest (IPCEI), including IPCEI on Next Generation Cloud Infrastructure and Services (IPCEI CIS) - provide competitive and fair access to next-generation cloud and edge capabilities.

Spain is actively participating in the European Union's Important Project of Common European Interest on Next Generation Cloud Infrastructure and Services (IPCEI-CIS). This initiative aims to develop a sovereign, interoperable cloud and edge computing infrastructure across Europe. Spain's involvement includes significant investments in national projects led by companies such as Telefónica, OpenNebula, and Arsys.

items.title: Programme for Modern Enterprises
items.org: Hungarian Chamber of Commerce and Industry
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Implemented by the Hungarian Chamber of Commerce and Industry, this programme assists SMEs in their digital transformation by providing resources and guidance on digital tools and technologies, including AI. It offers personalised IT audits, access to accredited IT suppliers, information on funding opportunities, thematic events, and a digital knowledge repository.

The “Vállalkozz Digitálisan!” programme, run by the Hungarian Chamber of Commerce and Industry (MKIK), supports SMEs in adopting digital technologies as part of their transformation journey. It provides tailored services such as personalised IT audits, recommendations, and connections to accredited IT suppliers.
The initiative also gives businesses access to a digital knowledge repository, organizes thematic events and training, and shares information on available funding opportunities. By combining practical guidance with direct support, it helps SMEs integrate tools including AI into their operations more effectively.

items.title: Plan to Promote Sectoral Data Spaces
items.original_name: Plan de Impulso de los Espacios de Datos Sectoriales
items.org: Plan de Impulso de los Espacios de Datos Sectoriales
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Plan de Impulso de los Espacios de Datos Sectoriales
items.body:
The Ministry for the Digital Transformation and Civil Service has presented an ambitious Plan for the Promotion of Sectorial Data Spaces. Its objective is to foster innovation and improve competitiveness and added-value in all economic sectors, promoting the deployment of data spaces where data can be securely shared. Thanks to them, companies, and the economy in general, will be able to benefit from the full potential of a European data single market.

Spain has introduced an ambitious initiative to enhance data-driven innovation across its economy through the "Plan for the Promotion of Sectoral Data Spaces." Led by the Ministry for Digital Transformation and Civil Service, this plan aims to establish secure, interoperable data ecosystems in key sectors such as healthcare, mobility, agriculture, and tourism. By facilitating the sharing of data among businesses and public entities, the plan seeks to unlock the full potential of a European data single market, fostering innovation and improving competitiveness.

items.title: Pladenj (System for Standardized Execution of Electronic Data Queries)
items.org: Ministry of Public Administration of the Republic of Slovenia
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
In December 2023, the platform Pladenj, a common central data exchange platform to facilitate seamless data and document exchange across many diverse systems and life events within the public administration, which since 2018 employs advanced AI machine learning techniques (to distribute network traffic for rush hour events between the application servers and their visitors), was upgraded to support cross-border exchanges in alignment with the EU Single Digital Gateway Regulation.

Slovenia’s Pladenj platform serves as the central hub for data and document exchange across public administration systems, helping to streamline processes tied to key life events. Since 2018, it has used AI and machine learning to manage heavy traffic loads during peak periods, improving system efficiency and reliability. In December 2023, the platform was upgraded to enable cross-border exchanges, aligning national digital services with the EU Single Digital Gateway Regulation and supporting more integrated public services across the EU.

items.title: PERTE Chip Semiconductor Ecosystem
items.original_name: Proyecto Estratégico de Microelectrónica y Semiconductores
items.org: Presidency of the Government of Spain
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Proyecto Estratégico de Microelectrónica y Semiconductores
items.body:
PERTE Chip aims to strengthen the design and production capabilities of the microelectronics and semiconductor industry in Spain and promote national and EU strategic autonomy in this sector, in line with the EU Chip Law. Its 4 strategic axes cover the entire value chain of the industry in different phases: conception, design, production of chips and manufacturing ICT electronic products, so that it acts as a generator of demand for the microchips produced and boosts the semiconductor ecosystem.

The following actions will be carried out:
- Strengthening scientific capacity. 
- Strengthen R&D&I on cutting-edge microprocessors and alternative architectures and integrated photonics, developing quantum chips and launching a line of financing to strengthen the Important European Project of Common Interest (IPCEI) on Microelectronics and Communication Technologies. 
- Design strategy. 
- Enhance Spanish capacity in microprocessor design through the creation of fabless companies for the design of cutting-edge microprocessors and alternative architectures; test pilot lines; semiconductor training network. 
- Construction of manufacturing plants. 
- To equip the national semiconductor production capacity for the manufacture of cutting-edge technology (below 5 nm) and mid-range (over 5 nm). 
- Boosting the ICT manufacturing industry. It includes actions such as the creation of a capital fund focused on chips to finance startups, scaleups and innovative SMEs in the national semiconductor sector, with an initial public allocation of 200 million euros. It is also aimed at strengthening the internal production of electronic product manufacturing – which uses microchips as an input – so that it acts as a driver for the semiconductor industry and absorbs part of its production.

items.title: OcéanIA Challenge
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The OcéanIA Challenge develops AI and mathematical modeling tools to improve understanding of the ocean. It focuses on the ocean’s structure, dynamics, and role in regulating the biosphere. The initiative also supports efforts to combat climate change.

The OcéanIA Challenge is a French initiative designed to advance scientific knowledge of the ocean through the application of AI and mathematical models. By analysing complex oceanic data, the initiative seeks to better understand the structure, functioning, and underlying mechanisms of the ocean and its ecosystems.
Key objectives include:
Developing AI-based tools for ocean observation, modelling, and predictionEnhancing knowledge of the ocean’s role in regulating the biosphereSupporting research that contributes to climate change mitigation and environmental protectionThe initiative encourages collaboration between research institutions, universities, and technology developers to ensure that AI tools are both scientifically rigorous and practically applicable. By combining cutting-edge AI with oceanography, OcéanIA helps inform policies and strategies related to climate adaptation and marine conservation.

items.title: Next Generation Energy Systems (NexSys)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Next Generation Energy Systems (NexSys) project develops pathways toward a net-zero energy system in Ireland. It uses AI in the Cities & Communities hub to analyse geospatial and sensor data for smarter energy use. The project combines big data analysis and citizen science to improve energy efficiency at neighbourhood and city levels.

The NexSys collaborative project aims to accelerate Ireland’s transition to a net-zero energy system by integrating research across five key areas:
Energy SystemsWaterTransportCities & Communities (CC)Offshore WindWithin the Cities & Communities hub, AI is applied to the Earth Observation Big Data work package to:
Mine geospatial data, including satellite imageryLeverage data from in-situ sensors to identify clusters of energy consumersEnable energy sharing, where the waste energy of one user can be repurposed as a resource for another, improving neighbourhood efficiencyThe initiative combines top-down big data mining with bottom-up citizen science activities, feeding into AI-augmented monitoring and decision-support tools. This approach helps communities optimise energy use, reduce waste, and support informed decision-making at both local and regional levels.

items.title: National Competence Centre SLING
items.org: Co-funded by the Ministry of Higher Education, Science and Innovation under EuroHPC JU coordination
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The National Competence Centre SLING helps users and in using High Performance Computing (HPC) to learn, access, use and learn about supercomputing.

The National Competence Centre SLING's mission is to promote the use of supercomputing capabilities for scientific and industrial research, academia and public service delivery. It was formed in the framework of the EuroCC project “National Competence Centres in the EuroHPC” and continues its activities in the EuroCC 2 project.

items.title: Memorandum with the Artificial Intelligence Center Hamburg (ARIC)
items.org: Riga Technical University, RTU Riga Business School, Latvian IT Cluster
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This partnership between Latvia’s Riga Technical University, RTU Riga Business School, and the Latvian IT Cluster with ARIC aims to enhance digital innovation in the logistics sector through AI. The collaboration focuses on advancing AI applications in supply chain management, automation, and optimisation while strengthening cross-border research and technology deployment.

The partnership between Riga Technical University, RTU Riga Business School, the Latvian IT Cluster, and the Artificial Intelligence Center Hamburg (ARIC) seeks to ensure stronger use of AI in the logistics sector. It is designed to promote digital innovation by focusing on AI applications for supply chain management, automation, and optimisation.
The collaboration also strengthens cross-border research and technology deployment, linking Latvia’s innovation ecosystem with Germany’s expertise in applied AI. By pooling resources and knowledge, the initiative aims to accelerate adoption of AI solutions in logistics and related industries.

items.title: Measures to reinforce Spain’s HPC capacity for AI development
items.org: Ministries for Digital Transformation and Public Function and Science, Innovation and Universities
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Several measures including: reinforcing capacity at Barcelona Supercomputing Center (BSC-CNS) so the MareNostrum 5 supercomputer exceeds 450 Pflops, making this capacity available to industry actors (objective of 20%), and reinforcing the Spanish HPC network.

Spain is enhancing its digital infrastructure by investing in the Barcelona Supercomputing Center's (BSC-CNS) MareNostrum 5 supercomputer. This initiative is part of the Spanish government's broader strategy to bolster artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities and support the digital transformation of the economy.

items.title: Measure for start-ups and spin-offs in the Vilnius region to develop innovative solutions and products in AI, blockchain technology and robotics process automation
items.org: Ministry of the Economy and Innovation of the Republic of Lithuania
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This measure aims to develop innovative solutions and products in AI, blockchain technology and robotics process automation (by the start-ups and spin-offs in the Vilnius region).

Lithuania’s Ministry of Economy and Innovation (EIMIN) has a measure that aims to support start-ups and university spin-offs in the Vilnius region to develop products in AI, blockchain, and robotic process automation. The call highlights use cases ranging from virtual assistants to autonomous recognition systems, seeking to accelerate commercialization and uptake of these technologies.
By providing additional funding, the programme seeks to ensure early-stage teams can build, test, and bring solutions to market, strengthening the local deep-tech ecosystem and creating spillovers for industry and public services.

items.title: MEGALITH project
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The MEGALITH project uses AI models to study and protect Malta’s megalithic temples. The models predict stone degradation under different weather and climate scenarios. This helps preserve these historic sites for future generations.

The MEGALITH project is a research initiative focused on preserving Malta’s ancient megalithic temples through the use of AI and simulation techniques. By training AI models on historical and simulated data, the project can predict how stones will degrade under varying meteorological conditions and climate change scenarios.
Key objectives include:
Assessing environmental impacts on megalithic structuresPredicting stone degradation over time to inform conservation strategiesSupporting preservation planning with data-driven insightsThe project combines expertise from heritage conservation, AI, and environmental science. The AI models allow researchers and policymakers to evaluate the effectiveness of preservation measures before implementation, reducing risks and costs.

items.title: Luxembourg National Research Fund
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Luxembourg National Research Fund provides a variety of research funding instruments that, while not exclusively focused on AI, are available to support AI-based projects. These include fellowships, PhD grants, and funding for companies looking to adopt innovative technologies.

Luxembourg’s National Research Fund (FNR) offers funding instruments that can support AI-based research and innovation, even though they aren’t AI-exclusive. Programmes span individual fellowships, PhD/doctoral training, bilateral/international schemes, and industry-oriented instruments that help companies adopt innovative technologies.
These calls seek to support projects from early-career researchers to collaborative R&D with firms, enabling AI work in areas such as health, finance, manufacturing, and public services—subject to each scheme’s scope and evaluation criteria.

items.title: Latvian National Center for Artificial Intelligence
items.org: State Chancellery of Latvia / Ministry of Economics
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The centre aims to advance AI adoption in Latvia by fostering collaboration between the public sector, private sector, and universities. Its objectives include pooling resources to drive AI innovation, supporting high-potential AI initiatives aligned with national interests, enhancing public AI literacy and access, and ensuring ethical, responsible AI use. The centre is expected to play a key role in AI research, education, and policy development.

The National Artificial Intelligence Centre in Latvia seeks to strengthen the country’s AI ecosystem by bringing together the public sector, private sector, and universities. Its role is to pool resources to stimulate innovation, back high-potential projects that align with national priorities, and make AI more accessible to citizens and businesses.
Beyond supporting research and commercial initiatives, the centre also aims to raise public AI literacy, promote ethical and responsible use, and contribute to policy development.

items.title: LIFE
items.org: Luxembourg's National Research Fund Green Era Hub
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The LIFE project focuses on creating climate-resilient, water-efficient, and self-sustainable agri-food systems. As climate change threatens food security, the project emphasises sustainable techniques like hydroponics and locally sourced fertilisers. It transforms animal manure into nutrient solutions for hydroponic farming, with Digital Twin technology optimising this process to increase efficiency and reduce resource consumption.

The LIFE project, led by the Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology (LIST), develops models for climate-resilient and water-efficient agri-food systems. It responds to growing pressures on food security by testing sustainable practices that reduce dependency on external inputs and improve resource efficiency.
A core element is the use of hydroponic farming, supported by nutrient solutions derived from recycled animal manure. This circular approach reduces waste while providing local fertiliser alternatives. The project also applies Digital Twin technology to simulate and optimise processes, ensuring that hydroponic systems use water, energy, and nutrients as efficiently as possible.

items.title: Irish Centre for High-End Computing (ICHEC)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
ICHEC organised the second European Quantum Technologies Conference in 2021. It is also part of the flagship project NEASQC (Next Applications of Quantum Computing), and it participates in the European High Performance Computing project HPCQS (High Performance Computer-Quantum Simulator).

The Irish Centre for High-End Computing (ICHEC) is Ireland’s national centre for high-performance computing and plays an active role in Europe’s quantum technology landscape. In 2021, it hosted the second European Quantum Technologies Conference, bringing together researchers, policymakers, and industry to explore advances in quantum computing and its applications.
ICHEC is also a partner in major European projects, including NEASQC (Next Applications of Quantum Computing), which develops near-term quantum computing use cases, and HPCQS (High Performance Computer–Quantum Simulator), which connects supercomputers with quantum simulators to explore hybrid computing solutions. Through these initiatives, ICHEC seeks to strengthen Ireland’s contribution to cutting-edge computing research and innovation at the European level.

items.title: IoT Connectivity Platform
items.org: Slovenia’s Ministry of Digital Transformation and The Agency for Communication Networks and Services
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
In 2023 an IoT Connectivity Platform pilot project was implemented, which was intended for users from the state administration. Technically it focuses on a key challenge, i.e. how to connect various IoT end devices like sensors, actuators, meters, dedicated devices,

The purpose of the IoT Connectivity Platform is to provide some sort of common denominator for all these various end devices by enforcing NGSI-LD specifications through the use of the FIWARE Context Broker central building block.

items.title: InoStartas, InoBranda ir InoPazanga
items.org: Ministry of Economy & Innovation, Republic of Lithuania
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Under these measures 47 projects are being implemented to develop AI solutions (by the companies in the middle-west region of Lithuania).

Lithuania runs several innovation support schemes to drive AI development. Under InoPažanga and InoBranda, 47 projects are underway in the middle-west region, with companies developing AI-based solutions aimed at scaling competitive products and services.
Alongside these, Inostartas specifically targets early-stage start-ups, offering co-financed grants to help transform ideas into prototypes or minimum viable products. The measure seeks to ensure that small firms can carry out R&D, validate markets, and prepare for certification or IP protection, laying the groundwork for commercialisation and follow-on investment.

items.title: Innovation Center for Artificial Intelligence (ICAI)
items.org: University of Amsterdam and Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
ICAI aims to position the Netherlands as a leader in AI knowledge and talent development. It aims to create a national AI ecosystem, leverage AI expertise across sectors, nurture academic and industry partnerships, and to ensure the sustainable use of AI resources.

The Innovation Center for Artificial Intelligence (ICAI) is a national initiative designed to strengthen the Netherlands’ role in AI research and talent development. It builds collaborative labs across universities, research institutes, and companies, where applied AI research is carried out on real-world challenges in fields such as healthcare, mobility, finance, and public services.
Through this structure, ICAI seeks to train the next generation of AI experts, retain talent within the country, and promote responsible AI use aligned with ethical and societal values.

items.title: Innovation Aid for SMEs Scheme
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Innovation Aid for SMEs Scheme provides grants to SMEs aiming to enhance their innovation performance. This includes projects leading to product, process, and organisational innovation through collaboration with Research & Knowledge-dissemination Organisations and access to innovation advisory and support services. This service is offered by the DiHubMT.

The Innovation Aid for SMEs Scheme, run by Malta Enterprise, supports small and medium-sized enterprises looking to strengthen their innovation capacity. It provides grants for projects that lead to new products, processes, or organisational improvements, while encouraging collaboration with Research & Knowledge-dissemination Organisations (RDIs).
The scheme also gives SMEs access to advisory and support services through DiHubMT, Malta’s Digital Innovation Hub, ensuring businesses can integrate expert guidance into their innovation activities.

items.title: Inclusion of the climate or environmental dimensions of AI in education and training
items.original_name: Intégration des dimensions climatiques ou environnementales de l’IA dans l’éducation et la formation
items.org: Ministry of Higher Education, Research and Innovation
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Intégration des dimensions climatiques ou environnementales de l’IA dans l’éducation et la formation
items.body:
In France, several initiatives integrate climate and environmental aspects of AI into education and training. These include university programmes, MOOCs, and educational content on sustainable digital technologies. The goal is to raise awareness of the environmental impacts of AI and ICT among students and professionals.

France has developed multiple initiatives to include climate and environmental considerations in AI education and training. The initiatives aim to combine technical knowledge of AI with an understanding of its environmental and societal impacts, preparing students and professionals to make sustainable decisions in digital innovation.
Key initiatives include:
University of Rennes AI Cluster label: Focused on AI applications for environmental modelingMOOC on Environmental Impacts of Digital Technologies: Provides accessible online training on the ecological footprint of digital technologies“Towards Real Green IT”: Educational content promoting frugal and sustainable ICT practicesThese efforts support the broader objectives of sustainable AI development by raising awareness, providing educational resources, and integrating environmental concerns into AI research and practice. They also encourage collaboration between universities, research centres, and educators to embed sustainability in AI curricula.

items.title: IT Competence Centre project “Information and Communication Technology Competence Centre for Digitisation”
items.org: IT Competence Centre (Information Technology Competence Centre)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This research-driven initiative aims at advancing AI applications across different sectors. Key projects include: 
i) developing AI-driven governance solutions for software supply chain security;
ii) using AI to optimise retail discounts and stock management; and 
iii) AI/ML-driven analysis and classification of user-generated digital content to improve decision-making in digital environments.

This research-driven initiative, led by the Latvian IT Competence Centre seeks to push forward AI adoption in multiple domains. Its objectives include developing governance tools to secure software supply chains; applying AI to retail problems like pricing and inventory optimisation; and analysing user-generated content via AI/ML to support better decisions in digital platforms.

items.title: IPCEI-CIS project on Cloud Edge
items.org: Ministry of the Economy, Tourism and Sport
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The first Important Project of Common European Interest on cloud and edge computing, this project targets the development of the first interoperable and openly accessible European data processing ecosystem, the multi-provider cloud to edge continuum. It will develop data processing capabilities, and software and data sharing tools that enable federated, energy-efficient and trustworthy cloud and edge distributed data processing technologies and related services.

11 companies from Slovenia are included in the consortium as indirect partners. The Ministry of Economy, Tourism and Sport has issued a call is to encourage Slovenian companies involved in the project of common European interest on a common European data and services infrastructure - the Next Generation Cloud Infrastructure and Services Project (IPCEI CIS) to carry out R&D activities, including the first industrial deployment of pilot solutions, in the framework of R&D projects in the field of cloud services and data infrastructures.

items.title: IPCEI on Microelectronics and Communication Technologies (IPCEI ME/CT)/ Project FANFARE
items.org: Department of Enterprise, Trade and Employment
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Investment by the State in Analog Devices Inc.’s Project FAN-FARE. Minister Coveney welcomes the European Commission’s approval of Government supported semiconductor investment.

The Department of Enterprise, Trade and Employment announced state support for Analog Devices Inc.’s Project FAN-FARE, a semiconductor investment that has also been cleared by the European Commission under EU state aid rules. The initiative is part of Ireland’s effort to anchor high-value semiconductor activity and align with Europe’s broader strategy to strengthen capacity in critical technologies.
The investment seeks to ensure that Ireland contributes to the development of advanced manufacturing and research in semiconductors while reinforcing its position within the European technology ecosystem.

items.title: I-NERGY
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The I-NERGY tool is an AI-driven platform that supports smart and optimized energy management. It unifies energy-related data and facilitates efficient data exchange. The tool helps improve energy efficiency and enhances predictive capabilities in energy management.

The I-NERGY initiative in Latvia aims to advance integrated and AI-powered energy management across the energy sector. By centralizing and unifying energy-related information, the platform enables better decision-making for energy providers, regulators, and large-scale consumers.
Key objectives of I-NERGY include:
Supporting integrated and optimized energy management using AI algorithmsFacilitating data exchange among energy stakeholders to improve coordinationEnhancing energy efficiency and predictive capabilities for more reliable energy planningPromoting smart energy solutions at both industrial and national levelsThe initiative fosters collaboration between energy companies, research institutions, and technology developers, ensuring that AI-driven solutions are practical, scalable, and aligned with Latvia’s energy goals.

items.title: Fit 4 Digital – AI
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
As of October 2024, an existing digitalisation support for SMEs has been augmented to focus on AI-specific measures. This program provides businesses with the opportunity to collaborate with an experienced AI consultant who will help identify challenges, set objectives, and prioritize development actions. The initiative includes a feasibility analysis of selected AI use cases, supported by a qualitative and quantitative review of internal data.

Luxembourg has augmented its SME digitalisation support with an AI-focused track run via Luxinnovation. It pairs companies with an experienced AI consultant who works to identify pain points, set objectives, and prioritise development actions—seeking to ensure AI efforts are targeted and realistic.
The service includes a feasibility analysis of chosen use cases, underpinned by a qualitative and quantitative review of internal data, so firms can decide whether to proceed to pilot or build. The approach aims to support SMEs in moving from exploration to concrete AI roadmaps with manageable next steps.

items.title: Experimental Regulatory Environments for AI
items.org: Authority for the Digitalization of Romania (ADR)
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
The Action Plan of Digital Transformation 2023-2026 includes the development of Experimental Regulatory Environments for AI. The first step of this project involved preparing a feasibility study for establishing an AI sandbox; the study proposed a set of legislative and technical tools, including a legal framework on the AI sandbox, necessary personnel capacities, and technical requirements. Based on this study, the preparatory phase of this pilot project is scheduled for 2025.

As part of Slovenia’s Action Plan for Digital Transformation 2023–2026, the government is preparing to establish experimental regulatory environments for AI. A feasibility study has already been carried out, outlining the legislative framework, staffing needs, and technical infrastructure required to set up an AI sandbox. Building on these findings, a pilot phase is planned for 2025, with the aim of testing how such a sandbox could support innovation while ensuring legal and technical safeguards are in place.

items.title: European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIH) in the Netherlands
items.org: Netherlands Enterprise Agency (RVO) & Ministry of Economic Affairs and Climate Policy
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Netherlands hosts six European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs), with five focusing on private-sector digitalisation and one on public-sector support. These hubs aim to accelerate AI and digital adoption in businesses and public services.

The Netherlands’ network of six European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs) provides tailored support for the digital transformation of both businesses and public institutions. Five hubs concentrate on advancing private-sector competitiveness, helping SMEs adopt AI, cloud, and data-driven technologies, while one hub is dedicated to public-sector innovation, guiding authorities in applying digital tools to improve services.
These hubs act as regional entry points into the EU-wide EDIH ecosystem, giving Dutch organisations access to expertise, testbeds, funding opportunities, and cross-border collaborations. They seek to lower barriers to AI uptake, ensuring that companies and public bodies alike can explore and implement trustworthy and efficient digital solutions.

items.title: European Digital Innovation Hubs
items.org: Institute of Electronics and Computer Science (EDI) as DAoL consortium lead
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Latvia is home to two European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs), which focus on accelerating AI adoption: First, Digital Accelerator of Latvia (DAoL) specialises in AI research and digital product development. Second, Latvian Digital Innovation Hub (EDIHLV) has established an Applied AI Knowledge Centre to analyse business processes and model AI implementation benefits. These hubs support AI-driven manufacturing, business process automation, and municipal digital transformation through training

Latvia hosts two European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs) that seek to ensure wider adoption of AI and digital technologies. The Digital Accelerator of Latvia (DAoL) focuses on AI research and digital product development, providing companies with expertise and tools to integrate advanced solutions. The second hub, EDIHLV, has established an Applied AI Knowledge Centre, which helps organizations analyses business processes and assess the potential benefits of AI implementation. Together, these hubs offer training and support in areas such as AI-driven manufacturing, process automation, and municipal digital transformation, contributing to Latvia’s broader digital transition.

items.title: Euro-Mediterranean Centre on Climate Change and the Cassandra supercomputer
items.original_name: Centro Euro-Mediterraneo sui Cambiamenti Climatici e il supercomputer Cassandra
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Centro Euro-Mediterraneo sui Cambiamenti Climatici e il supercomputer Cassandra
items.body:
The Euro-Mediterranean Centre on Climate Change (CMCC) is a research institution in Italy focused on climate variability and its socio-economic impacts. The deployment of the Cassandra supercomputer doubles CMCC’s computational capacity, enabling faster and more detailed climate simulations. This supports AI-driven climate research and strengthens CMCC’s role in tackling climate change challenges.

The Euro-Mediterranean Centre on Climate Change (CMCC), headquartered in Lecce, Italy, is a non-profit research organisation dedicated to studying climate variability and its impacts, with a particular focus on the Mediterranean region. CMCC brings together scientists, economists, and technicians to provide integrated analyses of climate effects on socio-economic systems.
To enhance research capabilities, CMCC has deployed the Cassandra supercomputer, which:
Doubles CMCC’s previous computational capacityEnables faster and more detailed climate simulationsSupports new AI applications in climate researchThe initiative’s objectives include:
Improving climate modelling and predictive accuracyEnabling AI-assisted analysis of climate impacts on socio-economic systemsStrengthening CMCC’s role as a regional and international hub for climate research

items.title: Establishment of Edge nodes indicators
items.org: Agency for Communication Networks and Services of the Republic of Slovenia (AKOS)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Slovenia is in the process of establishing indicator Edge nodes, in accordance with Article 5(1) of the Decision (EU) 2022/2481 in collaboration with the Agency of communication networks and services of the Republic of Slovenia.

Decision (EU) 2022/2481
Article 5
Monitoring of progress
1. The Commission shall monitor the progress of the Union towards the general objectives and the digital targets. To that end, the Commission shall rely upon DESI and shall set out, by means of an implementing act, the KPIs for each digital target. That implementing act shall be adopted in accordance with the examination procedure referred to in Article 23(2).

items.title: EDIH AI Boost
items.org: EDIH AI Boost (as part of the European Digital Innovation Hubs network)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
"One of seven Danish government-approved Research and Technology Organisations (GTS institutes), whose mission is to transfer research-based knowledge to industry and help drive innovation and growth in public and private organisations.
Provides research-based knowledge in the following areas:
•	Artificial intelligence (strong focus)
•	Computer vision
•	Cybersecurity
•	Digital sustainability
•	Digital health
•	IoT and smart products"

The AI Boost programme, hosted within one of Denmark’s seven government-approved Research and Technology Organisations (GTS institutes), is designed to transfer cutting-edge research knowledge into practical applications for industry and society. Its primary mission is to strengthen innovation capacity in both public and private organisations by bridging the gap between advanced research and real-world needs.
While the institute covers a broad range of digital technologies, it places a particular emphasis on artificial intelligence, supporting projects that explore AI applications across different sectors. Other areas of expertise include computer vision, cybersecurity, digital sustainability, digital health, and IoT/smart products, allowing companies to integrate AI in combination with complementary digital tools.

items.title: Disruptive Technologies Innovation Fund (DTIF)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
DTIF is a challenge-based fund established under Project Ireland 2040 and run with administrative support from Enter-prise Ireland. The types of projects that typically receive funding are partnerships to develop, deploy and commercialise disruptive technologies to transform business. AI relevant projects range from health-related applications of AI to technology, gaming and creative industries.

Ireland’s Disruptive Technologies Innovation Fund (DTIF) is a challenge-based funding programme created under Project Ireland 2040 and managed with support from Enterprise Ireland. It is designed to back collaborations that bring disruptive technologies from research into deployment and commercialisation, with a strong emphasis on projects that can transform business models and markets.
AI-related initiatives funded under DTIF cover a wide spectrum, from healthcare and medical diagnostics to gaming, creative industries, and advanced technology applications. By requiring partnerships between companies and research bodies, the fund hopes to ensure that innovations are grounded in both scientific expertise and real-world business needs.

items.title: Digitalised Yellow Book
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
AI-driven project to digitise handwritten complaint reports in the public administration’s Yellow Book, aiming to reduce processing time, enhance evaluation standards, and extend electronic support for complaints. The Yellow Book (Livro Amarelo) is a public administration tool that allows citizens to submit complaints, suggestions, and compliments regarding public services. It serves as a formal channel for feedback, helping to improve the quality and accountability of public administration.

Portugal’s Yellow Book (Livro Amarelo) is the main public platform for citizens to file complaints, suggestions, or compliments about public services. An AI-driven project has been introduced to modernise the system by digitising handwritten reports.
The project seeks to cut down processing times, improve the quality of evaluations, and provide more consistent support for users submitting feedback. By applying AI to recognise and classify handwritten text, the initiative helps transform citizen input into structured data, which can then be analysed more effectively to enhance accountability and service standards.

items.title: Digital Vouchers for SMEs
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The goal of this programme is to encourage micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) to improve their digitisation processes. It provides funding for companies to purchase digitisation and technology services.

Lithuania’s Ministry of Economy and Innovation announced an EU-backed measure that seeks to encourage micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises to advance their digitalization. The programme offers funding so firms can purchase digitization and technology services—from process optimization tools to IT upgrades—lowering upfront costs for first steps or scaling efforts. 
By targeting SMEs, the scheme aims to support productivity gains, better data use, and readiness for technologies like AI and automation, while building a broader base of digitally capable companies across the economy.

items.title: Digital Technologies Programme
items.org: Xjenza Malta (Research & Innovation Unit), in partnership with MDIA
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
