items.body:
The Digital Technologies Programme led by Xjenza Malta (XM) supports capacity-building efforts related to AI, digital trust, knowledge and data, representation and analysis, technology for sustainability, quantum computing and other emerging technologies. The capacity-building efforts are aimed at researchers, entrepreneurs, and organisations involved in these emerging technologies.

The Digital Technologies Programme 2025, coordinated by Xjenza Malta (XM), seeks to strengthen national expertise in AI and other advanced technologies by focusing on capacity-building. The initiative is directed at researchers, entrepreneurs, and organisations, helping them to develop skills and knowledge in areas such as AI, data use and analysis, digital trust, sustainability technologies, and quantum computing.
By combining research and innovation support, the programme hopes to create stronger links between scientific research and practical application, ensuring that Malta remains engaged with fast-evolving technological domains. In doing so, it also aims to prepare local stakeholders for both the opportunities and challenges that come with digital transformation.

items.title: Digital Pilot Farms
items.org: European Innovation Partnership for Agricultural Productivity and Sustainability
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Digital Pilot Farms project focuses on creating a pilot farm network to test innovative plant protection techniques. It aims to make the use of plant protection products (PPPs) more efficient, safe, and environmentally friendly by using a digital tool that provides targeted advice to farmers. This tool is openly accessible to all in Luxembourg, helping farmers better manage pests and weeds in a sustainable way.

The Digital Pilot Farms project in Luxembourg is building a network of farms to trial digital solutions for plant protection. Its main aim is to reduce reliance on plant protection products (PPPs) by providing farmers with a decision-support tool that delivers targeted advice on weed and pest management. The tool is designed to be openly accessible to all farmers in Luxembourg, promoting wider adoption of practices that are safer, more efficient, and environmentally friendly. By testing methods directly on pilot farms, the project hopes to ensure that recommendations are grounded in real-world conditions and can be scaled across the agricultural sector.

items.title: Development of a new big data-driven overhead power grid pre-storm damage prediction system
items.original_name: Jaunas lielo datu bāzētas augstsprieguma elektrotīkla bojājumu prognozēšanas sistēmas pirms vētras izstrāde
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Jaunas lielo datu bāzētas augstsprieguma elektrotīkla bojājumu prognozēšanas sistēmas pirms vētras izstrāde
items.body:
The Big Data-Driven Overhead Power Grid Pre-Storm Damage Prediction System in Latvia uses AI and machine learning to forecast potential storm damage to power grids. It provides real-time predictions for medium- and low-voltage networks. The system helps grid operators act proactively to prevent power outages.

This initiative focuses on developing a modular, scalable AI-powered system to predict damage to overhead power grids caused by storms. By leveraging big data and machine learning algorithms, the system can generate real-time forecasts of potential failures in medium- and low-voltage grids, helping operators plan preventive actions.
Key objectives include:
Predicting storm-related damage to power infrastructure before it occursSupporting proactive decision-making by grid operators to reduce outagesImproving resilience of the electrical grid through AI-driven monitoring and alertsThe system is designed to be modular and scalable, allowing it to adapt to different grid configurations and to expand as new data sources become available. By integrating advanced analytics with operational planning, the initiative strengthens energy reliability and disaster preparedness.

items.title: Data centres in Arnes
items.org: Ministry of Higher Education, Science and Innovation
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The construction of the data centre in Maribor, spearheaded by the Academic and Research Network of Slovenia (ARNES) is underway, implementing a 2023 action plan for open science, implementing “Measure 6.2: Open science to improve the quality, efficiency and responsiveness of research” within the Resolution on the Scientific Research and Innovation Strategy of Slovenia 2030 (ReZrIS30).

The primary objectives of this initiative are to establish a robust and internationally competitive research infrastructure that facilitates long-term data storage, supports the development of AI and HPC capabilities, and ensures compliance with the FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable) principles. By providing a central hub for open science and supercomputing, the data centre will enable Slovenian researchers to manage and share data more effectively, collaborate across borders, and contribute to the European Open Science Cloud (EOSC). \\
The Maribor data centre is designed with sustainability in mind, leveraging its proximity to the Dravske elektrarne Maribor hydroelectric plant to utilize renewable energy sources. Additionally, plans include the installation of solar panels and the use of surplus heat for district heating, further reducing its environmental footprint. The facility will also feature advanced infrastructure to support the Slovenian AI Factory, a €150 million EU-sponsored project aimed at fostering AI research and innovation.

items.title: Data Sandbox
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
The Data Sandbox managed by the Malta Digital Innovation Authority will provide a secure and controlled environment for organisations to experiment with data-driven technologies while adhering to data protection laws. The initiative will provide guidance on best practices for responsible data use, enabling companies to safely explore new technological applications.

The Data Sandbox run by the Malta Digital Innovation Authority (MDIA) seeks to create a secure and regulated environment where organisations can test data-driven technologies while complying with privacy and data protection rules. It offers guidance and oversight to ensure responsible use, providing a controlled space to explore new applications without exposing real-world systems prematurely.
By enabling experimentation in a compliance-aware setting, the initiative seeks to ensure companies can iterate, validate, and refine data-based solutions (e.g. AI, analytics, data sharing) more confidently. Over time, it may help reduce regulatory uncertainty and speed up innovation across Malta’s digital and data economy.

items.title: DRO Next
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The project "Establishment of Next-Generation Information Infrastructure (DRO Next)" focuses on developing advanced digital infrastructure that will enhance the capabilities for data management and processing at the edge, facilitating the use of edge computing technologies across various sectors, aiming to upgrade the current governmental private cloud.

The "Establishment of Next-Generation Information Infrastructure" (DRO Next) is a strategic initiative by the Slovenian government aimed at modernizing the country's digital infrastructure to better support data-intensive applications and services. The primary objective of DRO Next is to enhance Slovenia's governmental private cloud by integrating advanced edge computing technologies. This integration aims to improve the efficiency and responsiveness of public services by enabling faster data processing and reducing reliance on centralized cloud infrastructures.

items.title: Corallia Clusters Initiative
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Corallia Clusters Initiative implements targeted interventions of sustainable innovation ecosystems focusing on the management of Clusters, Incubators and Entrepreneurship Programmes. It supports SMEs by providing access to resources, mentorship, and networking opportunities.

The Corallia Clusters Initiative, part of the Athena Research Center in Greece, develops and manages innovation ecosystems through clusters, incubators, and entrepreneurship programmes. Its work is aimed at strengthening SMEs and start-ups by giving them access to mentorship, funding opportunities, and collaborative networks.
By coordinating resources across industry and academia, Corallia helps companies scale innovative solutions, improve competitiveness, and connect to international markets. Its cluster management model has been applied in high-tech fields, contributing to sustainable growth and cross-sector innovation in Greece.

items.title: Competence Centres Initiative
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
​Italy's Competence Centres Initiative, launched in 2023, is a strategic programme designed to accelerate the nation's digital and green transformation, building upon the previous Industry 4.0 framework. This initiative establishes a network of eight public-private partnerships, each serving as a hub for expertise in advanced technologies such as AI, the Internet of Things, collaborative robotics, automation systems, big data analytics, blockchain, and cloud computing.

Italy’s Competence Centres Initiative, launched in 2023, is a national programme under the Industrial Digitalisation Competence Centres (ICDI) framework. It builds on the earlier Industry 4.0 strategy and seeks to ensure faster progress in both the digital and green transition.
The initiative establishes a network of eight public–private partnerships, each acting as a specialised hub for advanced technologies. Their focus spans AI, IoT, collaborative robotics, automation, big data analytics, blockchain, and cloud computing, providing companies—especially SMEs—with access to applied expertise, training, and pilot projects.

items.title: Chip Chairs
items.org: The Ministry for Digital Transformation and Public Administration, through the Secretary of State for Telecommunications and Digital Infrastructures
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Creation of 17 university chairs focused on semiconductor scientific investigation and talent creation; 80 private sector companies involved.

Courses will be delivered at universities in nine autonomous communities to strengthen research, dissemination, and training in the field microelectronics, in particular: 
Design of microelectronic circuits
New materials and devices
Technological processes
Testing and encapsulation of chips

items.title: CeADAR Technology Centre and  CeADAR AI EDIH
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
CeADAR is Ireland’s National Centre for Applied AI. It is a market-focused technology centre for innovation and applied research in AI, machine learning and data analytics across all industry sectors. Enterprise Ireland is working with CeADAR on its next phase plan to scale up the centre.

CeADAR contains an AI focused EDIH offering companies and public service organisations access to training, prototype development, and feasibility studies to help them adopt AI and analytics. Other services offered include:
- Provide SMEs with funded training and upskilling in AI and digital technologies
- Help businesses explore proof-of-concept solutions and test prototypes.
- Foster AI adoption by offering feasibility assessments.
- Support digital transitions for SMEs through AI adaptation

CeADARs EDIH also delivers an AI Ecosystem Accelerator for Start-Ups It provides technical and commercial support to AI start-ups. The first cohort of 11 start-ups completed the pro-gramme in 2024. It is planned that there will be two more intakes, 2025 and 2026.

items.title: Call for projects between France and Germany on artificial intelligence technologies for risk prevention, crisis management, and resilience
items.original_name: Ausschreibung für Projekte zwischen Frankreich und Deutschland zu KI-Technologien für Risikoprävention, Krisenmanagement und Resilienz
items.org: Ministry of Economy and Climate Action, Germany; Ministry of Higher Education and Research, France
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Ausschreibung für Projekte zwischen Frankreich und Deutschland zu KI-Technologien für Risikoprävention, Krisenmanagement und Resilienz
items.body:
France and Germany launched a joint call for AI projects focused on risk prevention, crisis management, and resilience. One funded project, RenovAIte, develops AI-based software to optimise large-scale renovation of housing and roads. The initiative supports decision-making for engineering firms and local authorities.

France and Germany have established a binational call for projects on artificial intelligence (AI), aiming to strengthen cooperation on critical challenges such as risk prevention, crisis management, and resilience. This initiative reflects both countries’ commitment to joint innovation, cross-border collaboration, and applied AI research.
Among the selected projects is RenovAIte, which seeks to transform the way housing and road renovation is planned and executed. Its main features include:
Developing AI-based software to support renovation at scaleCovering the entire value chain, from data acquisition and analysis to decision-making toolsProviding tailored solutions for engineering firms, housing services, and road management authoritiesThe project contributes to greater efficiency, sustainability, and cost-effectiveness in infrastructure management. By applying AI, RenovAIte enables smarter resource allocation and reduces environmental impact while improving service delivery for citizens.

items.title: CONTRAILS project Call for projects between France and Germany on artificial intelligence technologies for risk prevention, crisis management, and resilience
items.original_name: CONTRAILS-Projekt: Aufruf für Projekte zwischen Frankreich und Deutschland zu KI-Technologien für Risikoprävention, Krisenmanagement und Resilienz
items.org: Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF), Germany; Ministry of Higher Education and Research, France
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: CONTRAILS-Projekt: Aufruf für Projekte zwischen Frankreich und Deutschland zu KI-Technologien für Risikoprävention, Krisenmanagement und Resilienz
items.body:
The CONTRAILS project is a joint French–German initiative using trusted AI methods and physical models to study and predict condensation trails. Its goal is to assess their climate impact and support strategies to reduce contrail formation. The project is part of a binational call on AI technologies for risk prevention, crisis management, and resilience.

The CONTRAILS project is carried out under the France–Germany Call for Projects on AI technologies for risk prevention, crisis management, and resilience (2022). It aims to combine trusted artificial intelligence techniques with physical modelling to advance understanding of condensation trails (contrails) and their role in climate change.
The project pursues several objectives:
Improve identification and characterisation of contrails through AI-supported analysisEnhance data assimilation and prediction models to forecast contrail formation and persistenceProvide tools to assess the impact of contrails on the climateSupport future trajectory optimisation tests designed to prevent or minimise contrail formationBy coupling AI technologies with environmental and atmospheric models, CONTRAILS contributes to climate mitigation strategies in aviation. It also demonstrates how cross-border collaboration can accelerate innovation in AI for climate resilience and risk management.

items.title: Athens Center for Entrepreneurship and Innovation (ACEin)
items.org: Athens University of Economics and Business
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The ACEin, the incubation & acceleration centre of the Athens University of Economics, among other public-private partnerships, incubators, and accelerators, offers mentorship, resources, and financial support to AI start-ups.

ACEin, the incubation and acceleration centre of the Athens University of Economics and Business (AUEB), supports start-ups through mentorship, resources, and access to finance. It provides an environment where young companies— including those developing AI-driven solutions—can refine business models, connect with experts, and gain exposure to investors. As part of a broader ecosystem of public–private partnerships, incubators, and accelerators in Greece, ACEin contributes to strengthening entrepreneurship by linking academic research with market-oriented innovation.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Security Research Centre at the Research and Academic Computer Network
items.original_name: Ośrodka Badań nad Bezpieczeństwem Sztucznej Inteligencji and Naukowa i Akademicka Sieć Komputerowa – NASK
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Ośrodka Badań nad Bezpieczeństwem Sztucznej Inteligencji and Naukowa i Akademicka Sieć Komputerowa – NASK
items.body:
In December 2024, the NASK announced a transformation of its AI division into the AI Security Research Centre, which will focus on scientific research the field of AI, with an emphasis on cybersecurity.

In December 2024, Poland’s NASK (National Research Institute) announced the creation of the AI Security Research Centre, marking the transformation of its previous AI division. The new centre is tasked with advancing scientific research on artificial intelligence, with a particular focus on cybersecurity and the safe use of AI technologies.
By concentrating expertise in one specialised unit, the centre seeks to address growing risks tied to AI adoption, from system vulnerabilities to malicious use. It will also play a role in shaping national and international approaches to AI safety, strengthening Poland’s position in the wider European debate on trustworthy and secure AI.

items.title: AiNed – “AI for energy and sustainability”
items.org: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Climate Policy
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
AiNed – “AI for Energy and Sustainability” is a public-private programme that explores how AI can accelerate the energy transition. It establishes AI Innovation Labs to develop practical solutions for sustainable energy. The initiative supports the Netherlands’ efforts to achieve climate goals by 2030 and beyond.

AiNed – “AI for Energy and Sustainability” is a multi-year public-private programme launched in 2021 to harness AI for the country’s energy and sustainability goals. The initiative focuses on creating AI Innovation Labs that explore applications of AI in renewable energy, energy efficiency, and other areas critical to the energy transition.
Key objectives of the programme include:
Accelerating the energy transition through AI-driven solutionsEstablishing AI Innovation Labs to test and deploy practical applicationsEnsuring alignment with the EU AI Act and broader sustainable energy frameworksContributing to a fair, reliable, and efficient energy systemThe programme encourages collaboration between industry, research institutions, and government to translate AI research into real-world solutions. By combining expertise from multiple sectors, AiNed seeks to create scalable, innovative approaches that can support the Netherlands’ climate targets and sustainable development ambitions.

items.title: AiNed
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
AiNed  is a multi-year public-private initiative that helps Dutch companies and public institutions capitalise on AI's economic and social opportunities. Funded by the National Growth Fund, AiNed focuses on AI investments in Ethical, Legal and Societal Aspects (ELSA) labs, learning communities, innovation labs, and SME innovations. It also supports research grants and the development of a robust AI ecosystem through start-ups and SMEs, aligning with EU AI legislation in a responsible manner.

The AiNed programme is a flagship Dutch initiative designed to strengthen the country’s position in artificial intelligence. Backed by the National Growth Fund, it pools resources from government, industry, and academia to accelerate AI development and adoption.
Its activities cover a wide range of areas: ELSA labs that address ethical, legal, and social aspects of AI; innovation and learning labs that connect researchers and practitioners; and targeted support for SMEs and start-ups to apply AI in practice. By fostering collaboration across sectors, AiNed seeks to build a cohesive AI ecosystem that balances innovation with responsibility, ensuring alignment with broader European AI regulatory frameworks.

items.title: ATMOSYS Air Quality Management System
items.org: Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The ATMOSYS Air Quality Management System provides software tools and web applications to monitor and manage air quality in Croatia. It uses machine learning to forecast air quality at national measurement sites. The system was adapted from a Belgian model to meet Croatian regional and urban requirements.

The ATMOSYS Air Quality Management System is a comprehensive platform designed to support the implementation of air quality legislation at regional and urban levels in Croatia. It provides authorities with software tools and web applications to monitor, analyse, and forecast air quality in real time.
Key objectives of the initiative include:
Enhancing air quality monitoring through advanced data analysis and forecastingSupporting compliance with national and EU air quality legislationProviding actionable insights for policymakers and environmental agenciesThe system leverages machine learning techniques to produce accurate forecasts at specific national measurement sites, helping authorities plan interventions and inform the public. The platform was successfully adapted from a Belgian system through the AIRQ project, ensuring it meets local Croatian environmental conditions and regulatory requirements.

items.title: ARTIQ - AI Centres of Excellence
items.org: National Science Centre & National Centre for Research and Development
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
In 2023, AGH University won a grant for the ARTIQ through the joint undertaking from the National Science Centre (NCN) and the National Centre for Research and Development (NCBR) to create a highly specialised research team to contribute to increasing Poland's scientific and R&D potential in the field of AI, with a project proposal titled “Integrating Reasoning, Learning, Optimization and Interpretability for accelerated commercialization of next-generation intelligent software systems.

The ARTIQ programme, launched in 2023 by Poland’s National Science Centre (NCN) and the National Centre for Research and Development (NCBR), is aimed at boosting the country’s capacity in advanced AI research and development. One of the key projects under this scheme is led by AGH University of Science and Technology, which secured funding to establish a specialised research team working on next-generation AI systems.
The winning project, titled “Integrating Reasoning, Learning, Optimization and Interpretability for Accelerated Commercialization of Next-Generation Intelligent Software Systems”, reflects the initiative’s focus on bridging fundamental AI research with practical applications. By combining areas such as machine reasoning, machine learning, and optimization with interpretability, the project seeks to strengthen both scientific knowledge and pathways for AI commercialisation.
Through such efforts, ARTIQ intends to reinforce Poland’s role in the European AI research landscape, while also creating opportunities for translating academic advances into market-ready solutions.

items.title: AI Factories Latvia
items.org: Ministry of Economics of the Republic of Latvia
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
AI Factories Latvia aims to drive AI innovation by supporting start-ups and established companies in developing and commercialising new AI products and services. A core focus is the creation of large language models tailored to regional languages to enhance translation, content creation, and communication technologies. Additionally, the initiative supports digital twin projects to strengthen cybersecurity and regional security simulations.

AI Factories Latvia seeks to ensure that Latvia becomes a hub for AI development and commercialisation. The programme is designed to support both start-ups and established companies in bringing new AI products and services to market.
A central priority is the creation of large language models tailored to regional languages, aimed at improving translation, content generation, and communication tools. Alongside this, the initiative backs digital twin projects, with applications in cybersecurity and regional security simulations, reinforcing both technological capacity and resilience.

items.title: AI European Digital Innovation Hub (EDIH) Hungary
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This project aims to foster AI-driven innovation across Hungarian SMEs, start-ups, and public sector organisations. It offers comprehensive services ranging from initial awareness-building to prototype development and marketisation, and targets seven priority industries, including manufacturing, healthcare, energy, agriculture, logistics, finance, and public administration.

AI EDIH Hungary is part of the European network of Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs), dedicated to helping businesses and public organizations adopt artificial intelligence. It provides companies—especially SMEs—with access to AI expertise, testing environments, and training, enabling them to explore and integrate digital solutions before making major investments. The hub also offers guidance on financing opportunities and supports networking within the wider European innovation ecosystem. By linking local enterprises with EU-level resources and expertise, AI EDIH Hungary strengthens the country’s capacity for digital transformation and fosters responsible AI uptake.

items.title: xPlain-AI
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
xPlain-AI is an educational app on AI-based technologies in the medical field and was funded by the Vienna Chamber of Labor (Arbeiterkammer Wien), which began in 2021 as part of the Artificial Intelligence Mission 2030.

The aim of the project is a training application to make complex AI-based projects "explainable" to employees at the interface between medicine and technology. A major disadvantage of AI-based technologies in the medical field is that these systems are not explained to users. Together with Women in AI and the DIO, "Xplain-AI" will explain innovative projects with AI-based content in a user-oriented way – for example, data-driven, automated technologies, integration of machine learning, recognition of biases in the application of algorithms. The training application is barrier-free, web-based and includes human-centered design with an adaptive, human-in-the-loop learning algorithm. The reinforcement learning process learns the individual preferences of the user - everyone can help shape his/her training content by evaluating the content.

items.title: p-NET Competence Center
items.org: General Secretariat for Research and Innovation (GSRI)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Founded in the context of the Competence Centers Act of the General Secretariat for Research and Innovation (GSRI) and backed by both private and public funding, p-NET, a network of twenty-one shareholders from industry leaders, SMEs, academia, research institutions, and consulting firms from Greece’s digital landscape supports innovation, entrepreneurship, and technological advancement in 5G communications and other emerging networks.

p-NET is a Greek competence centre established under the Competence Centers Act of the General Secretariat for Research and Innovation (GSRI). It brings together 21 shareholders from across the digital ecosystem, including large companies, SMEs, universities, research institutions, and consulting firms.
With support from both public and private funding, p-NET focuses on advancing 5G communications and emerging network technologies. Its role is to foster collaboration between research and industry, promote entrepreneurship, and accelerate innovation that strengthens Greece’s position in next-generation digital infrastructure.

items.title: WeedBot
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This AI-driven agricultural tool uses high-resolution imaging and laser technology to distinguish crops from weeds. By applying concentrated light or laser beams, the system removes weeds without damaging crops, reducing reliance on chemical herbicides and enabling more sustainable farming practices.

WeedBot is a precision farming start-up that develops laser-based weeding systems guided by AI and high-resolution imaging. The technology selectively targets weeds, helping farmers cut chemical use and protect crops with minimal soil disturbance. The company’s focus is on making large-scale weeding both environmentally sustainable and cost-efficient, offering a scalable alternative to herbicides that can be integrated into modern farming equipment.

items.title: The development of genomic research in Romania (ROGEN)
items.org: Carol Davila University of Medicine and Pharmacy, Bucharest
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The initiative aims to create an integrated approach to genomic medical research.

Romania aims to develop the National Genomic Research Network, 1+MG mirror groups, develop the national sequencing infrastructure, determine the national reference genome in connection with the Genome of Europe project and study personalised treatments for certain conditions.

items.title: TEF Health - AI in Medical Imaging
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
TEF Health, an initiative by the European Commission, aims to accelerate the adoption of AI and robotics in healthcare. In Slovakia, it focuses on using AI to analyse radiological images, enhancing the speed and accuracy of diagnoses for radiologists.

TEF Health, an initiative by the European Commission, aims to accelerate the adoption of AI and robotics in healthcare. In Slovakia, it focuses on using AI to analyse radiological images, enhancing the speed and accuracy of diagnoses for radiologists. The project provides a platform for testing and validating AI solutions in real-world healthcare settings. It involves collaboration between public and private sector entities to ensure the integration of innovative technologies. This initiative supports the broader goal of improving healthcare delivery through technological advancements.

items.title: T2O2 Regulation
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This project focuses on creating a biomass-based combustion control system to reduce pollutants in free-standing room heaters. Developed with industry partners, the T2O2 system applies the energy balance method and aims for market readiness after further optimisation.

T2O2 develops a combustion control system for freestanding room heaters, using the energy balance method to cut pollutant emissions and raise efficiency. The system is being advanced with industry partners and has been tested on demonstrator stoves.

items.title: Synergies between Digital Agricultural Strategy, AI Strategy, and the Digital Food Strategy
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Hungary’s agricultural and food industry digitisation efforts are underpinned by the Digital Agricultural Strategy, the AI Strategy, and the Digital Food Industry Strategy. Together, these initiatives aim to modernise the sector across three pillars: digitising production technologies, enhancing data-driven decision-making, and streamlining product pathways through digital tools.

The government has supported these efforts with financial schemes, including the Digital Agricultural Academy and Digital Producers' Market, which provide digital resources and support for producers. Although there is no direct funding for AI development, related AI initiatives can be integrated into broader innovation and processing plant development projects.

items.title: Support semiconductor ecosystem
items.org: The Ministry of Economics, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
As part of the national strategy on electronics, France supports initiatives aimed at developing advanced semiconductor technologies.

Nine EU Member States have launched the Semiconductor Coalition, marking an important step toward deepening cooperation Europe’s semiconductor ecosystem.
At the margin of the COMPET Council, responsible ministers of Austria, Belgium, Finland, France, Germany, Italy, Poland, Spain and the Netherlands issued a statement where they agreed to reinforce their cooperation to strengthen European’s competitiveness and strategic autonomy in the semiconductor sector by supporting research, expanding production capacity, and fostering a highly skilled workforce.

items.title: Smart and Social Home Care
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This initiative is a research and development project, aiming to create an innovative, secure, and privacy-preserving smart home system to support the health and well-being of elderly individuals living independently. By integrating technology, public health, and social sciences, the project addresses challenges such as social isolation and the need for assistance and safety. It adopts an interdisciplinary approach, involving social sciences, software development, smart environments & security.

As the population ages, it's essential to support elderly people in receiving care at home rather than moving into nursing homes. Solutions at the crossroads of technology, healthcare, public services, and social sciences can address two major challenges in home care: (1) combating social isolation and (2) meeting assistance and safety needs. The ongoing COVID-19 crisis has dramatically demonstrated the need for better care solutions for older citizens. The aim of this project is to develop a home care solution to assist elderly individuals who wish to remain in their homes and to coordinate the efforts of all stakeholders around them (social workers, caregivers, family, neighbors, etc.).

items.title: Smart Agro Hub
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Smart Agro Hub is the competence centre of the Agricultural University with the partnership of 12 other companies, forming an ecosystem of research, practical knowledge and entrepreneurship, contributing to the creation of a more environmentally friendly agricultural production system based on digital technologies.

Smart Agro Hub (Greece) is the Agricultural University’s competence centre, built with a partnership of 12 companies to form an ecosystem that links research, practical know-how, and entrepreneurship. Its purpose is to help move Greek agriculture toward more environmentally friendly production by using digital technologies.
In practice, the hub coordinates collaboration between the university and its partners to develop and test solutions, share expertise, and support business uptake. By joining academic research with real-world experience and entrepreneurial activity, it aims to speed up the adoption of digital tools across the agri-food sector and improve sustainability outcomes.

items.title: Slovak Quantum Communication Infrastructure
items.org: Institute of Physics of the Slovak Academy of Sciences
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Slovak Quantum Communication Infrastructure project is implemented by institute of Physics of the Slovak Academy of Sciences.

The Slovak Quantum Communication Infrastructure project is implemented by the Institute of Physics of the Slovak Academy of Sciences. It addresses the need for secure and reliable communication channels, which are critical for data in research, government, and industry. The project’s main objective is to develop a national quantum communication network that enables ultra-secure data transmission. It works by applying principles of quantum physics, such as quantum key distribution, to protect information against interception or tampering. The Institute of Physics leads the design, testing, and deployment, collaborating with national research institutions and technology partners.

items.title: Seerlinq
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This company leverages machine learning to analyse physiological data, tailoring treatment and diagnostics for cardiovascular diseases. It provides innovative tools that enhance patient care by improving diagnostic accuracy and treatment personalisation.

Seerlinq is a Slovak company that uses machine learning to analyse physiological data for cardiovascular care. It addresses the challenge that effective diagnosis and treatment of heart conditions often require complex interpretation of patient data. The company’s main objective is to provide tools that personalise diagnostics and treatment, improving accuracy and patient outcomes. Its solutions work by applying advanced algorithms to patient data, helping clinicians make informed decisions tailored to individual patients. Seerlinq collaborates with healthcare providers to integrate these tools into clinical workflows. By enhancing precision and personalisation in cardiovascular care, it supports better and more efficient patient management.

items.title: Research programme "Agroecology and ICT: data, agricultural equipment, and genetic resources in the service of the agroecological transition and adaptation to climate hazards"
items.org: French National Research Institute for Agriculture, Food and Environment; French National Institute for Digital Science and Technology
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The research projects selected and funded should implement multidisciplinary and systemic approaches based on the hybridisation of expertise from agronomy, ecology, genetics, physiology, ethology, digital technology, artificial intelligence, and social sciences (economics, sociology, management sciences, ergonomics). The funded infrastructures and equipment should be structured and provide data and methods for agroecological practices.

This project funds research that pairs agroecological practices with advanced digital tools including artificial intelligence. The goal is to speed up the transition to resilient, low-input farming by turning data, models, and decision-support into practical methods farmers and advisors can use.
Projects are collaborative and application-oriented: consortia build shared datasets, experimental platforms, and measurement equipment, then test solutions in real-world settings (e.g., field trials, living labs). Expected outputs include open methods and interoperable tools that improve monitoring, planning, and evaluation of agroecological systems.

items.title: Research Ireland research infrastructure programme awards
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Research Ireland Infrastructure Programme supports the research community in building and sustaining essential resources to conduct high-quality, innovative research across all disciplines. This programme recognises that robust research infrastructure is fundamental to advancing knowledge that contributes to Ireland’s cultural, social, environmental and economic development.

Research Ireland has funded core (national) infrastructure including five research infrastructure awards relating to semi-conductors, including:
- In-situ transmission electron microscopy for nanometre scale characterisation of materials at the University of Limerick 
- Advanced mass spectrometry infrastructure at Maynooth University to enable detection and enumeration of biomolecules. Applications in health, biotechnology and chemical sciences
- Experimental facilities at the Irish Microkelvin Laboratory for Advanced Quantum Materials Research, University College Cork (UCC) and at Tyndall National Institute
- Advanced Heterogeneous Device Integration facility to improve semiconductor performance
- Irish Quantum technology facility for advanced qubit manipulation.

items.title: Research Ireland Frontiers for the Future Programme (FFP)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
FFP provides funding for high-risk, high-reward research. It currently funds ~16 active awards in the field of AI.

The Programme will be run in collaboration with the Geological Survey of Ireland (GSI), the Sustainable Energy Authority of Ireland (SEAI), Breakthrough Cancer Research (BCR), and the Children’s Health Foundation (CHF). Research Ireland is open to forging new co-funding partnerships with agencies and organisations.

The programme comprises two streams: Projects and Awards. Projects provides funding for high-risk, high-reward research that facilitates highly innovative and novel approaches to research.
Awards provides larger scale funding for innovative, collaborative and excellent research programmes that have the potential to deliver economic and societal impact.

items.title: Projects under Food Vision 2030
items.org: Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Under Food Vision 2030, the Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine (DAFM) funds innovative agri-food research, including AI-driven projects. Recent AI-focused initiatives include improving productivity in the mushroom sector (MUSHNOMICS), food quality analysis using hyperspectral tech (SPECTROFOOD), AI in slaughterhouse inspections (RIBMINS), smart farming (APP4FARM), food system mapping, and AI-nutrition links in older adults (AMBROSIA).

Ireland’s Food Vision 2030 strategy positions research and innovation as key drivers of a more sustainable agri-food system, with funding from the Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine (DAFM). Within this framework, AI has become an important tool for addressing sectoral challenges ranging from productivity to food safety and public health.
Several recent projects highlight this trend: MUSHNOMICS applies AI to boost efficiency in mushroom production; SPECTROFOOD uses hyperspectral imaging for food quality control; RIBMINS explores AI-assisted methods in slaughterhouse inspections; APP4FARM develops smart farming solutions; AMBROSIA examines AI-supported nutrition for older adults; and food system mapping projects apply AI to track supply chains. Together, these initiatives are examples of how how AI research is being embedded across Ireland’s agri-food priorities under Food Vision 2030.

items.title: Projects from the National Institute of Geographic and Forestry Information (IGN)
items.org: National Institute for Geographic and Forestry Information
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The French National Institute of Geographical and Forest Information (IGN) leads several AI-enhanced projects supporting land use, ecology, and agriculture. These include LiDAR HD (3D national mapping), OCS GE (land cover classification), CarHab (habitat modelling), AI4GEO (automated 2D/3D mapping from satellite data), CAP monitoring (with MASA/ASP), and BDForêt (forest reference mapping), advancing data-driven public policy and environmental management.

The IGN has launched several projects with AI components: 
• Lidar HD: 3D mapping of the entire ground and above-ground of France, classified into several classes (ground, water, vegetation, buildings, bridges, permanent above-ground)
• OCS GE : a national reference usable at different territorial levels for the implementation of public land-use policies and the development of urban planning documents
• CarHab: national cartographic modeling of natural and semi-natural habitats for the terrestrial ecosystems of mainland and overseas France
• AI4GEO: an R&D programme with an industrial research phase aiming to overcome technological barriers to the automatic production of 2D and 3D Geographic Information with semantic content, based on satellite imagery data
• Monitoring of the Common Agricultural Policy (agreement with MASA and ASP)
• BDForêt: a geographic reference for forest professionals and for environmental and land-use planning stakeholders in mainland France.

items.title: Powerful Medical cardio mobile app
items.org: Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs of the Slovak Republic
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Clinical assistant that allows health care professionals to interpret an electrocardiogram (ECG), a recording of the heart's electrical activity, with the precision of a top cardiologist.

The Powerful Medical cardio mobile app is a clinical tool designed to help healthcare professionals interpret electrocardiograms (ECGs) in Slovakia. It addresses the challenge that accurate ECG interpretation requires specialized expertise, which is not always immediately available. The app’s main objective is to provide analysis with precision comparable to that of a top cardiologist, supporting faster and more reliable diagnosis. It works by using advanced algorithms to evaluate the heart’s electrical activity and highlight abnormalities for the clinician. Healthcare professionals can use it on mobile devices, integrating it into routine patient care without disrupting workflow. By improving access to expert-level ECG interpretation, the app enhances diagnostic accuracy and patient outcomes in clinical settings.

items.title: Optimization of Data Collection and Control Technology for Biomass Combustion Systems
items.original_name: Optimierung von Datenerfassung und Steuerungstechnik für Biomassefeuerungen, DigitalFire
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Optimierung von Datenerfassung und Steuerungstechnik für Biomassefeuerungen, DigitalFire
items.body:
DigitalFire aims to improve biomass combustion systems by using advanced data collection, machine learning, and predictive maintenance. The project is aimed at enhancing efficiency and reliability, providing cost-effective solutions for manufacturers and operators.

DigitalFire (Germany) is an FNR-funded project under the Federal Ministry of Food and Agriculture to improve the performance of biomass combustion systems. It addresses efficiency losses and downtime by applying advanced data collection, machine learning, and predictive maintenance in real operating conditions—aiming for more reliable, cost-effective operation for manufacturers and plant operators.
The project’s core objective is to use data-driven methods to detect issues earlier and optimize operation, thereby increasing efficiency and reliability. Results are intended to be practical for industry stakeholders in the biomass sector.

items.title: National programme on spintronics
items.original_name: Programme et Équipements Prioritaires de Recherche Exploratoire SPINtronique
items.org: CEA (French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission), under France 2030 strategy
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Programme et Équipements Prioritaires de Recherche Exploratoire SPINtronique
items.body:
Programme launched as part of France 2030 to promote frugal, agile and sustainable digital solutions. Spintronics is an emerging technology with multiple potential applications in the context of AI solutions.

As part of the France 2030 programme, this initiative promotes digital technologies that are affordable, flexible, and environmentally friendly. Many current AI systems use a lot of energy and costly hardware, so the programme focuses on new solutions that use fewer resources without losing performance.
One promising technology is spintronics, which uses the spin of electrons instead of their charge to handle information. Spintronics could make AI devices faster and more energy-efficient than traditional electronics, helping create sustainable digital solutions.
The programme supports collaboration between researchers, companies, and public bodies to develop practical AI applications based on spintronics. By encouraging innovation in this area, the initiative aims to build adaptable and greener digital technologies.
Over time, this work is expected to help spread the use of spintronics and other efficient technologies, contributing to France’s goals for innovation and sustainability.

items.title: National High-Performance Computing at Universities
items.org: Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Since 2021, the BMBF, in collaboration with the federal states, has supported HPC at universities, with an annual investment of EUR 62.5 million. This initiative provides the AI community with computing resources, specialised training, and consulting to strengthen research capabilities and advance scientific computing skills within academic institutions.

Having began in 2021, Germany’s Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF), together with the federal states, has funded high-performance computing (HPC) at universities through the National High Performance Computing Alliance (NHR). With an annual budget of EUR 62.5 million, the programme equips academic institutions with computing resources, specialised training, and expert consulting. For the AI community, this means access to the large-scale computing power needed for model training and data-intensive research.

items.title: National Genomic Data Infrastructure (GDI) Node and 1+ Million Genome Project
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Romania is working towards a national genome data infrastructure to contribute to the 1+ MG project and share its available genome data.

Romania is joining the European effort to share genome and clinical data through its involvement in the European Genomic Data Infrastructure (GDI), part of the wider 1+ Million Genomes (1+MG) initiative. This effort addresses the challenge that many countries have useful genetic and health data, but lack the systems and connections needed to use them safely across borders. By building its own infrastructure, Romania aims to make its data usable for research, medical advances, and improved patient care, while respecting privacy and legal rules.
The main goals are to enable secure access to high-quality human genome data and matching clinical information; to align Romania’s systems with agreed European standards so data can talk to each other; and to support national research and health services in using genome information for better diagnosis, treatments, and prevention. It also seeks to strengthen Romania’s role in European genomics, helping Romanian institutions participate fully in transnational research and healthcare innovations.
Romania has institutions like the Genomics Research and Development Institute and the Authority for Digitization of Romania participating in GDI. There is coordination with the “Carol Davila” University of Medicine and Pharmacy and the National Genomic Research Network. The plan is to establish a “National Mirror Group” or equivalent body, build or upgrade national genome data hubs, and ensure these meet legal, technical, and ethical standards required by the European framework (like data protection, data quality, interoperability). Romania contributes its existing genome datasets and clinical data under these conditions.

items.title: National Concept of Public Administration Informatization (NKIVS)
items.org: Ministry of Investments, Regional Development and Informatization (MIRRI)
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body: The NKIVS provides the framework for the informatisation of public administration, focusing on digital and data transformations as well as integration of cloud services into public administration processes, promoting the use of next-generation cloud technologies to improve efficiency, accessibility, and security in government operations It includes guidelines on adopting cloud services within public administration, ensuring secure and efficient digital services.

items.title: Microelectronics. Trustworthy and sustainable. For Germany und Europe
items.org: Federal Ministry of Education and Research
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Running from 2021-2024, this framework programme by the German Federal Government focuses on promoting research and innovation in microelectronics with a commitment to trustworthiness, sustainability, and technological sovereignty. It emphasizes the development of secure and reliable microelectronic components, aiming to reduce Europe’s dependence on non-European technologies. The programme also advocates for environmentally friendly manufacturing processes within the microelectronics sector.

The German Federal Government’s programme "Microelectronics. Trustworthy and sustainable. For Germany and Europe" (2021–2024) supports research and innovation in microelectronics. It addresses Europe’s reliance on non-European technologies by promoting the development of secure, reliable, and sustainable components made in Europe.
The programme’s main goals are to strengthen technological independence, improve cybersecurity, and reduce the environmental impact of microchip production. It supports projects focused on energy-efficient design, secure hardware, and environmentally friendly manufacturing.
Researchers, companies, and public institutions work together under this programme, especially in areas like healthcare, mobility, energy, and security—where trustworthy microelectronics are essential. The initiative also complements broader European efforts to build a stronger, more resilient tech industry.

items.title: Methodological Guidelines for Cloud Services
items.org: Ministry of Investments, Regional Development and Informatization (MIRRI)
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
These guidelines outline best practices and recommendations for integrating cloud services in public administration, supporting the goals of NKIVS, focussing on security, interoperability, and cost-efficiency in using cloud technologies.

The Methodological Guidelines for Cloud Services in the Slovak Republic provide practical recommendations for using cloud technologies within public administration. They address the challenge that adopting cloud services can be complex, with risks related to security, compatibility, and cost management. By offering clear guidance, the guidelines aim to help public institutions adopt cloud solutions safely and effectively.
The main objectives are to ensure security of public data, promote interoperability between systems, and encourage cost-efficient use of cloud technologies. They also aim to standardize approaches across different government bodies, improving coordination and consistency in digital services.
The guidelines were developed under the framework of NKIVS (National Concept of Informatization of the Slovak Republic), with input from government IT specialists and public sector stakeholders. They cover practical steps for selecting cloud providers, managing risks, ensuring legal compliance, and integrating cloud solutions with existing IT systems.

items.title: Medresyst
items.org: Walloon Region's Strategic Innovation Initiative “Health Reinforcement”
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The MedReSyst initiative seeks to revolutionise network and systems medicine through a holistic approach that considers the patient as a whole. By integrating biological data, exposomics, detailed clinical records, and advanced artificial intelligence (AI), MedReSyst aims to create individualised health profiles. These profiles map risk factors and protective elements unique to each person, enabling precise predictions of disease development and personalised treatment responses.

The rise in life expectancy and lifestyle changes has led to an increase in complex diseases like cancer, diabetes, and neurological disorders, burdening healthcare systems.
MedReSyst focuses on 4P medicine (Personalized, Preventive, Predictive and Participatory). It leverages network medicine by integrating biological, environmental, and clinical data with artificial intelligence to customize care, identify risks and predict treatment responses.
This initiative is based upon three strategic pillars :
-Acquisition of Multimodal Data: Collecting biological, exposomic, clinical, and imaging data through specific cohorts in collaboration with international bio-banks.
-AI Modeling: Developing explanatory models of pathogenesis to enable more personalized, effective treatments with fewer side effects.
-Personalized Clinical Strategies: Designing integrated screening, diagnostic, and treatment workflows for precision medicine, reducing costs, and improving care quality.

MedReSyst develops AI models with continuous learning, fostering a virtuous cycle between experts and technology for more transparent and flexible AI use in medicine.

items.title: MISSION KI
items.org: Federal Ministry for Digital and Transport (BMDV)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
MISSION KI, established by the Federal Ministry for Digital and Transport (BMDV), focuses on accelerating the transfer of cutting-edge AI research into practice and fostering the growth of outstanding AI innovations. To further advance the development of trustworthy AI by design, the initiative is developing and testing a voluntary AI quality standard and corresponding testing procedures, particularly for low-risk AI systems, in alignment with the EU AI Act.

Through AI Innovation and Quality Centres, MISSION KI supports companies in the development and implementation of trustworthy AI. Additionally, the AI Founder Fellowship is launching an innovative start-up programme aimed at bridging the gap between advanced AI research and successful start-ups, by supporting PhD students and postdoctoral researchers in transforming their AI research into innovative businesses.
MISSION KI also strategically connects AI start-ups and SMEs. By identifying the specific innovation needs of SMEs, the initiative works with partners to match them with suitable AI developers, fostering long-term collaborations that create mutual benefits.
To enhance the exchange and utilisation of data for cross-sector AI innovations and new business models, MISSION KI develops open-source products and services that focus on ensuring the interoperability of data spaces across industries and national borders.

items.title: Lunit INSIGHT MMG
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Lunit INSIGHT MMG is an AI solution for mammography that has been implemented with the private health sector to improve the detection of breast cancer.

Lunit INSIGHT MMG is an artificial intelligence system designed to assist in mammography imaging. It addresses the challenge that breast cancer can be difficult to detect early, and interpretation of mammograms can vary between radiologists. By supporting clinicians with AI analysis, it aims to improve the accuracy and consistency of breast cancer detection.
The main objective of Lunit INSIGHT MMG is to identify suspicious areas in mammograms, helping radiologists prioritize cases that may require further examination. This can lead to earlier diagnosis and treatment, ultimately improving patient outcomes.
The system works by analyzing digital mammography images using deep learning algorithms trained on large datasets of annotated scans. In practice, it highlights areas of concern on the images, which radiologists then review as part of their standard workflow. The solution has been implemented in collaboration with private healthcare providers, integrating into existing hospital imaging systems without disrupting normal operations.

items.title: International accelerator of Startup Lithuania, the national startup ecosystem facilitator, under the auspices the Lithuanian Innovation Agency
items.org: Startup Lithuania via Innovation Agency Lithuania
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This initiative offers start-up acceleration services and accelerates at least 60 start-ups.

Startup Lithuania is the national startup ecosystem facilitator between fast-growing business, venture capital funds, accelerators, startup friendly enterprises, and the government.
- Publishing startup ecosystem news, providing startups database and sending a weekly newsletter that covers the ecosystem.
- Organizing startup events: Seminars, Workshops, and Startup Fair – main international startup event in Lithuania.
- Consulting, advising, introducing, networking with stakeholders in everyone in the ecosystem.
- Educating the ecosystem and futurepreneurs.

items.title: Intelligent Digital Economy AlgorithmS (IDEAS) NCBR
items.org: National Centre for Research and Development (NCBR)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
IDEAS is a research and development centre operating in the field of artificial intelligence, whose mission is to support the development of this technology in Poland by creating a platform connecting the academic and business environments.

NCBR is a research and development centre operating in the field of artificial intelligence, established by the National Centre for Research and Development (NCBR). Its mission is to support the development of this technology in Poland by creating a platform connecting the academic and business communities, the largest space in Poland conducts innovative, world-class research, focused on the practical application of developed algorithms and their subsequent commercialisation in industry, finance, medicine, and other branches of the economy. The centre is also implementing grant projects including such funded by the European Research Council (ERC).
In 2023, IDEAS joined the European Lab for Learning & Intelligent Systems (ELLIS) and in 2024, the AI, Data and Robotics Association.

items.title: Institutional and Coordination Framework for Digital Transformation
items.org: Ministry of Investment, Regional Development and Informatization of the Slovak Republic (MIRRI)
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
This governance framework aims to enhance policy coordination, streamline digital transformation efforts, and align Slovakia’s regulatory approach with EU digital regulations.

The Institutional and Coordination Framework for Digital Transformation includes key mechanisms such as the Government Council for Digitalization, the Special Task Force for Digital Governance, and an analysis of the feasibility of establishing a Central Authority for Digital Market Oversight.

items.title: Important Project on Common European Interest in the field of mictroelectronics, including communication technology (IPCEI-ME/CT)
items.org: Ministry of Economy of the Slovak Republic
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Four Slovak companies have been approved by the European Commission to support research, innovation and the first industrial deployment of microelectronics and communication technologies across the value chain.

The Important Project of Common European Interest in Microelectronics and Communication Technology (IPCEI-ME/CT) supports research, innovation, and industrial deployment in microelectronics. It addresses the challenge that Europe needs advanced microelectronics capabilities to remain competitive in technology and communication sectors. Four Slovak companies have been approved by the European Commission to participate, contributing expertise in design, production, and applied research. The project’s main objectives are to advance next-generation microelectronics, develop innovative technologies, and strengthen Europe’s industrial base. By integrating these companies into collaborative R&D and initial industrial deployment, it fosters innovation and technology transfer. This initiative enhances Slovakia’s role in European microelectronics and communication technology development.

items.title: High- and Highest-Performance-Computing for the Digital Age
items.original_name: Hoch- und Höchstleistungsrechnen für das digitale Zeitalter
items.org: German Federal Ministry of Education and Research
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Hoch- und Höchstleistungsrechnen für das digitale Zeitalter
items.body:
This initiative by the BMBF aims to enhance Germany’s position in HPC through targeted investments. The SCALEXA programme focuses on developing new methods and technologies for exascale computing, which enables processing at a scale that is orders of magnitude beyond current capabilities. Secondly, the GreenHPC initiative promotes energy-efficient solutions in EuroHPC, addressing environmental sustainability concerns associated with large-scale computing infrastructures.

This initiative by the German Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF) supports the development of next-generation high-performance computing (HPC) in Germany. It addresses two main challenges: the need for much more powerful computing systems and the high energy consumption of large-scale data centres.
The SCALEXA programme focuses on exascale computing—systems that can perform extremely complex tasks at speeds far beyond current capabilities. These technologies are essential for fields like climate research, AI, and advanced simulations. The goal is to boost Germany’s role in cutting-edge HPC.
In parallel, the GreenHPC initiative promotes energy-efficient computing solutions within the European EuroHPC framework. It supports innovations that reduce the environmental impact of supercomputing, such as better cooling systems and energy-saving software.
Together, these programmes bring research institutions, industry, and government partners together to advance powerful yet sustainable HPC infrastructure in Germany and Europe.

items.title: HealthHub - Center for Innovative Healthcare
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Center for Innovative Healthcare, a European Digital Innovation Hub (EDIH), aims to drive structural reforms, innovation, and digital transformation in Slovakia's healthcare sector to enhance quality and efficiency. By 2025, it plans to establish a network of key Slovak companies and public institutions dedicated to modern healthcare solutions, with AI in healthcare as a priority area.

The Center for Innovative Healthcare, a European Digital Innovation Hub (EDIH), supports digital transformation and innovation in the Slovak Republic's healthcare sector. It addresses challenges such as fragmented systems, limited technology adoption, and the need to improve healthcare quality and efficiency. The center’s objectives include driving structural reforms, fostering innovation, and promoting digital tools across public and private healthcare institutions. AI in healthcare is a priority area, with projects supporting diagnostics, patient management, and clinical decision-making. The center works by connecting key Slovak companies, research institutes, and public bodies, creating a collaborative network for modern healthcare solutions. By establishing this ecosystem, it helps institutions adopt new technologies and modernize healthcare services across the country.

items.title: Health Data Agency
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Belgian Health Data Agency (HDA), working with regional and federal partners, is creating a framework to improve access to quality health and healthcare-related data in a uniform, secure, and transparent way. This framework aims to optimise the re-use of data for purposes such as population health management, prevention, and healthcare policy.

The Health Data Agency (HDA) is reshaping the Belgian health data landscape with a focus on the FAIR principles (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable). Introducing a comprehensive data catalog, the HDA tackles challenges in data access, simplifying the process of finding and combining information. Through strong data governance, the HDA ensures a more uniform, trustworthy, transparent, and secure approach to health data. By supporting research and innovation aligned with health needs and citizen engagement, the HDA contributes to better health outcomes and quality of life.

items.title: Greek satellite in AI-MATTERS
items.org: Laboratory for Manufacturing Systems and Automation (LMS)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This network of seven nodes and one satellite aims to increase the resilience and the flexibility of the European manufacturing sector through the deployment of the latest developments in AI and robotics, and intelligent, autonomous systems for flexible production.

The Greek satellite consists of the Laboratory for Manufacturing Systems and Automation (LMS), which by provides specialised, industrial customised services, products, and technology transfer to businesses, from SMEs to large corporations, aiming to aims to enhance the uptake of AI-based solutions in a) factory optimization, b) human robot interaction, c) circular economy, while exploiting the potential of emerging enabling technologies such as Machine Learning and Generative AI.

items.title: Gauss Centre for Supercomputing
items.org: Joint initiative between Germany's federal and state government, combining the three national supercomputing centres—HLRS, JSC, and LRZ
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Gauss Centre for Supercomputing (GCS) is a collaboration between Germany’s three leading national supercomputing centres: High-Performance Computing Centre Stuttgart (Höchstleistungsrechenzentrum Stuttgart, HLRS), Jülich Supercomputing Centre (JSC), and Leibniz Supercomputing Centre (Leibniz-Rechenzentrum, LRZ) in Garching. GCS provides Germany with HPC resources, supporting a wide range of scientific research and industrial applications.

The main mission for GCS is fostering scientific discovery through use of high-performance computing (HPC) and the sustained development of computer-aided scientific research in Germany and Europe. We achieve our goals by providing the highest level of HPC expertise, services, and support, as well as state-of-the art HPC resources.

items.title: Fraunhofer Society
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Fraunhofer Society consists of 76 institutes across Germany and facilitates the transfer of AI research into business applications. Institutes such as Fraunhofer IAIS, IPA, and IAO support companies—especially SMEs—through AI Innovation Centres with PoC projects, training, and advisory services. Over 250 companies have engaged with these services, with 30% deploying operational AI systems.

The Fraunhofer Society, with 76 institutes across Germany, plays a crucial role in transferring AI research into business applications. Three Fraunhofer Institutes are particularly relevant for the transfer of AI research: 
i) Fraunhofer Institute for Intelligent Analysis and Information Systems (IAIS); 
ii) Fraunhofer Institute for Manufacturing Engineering and Automation (IPA) (Fraunhofer IPA, 2024[318]); and 
iii) Fraunhofer Institute for Industrial Engineering (IAO).
Through their AI Innovation Centre, IPA and IAO offer companies support in exploring, assessing, and implementing AI solutions, including proof-of-concept projects. To date, over 250 companies, including many SMEs, have participated in these programmes, with 30% of them implementing operational AI systems.

items.title: Forestry 4.0 project
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The objective of the FOREST 4.0 project is to establish a Centre of Excellence to transform the forest environment monitoring, data acquisition, and analysis, and capture value from the collected data.

The FOREST 4.0 project in Lithuania aims to create a Centre of Excellence dedicated to advancing how forests are monitored and managed. Its focus is on upgrading data acquisition and analysis methods, using digital and AI-enabled tools to generate richer, more reliable insights.
By building systems that can capture and process large amounts of environmental data, the project seeks not only to improve forest monitoring but also to ensure that this information generates value—for research, policymaking, and practical forest management. The Centre brings together expertise from academia, industry, and technology partners to anchor innovation in the forestry sector.

items.title: Flemish AI Action Plan
items.org: Department of Economy, Science and Innovation
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
In terms of general AI, the Flemish group is moving ahead and is part of European groups. With an AI plan first created in 2019, it has a knowledge centre for data and society to provide legal advice, an AI board in its AI office, and an AI learning academy.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) and machine learning have progressed tremendously in recent years. All sectors and parts of society will be affected in the coming years by AI. Flanders has to be ready for this evolution and even has to take a leading role in rolling out AI.
For that purpose the Flemish Government launched the Flemish AI plan in 2019. It is good for an annual investment of 32 million euros focusses on strategic research, implementation activities, ethical issues and education and training.
According to this plan Flanders should make use of its assets and try to bring the best AI technology to Flanders.

items.title: Flemish AI Action Plan
items.org: Department of Economy, Science and Innovation
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
In terms of general AI, the Flemish group is moving ahead and is part of European groups. With an AI plan first created in 2019, it has a knowledge centre for data and society to provide legal advice, an AI board in its AI office, and an AI learning academy.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) and machine learning have progressed tremendously in recent years. All sectors and parts of society will be affected in the coming years by AI. Flanders has to be ready for this evolution and even has to take a leading role in rolling out AI.
For that purpose the Flemish Government launched the Flemish AI plan in 2019. It is good for an annual investment of 32 million euros focusses on strategic research, implementation activities, ethical issues and education and training.
According to this plan Flanders should make use of its assets and try to bring the best AI technology to Flanders.

items.title: Finnish Bioeconomy Strategy
items.org: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment; Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry; Ministry of the Environment
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Finnish Bioeconomy Strategy 2022-2035 notably promotes the use of AI and other technologies to enhance the efficiency and sustainability of bio-based industries. It supports the development of new bio-based products and services, contributing to Finland’s goal of becoming climate-neutral by 2035.

The goal of Finland’s Bioeconomy Strategy 2022–2035 is to to strengthen bio-based industries while steering the country toward its goal of climate neutrality by 2035. The strategy identifies digitalisation and AI as key tools to raise efficiency, cut emissions, and create more value from renewable resources.
It promotes innovation in areas such as new bio-based materials, advanced processing methods, and sustainable forestry and agriculture. By supporting the development of new products and services, the strategy aims to diversify the economy while reducing dependence on fossil-based raw materials.
Implementation involves collaboration between ministries, research bodies, and industry actors, with measures to foster R&D, scale up pilot projects, and integrate digital tools into bioeconomy sectors. In this way, the strategy links Finland’s climate goals directly with industrial competitiveness and technological development.

items.title: FactoryXChange EDIH
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The FactoryxChange (FXC) consortium is led by Irish Manufacturing Research and also integrates the National Centre for high performance computing (ICHEC), the National Centre for data analytics (INSIGHT).

FXC supports businesses in adopting AI, robotics, cybersecurity, and supply chain solutions, by:
- Enabling businesses to harness AI and other advanced technologies to improve operations.
- Facilitating the digital transformation of SMEs and start-ups through accessible AI solutions.
- Providing expert guidance on AI, robotics, cybersecurity and supply chain solutions and assisting in the adoption, strategy, and implementation of these technologies. 
- Supporting innovation and growth with services like digital advisory, funding, and learning resources.

items.title: FAIR Forward Open Data for Agriculture
items.org: Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (Bundesministerium für wirtschaftliche Zusammenarbeit und Entwicklung, BMZ) promotes environmental sustainability and AI with the FAIR Forward project. It provides partner countries in the Global South with access to climate-smart agricultural advice and includes a practitioner’s guide to green data centres, developed in collaboration with the World Bank, ITU, and GIZ.

FAIR Forward (a BMZ/GIZ initiative under Germany’s AI strategy) works with partner countries to make AI-ready datasets and resources more accessible for practical uses, including agriculture and climate resilience.
