Official materials note work with geo-referenced and satellite data for climate-smart agricultural use-cases, as well as efforts to provide open, non-discriminatory data and models that local actors can reuse.  On the ground, FAIR Forward has supported agriculture pilots (e.g., early-warning and precision-agriculture use cases in Kenya) and tested an Agriculture Information Exchange Platform with farmers and extension workers in Kenya and Bihar, India.

items.title: EquiFund & EquiFund II
items.org: Hellenic Republic in cooperation with the European Investment Fund (EIF)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This programme aims to boost entrepreneurship and innovation in Greece by providing financing to start-ups. Specific funds under the EquiFund umbrella, such as the Innovation Window and the Early-Stage Window, are designed to support tech start-ups, including those working with AI. These funds provide equity financing to help businesses grow from the seed stage to scaling up. EquiFund II focuses on start-ups in the areas of Life sciences & Healthcare and Sustainability & Social impact.

EquiFund is a Greek investment initiative designed to expand access to finance for start-ups and strengthen the country’s innovation ecosystem. Managed with support from the European Investment Fund (EIF) and national partners, it provides equity financing to help young companies move from the seed stage through to growth. Funds within the program - such as the Innovation Window and Early-Stage Window -  target technology-driven firms, including those applying AI. These funds channel capital to entrepreneurs developing scalable solutions, aiming to close the funding gap for high-potential start-ups.
The successor programme, EquiFund II, builds on this model with a focus on Life Sciences & Healthcare and Sustainability & Social Impact, ensuring that investment continues to flow into sectors with both economic and societal relevance.

items.title: EUCAIM – EUropean Federation for CAncer Images
items.org: European Institute for Biomedical Imaging Research (EIBIR)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body: The EUropean Federation for CAncer IMages project includes 76 partners across 14 countries including Portugal, bringing information from more than 91.000 patients with cancer. The EUCAIM’s objective is to build a central repository of cancer images, which will be used to develop and validate AI tools to support clinical decision making, diagnosis, and precision medicine.

items.title: EU4Health Program 2021-2027
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
In Romania, the EU4Health programme supports the creation of a National Health Data Observatory to improve how health information is collected and used for policymaking.
It also backs the development of an integrated e-health system, linking hospitals and digital health records across the country.
A further strand strengthens the digital literacy of medical staff, helping them use e-health tools and data securely in daily practice.

items.title: Digital Transformation of SMEs initiative
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The goal of this programme is to strengthen the digital maturity of the country's small and medium-sized enterprises operating in a wide range of sectors of the economy programme. It supports investments for the development of new products and services in the IT and communications sector and covers costs related to purchasing software, training staff, and integrating new digital solutions, including AI (via vouchers to SMEs).

The programmes target different areas:
Programme I: "Digital Media Tools" supports the SMEs in utilising new digital products and services. Providing vouchers for the acquisition of new digital tools
Programme II: "Development of Digital Products and Services" supports private businesses in implementing investment plans that cover the entire development cycle of digital products and services (new product development).
Programme III: "Digital Transactions" supports small and medium-sized enterprises in Greece, with the aim of adopting modern digital tools that will support the processes of invoicing, issuing and distributing tax documents and making electronic payments.

items.title: Digital Health Slovakia
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Digital Health Slovakia is a non-profit association dedicated to promoting interoperability and standardisation in healthcare within Slovakia. It supports sustainable, patient-centric healthcare by fostering a community of digital health standards users and experts.

Digital Health Slovakia is a non-profit association focused on promoting interoperability and standardisation in healthcare across Slovakia. It addresses challenges related to fragmented health IT systems and inconsistent data formats, which can hinder patient care and system efficiency. The association’s main objectives are to support sustainable, patient-centric healthcare and encourage the adoption of shared digital health standards. It works by fostering a network of healthcare professionals, IT experts, and institutions who implement and exchange knowledge on digital health standards. Through workshops, guidance, and collaboration, Digital Health Slovakia helps improve system compatibility and data exchange between providers. Its efforts contribute to a more connected, efficient, and patient-focused healthcare ecosystem in Slovakia.

items.title: Development and construction of a supercomputer
items.org: Slovak Academy of Sciences and Eviden, the Atos Group
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This project aims to construct high-performance computing capacities, adding to the procurement and operation of publicly accessible national high-performance computing infrastructure, which is set to serve not only the academic community, but also public and state administration institutions, as well as private research and development.

The supercomputer project in Slovakia, led by the Slovak Academy of Sciences in collaboration with Eviden and the Atos Group, addresses the growing need for high-performance computing (HPC) in research and public administration. Many scientific, administrative, and industrial tasks require computing power that exceeds what standard systems can provide, and this project seeks to fill that gap.
The main objective is to develop and operate a national HPC infrastructure that is publicly accessible. This system is designed to support advanced simulations, data analysis, and modeling for a wide range of users, including universities, research institutes, public institutions, and private R&D organizations.
The project involves constructing the physical supercomputing facility, installing hardware and software systems, and integrating it into the national HPC network. The Slovak Academy of Sciences provides scientific oversight, Eviden and the Atos Group contribute technical expertise in design, implementation, and operations, and various end-users from academia, government, and industry access the system for computational needs.

items.title: Development and Implementation of Automated Nursery Plant Thinning and Weeding Technology
items.org: Latvia University of Bioeconomy and Life Sciences (LBTU)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This AI-powered smart weeder uses advanced object-recognition technology to identify and remove unwanted plants with precision. The automated solution enhances efficiency, reduces labour costs, and supports sustainable farming by minimising the need for chemical herbicides.

The AI-powered smart weeder developed under the Latvian LAD project applies object-recognition technology to detect and remove weeds automatically. It attempts to help farmers reduce their reliance on chemical herbicides while maintaining crop health.
The system is designed to improve on-farm efficiency by cutting labour costs and speeding up weed control, offering a practical precision-farming tool that supports both economic and environmental sustainability.

items.title: Developing methodologies and recommendations for assessing the impact of AI technologies on sustainable, healthy and smart food ecosystems
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This project implemented will provide a platform and methodology for assessing the progress and maturity of the food ecosystem in its different parts (primary production, processing, distribution and marketing, consumption and waste management). Based on scientific sources and experience, it will identify the criteria needed to determine the level of maturity in the areas of sustainability, health-friendliness and digitalisation/artificial intelligence, creating a platform to assess maturity.

This project at Kaunas University of Technology (KTU) develops a structured way to assess how food systems are evolving toward sustainability, health, and digitalisation. It creates both a platform and a methodology for measuring maturity across all parts of the food chain, from production to processing, distribution, consumption, and waste management. The framework will be based on scientific literature and practical experience, defining clear criteria for evaluating aspects such as the use of AI, sustainability practices, and health impacts. By doing so, it aims to provide policymakers, businesses, and researchers with a common tool to track progress and identify areas for improvement in building smarter food ecosystems.

items.title: DeepGreen
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
In 2023, DeepGreen project partners launched the first open-source software platform for embedded AI: the Eclipse AIDGE platform.

The DeepGreen project addresses the need for AI systems that can run directly on small, low-power devices. Traditional AI often relies on cloud computing or large data centers, which are not suitable for devices like sensors, wearables, or industrial equipment that require fast, local processing. This creates a barrier to using AI in many real-world applications where speed, privacy, or limited connectivity are concerns.
In response, DeepGreen partners launched the Eclipse AIDGE platform in 2023 — the first open-source software platform dedicated to embedded AI. It allows developers to design, train, and deploy AI models directly on hardware devices, without sending data to external servers. The platform supports energy-efficient AI and helps reduce latency while improving data security. Being open source, it is freely accessible and can be adapted by developers, researchers, and companies of all sizes.
The platform was developed through collaboration between research institutions, technology companies, and open-source communities. It includes tools for building AI models, testing their performance, and running them on different types of hardware. This helps make embedded AI easier to develop and more reliable in everyday use.
By connecting expertise from various fields, the DeepGreen project has created a practical tool for applying AI outside the cloud directly where data is generated and decisions need to be made.

items.title: D4Health Tirol
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Project to integrate the federated secure data infrastructure to link data from hospitals, telemedicine services and Austria's death registry to support the application of machine learning and artificial intelligence in research and routine care.

This Austrian project aims to make better use of health data by securely linking information from hospitals, telemedicine services, and the national death registry. At the moment, these data sources are separate, making it hard to apply machine learning or artificial intelligence effectively in healthcare or research. The project addresses this by building a federated infrastructure, which allows data to be used across systems without moving or duplicating it.
The main goal is to support AI-based research and improve routine care, such as predicting health risks or personalising treatment. Data stays with the original institutions, but can be accessed securely under strict rules to protect privacy. Hospitals, digital health providers, researchers, and public authorities are all involved in building and using this system.

items.title: Crop Optimisation through Sensing, Understanding and Visualisation (CONSUS)
items.org: University College Dublin (UCD); Origin Enterprises PLC
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
CONSUS is a collaborative research partnership between UCD and Origin Enterprises PLC that has been supported through the Science Foundation Ireland (SFI) Strategic Partnership Programme. The project investigated digital, precision agriculture and crop science through a strong multi and inter-disciplinary approach that combined the leading expertise of UCD in data science and agricultural science with Origin’s integrated crop management research, systems, capabilities and on-farm knowledge.

CONSUS (Ireland) was a collaborative research partnership between University College Dublin (UCD) and Origin Enterprises PLC, supported under the Science Foundation Ireland (SFI) Strategic Partnership Programme. Its purpose was to advance digital and precision agriculture by bringing together UCD’s expertise in data science and agricultural science with Origin’s knowledge of crop management systems and on-farm practice.
The project combined research in crop science, digital technologies, and systems integration. By linking academic and industry expertise, the goal of CONSUS was to explore how data-driven methods could improve crop performance and sustainability in real-world farming contexts.

items.title: Control of the metabolic efficiency of selenium and iodine transfer to eggs, using AI technologies and assessment of the bioavailability of these necessary trace elements
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This project, implemented by the KTU Artificial Intelligence (AI) Center, uses AI technologies to assessment of the bioavailability of selenium and iodine in eggs, to assess metabolic efficiency.

This project, led by the Artificial Intelligence Center at Kaunas University of Technology (KTU), applies AI to study the transfer of selenium and iodine into eggs. By analysing metabolic processes, the project seeks to evaluate the bioavailability of these trace elements, which are important for both animal and human nutrition. The use of AI allows researchers to process complex biological data and improve the accuracy of assessments, providing new insights into how dietary supplements affect metabolic efficiency in poultry.

items.title: Company Level Spaces for Learning and Experimentation with AI (KI Lern- und Experimentierräume)
items.org: Federal Minsitry for Labour and Social Affairs
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Part of the New Quality of Work Initiative (Initiative Neue Qualität der Arbeit, INQA), this programme provides SMEs with dedicated spaces to experiment with and learn about AI applications within an operational context. Running from 2019 to 2024, the initiative aimed to demonstrate how AI can enhance workplace practices and benefit SMEs in various industries.

Germany’s INQA “Lern- und Experimentierräume KI” (2019–2024) gave SMEs practical spaces to test AI in workplace settings. Run by the Federal Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs under the New Quality of Work Initiative, it aimed to lower barriers to adoption, involve employees directly, and show how AI can improve work organisation.
The programme’s goals were to (1) lower entry barriers for SMEs, (2) co-design AI with employees and works councils, and (3) generate transferable methods, tools and training. Rather than funding generic research, it backed 11 applied pilots across sectors (e.g., care, manufacturing, services) that combined advisory support, worker participation, and external evaluation. Outputs include practical guides (e.g., on introducing AI in companies) and tested workflows that other firms can reuse.

items.title: Bioeconomy Strategy for R&I
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Investment and Development Agency of Latvia, in collaboration with different stakeholders, is developing a knowledge-intensive bioeconomy strategy for R&I. This strategy integrates aspects of digitalisation within the sector, including the application of AI. The strategy is accompanied by an action plan with defined timelines.

Latvia’s Investment and Development Agency, working with sectoral partners, is drafting a bioeconomy strategy for research and innovation that emphasises knowledge intensity and sustainability. A key feature of the strategy is the integration of digitalisation tools, including AI, to strengthen productivity, resource efficiency, and monitoring across bio-based industries. The strategy is linked to a structured action plan with timelines, ensuring that measures are not only conceptual but also accompanied by concrete steps for implementation. By embedding AI into the broader bioeconomy framework, Latvia aims to align innovation policy with its sustainability goals while giving local firms and research bodies clearer guidance on future priorities.

items.title: Baltic Satellite Service project ML4HealthyForest
items.org: Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This project develops a fully automated AI-powered service that provides objective forest management and thinning recommendations. By leveraging remote sensing data, machine learning, and automated forest growth models, the system enables data-driven decision-making for sustainable forestry practices.

ML4HealthyForest is a project by Baltsat that creates an automated, AI-based decision support tool for forest management. It combines remote sensing data, machine learning, and forest growth models to generate thinning and management recommendations without the need for manual assessment.
The service is designed to give forest owners and managers objective, data-driven guidance, helping them balance productivity with ecological sustainability. By automating monitoring and analysis, it hopes to reduce costs and increase accuracy, making sustainable forestry practices more accessible at scale.

items.title: Archimedes Unit at the Athena Research Center
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Archimedes Unit at the Athena Research Center, which aims to foster basic and applied research and innovation in AI and data science, algorithms by funding visiting researchers as well as PhD candidates, organising systematic training and educational programmes, and building bridges foreign academic institutions.

The Archimedes Unit at the Athena Research Center in Greece was created to strengthen both basic and applied research in AI and data science. It provides a framework for advancing theoretical work on algorithms while also encouraging innovation that can be applied across sectors. The unit supports this mission by funding PhD candidates and visiting researchers, organizing structured training and educational programmes, and building collaborations with international academic partners.

items.title: Ancient Woodlands Ireland project
items.org: Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The project builds on an established framework for identifying ancient woodlands. It will notably integrate AI-derived digital mapping of long-established woodlands.  By developing a methodology for integrating AI-derived digital mapping of historic maps and analysis of contemporary satellite imagery, this project can also help understand long-term changes of other land-cover types.

This project expands work on identifying ancient and long-established woodlands in Ireland by introducing digital and AI-based methods. Building on existing survey frameworks, it seeks to integrate AI-derived mapping from historic maps with analysis of modern satellite imagery. There are two primary goals: to improve accuracy in recognizing long-established woodland areas and to create a methodology that can track long-term land-cover changes more broadly. By combining historical cartographic sources with contemporary remote sensing, the project hopes to provide a replicable approach to understanding how landscapes evolve and where conservation priorities should be focused.

items.title: AiCatalyst
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Association of Artificial Intelligence – AiCatalyst is private network of industry and academic experts aiming to utilise and democratise AI solutions within an ethical, transparent, and explainable framework while, establishing a network between the academic research and innovative entrepreneurship. It is partnered with the European Institute of Technology’s AI Community and the European Digital Innovation Hub ‘Smart Attica'.

AiCatalyst is a Greek association that connects AI experts from industry and academia to promote responsible adoption of artificial intelligence. Its focus is on making AI solutions more accessible while ensuring they are developed within frameworks of ethics, transparency, and explainability. The association acts as a bridge between research and entrepreneurship, supporting collaboration, knowledge exchange, and innovation. Through partnerships with the EIT AI Community and the Smart Attica European Digital Innovation Hub, it links national initiatives to wider European networks.

items.title: Administrative Cloud Strategy (DVS)
items.org: Federal Government Commissioner for Information Technology
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Administrative Cloud Strategy (DVS) is part of Germany’s efforts to enhance digital sovereignty in public administration by establishing a standardized, modular federal cloud infrastructure. The strategy aims to enable interoperability across federal, state, and local government levels by creating open standards and interfaces. It seeks to reduce dependence on single providers by fostering a diverse ecosystem of specialized IT service providers.

The DVS focuses on five key areas: 
i) standardized development platforms, ii) application management, iii) code repository systems, iv) infrastructure services, and iv) a harmonized operational model. These measures collectively aim to make federal cloud solutions interoperable and compatible across all levels of government, thereby enhancing the efficiency and resilience of Germany’s public sector IT systems.

items.title: Acceleration strategy dedicated to the agritech industry
items.org: Ministry of Agriculture and Food Sovereignty
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
France's agritech acceleration strategy supports innovation in agriculture through AI-driven projects and targeted funding. Key initiatives include the development of smart farming solutions and data platforms. Notably, France has funded Agdatahub, a secure data intermediation platform designed to enhance data sharing across the agricultural and agri-food sectors.

France’s agritech acceleration strategy uses AI and France 2030 funding to promote digital farming and data platforms. A central project is Agdatahub, a neutral data intermediary that enables farmers, co-operatives, and agri-food companies to share information securely with clear consent rules. The platform underpins services like traceability, decision support, and interoperability, and is aligned with European initiatives such as Gaia-X and AgriDataSpace. Supported by national funding and private investment, Agdatahub is expanding from national deployment to a role in EU-wide data spaces, positioning France as a leader in agricultural data governance and innovation.

items.title: AI and Data Accelerator in the Field of Food and Agriculture
items.original_name: KI- & Daten-Akzelerator im Bereich Ernährung und Landwirtschaft, KIDA
items.org: Federal Ministry of Food and Agriculture
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: KI- & Daten-Akzelerator im Bereich Ernährung und Landwirtschaft, KIDA
items.body:
As part of the German AI strategy, KIDA serves as a cross-institutional service centre for AI use cases in the agri-food sector. Led by the Federal Ministry of Food and Agriculture (Bundesministerium für Ernährung und Landwirtschaft, BMEL), it enables AI and big data applications in agriculture, supporting subordinate authorities in handling AI and data cases.

Germany’s KIDA centre was set up under the national AI strategy to strengthen the use of artificial intelligence and big data in the agri-food sector. Managed by the Federal Ministry of Food and Agriculture, it provides a shared service for authorities and agencies, helping them design and apply AI-based solutions to agricultural challenges.
The centre develops reference use cases, offers technical guidance, and ensures that data-driven tools are applied responsibly and effectively. By pooling expertise across institutions, KIDA lowers barriers to adoption and creates a foundation for scaling AI in areas such as crop monitoring, food safety, and resource efficiency.

items.title: AI Politeai Lab at the IIT Demokritos
items.org: Institute of Informatics and Telecommunications, NCSR “Demokritos”
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The AI Politeia Lab, a project of the Institute of Informatics and Telecommunications (IIT), one of five National Centres for Scientific Research (NCSR) “Demokritos”, is an interdisciplinary lab set up to explore how to ensure a responsible and sustainable technology-enabled future by fostering innovative academic and industrial research across domains in a virtual environment.

The AI Politeia Lab, part of the Institute of Informatics and Telecommunications (IIT) at NCSR “Demokritos,” is an interdisciplinary research hub in Greece dedicated to studying how AI can be developed and applied responsibly. It was established to combine insights from technology, ethics, and policy in order to shape a sustainable, human-centred digital future. Working in a virtual, cross-domain environment, the lab fosters collaboration between academia and industry, supporting projects that test innovative approaches to governance, accountability, and the social impact of AI. Its role is to serve as a space where technological advances are critically assessed and aligned with long-term societal values.

items.title: AI Department and Institute of Digital Games, University of Malta
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The University of Malta has established an AI excellence research centre through its AI Department and the Institute of Digital Games. The department offers specialisations in various AI fields, including Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Digital Games, Virtual Reality, Augmented Reality, Robotics, Fintech, Big Data, Creative Technologies, Text Processing, IoT, Data Science, AI in Education, Generative AI, and Computer Vision.

The AI research group at the Institute of Digital Games is actively engaged in cutting-edge research at the intersection of AI and games. The group has received numerous awards for their contributions to fields such as AI, machine learning, affective computing, creative computing, and player modelling.

items.title: sustAIn.brussels
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
sustAIn.brussels is a European Digital Innovation Hub (EDIH) based in the Brussels Capital Region. It helps organisations adopt sustainable and digital innovations, including AI and other emerging technologies. The hub supports businesses in future-proofing operations while addressing economic, social, and environmental challenges.

sustAIn.brussels is a European Digital Innovation Hub (EDIH) that provides support and guidance for digital and sustainable transformation in the Brussels Capital Region. It focuses on helping organisations adopt AI, emerging technologies, and sustainable practices to enhance competitiveness and resilience.
Key objectives include:
Promoting digital and sustainable innovation across businessesSupporting the adoption of AI and emerging technologies for practical and scalable solutionsHelping companies address economic, social, and environmental challenges through digital transformationThe hub provides resources, expertise, and networking opportunities to assist organisations in implementing innovative solutions. By fostering collaboration among companies, research institutions, and public stakeholders, sustAIn.brussels helps ensure that digital transformation initiatives are both effective and sustainable.

items.title: eSam
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
41 government agencies are organized through eSam, a public collaboration mechanism for digitalization of the public sector, which has been implementing seven AI-related initiatives in 2023/2024, including i) use of AI in the creation of public documents, ii) Risks and prerequisites for exchanging models for AI development, iii) a common platform for chatbots, iv) practical application of AI solutions (interpretation), v) generative AI-based services, vi) AI for communication ops.

In Sweden, 41 government agencies work together through eSam, a cooperation forum for digitalisation of the public sector. The network coordinates projects to share knowledge, avoid duplication, and accelerate the responsible adoption of new technologies.

items.title: Women Go Tech
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This mentoring programme, implemented by a non-profit association, supports women’s careers in the spheres of IT and engineering, while promoting gender equality in the workplace.

The programme’s main objective is to support women in building the skills, confidence, and networks needed to start or shift their careers into technology. Between 2016 and 2021, 670 women have graduated from the programme, of which almost 500 have successfully started a career in IT or engineering. With the ambition to expand internationally, “Women Go Tech” aims to assist 25 000 women in the CEE region in requalifying for careers in technology by 2024.

items.title: Valbowal
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Valbowal is the Walloon strategic innovation initiative working on forestry. It aims to use AI to develop new construction products allowing a durable carbon capture and storage, but also new conception and production methods.

ValboWal is Wallonia’s strategic innovation initiative for the wood/forestry value chain under the “Circular Materials” domain. It brings together forest owners, processors, builders, research bodies and clusters to make better, higher-value use of regional wood, with the intent to extend product lifetimes, re-use structural timber, and improve traceability and logistics. The aim is to boost the sector’s economic and environmental value while keeping more of the wood’s carbon stored for longer.
In practice, ValboWal coordinates collaborative R&D and pilot projects on circular design and industrialized timber construction, plus digitalization, including AI for quality control, design optimization and process efficiency.

items.title: Transitional study support
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
To facilitate the re-skilling of professionals (not only on AI), in 2022, the government introduced the study support, which gives adults aged between 27 and 62 the opportunity to study and broaden their skills. For one year, professionals can receive a study grant equivalent to 80% of their pre-study salary, and for a further year, they can apply for a student loan.

In a rapidly changing job market, many adults need to update or learn new skills to stay competitive and meet the demands of evolving industries. This challenge is not limited to technology fields like artificial intelligence but affects a wide range of professions. To support working professionals in this transition, the government introduced a study support program in 2022. The program aims to help adults between the ages of 27 and 62 take time to study and expand their skills without losing financial stability.
The main goal of the program is to make it easier for adults to return to education and improve their qualifications, whether they want to specialize in new areas like AI or pursue other fields. To do this, the program offers financial aid that covers part of the individual’s income during their studies. Specifically, for the first year of study, participants receive a grant equal to 80% of their previous salary. This support helps reduce the financial risks involved in leaving work temporarily to focus on learning. After this initial year, those who want to continue their education can apply for a student loan to help cover the costs for a second year.
This initiative involves the government working together with educational institutions and financial agencies to manage the program and provide funding. Eligible adults can apply for this support and choose study programs that fit their career plans and the needs of the labor market. By providing both grants and loans, the program offers a flexible way for professionals to reskill or upskill in a way that suits their individual situations.
The initiative reflects a commitment to lifelong learning, helping workers remain employable and productive as industries evolve, especially with the ongoing impact of technologies like artificial intelligence.

items.title: Transitional study support
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
To facilitate the re-skilling of professionals (not only on AI), in 2022, the government introduced the study support, which gives adults aged between 27 and 62 the opportunity to study and broaden their skills. For one year, professionals can receive a study grant equivalent to 80% of their pre-study salary, and for a further year, they can apply for a student loan.

In 2022, the government launched a new program to help working adults improve and update their skills, not limited to artificial intelligence but covering a wide range of subjects. This initiative addresses the growing need for people to adapt to changes in the job market, where new technologies and shifting industries require continuous learning. Many professionals find it difficult to balance work and study because of financial constraints, so this program aims to make it easier for adults to return to education without losing their income security.
The main goal of this initiative is to support adults aged 27 to 62 who want to re-skill or broaden their knowledge. It gives them a chance to study for up to two years while providing financial assistance to reduce the risk of losing income during this time. For the first year, participants receive a study grant equal to 80% of their previous salary, making it possible to focus on learning without serious financial pressure. After the initial year, they can apply for a student loan to continue their studies for an additional year if needed.
The program works by offering direct financial support to eligible adults who choose to study. It is designed to be flexible, allowing people to pursue education that matches their career goals and the demands of the labor market. The government manages the program, likely in cooperation with educational institutions and financial agencies that handle grants and loans. This setup encourages more adults to take part in lifelong learning, whether by attending universities, polytechnics, or other training programs.
 this initiative has the potential to scale up and adapt as the needs of the workforce change. It provides a foundation for continuous professional development that can help individuals stay relevant in a rapidly evolving job market.

items.title: Towards the Food Factory of the Future
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Towards the Food Factory of the Future is an initiative led by Flanders’ FOOD that aims to drive the digital and sustainable transformation of the agri-food industry in Flanders. By bringing together research institutions, technology providers, and food manufacturers, the initiative fosters collaboration to enhance automation, AI-driven quality control, and energy-efficient production processes. It supports food companies in adopting cutting-edge digital technologies, such as machine learning

Towards the Food Factory of the Future is a roadmap by Flanders’ FOOD to modernize the agri-food sector in Flanders. It connects producers, researchers, and technology providers to make food production smarter, more sustainable, and more people-focused. The initiative targets four areas: better quality control through sensors and data, digital automation, circular use of resources, and workforce skills. Through projects and partnerships, it aims to especially help SMEs test and adopt tools like AI, machine learning, and energy-efficient systems.

items.title: The National Traffic Management Centre (NTMC)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The National Traffic Management Centre (NTMC) in Slovenia collects and analyses road and traffic data. It provides services for traffic control, management, and Intelligent Transport Systems (ITS). The NTMC supports safe and efficient traffic operations across the country.

The National Traffic Management Centre (NTMC) serves as the central hub for traffic data collection, processing, and analysis in Slovenia. Its primary purpose is to act as a data warehouse for all accessible traffic information, enabling authorities to monitor and manage traffic effectively.
Key objectives include:
Providing data and services for Intelligent Transport Systems (ITS)Supporting traffic control and management at national and regional levelsEnhancing road safety and efficiency through real-time information and analyticsThe NTMC became operational through the Coordination of National Access Points (NAPCORE) project, financed and initiated by the Ministry of Infrastructure. The system integrates data from multiple sources to improve traffic planning, forecasting, and response strategies.

items.title: Testing and experimentation facilities
items.org: The Ministry of Economics, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
France participates in the five Testing and experimentation facilities for AI. French players coordinate two of them (PREVAIL and AI MATTERS). France is also coordinating the ALT-EDIC initiative that integrates evaluation activities for advanced AI models.

France participates in the EU network of Testing & Experimentation Facilities (TEFs) to help companies trial AI in real-world settings and de-risk deployment. French actors are involved across all five TEFs and **coordinate two of them—PREVAIL and AI-MATTERS—**bringing national labs, firms, and public bodies together to run large-scale, sector-specific tests and share results.
In parallel, France leads the ALT-EDIC initiative, which integrates evaluation activities for advanced AI models, complementing TEF pilots with common methods, benchmarks, and governance so solutions proven in TEFs can be assessed consistently across the EU.

items.title: Sweden	FFI Strategic Vehicle Research and Innovation
items.org: FFI – Strategic Vehicle Research and Innovation
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The FFI Strategic Vehicle Research and Innovation programme is a joint initiative between the Swedish state and the automotive industry. It supports research and innovation to promote sustainable road transport. The programme funds R&D activities with around SEK 1 billion per year, shared equally between the state and industry.

The FFI Strategic Vehicle Research and Innovation programme, running since 2009, is designed to advance sustainable road transport in Sweden through targeted research and development. It brings together government and industry stakeholders to identify key priorities and fund projects that promote environmental sustainability, efficiency, and technological innovation in the automotive sector.
Key objectives include:
Promoting sustainable road transport through research and innovationFunding research and development activities with a combined annual budget of approximately SEK 1 billionFacilitating collaboration between the Swedish state, automotive manufacturers, and other industry partnersThe programme focuses on projects that address:
Energy-efficient vehicle technologiesLow-emission and electric transport solutionsInnovations in vehicle safety and automation

items.title: Support to SRIP ACS+ Strategic Research Innovation Partnership
items.original_name: Podpora SRIP ACS+ – Strateško partnerstvo za raziskave in inovacije
items.org: Ministry of Higher Education, Science and Innovation
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Podpora SRIP ACS+ – Strateško partnerstvo za raziskave in inovacije
items.body:
The SRIP ACS+ Strategic Research Innovation Partnership in Slovenia supports innovation and R&D in the engineering and automotive sectors. It provides funding and collaboration opportunities for companies, research institutions, and service providers. The ACS+ AV Living Lab offers a real-world environment to test autonomous vehicles and smart mobility technologies.

The SRIP ACS+ initiative is part of Slovenia’s Smart Specialisation Strategy, aiming to strengthen research, innovation, and technology adoption in the engineering and automotive industries. It supports partnerships between businesses, research institutions, and service providers to foster the development of products and services for the automotive supply chain.
Key objectives include:
Enhancing collaboration between industry and R&D partnersPromoting innovation in engineering, manufacturing, and automotive technologiesProviding a real-world testing environment through the ACS+ AV Living Lab for autonomous vehicles and smart mobility solutionsThe ACS+ AV Living Lab allows partners to develop, test, and validate automated transport technologies in realistic conditions. This contributes to faster technology adoption, reduces risks in innovation, and strengthens Slovenia’s position in the smart mobility and automotive sector.

items.title: Supek Supercomputer
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Operated by the University of Zagreb, the Supek Supercomputer is Croatia's first petascale supercomputer, offering energy-efficient, high-performance computing with 1.25 petaFLOPS capacity.

Located at the University Campus Borongaj in Zagreb, it provides advanced computing capabilities for resource-intensive academic applications across various fields of research.

items.title: Slovakia	Strategic Transport Development Plan of the Slovak Republic until 2030
items.original_name: Strateški načrt razvoja prometa Slovaške republike do leta 2030
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Strateški načrt razvoja prometa Slovaške republike do leta 2030
items.body:
The Strategic Transport Development Plan of the Slovak Republic until 2030 focuses on integrating AI technologies into transport infrastructure. It aims to improve traffic management, safety, and efficiency across road, rail, and water transport. The plan supports the development of intelligent transport systems (ITS) and multimodal transport solutions.

The Strategic Transport Development Plan of the Slovak Republic until 2030 sets out a comprehensive roadmap for modernizing Slovakia’s transport sector using AI and digital technologies. It emphasizes the systematic development of Intelligent Transport Systems (ITS) to enable real-time traffic management, automation, and operational efficiency across all transport modes.
Key objectives include:
Road transport: Developing peripheral infrastructure on highways and major roads to support intelligent transport technologiesRail transport: Modernizing the European Railway Traffic Management System (ERTMS) and the European Train Control System (ETCS) to improve automation and safetyWater transport: Implementing River Information Services (RIS) with AI-driven systems for better navigation and operational efficiencyMultimodal transport: Enhancing AI-based models for planning and operational coordination across transport modesThe plan reflects Slovakia’s commitment to adopting AI technologies in line with broader EU standards and objectives, aiming to increase safety, optimize traffic flows, and improve overall transport functionality. Implementation involves collaboration between national authorities, infrastructure providers, and technology developers to ensure cohesive and efficient deployment of AI solutions.

items.title: Skillsbridges
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
In the 2024/2025 academic year, Luxembourg's Ministry of Education is launching Skillsbridges, a new short-term professional training program. Aimed at helping adults adapt to evolving technologies and the changing job market, the initiative focuses on both upskilling and reskilling. Skillsbridges target a diverse audience, including both employed individuals and job seekers, addressing labor shortages and supporting professional transitions.

Programs covers a range of topics, including AI for administrative teams, and was delivered in person or through blended learning, with courses ranging from 40 to 240 hours.

items.title: Single Horizontal AI Platform
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Ministry of Digital Transformation has developed the pilot prototype “Semantični analizator” (Semantic Analyser), an open-source tool using AI techniques to process natural language. Building on these experiences, a single horizontal AI platform is planned for development to facilitate the processing of both public and non-public data. The platform will be modular, flexible, scalable, and upgradeable, ensuring adaptability to the diverse needs and requirements of individual authorities.

Slovenia’s Ministry of Digital Transformation has piloted an open-source tool called Semantični analizator (Semantic Analyser), which uses AI to process natural language. The prototype intends to demonstrate how AI can help public authorities manage and interpret growing volumes of text data more efficiently. By creating a unified AI infrastructure, the initiative seeks to provide cost-effective, flexible solutions that strengthen digital transformation across Slovenian administration.

items.title: SatGrass
items.org: Copernicus satellites from the European Earth Observation Programme
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Copernicus satellites from the European Earth Observation Programme can continuously monitor grassland and its use at the field level with high spatial resolution. The SatGrass project combines remote sensing and weather data into a model, calibrated with regional yield measurements and quality assessments, to analyse vegetation dynamics.

SatGrass has two main goals: i) Identify usage timings from Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 data to estimate yields, and ii) estimate yield and fodder quality dynamics over the vegetation period, considering usage, weather, and water balance. Locally, SatGrass helps farmers optimise cutting times to improve yield and quality. Regionally, it contributes to Austria's agricultural accounts and supports planning climate adaptation strategies to address the impacts of climate change on grassland and livestock farming.

items.title: SIRIUS Simulator Project
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The SIRIUS Simulator Project, led by Jetpack.AI, develops a decision support system for electricity network operators. It helps Distribution System Operators (DSOs) plan long-term investments and adapt grids to the increasing integration of renewable energy. The project provides data-driven insights to improve sustainable grid management.

The SIRIUS Simulator Project is designed to support electricity distribution network planning in the context of the energy transition. By providing a decision support system, it enables Distribution System Operators (DSOs) to make informed long-term investment decisions, taking into account the growing role of renewable energy sources.
Key objectives of the project include:
Improving planning and management of electricity distribution networksIntegrating renewable energy efficiently into existing gridsProviding data-driven insights to support sustainable and resilient network operationsThe tool combines advanced simulation capabilities with real-world data to model different investment scenarios and operational constraints. It allows DSOs to anticipate future challenges and optimize infrastructure development in line with environmental and regulatory goals.

items.title: Regional/local AI networks
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Several regional and local AI networks have developed in France, with missions including network development, raising awareness of the benefits of AI, and technology demonstration.

France counts 16 EDIHs with many of those focused on AI. In addition, regional and local AI networks have developed:
• Cité de l’IA : Based in the Hauts-de-France region. Aimed at creating a network and raising awareness among entrepreneurs and business executives on the benefits of AI and on opportunities to launch projects. Physical and virtual events (e.g. conferences, workshops) organised. A training certification for “AI project manager” roles is under development. 
• Maison de l’Intelligence Artificielle: Based in the Provence-Alpes-Côte-d’Azur region, and similar to Cité de l’IA. The main objective is also the acculturation of the public with a focus here not only on companies but also on young students. Dedicated spaces for demonstrating AI technologies as well as an AI lab and a training room for conferences and talks available.
• Industrial Council for AI Research: Group of large companies with research labs based in the Provence-Alpes-Côte-d’Azur region. Discussion about trends in AI and exchange of best practices.

items.title: REASSURE
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The REASSURE project develops a data analytics toolkit to improve the reliability of sustainable energy systems. It uses context-aware and predictive models to enhance energy efficiency and system robustness. The initiative helps energy networks adapt to changing conditions and operate more sustainably.

The REASSURE project, launched in 2022 in Belgium, focuses on improving the reliability and efficiency of sustainable energy systems through advanced data analytics. Its primary goal is to provide tools that allow energy operators to assess and optimise the performance of energy networks under varying conditions.
Key objectives include:
Developing a context-aware data analytics toolkit for energy systemsIntegrating predictive models to anticipate potential issues and improve reliabilityOptimising energy efficiency and sustainability across networksThe toolkit combines real-time data analysis with contextual information to ensure energy systems are robust, adaptable, and resilient. REASSURE supports decision-making for energy operators and policymakers, helping them manage both current operations and future energy challenges.

items.title: Projects focusing on AI-based solutions in agriculture under the research and development programme
items.org: Ministry of Food, Agriculture and Fisheries
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Under the research and development programme “Grønt Udviklings- og Demonstrationsprojekt” (GUDP), there are several examples of projects funded that investigate AI-based solutions in agriculture. GUDP supports the development and demonstration of knowledge and technologies that can make the food sector of the future greener. The second application round in 2025 with a focus on reducing emissions and nitrogen is now open for applications.

Denmark’s Green Development and Demonstration Programme (GUDP) funds projects that bring new technologies into practice in the food sector. Recent calls have highlighted AI-based tools for precision farming and emission reduction, encouraging collaborations between companies, researchers, and producers. The 2025 round places particular emphasis on lowering nitrogen use and greenhouse gas emissions, with support aimed at solutions that can deliver both environmental and economic benefits.

items.title: Programme to Support Applied Research of the Ministry of Agriculture for the period 2024 – 2032
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Ministry of Agriculture supports the development and implementation of AI within the framework of the Programme to Support Applied Research of the Ministry of Agriculture for the period 2024 – 2032. The programme is implemented in accordance with key strategic documents in the field of research, development and innovation (RDI). AI is supported under the Smart Farming area, which is one of the key areas of this programme.

The Czech Ministry of Agriculture runs a long-term Programme to Support Applied Research (2024–2032) that aligns with national RDI priorities and strategic policy goals. Within this framework, artificial intelligence is promoted under the Smart Farming area, which focuses on improving efficiency, sustainability, and resilience in agriculture.
By funding applied research projects, the programme helps integrate AI tools into areas such as precision farming, resource management, and livestock monitoring. It supports collaboration between research institutes, agribusinesses, and technology developers, aiming to deliver practical innovations that strengthen both the farming sector and national food security.

items.title: Prognostic Health Management and Improving Energy Production of Wind Turbine Parks
items.original_name: Prognostisch Gezondheidsbeheer en Verbetering van de Energieproductie van Windturbineparken
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Prognostisch Gezondheidsbeheer en Verbetering van de Energieproductie van Windturbineparken
items.body:
The Prognostic Health Management and Improving Energy Production of Wind Turbine Parks project uses AI for predictive maintenance in wind farms. It aims to optimise energy production, improve turbine reliability, and reduce operational costs. The initiative is part of Belgium’s broader Flanders AI Research Programme supporting AI innovation in the energy sector.

The project focuses on predictive maintenance and health management for wind turbine parks. By leveraging advanced AI techniques, it analyses operational data to predict failures, schedule maintenance efficiently, and enhance overall turbine performance. This approach reduces downtime and operational costs while maximising energy output.
Key objectives include:
Optimising energy production through AI-driven predictive analyticsImproving turbine reliability by anticipating maintenance needs before failures occurReducing operational costs by enhancing maintenance efficiency and asset managementSupporting AI integration in the energy sector as part of broader research and innovation effortsThe initiative is embedded within the Flanders AI Research Programme, which fosters collaboration between research institutions, energy companies, and technology providers. This ensures that AI solutions are both scientifically robust and practically applicable to real-world energy infrastructure.

items.title: Priority Research Programme and Equipment (PEPR) on Artificial Intelligence
items.org: Ministry of Higher Education and Research; ANR
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
As part of the national strategy for AI, it aims to develop breakthrough technologies that can help position France and Europe as leaders in strategic AI fields.

The programme is structured around three major research topics, that correspond to the key issues surrounding AI and sovereignty:
• Research on frugal AI and embedded AI - rationalise energy consumption of AI systems based on machine learning.
• Research on trustworthy and distributed AI -advance the state of the art in terms of robustness, confidentiality, and system security.
• Research on the mathematical foundations of AI to build and analyse the foundations of AI systems.

items.title: PAIDEIA project
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The PAIDEIA project is designed to upskill teachers in the use of AI in education and to develop an AI-related competence framework.

This competence framework aims to equip teachers with the skills and knowledge needed to integrate AI into teaching practices [106K].

items.title: Open Data Government Strategy / Laws
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
Several noteworthy initiatives:
Livre III du code des relations entre le public et l’administration. 
Justice administration :
•	2016 Law for a Digital Republic which lays the foundation of open public data: LOI n° 2016-1321 de 2016 pour une République numérique. 
•	Decree 2023-1199 on automatic per-sonal data treatment.
•	Open data related to court decisions have been publicly available since 2021 for the Supreme Court, and since 2022 for appeal courts in the civil, social and business.

In France, there has been a growing effort to make the justice system more transparent and accessible through digital means. Traditionally, court decisions and judicial information were not easy for the public to access, which limited understanding and trust in how justice is delivered. To address this, French lawmakers and institutions have launched several important initiatives aimed at opening up judicial data and using digital technology to improve public access to legal information.
One key step was the 2016 Law for a Digital Republic (Loi n° 2016-1321), which set the foundation for open public data in France. This law encouraged the government to share data more openly and laid the groundwork for making justice-related information publicly available. More recently, a 2023 decree (Décret n° 2023-1199) was introduced to regulate how personal data is automatically processed, ensuring that privacy rights are respected even as data becomes more accessible. These legal tools balance the need for openness with the protection of sensitive information.
As part of this initiative, France has made significant progress in publishing court decisions online. Since 2021, decisions from the French Supreme Court (Cour de cassation) have been openly available to the public. In 2022, this transparency was extended to include decisions from appeal courts in civil, social, and business matters. This allows lawyers, researchers, journalists, and citizens to consult real court rulings, helping to better understand how justice is applied across the country. Government agencies, courts, and data platforms work together to collect, anonymize where necessary, and publish these decisions in a clear and accessible way.

items.title: Net Zero Cities
items.org: Municipalities of Ljubljana, Kranj, and Velenje
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Net Zero Cities pilot in Ljubljana, Kranj, and Velenje upgrades urban digital platforms with public transport and traffic data. It integrates multiple data sources and installs new equipment to improve measurement accuracy. The pilot also develops a Mobility-as-a-Service (MaaS) mobile application to enhance sustainable urban mobility.

The Net Zero Cities pilot in Slovenia (2023–2025) focuses on improving urban mobility and data-driven city management across Ljubljana, Kranj, and Velenje. The initiative upgrades the cities’ digital platforms by integrating data from public transport operators and other sources, while installing additional sensors and equipment for more accurate and comprehensive data collection.
Key objectives include:
Enhancing the accuracy of traffic and mobility dataIntegrating multiple data sources to create unified platforms for urban mobility managementDeveloping MaaS mobile applications to improve public transport access and efficiencyThe pilot allows city planners, transport operators, and citizens to make better-informed decisions. It also supports Net Zero goals by promoting sustainable mobility and reducing emissions through smarter transport solutions.

items.title: National Real-Time Water Management System
items.original_name: Национална система за управление на водите в реално време
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Национална система за управление на водите в реално време
items.body:
The National Real-Time Water Management System in Bulgaria uses advanced technologies, including AI, to monitor and manage the country’s water resources. It tracks factors such as precipitation, snowmelt, and river flow in real time. The system aims to improve flood risk assessment and disaster preparedness.

The National Real-Time Water Management System is being developed as part of Bulgaria’s flood risk management measures. It is designed to provide continuous monitoring and analysis of the country’s water resources using advanced digital and AI tools.
Key goals include:
Monitoring critical factors such as precipitation, snowmelt, and river flows in real timeAssessing flood risks more accurately and earlierImproving disaster preparedness and response capacity at national and regional levelsBy integrating AI and real-time data into water resource management, the system will enable faster decision-making and better coordination between authorities responsible for flood prevention and emergency response. It represents a shift from reactive to proactive water management.

items.title: National Health Data Infrastructure
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
With recent legislative updates, the federal government, states, regional health funds, and the umbrella association of social insurance carriers are now required to establish and operate a national platform for the secondary use of health data. This platform, currently in development, aims to enable coordinated secondary use of health data by relevant public health authorities to inform public health policies.

Austria is developing a national platform to make better use of health data that has already been collected. This is known as "secondary use" of data — using information not to treat individual patients, but to help improve public health policies and healthcare planning. At present, much of this data is stored separately by hospitals, insurance providers, and health authorities, making it difficult to get a complete picture of the healthcare system. This new platform aims to solve that problem by bringing data together in a secure and coordinated way.
Recent legal changes require several public bodies to work together on this project. These include the national government, the provinces (Länder), regional health insurance funds, and the main social insurance organisation. Together, they are responsible for setting up and running the platform. The main goal is to allow public health authorities to analyse anonymised health data so they can make better decisions — for example, to track how diseases spread, improve the quality of care, or identify where the health system needs more support.
Although still under development, the platform will be built with strong protections for privacy and data security.

items.title: National Competence Center for HPC (EuroCC)
items.org: Ministry of the Economy and Sustainable Development / Central State Office for the Development of the Digital Society
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The National Competence Centre for high-performance computing (HPC) in Croatia serves as the central point of contact for HPC, High-Performance Data Analytics (HPDA), and AI Croatia. The Centre is a consortium led by the University Computing Centre, University of Zagreb, and includes several Croatian institutions such as the University of Zagreb, University of Osijek, University of Split, Ruđer Bošković Institute, and University of Rijeka.

This collaborative effort ensures a comprehensive approach to HPC services and expertise across the country.

items.title: NL AIC Working Group on Human Capital
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
As part of the NL AIC, the Human Capital Working Group focuses on improving AI education and reskilling efforts in the Netherlands.

By collaborating with various stakeholders, this working group aims to develop a workforce ready to capitalise on AI's societal and economic opportunities, with particular attention to filling talent gaps in AI across sectors.

items.title: NL AIC Training Platform
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The NL AIC launched a platform that provides an overview of over 600 university programmes, both ICT-focused and non-ICT, aimed at incorporating AI into higher education.

This initiative seeks to align and improve AI-related curricula, ensuring that AI skills are integrated across disciplines to prepare students for the growing demand for AI expertise in various fields​.

items.title: Luxembourg Tech School (LTS)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Luxembourg Tech School (LTS) is a digital education initiative allowing students aged 12 to 19 to learn about cutting-edge technologies while gaining business and industry knowledge. As a three-month extracurricular program, LTS uses a project-based approach to develop future digital leaders by involving students in hands-on, team-based projects in fields like coding, game development, fintech, AI, and space.

This initiative, with over 200 students participating across more than 10 schools, empowers young learners to apply technology in real-world and creative contexts, helping to meet Luxembourg’s growing demand for digital skills.

items.title: Kvanttinova piloting environment for microelectronics and quantum technology
items.org: VTT, Aalto University, Enter Espoo, FICCC, ChipsJU, Business Finland
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Finland will form an RDI environment and business cluster for specialised microelectronics and quantum technology, which will be one of the largest and most significant in Europe. These will enable the scaling of new products and services to an industrial scale. Co-financing of the EU Chips Act in accordance with the Government Programme will be ensured, and Business Finland will implement the chip technology programme. Preparations will be made for the establishment of a chip centre in Finland.

Finland is building a major research, development, and innovation (RDI) environment focused on specialised microelectronics and quantum technology. The aim is to establish one of the most significant technology clusters in Europe, enabling the development and scaling of new products for industrial use. This responds to the growing need for advanced, secure chip technologies and supports both national competitiveness and Europe's technological independence.
The initiative aligns with the EU Chips Act and includes national co-financing as outlined in Finland’s government programme. Business Finland will lead the implementation through a dedicated chip technology programme, and preparations are underway for a national chip centre. This centre will serve as a hub for research, testing, training, and collaboration between industry and academia.
In the Kvanttinova ecosystem, innovative circuit design and advanced materials are brought together to create new devices and products from technologies such as MEMS and MOEMS, CMOS, cryogenics, quantum, RF components, integrated photonics, and 2D materials. These technologies are essential for building the next generation of microelectronics and quantum devices that are smaller, faster, and more efficient.
The initiative will support companies of all sizes and foster strong collaboration between research institutions and industry. It also aims to develop local expertise and strengthen Finland’s long-term capabilities in chip and quantum technologies.

items.title: Interministerial framework for data administration
items.original_name: Cadre interministériel d’administration de la donnée
items.org: Ministry of Public Sector Transformation and the Civil Service
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.document_name: Cadre interministériel d’administration de la donnée
items.body:
As part of the public policy on data, algorithms and source codes, this document specifies the interministerial framework for administrations must register and describes the associated service offering. It covers data, algorithms, and source codes.

Governments today rely increasingly on data, algorithms, and software to provide public services and make decisions. However, managing these digital tools in a transparent and consistent way is a challenge. To address this, the government introduced a public policy focused on data, algorithms, and source codes. This policy sets out clear rules and a framework for government departments and agencies to register and document the data they use, the algorithms they develop, and the source codes behind their software. The aim is to improve transparency, coordination, and trust in how digital resources are managed across the public sector.
The main objective of this initiative is to create a unified approach to handling important digital assets within the government. By registering data sets, algorithms, and source codes in an organized system, administrations can avoid duplication of efforts, ensure quality and security, and provide easier access to these resources when needed. This approach helps different government bodies share knowledge and collaborate more effectively while also making it easier for citizens to understand how public digital tools work.
The framework involves multiple government ministries working together to establish common standards and practices. It defines how administrations should document their digital tools and outlines the services that support this registration process. This includes digital platforms where data and code can be stored and accessed, along with guidelines to ensure that information is kept up to date and properly maintained. The cooperation between ministries ensures that the policy is consistently applied across all government agencies.

items.title: Innocities
items.org: Finnish Government and participating university cities
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The state has signed long-term agreements with InnoCities on the allocation of RDI funding to strengthen globally competitive ecosystems. InnoCities covers all Finnish university and university consortium cities. The implementation mainly takes place with the financing of sustainable urban development of the EU programme period 2021–2027. The agreements develop close cooperation networks for innovation activity ecosystems, strengthen competence areas and increase the effectiveness of RDI.

Finland’s InnoCities initiative intends to tackle a common challenge: research and innovation activity is often fragmented, making it hard for regions to build globally competitive strengths. By coordinating funding and collaboration across all Finnish university and university-consortium cities, the programme seeks to pool capabilities, focus on shared priorities, and turn research into impactful solutions for businesses and society.
The main objectives are to strengthen regional innovation ecosystems, deepen cooperation between cities, universities, companies and public actors, and grow specific competence areas where Finland can compete internationally. Long-term agreements between the state and InnoCities set clear expectations for results and ensure that research, development and innovation (RDI) spending produces measurable impact across regions. In practice, implementation is largely financed through the EU’s 2021–2027 programme period for sustainable urban development.

items.title: Incubator of AI solutions for the public administration
items.org: Ministry for Digital Transformation and Civil Service
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Incubator focused on AI-based solutions for public sector organizations, with a focus on use cases involving generative AI. Although no public announcement had been issued at the time of writing, Spanish authorities report having received more than 300 requests from ministries. A prioritization protocol and development guidelines for the use cases are being developed.

Spain is preparing a new incubator focused on AI solutions for the public sector, with particular attention to generative AI. The aim is to develop practical use cases that can improve government services and administrative efficiency. Even before its launch, authorities received more than 300 requests from ministries for potential applications, showing strong demand across government.

items.title: Human Capital Agenda ICT
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Human Capital Agenda ICT, led by the Platform Talent for Technology, addresses the growing need for ICT talent in the Netherlands, including AI specialists.

This initiative works to attract and retain digital talent through training, reskilling, and initiatives aimed at closing the AI skills gap in the workforce.

items.title: Forest data collection and management
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Building on the Finnish open forest data system, which was launched in March 2018, new solutions are being developed for forest data collection and management. Many of these solutions involve the use of AI. The most recent projects use accurate forest maps and autonomous drones to help improve the harvesting quality. It is also being studied how gamified mobile apps can be used in the collection of forest data. There is also work on digital twins of forests.

Finland’s open forest data system, launched in 2018, made detailed information on forest resources freely accessible. This has created opportunities to modernize forest management through digital tools and AI. The aim is to support sustainable harvesting, improve efficiency, and provide new services for both forest owners and the wider bioeconomy.
Recent projects focus on advanced data collection methods. High-resolution forest maps and autonomous drones are being tested to monitor stands and guide harvesting operations with greater precision. Researchers are also exploring the use of digital twins of forests, which can simulate growth and management options, as well as gamified mobile apps that encourage users to contribute field data.

items.title: ForeSight Project
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The ForeSight Project is a European collaborative initiative that uses AI-powered tools to help civil protection agencies respond to emergencies. It focuses on predicting and managing wildfires and urban incidents. By combining advanced AI algorithms and real-time data, the project enhances safety and emergency response efficiency.

The ForeSight Project aims to strengthen the capabilities of civil protection agencies through AI-driven decision support systems. It provides tools that allow authorities to predict, monitor, and manage emergencies, including wildfires and urban crises, more effectively and proactively.
Key objectives include:
Developing AI algorithms for emergency prediction and risk assessmentIntegrating real-time data sources to improve situational awarenessEnhancing coordination and decision-making during emergency response operationsThe project is collaborative at the European level, bringing together research institutions, technology providers, and civil protection agencies. By leveraging shared expertise and advanced technology, it ensures that AI solutions are both practical and scalable across different regions.

items.title: Flanders Research Institute for Agriculture, Fisheries and Food (ILVO)
items.org: Research Institute for Agriculture, Fisheries and Food (ILVO)
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
ILVO conducts various AI-based projects, such as precision farming using data technology, climate-smart agriculture, and robotics for agrifood. It participates in the Testing & Experimentation Facility for AI on Agrifood, co-funded by the Flemish Government.

ILVO (Flanders Research Institute for Agriculture, Fisheries and Food) runs multiple AI-driven projects across the agrifood chain, including precision farming with sensor and satellite data, climate-smart cultivation (e.g., yield and disease forecasting), and field/packhouse robotics for monitoring and selective interventions. The goal is to help farmers and processors make better, faster decisions that cut inputs, raise quality, and reduce environmental impact.
ILVO is also a core partner in the EU Testing & Experimentation Facility for AI in Agrifood (TEF-Agrifood), co-funded by the Flemish Government.

items.title: FFI Traffic Safe Automation
items.org: FFI – Strategic Vehicle Research and Innovation
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The FFI “Traffic Safe Automation” programme in Sweden develops innovative solutions to make road safety a driver of vehicle automation. It focuses on safe, connected and automated vehicles that are prepared for sharing, aiming to improve road safety and promote sustainable transport.

The FFI “Traffic Safe Automation” programme is a national Swedish initiative that seeks to ensure road safety becomes a key force behind vehicle automation. By focusing on connected and automated vehicles (CAVs) designed for sharing, the programme addresses both safety and sustainability in road transport.
Its objectives include:
