Developing innovative solutions for traffic-safe automationPromoting safe, connected and automated vehicles prepared for sharingMaking road safety a central driver in the development of automation technologiesSupporting the transition to sustainable transport systems in SwedenThe programme is part of FFI – Strategic Vehicle Research and Innovation, a collaboration between Sweden’s government, automotive industry, and research organisations. It funds and coordinates R&D projects that bring together companies, universities, and public agencies to test and deploy new technologies.

items.title: European Master for High Performance Computing (EUMaster4HPC)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The EUMaster4HPC is a new EU-funded Master’s program aimed at developing a highly skilled workforce in HPC to support Europe’s digital transformation. Coordinated by the University of Luxembourg, the program brings together expertise from European universities, research centres, and industry to create a comprehensive graduate-level curriculum.

The two-year programme covers HPC fundamentals, offers specializations, mentorship, and internships, and is designed to equip students with the skills needed to drive the adoption of HPC technologies across Europe.

items.title: European Innovation Partnership Operational Groups
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The European Innovation Partnership Operational Groups in Bulgaria support innovative projects in agriculture, focusing on the integration of technologies such as AI and robotics. The initiative encourages collaboration among farmers, researchers, and SMEs to develop practical solutions that address real-world agricultural challenges.

In Bulgaria, European Innovation Partnership (EIP) Operational Groups bring together farmers, researchers, and SMEs to co-develop practical solutions for agriculture. Their projects often test and apply technologies such as AI, robotics, and precision farming tools, aiming to improve productivity, sustainability, and resilience. By fostering collaboration across the sector, a primary goal of this initiative is to ensure that innovations respond directly to real challenges faced on the ground.

items.title: EuroCC Cyprus
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Cyprus NCC hosts activities, strengthens competences and provides services to the Cyprus and regional computational communities in the fields of High Performance Computing (HPC), Machine Learning (ML), Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Data Science (DS) and their application in industry, academia and public sector.

The Cyprus NCC is part of a network of National Competence Centers in Europe made up of over 30 participating states established within the the EuroHPC EuroCC projects.

items.title: Elements of AI – Luxembourg
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Elements of AI course in Luxembourg offers a free, accessible introduction to artificial intelligence, tailored for individuals from all backgrounds.

The program combines online learning with webinars from local AI experts and support groups, helping participants understand AI’s fundamentals and its real-world applications. Upon completion, learners receive a certificate from the University of Luxembourg, contributing to the country’s goal of improving digital skills across its population.

items.title: Drive Sweden
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
Drive Sweden is a national Swedish initiative that develops and tests sustainable, connected, and automated mobility solutions. It brings together over 200 partners from business, academia, and the public sector. By financing innovations, it makes new AI-based transport solutions technically, commercially, and legally feasible.

Drive Sweden is a national strategic innovation programme launched in 2015 to build a more sustainable and efficient transportation system. It is jointly financed by Vinnova, the Swedish Energy Agency, and Formas. The programme coordinates a large ecosystem of over 200 stakeholders, including companies, research institutes, universities, and public authorities.
The programme’s objectives include:
Developing and testing shared, connected, and automated mobility solutions, including AI-based technologiesMaking new transport solutions technically, commercially, and legally feasibleEnsuring innovations are socially and environmentally beneficialDrive Sweden finances research, development, and pilot projects to demonstrate digitised, connected, and shared mobility services. AI plays a key role in many of these projects, from traffic prediction to autonomous vehicle systems and new business models for shared transport.

items.title: Digitisation of Railway and Road Infrastructure – Digitisation of Road Traffic
items.original_name: Digitalizacija železniške in cestne infrastrukture – digitalizacija cestnega prometa
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Digitalizacija železniške in cestne infrastrukture – digitalizacija cestnega prometa
items.body:
The Digitisation of Road Traffic project in Slovenia modernises the country’s road infrastructure management using digital technologies. It provides real-time information on traffic conditions and vehicle movement. The initiative aims to improve traffic efficiency, interoperability, and safety.

The Digitisation of Railway and Road Infrastructure – Digitisation of Road Traffic project (2021–2025) is led by Slovenia’s Ministry of Infrastructure. The initiative focuses on modernising road traffic management by integrating digital tools and systems that collect and exchange data in real time.
Key objectives include:
Ensuring interoperability between traffic systems and infrastructureEnhancing traffic safety by providing accurate and timely informationImproving efficiency in road traffic managementFacilitating real-time data acquisition and exchange regarding road infrastructure conditions and vehicle movementThe project enables better decision-making for traffic authorities and road users, supporting both operational efficiency and long-term infrastructure planning. It leverages digitalisation and data-driven management to optimise traffic flows and improve the safety of road networks.

items.title: Digital Nose
items.org: University of Applied Sciences Upper Austria
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Digital Nose project uses AI to detect stress-induced volatile organic compounds from trees and insect pheromones, combined with image data of typical damage patterns, to develop an early warning system for tree diseases, enabling climate-smart forestry and timely reactions to climate stress in forests.

The Digital Nose project tackles a core forestry challenge: early, non-invasive detection of tree stress and pest outbreaks. Its goal is to build an AI-enabled early-warning system that helps forest managers react sooner to drought, disease, and insect attacks—key for climate-smart forestry.
How it works: sensors capture stress-related volatile organic compounds (VOCs) from trees and insect pheromones, while imaging records typical damage patterns. AI models fuse these signals to flag emerging problems before they become visible at scale, with the goal of enabling targeted interventions and reducing losses.

items.title: Digital Commons for Generative Artificial Intelligence
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This call for projects aims to create and make accessible digital commons across the entire generative AI value chain to foster the development of innovative products or services.

France’s Digital Commons for Generative AI call addresses a key barrier to adoption: critical AI resources (data, models, tools, benchmarks) are scattered, proprietary, or hard to reuse. The aim is to build shared, open assets that lower costs and let innovators focus on real products and services. Its objectives are to create reusable “digital commons” across the whole gen-AI value chain, including curated datasets, foundation and domain models, evaluation suites, tooling, documentation, and governance. The call encourages collaboration between companies, research labs, and public actors to ensure quality, interoperability, and responsible use.
Projects funded under the call are expected to deliver accessible resources and demonstrators that others can adopt or build on.

items.title: Digibiocontrol
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Digibiocontrol focuses on integrating AI and digital tools into biocontrol solutions for agriculture. The initiative supports farmers in using data-driven strategies to optimise pest and disease management, promoting sustainable and eco-friendly agricultural practices.

Many farms lack easy-to-use digital tools and reliable data to time interventions. This initiative brings AI and digital technologies into biocontrol so decisions are based on evidence rather than routine spraying. Its objectives are to help farmers adopt data-driven strategies, improve the timing and targeting of biological control agents, and cut environmental impact. It does this by combining field and greenhouse data (e.g., sensors, scouting apps, imagery, weather) with AI models that predict pest pressure and recommend actions.

items.title: Develop and upscale quantum compute capacity
items.org: VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Further to the announcement by VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland that they would continue the development of a quantum computer with a minimum of 50 qubits for use in Finland by 2025, in its 2023 budget session, the Government of Finland allocated EUR 70 million to VTT for upscaling the quantum computer to 300 qubit by 2027. HPC will be leveraged through the development of a national quantum computing environment by linking the quantum computer with LUMI.

Quantum computing represents a new frontier in technology, promising to solve complex problems that are beyond the reach of today’s classical computers. Recognizing this opportunity, the VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland announced plans to develop a quantum computer with at least 50 qubits by 2025. This initiative addresses the challenge of advancing Finland’s technological capabilities and securing a position at the forefront of quantum research, which has the potential to revolutionize fields such as medicine, materials science, and cryptography.
The Finnish government supports this vision by dedicating significant funding to accelerate the project. In its 2023 budget session, the government allocated 70 million euros to VTT, with the goal of scaling up the quantum computer from 50 qubits to 300 qubits by 2027. Increasing the number of qubits is essential because it directly improves the computing power and practical applications of quantum machines. This funding reflects a strong commitment to boosting Finland’s innovation ecosystem and ensuring that the country remains competitive in this highly strategic area.
The initiative involves combining quantum computing with existing high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Specifically, the plan is to connect the quantum computer to LUMI, one of Europe’s most powerful supercomputers, to create a national quantum computing environment. This connection will allow researchers to use both classical and quantum computing strengths, supporting advanced simulations and data processing tasks. The collaboration between VTT, the government, and HPC infrastructure operators exemplifies a coordinated effort to build a robust ecosystem for future technologies.

items.title: DARS AI Initiative
items.org: DARS – Motorway Company of the Republic of Slovenia
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The DARS AI Initiative introduces artificial intelligence to predict congestion and accidents on Slovenia’s motorways. The initiative uses machine learning models to improve traffic management and road safety. All AI projects are linked to the National Traffic Management Centre to support real-time decision-making.

The DARS AI Initiative is a project of DARS, the motorway company of the Republic of Slovenia, aimed at integrating artificial intelligence into traffic management. Its main purpose is to predict motorway congestion and accidents, enhancing both safety and efficiency for road users.
Key objectives of the initiative include:
Developing an internal strategy for the use of machine learning models in traffic managementLinking all AI and machine learning projects to the National Traffic Management Centre for coordinated operationSupporting proactive traffic monitoring and real-time management of motorway conditionsImplementation focuses on collecting and analysing traffic data to improve predictive capabilities. By integrating AI into traffic operations, the initiative seeks to reduce congestion, prevent accidents, and optimise traffic flow across Slovenia’s motorway network.

items.title: Cultural AI Lab
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Cultural AI Lab explores the intersection of AI and the humanities. It focuses on using AI to study cultural artifacts while also ensuring that AI development is informed by public values such as diversity and inclusivity.

The lab aims to address ethical challenges, such as bias in AI systems, and promotes the use of AI to enhance cultural research.

items.title: Creation of a hybrid cloud to combine registers such as AJPES register
items.org: Ministry of Economic Development and Technology
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This project aims to create a hybrid cloud that will combine registers such as the AJPES register, the register of the Financial Administration of the Republic of Slovenia and, for example, court registers, with the aim of simplifying procedures for businesses in relation to the Ministry of Economic Development and Technology.

Slovenia plans a hybrid cloud to make it easier for businesses to deal with the state. Today, key company data live in separate registers (e.g., AJPES, the Financial Administration, and court registers), which means firms often must repeat filings and slows administrative processes. The project addresses this fragmentation by enabling secure, unified access to those records.
The main objectives are to simplify procedures for businesses interacting with the Ministry of Economic Development and Technology, reduce paperwork, and improve data quality and consistency. By linking existing registers through a common cloud layer, authorities can retrieve verified information once and reuse it where legally permitted.

items.title: Course on “Machine Learning and Computer Vision for the Environmental Sciences"
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The University of Malta offers a course focusing on applying Machine Learning and Computer Vision techniques to Geosciences. Students develop practical skills in using AI technologies to address environmental challenges, preparing them for research and professional applications in natural sciences.

The course is GSC3202 – Machine Learning and Computer Vision for the Environmental Sciences at the University of Malta, under the Geosciences degree. The course is part of the Bachelor of Science (Honours) in Geosciences programme, under elective streams (e.g. Oceans and Atmosphere).

items.title: Coordination Mechanisms for the Sharing of Energy (COOMEP)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Coordination Mechanisms for the Sharing of Energy (COOMEP) project helps households coordinate their energy usage to be more efficient and sustainable. It uses AI proxies—autonomous decision-makers configured by users—to optimise energy sharing and consumption. The initiative encourages collaboration among households to improve overall energy efficiency.

The COOMEP project focuses on creating transferable knowledge and expertise to support coordinated energy management among groups of households. By employing AI proxies, the initiative allows households to automate and optimise energy usage according to collective and individual needs.
Key objectives include:
Promoting sustainable energy consumption at the household levelUsing AI-driven tools to optimise energy sharing and reduce inefficienciesEncouraging collaboration and knowledge exchange between participating householdsThe project provides insights into how AI can facilitate energy coordination, helping communities make smarter energy decisions while reducing overall consumption. COOMEP also generates lessons that can be replicated and adapted in other regions or countries seeking similar energy efficiency solutions.

items.title: Cooperative Streets Project
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Cooperative Streets Project in Portugal pilots Cooperative Intelligent Transport Systems (C-ITS) in urban areas. It aims to improve road safety, reduce emissions, and encourage public transport use. The project also tests multimodal access, parking management, Mobility as a Service (MaaS), and smart infrastructure solutions.

Launched in 2019, the Cooperative Streets Project is a Portuguese initiative to test and deploy Cooperative Intelligent Transport Systems (C-ITS) across urban areas. Running until 2023, it serves as a large-scale pilot to modernise the country’s transport ecosystem by integrating smart mobility technologies.
The project’s key objectives are to:
Reduce accidents and incidents through connected and cooperative transport technologiesPromote decarbonisation of urban mobilityEncourage the use of public transportation by improving its integration and accessibilityDevelop and test MaaS (Mobility as a Service) solutions for citizens and operatorsPilot activities cover multimodal access management, smart parking systems, data-driven mobility planning, and connected infrastructure to support real-time communication between vehicles, infrastructure, and mobility services.
By combining new technologies with urban mobility planning, the project seeks to build a safer, cleaner, and more efficient transport system for Portuguese cities. Its findings are expected to inform national policy, local planning, and future deployments of C-ITS across the country.

items.title: Community of Professional Educators (COPE) sessions
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The COPE sessions are designed to enhance the professional development of teachers in Malta. These sessions aim to provide educators with the necessary tools and knowledge to improve their teaching practices and stay updated with the latest educational trends.

Organised by the Directorate for Digital Literacy and Transversal Skills (DDLTS), the CoPE sessions cover a range of topics, including digital literacy and the integration of AI in education.

items.title: Collaboration for AI in Municipalities and Civil Society
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
In this project, a targeted investment is made towards Sweden’s municipalities and civil society organisations. The aim is to provide tailored help and financial support that helps the target groups understand how AI can be used and to get started with their first concrete projects.

The programme consists of three parts:
The AI council: Representatives from twelve of the country's municipalities work on strategic issues for Swedish municipalities, identifying common opportunities, challenges, and needs.
Use cases: With funding from Vinnova, a number of municipalities and civil society organizations are working on diverse AI projects at different levels. These projects not only strengthen the AI competence of the participating organizations but also generate valuable lessons for others.
Tools: The AI Compass consolidates many of the lessons learned from the project in a tool that will help individual organizations get started practically, regardless of their current AI maturity and experience.

items.title: Cloud research programme (PEPR)
items.org: CEA & Inria (scientific co-leads); ANR operator; funded under France 2030
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Scientifically co-piloted by the CEA and Inria as part of the new “Digital, algorithms and software” programme. Its goal is to propose significant advances in the performance, security and frugality of cloud infrastructures and services while emphasising the transfer of innovative solutions from research to the industry.

On 4 April 2024, the PEPR Cloud programme, co-piloted by the CEA and Inria, will be officially launched. The programme, which has a budget of €51 million over 7 years, focuses on sovereignty, security and frugality.
The first stage of the programme was to map the research community, which made it possible to draw up a complete inventory of the players involved in research dedicated to the Cloud, in order to link them to the subjects defined as strategic.
At the same time, seven priority projects were identified for this PEPR. Five of these concern the software layers needed to deploy the distributed clouds of tomorrow, and two focus on the cross-functional aspects of infrastructure security and energy management, as mentioned above.
The PEPR roadmap also includes a call for projects focusing on two areas, the first on algorithmic work to optimise certain performance and reliability criteria for the software stacks developed, and the second on the impact of different application domains on the actual design of these software stacks. Finally, the programme includes a test bed in the form of a distributed experimental infrastructure.

items.title: Cloud Computing Platform "Vrančić"
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Cloud Computing Platform "Vrančić" launched by the University Computing Centre (Srce), is an advanced OpenStack-based infrastructure supporting scientific research in Croatia.

Featuring 11,520 processor cores, 16 GPUs, and 57 TB of working memory, Vrančić provides researchers with a flexible, high-performance computing environment that enables complex computational tasks across multiple scientific disciplines, integrating seamlessly with other advanced computing services.

items.title: Climate Change Cockpit
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Climate Change Cockpit provides a centralised platform for environmental data in Austria’s tourism sector. It consolidates information from multiple sources to give a comprehensive overview of environmental conditions and trends. The initiative helps tourism organisations make better decisions and plan strategically to address climate-related challenges.

The Climate Change Cockpit was created to tackle the problem of fragmented environmental data, which made it difficult for the tourism sector to gain a holistic understanding of climate impacts. By consolidating disparate data sources into a single, accessible platform, the initiative enhances transparency and usability of environmental information.
Key objectives include:
Centralising environmental data relevant to tourism and climate changeProviding real-time overviews of environmental conditions and trendsSupporting decision-making and strategic planning for climate adaptation in the tourism sectorThe initiative was co-developed by the Austrian National Tourist Office and the Austrian Federal Computing Center, ensuring that both industry and technical expertise contribute to the platform. Through this collaboration, tourism stakeholders can access reliable, actionable data to inform sustainable practices and climate resilience strategies.

items.title: Chips from the North Strategy
items.org: Semiconductor Branch Group, Technology Industries of Finland
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Initiative by the Technology Industries of Finland that benefits from public sector inputs in different areas, such as funding for RDI, R&D infrastructure, talent and education, and initiatives to attract international investments. The strategy aims to enhance Finland’s capabilities in semiconductor technology and ensure a competitive edge in the global market.

Semiconductor technology plays a critical role in almost every modern device, from smartphones to advanced medical equipment. As global demand for semiconductors grows—and international competition increases—Finland faces both a challenge and an opportunity: to strengthen its position in this vital sector. To respond, the Technology Industries of Finland launched an initiative to develop the country’s semiconductor capabilities. This effort is supported by various public sector measures, such as research funding, infrastructure development, education and training programs, and strategies to attract international investment.
The main goal of the initiative is to ensure Finland can remain competitive in the global semiconductor industry. This means building a strong foundation in research, innovation, and manufacturing capacity, while also making sure there is a skilled workforce to support long-term growth. By combining industry leadership with public support, the strategy aims to create the right conditions for companies to develop and apply advanced semiconductor technologies in Finland.
The initiative works by bringing together different areas of public and private cooperation. Public investment supports research and development (R&D), including infrastructure for testing and production. Education and talent development efforts are designed to train both current and future professionals in semiconductor-related fields. Additionally, the strategy includes targeted actions to attract international companies and investors, positioning Finland as a reliable and innovative partner in the semiconductor value chain.

items.title: Business Finland campaign on Generative AI
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The main goal of the campaign is to accelerate generative AI-driven innovations for improved productivity and efficiency to strengthen global competitiveness.

The Generative AI campaign focuses mainly on technology companies and ICT industry. The aim is to facilitate peer-to-peer learning within these industries, encouraging the adoption of best practices and supporting necessary research and development efforts together with research organizations.

The campaign has close cooperation with Teknologiateollisuus (Technology Industries of Finland) which has made significant investments to accelerate the utilization of artificial intelligence. Key initiatives include investing in AI projects by member companies, establishing the AI Finland network, and creating a new AI research center at Aalto University.

items.title: Bura Supercomputer
items.org: Centre for Advanced Computing and Modelling (CNRM) at the University of Rijeka
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Operated by the Centre for Advanced Computing and Modelling (CNRM) at the University of Rijeka, the Bura Supercomputer supports advanced research. Bura enables researchers to solve complex problems and perform advanced simulations across various scientific disciplines. Bura's peak performance is 233.6 teraflops.

The Bura supercomputer, hosted at the University of Rijeka’s Center for Advanced Computing and Modelling, addresses the need for powerful computing resources in Croatia’s research and innovation ecosystem. Many scientific and industrial projects require advanced simulations and data analysis that exceed the capacity of standard systems. Bura was developed to meet these demands, supporting disciplines such as engineering, physics, biotechnology, and environmental science.

items.title: Assignment to the Swedish Agency for Digital Government and the Swedish Authority for Privacy Protection to develop guidelines for the use of generative artificial intelligence in public administration
items.org: Swedish Agency for Digital Government; Swedish Authority for Privacy Protection
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
The government recently tasked two agencies with developing guidelines for generative AI, which are meant to be used to upskill civil servants.

In August 2024, the Swedish government asked the Agency for Digital Government (DIGG) and the Swedish Authority for Privacy Protection (IMY) to draw up national guidelines on the use of generative AI in the public sector. The task responds to the growing interest in generative tools but also the need to ensure they are applied responsibly, legally, and securely in government work.
The guidelines will cover both opportunities and risks, giving public bodies clear standards for testing and using generative AI. A key goal is to help upskill civil servants so they can make informed, competent use of new technologies while safeguarding citizens’ rights.

items.title: Application Hub for a Circular Economy for Plastic Packaging through AI Methods
items.original_name: Anwendungszentrum für eine Kreislaufwirtschaft für Kunststoffverpackungen mittels KI-Methoden
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Anwendungszentrum für eine Kreislaufwirtschaft für Kunststoffverpackungen mittels KI-Methoden
items.body:
The Application Hub for a Circular Economy for Plastic Packaging uses AI methods to improve recycling and reduce plastic waste. It supports research and innovation to enhance circular economy practices in Germany. The initiative aims to make plastic packaging management more efficient and sustainable.

The Application Hub for a Circular Economy for Plastic Packaging through AI Methods is a German initiative financed by the Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF). Its purpose is to develop and apply AI technologies that optimise the management and recycling of plastic packaging, supporting the country’s transition toward a circular economy.
Key objectives include:
Enhancing recycling efficiency using AI-based sorting, monitoring, and analysis toolsReducing plastic waste through smarter resource management and process optimisationSupporting research and innovation in materials, production, and recycling practicesThe hub fosters collaboration between academic institutions, industry partners, and technology providers, ensuring AI solutions are practical and scalable. By integrating AI into circular economy processes, the initiative contributes to both environmental sustainability and economic efficiency.

items.title: Analysing the impact of AI on educational programmes
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The government assigned the Swedish Higher Education Authority (UKÄ) the Swedish National Agency for Higher Vocational Education (MYH) with analysing the potential of impact artificial intelligence on the university's or polytechnic's education offerings in relation to the labor market's future skills needs.

The Swedish government has asked two important agencies—the Swedish Higher Education Authority (UKÄ) and the Swedish National Agency for Higher Vocational Education (MYH)—to work together on understanding how artificial intelligence (AI) might affect education at universities and polytechnics. This initiative addresses a key challenge: as AI rapidly changes many industries, there is uncertainty about how education systems should adapt to prepare students with the right skills for future jobs. By analyzing these changes, the agencies aim to help education providers align their programs with the evolving demands of the labor market.
The main goal of this effort is to study how AI impacts the types of skills students will need when they graduate. This means looking at current university and vocational programs and evaluating whether they are keeping pace with technological advances and labor market needs. The agencies want to identify any gaps or opportunities in education offerings so that graduates can be well-prepared for new roles created or changed by AI. Ultimately, this helps ensure that Sweden’s workforce stays competitive and ready for future challenges.
To carry out this work, UKÄ and MYH will collect information from various sources including employers, educators, and students. They will analyze trends in AI technology, the evolving job market, and education curricula. By bringing together knowledge from both higher education and vocational training sectors, the agencies can provide a comprehensive view of the situation. This collaboration also ensures that recommendations will consider the full spectrum of education pathways.

items.title: AgroHub.BG
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
AgroHub.BG serves as the country's Digital Innovation Hub (DIH) for agriculture. This platform facilitates communication and collaboration among various stakeholders in the agricultural sector, including farmers, technology providers, and policy institutions. AgroHub.BG aims to democratise access to knowledge and resources in the agrarian industry, enabling the development of innovative solutions to address sector-specific challenges. It is part of the AgroDigiRise project, funded by the EC.

As Bulgaria’s Digital Innovation Hub for agriculture, AgroHub.BG acts as a platform and network hub that connects farmers, tech providers, research bodies, and policymaking institutions. It aims to democratize access to agritech knowledge, tools, and resources so that innovative solutions can be developed to tackle agriculture-specific challenges. It is part of the AgroDigiRise project (financed by the European Commission), This project helps coordinate pilots, training, and collaborative innovation across the Bulgarian agricultural ecosystem.

items.title: Agriculture of the Future Programme
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Digibiocontrol focuses on integrating AI and digital tools into biocontrol solutions for agriculture. The initiative supports farmers in using data-driven strategies to optimise pest and disease management, promoting sustainable and eco-friendly agricultural practices.

Digibiocontrol is a Walloon innovation initiative led by Wagralim that integrates AI and digital tools into biological crop protection. The project supports farmers in adopting data-driven strategies to improve pest and disease management, aiming to reduce dependence on chemical pesticides. The programme brings together universities, research institutes, companies, and public partners to co-develop and validate solutions in real farming conditions.

items.title: Accelerating the use of generative AI in the economy
items.org: Ministry of Economy, Finance, Industrial and Digital Sovereignty
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This call for proposals focuses on the downstream part of the generative AI value chain by encouraging the development of advanced integrated generative AI solutions with a short-term adoption horizon. It aims at bringing together developers and users of generative AI solutions and develop demonstrators for potentially replicable and economically viable solutions.

France has launched a targeted call for proposals to speed up the adoption of generative AI in the economy. The initiative is managed by Bpifrance, acting as an operator of the government’s France 2030 investment plan, which is overseen by the Ministry of the Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty.
The call focuses on the downstream part of the generative AI value chain, prioritising projects that can deliver short-term, practical applications. Its aim is to bring together developers and users to create demonstrators that are replicable and economically viable, ensuring that investment leads to fast, tangible outcomes.

items.title: AI4T
items.org: France, Slovenia, Italy, Ireland and Luxembourg
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Erasmus+ project 'AI4T (AI for and by Teachers)' was a three-year collaboration involving partners from five European countries: France, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, and Slovenia. With contributions from ministries of education, universities, research centers, and private companies, the project aimed to develop a professional learning path for secondary school teachers. Its goal was to help teachers better understand the opportunities and risks associated with AI in the classroom.

The project resulted in a handbook and a tailored training program to challenge biases, deepen knowledge, and promote the informed use of AI in education.

items.title: AI-programmes in Business Finland’s Digital Native Finland mission
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The aim of the Digital Native Finland mission is to accelerate digital transformation and create a global competitive advantage for Finnish companies. By increasing digital capabilities, we can increase sustainable customer value and raise the productivity of companies to the next level.

The Digital Native Finland mission is an instrument of mission-based innovation policy aimed at accelerating the digital trans-formation of Finnish firms. The most AI-relevant programmes within this initiative include: 
6G Bridge Programme: provides innovation funding to Finnish companies, including AI start-ups, to develop and commercialise new technologies. The programme encourages collaboration between researchers and businesses to drive advancements in AI and telecommunications. 
Data Economy Programme: focuses on promoting data-driven business models and innovations. It offers funding and support to start-ups and scale-ups, including AI-focused, to help them leverage data for business growth.

items.title: AI use in processing VAT returns
items.org: Financial Administration of the Republic of Slovenia
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Financial Administration of the Republic of Slovenia (FURS) uses advanced artificial intelligence technologies (models for the use of predictive analytics in the implementation of business processes) in the process of acceptance of VAT returns. By using predictive analytics, FURS aims to increase the effectiveness of controls, both in terms of the number and of the additionally identified irregularities.

FURS - the Financial Administration of the Republic of Slovenia - handles large volumes of VAT returns, where manual checks alone can miss patterns and slow responses. To address this, FURS applies advanced AI and predictive analytics to spot risk signals in filings more quickly and consistently.
The objective is straightforward: make controls more effective and efficient. By prioritizing cases with a higher probability of errors or fraud, FURS can focus audit resources where they matter most, aiming to increase both the number of effective controls and the share of additionally identified irregularities. In practice, predictive models analyze VAT-return data and related variables to produce risk scores. These models are integrated into FURS’s business processes so caseworkers see ranked alerts and supporting indicators rather than raw data. Human officials still make decisions; the models help them triage, standardize checks, and improve overall throughput.

items.title: AI for SMEs Grants (KI4KMU)
items.org: Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The AI for SMEs grants support innovative AI projects led by SMEs in partnership with universities and start-ups. This programme encourages SMEs to explore advanced AI solutions in areas such as automated decision-making, privacy-by-design, and data engineering, with a focus on industry-specific applications like renewable energy, mobility, and manufacturing.

Germany’s AI for SMEs program provides targeted funding for small and medium-sized enterprises to explore and apply artificial intelligence in their operations. By requiring partnerships with universities, start-ups, and other innovation actors, the scheme hopes to help SMEs overcome resource and expertise barriers that might otherwise slow adoption. The grants support projects in fields like automated decision-making, privacy-by-design, and data engineering, with applications in sectors such as renewable energy, transport, and manufacturing.

items.title: AI for Education pilot project
items.org: Ministry for Education, Sport, Youth, Research, and Innovation
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Ministry for Education, Sport, Youth, Research, and Innovation is developing an AI-powered adaptive learning system scheduled for implementation in 2024-2025.

The project aims to deliver personalised learning programmes and support teachers in student assessment. With EUR 150k funding, partially supported by the National AI Strategy, this initiative represents a key step in integrating AI technology into Malta's education system.

items.title: AI Professorships
items.org: Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
As part of the national AI strategy, Germany aimed to fund 100 new AI professorships by 2025, a target achieved in 2022 with a total of 150 professorships created by 2023. These include positions supported by various measures, such as the Alexander von Humboldt Professorship for AI, university AI competence centres, the tenure-track programme, DFG projects, and collaborations with non-university research institutions.

Germany faced a shortage of long-term academic posts in AI, limiting teaching capacity and slowing research transfer. Under its national AI strategy, the federal government and Länder set a target of 100 new AI professorships by 2025 to expand expertise nationwide. That goal was reached ahead of schedule.
The initiative draws on several instruments: Alexander von Humboldt AI professorships to attract top international talent, AI competence centres at universities, tenure-track and DFG projects, and partnerships with non-university institutes.

items.title: AI Innovation Competition
items.org: Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The AI Innovation Competition, launched by the BMWK, provides funding for exceptional approaches to developing AI-driven platform economies in key sectors of the German economy. The initiative aims to leverage AI methods as catalysts for innovative value creation networks and the development of new products and business models across various industries. Since 2019, three funding calls have been issued, resulting in support for a total of 26 projects to foster the growth of AI ecosystems.

This project funds pioneering projects that use artificial intelligence to build platform-based business models and value networks. It supports collaborations between companies, research institutes, and start-ups that explore new ways of creating products and services across sectors. Since its launch in 2019, the competition has issued three funding calls and backed 26 projects. By doing so, it has helped shape AI ecosystems in Germany, encouraging the spread of AI methods into areas such as manufacturing, health, and mobility, while strengthening the competitiveness of the wider economy.

items.title: AI Idea Workshop for Environmental Protection
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The AI Idea Workshop for Environmental Protection in Germany helps NGOs, researchers, start-ups, and individuals develop AI applications for environmental protection. It combines funding, technical expertise, and networking to encourage civil society engagement in AI-driven environmental solutions.

The AI Idea Workshop for Environmental Protection is a German initiative aimed at advancing AI-based solutions for environmental challenges by empowering civil society actors. It supports NGOs, researchers, start-ups, and private individuals in designing and implementing AI applications for areas such as biodiversity conservation, pollution monitoring, and resource efficiency.
The initiative offers:
Technical expertise and mentoring for developing AI solutionsNetworking opportunities to connect participants with partners and expertsAn accessible funding programme to enable innovation at different scalesIts activities are structured around five key modules:
AI workshop to train and inspire participantsPilot projects to test new ideas in practiceEnvironmental data workshop to improve data availability and useMobile workshop to reach communities across regionsNetwork building to sustain cooperation and knowledge sharingThe AI Idea Workshop is part of the broader Civic Coding initiative, which promotes the socially responsible use of AI in Germany.

items.title: AI Cluster
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The National Strategy has allocated €560 million in 2023 to the initial and continuous training of AI experts and "AI+X" professionals with dual competencies. Within this framework, the AI Cluster initiative is dedicated to excellence in AI training in 9 universities and grandes écoles.

As part of France’s National AI Strategy, €560 million was allocated in 2023 to train both AI specialists and “AI+X” professionals who combine AI with expertise in other fields. A central element of this effort is the AI Cluster initiative, which brings together nine universities and grandes écoles to serve as hubs of excellence in AI education.
The clusters aim to raise the quality and scale of AI training, ensuring that France develops a broad talent base capable of advancing research and supporting industry. They provide initial education for students, continuous training for professionals, and foster collaboration between academia and business to align skills with economic and societal needs.

items.title: A project for digitally excluded people to improve their digital skills
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The project, implemented by the Information Society Development Committee (ISDC) together with partners Langas į ateitį Association and the Lithuanian National Library Martynas Mažvydas, aims to provide digital literacy training and other activities to help develop the population's ability to make full use of the digital solutions developed. It also aims to enable the most vulnerable social groups to make greater use of e-services.

The project works through practical courses and community-based activities delivered by the library network and partner organisations. Participants learn how to use online services, access information safely, and take advantage of digital solutions that can improve their quality of life. By targeting vulnerable groups in particular, the project ensures that those most at risk of exclusion gain the skills they need to participate more fully in the digital society.

items.title: Winter Road Maintenance Using AI in Kuldīga Municipality
items.original_name: Ziemas ceļu uzturēšana, izmantojot mākslīgo intelektu Kuldīgas novadā
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Ziemas ceļu uzturēšana, izmantojot mākslīgo intelektu Kuldīgas novadā
items.body:
The Winter Road Maintenance Using AI initiative in Kuldīga Municipality uses AI to monitor road conditions in real time. It predicts necessary maintenance actions and provides an interactive map for local authorities. The system improves collaboration between municipalities and road maintenance providers, increasing efficiency in winter road upkeep.

The Winter Road Maintenance Using AI initiative in Kuldīga Municipality applies artificial intelligence to optimise winter road maintenance. By analysing real-time road conditions, the system predicts where and when maintenance actions are needed, helping municipalities allocate resources more effectively.
Key objectives include:
Real-time assessment of road conditions during winterPredictive recommendations for maintenance actions to prevent accidents and improve road safetyInteractive mapping to visualise AI-generated guidance for local authorities and maintenance teamsFacilitating collaboration between municipalities and road maintenance providersThe initiative demonstrates how AI can improve public service efficiency, reduce costs, and enhance safety. By integrating predictive analytics and interactive visual tools, the programme supports better decision-making for winter road management.

items.title: Urban Mobility Data Integration
items.original_name: Integrazione dei Dati sulla Mobilità Urbana
items.org: Ministry of Infrastructure and Sustainable Mobility
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Integrazione dei Dati sulla Mobilità Urbana
items.body:
The Urban Mobility Data Integration initiative in Italy establishes a national registry of datasets and models for mobility applications. It supports the development of intelligent transport networks that can dynamically adapt to real-time demand, aiming to enhance urban mobility planning and decision-making.

The Urban Mobility Data Integration initiative is part of Italy’s “National Knowledge Assets: Datasets and Models” programme, which enables strategic actions using data-driven solutions. The initiative focuses on building a centralised national registry of datasets and models related to urban mobility, helping public authorities, researchers, and technology developers access consistent and high-quality data.
Key objectives include:
Establishing a national dataset and model registry to support urban mobility solutionsEnabling intelligent transport networks that can adapt in real-time to changing demandPromoting data-driven planning and innovation in urban transportThe initiative encourages collaboration between local authorities, mobility operators, and research institutions to ensure that datasets and models meet practical needs. By providing a structured and accessible data ecosystem, it allows cities to improve traffic management, reduce congestion, and optimise public transport services.
Future outlook:
Expansion of the registry to include additional mobility-related datasets and simulation modelsIntegration of AI and predictive analytics for smarter transport planningSupport for national and regional decision-making in urban mobility strategy

items.title: Testing authorisation regime and connected vehicle technology pilot
items.org: Connected and Automated Mobility (CAM) Interdepartmental Steering Group
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
The Connected and Automated Mobility (CAM) Interdepartmental Steering Group oversees the development of testing rules for connected and automated vehicles on public roads. A pilot project is running until the end of 2024, focusing on on-road connected vehicle technology (C-ITS). Around 1,500 drivers are participating to help test and evaluate these systems.

The CAM Interdepartmental Steering Group, established in November 2023, coordinates efforts across government departments to support the safe deployment of connected and automated mobility (CAM) technologies. One of its primary tasks is to develop a testing authorisation regime for CAM vehicles operating on public roads.
The ongoing pilot project is a key component of this initiative, aiming to test and validate Cooperative Intelligent Transport Systems (C-ITS), which enable vehicles to communicate with each other and with traffic infrastructure. Key elements include:
Participation of 1,500 drivers to gather real-world data and insightsTesting of connected vehicle technology on public roadsEvaluation of safety, reliability, and user experience for automated mobility solutionsThe initiative fosters collaboration between government authorities, transport agencies, technology providers, and road users, ensuring that regulatory frameworks and technical standards support both innovation and safety.
Future outlook:
Implementation of a formal testing authorisation framework for CAMExpansion of pilot projects and deployment of C-ITS solutionsStrengthening of policy and technical readiness for wider adoption of connected and automated mobility in public transport and road networks

items.title: Tampere City Lab
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Business Tampere operates several initiatives to support AI testing and experimentation, notably the Tampere City Lab, which is part of the EU-wide Citcom.ai initiative and network of testing and experimentation facilities to help bring AI innovations to market responsibly. It provides a combination of virtual and physical testbeds for smart city and AI-powered solutions and supports the development and testing of AI technologies in real-world urban environments.

The main objective of this project is to speed up the responsible use of AI in urban life by connecting developers with real infrastructure and data. The Lab reduces risk for both companies and public bodies while ensuring innovation is shaped by real city needs.
The initiative offers both virtual and physical testbeds. Virtual tools include Tampere’s IoT platform with sensor data, analytics, and development toolkits. Physical environments include Hervanta for autonomous vehicles, Tyyppaamo for energy and building systems, and the Nokia Arena for event-related solutions. Alongside access to these facilities, the Lab provides project support, partnerships, and guidance on intellectual property.
Tampere City Lab is also part of the EU-wide Citcom.ai network, which links similar testing facilities across Europe and enables shared learning and collaboration.

items.title: Sustainable Mobility
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Sustainable Mobility AI initiative in Italy develops AI applications for transportation to optimise energy use, manage traffic, and reduce emissions. It aims to improve quality of life through smarter and greener mobility solutions. The initiative is part of the Italian Strategy for AI 2024–2026.

The Sustainable Mobility initiative focuses on leveraging artificial intelligence to make transportation systems in Italy more efficient, environmentally friendly, and user-centric. By applying AI technologies, the programme seeks to optimise the use of energy and environmental resources and enhance traffic management to reduce congestion and emissions.
Key objectives include:
Developing AI solutions for sustainable and smart mobilityOptimising resource use, including energy efficiency in transportationReducing traffic-related emissions and environmental impactEnhancing overall quality of life through improved transportation systemsImplementation involves collaboration between public authorities, research institutions, and private transport and technology companies. AI technologies are applied to both urban and intercity mobility systems, allowing data-driven decision making for traffic control, route planning, and energy-efficient transport operations.
Future outlook:
Expansion of AI tools to integrate multimodal transportation systemsIncreased use of predictive analytics for traffic and energy managementAlignment with national sustainability and climate goalsContribution to the broader objectives of Italy’s AI Strategy 2024–2026

items.title: Strengthening the Digital Skills of Civil Servants
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This programme of the Administrative Academy (under the Ministry for Public Administration) aims to improve the competences of civil servants in core digital skills, including specialised skills on AI. The content of the programme is designed in accordance with the OECD Framework for Digital Talents and Skills in the Public Sector. The implementation of the programme is co-financed by the Republic of Slovenia, the Ministry of Public Administration, and the European Union - NextGenerationEU.

The Administrative Academy, part of Slovenia’s Ministry of Public Administration, has launched a training programme to strengthen the digital skills of civil servants. Many public officials face challenges in adapting to rapid technological change, particularly in areas such as artificial intelligence. By addressing these gaps, the programme ensures that the public sector can adopt new technologies effectively and responsibly. Its main objective is to improve both basic digital competences and more advanced skills, with a focus on AI. 
Training is delivered through the Administrative Academy and is co-financed by the Republic of Slovenia, the Ministry of Public Administration, and the European Union’s NextGenerationEU fund.

items.title: Smart Traffic Analysis and Traffic Safety (STATS)
items.org: Ministry of Infrastructure and Water Management
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Smart Traffic Analysis and Traffic Safety (STATS) project uses AI to improve traffic safety in urban areas. It applies computer vision and data analysis to monitor traffic patterns and enhance the safety of cyclists and pedestrians. The project aims to reduce accidents and create safer city streets.

The STATS project in the Netherlands focuses on applying AI and data science to improve urban traffic safety. By analysing traffic patterns, the project identifies risks for cyclists and pedestrians and develops strategies to prevent accidents.
Key objectives include:
Monitoring and analysing traffic flows using AI and computer visionEnhancing pedestrian and cyclist safety in urban environmentsProviding data-driven insights for local authorities to make streets saferThe project combines real-time traffic data, AI algorithms, and urban planning expertise to detect potential hazards and inform city safety measures. Collaboration between municipalities, research institutions, and technology providers ensures that solutions are practical and scalable.

items.title: Smart LED Light
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
AI-powered smart lighting solutions are used in Latvian cities to monitor and detect traffic violations. The system records incidents such as red-light running, misuse of public transport lanes, and illegal stopping. The data supports traffic law enforcement and improves urban mobility management.

The AI-powered smart lighting system in Latvian cities is designed to enhance road safety and traffic management through real-time monitoring. By integrating AI with street lighting infrastructure, the system can automatically detect and record a range of traffic violations, including:
Crossing intersections at a red lightImproper use of public transport lanesUnauthorised stopping at junctionsNon-compliance with other traffic signalsThe initiative serves multiple objectives:
Supporting traffic law enforcement by providing accurate and automated violation dataImproving urban mobility through analysis of traffic patterns and violationsEnhancing public safety in busy city areasImplementation relies on the integration of AI algorithms with smart city infrastructure, enabling continuous monitoring without requiring extensive human supervision. The collected data can also inform urban planning decisions, such as adjusting signal timing or redesigning intersections to improve safety and traffic flow.
Future outlook:
Expansion to additional cities and urban areas across LatviaIntegration with other smart city services for holistic urban managementUse of data for predictive traffic control and long-term mobility planning

items.title: Science, Technology and Society university programmes
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The University of Uppsala has complementary programmes in place to educate students of technology-focused subjects to consider the policy/societal impact of technology, while the University of Gothenburg has a research group on the same subject.

The initiative involves two Swedish universities working to connect technology education and research with the broader societal and policy implications of technology. As technology becomes increasingly central to daily life and industry, it’s important for students and researchers to understand not just how to build new systems, but also how those systems affect society, ethics, and policy decisions. This initiative addresses the challenge that technical education often focuses heavily on the skills to create technology, but less on reflecting about its consequences or how it should be governed.
At Uppsala University, this challenge is met through complementary programmes designed to teach students in technology-related fields about the societal and policy impact of the technologies they study. These programmes aim to broaden students’ perspectives, encouraging them to think about how technology influences people, communities, and decision-making processes. The goal is to prepare future engineers and technologists who are not only skilled in their craft but also aware of the responsibilities they have as creators and users of technology.
At the University of Gothenburg, there is a dedicated research group focusing on the relationship between technology and society. This group studies how technological developments interact with social systems, policy frameworks, and ethical questions. Their work helps inform both academic understanding and public debate, ensuring that technological progress is considered alongside its wider effects.
These efforts reflect a growing awareness in Swedish higher education of the need to combine technical skills with societal insight. By educating students and conducting research that spans technology and policy, these universities are helping shape a generation of professionals who can contribute to technology development in ways that are socially responsible and informed by real-world impact. Over time, these initiatives may expand, involving more students and researchers, and fostering stronger links between universities, policymakers, and industry.

items.title: Route 25 Project
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Route 25 project develops autonomous and connected transport systems in Portugal. It invests EUR 80 million and creates 488 new jobs to advance smart, sustainable, and inclusive mobility solutions. The project focuses on research and innovation in autonomous, intelligent, and interoperable transport technologies.

Route 25 is a national initiative designed to position Portugal at the forefront of smart and sustainable mobility. The project focuses on developing autonomous and connected transport systems, leveraging research and innovation to create disruptive technological solutions.
Key objectives include:
Developing autonomous, intelligent, interoperable, and inclusive mobility technologiesCreating high-skilled jobs (488 positions) and stimulating economic growthAdvancing smart and sustainable transport solutions across urban and regional areasThe initiative involves significant investment of EUR 80 million and combines efforts from industry, research institutions, and public authorities. It is structured to support both the research and deployment of next-generation transport technologies, ensuring practical applicability and societal benefits.

items.title: Open Government Action Plan
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
The Open Government Action Plan 2023-2027 supports the development of data policies that align with the principles of open government. It emphasises transparency, accountability, and citizen participation in government activities. It includes initiatives to enhance data accessibility and promote the use of open data.

The Open Government Action Plan 2023-2027 aims to make government data more open and accessible to the public. It focuses on improving transparency, ensuring governments are accountable, and encouraging citizens to participate in decision-making. The plan recognizes that sharing data openly helps build trust between governments and people.
To reach these goals, the plan promotes the use of open data, making it easier for anyone to access and use government information. This includes updating digital platforms and improving how data is organized and shared. The initiative involves various government bodies working together, often alongside civil society and private partners.
Building on previous efforts, the plan continues to expand open data availability and citizen engagement, helping governments become more open and responsive to public needs.

items.title: MIRRI Information hub for artificial intelligence (AI).
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The new website, created in collaboration with the National Artificial Intelligence Platform "AIslovakIA," aims to provide easy access to relevant legislation, documents, and initiatives in the field of AI. It is part of fulfilling the measures of the Action Plan for the Digital Transformation of Slovakia 2023-2026. The platform's main goal is to offer both experts and the general public access to information on AI legislation, events, study programmes related to AI.

Slovakia has launched a new website in collaboration with the National Artificial Intelligence Platform “AIslovakIA” to make information on AI more accessible. Until now, legislation, policy documents, and initiatives have often been scattered across different institutional portals, limiting their visibility to both experts and the wider public. By centralising these resources, the platform aims to support transparency and help citizens and professionals stay informed about how AI is being regulated and promoted in Slovakia.
The initiative forms part of the Action Plan for the Digital Transformation of Slovakia 2023–2026, which sets measures for strengthening digital governance and innovation. Its main purpose is to provide easy access to AI-related legislation, strategies, research documents, and official initiatives. Alongside legal texts, the site highlights AI-related events, conferences, and academic study programmes, giving users a clearer picture of the country’s AI ecosystem.
The platform is designed for multiple audiences: policymakers and researchers can find official resources and updates in one place, while businesses and citizens gain insight into opportunities to engage with AI projects or training.

items.title: LMT Traffic Monitoring Tool
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The LMT Traffic Monitoring Tool uses AI-powered video and machine vision to monitor traffic in real time. It detects traffic intensity and common violations, such as running red lights or illegal turns. The system improves road safety and supports traffic management.

The LMT Traffic Monitoring Tool is an AI-driven system designed to provide real-time monitoring of traffic conditions while fully complying with GDPR regulations. Using machine vision and video technology, it collects data on traffic flow, road users, and vehicle behaviour to support urban mobility planning and enforcement.
Key objectives include:
Monitoring traffic intensity and the movement of vehicles and pedestriansDetecting traffic violations, such as running red lights, misuse of public transport lanes, illegal turns, and stopping in intersectionsEnhancing road safety by providing actionable insights to authoritiesSupporting traffic management through accurate, real-time dataThe tool is expected to expand integration with city traffic management systems and potentially link to predictive analytics for congestion and accident prevention. By combining AI analysis with existing monitoring infrastructure, it helps cities improve both safety and efficiency on roads.

items.title: Investment C1.4 R5-I2 Autonomous Vehicles in Zagreb
items.original_name: Investicija C1.4 R5-I2 Autonomna vozila u Zagrebu
items.org: Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Investicija C1.4 R5-I2 Autonomna vozila u Zagrebu
items.body:
The Autonomous Vehicles in Zagreb initiative focuses on developing self-driving electric vehicles and the infrastructure needed for urban mobility. It aims to make transportation in Zagreb safer, more efficient, and environmentally friendly.

The Autonomous Vehicles in Zagreb initiative is part of Croatia’s investment in urban mobility innovation. It targets the development and testing of autonomous electric vehicles alongside the necessary supporting infrastructure, such as charging stations, traffic management systems, and smart road technology.
Key objectives include:
Developing and deploying autonomous electric vehicles suitable for urban transportCreating infrastructure that supports safe and efficient operation of self-driving vehiclesReducing emissions and traffic congestion by promoting electric and autonomous mobility solutionsThe initiative encourages collaboration between city authorities, technology providers, and research institutions to ensure the solutions are technically feasible and aligned with urban planning goals. It also serves as a pilot for smart city mobility, demonstrating how autonomous technologies can integrate into public and private transport networks.
Future outlook:
Broader deployment of autonomous vehicle fleets across Zagreb and other urban areasExpansion of smart infrastructure supporting autonomous and electric mobilityStrengthened research, innovation, and public-private partnerships in urban transport technologies

items.title: Intelligent Transport Systems (ITS)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Intelligent Transport Systems (ITS) project in Malta uses AI-driven tools to reduce traffic congestion and improve urban mobility. It optimises traffic re-routing, road closures, and low-traffic zones. The initiative also promotes multi-modal transport for seamless travel.

The Intelligent Transport Systems (ITS) project in Malta is designed to improve traffic flow, urban mobility, and environmental conditions through the use of AI technologies. By integrating real-time data, the system helps authorities manage traffic more efficiently and reduce congestion in key urban areas.
Key objectives include:
Optimising traffic re-routing to improve flow and minimise delaysCoordinating road closures and implementing no/low traffic zones to enhance urban spacesEnhancing route planning through the National Access Points (NAPs)Promoting multi-modal transport, including public transport, walking, and cycling, for seamless mobilityThe initiative is expected to evolve through continuous AI integration and improved data-sharing platforms. By expanding multi-modal transport solutions and smarter traffic management, ITS aims to make Malta’s transport system more sustainable, efficient, and user-friendly.

items.title: IRT SystemX
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
IRT SystemX is a French research institute that works with public and private partners on projects to validate the safety of autonomous vehicles through simulation. Projects such as SVA, 3SA, and SVR develop tools, scenarios, and methods to test autonomous driving systems, shuttles, and robot-taxis. The goal is to ensure these systems are safe, reliable, and can eventually be approved for real-world use.

IRT SystemX is a not-for-profit research establishment (Institut de Recherche Technologique) co-funded by both the public sector and private industry. Its mission focuses on digital engineering of complex systems, with special emphasis on mobility, autonomous transport, simulation, safety, and system validation. 
Here are some of the key autonomous mobility projects it leads:
SVA – Simulation for the Autonomous Vehicle Safety
Launched in 2015, this project develops methods and tools using digital simulation to validate the safety of autonomous vehicles. It addresses issues like sensor failures, environmental disturbances (rain, glare, etc.), and challenges in interpreting road features.3SA – Simulation for the Safety of Systems in Autonomous Vehicles
Started in 2019, this continues and extends SVA. It builds on simulation tools, sensor modeling, scenario libraries, and result analysis to deepen the safety demonstration of autonomous driving systems. SVR – Vehicle Robots and Autonomous Shuttles Scenarios
Also launched around 2019, SVR looks specifically at autonomous shuttles and robot-taxis. It aims to define shared test scenarios, build a national reference system, and use both digital simulation and infrastructure-based validation for operational safety. Expected outcomes and benefits include:
More robust methods for validating autonomous vehicle safety without relying only on physical tests.Shared scenario libraries & simulation frameworks to reduce duplication of effort across industry.Better alignment between regulatory authorities and technology developers in safety protocols.Enhanced public confidence in autonomous and robotic transport systems.Future directions may involve scaling up these simulation platforms, improving the realism of test scenarios (weather, traffic, infrastructure variety), integrating regulatory approval processes, and extending results to other autonomous mobility contexts globally.

items.title: Finnish AI Region (FAIR) European Digital Innovation Hub (EDIH)
items.org: City of Helsinki, Department Economic development division
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This initiative aims to foster collaboration and innovation in AI across various sectors, with a focus on the Helsinki region. It focuses on practical applications and aims to create a world-class AI research and innovation hub by pooling expertise and resources and supporting regional development and networking. Moreover, FAIR provides a range of experimentation and testing platforms and offers the opportunity to test products and services in real-world settings.

The Finnish AI Region (FAIR) helps SMEs in the Helsinki area adopt AI and digital tools by offering free expertise, training, and access to testing platforms. Its goal is to build a world-class hub for AI research and innovation by pooling resources from universities, companies, and public actors. FAIR allows businesses to experiment with new products and services in real-world settings, reducing risks and supporting regional growth. As part of the EU’s Digital Innovation Hub network, it also connects local firms with European partners.

items.title: Dublin City Council’s Smart Dublin initiative: Project on Using AI-Enabled Cameras to Understand Vehicular Flows
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The AI-Enabled Cameras for Vehicular Flows project uses video streams processed by AI to monitor traffic automatically. It identifies and reports traffic patterns, reducing the need for manual monitoring or storing large volumes of footage. The initiative improves traffic management efficiency.

The Proof of Concept project: Using AI-Enabled Cameras to Understand Vehicular Flows aims to enhance traffic monitoring and management through AI technology. By processing video streams automatically, the system can identify vehicles, track traffic flow, and generate reports without human intervention or large storage requirements.
Key objectives include:
Automating traffic monitoring to reduce manual observation and associated costsImproving efficiency in traffic management and infrastructure planningMinimising storage needs by processing video in real time using AIThe project demonstrates the potential of AI applications in urban mobility and transport planning, providing insights that can help city authorities and transport agencies optimise traffic flow, reduce congestion, and improve safety.
Future outlook:
Expansion to larger urban areas for real-time traffic analysisIntegration with smart city infrastructure and other AI-driven transport solutionsDevelopment of scalable AI traffic management tools that can support decision-making in municipal planning

items.title: Dublin City Council’s Smart Dublin initiative: Project on Mapping City Assets from Street Level Imagery
items.org: SFI ADAPT Research Centre for AI-Driven Digital Content Technology
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Mapping City Assets from Street Level Imagery initiative uses AI to detect urban assets such as traffic signs, bins, and storm drains. Each asset is assigned accurate GPS coordinates, creating a geospatial record. This information supports city planning, operations, and maintenance.

The Mapping City Assets from Street Level Imagery initiative leverages AI and computer vision to systematically map urban infrastructure. Using street-level imagery, the system identifies assets such as traffic signs, waste bins, and storm drains, and assigns precise geospatial coordinates to each item.
Key objectives of the initiative include:
Creating a comprehensive geospatial database of city assetsSupporting municipal operations, planning, and maintenance through accurate and up-to-date informationEnabling integration with other information systems for enhanced city managementThe initiative facilitates data-driven urban management by allowing city authorities to quickly locate and monitor assets, plan maintenance schedules, and optimise resource allocation. By combining AI detection with geospatial mapping, the programme reduces manual surveying costs and improves the accuracy of asset inventories.
Future outlook:
Expansion to additional types of urban assetsIntegration with smart city platforms for real-time monitoringEnhanced predictive maintenance and planning capabilities using AI-generated insights

items.title: Dublin City Council’s Smart Dublin initiative: Project on Delivery Robots using AI enabled computer vision to solve issues regarding ‘last mile delivery’
items.org: Enterprise Ireland and Dublin City Council
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Delivery Robots Pilot Project uses AI-powered computer vision to improve last-mile delivery. The initiative tests autonomous delivery robots to make logistics faster, safer, and more efficient. It aims to reduce delivery costs and enhance service quality for customers.

The Delivery Robots Pilot Project is a pilot initiative designed to explore the use of autonomous robots equipped with AI computer vision for last-mile delivery. It addresses challenges such as traffic congestion, high labour costs, and the growing demand for faster and more reliable delivery services.
Key objectives include:
