Testing AI-enabled robots in real-world delivery scenariosImproving delivery efficiency and reducing operational costsEnhancing safety and reliability in urban and suburban logisticsThe project involves collaboration between technology developers, logistics companies, and research institutions, ensuring that the robots can operate effectively in complex environments. AI computer vision is used for navigation, obstacle detection, and route optimisation, enabling autonomous operation without human supervision.
Future outlook:
Expansion of autonomous delivery solutions to more urban areasIntegration with existing logistics networks for scalable deploymentContribution to smart city logistics and innovation in last-mile delivery systems

items.title: Digital Compass/data policy
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
Finland’s Digital Compass encompasses data policy, e.g. it outlines the country’s vision and goals regarding data management, sharing, and use.

Finland’s Digital Compass is a national plan that defines how the country manages its digital transformation, with a strong focus on data. It addresses the need for clear and coordinated rules around how data is collected, shared, and used. As digital services become a bigger part of everyday life, there is growing pressure to make sure that data is handled in ways that are safe, efficient, and fair for everyone—from individuals and businesses to public institutions.
One of the key objectives of the initiative is to make data more available and easier to use while protecting privacy and personal rights. The plan supports the use of open data, where possible, to help improve public services and support innovation. At the same time, it sets clear expectations around data security, transparency, and ethical use. The goal is to allow both public and private sector actors to use data in ways that create value without compromising trust.
The Digital Compass brings together a wide range of participants. It is led by the Finnish government, but involves collaboration with municipalities, companies, researchers, and civil society. The policy also aligns with wider European efforts to create a more unified and secure digital space. Through shared rules and coordinated action, the initiative helps ensure that data can flow between sectors and across borders, when appropriate, under common standards.
The approach is practical and structured. It includes steps like developing national data spaces—systems that allow different organisations to access and share data more effectively—and improving digital infrastructure to support this. It also promotes training and awareness so that organisations understand how to manage data responsibly. By setting out clear roles, goals, and tools, Finland’s Digital Compass helps make the country’s digital landscape more connected, secure, and useful.

items.title: Central Government Guidelines on Cloud Policies
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
The Ministry of Finance updated the central government’s cloud guidelines on Cloud policies in 2023. The updated policies emphasise a “Cloud First” strategy, encouraging the use of cloud solutions as the primary option. They also address the handling of public and confidential data in cloud environments, ensuring that data protection and security measures are in place.

In 2023, Finland’s Ministry of Finance updated the central government’s guidelines on the use of cloud services. These changes respond to the growing need for more flexible, efficient, and secure digital systems across public administration. As government operations become increasingly digital, cloud services offer opportunities to improve service delivery, reduce costs, and support remote access. At the same time, these changes raise important questions about data protection, especially when handling confidential or sensitive information.
The main goal of the updated policy is to promote a “Cloud First” approach. This means that cloud-based solutions should be the default choice when public authorities plan new digital services or update existing systems. However, the policy also makes clear that security and legal requirements must always be met. Special attention is given to how public and confidential data is stored and managed in cloud environments, to ensure that information is handled responsibly and in line with national and EU data protection laws.
The updated guidelines provide practical support for government departments and agencies. They include rules on risk management, supplier responsibilities, and technical requirements for cloud use. The policy encourages organisations to evaluate the benefits and risks of cloud services early in the planning process. It also promotes cooperation between different public bodies to share knowledge and develop common practices.
These updates build on earlier cloud strategies and reflect Finland’s broader digital goals. As more government services move online, the new policy framework helps ensure that cloud adoption happens in a secure, consistent, and well-governed way across the public sector.

items.title: BikeSafeAI
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The BikeSafeAI project uses AI to analyse cyclist behaviour and traffic conditions to identify risky situations. It aims to reduce accidents and improve safety for cyclists in urban and regional settings. The project is a collaboration between multiple universities, government bodies, and mobility organisations in the Netherlands.

The BikeSafeAI initiative is a multidisciplinary research project started in February 2024, running through August 2026. Its main aim is to provide insights into cycling behaviour and traffic risk, by using advanced AI technologies to detect situations that could lead to accidents. These insights are intended to inform policymakers, educators, and urban planners.
Key objectives of BikeSafeAI include:
Analysing traffic situations involving cyclists to identify patterns of risk (e.g. near-misses, conflict points) using sensor data, cameras, or other source data. Supplying actionable information for decision-makers (cities, municipalities, mobility authorities) to design safer infrastructure and interventions. Enhancing public awareness about cyclist safety through data-driven visualisations or reports. Implementation involves multiple partners, including:
Universities (Hanze University of Applied Sciences, NHL Stenden, University of Groningen) Regional government authorities (Provinces of Fryslân and Utrecht; City of Leeuwarden) Safety and mobility research and NGOs (SWOV, Fietsersbond, etc.)

items.title: AI for traffic management pilot project
items.original_name: Proġett pilota ta’ AI għat-tmexxija tat-traffiku
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Proġett pilota ta’ AI għat-tmexxija tat-traffiku
items.body:
The AI for Traffic Management Pilot Project in Malta integrates AI into traffic control systems and GIS. It aims to reduce congestion and emissions, improve public transport planning, and monitor traffic behaviours. The project provides data-driven insights to support intelligent journey management and traffic enforcement.

The AI for Traffic Management Pilot Project seeks to modernise Malta’s transport systems by embedding AI technologies into traffic lights and Geographic Information Systems (GIS). The initiative is designed to make traffic management more efficient, sustainable, and data-driven.
Key objectives of the pilot project include:
Reducing traffic congestion and vehicle emissions to improve urban mobility and environmental outcomesIdentifying patterns in transport behaviours to better understand traffic flows and commuter habitsSupporting intelligent journey planning and the scheduling of public transport servicesAssisting with traffic monitoring, policing, and enforcement to improve road safety and complianceThe project involves collaboration between government transport authorities, urban planners, and technology providers, ensuring AI solutions are aligned with real-world traffic management needs. By leveraging AI insights, Malta aims to make its urban transport system more efficient, responsive, and sustainable.

items.title: AI for Smart Cities Mobility
items.original_name: AI per la Mobilità delle Città Intelligenti
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: AI per la Mobilità delle Città Intelligenti
items.body:
The AI-based Smart City Solutions initiative uses artificial intelligence to improve traffic management and public transport. It develops intelligent networks to reduce congestion in high-traffic areas. The programme also supports environmental sustainability goals as part of the broader digital transition.

The AI-based Smart City Solutions initiative aims to make urban mobility smarter, safer, and more efficient through the use of AI technologies. Its primary focus is on traffic optimisation, public transport management, and intelligent network development in areas with high congestion. These solutions contribute to reducing emissions and improving the environmental sustainability of cities.
Key objectives include:
Optimising traffic flows to reduce congestion and travel timesEnhancing public transport efficiency through AI-driven scheduling and routingDeveloping intelligent infrastructure networks that integrate real-time data for better urban managementSupporting environmental sustainability goals by lowering emissions and energy useImplementation involves collaboration between municipal authorities, technology providers, and transport operators, ensuring that AI solutions are practical and scalable. By combining data-driven insights with urban planning, the initiative helps cities adapt to growing populations and complex mobility challenges.

items.title: AI for Policymaking
items.org: Ministry of Investments, Regional Development and Informatisation
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Slovak government is exploring the use of AI for data-driven policymaking. This involves using AI to analyse large datasets to identify trends, predict outcomes, and inform policy decisions. Such initiatives aim to make policymaking more evidence-based and effective.

The Slovak government is exploring the use of artificial intelligence to strengthen data-driven policymaking. Public bodies hold large amounts of information, but turning this into timely insights is difficult. AI offers tools to analyse datasets more quickly, identify trends, and predict outcomes, supporting more evidence-based and effective governance.
The aim is to move policymaking from reactive to proactive. Applications include labour-market analysis, health forecasting, or infrastructure planning. By modelling likely impacts, AI can help policymakers anticipate challenges and make better use of public resources.
These efforts are guided by Slovakia’s national AI strategy and supported through partnerships with researchers and technology providers.

items.title: AI Hub Tampere
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
AI Hub Tampere is a research centre dedicated to applied AI hosted by Tampere University and funded by public instruments. Backed by a coalition of 25 professors combining multiple disciplines, AI Hub explores the diverse socio-technical aspects of AI transformation.

AI Hub Tampere is a research centre hosted by Tampere University and supported by public funding. Its mission is to advance the use of applied artificial intelligence by connecting academic expertise with the needs of industry and society. The hub was created to help organisations better understand how AI can be used in real-world contexts. The initiative brings together a coalition of around 25 professors from different disciplines, reflecting the diverse ways AI affects technology, business, and society. This interdisciplinary base allows the hub to study the technical aspects of AI, like machine learning methods and data analytics, as well as the wider socio-technical impacts of digital transformation, including ethics, regulation, and human interaction with intelligent systems. AI Hub Tampere offers workshops, demonstrations, and collaboration projects that help companies and public organisations explore AI opportunities.

items.title: A12 traffic forecaster
items.org: Ministry of Infrastructure and Water Management
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The A12 Traffic Forecaster is a machine learning-based application that predicts traffic levels on the A12 motorway. It combines historical data, roadwork schedules, and holiday periods to deliver real-time updates. This helps commuters plan their journeys more efficiently and avoid congestion.

The A12 Traffic Forecaster is an AI-powered tool designed to improve traffic management and commuter experience on one of the country’s busiest highways. Using machine learning algorithms, it analyses a wide range of inputs — including historical traffic data, scheduled roadworks, weather conditions, and holiday periods — to predict traffic levels with greater accuracy.
Key objectives include:
Providing real-time traffic forecasts to commuters and logistics operatorsReducing congestion by enabling better route planningImproving road safety and travel efficiencyBy integrating multiple data sources, the system not only benefits individual drivers but also supports public authorities and transport agencies in managing traffic flow and planning infrastructure. Over time, the model can be expanded to cover other motorways and urban areas, creating a smarter, data-driven transport network.

items.title: 3VisionD
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
3VisionD is an AI-powered video analytics system that detects objects and determines their locations in real-world 3D coordinates. It supports smart city applications such as traffic and parking management, urban planning, and harbour monitoring. The system enables automated parking violation detection, occupancy tracking, and adaptive street lighting based on real-time data.

3VisionD is an advanced AI-driven system designed to process video streams from multiple cameras and generate real-time 3D location data for objects in urban environments. By converting visual data into actionable information, it helps municipalities and city planners make better decisions and optimise urban operations.
Key objectives and applications include:
Smart traffic and parking management: automated detection of violations and monitoring of occupancyUrban planning support: providing real-time data for city infrastructure optimisationHarbour and logistics monitoring: tracking movement and positioning of vehicles or equipmentAdaptive street lighting: adjusting lighting based on real-time human presence in parking areasThe system is designed for scalable deployment in multiple urban contexts, integrating AI analytics with city infrastructure to improve efficiency, safety, and sustainability. It supports municipalities in making data-driven decisions while reducing manual monitoring needs.
Future outlook:
Broader integration across smart city infrastructureEnhanced AI capabilities for predictive analytics and automated managementExpansion to additional urban sectors, including public safety and mobility management

items.title: "Digitisation and decarbonisation of mobility" strategy
items.original_name: Stratégie d’accélération digitalisation et décarbonation des mobilités
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Stratégie d’accélération digitalisation et décarbonation des mobilités
items.body:
The “Digitisation and Decarbonisation of Mobility” strategy in France aims to speed up the use of digital technologies and low-carbon solutions in mobility systems. It supports projects that reduce emissions from passenger and freight transport using “smart”, automated, or connected mobility tools. With public funding, it encourages innovation in logistics, infrastructure, and transport services to make mobility greener and more efficient.

The strategy, launched under PIA4 (the fourth Investment Programme for the Future), allocates €570 million toward three main goals: improving ecological performance, enhancing economic competitiveness, and ensuring territorial cohesion while addressing sovereignty and resilience. ActuIA It brings together stakeholders including transport-sector actors, local authorities, research institutes, and federations to collaborate on deployment of digital & low-carbon mobility solutions. ActuIA
Key components include:
Calls for projects such as Logistics 4.0, the “Automated road mobility, connected and low-carbon service infrastructures”, and Digitalisation and Decarbonisation of Rail Transport. These focus on innovations in multimodal transport, connected infrastructure, and automation. ActuIACross-cutting measures: training and skills development, changes in professional practices, and reference system updates, especially in complex systems and safety. Also, research programmes (e.g. Priority Research Programme and Equipment, PEPR) to study flow of people/goods and lifecycle impacts. ActuIAOver time, the strategy is expected to lead to demonstration projects and prototypes, followed by industrial-scale deployment. It aims to integrate automated, connected, and low-carbon mobility solutions across regions, improve logistics chains, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, and strengthen France’s technological sovereignty in mobility innovation

items.title: Technology Incubation Project
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This initiative focuses on developing a network of technology incubation hubs in Czechia to foster the growth of start-ups and spin-offs, especially in innovative AI fields. By 2025, the project aims to support around 250 start-ups with both financial aid and mentoring, helping them bring new AI-driven products and services to market.

The Technology Incubation programme in Czechia supports early-stage start-ups and spin-offs in fields like AI, mobility, space, and sustainability. It was created to address the lack of early funding, mentoring, and customer access that often prevents young teams from growing. By 2025, the aim is to help around 250 start-ups bring new products and services to market.
Selected start-ups receive non-equity grants, tailored mentoring, and access to specialised hubs across the country. New cohorts are admitted in waves, and AI has emerged as one of the strongest tracks with dozens of projects already in incubation. The long-term plan is to build a national ecosystem where successful alumni and investors feed back into supporting the next generation of start-ups.

items.title: TWIST
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This initiative, running between 2025 and 2031, is aimed at strengthening innovation within existing companies and adapting to industrial and technological shifts. It emphasises supporting AI research and industrial applications through strategic investments, with a specific focus on AI, quantum technologies, and semiconductors. The first call for projects targets AI R&D.

The TWIST programme (2025–2031) is aimed at helping Czech companies adapt to rapid technological shifts. It focuses on strengthening innovation in key fields such as AI, quantum technologies, and semiconductors. The first call supports AI research and development, giving firms the chance to secure subsidies of up to CZK 30 million for projects that often involve cooperation with SMEs or research organisations.
Its main goal is to raise the innovation capacity of established companies and ensure they can compete in strategic technologies critical for long-term growth. The programme will gradually expand, with future calls expected to cover semiconductors and quantum projects, backed by significant state funding and linked to national infrastructure such as Digital Innovation Hubs.

items.title: Social Security Chatbot
items.org: Secretary of State for Digitalization and Administrative Modernization
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
A chatbot created during the COVID-19 crisis to answer citizens’ frequent questions, with future plans for full integration with the Social Security Portal and the addition of live chat options with human agents.

Portugal launched an AI-powered virtual assistant on the ePortugal portal during the COVID-19 crisis to make public services easier to access online. The tool answers frequent questions, guides users through procedures such as accessing their digital authentication systems, and is available in several languages.

items.title: Secure platform for developing transparent Danish language models
items.org: Danish Foundations Models consortium (Aarhus University, University of Southern Denmark, University of Copenhagen, Alexandra Institute)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This platform for developing and training language models will be established for Danish companies and authorities to freely access and use and further develop Danish language models for their own contexts. The initiative will be run under the auspices of the Danish Foundations Models – a collaboration between Aarhus University, the University of Southern Denmark, the University of Copenhagen and the Alexandra Institute on research-based development of language models.

Denmark is setting up a national platform so companies, public authorities, and researchers can freely access and develop Danish-language AI models. Today, most advanced language technologies are built for English or controlled by large foreign firms, leaving smaller languages and local institutions at a disadvantage. This initiative addresses that gap by offering secure, research-based tools tailored to Danish needs.
As Initiative 3 of Denmark's national AI strategy, the project is led by Aarhus University, the University of Copenhagen, the University of Southern Denmark, and the Alexandra Institute under the “Danish Foundation Models” programme. It will run on UCloud, a secure computing environment already connected to European supercomputers.

items.title: SME: Digital and Denmark’s Export and Investment fund (EIFO) digitalisation support for small businesses
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Support to SMEs through grants, mainly for the purchase of private advice to identify digitalisation potential (including an AI-dedicated strand) or advice on implementation. Other support measures include subsidies for investments; skills and management development; and guidance on digital development. In addition, since May 2023, the EIFO facilitates access to financing for smaller Danish companies for digitalisation.

Small and medium-sized firms often lack the resources to make full use of digital tools like AI. To address this, Denmark’s Export and Investment Fund (EIFO) supports SMEs with grants for expert advice on digitalisation and AI, as well as subsidies for investments, training, and management development. Since May 2023, EIFO has also worked with the European Investment Fund to make financing more accessible, unlocking more than DKK 300 million for smaller firms to upgrade their digital capacity.
EIFO combines grants, loans, equity, and guarantees to help companies adopt new technologies and build skills. In 2024, it invested in nearly 80 companies and over a dozen funds, including in AI infrastructure. Over time, EIFO’s support is expected to reach more sectors and firms, spreading digital know-how and strengthening Denmark’s competitiveness in the digital economy.

items.title: PlanAPP Project
items.org: Centre for Planning and Evaluation of Public Policies
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The project is an EU-funded initiative led by the public administration planning, policy, and foresight competence centre. This project focuses on applying AI to enhance regulatory impact assessments. By leveraging AI, PlanAPP aims to improve the quality and efficiency of regulatory analysis at both national and European levels. The project collaborates with Nova Information Management School.

The PlanAPP / IA2AI project was created to make regulatory impact assessments in Portugal more reliable and efficient. Many laws are passed without fully anticipating their costs or side effects, which can weaken trust and create unnecessary burdens. By introducing AI into the process, the project helps analysts test draft legislation more quickly, spot risks, and compare alternatives before decisions are made.
Led by PlanAPP, Portugal’s public administration centre for planning and foresight, the initiative builds on earlier work by the Technical Unit for Legislative Impact Assessment. It works in partnership with Nova Information Management School and other experts to design AI tools that support ministries and agencies. The project began under EU funding and has since been integrated into PlanAPP’s broader work. It aims to extend use across more policy areas and levels of government, improving regulatory quality at both national and European scales.

items.title: Order no. 234/2022 regarding professional training and development programs for civil servants
items.original_name: ORDIN nr. 234/2022 pentru stabilirea domeniilor prioritare de formare și perfecționare profesională și a tematicii specifice programelor de formare și perfecționare profesională a funcționarilor publici
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: ORDIN nr. 234/2022 pentru stabilirea domeniilor prioritare de formare și perfecționare profesională și a tematicii specifice programelor de formare și perfecționare profesională a funcționarilor publici
items.body:
The purpose of this initiative is to train civil servants in ICT and emerging technologies, including AI, as foreseen in the Order of the National Agency of Public Officers no. 234/2022.

Romania has introduced a training programme for civil servants under Order no. 234/2022, issued by the National Agency of Public Officers. The goal is to update staff skills in ICT and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, to meet the growing digital demands of public administration.
The Order sets out priority areas (including digital literacy, cybersecurity, data management, and AI awareness) that ministries and agencies must include in their annual training plans. Courses are delivered through the National Institute of Administration and accredited providers, ranging from introductory modules to more advanced training.

items.title: ION
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
An initiative to support citizen engagement in the public sector, ION, an AI counsellor designed to serve as a link between Romanian citizens and the executive branch of government, leveraging natural language processing and computer vision techniques with the aim of capturing the sentiments of Romanian citizens in real time. This tool was developed with a Bucharest-based company - Humans.ai - in collaboration with Romanian AI researchers and computer science professors.

Romania’s ION is an AI “counsellor” launched in 2023 to improve how the government listens to citizens. Developed with the Bucharest-based company Humans.ai and local researchers, it was presented by the prime minister as the world’s first AI honorary government adviser.
The tool gathers input directly from citizens through an online platform and also scans social media to track public concerns. Using natural-language processing, it identifies key topics and measures sentiment, offering officials a quicker view of what matters to the public. A mirror-like installation also allows people to leave messages in person.
ION’s main goals are to strengthen citizen engagement, reduce the delay in detecting issues, and bring real-time evidence into policymaking.

items.title: European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs)
items.org: Ministry of Investments, Regional Development and Informatization
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs) in Slovakia play a crucial role in supporting the uptake of AI and other innovative technologies in public sector organisations. These hubs provide resources, expertise, and support for implementing AI-driven solutions to enhance public service delivery.

Slovakia’s European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs) help public bodies and businesses adopt AI and other digital tools. Many administrations lack expertise and struggle to test solutions before use; the hubs act as one-stop shops, offering guidance, pilot projects, and training.
Their main objectives are to provide “test-before-invest” services, build staff skills, and connect public organisations with researchers and technology providers. This supports more efficient service delivery - for example through AI-based document handling, data analysis, or cybersecurity tools - while reducing risks and costs.
The Slovak network includes the SKAI-eDIH led by the Kempelen Institute of Intelligent Technologies, as well as hubs like the Center for Innovative Healthcare (CIH) and Cassovium in Eastern Slovakia.

items.title: DigitalLead
items.org: DigitalLead is co-financed by the Danish Agency for Higher Education and Science, the Danish Business Development Agency and the European Regional Development Fund.
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Part of the business promotion system and Denmark's national cluster for digital technologies, serves as a hub for digital innovation – both for companies developing digital solutions and for other sectors in need of innovative digital solutions. The cluster build bridges between businesses, entrepreneurs, and knowledge institutions.

DigitalLead is Denmark’s national cluster for digital technologies and part of the country’s business promotion system. It was created to bridge the gap between companies developing digital solutions and sectors that need help adopting them, such as healthcare, energy, and manufacturing. The cluster’s aim is to boost digital innovation across the economy. For tech developers, it offers access to networks, research, and funding opportunities. For other industries, it provides guidance on identifying and testing solutions, ensuring digital tools are effectively applied. DigitalLead brings together businesses, entrepreneurs, universities, and knowledge institutions through joint projects, training, and matchmaking activities. This creates pathways for research results and new ideas to be turned into practical services and products.

items.title: Digital Research Centre Denmark (DIREC)
items.org: Ministry of Higher Education and Science, Innovation Fund Denmark
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
DIREC’s research spans ten areas in advanced digital technology. It aims to develop and support research in AI, big data, IoT, and IT Security.

Digital Research Centre Denmark (DIREC) was created to strengthen Denmark’s position in digital technologies such as AI, big data, IoT, and cybersecurity. Many advanced digital tools are still developed abroad, and Denmark risks falling behind if it does not invest in its own research capacity. DIREC addresses this by uniting universities, companies, and public institutions to develop new knowledge and practical solutions, while also ensuring that digital innovation reflects Danish values and priorities.
The centre is a non-profit partnership of eight Danish universities and the Alexandra Institute. It funds and coordinates projects where researchers and industry work together on concrete challenges, from safer digital infrastructures to smarter health technologies. Since 2020, DIREC has expanded to dozens of projects and more than fifty partners.

items.title: Digital Croatia Strategy
items.org: Government of the Republic of Croatia
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
A comprehensive national digital transformation strategy that aims to strengthen the Croatian market's investment cycle through additional financial resources for new technologies, including AI and green technologies.

The strategy particularly emphasizes supporting SMEs and accelerating the digital transformation of Croatian companies through increased adoption of AI technologies.

items.title: Centre for Artificial Intelligence in Society
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Danish government establish an interdisciplinary centre for research and advice on using AI in society. The centre will work closely with the Pioneer Centre for Artificial Intelligence. The centre will serve as a single point of access to knowledge and advice on how authorities and companies can best use AI in practice and will also conduct independent research and practice-oriented evaluation and monitoring of generative AI.

Denmark has launched a new interdisciplinary centre to guide how AI is used in society. Many public authorities and companies face uncertainty about when and how to apply AI responsibly, and the centre will act as a single point of access for advice and knowledge. It will also carry out independent research and evaluate the impact of generative AI.
The main goals are to strengthen responsible innovation, provide practical guidance, and build public trust in AI. The centre brings together experts from different fields and works closely with the Pioneer Centre for Artificial Intelligence, combining technical and policy expertise. Over time, it is expected to expand its monitoring role and partnerships, making it a lasting national resource for evidence-based AI governance.

items.title: Caixa Geral de Aposentações AI Virtual Assistant
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The General Retirement Fund has implemented an AI-based virtual assistant on its portal. This virtual assistant is designed to answer frequently asked questions (FAQs), thereby improving user navigation and reducing wait times for responses. It helps users find the information they need more efficiently and enhances the overall user experience on the CGA portal (CGA, 2023[759]). The CGA is a Portuguese institution responsible for managing the social security regime for public sector employees.

The General Retirement Fund (CGA), which manages pensions for Portuguese public sector employees, has introduced an AI-based virtual assistant on its portal. The tool was created to address the high volume of recurring questions about pensions, documents, and procedures, which often caused delays on phone and email channels.
The assistant’s main role is to answer FAQs instantly, guide users to relevant forms or services such as CGA Directa, and ensure replies are consistent. By working around the clock, it reduces waiting times and improves navigation, while also collecting insights into which topics generate the most confusion

items.title: Advanced digital skills training program for civil servants
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The objective of this investment (under the RRP) is to increase the advanced digital skills of the civil servants, aiming to support the digitalisation of the public services by improving the availability of a qualified workforce for internal IT&C operations. The investment consists of training for advanced digital skills (database management, system management, business analysis, data analysis, programming) for 32,500 civil servants
(out of which 2,500 seniors).

As part of its Recovery and Resilience Plan (RRP), Romania is investing in advanced digital training for civil servants to accelerate public sector digitalisation. Many institutions lack in-house expertise for IT and data operations, slowing reform and leaving them dependent on external providers. The program aims to train 32,500 officials, including 2,500 senior staff, in areas such as database and system management, business and data analysis, and programming. By developing these skills internally, the government hopes to build a more resilient, capable workforce for ongoing digital transformation.
The initiative is coordinated by the National Agency for Civil Servants with training providers like the National Institute of Administration. It runs until June 2026 and is tied to specific milestones under the RRP.

items.title: AEXCIA Platform
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Over the next two years, the AEXCIA platform, an AI-powered consumer experience management tool, will automate the handling of citizens’ complaints and information requests while analysing consumer behaviour, particularly on social networks. Designed to enhance efficiency, AEXCIA will support regulatory and supervisory activities by providing insights into consumer satisfaction and company conduct, ultimately improving consumer experience management through advanced AI capabilities.

The AEXCIA platform is being developed to help regulators manage the growing number of consumer complaints and requests, which are often too complex and numerous for traditional systems to handle efficiently. Citizens increasingly use digital channels and social media to voice concerns, and this creates both opportunities to better understand public sentiment and challenges in processing large volumes of data.
AEXCIA’s main goal is to strengthen consumer protection by automating the intake and processing of complaints while also analysing patterns in consumer behaviour. Portugal’s communications regulator (ANACOM) will use it to support supervisory work, improve oversight of service providers, and design policies that better reflect consumer needs. By reducing manual work and providing actionable insights, the tool aims to increase both efficiency and transparency.

items.title: nxtAIM
items.org: Ministry for Economic Affairs and Climate Action
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Funded by the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Climate Action (BMWK), this joint project develops and trains generative AI methods for autonomous driving. It seeks to remove barriers to the deployment of automated and autonomous vehicles. For the first time, participating companies are sharing proprietary datasets to jointly train foundation models.

This joint project is part of Germany’s New Vehicle and System Technologies programme and is funded by the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Climate Action (BMWK). Its main goal is to develop and train generative AI models that can accelerate the safe and large-scale deployment of automated and autonomous vehicles.
The project tackles several key challenges:
Overcoming technical and operational barriers to autonomous drivingCreating foundation models for self-driving systems using generative AIPooling proprietary datasets from multiple companies for the first time to train large, high-quality AI models collaborativelyThe initiative is also designed to strengthen Germany’s position in AI-powered mobility innovation, by promoting cross-industry collaboration and reducing duplication of effort in data collection and model training.
Future outlook:
Development of robust, scalable generative AI models for autonomous drivingBroader data-sharing frameworks between companies to accelerate innovationFaster, safer deployment of automated and autonomous vehicles on public roads

items.title: Wizards (Teachers Lead Tech)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This programme helps all computer science teachers in grades 1-4 and 5-8 to creatively integrate computer science into their lessons.

The programme offers a team of education and learning experts who provide teachers and children with the tools intended to unlock the potential of technology and use it for creativity.

items.title: Web-based advice on AI in education
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The National Agency for Education provides a web-based support tool for teachers, schools leaders and school providers on the risks and opportunities of AI in schools, particularly in view of generative AI-powered chatbots.

The rise of AI tools like generative chatbots brings both new chances and challenges for schools. Teachers and school leaders need guidance on how to use these tools responsibly while avoiding problems like cheating or privacy issues. To help with this, the National Agency for Education has created a web-based support tool for educators and school administrators.
The tool’s main goal is to provide clear advice on the risks and benefits of AI in schools. It helps users understand how AI can support learning and what steps to take to ensure ethical use and protect academic integrity. It covers practical topics like digital skills, data privacy, and responsible AI use in teaching.
Developed by the National Agency for Education, the tool is freely available online and designed for teachers, school leaders, and school providers. It is regularly updated to reflect changes in AI technology and real experiences from schools, helping educators adapt and use AI in a safe and effective way.

items.title: Walloon Export and Foreign Investment Agency (Agence wallonne à l'Exportation et aux Investissements étrangers, AWEX)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
AWEX supports the development of large-scale data centres in Wallonia.

This initiative is part of broader regional efforts to enhance ICT infrastructure, drive data innovation, and attract foreign investment to strengthen Wallonia's position in the digital economy.

items.title: Wallonia Undertaking  (Wallonie Entreprendre)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Wallonie Entreprendre supports strategic investments in large-scale data centres to bolster regional ICT infrastructure and facilitate the growth of Wallonia’s data-driven economy.

The initiative’s main objective is to provide the ICT backbone that enables businesses, researchers, and public actors to make full use of AI and data technologies. By funding and facilitating the development of modern data centres, Wallonie Entreprendre helps ensure that companies can access the computing power and storage they need to grow. In the future, this investment is expected to attract more technology-driven firms to the region, create new partnerships with international actors, and prepare the local economy for further AI applications across sectors such as healthcare, manufacturing, and public services.

items.title: Vlaams Supercomputer Centrum (VSC)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The VSC operates Flanders’ Tier-1 and Tier-2 HPC systems, supporting cutting-edge research in AI, machine learning (ML), and computational science.

This initiative offers comprehensive access to resources for academia and industry, facilitating advancements in areas such as natural language processing (NLP), genomics, and climate modelling.

items.title: Urban Data Space
items.org: GATE Institute (Big Data for Smart Society), Sofia University
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Led by GATE, the Urban Data Space is the first sectoral data space in Bulgaria. It facilitates data sharing and access between organisations to enable the development of new business products and services.

With a particular focus on urban services, it serves as a model for future sector-specific data spaces in Bulgaria by demonstrating how data-driven decision-making and cross-organisational collaboration can enhance service delivery.

items.title: Update to the general programme of computer science (classes 1-12)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This initiative examines AI topics and intends to improve AI literacy skills.

This initiative assesses the reliability of data and information, discuss the advantages and possible dangers of AI, recognize the areas of application of AI and neural networks, evaluate advantages and threats.

items.title: Transversal Cloud Adoption Plan
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Transversal Cloud Adoption Plan proposes a unified framework for adopting secure public cloud solutions across federal institutions. It includes capacity-building measures, governance structures, and guidelines for a consistent cloud policy to enhance efficiency and security in the public administration.

This initiative includes capacity-building measures, governance structures, and guidelines for a consistent cloud policy to enhance efficiency and security in the public administration.

items.title: The Wallenberg AI and Transformative Technologies Education Development Program
items.org: Wallenberg AI and Transformative Technologies Education Development Program
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Denmark has started collaborating with NVIDIA in 2024 to establish the centre for AI innovation that will host one of the world’s most powerful AI supercomputers (Gefion). Researchers from Denmark’s public and private sectors will gain access to a state-of-the-art supercomputer optimised for large-scale projects using AI as well as  software platforms, training, and expertise (Novo Nordisk Foundation, 2024).

As artificial intelligence continues to develop rapidly, having access to powerful computing resources is essential for researchers aiming to push the boundaries of AI. To meet this need, Denmark began collaborating with NVIDIA in 2024 to create the Centre for AI Innovation. This new centre will host Gefion, one of the world’s most powerful AI supercomputers, designed to support large-scale AI projects. This initiative addresses the challenge of providing Danish researchers from both public institutions and private companies with advanced tools and infrastructure necessary for innovative AI work.
The primary objective of this collaboration is to offer widespread access to state-of-the-art AI computing power, along with software platforms, training, and expert support. Gefion will enable users to work with extensive datasets, develop sophisticated AI models, and explore new applications that require significant processing capabilities. The centre aims to accelerate AI research and development across Denmark by equipping researchers with the resources and knowledge needed to succeed.
The centre brings together stakeholders from Denmark’s public research sector, private industry, and technology partners. NVIDIA provides the supercomputing technology and technical expertise, while Danish universities, research institutions, and companies contribute projects, data, and skilled researchers. This partnership creates a collaborative environment that promotes knowledge sharing and innovation within Denmark’s AI community.
Since its launch, the centre is expected to grow both in capacity and influence. As more researchers and organizations utilize Gefion and the related services, Denmark plans to expand training programs, software tools, and support services to keep pace with evolving AI demands. This growth will help maintain Denmark’s position as a leading country in AI research and innovation.

items.title: TRANSPORT 2030
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The TRANSPORT 2030 programme supports applied research and innovation in the transport sector in the Czech Republic. It emphasises AI, automation, digitalisation, and advanced transport technologies across all modes of transport. The programme brings together research organisations, private companies, and public entities to develop next-generation transport solutions.

The TRANSPORT 2030 programme is a national initiative aimed at promoting applied research and development in the transport sector. Managed jointly by the Technology Agency of the Czech Republic and the Ministry of Transport, it provides funding and coordination to drive innovation across road, rail, air, and water transport.
Its objectives include:
Advancing AI-based automation and digitalisation in transport systemsSupporting the development and testing of advanced transport technologiesEncouraging collaboration between research institutions, businesses, and public authoritiesStrengthening the competitiveness and sustainability of the Czech transport sectorThe programme funds projects across all modes of transport, ensuring that innovative solutions are shared and scaled throughout the industry. By prioritising AI and digitalisation, TRANSPORT 2030 helps modernise infrastructure, improve safety, and enhance efficiency in both passenger and freight transport.
Looking ahead, the initiative aims to continue expanding support for pilot projects, integrate emerging technologies such as autonomous mobility and smart infrastructure, and build a stronger link between research outcomes and real-world implementation.

items.title: Strategic projects for economic recovery and transformation (PERTE) of the new language economy
items.original_name: PERTE Nueva Economía de la lengua
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: PERTE Nueva Economía de la lengua
items.body:
The plan, which also covers dimensions beyond AI proper, aims to contribute to AI learning in Spanish and co-official languages.

Partly implemented through the National Plan for Language Technologies, which encompasses all initiatives related to developing language technologies and AI in Spanish and co-official languages, in particular:
Linguistic corpora will be developed made up of texts of different kinds (novels, plays, film scripts, press news, etc.), but also that consider singing, oral or sign language, including terminologies and the generation of a metasearch engine for terms as well as technologies for the extraction and processing of neologisms (TeresIA project).Support for the Spanish Language and Artificial Intelligence Project (LEIA) to create a language data bank, enriched with contributions from the autonomous communities. Projects underway include AINA (Catalan), GAITU (Basque), NÓS (Galician) and VIVES (Valencian).Related initiatives concern the development of testing and validation of language models through actions led by the Royal Language Academy and the National Observatory on Society and Information Society (ONTSI, project ODESIA).Development of the ALIA language models, which will contribute to developing a GenAI foundation for the implementation of public administration use cases, AI services within the Spanish AI Factory, and the Spanish GenAI ecosystem more broadly.

items.title: State programme for developing, attracting and retaining talent – specific call on AI
items.original_name: Programa Estatal para Desarrollar, Atraer y Retener Talento
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Programa Estatal para Desarrollar, Atraer y Retener Talento
items.body:
Within the general objective of promoting the consolidation of the professional career of researchers in any thematic area, this call specifically promotes the consolidation of people whose field of research is framed within a strategic theme related to either AI or microelectronics and semiconductors.

The promotion of the consolidation of researchers' professional careers, encouraging the creation of permanent positions within their host institutions and supporting the start or strengthening of a research line through the funding of an individual R&D&I project, as well as the adaptation and renovation of spaces and laboratories and the improvement of equipment necessary for its implementation.
Within the general objective of promoting the professional career consolidation of researchers in any thematic area, this call specifically supports the consolidation of researchers whose field of study falls within a strategic area related to either Artificial Intelligence (AI) or microelectronics and semiconductors (Chips), for which an additional budget will be allocated.
The eligible activities under this initiative include:
a) An incentive for the creation of a permanent position in the principal investigator’s area of expertise, if applicable.
b) The implementation of an individual R&D&I project led by the principal investigator.
c) The adaptation of spaces, renovation of laboratories, and improvement of equipment necessary to launch or strengthen the principal investigator’s research line.

items.title: SolidLab Flanders
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
SolidLab Flanders is a research initiative to advance the use of solid-based personal data vaults for privacy-preserving data management. It works together with Flemish and international data-initiatives to create applications built on the Solid standard.

Initially funded by the Flemish Government and the RRF for its first two working years, it aims to position Flanders as a leader in personal data technology and create a collaborative data ecosystem involving policymakers, citizens, and businesses. In 2023, the initiative received additional funding from the Flemish government for the last two years of its work programme.

items.title: Silicon Economy Ecosystem
items.org: Ministry of Transport and Digital Infrastructure
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Silicon Economy Ecosystem project helps logistics companies of all sizes use AI-based tools to automate supply chain processes. It provides open-source data models, interfaces, and software/hardware components free of charge. The initiative aims to increase efficiency and innovation in the logistics sector.

The Silicon Economy Ecosystem is a research project funded by the German Federal Ministry for Digital and Transport. It focuses on developing AI-based solutions that allow logistics companies to intelligently automate business processes across the supply chain. By creating standardized components and interfaces, the project helps companies of all sizes adopt advanced logistics technologies efficiently.
Key objectives include:
Developing data models and AI-based software/hardware components to automate supply chain operationsMaking all tools and components open-source and freely available to companiesSupporting digital transformation and innovation in the logistics sectorThe initiative encourages collaboration between research institutions, technology providers, and logistics companies, ensuring that solutions are practical and scalable. By providing free access to high-quality AI components, the project lowers the barrier to adoption, particularly for small and medium-sized enterprises.
Future outlook:
Broader adoption of AI-enabled logistics solutions across the supply chainContinued development of open-source tools for process automationStrengthening Germany’s digital and AI capabilities in transport and logistics

items.title: School of Computational Thinking and Artificial Intelligence (EPCIA)
items.org: Ministry of Education and Vocational Training
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The School of Computational Thinking and AI is an experimental project developed aimed at exploring the possibilities of introducing computational thinking and AI for learning in the classroom. To this end, educational and training resources are created, classroom practices are carried out with students and impact research is developed. Resource on AI in education has also been developed.

The School of Computational Thinking was set up in the academic year 2018/19 to train teachers to develop programming and robotics in their classrooms. This initiative is coordinated by the National Institute for Education Technologies and Teacher Training (INTEF) in collaboration with the Autonomous Communities, which provide their own teachers for the project, as the education ministry does not have the competence for the teacher training in the regions.
In primary education, teachers use computer programming using Scratch 3.0 as a resource to learn mathematics. Arduino (open-source electronic prototyping platform enabling users to create interactive electronic objects) and working with cooperative learning structures let lower secondary education students enjoy creative technology classes.
Upper secondary (Bachillerato) and VET students begin practising Python language, mechanics and electronics contents using a simulator that enable them to programme devices such as drones, autonomous Formula 1 cars or robots. The website CodeIntef offers additional resources and information.

items.title: RICAIP - Research and Innovation Centre on Advanced Industrial Production
items.org: Czech Institute of Informatics, Robotics and Cybernetics (CIIRC CTU)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
RICAIP is an international research centre that connects testbeds in Prague, Brno, and Saarbrücken, Germany. It focuses on Industry 4.0 innovations and the application of AI in industrial production, promoting modular, distributed production methods. The centre aims to integrate AI into production processes, making them more adaptive to market needs.

RICAIP is an international research centre that develops and tests new models of smart manufacturing. By linking experimental facilities in Prague, Brno, and Saarbrücken, it provides a space where researchers and companies can trial artificial intelligence in real production environments. The aim is to design more flexible factories that can adapt quickly to changing demand, drawing on modular and distributed production methods. As the centre expands, it is strengthening cooperation between Czech and German institutions and contributing to Europe-wide efforts to apply AI in industry.

items.title: Public Administration Data Strategy
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Public Administration Data Strategy 2023–2027 is a cornerstone of Malta’s digital transformation in public administration, both from a technological and a governance standpoint.

The Public Administration Data Strategy  aims to enhance the digital information framework from both technological and governance perspectives through regulations, guidelines, measures for data protection, effective use, and interoperability of data. The strategy will establish single, centralised registers for individuals, organisations, geospatial data and government administrative data.

items.title: Programme for the development of AI skills
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
A specific programme for the development of AI skills (under development at the time of writing) will be launched as part of the national plan for digital competency enhancement (Plan Nacional de Competencias Digitales).

Initiatives proposed in the Plan (2021) relating to IA include: 
-Promote new technical degrees and/or increase the number of places in existing university degrees and speed up procedures so that new university degrees can be launched more quickly, opening up the field of collaboration with other fields of knowledge.
-Public-private partnerships to promote training on AI (e.g. non-formal learning programmes).
-Workforce transition programmes for the development of job-relevant skills in the area of AI.

items.title: Operation Programme Research, Development and Education
items.original_name: Operační program Výzkum, vývoj a vzdělávání
items.org: Ministry of Education, Youth and Sports
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Operační program Výzkum, vývoj a vzdělávání
items.body:
This programme has been the largest state-funded initiative in AI research and development in Czechia, supporting 23 AI-related projects. Its main focus is on bolstering AI innovation through educational and research efforts, facilitating advancements in both academic and applied AI fields.

In Czechia, the Operation Programme Research, Development and Education (OP VVV) is the largest state-funded initiative supporting artificial intelligence. It was launched to address a key challenge: many AI projects lack stable funding to move from research ideas to practical applications. By providing long-term support, the programme helps promising initiatives grow and strengthens the country’s capacity in this field.
The programme’s main aim is to foster AI innovation in both academic and applied settings. So far, it has supported 23 projects, ranging from fundamental research on algorithms to practical applications in areas such as health, manufacturing, and public services. This breadth ensures that AI development is not limited to a single sector but contributes to Czechia’s wider innovation ecosystem.
OP VVV works by funding projects led by universities, research institutes, and industry partners. Grants cover staffing, equipment, and infrastructure, while also encouraging collaboration and knowledge sharing across institutions. The programme is expected to expand its reach and strengthen ties with European AI initiatives, making Czech research more connected and internationally competitive.

items.title: Open Data Portal (Public Sector Data)
items.org: Council of Ministers of the Republic of Bulgaria
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This platform is designed to share a wide range of public sector data, including scientific data.

This Open Data Portal features over 47 000 resources and 4 000 registered users. While valuable for scientific collaboration, the portal faces limitations in hosting raw data, with resources primarily comprising articles or PhD dissertations.

items.title: Open Data Policy / Open Data Portal
items.org: Government of the Republic of Croatia
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Open Data Policy establishes a comprehensive framework for public sector data sharing, aiming to enhance transparency and create economic opportunities. The policy enables unrestricted access to government data for both domestic and international users, including researchers from academia and industry.

Through the Open Data Portal, which serves as a centralised repository, public authorities publish their datasets to foster innovation, support research initiatives, and promote government accountability.

items.title: National center for AI innovation
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Denmark has started collaborating with NVIDIA in 2024 to establish the centre for AI innovation that will host one of the world’s most powerful AI supercomputers (Gefion). Researchers from Denmark’s public and private sectors will gain access to a state-of-the-art supercomputer optimised for large-scale projects using AI as well as  software platforms, training, and expertise (Novo Nordisk Foundation, 2024).

In 2024, Denmark partnered with NVIDIA to create the Centre for AI Innovation, which will host Gefion—one of the world’s most powerful AI supercomputers. This initiative addresses the need for advanced computing resources to support large-scale AI research and development in Denmark.
The main goal is to provide researchers from universities, research institutes, and companies with access to cutting-edge AI hardware, software, training, and expertise. This will help them handle complex AI projects involving big data and advanced models more effectively.
The centre brings together public and private sectors to foster collaboration and innovation. NVIDIA supplies the supercomputing technology and support, while Danish institutions contribute research and talent.

items.title: National Strategy for Research Data Management
items.org: Ministry of Higher Education and Research, through the Danish e-Infrastructure Consortium (DeiC)
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
DeiC is also leading the work to implement the National Strategy for Research Data Management. The strategy targets research institutions and research funding organisations. It defines several principles and areas of action to strengthen the dissemination and financing of good data management practices, resulting in more FAIR research data (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) in Denmark.

Research today generates large amounts of data that need to be carefully managed to ensure quality, transparency, and usefulness. Without clear guidelines, researchers and institutions can struggle to store, organize, and share their data properly. To tackle this, Denmark created a National Strategy for Research Data Management, and DeiC leads the effort to put this strategy into practice.
The strategy targets research institutions like universities and the organizations that fund research. Its main goal is to promote better data management so that research data becomes easier to find, access, and reuse. This aligns with the FAIR principles—making data Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable—which help improve the transparency and impact of Danish research.
DeiC coordinates the work by collaborating with universities, funders, and other partners to develop tools, guidelines, and funding methods that encourage good data management. It supports training, sets standards, and helps build systems to store and share data securely. This national effort ensures that researchers across Denmark follow common practices, making research data a valuable shared resource.

items.title: National Strategy for Quantum Technology
items.org: Danish Ministry of Higher Education and Science
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
In 2022, the Danish Agency for Higher Education and Science published a research mapping on the quantum field. This shows that Danish quantum research is considered to be world-class in a number of fields and enjoys great international recognition. Over the last ten years, the activities of the Danish research institutions within the quantum area have been on the rise. New research groups have been established, and we have succeeded in recruiting several international top researchers.

In 2022, the Danish Agency for Higher Education and Science published a research mapping focused on quantum science and technology. This study showed that Danish quantum research is considered world-class in several areas and enjoys strong international recognition. Quantum science holds great promise for advancing computing, communications, and other technologies, and Denmark’s strong position highlights its potential to contribute significantly to these fields.
The main goal of the mapping was to assess Denmark’s strengths and identify opportunities in quantum research. This helps guide national policies and funding decisions to support and grow the country’s expertise in this important area. By understanding where Denmark stands globally, the government can better target investments and collaborations.
Over the past ten years, Danish research institutions have increased their quantum activities significantly. New research groups have been formed, and several top international researchers have been recruited. Universities and research centers across Denmark have created a vibrant environment for quantum research, often collaborating internationally. The Danish Agency for Higher Education and Science supports this work by monitoring progress and providing strategic backing.

items.title: National Plan on Vulnerable Collectives
items.org: Ministry of Social Rights, Consumption and Agenda 2030
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Spanish government is working towards the development of a National Plan on Vulnerable Collectives. A study on the impact of AI use on vulnerable collectives was expected to be conducted in Q4 2024.

he Spanish government is working to understand and address how artificial intelligence (AI) affects vulnerable groups in society. As AI becomes more common, there is concern that people like the elderly, those with disabilities, or low-income communities could be unfairly impacted or excluded. To ensure AI benefits everyone fairly, Spain is developing a National Plan focused on these vulnerable collectives and their experiences with AI.
The main aim of the plan is to identify potential risks AI poses to vulnerable groups and to promote their inclusion in the digital world. To support this, a detailed study is planned for late 2024 to examine how AI affects these populations. This study will gather insights from experts across various fields and include input from the vulnerable groups themselves. It will look at issues such as accessibility, privacy, bias, and social exclusion.
The results of the study will guide the creation of the National Plan, which will propose actions and policies to ensure AI is developed and used responsibly and inclusively.

items.title: National Data Governance Reference Framework (NDGRF)
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
A framework under development that will establish comprehensive standards for data management across Bulgaria's digital ecosystem. The NDGRF is established by decision of the Minister of Electronic Governance and regards the national public administration as a whole. This framework encompasses standards for data collection, quality assurance, storage protocols, and exchange mechanisms.

The National Data Governance Reference Framework (NDGRF) includes detailed procedural guidelines, metadata standards, and stakeholder engagement processes, with specific focus on developing and managing interoperable data spaces.

items.title: Mobility Innovation Hub
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Mobility Innovation Hub in Czechia is part of the National Technology Incubation framework. It connects start-ups, businesses, and research institutions to develop sustainable mobility and transportation technologies. The Hub accelerates innovation in urban transport, electrification, autonomous vehicles, and smart mobility.

The Mobility Innovation Hub serves as a central platform for innovation in sustainable mobility within Czechia’s National Technology Incubation framework. It was created to address pressing challenges in transportation by promoting the development of advanced mobility solutions.
Its main goals are to:
Foster collaboration between start-ups, established companies, and research institutionsAccelerate innovation in sustainable and smart mobility technologiesSupport the development of solutions in urban transportation, electrification, autonomous vehicles, and smart mobility systemsThe Hub functions as a bridge between research and industry, enabling new technologies to move from concept to market faster. By providing access to expertise, networking, and funding opportunities, it helps Czech companies and innovators remain competitive in the fast-evolving mobility sector.
Future outlook:
Expansion of innovation support services to more start-ups and SMEsStrengthening Czechia’s position in European mobility and transportation innovation networksContinued focus on green and digital transformation in transport

items.title: Legislative amendments for road transport automation
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
The Ministry of Transport and Communications in Finland is preparing legislative changes to enable road transport automation. A public consultation on the proposed amendments was held until 17 May 2024. The ministry aims to submit the government proposal to Parliament in autumn 2025.

The initiative seeks to create a legal framework for automated road transport in Finland, ensuring that emerging technologies can be safely and efficiently deployed. The ministry prepared a memorandum assessing necessary legislative amendments, which was made available for public and stakeholder comments until 17 May 2024.
Key objectives of the initiative include:
Updating road transport laws to accommodate automated vehiclesEnsuring safety and regulatory compliance while supporting innovationIncorporating stakeholder feedback into the legislative drafting processFollowing the consultation, officials at the Ministry of Transport and Communications will continue drafting the legislation. The goal is to submit a government proposal to Parliament during the autumn 2025 session, establishing a clear, robust, and forward-looking framework for automated road transport in Finland.
Future outlook:
Adoption of modernised transport legislation that supports automationEnhanced safety and operational standards for automated vehiclesCreation of an enabling environment for innovation and commercial deployment in Finland’s transport sector

items.title: Hybrid Cloud Enabling Infrastructure
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Platform providing government entities with suitable data hosting options.

The Malta Information Technology Agency (MITA) manages the Government's Hybrid Cloud Platform (HCP), which combines on-premise Tier 3 Datacentre infrastructure with Microsoft Data Centres in Europe. Connected to the Malta Government Network (MAGNET), this platform provides government entities with secure, flexible hosting options that meet regulatory requirements while enabling self-service deployments.

items.title: GovCloud
items.org: Danish Agency for Governmental IT Services (SIT)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Cloud service for governmental bodies hosted by the Danish Agency for Governmental IT Services (SIT) on the platform https://www.dmi.dk/frie-data, which is delivered as community cloud for SIT customers and offers data hosting on Danish territory. Used for distributing open meteorological data and for the National Data Portal among others.

The Danish Agency for Governmental IT Services (SIT) runs a cloud service specifically for government bodies. This service provides a secure, nationally hosted platform that meets the needs of public institutions requiring reliable access to data while ensuring it stays within Danish borders for legal and privacy reasons. It helps agencies share and manage data efficiently and safely.
The service’s main goal is to offer a shared digital platform where government agencies can host and distribute data. It is used for important functions such as distributing open meteorological data and supporting the National Data Portal, a central hub for government data. By centralizing these services, the cloud reduces costs, improves collaboration, and enhances data availability for public use.
Hosted entirely in Denmark, the cloud operates as a community resource shared among various government users but with strong security and control measures. The platform is provided by the Danish Meteorological Institute (DMI) at https://www.dmi.dk/frie-data, while SIT oversees the infrastructure and customer support.

items.title: Future Mobility Finland
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Future Mobility Finland is a national initiative that supports sustainable and innovative transport solutions. It promotes the use of AI technologies across public transport, private vehicles, and logistics. The initiative fosters collaboration and knowledge sharing to accelerate the transition to smarter, greener mobility.

Future Mobility Finland is a communication and collaboration platform designed to drive sustainable and innovative mobility solutions in Finland. It encourages the development and adoption of AI technologies to improve efficiency, safety, and environmental performance across multiple transport modes, including public transport, private vehicles, and logistics operations.
The programme’s objectives include:
Promoting AI integration in mobility and transport solutionsSupporting sustainable growth in the transport sectorFacilitating collaboration and knowledge exchange among companies, researchers, and policymakersAs part of the Finnish National Programme for Sustainable Growth in the Transport Sector (2021–2023), the initiative connects stakeholders to pilot projects, research efforts, and innovation activities that advance AI-driven mobility solutions.
Future outlook:
Expansion of AI-based solutions across all transport modesGreater integration of smart mobility services for citizens and businessesStrengthened positioning of Finland as a leader in sustainable, AI-enabled transport

items.title: Forma Program for Artificial Intelligence
items.org: Ministry of Science, Innovation and Universities
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The programme will finance up to 80% of the enrollment fee of nearly 8,000 young people studying AI in Spanish universities, both public and private.

As the demand for artificial intelligence (AI) skills grows, Spain is working to make AI education more accessible to young people. One of the main barriers for students is the cost of university tuition, especially in specialized areas like AI. To address this, a national programme has been launched to reduce financial obstacles and encourage more students to enter this high-demand field.
The initiative will finance up to 80% of enrollment fees for around 8,000 young people studying AI at universities across Spain—both public and private. Its main goal is to increase the number of trained professionals in AI and related areas, while also ensuring that access to education is not limited by personal financial circumstances.
The programme is managed at the national level and works in collaboration with universities. Students who meet the eligibility criteria can apply through their institution to receive this tuition support. This direct financial assistance helps broaden participation in AI studies and supports a more diverse and skilled future workforce.

items.title: European Testing and Experimentation Facility (TEF) Manufacturing
items.org: Three Czech universities, as part of the EU TEF Manufacturing consortium
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
This TEF project aims to boost the resilience and flexibility of the manufacturing sector by integrating AI and robotics into production. Czechia is represented by three universities collaborating with European partners to implement AI-based automation and intelligent systems for advanced manufacturing.

In Czechia, the Testing and Experimentation Facility (TEF) for manufacturing brings together three universities to help modernize production through artificial intelligence (AI) and robotics. Czech manufacturers, like many across Europe, face pressure to remain competitive while dealing with rising costs, supply chain disruptions, and the need for more sustainable processes. The TEF gives them access to advanced testing spaces where new technologies can be tried out in realistic industrial settings before being adopted on the factory floor.
