The main goal is to strengthen the resilience and flexibility of Czech industry. By supporting AI-driven automation, the TEF helps production lines adjust quickly to market changes, reduce errors, and manage resources more efficiently. Local companies can present specific challenges to the facility and receive support from researchers and engineers in designing practical solutions. At the same time, the project provides training opportunities so that workers gain the skills needed to use these tools effectively.
As part of a wider European network, the Czech TEF will benefit from shared expertise and common standards developed across the EU.

items.title: European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs)
items.org: EDIH Czech Technical University in Prague
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Czechia hosts key European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs) that facilitate the digital transformation of enterprises and public organisations. For instance, EDIH CTU focuses on supporting AI and HPC applications, offering tailored solutions for SMEs and the public sector through expert consultations, training, and access to cutting-edge infrastructure. Another notable hub, EDIH Testbed for Industry 4.0, specialises in advanced manufacturing technologies, helps organisations adopt Industry 4.0.

Czechia hosts several European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs) that help businesses and public institutions adopt advanced digital tools. Many organisations, especially small and medium-sized enterprises, face barriers such as high costs, limited expertise, and uncertainty about how technologies like artificial intelligence (AI) or high-performance computing (HPC) can be applied. The hubs address this by offering a safe space to test solutions, build skills, and access expert guidance before making large investments.
One example is EDIH CTU at the Czech Technical University in Prague, which supports AI and HPC applications. It provides consultations, training, and access to powerful computing resources so organisations can experiment with practical uses of AI. Another is the EDIH Testbed for Industry 4.0, which focuses on advanced manufacturing. Here, companies can trial robotics and automation technologies, working directly with researchers to solve production challenges and train staff in new methods.
Over time, Czech EDIHs are expected to deepen their links with the wider European network, giving local firms access to shared expertise across the EU. This scaling up will make it easier for Czech industry to adopt digital tools and remain competitive, resilient, and innovative.

items.title: Ethics Commission for the Assessment of Automated and Autonomous Vehicles
items.original_name: Etická komise pro posuzování automatizovaných a autonomních vozidel
items.category: National – AI governance bodies or mechanisms
items.document_name: Etická komise pro posuzování automatizovaných a autonomních vozidel
items.body:
The Ethics Commission for the Assessment of Automated and Autonomous Vehicles provides guidance on the ethical aspects of researching, testing, and deploying automated mobility, including AI-related systems. Established in 2020, it issues guidelines to ensure autonomous vehicle development follows ethical standards.

The Ethics Commission for the Assessment of Automated and Autonomous Vehicles was created in 2020 to address the ethical implications of introducing automated and autonomous mobility solutions. Its work covers the full spectrum of AI-related aspects in this field — from research and testing to deployment in real-world contexts.
The commission’s objectives include:
Ensuring that ethical considerations are integrated into the design, testing, and use of automated and autonomous vehiclesProviding guidelines and recommendations for policymakers, researchers, and companies developing or deploying such systemsPromoting public trust and safety by aligning autonomous mobility with ethical and societal valuesBy issuing guidelines, the commission supports the responsible development and roll-out of automated mobility. It helps governments, industry, and researchers understand the ethical boundaries and societal expectations associated with AI-driven vehicles.
Looking ahead, the commission is expected to update and expand its guidelines as technology and societal expectations evolve. This ongoing work helps ensure that autonomous vehicle deployment remains safe, transparent, and ethically sound.

items.title: Digital for Care: Digital Health Framework 2024-2030
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This framework has been developed to reflect recently established six HSE health regions in Ireland. The mission of the framework is to harness the power of new technologies, digital and data to transform how health and social care services are delivered for its population.

It sets out a roadmap to digitally transform health services in Ireland and improve access for patients through six key principles: patient as an empowered partner, workforce and workplace, digitally enabled and connected care, data-driven services, digital health ecosystem and innovation, and secure foundations and digital enablers.

items.title: Digital entrepreneurship programme for schoolchildren in grades 5-8 of the Ministry of Economy and Innovation
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This initiative aims to create a methodology for learning digital entrepreneurship to bring integrated, relevant, creative computer science and entrepreneurship lessons to students in grades 5-8.

Lithuania’s Ministry of Economy and Innovation has launched a Digital Entrepreneurship Programme to address the lack of early exposure to digital and entrepreneurial skills among pupils in grades 5–8. Many students at this age miss the opportunity to connect computer science with creativity and business thinking. The programme aims to fill that gap by designing a clear methodology for teaching digital entrepreneurship that is both practical and engaging.
The initiative works by developing integrated lessons that combine computer science, problem-solving, and entrepreneurship, tailored to young learners. Delivered in schools with support from trained educators, it encourages students to apply digital tools in creative ways while learning the basics of entrepreneurship. Over time, the programme plans to scale up across Lithuania, ensuring that more pupils gain the confidence and skills needed to participate in a digital economy.

items.title: Digital Transformation of Bulgaria Strategy 2024-2030
items.original_name: ЦИФРОВА ТРАНСФОРМАЦИЯ НА БЪЛГАРИЯ  ЗА ПЕРИОДА 2024-2030 г.
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: ЦИФРОВА ТРАНСФОРМАЦИЯ НА БЪЛГАРИЯ  ЗА ПЕРИОДА 2024-2030 г.
items.body:
The Digital Transformation of Bulgaria Strategy for 2024-2030 is a comprehensive framework that outlines Bulgaria's vision for digital development.

This framework incorporates initiatives related to AI and data governance, aligned with EU regulations and targets. The strategy emphasises enhancing digital skills, deploying secure infrastructure, promoting digitalisation in enterprises, improving public services, fostering research and innovation, and leveraging the potential of data.

items.title: Digital Decade: no one is left behind
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This initiative is aimed at reducing the digital exclusion of the Lithuanian seniors through a multi-year project by the Communications Regulatory Authority (CRA), consisting of a tour across communities of Lithuania to educate seniors on how to use digital services conveniently, how to protect themselves from fraud and what their rights as consumers are.

The Communications Regulatory Authority (CRA) in Lithuania launched the project “Digital Decade: no one is left behind” to address the digital exclusion of seniors. Many older citizens face difficulties using online services or recognising online fraud, which limits their ability to benefit from digital tools and puts them at risk. The project’s main goal is to ensure that seniors can access digital services confidently, safely, and with a clear understanding of their consumer rights.
The initiative works as a multi-year tour across Lithuanian communities, where CRA experts meet seniors directly, offer practical training, and provide guidance on everyday digital tasks. Participants learn how to use online services more easily, how to stay safe from scams, and where to seek help if needed. Over time, the project plans to expand its outreach, ensuring that more communities benefit and that seniors are better integrated into the country’s digital transformation.

items.title: Developing AI solutions at all education levels
items.org: Ministry of Education, Science and Sport
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This reform intends to apply international recommendations in Lithuanian educational institutions and integrate AI solutions into lessons safely, including by providing consultations and training for teachers on AI related issues.

Lithuania’s Ministry of Education, Science and Sport is leading a reform to bring artificial intelligence into classrooms at all levels of education. The initiative responds to the growing need for students and teachers to understand and use AI in a safe, informed way. Its main objective is to apply international recommendations on AI in schools and ensure that lessons integrate these tools responsibly and effectively.
The programme is coordinated with the National Education Agency and the Lithuanian Artificial Intelligence Association, which provide consultations, guidance, and teacher training. This support helps educators learn how to use AI in teaching while addressing ethical and safety concerns.

items.title: Data strategy for local governments
items.org: KL (Local Government Denmark), Agency for Digital Government
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Since 2001, Denmark's central, regional, and local governments have jointly developed digital strategies, forming the foundation for a future-ready public sector through multi-year agreements on digital direction. In 2022, the association of Danish municipalities published its data strategy for local governments (KL), which notably calls upon municipalities to make standardised data available.

Since 2001, Denmark’s central, regional, and local governments have worked together to create digital strategies that guide the development of a modern public sector. These strategies, agreed upon through multi-year plans, aim to make government services more efficient and accessible by coordinating digital efforts across different levels of government.
The initiative addresses the need for better access to and sharing of data within the public sector. Standardizing data is essential for smooth communication and collaboration between various government bodies, which ultimately helps provide better services to citizens.
In 2022, the association of Danish municipalities (KL) introduced a data strategy asking local governments to make their data available in a standardized way. This encourages greater efficiency, transparency, and easier access to information for both the public and businesses.
Going forward, the initiative will continue to evolve by expanding cooperation and improving how data is shared and used across all levels of government. This ongoing effort ensures that Denmark’s public sector stays prepared to meet future challenges with better digital tools and services.

items.title: Danish e-infrastructure Consortium (DeiC)
items.org: Danish e-Infrastructure Consortium (DeiC), Danish Research Network
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
DeiC is “the collaboration with and between the Danish universities. DeIC coordinates the delivery and development of the national digital research infrastructure. Its “purpose is to ensure that computing power, data storage and network infrastructure are available for Danish research and education”.

DeiC was created to ensure that researchers and universities across Denmark have access to the digital tools they need for modern scientific work. Today’s research depends heavily on powerful computing, secure data storage, and fast networks. Without a coordinated effort, these resources could be unevenly distributed or too expensive for individual institutions. DeiC brings all Danish universities together to share and develop this national digital infrastructure.
The main goal of DeiC is to provide reliable access to computing power, data services, and high-speed connections for all researchers in Denmark. This supports tasks like running complex simulations, managing large datasets, and collaborating internationally. DeiC also sets standards and works with partners across Europe to keep Denmark’s research connected and competitive.
DeiC is a collaboration between Danish universities, supported by the Ministry of Higher Education and Science. It also connects with European initiatives like the European Open Science Cloud, ensuring Danish researchers benefit from international cooperation. Each university both contributes to and benefits from this shared infrastructure.
DeiC is expanding to support better data management and secure platforms, especially as research grows in areas like AI and climate science. The initiative plans to scale up services and deepen its role in European research networks to meet future digital needs.

items.title: Business and scientific organisations Platform (S2B)
items.org: National Centre for Information and Documentation (NACID)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Platform aims to foster effective collaboration in research and innovation between the government, universities, scientific organizations, and businesses.

Through the Platform, small and medium-sized enterprises can access research and innovation services provided by universities, scientific organizations, Centers of Excellence, Competence Centers, Digital Information Hubs, Sofia Tech Park, and other entities within the regional R&D and innovation ecosystem.

items.title: Bulgarian Portal for Open Science (BPOS)
items.org: National Centre for Information and Documentation (NACID)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Bulgarian Portal for Open Science (BPOS) was created by the National Centre for Information and Documentation in line with the EC Recommendation No. 790 of 25 April 2018 on access to and preservation of scientific information, as well as Bulgaria’s commitments to the European Open Science Cloud (EOSC).

The Portal offers a single-entry point for easy and fast access to scientific information and the results of publicly funded research. It provides a secure online space where scientists and institutions can store and disseminate scientific publications and other research outputs on a long-term basis. Currently, the Portal contains over 73,000 documents, including scientific publications, dissertations, conference proceedings, preprints, project reports, and more. The registered scientists are over 5,200 (https://bpos.bg/).

items.title: Autonomous mobility projects PRISSMA Project - Research and Investment Platform for the Safety and Security of Autonomous Mobility
items.original_name: Projets de mobilité autonome Projet PRISSMA – Plateforme de recherche et d’investissement pour la sûreté et la sécurité de la mobilité autonome
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Projets de mobilité autonome Projet PRISSMA – Plateforme de recherche et d’investissement pour la sûreté et la sécurité de la mobilité autonome
items.body:
The PRISSMA Project develops a platform for the safety and security of autonomous mobility. It focuses on validating automated road transport systems, including AI components, to ensure safe operation. The project is part of an AI Challenge organised by the Innovation and Industry Fund.

The PRISSMA Project (Research and Investment Platform for the Safety and Security of Autonomous Mobility) is designed to support the development and validation of automated road transport systems. Its goal is to ensure that autonomous vehicles operate safely within predefined routes or areas. AI is integrated as part of the overall system-of-systems concept, allowing individual components to be tested and verified within a broader transport network.
Key objectives of the project include:
Verifying the safety and reliability of automated transport systemsIntegrating AI components into autonomous mobility platformsSupporting innovation in autonomous transport through targeted research and investmentThe project is part of a wider AI Challenge organised by the Innovation and Industry Fund, which selects and supports high-impact AI projects. Since its inception, five major AI-related challenges have been addressed under this initiative, demonstrating a strong focus on applied research and practical implementation.
Future outlook:
Expansion of autonomous mobility testing and validation in real-world environmentsContinued integration of AI-driven safety and monitoring systemsStrengthened collaboration between industry, research institutions, and funding bodies to accelerate innovation in autonomous transport

items.title: AIAMO Mobility Data Hub & Services
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The AIAMO initiative develops a data-sovereign platform for mobility services to support SMEs and smaller cities. It uses AI applications to simplify data collection and provide insights for environmentally friendly and multimodal traffic management. The project aims to improve reliable mobility options while prioritising climate protection.

The AIAMO initiative, led by the Federal Ministry for Digital and Transport (BMDV) in Germany, addresses the challenge of providing reliable, sustainable mobility while supporting climate protection goals. The initiative focuses on creating a data-sovereign platform that integrates multiple mobility services and makes them accessible to SMEs and smaller municipalities.
Key objectives include:
Simplifying data collection in the mobility sector to generate actionable insightsSupporting environmentally friendly and multimodal traffic managementEnabling SMEs and cities to access research findings and deploy AI applications for improved mobilityImplementation revolves around an interconnected integration zone, where trusted AI applications provide guidance for mobility solutions and ensure that SMEs and municipalities can make informed, sustainable decisions. The initiative combines data integration, AI-driven analytics, and practical service deployment to foster smarter, greener urban mobility.
Future outlook:
Expanded use of AI for traffic and mobility optimisation across smaller cities and regionsEnhanced access to market-ready AI solutions for SMEsContribution to Germany’s climate protection and sustainable transport goals

items.title: AI applications in mobility and logistics
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The AI applications in mobility and logistics initiative in Germany supports the use of AI for analysis, forecasting, and information systems. It aims to improve safety, efficiency, sustainability, and convenience in transport and logistics. The programme also promotes transferable AI concepts that can be applied across the sector.

The AI applications in mobility and logistics initiative, led by Germany’s Federal Ministry for Digital and Transport (BMDV), focuses on accelerating AI adoption in transportation and logistics. It supports the development of advanced AI-based systems for analysis, forecasting, and decision-making to make mobility safer, more efficient, and environmentally sustainable.
Key objectives include:
Enhancing safety in transportation through AI-supported monitoring and predictive systemsImproving efficiency and resource use in logistics operationsIncreasing convenience for users of transport systemsPromoting transferable concepts that can be applied across different mobility and logistics contextsThe initiative encourages collaboration between public authorities, research institutions, and private sector partners to ensure that AI solutions are practical, scalable, and aligned with real-world operational needs. Funding and technical support enable projects to develop innovative AI applications that can be implemented across the mobility and logistics sector.
Future outlook:
Broader deployment of AI technologies across transport networks and logistics chainsIntegration of AI into smart mobility solutions and automated transport systemsStrengthened coordination between research, industry, and policy to foster innovation and sustainability in mobility

items.title: A joint project of the education and learning programme "Vedliai" and "Lietuvos Junior Achievement" (LJA)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This joint project intends to bring integrated, relevant, creative computer science and entrepreneurship lessons for pupils in grades 5-8 to Lithuanian schools.

This joint initiative by the education programme Vedliai and Lietuvos Junior Achievement (LJA) addresses the gap in practical digital and entrepreneurial education for young students in Lithuania. Many pupils in grades 5–8 are not exposed early enough to how computer science and entrepreneurship can connect to real-world opportunities. The project aims to change this by offering integrated lessons that combine coding, digital creativity, and business thinking in ways that are accessible and engaging.
The programme is delivered directly in schools, supported by trained teachers and mentors who adapt the lessons to pupils’ age and interests. By blending computer science with entrepreneurship, it equips students with both technical and problem-solving skills while encouraging creativity and teamwork. Over time, the project plans to expand to more schools across Lithuania, ensuring that a larger share of pupils gain the knowledge and confidence needed to participate in the country’s growing digital economy.

items.title: Training scholarships
items.original_name: Programa para la formación en IA
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Programa para la formación en IA
items.body:
The program grants 374 training scholarships lasting four years in the field of AI and related areas such as massive data and information processing technologies; high performance computing; cloud computing; cybersecurity; biotech, medical devices, medical imaging; robotics or quantum technologies.

Spain faces an important challenge and opportunity as technology rapidly reshapes its economy and society. Fields like artificial intelligence (AI), data processing, and advanced computing are playing an increasingly central role across industries such as healthcare, manufacturing, and cybersecurity. However, Spain, like many countries, needs more highly trained experts to fully take advantage of these technologies and drive innovation. This program directly addresses that need by providing 374 scholarships for in-depth training in AI and several related high-tech areas.
The program’s main goal is to support students, researchers, and professionals over four years of study and research in fields that are crucial for Spain’s technological future. Besides AI, it includes disciplines like massive data and information processing, high-performance computing, cloud computing, cybersecurity, biotechnology, medical devices, medical imaging, robotics, and quantum technologies. By focusing on these key sectors, the initiative aims to build a strong, specialized workforce ready to contribute to Spain’s scientific progress and economic competitiveness.
Managed by government agencies or educational institutions in Spain, the scholarships provide recipients with the financial resources to fully commit to their training and research projects. This helps ensure that talented individuals can develop deep expertise without financial barriers. The program’s structure supports long-term skill development, recognizing that mastery in these complex, interdisciplinary fields takes time and dedicated effort.

items.title: Training of Professional and Managerial Staff in Education
items.org: Ministry of Education, Science and Sport
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Ministry of Education launched a public call for training of professional and managerial staff in education to strengthen competences for sustainable development and financial literacy as well as digital competences, which includes the field of AI.

he Ministry of Education has launched a national initiative to improve the skills of professionals and managers working in education. This initiative focuses on three key areas: sustainable development, financial literacy, and digital skills, which includes training in the field of artificial intelligence (AI). The aim is to prepare educational staff to better respond to current and future challenges by giving them the knowledge and tools they need to lead, teach, and support students in a rapidly changing world.
At its core, the initiative addresses the growing need for schools and educational institutions to keep up with major societal and technological changes. Issues like climate change, economic inequality, and the digital transformation are shaping how we live and work. Education systems play a key role in preparing future generations to deal with these challenges. However, many educators and school leaders feel they lack the specific training to teach about sustainability or manage digital tools like AI effectively. By offering targeted training, this initiative helps bridge that gap.
The programme is designed for both professional educators—such as teachers and trainers—and for those in leadership or administrative roles within education. It offers training modules, workshops, and courses that cover sustainable development goals (SDGs), basic and advanced financial literacy, and a broad set of digital skills, including an introduction to artificial intelligence. While details may vary by region or institution, the training is typically delivered by certified providers or in cooperation with universities and public education institutes. Participants not only gain technical knowledge but also explore how to apply it in practical, classroom-based or institutional settings.
In the future, the programme is expected to expand, both in terms of content and scale. As digital tools and AI technologies evolve, so will the training materials, ensuring that educators stay up to date with the latest developments. There may also be efforts to extend the reach of the programme beyond formal education settings—such as into vocational training or adult education. Overall, the initiative lays the groundwork for a more resilient, future-ready education system by investing in the people who shape it.

items.title: Danish Data Portal
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
www.datavejviser.dk aims at enabling access to available data from the public sector and engaging in dialogue with users on their demand for further access to data so that future investments in quality and availability of public sector data is demand-driven.

Datavejviser.dk is a platform created to help people find and use data collected by public authorities in Denmark. The initiative recognizes that while a lot of data is available, it can be difficult for users to locate the right information or understand where to get it. By providing a clear, centralized directory of datasets, Datavejviser.dk makes it easier for businesses, researchers, government workers, and citizens to find the data they need and use it effectively.
The main goal of the platform is to improve transparency and support innovation by making public data more accessible. It does this by listing and describing data from many government agencies and linking users directly to the sources. This way, users don’t have to search through multiple websites or databases. Instead, they can use the platform as a one-stop resource to discover data on topics like the environment, economy, demographics, and more.
Datavejviser.dk works by collecting information about datasets available across the public sector and organizing them in a simple and consistent way. It uses standard formats to make sure the data is easy to find and compatible with different systems. The Danish Agency for Digital Government manages the platform, regularly updating it and responding to user feedback. This approach helps ensure that the platform stays relevant and continues to meet the needs of its users.
Looking to the future, the platform plans to expand its offerings and improve its features. It aims to include more datasets and improve user interaction by listening to what people want and need. By doing so, it hopes to encourage greater use of public data in areas such as research, business innovation, and public planning. Overall, Datavejviser.dk is a step toward making government data more open, useful, and aligned with the needs of society.

items.title: e-Farming, Food and Forestry Project under RRF
items.org: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Food
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Slovenia e-Farming, Food and Forestry Project is a digitalisation initiative under the Recovery and Resilience Plan (RRF). It aims to modernise agriculture, food, and forestry sectors through technology and digital solutions. The project includes the establishment of the National Food Institute to support research and innovation.

The Slovenia e-Farming, Food and Forestry Project is a comprehensive digitalisation programme consisting of eight sub-projects under the national Recovery and Resilience Plan (RRF). Its goal is to enhance efficiency, innovation, and sustainability in agriculture, food production, and forestry by introducing digital tools and practices.
Key objectives include:
Modernising agricultural, food, and forestry processes through digital solutionsPromoting research and innovation via the newly established National Food InstituteEnhancing sectoral efficiency and sustainability through technology adoptionThe project brings together public institutions, research organisations, and industry stakeholders to ensure that digitalisation efforts respond to real sectoral needs. By integrating multiple sub-projects under a single programme, it provides a coordinated approach to technology-driven transformation.
Future outlook:
Expansion of digital tools and smart farming solutions across SloveniaStrengthened research and development capabilities in food and forestry sectorsImproved collaboration between industry, academia, and public institutions for innovation and competitiveness

items.title: Using generative artificial intelligence for and in education
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Ministry of Education has published this public call for proposals with regard to the use of generative artificial intelligence for and in education, including content development for primary and secondary school, in line with the with the Recovery and Resilience Plan (RRP) within the development area of Smart, Sustainable and Inclusive Growth.

The growing presence of generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools — such as language and image generation software — is reshaping many areas of society, including education. These technologies offer new opportunities for creating learning content, personalising instruction, and assisting teachers. However, their integration into schools also brings challenges, including questions of digital safety, educational value, and the role of AI in shaping how students learn. Recognising both the potential and the risks, the Slovenian Ministry of Education has issued a public call for proposals on the use of generative AI in education, with a focus on primary and secondary schooling.
The main objective of this call is to support the development and testing of AI-driven educational content and tools that are aligned with Slovenia’s national curriculum. Applicants are encouraged to propose projects that use generative AI in practical, responsible, and innovative ways — for example, to support teachers in lesson planning, generate customised learning materials, or help students with different learning needs. The initiative is not just about experimenting with new technologies, but about making sure they serve the real needs of educators and students in the classroom.
This initiative is part of Slovenia’s Recovery and Resilience Plan (RRP), under the broader strategic focus on Smart, Sustainable and Inclusive Growth. The plan is supported by the European Union’s Recovery and Resilience Facility, aimed at helping member states recover from the impacts of the COVID-19 crisis while accelerating digital and green transitions. In this context, the Ministry’s call is both a response to immediate educational needs and a long-term investment in digital innovation. Public and private institutions, including schools, research organisations, and education technology developers, are eligible to submit proposals.
The projects selected through this call could influence how Slovenia’s education system evolves in the coming years. Pilot initiatives may be scaled up, used to develop national guidance, or feed into broader curriculum reform. As more schools begin to explore and test generative AI tools, this initiative will help build the evidence base needed to make informed decisions about their wider use. It reflects Slovenia’s proactive approach to shaping the role of AI in education — balancing innovation with responsibility, and experimentation with clear educational goals.

items.title: Training for children and young people to strengthen digital competences and to promote natural sciences and technical professions
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Ministry of Digital Transformation co-funds training for children and young people to strengthen digital competences and encourage and promote science and technology careers. The 2023-2024 project included AI content in part B: Advanced digital technologies. A further public call was launched in Q3 2024 with a special lot dedicated to AI.

n today’s digital world, young people need strong digital skills not only to navigate everyday life but also to succeed in future careers. Many students, however, still lack access to opportunities that help them develop these skills, particularly in advanced areas like artificial intelligence (AI). To address this gap, the Slovenian Ministry of Digital Transformation has been co-funding training programmes aimed at children and young people. These programmes are designed to strengthen digital competences and to spark interest in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) careers.
The core goal of the initiative is twofold: to ensure that students are confident users of digital technologies and to help them understand and explore more advanced topics that will shape the future — such as artificial intelligence. The Ministry supported these goals through a national training project running from 2023 to 2024, which included a dedicated section — Part B: Advanced Digital Technologies — that featured content related to AI. This ensured that participants were not only improving basic digital literacy, but also being introduced to the tools and concepts behind the intelligent systems that increasingly influence society, industry, and innovation.
The programme is delivered through a network of training providers and educational partners who offer hands-on workshops, classes, and interactive activities across Slovenia. It targets school-age children and teenagers, with special emphasis on those who may have fewer opportunities to access digital learning outside of school. In addition to teaching practical skills, the training aims to boost curiosity and confidence, encouraging young people to consider careers in digital and technical fields. The inclusion of AI content helps demystify the subject and makes it accessible, even for younger age groups.
Building on the results of the 2023–2024 project, the Ministry launched a new public call in the third quarter of 2024, this time with a special lot specifically focused on AI. This step reflects growing national interest in preparing the next generation for an AI-driven future. As the programme evolves, it may expand to reach more students, offer more specialised training, or integrate more closely with school curricula. The long-term aim is to make AI and digital education a regular and supported part of learning in Slovenia — not only to meet labour market needs but to empower young people to understand and shape the technologies of tomorrow.

items.title: The swedish Digitalisation Strategy 2025–2030
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
AI is part of the cross-cutting themes throughout the entire strategy and are integrated across all five strategic areas - digital skills, private sector, public administration, public welfare, and connectivity.

1. Digitalisation of the private sector - AI is highlighted as a key technology for strengthening companies’ capacity for innovation, competitiveness, security, and sustainability. The strategy emphasizes the importance of collaboration between the government, businesses, and organizations to promote the use of AI in the business sector.
2. Public administration - AI will be used to streamline digital services within the public sector. The aim is to create user-friendly, secure, and reliable services through AI- and data-driven development.
3. Public welfare - AI is expected to contribute to more preventive, person-centered, and location-independent services. The goal is to improve quality of life for citizens and the working environment for staff.

items.title: The Knowledge Hub for the Digitalization of Agriculture
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The National Knowledge Hub for Digitisation in Agriculture in Sweden helps the agricultural sector understand and use digital technologies. It collects, refines, and shares knowledge to support modern farming practices. The hub is led by Linköping University on behalf of the Swedish Board of Agriculture.

The National Knowledge Hub for Digitisation in Agriculture is a Swedish initiative designed to promote digital transformation in agriculture. Appointed by the Swedish Board of Agriculture, Linköping University leads the project, which aims to demonstrate the benefits and opportunities of digitisation for farmers and agri-businesses across the country.
Key objectives include:
Highlighting opportunities offered by digital technologies in agricultureRefining and packaging knowledge from research and practical applicationsDisseminating information to farmers, agribusinesses, and industry stakeholdersThe hub serves as a central resource for the agriculture sector, supporting informed decision-making and encouraging the adoption of digital tools. By connecting research, education, and industry, the initiative aims to strengthen Sweden’s competitiveness and innovation in the agri-food sector.
Future outlook:
Expansion of knowledge-sharing and best practices for digital agricultureIncreased awareness and adoption of smart farming technologiesStronger collaboration between universities, industry, and policymakers to support digital transformation

items.title: Testbed Digitalized Agriculture
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The RISE Test Bed for Digitised Agriculture allows companies and researchers to develop new technologies and data-driven innovations for agriculture. It focuses on making farming more sustainable, climate-smart, and profitable. The test bed supports collaboration and experimentation in real-world agricultural environments.

The RISE Test Bed for Digitised Agriculture is designed to accelerate the development and adoption of digital technologies in agriculture. It provides a real-world testing environment where companies and research institutions can create, trial, and refine:
New technologies for smart farmingApplications and system solutions for efficient agricultural managementData-driven innovations that enhance sustainability and productivityKey objectives of the test bed include:
Supporting climate-smart and sustainable agricultural practicesEnabling profitability improvements for farmers and agri-businessesFostering collaboration between research, industry, and technology developersBy providing access to infrastructure, expertise, and practical testing opportunities, the test bed helps ensure that innovations are ready for real-world deployment. In the future, it aims to expand the adoption of digital and data-driven solutions across Sweden’s agricultural sector, strengthening sustainability, efficiency, and competitiveness.

items.title: Technological and Territorial Network Project for forest monitoring and reduction of environmental disasters as levers for the development of the forest bioeconomy (RetechFOR)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The RetechFOR project is a regional consortium in Spain that applies AI to forest monitoring and disaster reduction. It aims to support the sustainable management and development of the forest bioeconomy. The initiative helps prevent environmental disasters while promoting the productive use of forest resources.

The Technological and Territorial Network Project for Forest Monitoring and Reduction of Environmental Disasters (RetechFOR) is designed to strengthen forest management and resilience using AI technologies. The project combines environmental monitoring, predictive analytics, and risk management to reduce the impact of wildfires and other forest-related disasters.
Key objectives include:
Monitoring forest health and environmental risks through AI-driven technologiesReducing the frequency and impact of environmental disasters, such as wildfiresPromoting sustainable forest management and bioeconomic development by integrating forestry preservation and exploitationThe initiative is implemented by a regional consortium of organisations, each focusing on different aspects of forest AI applications, including monitoring, conservation, and the development of forest-based economic activities. Collaboration ensures that technological solutions are tailored to local ecosystems and forest management practices.
Future outlook:
Expansion of AI-based monitoring tools across more forested areasIncreased integration of sustainable practices in forest bioeconomy initiativesStrengthened regional capacity for environmental disaster prevention

items.title: Strategic plan for the common agricultural policy for the 2023–2027 period
items.original_name: Strateški načrt skupne kmetijske politike za obdobje 2023–2027
items.org: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Food
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Strateški načrt skupne kmetijske politike za obdobje 2023–2027
items.body:
Slovenia’s Strategic Plan for the Common Agricultural Policy 2023–2027 supports the use of AI and digital technologies in agriculture. It funds modern machinery, IT solutions, and precision farming practices, especially in fruit and vegetable production. The initiative aims to increase efficiency, productivity, and innovation in the agricultural sector.

The Slovenian Strategic Plan for the Common Agricultural Policy (2023–2027) is designed to modernise agriculture through the adoption of digital technologies and advanced production methods. The strategy provides targeted support for farmers and agribusinesses to implement AI and machine learning solutions in their production and processing activities.
Key objectives of the initiative include:
Supporting investment in modern machinery and equipment with integrated IT solutionsPromoting precision agriculture techniques for better resource management and productivityEncouraging sectoral interventions in fruit and vegetable growing to enhance digitalisation and innovationIntegrating AI and machine learning into production and processing processes to optimise operationsThe plan also emphasises collaboration between farmers, technology providers, and research institutions to ensure that digital solutions are both practical and effective. By funding these modernisation efforts, Slovenia aims to increase the competitiveness and sustainability of its agricultural sector.
Future outlook:
Broader adoption of smart farming practices across the countryEnhanced digital skills and AI capabilities among farmers and agribusinessesStrengthened alignment between technology, innovation, and sectoral development priorities

items.title: Smart Specialization Technologies for Agro-ecology and Forestry (PNRR) in the context of the National Forest Strategy 2030
items.original_name: Tehnologii de specializare inteligentă pentru agroecologie și silvicultură (PNRR) în contextul Strategiei Naționale pentru Păduri 2030
items.org: Ministry of Research, Innovation and Digitalisation
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Tehnologii de specializare inteligentă pentru agroecologie și silvicultură (PNRR) în contextul Strategiei Naționale pentru Păduri 2030
items.body:
The National Forest Strategy 2030 in Romania supports the creation of innovation and technology centres in the smart specialisation area of agro-ecology and forestry. Its main investment is the development of an integrated IT system to monitor forest integrity, wood transport, and biodiversity. This system will also connect to SUMAL 2.0, Romania’s new wood traceability system.

The National Forest Strategy 2030 sets out to strengthen Romania’s capacity for sustainable forest management and environmental protection. It targets the smart specialisation subdomain of “Smart Specialisation Technologies for Agro-ecology and Forestry” by supporting the establishment of innovation and technology centres.
The flagship investment under this strategy is the creation of an integrated IT system to:
Support sustainable development and improve environmental qualityProtect nature and preserve biodiversitySupervise and control forest integrity and the transport of woodThis investment is implemented in two phases:
Installation and configuration of the IT system, including security solutions for confidentiality and training of personnelOperationalisation of a platform for investigations and alertsThe system will be integrated with SUMAL 2.0, the Romanian wood traceability system currently under development. It will monitor:
Compliance with legal obligations on wood harvestingTimely forest regenerationForest health and habitat conservation statusClimate change impacts and adaptation of different forest ecosystemsAll data centres for this system will comply with the European Code of Conduct on Data Centre Energy Efficiency, ensuring sustainability and high operational standards.
Future outlook:
Increased transparency and control of Romania’s forest resourcesEnhanced data-driven decision-making for forest conservationStronger alignment with EU environmental and climate objectives

items.title: Smart Data Sciences Market Consultation
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Smart Data Sciences Market Consultation, conducted by FPS Policy and Support from 2022 to 2023, aimed to create intelligent data services by maximizing the re-use of government data.

This initiative supported the five objectives of the Unleashing Government Data programme under the RRF, focusing on leveraging data, processes, and results to enhance efficiency and innovation across public services. Notably, the consultation was completed without a dedicated budget.

items.title: Smals
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Smals provides advanced IT and data centre solutions tailored to the needs of government, social, and healthcare organizations.

The initiative focuses on delivering secure infrastructure services that support digital transformation and enhance operational efficiency in the public sector.

items.title: Skills for entrepreneurs
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This initiative provides training for micro, small, medium, and large enterprises to help businesses acquire digital transformation competencies.

This programme covers skills in robotics, automation, AI, and high-level digital governance, enabling businesses to leverage digital technologies in their operations. A key focus of the programme is to enhance the digital skills of Latvian entrepreneurs to strengthen competitiveness and innovation, particularly in export-driven sectors.
RRF total budget: EUR 16.48 million (Phase 1: EUR 11.55 million; Phase 2: EUR 4.94 million)

items.title: Research on artificial intelligence systems and discrimination aspects
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This research study examines the risks of AI-related discrimination and the adequacy of Latvia’s legal and regulatory framework in addressing algorithmic bias.

The study analyses the impact of AI systems on various demographic groups, including gender, disability, race, ethnicity, social status, age, and sexual orientation. It also provides an overview of international best practices and offers recommendations for mitigating AI-driven biases in decision-making processes.

items.title: Requalification of Women in ICT Professions
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
As part of the National Strategic Plan for the Digital Decade, the Ministry of Digital Transformation has launched an initiative aimed at requalifying women over the age of 18 in the field of information and communication technologies (ICT).

The initiative offers both short-term (15 hours) and long-term (24 hours) training programmes for various ICT professions, including: 

• Cybersecurity Specialist
• Data Analyst
• IT Support Specialist
• IT Project Manager
• UX Designer
• AI Specialist

The primary goal of this initiative was to enhance digital literacy, encourage greater interest among women in ICT careers, and provide training that would enable participants to pursue careers in the ICT sector. The initiative achieved positive results, with over 500 women participating in the training programmes. Women over the age of 18 could apply without any additional requirements. Many of these participants reported an increased interest in digital technologies and pursuing careers in this field. A total of 23 training sessions were conducted as part of the initiative, including four specifically focused on AI. The AI Specialist training programme was completed by 89 participants. The AI Specialist curriculum training included several key topics in: the fundamentals of AI and its primary applications, future development opportunities, as well as the basics of machine learning, deep learning, and neural networks. For the longer training programmes, they had to include additional topics, e,g. understanding algorithms for data analysis.
In addition to these training programmes, the initiative also featured events specifically focused on ICT skills for women. These events aimed to showcase various ICT roles, career paths, and opportunities for education and certification. They also offered networking opportunities within the ICT community, job search support, and options for further training, mentorship, and ongoing support.
The initiative, in place since 2023, is financed through the national budget with EUR 2.95 million, with approx. EUR 22k focused on AI.

items.title: Reform of Higher Education for a Green and Resilient Transition to Society 5.0
items.org: Ministry of Education, Science and Sport
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This reform supports the digital transformation of education by improving digital skills and teaching practices in higher education. It includes pilot projects in AI, cybersecurity, and other advanced technologies, as well as training for educators. It also introduces micro-credentials to quickly meet changing skill needs.

Slovenia is actively working to modernize its higher education system by supporting the digital transformation of teaching and learning. The goal is to equip both students and educators with the skills needed to succeed in a world shaped by advanced technologies like artificial intelligence (AI), cybersecurity, and blockchain. This reform addresses the urgent need to update digital skills and teaching methods so that graduates are prepared for the demands of the modern labor market, especially in fast-growing tech sectors.
As part of a broader education reform, guidelines and an implementation plan were developed to enhance digital competencies through pilot projects and targeted training. The initiative focuses on advanced digital skills such as AI, blockchain, and cybersecurity, and aims to strengthen digital teaching abilities in higher education. A key element is the introduction of micro-credentials, enabling universities to respond flexibly to evolving labor market demands, particularly in emerging tech fields like AI, though funding for AI-specific actions is still being finalised. These micro-credentials provide a way for students and professionals to gain recognition for specific skills in a short time, helping to keep pace with rapid changes in technology and industry needs.
The reform includes pilot projects that test new approaches to teaching with digital tools and technologies in Slovenian universities. Educators receive focused training to better incorporate these advanced subjects into their courses. Collaboration among universities, government bodies, and industry stakeholders ensures that the curriculum remains relevant and aligned with the skills required in the workplace. By embedding these practices within higher education, Slovenia aims to create a learning environment that balances theoretical knowledge with practical application of digital technologies.
Looking to the future, this initiative is expected to grow as additional funding becomes available, especially for AI-related activities. The use of micro-credentials offers a flexible, scalable solution that allows universities to quickly adapt and introduce new programs aligned with the evolving needs of the digital economy. Through these efforts, Slovenia is building a foundation for ongoing improvement in digital education, helping students and educators stay ahead in a rapidly changing technological landscape.

items.title: Quantum Austria
items.org: Federal Ministry of Education, Science and Research (BMBWF) and funded by the European Union
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
On behalf of the Federal Ministry of Education, Science and Research (BMBWF) and funded by the European Union under the Development and Resilience Plan (2020-2026), the Austrian Research Promotion Agency (FFG) and the Austrian Science Fund (FWF) are implementing the Quan-tum Austria Funding Initiative. Part of the funding is provided for research infrastructure in the fields of next generation HPC, quantum computing as well as their interconnection.

One of the primary objectives is the development of the Multi-Site Computer Austria (MUSICA), envisioned to become Austria’s fastest HPC system (https://eurocc-austria.at/en/news/musica-austrias-next-supercomputer). The scientific issues of the projects in the field of quantum research and quantum technology may cover, for example, new algorithms and mathematical theoretical concepts that make use of the superposition and entanglement of quantum states, or developments and applications in quantum communication.

items.title: Pumice
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Ministry of Digital Transformation co-funds the project, the goal of which it is to develop educational content and examples of AI’s use in various subjects and activities in primary and secondary schools, with a focus on practical demonstrations of AI’s usefulness in teaching subject content, e.g. Slovenian language, history, chemistry, biology, art.

As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes more common in daily life, there is growing need for students—not just in technical fields—to understand how AI works and how it affects the world around them. Many students encounter AI only through media or social platforms, with limited opportunities to explore its educational value. To change this, the Slovenian Ministry of Digital Transformation is co-funding a project aimed at introducing AI into primary and secondary school classrooms—not as a separate subject, but as a tool to enhance learning in a wide range of subjects.
The main goal of the project is to create educational content and practical examples that show how AI can be used in the teaching of existing subjects. This includes disciplines such as Slovenian language, history, chemistry, biology, and art. Instead of treating AI as something only for computer science classes, the project focuses on how it can support learning across the curriculum. For example, AI tools might be used to help students explore historical data, analyse language patterns, or generate visual representations in art lessons. This approach helps students see AI as a useful and relevant part of their education, not just a complex or distant technology.
The project is being carried out in partnership with educators, content developers, and experts in both AI and pedagogy. These teams are working together to design and test new teaching materials that use AI in ways that are meaningful, age-appropriate, and aligned with national learning goals. Special emphasis is placed on practical demonstrations, making sure teachers and students can directly see how AI adds value to their lessons. The Ministry provides financial support and strategic guidance, helping to ensure that the content developed is both high quality and suitable for broader adoption.
In the future, the results of this project may lead to a wider rollout of AI-integrated teaching practices across Slovenian schools. If successful, the content and methods developed could be included in national guidelines, teacher training programmes, or even embedded in digital learning platforms. By starting with small-scale, subject-based integration, Slovenia is taking a measured and inclusive approach to preparing young learners for an AI-influenced world—where understanding and applying these technologies will be increasingly important across all areas of life and work.

items.title: Proloog Mobilidata 2
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Proloog Mobilidata 2 programme supports development of mobility technologies including remote driving. In spring 2024, it held a “Remote Driving Test Week” to evaluate safety, efficiency, and real-world feasibility. The initiative is designed to test advanced vehicle operation under actual conditions.

The Proloog Mobilidata 2 initiative aims to push forward cutting-edge mobility solutions, with a particular focus on remote driving technologies. It is built around testing in real-world environments to assess how safe, efficient, and practical remote vehicle operation can be.
One of its notable planned activities was a Remote Driving Test Week in spring 2024, during which remote-driven vehicles were trialled under realistic conditions. These trials are intended to provide evidence about performance, safety, system reliability, and potential deployment constraints.
By combining experimentation, testing, and evaluation, the programme seeks several outcomes:
Establishing best practices and safety standards for remote drivingUnderstanding technical, regulatory, and operational challengesInforming future scaling and wider implementation of remote vehicle technologiesGoing forward, Proloog Mobilidata 2 is likely to evolve by incorporating lessons from test weeks into broader trials, influencing regulation, and possibly enabling commercial use, once safety and feasibility are proven.

items.title: National IT Academy project on the creation of study materials for new and innovative subjects in the field of artificial intelligence
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
A project of the National IT Academy has focused on creating study materials for new and innovative subjects in the field of artificial intelligence at higher education institutions. These subjects included topics such as introduction to neural networks, neural networks, artificial intelligence, and programming languages for artificial intelligence.

Slovakia is actively working to improve education in artificial intelligence (AI) at its universities to better prepare students for a future where digital technologies are increasingly important. Many higher education institutions currently lack up-to-date resources and courses focused specifically on AI, which limits students’ ability to develop the relevant skills needed in this fast-growing field. This gap presents both a challenge and an opportunity. By providing  new courses, Slovakia can help students become qualified AI professionals who contribute to the country’s economic and technological growth.
 Subjects include such as the basics of artificial intelligence, an introduction to neural networks, more advanced topics on neural networks, and programming languages used for AI development. The goal is to offer students a strong foundation in both AI theory and practical skills. These courses are designed to be accessible for students from various technical backgrounds, helping to build a wider pool of specialists who understand AI technologies and how to apply them in real situations.
In collaboration with the Digital Coalition, the Government of Slovakia supported the implementation of the national “IT Academy − Education for the 21st Century” project to educate the top ICT specialists, prepare the pilot projects for digital transformation of the education system and schools to identify and enhance the digital economy competencies, digitally transform the vocational education and training at all its levels of education, including the higher vocational education and post-secondary specialized education, with the option to offer a free choice of educational path by choosing the bachelor’s higher education degree, or by recognising tertiary education completed with the possibility of a smooth transition to higher university study of the second degree.
This initiative brings together universities, government bodies, and industry experts to ensure the new study materials are accurate and relevant to the needs of employers and society. Universities pilot these new subjects and give feedback to improve the materials. Teachers receive support to help them introduce these courses effectively. Cooperation among different partners helps make sure the reforms are well coordinated and meet the standards expected in modern digital education. 
Looking ahead, the project aims to grow and adapt as AI technology evolves. This could include creating more advanced courses or introducing new topics like AI ethics, industry-specific applications, or ongoing training for current professionals. The broader educational reform linked to the “IT Academy − Education for the 21st Century” project supports this growth by promoting digital transformation across all levels of education. Slovakia hopes to build a workforce ready to meet future challenges and opportunities in AI and the digital economy.

items.title: National Funding Call “Mobility Transition 2024/1 – Mobility Technologies and Components”
items.org: Ministry of Climate Action, Environment, Energy, Mobility, Innovation, and Technology
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The AI for Mobility Technologies funding initiative supports the development of AI-driven solutions for sustainable mobility. It focuses on projects that help avoid, shift, and reduce environmental impact in transport. The programme encourages innovation that contributes to the mobility transition in line with national climate and environmental goals.

The AI for Mobility Technologies initiative, launched by the Federal Ministry of Climate Action, Environment, Energy, Mobility, Innovation, and Technology, aims to promote AI applications that support the sustainable transformation of transport systems.
Key objectives include:
Supporting the development of AI-driven mobility technologies that reduce environmental impactEncouraging projects that align with the mobility transition goals: avoid unnecessary travel, shift to sustainable modes, and reduce emissionsStimulating innovation in mobility solutions through targeted fundingThe funding call is designed to foster collaboration between research institutions, companies, and technology developers, ensuring that AI solutions are practical and contribute to real-world mobility challenges. By focusing on environmental sustainability, the programme helps align technological development with national climate and mobility policies.
Future outlook:
Expansion of AI applications in transport planning and operationsDevelopment of smarter, greener mobility solutionsContribution to long-term mobility transition and climate action objectives

items.title: National Data Strategy
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
Austria has published its first national data strategy in October 2024 (Federal Chancellery of Austria, 2024).

The strategy comprises 45 measures, encompassing areas such as sustainable infrastructure sharing and innovative data culture/data literacy. The strategy was developed with a broad stakeholder involvement. It is designed to be aligned with the European vision to enable a single market for data and to strengthen the data economy.

items.title: NAVAJO
items.org: Digital Wallonia (Agence du Numérique – Walloon Digital Agency)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The NAVAJO pilot project introduces an autonomous shuttle service in Ottignies-Louvain-la-Neuve, Belgium. It tests and validates autonomous transport technologies for use in urban mobility systems. The project is financed through Digital Wallonia’s “Intelligent Territories” call for projects to support smart mobility solutions.

NAVAJO is a pilot project designed to enhance smart mobility by deploying an autonomous shuttle service in Ottignies-Louvain-la-Neuve. Its main purpose is to test and validate autonomous transport technologies and assess how they can be integrated into existing urban mobility frameworks.
The initiative supports:
Evaluation of safety, reliability, and efficiency of autonomous shuttles in real-life conditionsDevelopment of guidelines and best practices for incorporating autonomous vehicles into public transport networksDemonstration of smart mobility solutions for medium-sized citiesFunded under Digital Wallonia’s “Intelligent Territories (Territoires Intelligents)” call for projects, NAVAJO helps the Walloon Region explore how innovative technologies can improve connectivity, sustainability, and public transport options.
Looking ahead, the project may inform the wider rollout of autonomous shuttles and other intelligent transport systems across the region. Insights gained from NAVAJO will support urban planners, policymakers, and transport operators in designing future mobility solutions.

items.title: Mistra Digital Forest
items.org: Swedish Foundation for Strategic Environmental Research
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Mistra Digital Forest is a research programme that uses digital technologies to support sustainable forestry. It develops digital tools and automation techniques to make use of large amounts of forestry data. The initiative aims to improve decision-making and sustainability in the forestry sector.

Mistra Digital Forest is a Swedish research programme focused on harnessing digitalisation for sustainable forestry. The programme develops practical tools and automation techniques that allow the forestry sector to better utilise large-scale data and improve operational efficiency while supporting environmental sustainability.
Key objectives of the programme include:
Developing digital tools and automation solutions tailored for forestry operationsSupporting sustainable forest management through improved data-driven decision-makingPromoting collaboration between researchers and the forestry industry to ensure relevance and usability of solutionsThe programme is implemented through close cooperation between academic institutions and industry partners, enabling innovation that addresses both environmental and operational challenges. By combining research expertise and industry knowledge, the initiative helps accelerate adoption of digital solutions across the sector.
Future outlook:
Broader implementation of AI and digital tools in forestry managementEnhanced sustainability and efficiency in forest operationsContinued integration of research findings into industry practices to strengthen Sweden’s leadership in sustainable forestry

items.title: Latvian Employers for Green and Digital Transition
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This initiative, implemented by the Employers' Confederation of Latvia (LDDK) in collaboration with BusinessEurope, supports businesses in adapting to digitalisation and the green transition.

The project strengthens industry awareness of digital and sustainability-related policies and aligns Latvia’s labour market with EU-level initiatives such as the European Green Deal. The programme also aims to improve employer capacity in implementing digital and green policies.

items.title: Improving access to data (strategy for digitalisation)
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
One of the key areas covered by the national strategy for digitalisation, "A strong, ethical, and responsible digital foundation", includes the objective of improving access to data.

Denmark’s national strategy for digitalisation is built on the understanding that the country’s future depends on a secure, inclusive, and innovative digital environment. One of the key areas within this strategy is titled “A strong, ethical, and responsible digital foundation,” which includes an important objective: improving access to data. This focus recognizes that data is essential for innovation, effective public services, and economic growth, but it must be handled carefully to respect privacy and ethical standards. By enhancing data accessibility while maintaining trust and security, Denmark aims to create a solid basis for digital transformation across all sectors.
The strategy calls for broad collaboration between public, private and civil society actors. The strategy contains nine visions for the next steps in Denmark’s digital development.
Vision 1: Strengthened cyber and information security
Vision 2: Coherent service for people and businesses
Vision 3: More time for welfare through increased use of new technology
Vision 4: Increased growth and digital SMEs
Vision 5: The digital healthcare of the future
Vision 6: Acceleration of the green transition through digital solutions
Vision 7: A strong, ethical, and responsible digital foundation
Vision 8: Denmark at the centre of international digitalisation
Vision 9: A population ready for a digital future
This initiative addresses the challenge of balancing the vast potential of digital technologies with the need for responsible governance. Data access can drive innovation in fields like healthcare, environmental sustainability, and business growth, but it requires systems that protect individuals’ rights and prevent misuse. The main objectives include not only opening up data to fuel research and development but also ensuring that such access is managed under strict ethical guidelines. The initiative supports investments in infrastructure, legal frameworks, and education to make data use more transparent, secure, and efficient.
The strategy operates through cooperation among government agencies, private companies, academia, and civil society organizations. These stakeholders work together to develop standards, pilot projects, and new services that embody the strategy’s visions. For example, enhancing cybersecurity (Vision 1) supports safe data sharing, while promoting digital SMEs (Vision 4) encourages innovation using data-driven tools. As the digital landscape evolves, Denmark plans to expand these efforts, scaling successful projects and continuously updating regulations to meet new challenges. The ultimate goal is to build a digital society where data empowers citizens and businesses while respecting privacy and ethical values.

items.title: Imec’s Participation in PREVAIL
items.org: Digital Europe Programme and the Flemish Government
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Imec’s involvement in the PREVAIL project facilitates the development of AI hardware through a multi-hub European network.

This initiative supports edge AI research and innovation by providing prototyping and testing capabilities for advanced chip designs. PREVAIL is co-funded by the Digital Europe Programme and the Flemish Government.

items.title: INNOAIR
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The INNOAIR Project in Sofia, Bulgaria, uses AI and sustainable transport solutions to improve urban mobility and cut air pollution. Supported by the Urban Innovative Actions programme, it optimises public transport routes based on real-time demand. Key innovations include an on-demand electric minibus service connecting underserved areas to Sofia’s metro system.

The INNOAIR Project is an innovative urban mobility initiative led by the Municipality of Sofia. It aims to reduce air pollution and traffic congestion by introducing AI-enabled, sustainable transport services. The project is supported by the Urban Innovative Actions programme under the European Regional Development Fund, which funds experimental solutions to urban challenges.
Core elements of the project include:
Optimising public transport routes based on real-time passenger demand using AI algorithmsLaunching an on-demand electric minibus service with flexible routes tailored to user needsConnecting underserved peri-urban areas to Sofia’s metro system, improving accessibility and reducing car dependencyIntegrating booking and payment via the BUSINN app, which links seamlessly with Sofia’s public transport systemThese measures not only improve the efficiency of public transport but also contribute to cleaner air, lower carbon emissions, and a more inclusive transport network.
Future outlook:
Expansion of on-demand AI-powered services to other areas of SofiaIntegration of additional sustainable mobility solutions such as shared electric vehicles and micro-mobility optionsProviding a model for other European cities looking to adopt similar AI-driven approaches to public transport and environmental improvement

items.title: HPC “Lucia”
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
"Lucia" is a state-of-the-art supercomputing facility in Wallonia designed to meet the region's research and innovation needs. It includes advanced GPU nodes for AI applications and supports academic research and business projects in areas such as energy, health, and advanced manufacturing.

The system, which is partially funded by Walloon regional authorities, includes advanced GPU nodes for AI applications and supports academic research and business projects in areas such as energy, health, and advanced manufacturing.

items.title: HPC “CÉCI”
items.org: Joint initiative between the EU, European countries and private partners
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
“CÉCI” is a Tier-2 supercomputing initiative integrating multiple smaller clusters to support advanced computational research.

It provides HPC resources to researchers across Belgium in diverse fields such as physics, biology, and materials science, enabling significant scientific advancements.

items.title: Green.Dat.AI
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
GREEN.DAT.AI is a Horizon Europe project that develops energy-efficient, large-scale data analytics services for use in industrial AI systems. It aims to reduce the environmental impact of data management while demonstrating new analytics services in sectors such as energy, agriculture, mobility, and banking. In Slovenia, the Innovation Technology Cluster (ITC) coordinates pilots on smart farming and smart water management.

GREEN.DAT.AI is a Horizon Europe research and innovation project focused on creating energy-efficient, large-scale data analytics services that can be directly integrated into AI-based industrial systems. By reducing the environmental footprint of data management, the project combines technological advancement with sustainability.
The project demonstrates its new analytics services across four industries — Smart Energy, Smart Agriculture/Agri-food, Smart Mobility, and Smart Banking — and six different application scenarios (pilots) to showcase their efficiency and scalability. This approach leverages European Data Spaces to ensure secure, interoperable, and cross-sectoral data usage.
In Slovenia, the Innovation Technology Cluster (ITC), a national business support organisation, is responsible for coordinating and implementing two pilots:
Smart farming optimisation through digital twinsSmart water managementFuture outlook:
Broader roll-out of green data analytics solutions across European industriesIncreased energy efficiency and lower environmental impact of AI-based data systemsStrengthened cross-border collaboration and use of European Data Spaces for sustainable digital transformation

items.title: Flemish Task Force on Automated Driving
items.org: Department of Economy, Science and Innovation
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
A task force initiated by the Flemish Departments of Economy, Science, and Innovation (EWI) and Mobility connects research, innovation, and mobility stakeholders. It aims to build an ecosystem for shared automated road mobility and speed up the development of autonomous driving technologies in Flanders.

The task force was created as a collaboration platform by the Flemish Departments of Economy, Science, and Innovation (EWI) and Mobility. It brings together research institutions, innovation actors, mobility stakeholders, and logistics operators to strengthen cooperation on automated and connected transport systems in Flanders.
Its main goals are to:
