Foster an ecosystem for shared automated road mobilityAccelerate development and deployment of autonomous driving technologiesConnect key actors across research, policy, and industry to stimulate innovationAlthough not yet a formal project, the task force has been proposed for funding under a cross-border Interreg initiative, which is currently under evaluation. If funded, it could become a major driver for cross-border testing, policy alignment, and large-scale deployment of autonomous and shared mobility solutions in the region.
Looking ahead, the task force is expected to expand partnerships, develop pilot projects, and strengthen the regulatory and innovation environment for autonomous mobility in Flanders and neighbouring regions.

items.title: Flemish Data Strategy
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Flemish Data Strategy aims to transform governance by fostering collaboration between local and regional authorities to enable data-driven decision-making.

The Strategy promotes Open Data availability, standardisation, and interoperability to stimulate economic growth and innovation. Work is underway on an updated version of the strategy, focusing on advanced data management models and high-performance data systems.

items.title: Federal Data Strategy
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Federal Data Strategy, coordinated by FPS Economy, focuses on creating a robust data ecosystem across sectors such as mobility, energy, manufacturing, and health.

The strategy will include recommendations to foster data literacy among citizens, develop necessary skills for a data-driven economy, and establish ethical guidelines for data governance.

items.title: EuroCC Belgium
items.org: Belgian National Competence Centre for High‑Performance Computing
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
EuroCC Belgium serves as the National Competence Centre for HPC, high-performance data analytics (HPDA), and AI.

EuroCC Belgium aims to enhance the adoption of HPC technologies in industry and academia by providing technical support, training programmes, and access to infrastructure. The centre also promotes industrial innovation through strategic collaborations (EuroCC Belgium, 2024).

items.title: Digital Transformation of Education EdTech
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This initiative promotes the use of state-of-the-art educational technologies in the education sector by training teachers and supporting digital content and solutions for teaching methods, through an educational technology testing platform (testbed).

The “EdTech Center” of the National Agency for Education has been established for the coordination of digital transformation in all educational institutions. [EUR 30 million (via RRF)].

items.title: Digital Competences and Basic Knowledge of Computer and Information Science
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Ministry of Education has run two public tenders to carry out experimental projects for the development and verification of digital competences and basic knowledge of computer and information science in innovative departments or groups at educational institutions.

As digital technologies become more central to education, there is growing recognition of the need to improve students’ digital skills from an early age. Many school systems face challenges in adapting their teaching methods and curricula to support this shift. In Slovenia, the Ministry of Education has taken steps to address this issue by launching targeted public tenders to support innovative projects in schools. The aim is to build and test new ways of teaching digital skills — especially digital literacy and foundational knowledge in computer and information science — in real classroom settings.
The Ministry has run two public tenders to fund experimental projects in selected schools or groups within schools. These projects are designed to explore new methods for developing digital competences and computer science knowledge, particularly in departments or learning groups that take an innovative approach to teaching. The goal is not only to improve students’ technical understanding but also to strengthen problem-solving, logical thinking, and digital creativity. This approach supports a more hands-on and engaging learning experience that reflects how digital technologies are used in everyday life and in the workplace.
The selected projects are carried out in cooperation with educational institutions, teachers, and subject experts. Each participating school or department proposes its own concept for how digital competences will be taught and tested, often using new tools, interdisciplinary methods, or flexible teaching formats. The Ministry supports these efforts by funding their implementation and evaluation. Over time, the results of these experimental efforts help the Ministry identify effective practices and consider how they might be scaled across the education system.
Looking forward, these projects may influence broader curriculum reforms or lead to the development of new national standards for digital competence education. By testing ideas on a smaller scale first, the Ministry can better understand what works in different educational contexts. This initiative reflects Slovenia’s wider goal of preparing students for a digital future — not just by giving them access to technology, but by teaching them how to use it meaningfully and confidently in all areas of life.

items.title: DiTEdu
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The goal of the national project “Support for the Digital Transformation of Education” (DiTEdu) is to create innovative teaching methodologies for preschools, primary schools, and secondary schools that will reflect the latest trends in digitalisation.

The goal of the national project “Support for the Digital Transformation of Education” (DiTEdu) is to create innovative teaching methodologies for preschools, primary schools, and secondary schools that will reflect the latest trends in digitalisation. It builds upon the project of the National IT Academy along with partners, the Pavol Jozef Šafárik University in Košice (UPJŠ) and Comenius University in Bratislava (UK), Ministry of Education, Science, Research and Sport of the Slovak Republic (MŠVVaM SR), to create study materials for new and innovative subjects in the field of artificial intelligence, including topics such as Introduction to Neural Networks, Neural Networks, Artificial Intelligence, and Programming Languages for Artificial Intelligence. 

The activity “Support for the Digital Transformation of Education” will be implemented, divided into nine sub-activities with nationwide impact. These will involve formal and informal education of school digital coordinators, principals, teaching and professional staff of kindergartens, primary and secondary schools, students of teaching programmes at universities, updating and creating innovative methodologies, networking schools and staff, certifying the quality of digital schools, and popularization. Educational research aims to improve the quality of the provided support, ensure the safety of digital transformation considering its risks, and communicate the acquired knowledge with the international community. The activity is divided into 9 sub-activities:

1. Education and continuous methodological support for school digital coordinators.
2. Adaptation of the EU DigCompEdu framework into undergraduate education and professional development of teaching and professional staff of kindergartens, primary and secondary schools.
3. Creation and use of methodological materials to support the digital transformation of education.
4. Establishing a community of cooperation with other organisations and departments of the Ministry of Education, the academic community, primary and secondary schools, public administration and self-government bodies, other entities, and the public in the field of utilising and exchanging experiences of practitioners in the field of digital transformation of education.
5. Creation of analyses, expert opinions, standards, recommendations, criteria, and mechanisms for implementing measures in the field of digital transformation of education.
6. Implementation and support of educational research in the field of digital transformation of education.
7. Preparation, implementation, and certification of the quality of educational content, teaching methods, and schools of digital excellence.
8. Experimental verification of a new study programme “Gymnasium” with a focus on informatics.
9. Popularisation activities and support for public awareness of the needs of digital transformation of education.

items.title: Data Intelligence Offensive
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Data Intelligence Offensive (DIO) aims to advance and promote business models for data exchange and monetisation, adhering to the highest ethical and legal standards.

As part of this initiative, data spaces are being developed across various sectors including tourism, health and agriculture. Moreover, the DIO supports the regional data space datahub.tirol.

items.title: Cross-cutting platform of artificial intelligence applied to the agri-food sector
items.original_name: Plataforma Agroalimentaria en RED, Proyecto PAN
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Plataforma Agroalimentaria en RED, Proyecto PAN
items.body:
The Proyecto PAN in Spain is a platform that applies artificial intelligence (AI) to the agri-food sector. It supports the adoption of disruptive technologies to improve productivity and innovation. The initiative encourages collaboration across regions and stakeholders in the sector.

The Cross-cutting platform of AI applied to the agri-food sector (Proyecto PAN) is a regional consortium initiative launched in 2023. It aims to create a transversal AI platform that integrates various stakeholders, technologies, and services to enhance the agri-food value chain. By leveraging disruptive technologies, the platform seeks to improve efficiency, sustainability, and competitiveness in agriculture and food production.
Key objectives include:
Promoting the use of AI and advanced technologies across the agri-food sectorFostering collaboration between companies, research centres, and public institutionsEnhancing innovation and competitiveness in regional and national agri-food industriesThe platform operates as a shared ecosystem, allowing stakeholders to exchange data, tools, and best practices. It also facilitates research, pilot projects, and knowledge transfer, ensuring that AI solutions can be applied effectively in real-world agricultural and food production settings.
Future outlook:
Scaling AI adoption across multiple agri-food sub-sectorsExpanding regional and national collaboration networksDriving digital transformation and sustainable innovation in the sector

items.title: Component 7, Reform 1 of the curriculum reform of the Slovak education system
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Slovak education system is preparing to improve skills related to AI, primarily through curriculum reform and textbook reform for primary and secondary education as well as vocational training. These topics are included in the areas of computer literacy, digital society, media literacy skills, and exploration of traditional and modern technical environments.

Slovakia is taking steps to better prepare its students for a future where artificial intelligence (AI) plays an increasingly important role in everyday life and the job market. The current education system has not yet fully adapted to the rapid changes brought about by digital technologies, including AI. Many young people lack the skills needed to understand or work with these tools. To address this, Slovakia is focusing on making changes in how digital and technical topics are taught in primary schools, secondary schools, and vocational training programmes. This effort is part of a broader plan to ensure students have the foundational knowledge needed to navigate a society shaped by digital technologies.
The main goal of this initiative is to improve digital and technical education, with a special focus on AI. Rather than introducing AI as a completely separate subject, the plan is to include it within broader areas like computer literacy, digital citizenship, and media literacy. This way, students will learn not only how AI works in a basic sense, but also how it affects the way we live, communicate, and make decisions. The reforms also aim to help students understand both the opportunities and the risks that come with using digital tools and AI systems.
To make this happen, Slovakia is updating its national curriculum and revising textbooks to reflect modern technological developments. These changes will apply to different levels of the school system, including primary education (for younger children), secondary education (typically ages 12–18), and vocational schools that prepare students for specific careers. Teachers will be supported through training and new teaching materials, ensuring they can confidently deliver this updated content. The government is working together with education experts, curriculum developers, and possibly EU partners to align these reforms with European standards for digital and AI education.
Looking ahead, the changes are expected to be rolled out gradually over the coming years. The long-term aim is to create a more modern education system that prepares young people not just to use technology, but to think critically about it and contribute to its development. As the reform progresses, there may also be efforts to share resources and teaching models with other countries, or to expand the programme into lifelong learning initiatives for adults. This approach reflects a recognition that AI is not just a technical topic for specialists, but a societal issue that everyone needs to understand to some degree.

items.title: Cloud Strategy for the Flemish Administration
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Cloud Strategy for the Flemish Administration provides a phased roadmap to modernise public ICT infrastructure by adopting a “public cloud first” approach.

It aims to improve the efficiency, scalability, and security of administrative services while aligning with the broader Flemish Digital Strategy. The strategy incorporates clear principles for cloud computing investments and operational changes (Digitaal Vlaanderen, 2019)

items.title: CitCom.ai TEF
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
CitCom.ai is an EU test and experimentation facility that provides both physical and virtual environments where AI and robotics solutions can be validated under real smart-city conditions. It helps innovators with services like algorithm validation, ethics and compliance guidance, and impact assessment. The goal is to support the creation and deployment of AI solutions that are safe, effective, and aligned with regulations.

CitCom.ai (Smart Cities & Communities TEF) is designed to support the development and deployment of AI/robotics solutions in urban environments by offering real-world testing and experimentation. It addresses the challenge that many AI innovations are developed in laboratory settings but struggle to meet technical, societal, regulatory, or environmental requirements in actual city settings. By bridging that gap, it helps ensure that AI systems work reliably among people, infrastructure, mobility systems, and public spaces. 
Its objectives include:
Validating new AI algorithms and robotics hardware/software.Providing guidance on ethics, compliance, regulations (including upcoming EU AI-related laws) to ensure innovations are lawful and socially acceptable.Assessing risks and opportunities of AI in urban and communal settings (mobility, connectivity, power systems, public spaces) to inform both innovators and policy makers.Facilitating ecosystem engagement—connecting innovators, public authorities, R&D institutions, and citizens—to foster collaborative development and responsible adoption.In its implementation, CitCom.ai operates through a consortium spanning 11 EU countries and several partner nodes (“super-nodes”) grouped by thematic focus (Power, Move, Connect) that cover various spatial and sectoral sub-nodes. It offers services such as testbeds, living labs, digital twins, virtual and physical validation environments, and guidance on complying with relevant regulatory frameworks.

items.title: BrAIn - BRinging Artificial INtelligence towards SMEs
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The BrAIn – Bringing Artificial Intelligence towards SMEs project is part of the Interreg DANUBE transnational programme. It aims to boost the competitiveness of SMEs in the Danube Region by transferring AI knowledge and technologies to sectors such as manufacturing, agri-food, and healthcare. In Slovenia, the ITC – Innovation Technology Cluster manages activities related to the agri-food area.

The BrAIn (Bringing Artificial Intelligence towards SMEs) initiative is an international project under the Interreg DANUBE transnational programme. Its primary purpose is to increase the competitiveness of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in the Danube Region by promoting the adoption and transfer of AI solutions across key sectors.
Key objectives include:
Facilitating knowledge and technology transfer of AI-based solutionsStrengthening SMEs’ innovation capacity in manufacturing, agri-food, and healthcareBuilding cross-border networks to share expertise and best practicesThe programme involves partners from multiple countries in the Danube Region. In Slovenia, the ITC – Innovation Technology Cluster is responsible for managing the agri-food component, coordinating projects and activities that help agri-food SMEs adopt AI-driven tools and practices.
Future outlook:
Increased cross-sector and cross-country collaboration for AI adoptionBroader uptake of AI technologies by SMEs in the regionEnhanced competitiveness and sustainability of manufacturing, agri-food, and healthcare SMEs

items.title: Belgium’s Participation in EuroHPC Joint Undertaking
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Belgium is participating in the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking, which aims to develop world-class HPC infrastructure across Europe.

Through this initiative, Belgium contributes to the development of supercomputers and advances in quantum compu-ting. The EuroHPC Summit 2024, hosted in Antwerp, demonstrated Belgium's commitment to fostering international collaboration in HPC innovation (EuroHPC, 2024)

items.title: Baltic first AI Hackathon
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This hackathon brought together students from various fields to work on generative AI solutions aimed at addressing challenges in education, social inclusion, sustainability, and public services.

Participants collaborated with institutions such as Riga Stradiņš University, the University of Tartu, the Latvian State Radio and Television Center, and the Central Finance and Contracting Agency. The event provided an opportunity to foster innovation and encourage interdisciplinary cooperation in AI.

items.title: Austrian Scientific Computing (previously Vienna Scientific Cluster)
items.org: The ASC Research Center, together with Campus IT of TU Wien
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body: The Vienna Scientific Cluster (VSC) is a collaboration of several Austrian universities that provides supercomputer resources and technical support to their users. The current flagship systems of the VSC family are VSC-4 and VSC-5, currently the fastest supercomputers in Austria. Both systems are powering science and research at the leading academic institutions in Austria and fulfil the demand for high computing power in the areas such as physics, chemistry, meteorology and life sciences.

items.title: Athumi
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The three agencies Austria Wirtschaftsservice GmbH (aws), the Aus-trian Research Promotion Agency (FFG) and the Austrian Science Fund (FWF) offer funding for basic research, applied research and its entrepreneurial implementation under the title ‘AI Mission Austria’ (AIM AT).

The funding initiative was implemented for 2022 and 2023 with funds from the Fonds Zukunft Österreich (FZÖ).

items.title: Area Monitoring System (AMS)
items.org: Agency for Agricultural Markets and Rural Development
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Area Monitoring System (AMS) uses satellite images and machine learning algorithms to track and assess agricultural land in Slovenia. Managed by the Agency for Agricultural Markets and Rural Development, it provides up-to-date information on land use and conditions. In 2024, the Ministry of Agriculture launched a project group to explore further digitisation and AI applications in agriculture.

The Area Monitoring System (AMS), deployed by the Agency for Agricultural Markets and Rural Development in Slovenia, is a software-supported platform that uses processed satellite images from Sentinel and commercial providers to monitor agricultural areas. By applying machine learning algorithms, the system determines the status and changes of agricultural surfaces over specific periods, improving the accuracy and efficiency of monitoring.
In early 2024, the Ministry of Agriculture established a special project group to explore the introduction and development of digitisation and AI in agriculture. This group examines both administrative and technological aspects, with the aim of integrating digital and AI solutions into existing systems and processes.
Key aims include:
Evaluating the potential for expanding AMS applications into agricultural productionExploring integration with commercial digital and AI solutionsImproving data-driven decision-making in agriculture and rural developmentLooking forward, the initiative seeks to broaden AMS’s scope beyond administrative monitoring to include practical tools for farmers and agricultural producers, enabling smarter, more sustainable farming practices. By combining public systems with commercial AI innovations, Slovenia aims to create a more digitally advanced agricultural sector.

items.title: Agrifood TEF
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
The Agrifood TEF initiative in Spain promotes innovation in AI and robotics for the agri-food sector. It supports the development and adoption of smart technologies to improve efficiency and productivity. The programme fosters collaboration between research centres, companies, and technology providers.

he Agrifood TEF initiative aims to strengthen AI and robotics applications in the Spanish agri-food industry. By supporting research, development, and experimentation, it seeks to modernise agricultural practices, enhance production efficiency, and improve competitiveness across the sector.
Key objectives include:
Developing AI-driven automation and robotic solutions for agriculture and food processingFacilitating adoption of smart technologies by farms and agri-food companiesPromoting collaboration between research institutions, technology providers, and businessesImplementation focuses on funding projects, pilot tests, and applied research, allowing innovations to move from the lab into practical, real-world use. The programme also aligns with broader European initiatives to digitalise agriculture and increase sustainability in food systems.

items.title: Agriculture and Rural Development - ADER 2026
items.org: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Sectoral Plan for Research and Development in Agriculture and Rural Development 2023–2026 (ADER 2026) funds projects to build a smart, resilient, and diversified agricultural sector. It supports research on climate change adaptation, natural resource management, biodiversity conservation, innovative technologies, and digitalisation in agriculture and forestry.

Introduced in 2023, the Sectoral Plan for Research and Development in the Field of Agriculture and Rural Development 2023–2026 (“ADER 2026”) aims to identify and support innovative solutions to make the agricultural sector smarter, more resilient, and more diverse. It directs funding to projects that help agriculture and forestry meet new challenges, from climate change to sustainability.
Key areas of focus include:
Adaptation to climate change in agricultural and forestry sectorsEfficient management of natural resources and production inputsConservation of biodiversity and adoption of environmentally friendly practicesImplementation of innovative technologies and processes to reduce greenhouse gas emissionsProduction of healthy agri-food products and promotion of the circular economyDigitalisation of agricultural and forestry activitiesThe plan encourages collaboration between research institutions, agricultural organisations, and technology providers, ensuring that innovative solutions are effectively transferred to practice. By funding projects in these priority areas, ADER 2026 helps strengthen the sustainability and competitiveness of rural areas.
Future outlook:
Continued support for innovative, environmentally friendly practicesGreater emphasis on digitalisation and climate-smart technologiesA stronger, evidence-based approach to sustainable agriculture and forestry

items.title: AgrarIA: AI applied to the value chain ​​of agricultural production 2050
items.original_name: AgrarIA: IA aplicada a la cadena de valor de la producción agrícola 2050
items.org: Ministry for Digital Transformation and Public Service
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: AgrarIA: IA aplicada a la cadena de valor de la producción agrícola 2050
items.body:
This project explores the use of AI and other technologies to develop new agricultural production methods. It investigates solutions such as natural pest control, collaborative robotics, quantum computing, and digital twins. The goal is to make agricultural production more efficient, sustainable, and innovative.

The project is focused on assessing the applicability and viability of AI alongside other advanced technologies in agriculture. It seeks to create innovative solutions that improve productivity, sustainability, and efficiency across different stages of agricultural production.
Key potential initiatives include:
Development of new natural products for pest and disease control, offering alternatives to chemical synthesis while maintaining effectivenessUse of collaborative robotics to optimise product transformation and processing phasesApplication of quantum computing for managing and analysing satellite imagery to optimise agricultural productionImplementation of digital twins to enhance energy efficiency in refrigeration and storage facilitiesThe project encourages collaboration between research institutions, technology providers, and agricultural stakeholders to ensure practical, scalable solutions. By integrating cutting-edge technologies, it aims to modernise agriculture while promoting sustainability and competitiveness.
Future outlook:
Adoption of AI-driven and technology-enhanced production methods across farmsIncreased efficiency, sustainability, and resilience in agricultural operationsDevelopment of new methodologies that can be scaled and applied to various crops and production systems

items.title: AI-specific programmes
items.org: Slovak University of Technology in Bratislava (STU), Technical University of Košice (TUKE), Comenius University in Bratislava (Comenius University), University of Economics in Bratislava (EU), University of Žilina (UNIZA), University of Martin,
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Twenty-two degree programmes in artificial intelligence are now offered at six Slovak universities. These programmes benefit students interested in studying AI and related fields. The initiative addresses growing demand for AI skills in education and the tech job market.

Slovakia is responding to the growing global demand for artificial intelligence (AI) expertise by expanding its higher education offerings in this field. The increasing importance of AI across industries has created a clear need for well-trained professionals who can build, apply, and manage intelligent systems. In Slovakia, this demand is seen both in the technology sector and in areas such as healthcare, transportation, finance, and public administration. By offering more specialised academic programmes, the country is creating new opportunities for students to gain skills that are valuable in the job market while also helping to strengthen its digital economy.
The main goal of this initiative is to give students structured, in-depth training in AI and related subjects like data science and intelligent systems. Twenty-two degree programmes in artificial intelligence are now offered at six Slovak universities. These programmes benefit students interested in studying AI and related fields. They provide a pathway to careers in software development, machine learning, robotics, data analytics, and research, among others. Courses typically combine theoretical foundations with practical applications, helping students to understand not only how AI works, but also how to use it to solve real-world problems.
According to AIpoint.SK, six universities in Slovakia collectively offer 22 AI‑specific degree programmes. These programmes cover undergraduate and graduate study in AI, data science, intelligent systems, and related areas, and are available at leading institutions such as the Slovak University of Technology in Bratislava, Technical University of Košice, Comenius University, University of Žilina, Pavol Jozef Šafárik University, and Pan‑European University. The aim is to prepare a skilled workforce in AI and advanced data technologies aligned with industry demand and educational advancement across the country.
The development of these programmes reflects cooperation between universities, government agencies, and private sector stakeholders. It also shows a clear national commitment to preparing the next generation of digital professionals. Looking forward, the initiative may grow by adding more advanced courses, increasing partnerships with tech companies, or offering new specialisations based on industry trends. As AI continues to evolve, Slovakia’s universities are positioning themselves to train students who can lead in both domestic and international innovation landscapes.

items.title: AI-related training courses in the State Employment Agency’s Reskilling and Upskilling training programmes
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This initiative provides AI-related training courses as part of Latvia’s broader reskilling and upskilling efforts. Training options include online courses via Google AI Basics, ICT training programmes based on DigComp Level 4, and short AI-focused courses ranging from 8 to 80 hours. The programme targets unemployed individuals, job seekers, and people at risk of unemployment, aiming to improve their employability through the development of digital and AI skills.

RRF EUR 28.71 million, National Budget EUR 1.44 million.

items.title: AI-Empowered Teaching: Unlocking the Future of Digital Education for Teachers (AI-EmpaTe)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This international project aims to enhance the AI-related competencies of educators by developing online training modules tailored for teacher education students and professional development programmes for primary and secondary school teachers.

Running until 2026, the project is a collaboration between institutions from Czechia, Slovakia, and Israel, and seeks to equip educators with the necessary skills to integrate AI technologies into their teaching practices.

items.title: AI in social sciences
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This study course is designed for educators and aims to introduce them to the fundamentals of AI and its applications in the fields of humanities and education.

The course provides an overview of AI as a subfield of computer science, focusing on problem-solving, machine learning, data representation, and decision-making. The goal is to equip educators with the necessary knowledge to incorporate AI concepts into their teaching.

items.title: "AI Essentials" courses for women
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This beginner-friendly course, developed by Google.org and implemented by Riga TechGirls, aims to help women harness AI to enhance productivity and efficiency in their daily tasks. The course provides practical AI tools and knowledge, enabling participants to integrate AI into their professional and personal activities.

The AI Essentials course, offered by Riga TechGirls with support from Google.org, is designed to help women take their first confident steps into the world of artificial intelligence. Many women, especially those with no technical background, may feel excluded from digital change. This course addresses that gap by showing how AI can be a practical tool in everyday work and life.
The main aim is to make AI accessible, useful, and safe. Through a series of short, self-paced modules, participants learn what AI is, how to use simple AI tools to boost productivity, and how to apply them responsibly. The training covers everyday tasks such as writing, organising, and idea generation, while also highlighting how to spot risks like bias or misuse. No coding or prior expertise is required.
By focusing on women—including mid-career professionals who want to update their skills—the initiative helps ensure they are not left behind in a rapidly changing labour market. As demand grows, Riga TechGirls plans to expand enrolment and adapt the programme to different professions, making sure women continue to benefit from the opportunities AI can offer.

items.title: Satellite Crop Monitoring System
items.original_name: System Satelitarnego Monitorowania Upraw Rolnych, S2MUR
items.org: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: System Satelitarnego Monitorowania Upraw Rolnych, S2MUR
items.body:
The S2MUR project provides detailed monitoring of agricultural crops and forecasts adverse weather events that may cause crop losses. It generates maps and reports to estimate crop damage and support decision-making. The project uses satellite, meteorological, soil, and statistical data, combined with machine learning models, to improve agricultural risk management.

The S2MUR project aims to enhance agricultural monitoring and forecasting to reduce crop losses. It provides farmers, policymakers, and stakeholders with comprehensive knowledge about crop conditions and predicts the impact of adverse weather events, such as droughts or storms. The project also generates maps and reports to estimate losses and calculate potential crop damage.
Key features of the initiative include:
Development of an information system that integrates satellite imagery, meteorological, soil, and statistical dataCreation of a repository of machine learning (ML) models for analyzing crop conditions and forecasting risksProvision of a production environment to apply ML models and an environment for developing and training ML modelsFocus on estimating losses due to drought and other crop hazardsThe project’s future goals include expanding the range of ML models, improving prediction accuracy, and enhancing the system’s usability for farmers and agricultural authorities. By combining data-driven insights with machine learning, S2MUR supports more informed agricultural management and helps mitigate the economic impact of crop losses.

items.title: SOLAS Skills to Advance and eCollege ICT Development Pathways
items.org: Department of Further and Higher Education, Research, Innovation and Science
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
SOLAS, the Irish state agency for further education and training, is developing a suite of digital upskilling micro-qualifications such as Introduction to AI, Cloud Computing, and Big Data. Its eCollege platform offers self-paced, tutor-supported online courses in Digital Skills and ICT.

SOLAS, an agency of Ireland’s Department of Further and Higher Education, Research, Innovation and Science, is leading efforts to expand access to digital skills training. It is developing a suite of micro-qualifications to help learners quickly gain expertise in high-demand areas, including:
Introduction to AICloud ComputingDatafication/Big DataIn parallel, SOLAS eCollege provides self-paced, tutor-supported online courses in Digital Skills and ICT Development Pathways, offering flexible training opportunities to individuals and employees seeking to upgrade their digital competencies.
These initiatives aim to:
Address skills shortages in Ireland’s digital economyEnable lifelong learning and upskilling for workers across sectorsSupport businesses and public organisations in adopting new technologiesLooking ahead, SOLAS plans to expand the range of micro-qualifications and strengthen its eCollege offerings, ensuring that learners can continually develop the digital skills needed in a rapidly evolving labour market.

items.title: National Living Lab for Precision Agriculture (NPPL)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The National Precision and Productivity Lab (NPPL) helps farmers use precision farming techniques, including AI-driven tools for crop monitoring and irrigation. By leveraging open weather and soil data, it promotes sustainable agriculture. The initiative also provides insights that support policy development.

The NPPL is designed to support the adoption of precision farming and AI-driven agricultural solutions. It enables farmers to make data-driven decisions through access to real-time information on weather, soil, and crop conditions. By integrating AI technologies, the initiative enhances efficiency, productivity, and sustainability in farming practices.
Key objectives include:
Promoting sustainable and efficient agricultural practicesSupporting farmers in adopting AI and digital solutionsGenerating data-driven insights for policy makers and the agricultural sectorThe NPPL uses open data sources to inform decision-making and improve farm management, from automated crop monitoring to precision irrigation systems. Its work also helps guide policy and regulatory frameworks for modern agriculture.
Future outlook:
Expansion of AI applications and digital tools in agricultureBroader adoption of sustainable practices across farms in the countryContinued data collection and analysis to inform both farmers and policymakers

items.title: NXTGEN High-Tech – Agri-Food
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
NXTGEN develops autonomous agricultural machinery and smart production lines to improve efficiency and safety in the agrifood sector. It uses AI, robotics, and automation to reduce waste and optimise resource use. The initiative promotes collaboration between technology experts and the farming industry.

NXTGEN is a technology-driven initiative aimed at modernising the agrifood sector through automation and intelligent systems. Its primary goal is to develop autonomous machinery and smart production lines that make farming practices safer, more efficient, and less wasteful.
Key objectives include:
Automation of agricultural processes using AI and roboticsOptimisation of resource use to reduce waste and improve sustainabilityCollaboration with experts in technology and agrifood production to foster innovationThe initiative focuses on bridging the gap between cutting-edge technology and practical applications in farming. By deploying autonomous machinery and smart production systems, NXTGEN supports precision agriculture, enhances productivity, and strengthens the competitiveness of agrifood businesses.
Future outlook:
Expansion of autonomous and AI-driven solutions across different farming sectorsBroader adoption of smart production lines to improve efficiency and sustainabilityContinued partnerships with research institutions and industry players to drive innovation

items.title: Méi Weed
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Méi Weed initiative adapts a grass growth prediction model to Luxembourg’s soil and climate conditions. Delivered through a digital tool, it helps farmers manage pastures more effectively, respond to climate change, and improve both economic efficiency and sustainability.

The Méi Weed initiative, part of the EIP-AGRI (European Innovation Partnership for Agricultural Productivity and Sustainability) programme, aims to optimise grazing management in Luxembourg. By adapting an existing grass growth prediction model to the country’s pedoclimatic conditions, the project offers farmers more accurate data for planning pasture use.
Key objectives include:
Providing forecasts that help farmers adjust grazing areas and supplement livestock feedEnabling better pasture management to cope with climate change impactsImproving economic efficiency and sustainability in livestock farmingThe model is delivered through a digital tool, making it easy for farmers to access and use the forecasts in day-to-day decision-making. This innovation helps farmers not only improve productivity but also reduce environmental pressures from overgrazing and inefficient feed use.
Looking forward, the project could be expanded to integrate additional environmental indicators, link to broader EU agricultural data platforms, and support wider adoption of climate-smart farming practices across Luxembourg and potentially other regions.

items.title: Knowledge and Innovation Agenda for Agriculture, Water and Food (KIA LWV)
items.original_name: Kennis- en Innovatieagenda voor Landbouw, Water en Voedsel (KIA LWV)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Kennis- en Innovatieagenda voor Landbouw, Water en Voedsel (KIA LWV)
items.body:
The KIA LWV programme develops key technologies, including AI, for the agriculture, horticulture, and water sectors. It aims to make systems more efficient, intelligent, and environmentally friendly. The programme uses tools such as sensors, robots, and digital twins to support sustainability goals.

The KIA LWV programme focuses on integrating advanced technologies into agriculture, horticulture, and water management to improve efficiency, intelligence, and sustainability. By combining AI with tools like sensors, robots, and digital twins, the programme helps optimise production processes, reduce environmental impacts, and enhance decision-making.
Key objectives include:
Developing AI-driven solutions for precision agriculture and water managementImproving operational efficiency and resource use in farms and horticultureSupporting environmentally sustainable practices through smart technologiesImplementation involves collaborating with research institutes, technology developers, and industry stakeholders to ensure that innovations are practical, scalable, and aligned with sector needs.
Looking ahead, KIA LWV seeks to expand the adoption of digital and AI technologies across the agriculture and water sectors, contributing to long-term sustainability, productivity, and resilience in these critical areas.

items.title: Fruit and vegetable price monitoring and forecasting
items.original_name: Monitoraġġ u previżjoni tal-prezz tal-frott u l-ħaxix
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Monitoraġġ u previżjoni tal-prezz tal-frott u l-ħaxix
items.body:
The Malta Food Agency is developing a project to monitor and forecast fruit and vegetable prices. The initiative uses AI and advanced technologies to analyse market data and predict price trends. This will help stakeholders make better decisions in the food supply chain.

The project by the Malta Food Agency aims to improve market transparency and predictability in the fruit and vegetable sector. By using AI and advanced data analytics, the initiative will:
Monitor current market prices of fruits and vegetablesForecast future price movements to support planning and decision-makingProvide insights to farmers, retailers, and policymakers for better market strategiesThe main objectives of the project are to:Enhance efficiency in the food supply chainReduce market uncertainty for producers and consumersSupport data-driven decision-making in the agriculture sectorLooking ahead, the initiative could expand to include additional commodities and integrate real-time market intelligence, helping Malta’s food sector become more resilient and responsive to market fluctuations.

items.title: Data-Driven Agriculture course
items.original_name: Curso de Agricultura Orientada por Dados
items.org: NOVA Information Management School (NOVA IMS), Universidade Nova de Lisboa
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Curso de Agricultura Orientada por Dados
items.body:
The Data-Driven Agriculture course helps agricultural companies adopt digital and precision agriculture techniques. It teaches skills in data collection, governance, analysis, and technological solutions. The course is a collaboration between CAP and NOVA IMS, supporting the digital transformation of the agricultural sector.

The Data-Driven Agriculture course is designed to support the digital transformation of agricultural companies in Portugal through intelligent and precision agriculture. It provides practical training on how to use data and technology to improve productivity, sustainability, and competitiveness in the sector.
Key objectives of the course include:
Teaching data collection, governance, processing, and analysis techniquesIntroducing technological solutions for precision and intelligent agricultureHelping companies integrate digital tools into everyday farming practicesThe course is delivered through a collaboration between the Confederation of Farmers of Portugal (CAP) and the Universidade Nova de Lisboa – NOVA Information Management School (NOVA IMS). This partnership ensures that the training is both practical and academically rigorous, addressing real-world challenges faced by agricultural businesses.
Future outlook:
Expand access to more agricultural companies across PortugalPromote the adoption of precision agriculture and AI-based solutionsEnhance competitiveness, sustainability, and innovation in the agricultural sector

items.title: Clean Forest Project
items.org: NOVA Laboratory for Computer Science and Informatics
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Forest Fire Protection AI Project uses AI and augmented reality to monitor forest fire protection zones. It aims to reduce the risk and impact of forest fires. The project combines automatic and participatory surveillance for more effective forest safety.

The initiative focuses on improving forest fire prevention and management through advanced technology. By applying AI algorithms and augmented reality tools, the project enables real-time monitoring of forest fire protection zones and supports decision-making during potential fire events.
Key objectives include:
Automatic detection of fire risks in protected forest areasParticipatory monitoring, allowing local communities and authorities to contribute to surveillanceMinimising the impact of forest fires through early warning and rapid responseThe project is led by the NOVA Laboratory for Computer Science and Informatics, which integrates cutting-edge research with practical applications. By combining AI, augmented reality, and community participation, the initiative seeks to enhance environmental protection and reduce forest fire-related damages.
Future outlook:
Expansion of surveillance capabilities using more advanced AI modelsIncreased community involvement in forest monitoringPotential replication of the system in other regions at risk of forest fires

items.title: COMPETE 2030 Program
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The programme provides funding for research and innovation projects in agriculture, including the development of AI solutions. Projects focus on areas such as precision agriculture and data analytics to improve productivity and decision-making. It supports collaboration between researchers, companies, and other stakeholders in the agricultural sector.

This funding programme aims to accelerate innovation and adoption of AI in agriculture by supporting research and development projects. It targets initiatives that use AI to improve efficiency, sustainability, and competitiveness in the sector. Key areas include:
Precision agriculture: Using AI to optimise planting, irrigation, fertilisation, and harvestingData analytics: Leveraging AI to analyse large datasets, predict yields, detect crop diseases, and improve decision-makingThe programme encourages collaboration between academic institutions, research centres, companies, and farmers, fostering knowledge exchange and the practical application of AI technologies. By providing financial support and technical resources, it helps projects move from concept to real-world implementation.
Future outlook:
Expansion of AI-driven solutions across more agricultural areasIncreased use of data-driven decision-making in farmingStrengthening the competitiveness and sustainability of the agricultural sector through technology adoption

items.title: Agricultural scenario-pilot to develop AI models2-
items.original_name: Rolniczy scenariusz-pilot do opracowania modeli SI
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Rolniczy scenariusz-pilot do opracowania modeli SI
items.body:
The AI4EOSC project expands the European Open Science Cloud (EOSC) to include AI, machine learning, and deep learning services. It develops AI models for agriculture, helping to assess crop disease and pest risks and track plant growth. The initiative supports data-driven decision-making in the agricultural sector.

The AI4EOSC project aims to enhance the European Open Science Cloud (EOSC) ecosystem by integrating services related to artificial intelligence, machine learning, and deep learning. By leveraging EOSC infrastructure, the project provides researchers and practitioners with advanced tools for data-driven applications.
A key component is the agricultural scenario-pilot developed by the Wielkopolska Agricultural Advisory Center (WODR) in Poznań together with the Poznań Supercomputing and Networking Center. This pilot focuses on:
Predicting risks of diseases and pests in agricultural cropsDetermining plant growth phases using AI modelsSupporting farmers and advisors with actionable insights for crop managementThe project’s objectives are to:
Expand the EOSC ecosystem with AI-enabled servicesFacilitate applied research in agriculture using AI and machine learningStrengthen collaboration between research centers and agricultural practitionersFuture outlook: The AI4EOSC project is expected to scale by incorporating additional agricultural scenarios, integrating more AI models, and expanding services across Europe, promoting sustainable and precision agriculture through AI-driven insights.

items.title: Agricultural Research and Innovation Hub (AgriHub)
items.original_name: Ċentru ta’ Riċerka u Innovazzjoni Agrikola (AgriHub)
items.org: Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Animal Rights
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Ċentru ta’ Riċerka u Innovazzjoni Agrikola (AgriHub)
items.body:
The AgriHub brings together researchers, innovators, and farmers to improve farming practices in Malta. It focuses on developing the country’s first Integrated Pest Management programmes for key crops. AI-enabled monitoring systems and remote data collection support more efficient and sustainable pest management.

The AgriHub is an initiative under the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Animal Rights in Malta. It is designed to act as a collaboration platform for researchers, innovators, and farmers to test and apply new agricultural technologies.
The main goal of the AgriHub is to develop Malta’s first local Integrated Pest Management (IPM) programmes for key crops. By integrating AI-enabled monitoring systems and remote data collection tools, the initiative aims to:
Improve the efficiency and accuracy of pest detectionReduce the use of harmful pesticidesPromote more sustainable and resilient farming practicesOver time, the AgriHub is expected to expand to other areas of agricultural innovation, helping Malta’s farming community adopt data-driven and environmentally friendly practices. This will strengthen the competitiveness of local agriculture while protecting the island’s ecosystems.

items.title: Adoption and Exploitation of AI in Agriculture
items.original_name: Adoptarea și valorificarea inteligenței artificiale în agricultură
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Adoptarea și valorificarea inteligenței artificiale în agricultură
items.body:
The Adoption and Exploitation of AI in Agriculture programme supports the use of AI-driven automation in agriculture and industry. It funds R&D projects, including EU-supported initiatives, to promote digitalisation in agriculture and food sectors. The initiative aims to increase efficiency and innovation in farming and agri-food operations

The Adoption and Exploitation of AI in Agriculture programme is designed to accelerate AI and automation uptake in the agricultural and industrial sectors. It focuses on providing practical support for AI applications, such as robotics and smart farming technologies, to improve productivity and sustainability.
Key objectives include:
Stimulating development and application of AI-driven automation solutions in agriculture and industrySupporting R&D projects, including those funded under Horizon Europe, to advance digitalisation in agriculture and food systemsPromoting innovation and competitiveness in the agri-food sectorThe programme encourages collaboration between research institutions, companies, and technology providers to ensure AI solutions meet real-world needs. By combining public and EU funding, it enables projects that might otherwise be too risky or resource-intensive for individual organisations.
Future outlook:
Expanded AI adoption across farms and industrial food processingIntegration of smart technologies and robotics into everyday agricultural practicesStrengthened linkages between research, innovation, and commercial deployment in the agri-food ecosystem

items.title: Action Program Digitalisation (ADP)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Action Program Digitalisation (APD) supports the digital transformation of agriculture in the Netherlands. It funds training and the development of AI systems for smart farming, autonomous greenhouses, and precision agriculture. The programme helps make food production more efficient and sustainable.

The Action Program Digitalisation (APD), led by the Ministry of Agriculture, is designed to create the conditions for digital innovation in the agricultural sector. Its purpose is to support farmers and agribusinesses in adopting modern technologies and AI applications that improve productivity and sustainability.
Key objectives of the programme include:
Providing training and resources to farmers and agricultural workersDeveloping AI-driven solutions for smart farming, autonomous greenhouses, and precision agricultureSupporting sustainable and efficient food production through digital toolsThe APD facilitates collaboration between farmers, technology providers, and research institutions, enabling the agricultural sector to leverage data-driven insights and automation.Future outlook:
Expansion of AI and digital tools in mainstream agricultural practicesStrengthened integration of technology into everyday farmingEnhanced sustainability, efficiency, and competitiveness in Dutch agriculture

items.title: Action Plan for the Sustainable Bioeconomy
items.original_name: Plano de Ação para a Bioeconomia Sustentável
items.org: Presidency of the Council of Ministers
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Plano de Ação para a Bioeconomia Sustentável
items.body:
The Portuguese Action Plan for the Circular Bio-economy promotes the transition of the economy toward sustainable and circular practices. It uses advanced technologies, including AI, robotics, and big data, in sectors like agriculture and forestry. The plan supports innovation and resource-efficient growth.

The Action Plan for the Circular Bio-economy is a strategic initiative designed to accelerate the shift to a sustainable and circular economy in Portugal. Its primary focus is on leveraging advanced technologies, including AI, robotics, and big data, to improve efficiency and sustainability in key sectors such as agriculture, forestry, and bio-based industries.
Key objectives of the plan include:
Promoting sustainable use of natural resourcesIncreasing the adoption of AI and digital technologies in bio-economy sectorsSupporting innovation and competitiveness of Portuguese companiesEncouraging circular practices to reduce waste and environmental impactImplementation involves collaboration between government, industry, and research institutions, ensuring that technological advancements are effectively applied in real-world settings. The plan is intended to stimulate innovation, job creation, and economic growth while supporting environmental sustainability.
Future outlook:
Broader integration of AI and digital tools across bio-economy sectorsExpansion of circular economy practices nationwideStrengthened linkages between research, industry, and policy to maintain long-term sustainability and competitiveness

items.title: AI-related university courses
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Under Italy’s AI Strategy 2024-2026, Italian universities are expanding their AI research and teaching capacities. Over 53 universities now offer more than 160 AI-related courses, equipping students with essential AI skills.

Italy’s AI Strategy 2024-2026 has significantly boosted the development of AI research and education within the country’s universities. By expanding both teaching capacity and course offerings, the initiative seeks to make AI a core competence for students across disciplines.
Currently, more than 53 universities in Italy provide over 160 AI-related courses, ranging from introductory modules to advanced specialisations. This rapid expansion of AI education is designed to:
Equip students with key AI knowledge and skillsStrengthen research capacity and innovation within higher education institutionsSupport the country’s broader digital transformation goalsLooking ahead, the initiative is expected to further increase the number of AI-focused programmes, strengthen collaboration between universities and industry, and foster an ecosystem where graduates can contribute to Italy’s competitiveness in AI research and application.

items.title: AI in Primary and Secondary school
items.original_name: IA nella scuola primaria e secondaria
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: IA nella scuola primaria e secondaria
items.body:
As part of Italy’s AI Strategy 2024–2026, the Ministry of Education has launched the “AI in Primary and Secondary Education” initiative. Starting in 2024–2025, 15 schools across Calabria, Lazio, Tuscany, and Lombardy will pilot AI-integrated lessons. The programme aims to give students foundational digital and AI skills and help teachers deliver personalised learning experiences.

The “AI in Primary and Secondary Education” initiative is a national pilot designed to bring AI into Italy’s school curriculum. It forms a key part of the AI Strategy 2024–2026 and responds to the country’s need to address the digital skills gap in education.
Beginning with the 2024–2025 academic year, 15 schools across Calabria, Lazio, Tuscany, and Lombardy will test AI-integrated lessons. The pilot will:
Equip students with foundational knowledge of AI and essential digital competenciesUse AI tools as virtual assistants to facilitate personalised learning experiencesSupport teachers in developing tailored educational approaches that meet diverse student needsThis initiative is also intended to scale up in the coming years as part of Italy’s broader push to promote advanced technologies in education. By embedding AI early into learning environments, Italy aims to prepare a new generation of students for an increasingly digital economy and society.

items.title: AI in Animal and Terrestrial systems - WUR
items.original_name: AI in Dier- en Terrestrische Systemen - WUR
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: AI in Dier- en Terrestrische Systemen - WUR
items.body:
This initiative applies AI in agriculture to improve sustainability and efficiency. It includes projects that enhance livestock management and land-use optimisation. The research supports farmers and agricultural stakeholders in making data-driven decisions.

The initiative focuses on leveraging AI technologies in animal and terrestrial systems to address sustainability and efficiency challenges in agriculture. By using data-driven approaches, the project aims to improve productivity, environmental outcomes, and resource management.
Key objectives include:
Enhancing livestock management through AI-based monitoring and predictive toolsOptimising land use and crop management to improve sustainabilitySupporting farmers and agricultural stakeholders in making informed, data-driven decisionsThe initiative brings together multiple research projects and stakeholders to test, develop, and implement AI solutions in real agricultural environments. By integrating AI into agricultural practices, it seeks to increase efficiency, reduce environmental impact, and strengthen the competitiveness of the sector.
Future outlook:
Expansion of AI applications across more areas of agriculture and land managementContinuous innovation in sustainable farming practicesStronger integration between research outputs and practical farming solutions

items.title: AI Excellence Centres
items.org: Italian Institute of Artificial Intelligence for Industry (AI4I)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Italy has created several centres of excellence to advance AI research and applications. These include the Italian Institute of Artificial Intelligence for Industry (AI4I) in Turin, the ELLIS Unit in Milan, and the Alma Mater Research Institute for Human-Centred AI in Bologna. Together they strengthen AI innovation, fundamental research, and human-centred applications.

Italy is investing in a network of centres of excellence dedicated to advancing artificial intelligence research and its real-world applications. These centres combine academic expertise, industrial partnerships, and societal focus to position the country as a leader in AI innovation.
Key centres include:
Italian Institute of Artificial Intelligence for Industry (AI4I), Turin
Focuses on application-oriented AI research to drive industrial innovation and economic growth.European Laboratory for Learning and Intelligent Systems (ELLIS) Unit, Milan
Contributes to fundamental AI research and its applications across multiple sectors.Alma Mater Research Institute for Human-Centred Artificial Intelligence, Bologna
Emphasises human-centred AI, exploring applications in health, industry, and society.Together, these initiatives promote cross-sector collaboration, strengthen Italy’s AI research capacity, and ensure that AI technologies are innovative, ethical, and beneficial to society. They also contribute to Europe-wide efforts to build trusted, cutting-edge AI ecosystems.

items.title: AGRISPACE
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Portuguese AGRIculture Data SPACE consortium was created to support the digitalisation of agriculture in Portugal. It focuses on developing a Data Space to collect, manage, and share agricultural data. The initiative helps improve efficiency, decision-making, and innovation in the agricultural sector

The Portuguese AGRIculture Data SPACE consortium is part of the national and European strategy for the digitalisation of agriculture. Its main goal is to develop a Data Space that allows for the collection, integration, and sharing of data across the agricultural sector. This approach supports better decision-making, innovation, and sustainability in agriculture.
Key objectives include:
Creating a secure and interoperable Data Space for Portuguese agricultureEnhancing data-driven decision-making for farmers, researchers, and policymakersSupporting innovation in agri-food production and supply chainsThe initiative promotes collaboration among public institutions, research centres, and private stakeholders to ensure that agricultural data can be used efficiently and safely. By leveraging advanced digital technologies, it aims to improve productivity, sustainability, and competitiveness in the sector.
Future outlook
Expansion of the Data Space to cover more agricultural domains and stakeholdersIntegration with European agricultural data initiativesContinued support for research, innovation, and policy development based on high-quality agricultural data

items.title: Supply of robotics and STEM equipment for education
items.original_name: Προμήθεια εξοπλισμού ρομποτικής και STEM για την εκπαίδευση
items.org: Ministry of Education and Religious Affairs
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Προμήθεια εξοπλισμού ρομποτικής και STEM για την εκπαίδευση
items.body:
This programme funds the provision of robotics kits to primary and secondary schools across the country. Each kit combines building blocks and software so students can both construct and program their own projects. It aims to promote STEM learning and digital skills from an early age.

The programme supports schools nationwide by supplying robotics kits to kindergartens, elementary schools, and high schools. These kits include hardware and software that allow pupils to build and program complete projects, combining hands-on learning with digital problem-solving.
Its main objectives are to:
Introduce robotics and coding into early educationEncourage STEM skills development among children and teenagersProvide equal access to modern educational tools in schools across the countryBy equipping classrooms with robotics kits, the initiative helps teachers integrate interactive, project-based learning into their lessons. It also supports the development of critical thinking, creativity, and collaboration skills that are essential for future careers.
In the future, the programme may expand the range of kits and training offered, ensuring that both teachers and students can keep pace with technological advances and develop the competencies needed for a digital economy.

items.title: Skillnet Ireland
items.org: Department of Further and Higher Education, Research, Innovation and Science
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Skillnet Ireland Business Networks provides digital skills programmes to support SMEs and develop specialised talent in new and emerging technologies. Several networks focus on AI training, including Technology Ireland ICT Skillnet and Tech Industry Alliance Skillnet. New academic programmes in AI, such as MSc and PhD degrees, further strengthen Ireland’s AI talent pipeline.

Skillnet Ireland Business Networks delivers a range of digital skills and training programmes aimed at both enabling SME digital transformation and building specialised talent for emerging technologies like AI. The initiative works through multiple networks, including:
Technology Ireland ICT SkillnetTechnology Ireland Digital Skillnetitag SkillnetTech Industry Alliance SkillnetThese networks provide upskilling and specialised training in AI to meet the needs of businesses and professionals across the technology sector.
In parallel, several academic programmes in AI have been developed to strengthen Ireland’s talent pipeline. These include:
MSc in AIMSc in Computer Science with AI specialisationPostgraduate Certificate in AIPhD in Data ScienceFoundation Certificate in AIFuture outlook:
Expansion of AI-focused training for SMEs and technology professionalsContinuous development of academic programmes to meet evolving AI skill requirementsSupport for Ireland’s position as a competitive hub for AI talent and innovation

items.title: ReGeneration Initiative
items.org: ReGeneration (Global Shapers Athens Hub / World Economic Forum initiative)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Under the Hellenic Ministry of Digital Government, Microsoft and ReGeneration run Greece’s largest programme to upskill young people in digital and soft skills. The initiative, “The ReGeneration Initiative: Upskilling Greek Youth for the Digital Era powered by Microsoft,” offers extensive training in AI and other emerging technologies. Its goal is to prepare young people for modern job market demands.

The ReGeneration Initiative: Upskilling Greek Youth for the Digital Era powered by Microsoft is Greece’s largest digital literacy and upskilling programme for youth. Implemented under the auspices of the Hellenic Ministry of Digital Government, it is a collaboration between Microsoft and ReGeneration, aiming to close the gap between young people’s skills and the needs of the modern job market.
The programme provides:
Training in AI and emerging technologiesAround 20,000 hours of instruction for 1,000 young beneficiariesCourses in soft and digital skills, such as:Office automationMobile applicationsInformation systemsData visualisationCloud technologiesDigital marketingUI/UX designIts objectives are to:
Equip youth with in-demand digital and soft skillsSupport employability and career development in Greece’s growing tech sectorFoster a future-ready workforce able to adapt to new technologiesThe initiative builds on ReGeneration, which is the largest employment and training programme in Greece, created by the Global Shapers Athens Hub in cooperation with the World Economic Forum.
Looking ahead, the programme seeks to scale up its training efforts to reach more young people, broaden the range of digital skills offered, and strengthen the pipeline of AI and tech talent in Greece.

items.title: Pioneers in AI
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The project “Students of Natural Sciences: Pioneers in Artificial Intelligence” offers an online AI course designed for science students. Developed under the “Science For You – SciFy” initiative with support from the Education Office of NCSR “Demokritos”, it includes videos, exercises, and other interactive materials to make AI learning accessible.

The project “Students of Natural Sciences: Pioneers in Artificial Intelligence” is part of the wider “Science For You – SciFy” initiative aimed at engaging students with cutting-edge technologies. It creates an online AI course tailored specifically to the needs of science students.
The course is enriched with:
Instructional videos explaining core AI conceptsInteractive exercises to deepen understandingAdditional educational elements to support self-paced learningBy combining engaging content with accessible delivery, the project helps science students gain practical knowledge of AI early in their education, equipping them with skills that are increasingly valuable in research and industry.
Looking forward, the initiative aims to expand its course offerings and strengthen cooperation between educational institutions and research centres to build a pipeline of AI-competent graduates.

items.title: Panhellenic Educational Robotics Competition
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The National Competition on Educational Robotics introduces robotics and STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics) into the official school system. It helps students develop 21st-century skills and promotes STEM as a core teaching methodology in compulsory education.

The National Competition on Educational Robotics is designed to integrate educational robotics and the broader STEM approach into mainstream education. It serves as a platform where students, teachers, and schools can explore hands-on learning, creativity, and problem-solving through robotics projects.
The competition’s objectives include:
Introducing robotics into classrooms as part of the official curriculumPromoting STEM as a teaching methodology for compulsory educationDefining clear ways for students to acquire 21st-century skills, such as critical thinking, collaboration, and digital literacyThrough national-level contests and activities, students gain practical experience in building and programming robots while learning scientific principles. Teachers receive guidance on how to integrate STEM concepts into their lessons, creating a pipeline of future innovators and technology-savvy professionals.
Looking ahead, the competition aims to expand participation across regions, strengthen partnerships with schools, and further embed STEM-based learning in the education system to enhance the country’s innovation capacity.

items.title: Human Capital Initiative (HCI) and Springboard+
items.org: Department of Further and Higher Education, Research, Innovation and Science,
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Springboard+ and Human Capital Initiative (HCI) programmes in Ireland provide AI-focused training courses to support reskilling and upskilling. In 2023–2024, these initiatives offered courses in AI, including AI in Medicine, with several hundred training places available. These programmes help workers gain skills for AI-related roles.

As of early 2024, the Springboard+ and Human Capital Initiative (HCI) programmes have delivered targeted AI training courses to meet the growing demand for AI skills in Ireland. Key achievements include:
Springboard+ 2023 programme: 3 AI courses offering 78 placesHCI Pillar 1 (reskilling): 3 courses providing 55 placesHCI Pillar 3 (AI and AI in Medicine): 395 additional places available for learnersThese initiatives aim to:
Support reskilling and upskilling of the workforce in AI-related fieldsIncrease access to specialised training in AI applications, including healthcareAlign education and training provision with labour market needs in AILooking ahead, both programmes plan to expand course offerings and increase capacity to ensure that more learners can develop AI competencies, strengthening Ireland’s workforce and enhancing innovation capacity across industries.

items.title: Digital Culture Curriculum
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Digital Culture Curriculum in Hungary introduces students in grades five and eleven to the foundational concepts of AI. It builds a basic understanding of the technology from an early age. Teacher training programmes support this effort by equipping educators with the skills to effectively deliver AI education.

The Digital Culture Curriculum is a national education initiative in Hungary designed to ensure that young people gain early exposure to artificial intelligence concepts. By embedding AI into the curriculum for grades five and eleven, it fosters basic technological literacy and prepares students for a future shaped by digital technologies.
To ensure high-quality instruction, the initiative also provides teacher training programmes. These courses equip educators with the knowledge, skills, and confidence needed to teach AI concepts effectively, ensuring consistency and depth across schools.
The curriculum aims to:
Introduce core AI principles and digital competencies at an early agePrepare students to navigate and shape the digital future responsiblySupport educators with continuous training and professional developmentLooking ahead, the programme may expand to additional grade levels and subjects, deepening AI education across Hungary’s school system and strengthening the pipeline of digitally literate, AI-aware citizens.

items.title: AI in Schools (various initiatives)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Ireland participated in the AI4T Erasmus+ project to explore the use of AI in education and generate practical policy recommendations. Oide Technology in Education provides an AI Hub with resources, a one-hour online course, and guidance for teachers and school leaders. Post-primary teachers engaged in workshops and pilots to develop practical AI use cases in schools.

Ireland’s participation in the AI4T Erasmus+ project (AI FOR and BY teachers, 2021–2024) focused on exploring AI applications in education and producing policy recommendations. The project addressed key areas including:
Professional learning pathways for educatorsCross-national cooperation to strengthen EU AI capacityEthical and legal considerations for AI use in schoolsGuidance requirements from education authoritiesTargeted training for inspectors and teacher trainersEvaluation of student outcomes and experiencesComplementing this, Oide Technology in Education provides an AI Hub with practical resources on the safe, effective, and ethical use of AI in education. The platform includes:
A video series and AI online course (AI for Schools, 1-hour) for teachers and school leadersGuidance on AI benefits, limitations, and challengesOpportunities for teachers to engage in Think-In events, sharing knowledge and discussing AI integrationSeveral pilot activities were conducted in schools to develop practical use cases, gather insights, and inform policy development. Additionally, AI guidelines for schools are under development, with publication expected in early 2025.

items.title: AI and academic integrity guidelines
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The National Academic Integrity Network provides guidance for educators on the use of generative AI in education. It also offers resources for handling academic misconduct cases. The initiative helps ensure ethical and responsible use of AI in academic settings.

The National Academic Integrity Network, facilitated by Quality and Qualifications Ireland (QQI), supports educators and institutions in maintaining academic integrity while integrating new technologies, including generative AI.
