In 2023, the Network developed guidelines for educators on responsible AI use in teaching, assessment, and research.
Key objectives include:
Promoting ethical and responsible use of AI in educationProviding practical guidance for academic staff on AI-related issuesOffering resources for academic misconduct investigation and case managementThe initiative also includes a Framework for Academic Misconduct Investigation and Case Management, which helps institutions manage incidents consistently and fairly. By providing these tools, the Network aims to support high standards of integrity while enabling the educational benefits of emerging technologies.

items.title: AI Challenge
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Hungary AI Challenge is an introductory programme to raise awareness and understanding of AI. It is part of Hungary’s National AI Strategy. The programme aims to engage citizens, students, and professionals in learning about AI concepts and applications.

The Hungary AI Challenge was launched to increase AI literacy and awareness among a broad audience. It is part of Hungary’s National AI Strategy and serves as an entry point for individuals to learn about AI technologies, their uses, and societal impacts.
Key objectives include:
Introducing AI concepts to citizens, students, and professionalsEncouraging practical engagement through challenges and learning activitiesRaising general awareness about AI’s potential and ethical considerationsThe initiative is designed to be accessible and inclusive, offering materials and activities that do not require prior technical knowledge. By fostering early understanding of AI, the programme supports future education, workforce development, and public dialogue about AI in Hungary.
Future outlook:
Expansion to reach more participants across schools, universities, and the general publicIntegration with other national AI education and training programmesSupport for building an AI-literate workforce and citizenry

items.title: “I’m in a Course” Initiative
items.org: Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The online platform developed by the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs (MoLSA) serves as a national gateway for retraining and further education opportunities, with a strong emphasis on digital skills including AI programming and usage.

Launched by the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs (MoLSA), this platform is designed to:
Connect individuals (jobseekers, employees, and those seeking upskilling) with training providers offering courses in digital competencies, including AI-related skills.Match training supply and demand, acting as a one-stop shop for career development and reskilling opportunities.Support the transition to an AI-driven and digital economy by promoting accessible education in emerging technologies.Provide search and filter tools for tailored course recommendations across regions, skill levels, and employment sectors.By linking jobseekers and employers with training providers, the platform helps address skills gaps in AI and other digital technologies, contributing to a more adaptable and future-ready workforce.

items.title: “Digital problem solving” in Preparatory Adult Education (FVU)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
As of January 2024, the FVU (Preparatory Adult Education) programme in Denmark includes new learning objectives on digital problem solving. The curriculum introduces basic concepts of generative AI, its uses, limitations, and practical applications in everyday life. It helps adults develop digital skills relevant to employment, education, and personal life.

In January 2024, Denmark updated its Preparatory Adult Education (FVU) curricula to include a focus on digital problem solving, with specific attention to generative AI. The initiative addresses the need to equip adults, particularly low-skilled learners, with practical digital skills that are increasingly relevant in daily life, work, and study.
The curriculum aims to help students:
Understand generative AI and its basic concepts.Recognize practical applications of AI in personal and professional contexts.Identify possibilities and limitations of AI tools for solving everyday tasks.Apply AI tools to tasks related to employment, further education, or private life.While the main target group remains low-skilled adults, the educational offer has been expanded to a broader audience. This ensures more learners have access to essential digital skills that support employability and personal development.
The initiative also reflects a broader trend in adult education towards integrating digital literacy and AI awareness into foundational programmes. Over time, the curriculum is expected to evolve, incorporating more interactive tools, practical exercises, and guidance to help learners effectively navigate AI technologies in their personal and professional lives.

items.title: prg.ai Minor
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The prg.ai Minor is a specialised AI education programme created and managed by the NGO prg.ai in collaboration with Prague universities. It provides students from different disciplines with foundational AI knowledge and skills, combined with lectures and networking sessions with top technology companies, to help them apply AI across diverse fields.

The prg.ai Minor is an innovative educational initiative designed to expand access to high-quality AI education in the Czech Republic. It:
Is coordinated by the NGO prg.ai in partnership with leading Prague universities, ensuring cross-institutional collaboration.Equips students from multiple disciplines — not only computer science — with core knowledge and practical skills in AI, enabling them to apply AI in various sectors.Features regular lectures, workshops, and networking sessions with top technology companies, linking students to industry leaders and real-world applications.Aims to foster interdisciplinary AI talent, bridging the gap between academic learning and practical industry needs.By combining academic expertise with industry engagement, the prg.ai Minor helps to create a new generation of professionals capable of integrating AI solutions across a wide range of fields.

items.title: Technology Comprehension in traditional subjects
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
As part of a 2024 political agreement on quality in Danish primary and lower secondary education, Technology Comprehension will be integrated into traditional subjects. The goal is to ensure students can critically reflect on and competently use new digital technologies, with an expert group deciding the subjects and grade levels for implementation.

In March 2024, the Danish government reached a political agreement to enhance the quality of primary and lower secondary education, introducing Technology Comprehension as a new element in the curriculum. This initiative aims to:
Embed Technology Comprehension into traditional subjects, ensuring students develop digital literacy and critical thinking skills.Provide students with the ability to reflect critically on, and competently use, emerging digital technologies, including AI tools.Assign an expert group to determine the subjects and grade levels where Technology Comprehension will be integrated, ensuring age-appropriate learning outcomes.Support the broader goal of preparing students for a digitally advanced society, enhancing both educational quality and digital readiness.By integrating Technology Comprehension, the initiative seeks to equip students with essential skills for the digital age, fostering both practical competence and ethical awareness in technology use.

items.title: Strengthen and retain specialised IT talent and skills
items.original_name: Styrk og fasthold specialiseret IT-talent og kompetencer
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Styrk og fasthold specialiseret IT-talent og kompetencer
items.body:
Denmark’s national IT education strategy aims to strengthen continuing and further education in IT, enhance professional Master’s programmes, and retain international students in the Danish job market to meet the growing demand for specialised IT competencies.

The national IT education strategy is designed to address the shortage of specialised IT skills in Denmark and to ensure the workforce is prepared for a technology-driven economy. It focuses on:
Expanding continuing and further education programmes in IT, enabling professionals to update and deepen their technical competencies.Enhancing professional Master’s programmes in IT education, ensuring high-quality advanced training aligned with industry needs.Attracting and retaining international students, supporting their integration into the Danish labour market to strengthen the pool of skilled IT professionals.Aligning educational pathways with emerging technology trends, including digitalisation, AI, cybersecurity, and advanced computing.Through these measures, the strategy seeks to boost Denmark’s IT workforce, maintain global competitiveness, and address the country’s demand for highly qualified technology professionals.

items.title: Recommendations on AI in education, teaching and training
items.org: National Agency for Education and the Ministry of Education and Culture
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Finland’s Ministry of Education and Culture and the National Agency for Education are developing recommendations on AI in education. The guidance aims to help teachers and learners use AI safely and responsibly. It also seeks to ensure that all students have equal opportunities to benefit from AI in learning.

The initiative focuses on creating clear recommendations for the use of artificial intelligence in education, teaching, and training. It responds to the growing role of AI in schools and educational institutions, aiming to ensure that AI tools are used responsibly, safely, and effectively. The initiative also seeks to increase understanding of AI among educators and learners.
The main objectives of the recommendations are to:
Enhance knowledge and awareness of AI in educational contexts.Promote responsible and safe use of AI tools by teachers and students.Support equality in learning, ensuring all learners can access the benefits of AI technology.The initiative is being developed collaboratively by the National Agency for Education and the Ministry of Education and Culture, reflecting a coordinated approach that includes policymakers, educators, and experts. The recommendations will provide guidance for schools, training institutions, and educational organisations across Finland.
In the future, the recommendations are expected to be integrated into educational policies and teaching practices. As AI continues to evolve, these guidelines may expand to include new technologies and applications, helping Finland maintain a safe, innovative, and inclusive learning environment for all students.

items.title: Recommendations on AI based tools for examinations in primary, lower and upper secondary school
items.original_name: Anbefalinger om AI-baserede værktøjer til prøver i folkeskole og ungdomsuddannelser
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Anbefalinger om AI-baserede værktøjer til prøver i folkeskole og ungdomsuddannelser
items.body:
In 2023, the Ministry of Children and Education in Denmark established an expert group to issue recommendations on the use of AI-based tools in school examinations. Published in April 2024, the recommendations emphasise diverse testing methods and the need for students to use and critically reflect on digital tools, shaping the Ministry’s future policies in this area.

In May 2023, the Ministry of Children and Education set up an expert group to examine the implications of AI-based tools in primary, lower, and upper secondary school examinations. This group:
Developed recommendations issued in April 2024 on how to integrate AI-based tools into assessments.Proposed the use of different testing methods to better evaluate students’ knowledge, skills, and ability to critically use digital tools.Highlighted the importance of aligning examinations with real-world digital competencies, ensuring students are not only knowledgeable but also able to apply and reflect critically on technology use.Provides a foundation for the Ministry’s future work in shaping policies and frameworks on AI and digital tool use in education.This initiative marks a proactive approach to digital-era assessment, aiming to ensure that educational evaluations remain relevant and equitable in a rapidly evolving technological landscape.

items.title: Re- and up-skilling initiatives
items.org: Service Centre for Continuous Learning and Employment
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The digital service bundle for continuous learning and the Digivisio 2030 programme provide online tools and courses to help individuals develop skills and make informed career choices. AI is used to personalise learning and support guidance in higher education and workforce development. The Service Centre for Continuous Learning and Employment (SECLE) connects labour market needs with training, helping SMEs and academic institutions strengthen AI skills.

The Digital Service Bundle for Continuous Learning is designed to offer a flexible, customer-oriented service package that crosses administrative boundaries. Its main goals are to:
Support individuals in maintaining and developing their skills throughout their careersHelp people make informed education and career decisionsAlign labour market demand with education supplyAI technologies are integrated into the service bundle to enhance personalisation, guidance, and the delivery of learning services.The Digivisio 2030 programme complements this effort by bringing existing online digital competence courses into a common digital platform for higher education institutions. Key features include:
AI-supported guidance and counselling services for studentsFacilitating digital skill development across higher educationPromoting accessibility and standardisation of online learningBoth initiatives are funded by the Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF), ensuring resources for implementation and expansion.The Service Centre for Continuous Learning and Employment (SECLE) focuses on bridging gaps between labour market needs and employee skills. Its activities include:
Conducting foresight analysis to anticipate skill needsProcuring AI-related training for SME personnelSupporting integration of AI skills into academic curriculaFuture outlook:
Expansion of digital platforms and services for lifelong learningBroader adoption of AI-driven personalised learning toolsEnhanced alignment between education, workforce skills, and market needsTogether, these initiatives aim to strengthen employability, support lifelong learning, and prepare individuals and organisations for evolving labour market demands.

items.title: RRF 3.1 Innovation in education in the context of digitization
items.original_name: Projekt AIDIG: Podpora umělé inteligence ve vzdělávání a rozvoj digitálních dovedností učitelů
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Projekt AIDIG: Podpora umělé inteligence ve vzdělávání a rozvoj digitálních dovedností učitelů
items.body:
The AIDIG project, implemented by the National Pedagogical Institute of the Czech Republic, helps schools integrate the European framework for teachers’ digital skills (DigCompEdu). Funded by the National Recovery Plan (NPO 3.1), it trains teachers in emerging technologies such as AI, cybersecurity, digital well-being, and media literacy to improve students’ digital competencies.

Launched in 2024, the AIDIG project supports the systematic integration of digital skills and emerging technologies in Czech schools. It:
Implements the DigCompEdu framework to enhance teachers’ digital competencies.Focuses on emerging digital technologies — including AI, cybersecurity, digital well-being, and financial and media literacy — to prepare students for the demands of a modern, digital society.Trains teachers to pass on advanced IT and digital skills to students, helping them develop critical thinking and responsible technology use.Is funded by the National Recovery Plan under NPO 3.1, ensuring alignment with national and EU priorities in digital transformation.By improving the capacity of teachers to use and teach digital technologies, the AIDIG project strengthens the digital readiness of students and contributes to the long-term development of digital education in the Czech Republic.

items.title: Promotion of inclusion and diversity in AI ecosystems
items.original_name: Promotion de l’inclusion et de la diversité dans les écosystèmes d’IA
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Promotion de l’inclusion et de la diversité dans les écosystèmes d’IA
items.body:
The “Women in AI” and “Inclusive AI” initiatives in France aim to promote diversity in AI education and careers. They support women and underrepresented groups in entering and thriving in the AI sector. Additional projects, such as TechPourToutes, are being developed to further strengthen inclusion in AI.

Several initiatives in France focus on diversity and inclusion in AI:
Women in AI:Supports the attraction and retention of women in AI education and careersEncourages participation in AI research and professional rolesInclusive AI:Promotes diverse teams in AI developmentEnsures that AI technologies are developed inclusively, reflecting different perspectives and needsOther initiatives (in development):TechPourToutes and similar projects aim to expand opportunities for underrepresented groups in technology and AIObjectives:
Increase gender and diversity representation in AI education and the workforcePromote inclusive practices in AI developmentBuild a more equitable AI ecosystem in France

items.title: National Artificial Intelligence Competition (NAIC)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The ARCHIMEDES Unit of the Athena Research Center, together with key Greek AI and education organisations, organises the National Artificial Intelligence Competition (NAIC) for middle and high school students. The competition introduces students to AI techniques such as machine learning, computer vision and natural language processing. Winners represent Greece at the International Olympiad in Artificial Intelligence.

The National Artificial Intelligence Competition (NAIC) is a national initiative in Greece aimed at familiarising middle and high school students with artificial intelligence and developing practical skills in emerging technologies. Organised by the ARCHIMEDES Unit of the Athena Research Center, the competition is held in collaboration with:
Hellenic Society of Computer Scientists and Professionals in Communications (GCP)Hellenic Society for Artificial Intelligence (EETN)Institute of Educational Policy (IEP)The competition introduces participants to modern AI techniques and applications, including:
Machine learningComputer visionNatural language processingStudents work on real-world challenges based on these technologies, gain experience collaborating with industry experts, and build teamwork and problem-solving skills.
Top-performing students have the opportunity to represent Greece at the International Olympiad in Artificial Intelligence, raising the country’s profile in global AI education and innovation.
Future outlook:
Expansion of the competition to include more schools and students nationwideBroader partnerships with industry and academia to deepen mentoring and resourcesContinued alignment with international standards in AI education and competitions

items.title: LaborIA
items.org: Ministry of Labour, Health, Soldiarity and Family
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
LaborIA is responsible for analysing and addressing reskilling needs arising from AI developments. It helps workers and organisations adapt to changes in the labour market caused by AI. Other initiatives, such as IA Clusters and AMI CMA projects, also support continuing education and reskilling.

The LaborIA initiative focuses on understanding and addressing the reskilling requirements created by the growing adoption of AI across industries. Its main objectives include:
Analysing workforce skills gaps in the context of AI deploymentRecommending strategies for reskilling and upskilling workersSupporting organisations in adapting to labour market changes driven by AIIn addition, ongoing initiatives such as IA Clusters and AMI CMA projects complement LaborIA by providing continuing education and training opportunities tailored to the needs of workers in AI-related sectors. These initiatives collectively aim to strengthen the workforce’s capacity to adapt to technological change and foster a culture of lifelong learning.
Future outlook:
Expansion of reskilling programmes to cover more industries affected by AIGreater integration with regional clusters and industry networks to maximise impactSupport for continuous adaptation of workforce skills to evolving AI technologies

items.title: Konrad Zuse Schools of Excellence in AI
items.org: Federal Ministry of Education and Research
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Konrad Zuse Schools of Excellence in AI in Germany attract international master’s and PhD students to high-quality English-language programmes. They combine teaching and research with close links to industry, connecting top scientists and industry fellows. The initiative is funded by the German Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF) through the German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD).

The Konrad Zuse Schools of Excellence in AI are designed to build a world-class training and research environment for artificial intelligence. They focus on:
Attracting international talent at the master’s and PhD levelsOffering English-language teaching and research programmes in AIConnecting academia and industry to foster innovation in AI education and researchFunded by the German Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF) through the German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD), the schools create an integrated learning and research experience. Students benefit from high-level academic instruction, while industry fellows bring practical expertise to teaching and collaborative projects.
By combining scientific excellence with practical application, the Konrad Zuse Schools support the training of future AI experts, strengthen Germany’s AI research capacity, and enhance the international visibility of its AI ecosystem.
Looking ahead, the schools aim to expand their network of industry partners, broaden their programme offerings, and continue attracting top-tier international students and researchers to Germany.

items.title: Funding Programme  for Female AI Junior Scientisits
items.org: Federal Ministry of Education and Research
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF) in Germany funds a programme to support female-led junior research groups in AI. It aims to increase the share of qualified women in leadership positions within German AI research. The programme also considers family–work balance in its funding criteria.

This programme is run by the Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF) to strengthen gender diversity and leadership in German AI research. Its main objectives are:
Support female-led junior research groups in AIIncrease the proportion of qualified women in leadership roles within AI researchEncourage innovative AI research topics through targeted fundingIntegrate family–work balance conditions into funding allocation criteriaA new call for applications was issued in 2023 to expand support for female AI scientists, ensuring broader participation and greater visibility for women in cutting-edge AI fields. By linking funding with inclusive conditions, the initiative promotes both excellence in research and equal opportunities in the German AI ecosystem.
Future outlook:
Expansion of the number and scope of female-led AI research groupsBroader integration of gender equality measures into AI research fundingEnhanced visibility of women leaders in AI at national and international levels

items.title: Digital Pact for Schools
items.org: Federal Ministry of Education and Research
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Digital Pact for Schools supports Germany’s federal states in integrating AI technologies into education. It funds digital learning materials, adaptive learning systems, and student support to strengthen digital and AI-related skills. The initiative invests EUR 92 million in AI-related educational media infrastructure across nine cross-state projects.

The Digital Pact for Schools is a nationwide initiative in Germany designed to help federal states integrate AI technologies and digital tools into their education systems. It establishes the technical foundations needed for both teachers and students to acquire digital and AI-related competences.
Its key objectives include:
Funding and support for AI-based digital learning materials and adaptive learning systemsProviding targeted student support through technology-enabled approachesEnhancing educational media infrastructure across multiple federal statesThe initiative allocates EUR 92 million to nine cross-state projects, strengthening the infrastructure required for AI-related educational media. This funding ensures that schools have access to modern tools, platforms, and content that support innovative teaching and personalised learning.
Looking ahead, the Digital Pact for Schools is expected to expand its scope as AI and digital technologies continue to evolve. By embedding these tools into classrooms and teacher training, the programme builds long-term capacity for Germany’s education system to remain competitive and future-ready.

items.title: Compulsory training in digital skills across subjects (Act on Upper Secondary Education)
items.original_name: Anbefalinger til brugen af generativ kunstig intelligens i ungdomsuddannelser
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Anbefalinger til brugen af generativ kunstig intelligens i ungdomsuddannelser
items.body:
The Act on Upper Secondary Education in Denmark mandates that students develop digital competencies across subjects, including AI-related skills, enabling them to critically assess digital content and participate effectively in digital communities.

Under the Danish Act on Upper Secondary Education, upper secondary students are required to:
Develop digital competencies across all subjects, ensuring a holistic integration of technology in learning.Acquire AI-related skills as part of digital literacy, enabling them to understand, use, and critically evaluate AI tools and applications.Critically assess digital content and engage responsibly in digital communities, promoting informed and ethical participation in online environments.Support Denmark’s broader digital education strategy, preparing students for higher education, the workforce, and a society increasingly shaped by AI and other emerging technologies.This legislation ensures that AI and digital literacy are systematically embedded in upper secondary education, fostering a generation of students capable of navigating a digitally complex world.

items.title: Competence Centres for Digital and Digitally Supported Teaching in Schools and Continuing Education
items.original_name: Kompetenzzentren für digitales und digital gestütztes Unterrichten in Schule und Weiterbildung
items.org: Federal Ministry of Education and Research
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Kompetenzzentren für digitales und digital gestütztes Unterrichten in Schule und Weiterbildung
items.body:
The Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF) in Germany funds centres to improve digitalisation-related teacher training. These centres support research, innovation, and knowledge transfer until 2026. AI-supported systems are used to enhance teaching practices in schools.

The initiative, funded by the BMBF under the EU Recovery and Resilience Facility, focuses on enhancing the quality of teacher training in digital skills. The centres aim to combine research, innovation, and practical knowledge transfer to support the professional development of teachers.
Key objectives include:
Improving digital competence in teacher training programmesPromoting pedagogically effective use of AI-supported systems in schoolsFacilitating innovation and knowledge transfer between research institutions and schoolsThe initiative operates until the end of 2026, providing structured support for teacher training institutions to integrate AI tools into curricula. By doing so, it enhances both the quality of teaching and the preparedness of students for a digitalised world.
Future outlook:
Further integration of AI tools in teacher educationContinuous research on effective digital teaching methodsPotential scaling of best practices across German schools and training centres

items.title: Choose France programme
items.org: National Research Programme on Artificial Intelligence
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The ChooseFrance talent programme is designed to attract and support international AI professionals in France. It is led by the IA Cluster initiative and the National Research Programme on Artificial Intelligence (PEPR IA). The programme helps connect talent with research and industry opportunities in AI across the country.

The ChooseFrance talent programme aims to strengthen France’s AI ecosystem by attracting, retaining, and supporting international researchers and professionals in artificial intelligence. Key objectives include:
Talent attraction: Bringing AI experts from abroad to contribute to research and innovationSupport for integration: Facilitating entry into French research institutions and companiesStrengthening the AI ecosystem: Linking international talent with research projects, clusters, and industry partnersThe programme is driven by:
The IA Cluster initiative, which coordinates AI research and innovation efforts across FranceThe National Research Programme on Artificial Intelligence (PEPR IA), which provides strategic support and funding for AI research and developmentFuture outlook:
Expansion of opportunities for international AI talent in both academic and industrial sectorsIncreased collaboration between research institutions, clusters, and private companiesContribution to France’s global leadership in AI research and innovation

items.title: Call for expressions of interest for Skills and professions of the future
items.original_name: (Appel à manifestation d’intérêt pour les Compétences et métiers d’avenir, AMI-CMA
items.org: Ministry of Labour, Health, Solidarity and Family
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: (Appel à manifestation d’intérêt pour les Compétences et métiers d’avenir, AMI-CMA
items.body:
The AMI-CMA programme in France supports the development of digital and AI training curricula across all education levels, from secondary school to PhD. It aims to train 400,000 individuals per year by 2030 and adapt curricula to the evolving professional use of digital tools. Selected projects, such as MACMIA and AISorb, create specialised training to enhance employability in AI-related fields.

The AMI-CMA initiative seeks to transform digital and AI education in France by supporting original curricula across secondary and higher education. The programme focuses on preparing individuals for widespread adoption of digital tools in professional environments and addressing the gap between training supply and labour market demand. Projects are selected through evaluation by an international and independent jury.
Key objectives of the programme include:
Supporting the creation of new digital and AI training curricula at all education levelsContributing to diagnostics of digital training demand and supply in FrancePreparing individuals for professional use of digital technologies and AIExamples of funded projects:
MACMIA: Organises training courses for technicians, engineers, and managers with dual skills in AI and “Industry of the Future.” It also covers dual skill areas such as embedded AI & intelligent mobility, AI & Health, and AI & Distribution.AISorb: Develops training at the intersection of AI and social sciences and humanities (SHS) to improve employability in professions transformed by AI.Future outlook:
Expand the reach and impact of AI and digital training to 400,000 learners annually by 2030Strengthen the alignment between education, skills development, and professional needsFoster innovation in curricula to ensure French students and professionals acquire skills relevant to a digital and AI-driven economy

items.title: Attracting and retaining AI-related talent
items.original_name: Suomen tohtoriohjelmien verkosto tekoälyn alalla (AI-DOC); Työ Suomessa -ohjelma
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Suomen tohtoriohjelmien verkosto tekoälyn alalla (AI-DOC); Työ Suomessa -ohjelma
items.body:
The Ministry of Education and Culture in Finland provides funding to universities to pilot new practices in doctoral education, including support for 1,000 doctoral researchers. The Finnish Doctoral Programme Network in AI is among the recipients. The Work in Finland programme helps Finnish companies, including AI firms, attract and retain international talent.

The initiative aims to strengthen doctoral education and AI talent development in Finland through targeted funding and support programmes. Key aspects include:
Funding allocation: 1,000 doctoral researchers will receive three-year employment contracts (2024–2027) to complete their degreesProgramme participation: The Finnish Doctoral Programme Network in AI is among the beneficiaries, supporting research and training in AIAs part of the national Talent Boost programme, Work in Finland at Business Finland focuses on labour and study-based migration, supporting the attraction and retention of international talent, particularly in IT and AI sectors. Activities include:
Helping companies recruit and retain highly skilled international employeesSupporting AI and technology firms in building a competitive workforceFacilitating integration of international talent into the Finnish labour marketFuture outlook:
Expansion of doctoral AI education and research networksContinued strengthening of Finland’s international AI talent poolAlignment between higher education, research, and industry needs to support innovation and competitiveness

items.title: Allowance for the payment of digital training courses
items.org: Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
As part of the Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF), the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs (MoLSA) provides financial support to individuals for enrolling in digital training courses, including AI-focused ones. The initiative covers up to 82% of course costs (up to about EUR 2,000 per person over three years), making digital upskilling more accessible through the “I’m in a Course” platform.

This initiative, launched under the RRF, is designed to expand access to digital and AI training for individuals across the Czech Republic. It:
Subsidises course fees, covering up to 82% of costs (maximum ~EUR 2,000 per person over three years), reducing financial barriers to upskilling.Is administered via the “I’m in a Course” platform, which acts as a one-stop shop for available training opportunities.Encourages participation in digital and AI-focused courses, from basic digital literacy to advanced AI programming and applications.Aims to support lifelong learning and workforce adaptability, equipping people with in-demand skills needed for the green and digital transitions.By reducing costs and centralising course offerings, the initiative broadens participation in digital upskilling, helping individuals and employers respond to rapid technological change.

items.title: AI for Children
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The “AI for Children” initiative promotes the integration of AI concepts into primary and secondary education, providing teachers and schools with resources and guidance to help young learners develop digital literacy and a practical understanding of AI technologies.

The AI for Children programme is designed to:
Support teachers in adopting AI tools and educational practices in the classroom.Provide a comprehensive range of educational resources (lesson plans, toolkits, interactive materials) to enhance digital and AI literacy among children.Engage students and young people in hands-on learning about AI concepts, ethics, and applications.Foster curiosity and critical thinking around emerging technologies and prepare the next generation for a digital and AI-driven future.Through these activities, the initiative builds a foundation of AI awareness and competence in schools, empowering both teachers and students to navigate and benefit from the opportunities of artificial intelligence.

items.title: A world-class AI Research and Educational Institute
items.original_name: Σχέδιο για τη μετάβαση της Ελλάδας στην εποχή της Τεχνητής Νοημοσύνης
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Σχέδιο για τη μετάβαση της Ελλάδας στην εποχή της Τεχνητής Νοημοσύνης
items.body:
Under Greece’s Blueprint for AI Transformation, a flagship project plans to create a new graduate school and research centre focused on artificial intelligence. The centre will conduct research and deliver training programmes to build national AI capacity.

This flagship initiative, part of the Blueprint for Greece’s AI Transformation, aims to strengthen the country’s AI ecosystem by establishing a new graduate school and research centre dedicated to artificial intelligence.
Its main objectives are to:
Conduct advanced research in AI and related fieldsProvide postgraduate training to develop a highly skilled AI workforceSupport national AI innovation and knowledge transfer between academia and industryThe graduate school and research centre are expected to serve as a hub for AI talent in Greece, offering opportunities for international collaboration, joint research projects, and industry partnerships. By aligning with national AI priorities, the centre will help close the gap between academic expertise and market demand, accelerating Greece’s digital transformation.
Future outlook:
Expansion of graduate programmes in cutting-edge AI topicsAttraction of international researchers and students to GreeceIntegration with national and European AI strategies to promote sustainable growth and innovation

items.title: A central AI Educational Platform
items.original_name: Σχέδιο για τη μετάβαση της Ελλάδας στην εποχή της Τεχνητής Νοημοσύνης
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Σχέδιο για τη μετάβαση της Ελλάδας στην εποχή της Τεχνητής Νοημοσύνης
items.body:
This flagship project under the Blueprint for Greece’s AI Transformation aims to create a shared virtual space where AI experts from academia and industry can develop educational material. Its goal is to build a dynamic and sustainable ecosystem for AI education in Greece.

The initiative is a flagship project of the Blueprint for Greece’s AI Transformation. It is designed to operate as a shared virtual space where AI experts from academia and industry collaborate to produce high-quality educational resources.
Its main objectives are to:
Foster collaboration between universities, research institutions, and industry experts in AIDevelop and share educational material to enhance AI training and awarenessBuild a sustainable ecosystem for AI education that supports Greece’s digital transformation goalsBy creating a centralised digital hub for AI learning materials, the initiative seeks to ensure broad access to up-to-date knowledge and best practices. This approach is expected to strengthen Greece’s ability to train AI professionals, increase industry–academia cooperation, and develop a skilled workforce to support the country’s AI-driven future.
Looking ahead, the project aims to expand the range of educational materials, involve more institutions, and potentially integrate with European-level AI education initiatives. This would position Greece as a regional leader in AI education and skills development.

items.title: Women in Digital
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Belgium’s national and intersectoral strategy “Women in Digital 2021–2026” aims to increase women’s representation in the digital sector by tackling cultural and systemic barriers. Coordinated by the FPS Economy, the five-year plan sets out concrete actions to boost women’s participation and retention in digital education and careers, challenge stereotypes, and bridge the gender gap in specific target groups.

The “Women in Digital 2021–2026” strategy provides a coordinated framework to promote gender diversity in Belgium’s digital economy. Its key features include:
Strategic coordination: Managed by the Federal Public Service (FPS) Economy as an intersectoral plan.Five strategic objectives:Increase the number of women graduating in digital fields.Promote integration of women into the digital workforce.Support retention of women in digital jobs through targeted policies.Challenge stereotypes and create role models to inspire girls and women.Bridge the gender gap in specific groups, including vulnerable populations.Cross-sectoral collaboration with education providers, businesses and civil society to implement actions.Monitoring and evaluation to track progress and adjust measures where needed.Through these measures, Belgium seeks to create a more inclusive and balanced digital sector, encouraging more women to study, enter, and remain in digital and AI-related careers.

items.title: Women Award in Technology and Science
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This Innoviris initiative aims to inspire young women in Brussels to pursue STEM careers. Each year, a EUR 10 000 award is granted to a Science Ambassadress, who organises events and workshops to encourage girls and young women to engage with science and technology, addressing gender imbalances in the STEM field.

Run by Innoviris (the Brussels Institute for Research and Innovation), the programme tackles the underrepresentation of women in science and technology by:
Selecting a Science Ambassadress annually to act as a role model for girls and young women.Providing funding (EUR 10 000) for outreach activities, workshops, talks and school visits that promote STEM disciplines, including AI and digital technologies.Fostering interest and confidence among young women in pursuing STEM studies and careers.Contributing to a more inclusive innovation ecosystem in Brussels by creating visibility and networking opportunities for women in science and technology.Through this initiative, Innoviris strengthens the pipeline of future female talent in STEM and promotes gender diversity across research, innovation and the tech sector.

items.title: University of Zagreb University Computing Centre (SRCE) ICT Education Programme
items.original_name: Sveučilišni računski centar Sveučilišta u Zagrebu (SRCE) – Program obrazovanja u području ICT-a
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Sveučilišni računski centar Sveučilišta u Zagrebu (SRCE) – Program obrazovanja u području ICT-a
items.body:
The University Computing Centre (SRCE) at the University of Zagreb provides ICT training and educational activities for both the academic/research community and the general public. Courses are self-paced and integrated into the E-citizens portal, making digital education widely accessible across Croatia.

The SRCE initiative plays a foundational role in Croatia’s digital education infrastructure, offering training that spans basic ICT skills to advanced digital competencies. Key features include:
Wide accessibility: Courses are self-paced and available online, integrated with the E-citizens portal, ensuring broad reach to the general public.Targeted audiences: Designed for students, researchers, educators, and citizens, providing opportunities for upskilling and lifelong learning.ICT and digital skills training: Covers topics from fundamental ICT literacy to advanced tools, complementing emerging AI-focused programmes.Support for research and academic community: Provides training and resources that enhance digital competence in research and teaching.Strategic role in national digital transformation: Contributes to wider digital inclusion, workforce readiness, and preparation for AI and technology-driven sectors.By offering flexible, widely accessible digital education, the University Computing Centre supports Croatia’s efforts to upskill its population, strengthen the academic and research ecosystem, and complement AI-specific initiatives across the country.

items.title: Technocité
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Technocité is a regional competence centre in Belgium offering training in ICT, creative, and cultural industries. It addresses digital skill gaps by providing tailored programmes for individuals and businesses, emphasising digital inclusion and equipping participants with the skills needed to thrive in a tech-driven economy.

Located in Wallonia (Belgium), Technocité is recognised as a key training hub for the digital and creative sectors. Its mission is to:
Provide specialised training in ICT, multimedia, gaming, digital design, and cultural industries.Support companies in upskilling their workforce to adopt emerging technologies, including AI and digital production tools.Promote digital inclusion by offering accessible learning paths for jobseekers, students, and professionals seeking to transition into the tech and creative industries.Partner with regional and European programmes to foster innovation, creativity, and workforce readiness for the digital economy.By combining technical skills development with industry-specific expertise, Technocité helps build a highly skilled workforce and strengthens the digital and creative ecosystems in Belgium.

items.title: Smart Education @ Schools
items.org: Imec research group at KU Leuven
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
An Imec-led initiative integrates digital tools and AI technologies into classroom settings to enhance learning. It provides funding and resources for innovative educational projects, helping schools incorporate smart technologies into their curricula.

This initiative, led by Imec (Belgium’s world-leading research centre for nanoelectronics and digital innovation), is part of its strategy to tap into the potential of data and foster critical computing capacity. It:
Supports schools and teachers in adopting AI-enabled digital tools to improve learning outcomes.Funds pilot projects to test and implement innovative approaches to teaching, such as smart classrooms, adaptive learning platforms, and AI-based student feedback systems.Promotes collaboration between researchers, technology providers, and education professionals to scale effective practices.Develops a knowledge base on the impact of digital and AI technologies on teaching and learning processes.By blending AI research with practical educational innovation, Imec’s initiative contributes to a future-ready education system in Belgium and strengthens the country’s digital skills ecosystem from an early age.

items.title: Short-term Teacher Training Programme
items.org: Ministry of Education and Municipality Burgas
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
A specialised programme in partnership with “Prof. Asen Zlatarov” University in Bulgaria focuses on enhancing teachers’ digital competencies. It aims to train 225 teachers in the use of augmented and virtual reality (AR/VR) software for educational purposes, helping them create more engaging and interactive learning experiences.

This Bulgarian initiative, developed in cooperation with “Prof. Asen Zlatarov” University, seeks to equip teachers with cutting-edge digital skills to transform teaching practices. Key elements include:
Focus on AR/VR technologies: Training teachers to integrate immersive software into classrooms.Capacity-building for 225 educators: Strengthening their ability to design interactive lessons that increase student engagement.Enhancing digital pedagogy: Encouraging innovative teaching methods that align with 21st-century learning goals.Supporting national education policy: Contributing to Bulgaria’s broader objectives of digital transformation in schools.By combining academic expertise and practical training, the programme aims to modernise teaching approaches, foster student interest, and position Bulgaria’s education system at the forefront of technology-enabled learning.

items.title: Operation “New Skills”
items.original_name: Квалификация и нови умения на служителите
items.org: Ministry of Labor and Social Policy
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Квалификация и нови умения на служителите
items.body:
Operation "New Skills" is a Bulgarian training programme designed to enhance the competencies of 53,200 employees. It focuses on digital skills and other employer-requested competencies, helping workers improve employability and adaptability in a rapidly evolving job market.

Operation "New Skills" aims to strengthen Bulgaria’s workforce by providing targeted upskilling and reskilling opportunities. Key aspects include:
Tailored training for employees: Addresses skills demanded by employers, including digital literacy, AI-related competencies, and other essential professional skills.Large-scale reach: Designed to benefit over 53,000 workers across multiple sectors.Enhancing employability: Prepares employees for changing job requirements, technological advancements, and new roles in the modern labour market.Promoting workforce adaptability: Helps employees adapt to digital transformation, automation, and AI integration in their workplaces.Supporting economic competitiveness: Contributes to a skilled, resilient, and flexible workforce, supporting Bulgaria’s economic growth and technological innovation.By combining practical, employer-driven training with a focus on digital and AI skills, Operation "New Skills" ensures that Bulgaria’s workforce remains competitive and future-ready in a rapidly evolving labour market.

items.title: Operation “Digital Skills”
items.org: Ministry of Labor and Social Policy
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Operation "Digital Skills" is a Bulgarian training programme aimed at improving employability by equipping unemployed and inactive individuals with essential digital skills. The initiative seeks to reduce digital divides and prepare participants for the AI-driven economy.

Operation "Digital Skills" is designed to address gaps in digital literacy and workforce readiness among vulnerable populations in Bulgaria. Key features include:
Targeted digital skills training: Focused on basic and intermediate digital competencies, including use of software tools, online collaboration platforms, and AI-related technologies.Improving employability: Equips participants with skills that are increasingly demanded by the digital and AI-driven labour market.Inclusive participation: Aims to reduce inequalities by providing access to digital education for unemployed or inactive persons, ensuring broader societal participation in digital transformation.Alignment with economic needs: Prepares learners to take advantage of emerging opportunities in technology, AI applications, and digital services.Support for lifelong learning: Encourages continued professional development and integration into AI and technology-focused employment sectors.By focusing on skills development and inclusion, Operation "Digital Skills" contributes to closing the digital divide in Bulgaria and ensures that a wider population is equipped for the challenges of the AI-driven economy.

items.title: National Competence Centre for Semiconductors and Microelectronics
items.original_name: Nacionalni centar kompetencija za poluvodiče i mikroelektroniku
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Nacionalni centar kompetencija za poluvodiče i mikroelektroniku
items.body:
The National Competence Centre acts as a one-stop-shop for research and development, prototyping, testing, and training in advanced semiconductor technologies, fostering innovation and skills development in a strategically important sector.

The National Competence Centre for Advanced Semiconductor Technologies is a strategic initiative aimed at boosting Europe’s and Croatia’s (or the respective country’s) capacity in semiconductors. It:
Provides integrated services in R&D, prototyping, testing, and training related to semiconductors.Serves as a hub for collaboration between academia, industry, and government in developing next-generation chip technologies.Offers specialised training programmes to develop a highly skilled workforce in semiconductor design, fabrication, and testing.Facilitates innovation and commercialisation of semiconductor-related research outputs.Supports the digital and green transitions by enabling access to cutting-edge microelectronics and semiconductor capabilities.By functioning as a centralised resource, the Centre accelerates the development of critical technologies, strengthens regional and national semiconductor ecosystems, and ensures long-term competitiveness in the global market.

items.title: NRRP Labour Market and Social Protection Component
items.original_name: Komponenta tržišta rada i socijalne zaštite NPOO-a
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Komponenta tržišta rada i socijalne zaštite NPOO-a
items.body:
The Ministry of Labour in Croatia offers a voucher scheme for digital skills improvement, including AI-related skills. The programme supports lifelong education, focusing on competencies needed for the green and digital transition.

This national voucher programme is a strategic initiative by the Croatian Ministry of Labour, Pension System, Family and Social Policy to boost the digital and green competencies of the workforce. It:
Provides vouchers to individuals to undertake training in digital skills, including AI and other advanced technologies.Prioritises lifelong learning and employability, helping citizens adapt to changing labour market demands.Conducts a comprehensive skills mapping exercise to identify digital and green skills gaps, informing training provision.Contributes to the development of a national skills catalogue to guide future workforce development and policy measures.Supports the green and digital transition by equipping workers with relevant skills needed in emerging sectors.Through this programme, the Ministry aims to expand access to training, promote inclusive participation, and ensure the Croatian workforce is prepared for future labour market needs in a digital and AI-driven economy.

items.title: International AI Olympiad
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
An international AI competition for high school students, launched in 2024 in Bulgaria, brings together young talent to develop AI models and solutions. The inaugural event attracted over 200 participants from around 40 countries, fostering innovation and early engagement in AI education.

This initiative provides a global platform for high school students to explore and develop artificial intelligence skills. Key elements include:
International participation: Over 200 students from approximately 40 countries competed in the first edition.AI-focused challenges: Teams developed and tested AI models and innovative solutions, gaining practical experience in programming, problem-solving, and data analysis.Skill development and talent cultivation: The competition encourages participants to enhance their technical skills, teamwork, and creative thinking in AI.Promoting AI education in Bulgaria: Demonstrates Bulgaria’s commitment to building a strong foundation for AI learning and fostering future AI talent.Networking and collaboration: Provides opportunities for students to interact with peers, educators, and industry professionals in the AI field.By combining competition, learning, and international exposure, the initiative inspires young innovators and contributes to global AI education while positioning Bulgaria as a hub for youth-focused AI activities.

items.title: Interface3
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Interface3 is a Belgian training centre that promotes digital inclusion, with a special focus on women. It offers comprehensive training programmes in ICT, including coding, digital tools, and technology careers, aiming to empower underrepresented groups and close the digital skills gap in the workforce.

Interface3 (Brussels) is a long-established non-profit training centre dedicated to fostering diversity and inclusion in the digital sector. Its programmes are designed to:
Equip women and underrepresented groups with ICT skillsTraining includes web development, coding, office software, digital marketing, and IT support.Support entry and progression into tech careersProvides career guidance, internships, and job placement support to help trainees enter the ICT workforce.Promote gender diversity in digital industriesWorks closely with employers, public bodies, and community organisations to bridge the gap between skills supply and labour market demand.
By combining technical training with career support, Interface3 empowers women and underrepresented groups to access sustainable careers in technology and contribute to a more inclusive digital economy in Belgium.

items.title: Innoviris’ Funding Programmes on STEM
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Innoviris, the public research and innovation institute of the Brussels-Capital Region, funds and supports initiatives to spark interest in science, technology, and AI among youth and other groups. Programmes include coding training, interdisciplinary academies combining technology and art, and robotics competitions that cultivate digital and STEM skills.

As the regional research and innovation funding agency, Innoviris plays a key role in promoting STEM, digital skills, and AI awareness in the Brussels-Capital Region. It backs initiatives aimed at young people and underrepresented groups to encourage participation in technology, science, and innovation.
Examples include:
Capital Digital – provides coding training to children and young adults in the Brussels Canal Zone to build digital literacy and programming skills.S+T+ARTS Academy – fosters creativity at the intersection of science, technology, AI, and art, encouraging innovative thinking in areas such as robotics, digital media, and smart cities.Robotics competitions (VEX Benelux Championship) – engages participants aged 8 to 18 in hands-on robotics projects, cultivating teamwork, problem-solving, and leadership skills.By combining education, innovation, and practical experience, Innoviris helps inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, and AI professionals, ensuring that Brussels develops a skilled, creative, and future-ready workforce.

items.title: InnoVET
items.org: Flemish Ministry of Education and Training
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
InnoVET is a programme supporting innovation in vocational education and training (VET). It equips learners with digital and technological skills aligned with labour market needs and fosters closer collaboration between education providers and industry.

InnoVET focuses on transforming vocational education and training to meet the challenges of the digital economy. It aims to ensure that VET students acquire the skills demanded by industries, particularly digital and technology-related competencies, helping create a skilled workforce ready for emerging sectors.
Key elements of InnoVET include:
Innovation in VET curricula – integrating digital tools and methods into teaching and learning.Bridging education and labour market – supporting projects that link schools, training centres, and employers to better match skills supply with demand.Enhancing digital and technological skills – equipping learners with future-ready competencies, including those relevant to AI and advanced technologies.Supporting pilot and collaborative projects – to test and scale innovative practices in VET across regions and sectors.By fostering collaboration between education providers, employers, and policymakers, InnoVET helps strengthen vocational training systems, ensuring that learners are prepared for the evolving needs of the digital and AI-driven economy.

items.title: INSAIT Research Programmes
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The INSAIT Research Programmes at Sofia University advance research in computer science and AI, hosting over 20 international researchers. They provide competitive internships for students worldwide and focus on areas such as AI, machine learning, robotics, and computer vision.

The INSAIT Research Programmes are designed to foster cutting-edge research and global collaboration in artificial intelligence and computer science. Key aspects include:
International research community: Hosting more than 20 researchers from around the world, the programmes create a diverse and collaborative research environment.Advanced AI research: Focuses on machine learning, robotics, computer vision, and other emerging AI technologies.Student opportunities: Offers competitive internships for students globally, providing hands-on experience in innovative projects.Global collaboration and innovation: Encourages partnerships with international institutions, industry, and academia to advance research and practical AI applications.Talent development: Prepares the next generation of AI researchers and practitioners, strengthening Bulgaria’s position in the global AI research landscape.By combining high-level research, international cooperation, and student engagement, the INSAIT Research Programmes contribute to advancing AI knowledge and innovation while building a skilled, globally connected talent pool.

items.title: INSAIT Explorer Programme
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The INSAIT Explorer Programme is a fellowship initiative by INSAIT at Sofia University targeting talented high school students. It combines a four-year Bachelor’s degree with research opportunities in AI, machine learning, robotics, and quantum computing, aiming to cultivate Bulgaria’s top tech talent.

The INSAIT Explorer Programme is designed to nurture exceptional students in computer science and AI through a unique integration of academic study and hands-on research. Key features include:
Bachelor’s degree integration: Students complete a four-year undergraduate programme at Sofia University while participating in research at INSAIT.Advanced AI curriculum: Covers machine learning, robotics, quantum computing, and other emerging technologies.Research opportunities: Fellows work alongside researchers on cutting-edge AI projects, gaining practical skills and experience.Industry-supported: Funded through donations and partnerships with private sector companies, ensuring exposure to real-world applications.Talent cultivation: The programme aims to develop future leaders in AI and technology in Bulgaria, bridging the gap between education, research, and industry.By combining rigorous academic study with applied research, the INSAIT Explorer Programme creates a pipeline of highly skilled AI professionals, positioning Bulgaria as a competitive player in the global AI and technology ecosystem.

items.title: HRDA AI courses
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Human Resource Development Authority of Cyprus (HRDA) offers a range of training courses related to artificial intelligence, aimed at equipping the Cypriot workforce with the skills needed for a technology-driven economy.

The HRDA is Cyprus’s national agency responsible for workforce training and development. Through its accredited training providers, it:
Designs and funds courses that include AI-related topics, such as machine learning, data analytics, robotics, and automation.Targets employers, employees, jobseekers and unemployed individuals, enabling them to upgrade or reskill in emerging digital technologies.Provides financial incentives and subsidies to organisations that invest in training staff in AI and other digital skills.Contributes to the national digital transformation strategy by strengthening AI competencies across key economic sectors.By offering these AI-related training opportunities, the HRDA plays a pivotal role in preparing Cyprus’s workforce for future labour market demands and supporting the adoption of innovative technologies.

items.title: GATE’s Internship Programme
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The GATE Centre of Excellence internship programme offers hands-on experience in Big Data and AI for students and young professionals. Interns work on interdisciplinary research projects, developing skills in data management, analytics, and visualisation under the guidance of experienced researchers.

The internship programme at GATE Centre of Excellence is designed to bridge the gap between academic knowledge and practical industry experience in Big Data and AI. Key features include:
Practical project-based learning: Interns participate in real-world projects in data analytics, AI applications, and visualisation techniques.Mentorship from experts: Guidance is provided by experienced researchers from academia and industry to enhance professional development.Collaboration across sectors: The programme fosters interaction between government, industry, and academic institutions, enabling exposure to multidisciplinary perspectives.Skill development: Interns gain competencies in data management, machine learning, AI model implementation, and analytical tools.Career preparation: By providing applied experience and networking opportunities, the programme prepares participants for advanced careers in AI, data science, and technology sectors.Through this initiative, the GATE Centre of Excellence strengthens Bulgaria’s AI and Big Data talent pipeline, supporting both research innovation and workforce readiness in emerging technologies.

items.title: GATE Master’s Programme “Big Data Technologies”
items.org: GATE Institute and Sofia University's Faculty of Mathematics and Informatics
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This advanced Master’s programme, jointly offered by GATE Institute and Sofia University’s Faculty of Mathematics and Informatics, provides specialised training in Big Data and AI applications. Launched in the 2023–2024 academic year, it prepares graduates for professional roles in data science and AI.

The programme is designed to equip students with highly specialised knowledge and skills in artificial intelligence, data analytics, and Big Data technologies. Key features include:
Collaboration between academia and research institutes: The programme combines the expertise of Sofia University and GATE Institute.Comprehensive AI and Big Data curriculum: Students gain theoretical knowledge and practical experience in machine learning, data processing, and AI applications.Industry-relevant training: Focused on professional readiness, the programme prepares graduates for careers in data science, AI development, and related sectors.Hands-on learning opportunities: Includes projects, case studies, and potential internships to bridge academic knowledge with real-world applications.Launch and reach: Initiated in the 2023–2024 academic year, it contributes to Bulgaria’s goal of developing a skilled workforce in AI and data-driven technologies.Through this programme, students gain advanced competencies that make them competitive in the rapidly evolving AI and data industries, supporting Bulgaria’s national strategy to strengthen its digital and AI talent pool.

items.title: Croatian Association for Artificial Intelligence (CroAI)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
CroAI is a business community initiative in Croatia bringing together over 300 members, including AI enterprises, start-ups, universities, and enthusiasts. It offers introductory AI courses and facilitates connections between leading companies and start-ups in the AI ecosystem.

CroAI serves as a central hub for the Croatian AI community, promoting knowledge sharing, networking, and collaboration. Key features include:
Diverse membership: Comprises AI companies, start-ups, scale-ups, academic institutions, and enthusiasts, fostering cross-sector collaboration.Educational activities: Offers free introductory AI courses, workshops, and seminars to develop foundational skills among participants.Networking and collaboration: Connects leading enterprises with start-ups, promoting partnerships, mentorship, and innovation in AI.Community-building: Organizes events and forums to strengthen the AI ecosystem in Croatia and encourage knowledge exchange.Support for AI growth: By linking research, industry, and emerging start-ups, CroAI helps accelerate AI adoption and development in the country.Through these activities, CroAI nurtures talent, fosters innovation, and consolidates Croatia’s AI ecosystem, creating opportunities for collaboration, skill-building, and AI-driven economic growth.

items.title: Adult Learning Platform
items.org: Ministry of Labor and Social Policy
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This comprehensive digital platform in Bulgaria aims to democratise access to digital and AI skills training. It aims to provide digital clubs and tailored support for disadvantaged groups, along with certification pathways to validate skills and enhance career opportunities in the digital sector.

The platform is designed to ensure inclusive participation in Bulgaria’s digital transformation. Key features include:
Digital clubs and learning hubs: Offer interactive training sessions, workshops, and collaborative learning opportunities for individuals of all backgrounds.Support for disadvantaged groups: Tailored programmes ensure equal access to AI and digital skills, helping to reduce social and digital inequalities.Certification pathways: Participants can obtain formal recognition of their acquired skills, enhancing employability and career progression in technology-driven industries.Broad skill coverage: Training encompasses digital literacy, AI tools, data skills, and other emerging technologies, providing a strong foundation for workforce readiness.Empowerment and career development: By equipping learners with validated competencies, the initiative helps them advance professionally and participate fully in the digital economy.Through this initiative, Bulgaria promotes equitable access to AI and digital education, supporting both individual empowerment and the nation’s overall digital competitiveness.

items.title: Adult Education Act Implementation Programme
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Ministry of Science and Education runs a programme to encourage unemployed persons’ inclusion in the labour market, with a strong focus on digital skills development and lifelong learning, as part of its active employment policy measures.

This national programme, implemented by Croatia’s Ministry of Science and Education, aims to:
Support unemployed persons in acquiring new digital and transversal skills to increase their employability.Provide lifelong learning opportunities, including training in AI-related and other emerging digital competencies.Strengthen the connection between education and labour market needs through tailored upskilling and reskilling activities.Complement other active employment policies by offering certified courses, career guidance, and links to employers.Contribute to the country’s digital transformation and green transition by addressing current and future skills gaps.Through these measures, the programme helps ensure a more inclusive labour market, empowering unemployed people to participate in the digital economy and AI-driven sectors.

items.title: AI Programmer Vocational Education
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
AI Programmer Vocational Education is a specialised vocational training programme that integrates the “Programmer with AI” profession into high school curricula. In the 2023/2024 academic year, it engaged 580 students across 13 schools, equipping them with practical AI programming skills and preparing them for careers in AI and technology.

The AI Programmer Vocational Education programme in Bulgaria addresses the growing need for AI-skilled professionals by introducing vocational education focused on AI development at the high school level. Key aspects include:
Integration into high school curricula: The programme creates a structured pathway for students to become certified AI programmers.Practical skills development: Students gain hands-on experience in AI programming, machine learning, and related digital technologies.Broad reach: During the 2023/2024 academic year, the programme engaged 580 students across 13 schools, demonstrating its scalability and impact.Career preparation: Equips students with the competencies needed to pursue AI development careers or further studies in technology and computer science.Future-focused education: Supports Bulgaria’s efforts to strengthen the national AI workforce and prepare youth for a digital economy.By embedding AI vocational training in secondary education, the initiative contributes to closing the AI skills gap, fostering early professional development, and creating sustainable pathways into the tech industry for Bulgarian students.

items.title: AI Guidelines for Education System
items.original_name: Изкуственият интелект влиза в училище - Труд
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.document_name: Изкуственият интелект влиза в училище - Труд
items.body:
The Ministry of Education and Science of Bulgaria has released guidelines for the use of AI in schools. These guidelines are designed to help teachers, school administrators, and students integrate AI ethically and effectively into educational processes and programmes.

The initiative by Bulgaria’s Ministry of Education and Science introduces a structured framework for the responsible integration of AI in schools. It aims to:
Support teachers and school leaders in understanding how AI tools can enhance teaching and learning.Ensure the ethical and safe use of AI, including privacy, security, and fairness considerations.Provide practical recommendations for incorporating AI-based educational resources, platforms, and tools into curricula.Equip students with basic knowledge about AI and its implications to build digital literacy and critical thinking skills.The guidelines act as both a policy and practical tool, encouraging schools to experiment with innovative technologies while safeguarding ethical standards and data protection. Over time, they are expected to evolve alongside advances in AI and Bulgaria’s broader digital education strategy.

items.title: e-cl@sses
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
e-cl@sses is a Walloon initiative providing digital education resources for teachers and students. It offers interactive lessons, educational content, and tools for primary and secondary education, supporting digital literacy and the integration of AI in learning.

The e-cl@sses initiative, launched by the Region of Wallonia, is designed to enhance digital education across primary and secondary schools. The programme provides a comprehensive platform of digital resources, including interactive lessons, educational content, and tools that help both teachers and students effectively use digital technologies in the classroom.
Key features include:
Digital literacy promotion – equipping students with essential skills for the digital economy.Support for modern teaching methods – enabling teachers to integrate digital tools and interactive content into their lessons.AI-focused research – in 2023, e-cl@sses conducted a study on the impact of AI in education, exploring opportunities and challenges for AI integration in teaching and learning.Extensive resources for primary and secondary education, providing tailored content that aligns with curricular objectives.Through training, educational resources, and research, e-cl@sses helps Wallonia’s education system adapt to digital transformation and prepare students for future AI-driven workplaces, ensuring that both teachers and students can leverage technology effectively and responsibly.

items.title: Wallenberg AI, Autonomous Systems and Software Program
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Wallenberg AI, Autonomous Systems and Software Program (WASP) is Sweden’s largest research programme, focusing on artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, and software. It supports strategically motivated basic research, education, and international faculty recruitment to establish Sweden as a global leader in these areas.

The Wallenberg AI, Autonomous Systems and Software Program (WASP) is the largest individual research programme ever in Sweden, funded by the Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation. Its main objective is to strengthen Sweden’s competitiveness and international position in the fields of artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, and advanced software engineering.
The programme’s AI tracks emphasise machine learning, explainable AI (MLX), and the mathematical foundations of AI, thereby fostering cutting-edge research at the intersection of science, technology, and society.
Key elements include:
