A major research programme supporting strategically important AI topics.A national graduate school to educate a new generation of AI researchers and engineers.International faculty recruitment to bring leading global experts to Sweden.Research arenas and university partnerships to promote collaboration and knowledge transfer.Communication, events, and networking to build an active, integrated research community.Supported by Swedish industry and implemented in collaboration with five major universities, WASP aims to create an environment where basic and applied research, talent development, and innovation can thrive together. The ultimate goal is to advance Sweden into a globally recognised and leading position in AI, autonomous systems, and software development.

items.title: Start your AI journey
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
“Start Your AI Journey” is a Swedish initiative designed to help SMEs adopt artificial intelligence. Managed by Vinnova, it funded 51 small projects with grants of around EUR 43,000 (SEK 500,000) each to support companies in exploring and starting their AI transformation.

The “Start Your AI Journey” initiative, launched by Vinnova in 2019, was created to accelerate the adoption of AI by small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Sweden. Recognising that many SMEs lack the initial knowledge, resources, or confidence to integrate AI into their operations, the programme provided targeted financial and advisory support to kickstart AI initiatives at the company level.
Key features include:
Focus on SMEs – supporting companies at the very beginning of their AI adoption journey.51 projects funded, each receiving approximately EUR 43,000 (SEK 500,000) to explore AI solutions.Support for experimentation – funding early-stage projects to identify AI opportunities, test proofs of concept, or build pilot models.Practical impact – enabling SMEs to increase their digital maturity, improve competitiveness, and prepare for more advanced AI integration in the future.By lowering the entry barrier to AI adoption, the initiative helped SMEs gain first-hand experience with AI technologies, paving the way for broader digitalisation and innovation in Sweden’s small-business sector.

items.title: Schoolpackage AI
items.org: Ministry of Education, Science and Research
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Schoolpackage AI is an Austrian government initiative aimed at enhancing AI knowledge in primary and secondary education. It targets both teachers and students, promoting the use of AI tools, including generative AI, through pilot programmes in selected schools.

The Schoolpackage AI programme, led by the Austrian Federal Ministry of Education, Science and Research (BMBWF), seeks to integrate artificial intelligence into the educational system. Its objective is to build foundational AI literacy among students while equipping teachers with the knowledge and tools to incorporate AI in their teaching.
Key elements include:
Pilot programmes in selected schools, which are scientifically monitored to evaluate effectiveness and outcomes.Use of AI tools in teaching, including generative AI applications, to enhance learning experiences.Teacher training and support, ensuring educators are prepared to guide students in AI-related subjects.Research on AI in education, promoting evidence-based strategies for integrating AI technologies into curricula.The initiative aims to prepare students for a digital future, fostering AI literacy and understanding from an early age. By combining hands-on experience, teacher training, and research, Schoolpackage AI supports Austria’s goal of creating a digitally competent and AI-aware generation.

items.title: Research and innovation bill
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
In 2024, Sweden adopted its largest-ever research and innovation bill, allocating substantial funding to strengthen excellent research, higher education, research infrastructure, and groundbreaking technologies (including AI).

The Swedish Government has presented the Research and Innovation Bill 2024, which represents the largest investment in research and innovation in the country’s history. The bill aims to ensure that Sweden remains a leading knowledge nation and a hub for innovation and advanced technologies.
Key elements include:
Funding for excellent research – significantly increased and long-term support for world-class research projects.Increased and competitive funding for higher education institutions – to strengthen their research capabilities and improve international competitiveness.Enhanced research infrastructure – investments in cutting-edge laboratories, data facilities, and national research resources.Investments in groundbreaking technologies – support for emerging and transformative technologies, such as artificial intelligence, quantum technologies, and advanced life sciences.Objectives:
Consolidate Sweden’s position as a global leader in science, innovation, and technology.Provide sustainable and competitive funding for universities and research institutes.Facilitate the development of high-impact research infrastructures.Support breakthrough technologies that address societal and environmental challenges.This new bill underscores the Swedish Government’s commitment to research excellence and to fostering an environment where cutting-edge innovation – including in AI – can thrive.

items.title: National Competition for AI
items.org: Ministry for Innovation, Mobility and Infrastructure
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Austrian National Competition for AI is a programme for students aged 14 to 19, encouraging them to explore and develop skills in artificial intelligence. The competition fosters young talent and innovation in AI, and its third edition was held in 2023.

The Austrian National Competition for AI, organised by the Bundesministerium für Wirtschaft und KI (BWKI), aims to inspire and engage the next generation of AI professionals. It provides students with opportunities to work on AI projects, solve problems, and apply theoretical knowledge in practical ways.
Key features include:
Target group: students aged 14–19 with an interest in AI and digital technologies.Practical AI experience: participants develop projects or prototypes to demonstrate their skills and creativity.Innovation and talent development: the competition encourages students to experiment, innovate, and pursue further studies or careers in AI.National recognition: the competition highlights exceptional young talent and contributes to building Austria’s future AI workforce.Held for the third time in 2023, the initiative helps create early exposure to AI, fostering curiosity, critical thinking, and technical skills among Austria’s youth, and supporting the country’s broader goal of developing a digitally skilled population ready for AI-driven industries.

items.title: European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs)
items.org: Vinnova and the Swedish Agency for Economic and Regional Growth
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Sweden has co-financed four European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs) approved by the European Commission and continues to support five additional hubs through the EC’s “Seal of Excellence”. The creation and operation of these hubs is a joint effort between Vinnova (the Swedish Innovation Agency) and Tillväxtverket (the Swedish Agency for Economic and Regional Growth).

Sweden is actively strengthening its digital and AI ecosystem through European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs). These hubs serve as one-stop shops helping companies—particularly SMEs and public organisations—access expertise, test technologies, and scale digital solutions, including artificial intelligence.
Key aspects of the Swedish approach include:
Co-financing four EDIHs approved by the European Commission, ensuring they have the necessary resources to offer cutting-edge services.Maintaining five additional hubs with the EC “Seal of Excellence”, showing Sweden’s commitment to a larger innovation network beyond the formally funded hubs.Joint coordination by Vinnova and Tillväxtverket, combining national innovation policy with regional growth support to make hubs accessible throughout the country.These hubs provide:
Testing and experimentation environments for digital and AI solutions.Access to advanced technologies and training to boost digital maturity.Support for financing and networking to accelerate innovation in SMEs.Through this co-financing and organisational support, Sweden is building a comprehensive innovation hub infrastructure, enabling companies and public institutions to adopt AI and digital technologies faster and more effectively while fostering regional economic development.

items.title: Edge Learning Lab of AI Sweden
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Sweden offers a broad network of test facilities for AI systems and applications, including dedicated environments specifically built for AI. One example is the Edge Learning Lab at AI Sweden, which allows researchers to explore decentralised and edge learning.

Sweden has developed an extensive ecosystem of test facilities that enable researchers, companies, and public organisations to develop, test, and validate AI technologies in real or simulated environments. These facilities cover a wide range of sectors and technology areas, providing infrastructure and expertise for experimentation, prototyping, and scaling AI solutions.
A prominent example is the Edge Learning Lab at AI Sweden. This facility is designed as a cutting-edge testing environment where researchers and innovators can explore the possibilities and limitations of decentralised and edge learning, a critical area for next-generation AI applications. By enabling experimentation at the edge rather than in centralised systems, it supports innovation in areas such as autonomous vehicles, smart cities, and IoT-based services.
Key features of Sweden’s AI test-facility ecosystem include:
Specialised environments for AI testing, including decentralised and edge AI.Support for collaboration between researchers, industry, and the public sector.Infrastructure for experimentation and scaling, from prototypes to full-scale systems.Promotion of innovation through real-world testing conditions and knowledge sharing.By providing these facilities, Sweden is strengthening its position as a hub for AI development and experimentation, ensuring that new AI systems and applications can be safely, efficiently, and ethically tested before large-scale deployment.

items.title: DigiSkills Platform
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
DigiSkills Belgium is a national platform that promotes reskilling and upskilling in AI and digital competencies. It connects learners with training opportunities across sectors to help close skill gaps and enhance employability in AI-driven industries.

DigiSkills Belgium is a comprehensive initiative aimed at strengthening the digital and AI skills of the Belgian workforce. The platform provides access to a wide range of training programmes, courses, and resources to support learners, employees, and professionals in adapting to the increasing digitalisation of workplaces.
Key features include:
Reskilling and upskilling opportunities in artificial intelligence, data analytics, and other digital technologies.Sector-wide reach, connecting learners with training options across multiple industries.Resources to address skill gaps, helping individuals stay competitive in AI-driven job markets.Enhanced employability, enabling participants to acquire practical knowledge and experience with AI tools and applications.By providing targeted learning pathways and facilitating access to educational resources, DigiSkills Belgium supports a future-ready workforce, capable of navigating and contributing to Belgium’s growing AI and digital economy.

items.title: AI-specific research and innovation programme administered by Vinnova, Sweden’s innovation agency
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Since 2009, Vinnova—Sweden’s innovation agency—has supported over 800 AI-related projects. Its current programme, “Advanced digitalisation – future solutions in Swedish industry”, includes funding calls for start-ups and SMEs with AI-specific themes, such as “AI from research to innovation”, “AI in the service of the climate” and “AI for Advanced Digitalization”. Most of the funding has gone to SMEs as providers or users of AI solutions.

Vinnova, Sweden’s government agency for innovation, plays a central role in financing AI-related research, innovation, and adoption across the country. Since 2009, it has administered more than 800 projects in artificial intelligence, ranging from basic research to applied solutions across industry and society.
Since 2019, much of this work has been organised under the “Advanced digitalisation – future solutions in Swedish industry” programme. This initiative seeks to accelerate Sweden’s digital and AI transformation by funding projects that bridge the gap between research and innovation, especially in the industrial sector.
Key features of the programme include:
Targeted funding calls with AI-specific themes, such as:“AI – from research to innovation”“AI in the service of the climate”“AI for Advanced Digitalization”Strong support for SMEs, both as providers and adopters of AI solutions.Large-scale investments – approximately SEK 1.3 billion of SEK 1.5 billion since 2019 directed to SMEs.Through these initiatives, Vinnova is fostering a vibrant AI ecosystem where start-ups, SMEs, academia, and larger companies can collaborate, innovate, and scale solutions. The focus on sustainability, climate-friendly applications, and industry-driven innovation helps ensure that AI contributes to Sweden’s long-term competitiveness and societal benefit.

items.title: AI Radar
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
AI Radar is an Austrian project offering reskilling and upskilling programmes in AI for the tourism sector, mainly through online webinars and workshops. It tracks AI innovations, recognises trends, and helps tourism professionals strengthen their skills and develop prototypes.

The AI Radar initiative, coordinated by Austria Tourism, is designed to prepare the tourism sector for the opportunities and challenges of artificial intelligence. It provides structured training, awareness, and networking opportunities to help tourism businesses and professionals understand and use AI technologies effectively.
Key objectives include:
Monitoring AI innovations and identifying their potential applications in tourism.Recognising trends and experimenting with new technologies to anticipate future developments.Strengthening skills and capacities of tourism professionals through regular (online) webinars and workshops.Developing prototypes and promoting networking to encourage collaboration between businesses, experts, and innovators.By combining training with trend analysis and prototype development, AI Radar helps Austria’s tourism industry to adopt AI-based solutions more quickly and confidently. The programme thus contributes to future-proofing the sector, improving competitiveness, and enhancing the visitor experience through smarter, more efficient, and innovative services.

items.title: #BeDigitalTogether
items.org: Public Service for Economy, SMEs, Self-Employed and Energy
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Belgium’s #BeDigitalTogether programme promotes inclusion and diversity in the digital sector, including AI. It seeks to reduce barriers for underrepresented groups and ensure equitable access to opportunities in technology careers.

The #BeDigitalTogether initiative in Belgium focuses on fostering a more diverse and inclusive digital workforce, with a particular emphasis on artificial intelligence and related technologies. By targeting underrepresented groups, the programme aims to create equal opportunities for participation, learning, and career advancement in the tech sector.
Key objectives include:
Reducing barriers to entry for underrepresented populations in the digital and AI workforce.Promoting equitable access to training, mentorship, and employment opportunities.Raising awareness about the importance of diversity in technology and AI development.Supporting a sustainable and inclusive tech ecosystem, which leverages diverse perspectives for innovation.Through workshops, outreach, and networking initiatives, #BeDigitalTogether helps build a more inclusive digital landscape in Belgium, ensuring that AI and other emerging technologies benefit from a broader range of skills, experiences, and viewpoints.

items.title: Spain Neurotech
items.org: Ministry of Science, Innovation and Universities.
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Spain has signed an agreement to create the National Center for Neurotechnology (Spain Neurotech) on the campus of the Autonomous University of Madrid. The centre will focus on neuroscience, brain science, and artificial intelligence, acting as a national hub for research and innovation in these fields.

The National Center for Neurotechnology – Spain Neurotech is a new flagship initiative led by the Ministry of Science, Innovation and Universities (Ministerio de Ciencia, Innovación y Universidades). Located at the Autonomous University of Madrid, the centre will combine cutting-edge research in neuroscience, brain science, and AI to develop novel technologies, treatments, and scientific breakthroughs.
Key objectives include:
Advance interdisciplinary research by integrating neuroscience, AI, and brain science.Develop innovative tools and applications for health, cognition, and human–machine interaction.Strengthen Spain’s position as a European leader in neurotechnology and AI.Foster collaboration between academia, industry, and international research centres.The signing of the agreement marks the formal establishment of the centre, which will serve as a national reference point for innovation in neurotechnology. It aligns with Spain’s broader strategy to invest in emerging technologies and strengthen the connection between science and industry.
Once operational, Spain Neurotech is expected to contribute to medical breakthroughs, new AI models inspired by the brain, and the training of highly skilled researchers in this rapidly evolving field.

items.title: RETECH IA
items.org: Ministry of Science, Innovation and Universities
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Spain’s Territorial Networks of Technological Specialisation (RETECH) IA bring together 13 flagship projects to promote artificial intelligence across Spanish regions. The initiative strengthens interregional cooperation and supports the development and deployment of AI solutions.

The RETECH IA programme is part of Spain’s broader Territorial Networks of Technological Specialisation (RETECH) framework, coordinated by the Government of Spain (Gobierno de España). It is designed to connect regions, institutions, and companies to develop and implement artificial intelligence solutions with national and European impact.
Key aspects include:
13 flagship projects (see Box 1) covering different domains and use cases of AI, from research to applied innovation.Interregional cooperation – building synergies between Spain’s autonomous communities and avoiding duplication of efforts.Public–private collaboration – involving technology centres, companies, universities, and public administrations.Support for scaling and deployment – helping AI projects move from pilots to full-scale implementation.The main objectives of RETECH IA are to:
Strengthen Spain’s AI capabilities at a territorial level.Encourage shared infrastructures, data spaces, and standards.Facilitate cross-regional knowledge transfer and innovation.Align national efforts with the EU’s Digital Europe Programme and other European initiatives.By aggregating resources and expertise across regions, RETECH IA accelerates the adoption of AI technologies and contributes to Spain’s leadership in the European digital economy.

items.title: Initiatives to help start-ups and/or scale-ups access financing
items.original_name: Iniciativas para ayudar a las start-ups y/o scale-ups a acceder a financiación
items.org: Ministry of Science, Innovation and Universities
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Iniciativas para ayudar a las start-ups y/o scale-ups a acceder a financiación
items.body:
Spain supports innovation and technology adoption—including AI—through a range of national funding programmes. These include large-scale funds such as Next Tech Fund, FOCO, INNVIERTE, Fond-ICO Global, ENISA participatory loans, and Women’s Digital Entrepreneurs, providing billions of euros in financing for start-ups, scale-ups, and SMEs.

Spain has established multiple public funding instruments to stimulate innovation across all technological sectors, including artificial intelligence. These initiatives are designed to provide capital, co-investment, and participatory financing to companies at different stages of development, from early-stage start-ups to growth-focused SMEs.
Key programmes include:
Next Tech Fund – €4 billion to support early-stage and high-tech companies, including AI ventures.Co-investment Fund (FOCO) – €2 billion for co-investment in innovative companies, leveraging private sector funding.INNVIERTE programme – supports the growth of innovative enterprises through venture capital and seed investments.Fond-ICO Global – €4.5 billion in financial instruments to back technology-driven projects.ENISA participatory loans – targeted loans for SMEs and start-ups to foster innovation and competitiveness.Women’s Digital Entrepreneurs – €51 million dedicated to supporting female-led digital and technology initiatives.These initiatives aim to:
Accelerate digital and technological transformation, including AI adoption.Enhance access to capital for innovative projects and companies.Promote gender equality in entrepreneurship, particularly in the digital sector.Foster public–private collaboration, combining government support with private investment.Together, these funding instruments create a robust innovation ecosystem, encouraging technological advancement and the integration of AI across Spanish industry and society.

items.title: Initiatives to help SMEs adopt digital or novel technologies including AI
items.original_name: Iniciativas para ayudar a las pymes a adoptar tecnologías digitales o innovadoras, incluida la inteligencia artificial
items.org: Ministry of Science, Innovation and Universities
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Iniciativas para ayudar a las pymes a adoptar tecnologías digitales o innovadoras, incluida la inteligencia artificial
items.body:
Spain offers several national digitalisation support programmes for companies, including SMEs. Key initiatives include Digital Kit, Kit Consulting, Activa Startups, and Generación Digital Pymes, which provide guidance, training, and funding to promote digital transformation and innovation. While not exclusive to AI, these programmes also support AI adoption.

Spain has developed a range of programmes to help companies adopt digital technologies and accelerate their innovation capabilities. These initiatives target different aspects of digital transformation, from training and advisory services to fostering collaboration between start-ups and established companies.
Key programmes include:
Digital Kit & Kit Consulting – provide SMEs with consultancy, guidance, and support for implementing digital tools and strategies.Activa Startups – promotes collaboration between innovative start-ups and established companies to drive technology transfer and innovation.Generación Digital Pymes – equips SME employees with the skills, knowledge, and tools needed to implement digital transformation within their organisations.Objectives of these programmes are to:
Support digitalisation and innovation across SMEs and other companies.Encourage collaboration between start-ups and established companies with growth potential.Develop digital skills among employees to ensure effective technology adoption.Promote the growth of “new generation” companies, enhancing competitiveness and productivity.Although these initiatives are technology-agnostic, they include support for AI adoption, making it challenging to isolate AI-specific funding. Nevertheless, they provide an essential ecosystem for SMEs and companies to experiment with and integrate AI technologies alongside other digital solutions.

items.title: Financing of cooperative research plans in the area of ​​AI developed by interdisciplinary research groups
items.original_name: Redes sectoriales de excelencia en Inteligencia Artificial
items.org: Ministry of Science, Innovation and Universities
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Redes sectoriales de excelencia en Inteligencia Artificial
items.body:
Spain is creating 15 sectorial networks of excellence to strengthen research and innovation in artificial intelligence. These networks cover areas such as theoretical challenges, cognition, advanced algorithms, physics, human–computer interaction, social and environmental challenges, quantum, and new AI applications. The selection of participating organisations is being finalised.

The Ministry of Science, Innovation and Universities (Ministerio de Ciencia, Innovación y Universidades) is establishing 15 sectorial networks of excellence as part of its national strategy to boost artificial intelligence research and development.
Each network focuses on a specific area of AI to foster collaboration between research institutions, universities, and industry:
AI and theoretical challengesAI and cognitionAI and advanced algorithmsAI and physicsAI and human–computer interactionAI and social challengesAI and environmental challengesAI and quantumNew applications for AIThe main objectives are to:
Strengthen Spain’s research capacity in critical AI domains.Encourage knowledge exchange between academia, industry, and public institutions.Promote excellence and international competitiveness of Spanish AI research.Create a coordinated national AI research ecosystem integrated with European initiatives.At the time of writing, the selection process for the participating institutions was still underway. Once launched, these networks are expected to become national reference points for AI research and innovation, driving progress in science, technology, and practical applications.

items.title: AI4ES (Network of Excellence in AI)
items.original_name: Red de excelencia en tecnologías habilitadoras basadas en el dato
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Red de excelencia en tecnologías habilitadoras basadas en el dato
items.body:
AI4ES is a Spanish network of excellence created to strengthen the country’s data- and AI-based economy. It brings together four leading technological centres to transfer AI capabilities, results, and technologies to industry.

The AI4ES Network of Excellence aims to aggregate and harmonise Spain’s capacities, infrastructures, and R&D activities in artificial intelligence and data analytics. By uniting leading technological centres, it fosters collaboration and accelerates the translation of research into real-world applications.
The network is coordinated by the Instituto Tecnológico de Informática (ITI) and includes:
Fundación CTIC Centro TecnológicoEurecatTecnaliaTogether, these centres mobilise nearly 300 professionals with research and technical expertise across multiple sectors, providing a strong foundation for multi-sector R&D projects in AI and data analytics.
Key objectives of AI4ES include:
Boost Spain’s data- and AI-based economy by facilitating knowledge and technology transfer to the productive fabric.
Strengthen national infrastructures and capacities in AI and data analytics.
Promote collaboration between research centres and industry, enabling innovative products and services.
Support the development of advanced digital skills and the uptake of AI across sectors.
Through this initiative, Spain positions itself to expand its AI ecosystem, create synergies between research and industry, and enhance competitiveness in Europe’s digital economy

items.title: The National AI Policy
items.org: Ministry of ICT and Innovation, Rwanda Utilities Regulatory Authority
items.category: National – Strategy
items.body:
The Rwanda AI policy aims to achieve the following national objectives:
• Positioning Rwanda as Africa's AI Lab and Responsible AI Champion
• Building 21st Century Skills and AI Literacy
• Creating an Open, Secure, Trusted Data Ecosystem as an Enabler of the AI Revolution
• Driving Public Sector Transformation to Fuel AI Adoption
• Accelerating Responsible AI Adoption in the Private Sector

The vision of the strategy is to become a global center for AI research and innovation. The mission is to leverage AI to power economic growth, improve quality of life and position Rwanda as a global innovator for responsible and inclusive AI.
Six priority policy areas have been identified to accelerate the responsible development and deployment of AI across the nation. These priority areas are categorised as enablers, accelerators or safeguards. 
Priority areas categorised as enablers are 1) 21st century skills and high AI literacy, and 2) reliable infrastructure and compute capacity, and 3) robust strategy. Priority areas categorised as accelerators are 1) trustworthy AI adoption in the public sector, and 2) widely beneficial AI adoption in the private sector. The priority area categorised as safeguard is practical ethical guidelines.
The National AI Policy includes the recommendation to establish a Responsible AI Office (RAI Office) during the first year of this policy, housed within MINICT. The RAI Office will have the coordinating responsibility of driving the AI policy Implementation Plan. The RAI Office is to be given the mandate to implement the National AI Policy by coordinating stakeholders across institutions and championing the responsible development and deployment of AI across the Rwandan public and private sectors. 
Beyond domestic engagement, the RAI Office may participate in global AI governance efforts, e.g. by the OECD/Global Partnership on AI (GPAI), ITU, and UNESCO. Besides, the RAI Office will be tasked with the monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of the policy, the integration of the implementation plan in regional-level policies and actors, as well as with leading communications around the National AI Policy. Rwanda has a momentous opportunity to leverage advancements in AI to achieve national objectives outlined in Vision 2050. By launching the Responsible AI Office, coordinating key actors and driving action, MINICT accelerates AI adoption in Rwanda to achieve objectives linked to sustainable and inclusive development and capacity building in Rwanda.

items.title: Strategic materials of the Ministry of Investment, Regional Development and Informatisation of the Slovak Republic (MIRRI)
items.original_name: Ministerstvo investícií, regionálneho rozvoja a informatizácie SR
items.org: Ministry of Investment, Regional Development and Informatisation
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Ministerstvo investícií, regionálneho rozvoja a informatizácie SR
items.body:
The Slovak government has introduced measures to strengthen digital skills in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). These include training programmes to help companies understand and integrate artificial intelligence into their daily operations. The aim is to boost competitiveness and support digital transformation.

The Government of Slovakia has recognised the importance of digital skills as a cornerstone of competitiveness and innovation in the private sector. To this end, it has incorporated specific measures into its national strategic frameworks to improve the digital capabilities of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).
The initiative focuses on:
Training programmes for SME employees and managers, ensuring they can use and benefit from digital tools.Specialised AI modules that introduce businesses to the opportunities and practical applications of artificial intelligence.Capacity-building measures to help SMEs integrate AI into production, management, and service delivery processes.These measures are designed to ensure that SMEs can adapt to technological change, maintain competitiveness in a rapidly evolving digital economy, and actively participate in AI-driven innovation. By combining education with practical business applications, the government aims to bridge the skills gap that often prevents smaller companies from adopting advanced digital solutions.
Looking ahead, these measures are expected to be expanded and linked with other national and EU initiatives, including the European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs) and training programmes under the Digital Europe Programme. This integration will help SMEs scale their digital maturity, strengthen their workforce, and seize opportunities brought by artificial intelligence and other advanced technologies.

items.title: Slovene Early Stage Innovation Fund
items.original_name: Slovenski sklad za inovacije v zgodnji fazi
items.org: Public fund of Republic of  Slovenia for Entrepreneurship
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Slovenski sklad za inovacije v zgodnji fazi
items.body:
The Slovene Enterprise Fund equity financing scheme provides equity capital to innovative micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). It supports companies that contribute to the green and digital transition and promotes the growth of globally oriented start-ups and scale-ups.

This equity financing programme, offered by the Slovene Enterprise Fund, targets innovative SMEs with strong growth potential and an international orientation. Its main goal is to accelerate the development and scaling of companies that are advancing Slovenia’s green and digital transformation.
Key features include:
Equity capital provision – offering funding to early-stage and growth-phase SMEs that might otherwise face difficulty accessing traditional financing.Target beneficiaries – innovative micro, small, and medium-sized companies contributing to sustainability, digitalisation, and technological innovation.Focus on global growth – supporting start-ups and scale-ups that aim to compete and expand internationally.Alignment with national and EU priorities – advancing both green transition goals and digital economy objectives, in line with EU frameworks.Through this initiative, the Slovene Enterprise Fund helps companies:Access capital for product development, market expansion, and innovation.Enhance competitiveness and technological capabilities.Contribute to national strategic goals, including sustainability, digitalisation, and global economic integration.This programme complements Slovenia’s broader ecosystem of start-up and innovation support, working alongside initiatives such as P2, Digital Transformation incentives, and SID Bank equity financing to provide a comprehensive set of funding instruments for high-tech and innovative SMEs.

items.title: R&D projects for smart specialisation and specific economic objectives
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Slovenia supports R&D projects at TRL 3–6 in line with its Sustainable Smart Specialisation Strategy for Advanced Technologies. The initiative funds applied research and prototype development in strategic technology areas, including AI, to foster innovation and strengthen the national research ecosystem.

The Slovenian Sustainable Smart Specialisation Strategy for Advanced Technologies provides a framework for funding research and development projects with Technological Readiness Levels (TRL) 3–6, which encompass experimental proof-of-concept, prototype development, and validation in operational environments.
Key objectives of this initiative include:Promoting applied research in priority technology areas such as artificial intelligence, advanced manufacturing, quantum technologies, and digital solutions.Supporting technology development from conceptual stages to validated prototypes, bridging the gap between research and practical application.Enhancing Slovenia’s innovation ecosystem by funding projects with high potential for industrial and societal impact.Fostering collaboration among universities, research institutes, and industry partners to strengthen national R&D capacity.Through these measures, Slovenia aims to align its research investments with European and national priorities, encourage innovation-driven growth, and ensure that emerging technologies contribute to sustainable economic and societal development.
Looking forward, the strategy is expected to expand the scope and scale of applied R&D, create new opportunities for knowledge transfer, and position Slovenia as a competitive player in the European technology landscape, particularly in AI and other advanced digital technologies.

items.title: R&D projects for ICT and specific economic purposes
items.original_name: Javni razpis za sofinanciranje raziskovalno-razvojnih projektov podjetij za konkretne cilje: prispevek k zeleni preobrazbi, povečanje vlaganj v raziskave in razvoj, povečanje produktivnosti ter okrepitev konkurenčnosti gospodarstva
items.org: Ministry of the Economy, Tourism and Sport
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Javni razpis za sofinanciranje raziskovalno-razvojnih projektov podjetij za konkretne cilje: prispevek k zeleni preobrazbi, povečanje vlaganj v raziskave in razvoj, povečanje produktivnosti ter okrepitev konkurenčnosti gospodarstva
items.body:
In 2022, Slovenia’s Ministry of the Economy, Tourism and Sport co-funded 95 R&D projects led by consortia of companies, with 18 of these projects explicitly based on AI. The initiative supports innovation aligned with green transition, productivity growth, and competitiveness, with AI integrated into the ICT programme and other sectoral priorities.

In 2022, the Ministry of the Economy, Tourism and Sport launched a public call for R&D project proposals, with the following strategic objectives:
Contributing to the green transition, supporting sustainable and environmentally friendly solutions.Increasing investment in research and development, to strengthen Slovenia’s innovation capacity.Enhancing productivity, including material and energy efficiency, through advanced technologies.Boosting the competitiveness of the economy, particularly by fostering innovation-driven growth.From this initiative:
95 R&D projects carried out by consortia of companies received public co-funding.18 projects specifically focused on the application of artificial intelligence, underscoring the growing importance of AI in economic transformation.AI was integrated not only within the ICT programme, but also partially into nine other sectoral programmes overseen by the ministry.This initiative illustrates how Slovenia is embedding AI into broader economic development and innovation strategies, ensuring that digital technologies contribute to sustainability, competitiveness, and long-term growth.
Looking ahead, these measures are expected to stimulate AI adoption across industries, foster cross-sectoral innovation, and further align national R&D with EU green and digital priorities.

items.title: PoVejMo
items.org: Ministry of Higher Education, Science and Innovation
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The PoVejMo programme supports research on adaptive natural language processing using large-scale language models. It funds collaborative projects through a public call from the Ministry of Higher Education, Science and Innovation. The programme aims to advance AI-driven language technologies in Slovenia.

The PoVejMo programme is a Slovenian research and innovation initiative focused on adaptive natural language processing (NLP) with large-scale language models. The programme is implemented via a public call for co-funding of longer-term, large collaborative research and innovation projects, targeting Technical Readiness Levels (TRL) 3–6, which cover experimental proof-of-concept through to prototype validation.
Key objectives of the programme include:
Advancing research in NLP by leveraging AI to create models capable of understanding and generating human-like language.Promoting collaborative innovation by funding multi-institutional projects that involve universities, research institutes, and industry partners.Strengthening Slovenia’s AI ecosystem, particularly in the field of language technologies.Bridging fundamental research and applied AI solutions, enabling technologies that can be deployed in industry, public administration, and services.The initiative is overseen and co-funded by the Ministry of Higher Education, Science and Innovation, ensuring alignment with national research priorities and European AI strategies. Through PoVejMo, Slovenia seeks to enhance its capacity in AI-driven language technologies, support interdisciplinary collaboration, and strengthen the country’s position in the European AI landscape.
Looking forward, the programme is expected to foster scalable AI language solutions, contribute to digital innovation in society and industry, and support researchers in developing cutting-edge tools that are both technically advanced and practically applicable.

items.title: Pilot demonstration projects
items.original_name: Javni razpis za sofinanciranje pilotno-demonstracijskih projektov na področju krožnega gospodarstva v skladu z NEPN
items.org: SPIRIT Slovenia – Public Agency for Entrepreneurship, Internationalisation, Foreign Investments and Technology
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Javni razpis za sofinanciranje pilotno-demonstracijskih projektov na področju krožnega gospodarstva v skladu z NEPN
items.body:
Slovenia funded 21 consortia to run pilot projects supporting the circular economy as part of its National Energy and Climate Plan (NEPN). These projects aim to test and demonstrate innovative solutions that reduce environmental impact and improve resource efficiency. Three of the projects apply artificial intelligence to advance sustainability goals.

The pilot demonstration projects were launched to help Slovenia meet the environmental targets of the National Energy and Climate Plan (NEPN). By supporting circular economy initiatives, the programme promotes innovation that reduces waste, optimises resource use, and fosters sustainable growth.
Out of the 21 projects funded, three specifically focus on applying artificial intelligence. These AI-driven projects are used to optimise processes, enhance monitoring and data analysis, and enable smarter decision-making in resource management. This reflects Slovenia’s broader strategy to integrate digital and green technologies for climate action.
The projects are implemented by consortia bringing together companies, research institutions, and public bodies. By working in partnership, these actors ensure that solutions are both technologically advanced and practically applicable.
Looking ahead, these pilots are expected to provide scalable models that can be replicated across industries and regions, strengthening Slovenia’s contribution to the EU’s climate and sustainability targets while also enhancing its national innovation ecosystem.

items.title: P4D grants for digital transformation
items.original_name: P4D nepovratna sredstva za digitalno preobrazbo
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: P4D nepovratna sredstva za digitalno preobrazbo
items.body:
The Ministry of Economy, Tourism and Sport, in cooperation with the Slovene Enterprise Fund, provides grants of up to €100,000 to support the digital transformation of SMEs. The programme also encourages adoption of advanced technologies, including artificial intelligence, to modernise business operations.

This initiative aims to help micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Slovenia adopt digital technologies and improve competitiveness. Grants can be used for technology investments, digital strategy development, software and hardware implementation, and upskilling staff.
Key features of the programme include:
Funding amount: up to €100,000 per enterprise.Target technologies: digital tools, advanced technologies such as AI, automation, data analytics, and cloud solutions.Scope of support: includes purchases of ICT equipment, software development, robotic process automation, AI systems, cloud services, digital marketing, and staff training.Implementation: delivered jointly by the Ministry of Economy, Tourism and Sport and the Slovene Enterprise Fund, in alignment with EU guidelines for SME digitalisation.Through this programme, Slovenian SMEs are empowered to:Modernise business processes and adopt AI-driven solutions.Increase productivity and competitiveness in domestic and international markets.Strengthen workforce digital skills, ensuring sustainable technology adoption.The initiative supports Slovenia’s broader strategy for digital transformation, innovation, and economic growth, making SMEs more resilient and technologically capable.

items.title: P2 subsidies for start-ups
items.original_name: P2 SEF spodbuda za pospeševanje zagonskih podjetij
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: P2 SEF spodbuda za pospeševanje zagonskih podjetij
items.body:
The P2 programme, managed by the Ministry of Economy, Tourism, and Sport and implemented via the Slovene Enterprise Fund, co-finances innovation-driven start-ups. It supports the development and commercialisation of innovative products, including solutions based on artificial intelligence.

The P2 programme aims to accelerate the growth of innovation-driven companies in Slovenia by providing targeted financial and advisory support. The programme focuses on helping start-ups and early-stage companies develop, test, and bring innovative products to market, including solutions that leverage artificial intelligence.
Key objectives include:
Co-financing product development – reducing financial barriers for companies creating innovative technologies.Supporting commercialisation – helping start-ups move from prototype to market-ready solutions.Promoting AI and advanced technologies – ensuring new products incorporate cutting-edge digital solutions where relevant.Strengthening the start-up ecosystem – encouraging entrepreneurship and collaboration among SMEs, research institutions, and investors.By combining funding with guidance, the P2 programme facilitates faster innovation cycles, supports high-potential technology ventures, and strengthens Slovenia’s competitiveness in the digital and AI sectors.

items.title: National Multi stakeholder consultation forum for AI policy and regulation
items.org: Ministry of Innovation Science and Technology
items.category: National – AI governance bodies or mechanisms
items.body:
The expert forum will assist in developing a governmental strategy and policy for promoting the safe use of artificial intelligence, aiming to encourage innovation and maximize the technology’s social and economic benefits.

The Ministry of Innovation, Science, and Technology has established a national expert forum on artificial intelligence, following an open call for candidates. The forum includes experts from academia, industry, and leading civil society organizations.
The expert forum will assist in developing a governmental strategy and policy for promoting the safe use of artificial intelligence, aiming to encourage innovation and maximize the technology’s social and economic benefits. It is established and led by the Government Center for AI Regulation and Policy within the Ministry of Innovation and Science, which was created by Government Resolution 173.

items.title: Legal Guide for Designing Regulatory Sandboxes
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
This guide was written for Israeli regulators to support the design of a responsible, innovation-friendly regulatory framework. It introduces the "regulatory sandbox" tool, explains its use in Israel, outlines its advantages and disadvantages, and provides examples from Israeli law to support better rulemaking.

The Regulatory Sandbox Legal Guide is a legal and policy tool developed to support Israeli regulators in creating structured mechanisms for safe experimentation with innovative technologies. It responds to a critical governance challenge: how to regulate fast-evolving sectors such as artificial intelligence, digital finance, and health innovation within legal systems that are often rigid, outdated, or fragmented. The guide enables regulators to authorize time-bound testing environments in which companies can trial new business models or technologies under supervision, subject to partial regulatory exemptions and risk controls.
Beyond outlining the core principles of a regulatory sandbox — such as eligibility criteria, clear objectives, and institutional accountability — the guide focuses on the legal design of sandbox regimes. It provides structured legislative models that can be embedded in both primary and secondary laws, and includes examples from existing Israeli statutes to support tailored implementation. It stresses the need for legislative clarity and normative certainty, while also enabling proportional regulatory discretion and adaptive oversight.
The guide is designed to promote innovation while protecting the public interest. It establishes a process of learning-based regulation, allowing adjustments grounded in real-world experience. The sandbox model fosters dialogue between regulators and innovators, builds institutional capacity, and helps reduce uncertainty in the face of novel and complex technologies.
Looking ahead, the initiative is expected to expand through the enactment of a cross-sectoral statutory framework, empowering the establishment of dedicated sandboxes via secondary legislation and through other coordinated efforts by an inter-ministerial team promoting regulatory experimentation. Over time, the sandbox model may serve as a stepping stone toward broader innovation-friendly reforms, including adaptive regulation and dynamic oversight mechanisms. The guide reflects an evolving shift in regulatory governance — moving from static rulemaking toward flexible, learning-oriented approaches — and is expected to shape how Israeli regulators engage with uncertainty, technological complexity, and cross-sector innovation.

items.title: Increasing the number of AI experts from overseas in Israeli industry (returning residents, new immigrants, foreign experts)
items.original_name: הגדלת מספר מומחי הבינה המלאכותית מחו"ל המשולבים בתעשייה הישראלית (תושבים חזרים, עולים חדשים, מומחים זרים)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: הגדלת מספר מומחי הבינה המלאכותית מחו"ל המשולבים בתעשייה הישראלית (תושבים חזרים, עולים חדשים, מומחים זרים)
items.body:
Shortage in AI experts with graduate-level academic qualifications constitutes a barrier to the local high-tech industry’s ability to fulfil its potential for AI-driven innovation. Some 300-400 advanced degree graduates complete their studies each year and join the high-tech industry in research roles. Yet the demand for such experts is much higher. Attracting foreign talent into the Israeli high-tech eco system serves to expand and diversify the local expert pool.

Considering the talent shortage in AI, countries worldwide are competing for experts. As part of a call for proposals completed in 2024, the Innovation Authority chose 3 entities to locate and bring to Israel foreign AI researchers with a relevant academic education from well-known institutions and relevant work experience overseas, who wish to work in Israeli high-tech companies as AI researchers and lead their development teams. Target audiences include immigrants who are entitled to settle in Israel, Israelis who emigrated overseas and wish to return to Israel, as well as foreign experts who wish to relocate. The chosen entities will also be responsible for the AI experts’ placement and assimilation in Israel. 

The purpose of government support in this case is to reduce the financial risk associated with establishing an international identification, recruitment, and selection apparatus. The ultimate goal is to allow the chosen entities, after an initial time-limited governmental support, to continue and expand their effort to attract foreign talent organically, without the need for continuous governmental intervention.

items.title: High-tech equity financing programme
items.original_name: Program financiranja lastniškega kapitala za visoke tehnologije
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Program financiranja lastniškega kapitala za visoke tehnologije
items.body:
The SID Bank programme provides equity financing to innovative and high-tech start-ups and scale-ups in Slovenia. It offers seed capital and convertible loans to support early-stage development, product commercialisation, and scaling of technology-driven businesses.

Following a previous initiative by the Slovene Enterprise Fund (2014–2020), the SID Bank continues to support Slovenia’s innovation ecosystem by providing equity-based funding to start-ups and scale-ups. The programme targets companies developing high-tech solutions, including those using artificial intelligence, advanced digital technologies, and other innovative products.
Key features of the programme include:Equity financing instruments: seed capital and convertible loans that provide flexible funding while sharing risk between investors and the company.Target beneficiaries: innovative start-ups and scale-ups with high-growth potential in technology-driven sectors.Purpose: accelerate development, enable commercialisation of new products, and support company growth.Alignment with national strategies: complements other Slovenian programmes for SME digitalisation, R&D, and AI adoption.Through this initiative, the SID Bank helps Slovenian start-ups access capital that may be difficult to secure from traditional financing channels, while fostering innovation, technology-driven growth, and international competitiveness.

items.title: Gravity and Strategic projects
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Gravity Projects initiative funds four major research consortia in Slovenia, each focusing on a high-impact technology area: AI, semiconductors, language technologies, and quantum technologies. Co-funded by the Ministry of Higher Education, Science and Innovation and the Ministry of Digital Transformation, the projects support research from early-stage concept (TRL 1/2) to validated prototypes (TRL 4/5).

The Gravity Projects initiative is a Slovenian national programme designed to accelerate innovative and high-impact research in strategically important technology areas. The initiative supports four consortia of researchers, each dedicated to a different thematic domain:
Artificial Intelligence (AI)Semiconductor technologiesLanguage technologiesQuantum technologiesThese projects target research and technological development at TRL 1/2 to TRL 4/5, covering early conceptual work through experimental validation and prototype development. This enables the transition from fundamental research to applied solutions that can have tangible societal and industrial impact.
The initiative is co-funded by the Ministry of Higher Education, Science and Innovation and the Ministry of Digital Transformation, ensuring that national priorities are aligned with research investments. Key objectives include:Advancing cutting-edge research in emerging and strategically important technologies.Fostering collaboration among universities, research institutes, and industry partners.Strengthening Slovenia’s innovation ecosystem by supporting projects with high scientific and economic potential.Facilitating technology transfer from research outputs to practical applications in industry and public services.Looking forward, the Gravity Projects are expected to create sustainable centres of expertise in each of the four thematic areas. The initiative also aims to build national and international research networks, attract top talent, and enhance Slovenia’s position in global innovation and digital transformation.

items.title: European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Slovenia hosts two European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs) with dedicated services to support AI start-ups and scale-ups in accessing financing and advancing digital transformation. These are: Smart, Resilient and Sustainable Communities (SRC-EDIH) and DIGI-SI.

The two Slovenian EDIHs form part of the European Digital Innovation Hub network funded under the Digital Europe Programme and national support. They serve as regional one-stop shops to accelerate the digital transformation of SMEs, start-ups, scale-ups, and public sector organisations, with a strong emphasis on AI and other enabling technologies.
Smart, Resilient and Sustainable Communities (SRC-EDIH):
SRC focuses on state and local governments as well as SMEs, supporting them in testing products, solutions, and components in real environments. It helps organisations upgrade their digital processes and business models while aligning growth with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Core areas of support include High-Performance Computing (HPC), AI, cybersecurity, robotics, and blockchain technologies, with particular targeting of the manufacturing and public services sectors.DIGI-SI:
DIGI-SI aims to foster the digital transformation of SMEs, start-ups, scale-ups, and public administration in four strategic priority areas: Agri-food, Health, Tourism, and Manufacturing. It provides services in AI, cybersecurity, HPC, and advanced digital skills, with tailored support for food producers, healthcare providers, tourism operators, and manufacturing firms.Both hubs play a dual role:
Technology adoption – providing expertise, testing facilities, and infrastructure.Access to finance – supporting AI start-ups and scale-ups in connecting with investors, funding schemes, and EU programmes.Together, SRC-EDIH and DIGI-SI enhance Slovenia’s innovation ecosystem, ensure SMEs and start-ups can benefit from the latest digital technologies, and strengthen the country’s integration into the European digital single market.

items.title: European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Slovakia hosts several European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs) that support digital transformation across sectors. These hubs assist SMEs, hospitals, companies, and public institutions in adopting advanced digital technologies, including AI. Their implementation is coordinated by the Ministry of Investment, Regional Development, and Informatization.

The European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs) in Slovakia are part of the EU-wide initiative under the Digital Europe Programme that helps businesses and public sector organisations accelerate digital transformation. In Slovakia, these hubs provide test-before-invest services, training, and access to expertise, with a focus on artificial intelligence and other advanced technologies. The Ministry of Investment, Regional Development, and Informatization of the Slovak Republic oversees their implementation and launch.
The Slovak EDIHs include:
HealthHub – Centre of Innovative Health Care: Supports hospitals and healthcare facilities in digital transformation and innovation.Cassovium: Creates a unique platform for the implementation and development of digital technologies in Eastern Slovakia.Expandi 4.0: Assists SMEs in digital transformation by guiding them through innovation processes and developing the skills needed for success.Hopero: Helps companies and public institutions prepare and implement AI projects, secure funding, and connect with innovators in Slovakia’s ecosystem.SCDI (Slovak Centre of Digital Innovations): Focuses on SME digitalisation with emphasis on environmental sustainability, workforce development, and the digital technology industry.KInIT (Kempelen Institute of Intelligent Technologies): An independent, non-profit institute that advances research in AI and computer science, bridging expertise across public and private sectors.Together, these hubs play a crucial role in:
Supporting SMEs and public organisations in adopting AI and digital tools.Strengthening Slovakia’s innovation ecosystem by linking research, industry, and government.Improving competitiveness and resilience across sectors, including healthcare, manufacturing, and public services.Building skills and training for digital and AI adoption.Looking forward, the Slovak EDIHs are expected to expand their services, strengthen international cooperation within the EU-wide network of hubs, and contribute to making Slovakia more competitive and innovative in the digital age.

items.title: Establishment of a Moonshot AI Applied Research Consortium
items.original_name: קול קורא להקמת מאגד בתחום הבינה המלאכותית
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: קול קורא להקמת מאגד בתחום הבינה המלאכותית
items.body:
The Israel Innovation Authority invites proposals for the establishment of an applied research consortium dedicated to the development of groundbreaking technologies in the field of artificial intelligence (AI). These technologies should be at the forefront of global R&D and have the potential to provide Israeli industry with a competitive edge in the international market.

The term Moonshot project refers to broad research efforts, at the forefront of global knowledge, which require collaboration by several different research teams. Projects may differ in nature on the range between basic and applied research, but all will have a relatively broad scope of research activity and a high rate of uncertainty about whether the challenge can be solved, or the research question answered (high risk – high gain).

Such research characteristics ensure that even in case of “failure” to solve the challenge, the generated intellectual property is expected to be substantial, positioning the researchers involved at the vanguard of global research. Moreover, groundbreaking, and broad-scope research projects are expected to help draw leading global researchers, and to establish Israel’s research reserve.

Various projects are to be launched by different entities that take part in the program, in accordance with the research question. Projects pertaining to the foundations of AI technology will be launched by the Planning and Budgeting Committee, projects that are more applicative will be launched by the Innovation Authority, and projects pertaining to the dual needs of the defense system will be led by the Directorate of Defense Research & Development.

Each such project is expected to span several research teams from different disciplines and institutions, working together for a period of two to three years. Subjects for challenge projects will be chosen by a combination of open calls for proposals (bottom-up approach), and general guidance towards broad and relevant spheres of interest (top-down approach). The research activity’s operational mechanism will be derived from the leading entity’s toolbox. Chosen projects may include a variety of research fields, combining software, hardware, robotics including humanoid robotics, and others.

items.title: EUROPEUM-EDIC
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The European Blockchain Partnership and European Blockchain Services Infrastructure (EBSI) EDIC brings together EU countries to build secure and interoperable blockchain services. Its goal is to support cross-border cooperation between public authorities and ensure blockchain solutions work seamlessly with other technologies like AI, cloud, and data spaces. The initiative also creates better conditions for innovation in decentralised technologies.

The European Blockchain Partnership (EBP) and the European Blockchain Services Infrastructure (EBSI) have been established as a European Digital Infrastructure Consortium (EDIC) to accelerate the use of blockchain across Europe. This initiative seeks to provide trustworthy, cross-border digital public services by leveraging decentralised technologies.
The project pursues several core objectives:
Facilitate cross-border cooperation among public authorities to deploy and scale blockchain solutions across the EU.Ensure interoperability of blockchain solutions at multiple levels — protocol, smart contract, and application.Foster integration with other key digital technologies such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, data spaces, and cybersecurity.Enable innovation-friendly conditions by supporting collaboration with blockchain and non-blockchain initiatives, as well as with other EDICs.By advancing European blockchain services, the initiative is expected to:Increase trust and transparency in digital transactions across member states.Support efficient and secure public services, such as digital identity, document verification, and supply chain monitoring.Provide a foundation for innovation ecosystems, allowing SMEs, startups, and public bodies to develop applications that rely on secure decentralised infrastructure.Over time, the EBSI EDIC is intended to become a pan-European blockchain infrastructure, supporting both the public sector and private innovation. Its role in promoting interoperability and cooperation with other digital fields will ensure that blockchain is not developed in isolation but as part of a broader European digital ecosystem.

items.title: Digital transformation incentives programme of the Slovene Enterprise Fund
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Slovene Enterprise Fund provides grants and blended financing to micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) through its Digital Transformation incentives. The programme supports investment in digital technologies and skills, helping SMEs modernise operations and increase competitiveness.

The Digital Transformation incentives are part of the Slovene Enterprise Fund’s broader support programmes for SMEs. The initiative is designed to assist companies in adopting digital tools, technologies, and processes that improve efficiency, productivity, and innovation.
Key features of the programme include:
Grant support and blended financing – combining repayable and non-repayable funding to reduce financial risk for SMEs.Alignment with EU guidelines – ensuring that investments comply with European Union frameworks for development incentive programmes.Targeted beneficiaries – micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises across various sectors seeking to implement digital technologies.The incentives help SMEs:
Modernise operations and workflows through digitalisation.Integrate AI, data analytics, cloud computing, and other advanced technologies.Build digital skills and capabilities among employees.Strengthen competitiveness at national and European levels.By combining financial support with strategic guidance, the programme contributes to a sustainable and innovation-driven SME ecosystem in Slovenia, fostering long-term growth and integration into the digital economy.

items.title: Digital Innovation Hub Slovenia
items.org: Ministry of the Economy, Tourism and Sport
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Slovenia’s national Digital Innovation Hub (DIH Slovenia) serves as a one-stop shop supporting the digitalisation of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). It provides financial and advisory support through vouchers that help companies strengthen their digital skills, develop strategies, improve digital marketing, and enhance cybersecurity.

The national Digital Innovation Hub plays a key role in advancing digital transformation among Slovenian SMEs. Its services are designed to lower barriers to adopting advanced digital solutions and to build long-term competitiveness.
The support instruments are primarily delivered through voucher schemes, which allow SMEs to access tailored expertise and resources in several areas:
Digital competences – improving the skills of employees and management to use digital tools effectively.Digital strategies – supporting the design and implementation of company-wide digitalisation roadmaps.Digital marketing – helping businesses improve their online presence, customer outreach, and use of digital channels.Cybersecurity – strengthening resilience against cyber threats and ensuring secure use of digital technologies.By providing both financial support and practical expertise, the Hub acts as a trusted intermediary between SMEs, technology providers, and research institutions. It also plays a wider role in building a digital innovation ecosystem in Slovenia, connecting companies with relevant partners and facilitating participation in EU-level initiatives such as the European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs).
This initiative aligns with Slovenia’s national strategies for digitalisation, SME competitiveness, and innovation-driven growth, making it an important driver of the country’s economic transformation.

items.title: CitiVERSE
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Connected Local Digital Twins for CitiVERSE (LDT CitiVERSE EDIC) links digital twins of cities across Europe to form a shared CitiVERSE. These virtual city models use AI and data to simulate real-world conditions and improve decision-making. The initiative helps cities test solutions for issues like traffic, air quality, and urban planning, while also enhancing citizen engagement through interactive tools.

The Connected Local Digital Twins for CitiVERSE (LDT CitiVERSE EDIC) is a European initiative designed to connect existing local digital twins and establish the foundation of the EU CitiVERSE. A digital twin is a virtual representation of a city’s physical assets, processes, and systems, combining real-time data, analytics, and AI to create models that simulate urban dynamics.
The CitiVERSE initiative pursues several key objectives:
Integration of local digital twins into a Europe-wide network, enabling knowledge-sharing and interoperability.Use of AI-driven simulations to test scenarios such as the effects of traffic flow changes on air quality, congestion, and decarbonisation efforts.Application of generative AI and virtual reality tools to enhance citizen participation, making consultations on urban planning more engaging and easier to understand.By focusing on smart city development, CitiVERSE enables municipalities to:
Improve urban decision-making with real-time and predictive modelling.Foster sustainable and climate-friendly solutions, aligned with EU Green Deal goals.Strengthen citizen engagement by providing accessible and immersive digital tools.In the longer term, the CitiVERSE project is expected to evolve into a pan-European platform for digital urban innovation. It will support cities in scaling and integrating digital twin solutions, while ensuring interoperability across borders. The initiative also acts as a testing ground for cutting-edge generative AI applications, positioning Europe at the forefront of AI-driven smart city technologies.

items.title: COFUND SMASH project
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The SMASH programme brings together leading Slovenian universities, research institutes, and public bodies to attract 50 outstanding postdoctoral researchers from around the world, including Slovenians abroad. Using machine learning, AI, and the Vega supercomputer, researchers will work across multiple scientific and humanities fields. The initiative strengthens Slovenia’s role in global research while supporting the return of local talent.

The SMASH programme (funded under the Horizon Europe Marie Skłodowska-Curie COFUND Actions) is an intersectoral, career-development training initiative designed to attract international talent and support Slovenia’s digital and scientific ambitions. Coordinated by the University of Nova Gorica, with key partners including the University of Ljubljana, the Jožef Stefan Institute, the Slovenian Environment Agency, and the Maribor Institute of Information Sciences, the programme integrates advanced research infrastructures and interdisciplinary collaboration.
The core goals of SMASH are to:Recruit 50 top postdoctoral researchers from around the world, with a focus on both global talent and Slovenian researchers working abroad.Leverage machine learning, AI, and the Vega supercomputer to conduct research across disciplines, from natural sciences and engineering to social sciences and humanities.Strengthen Slovenia’s research ecosystem, embedding international expertise and fostering cross-sectoral collaboration.Beyond research, the programme also aligns with national talent and innovation policies. With support from the Ministry of Higher Education, Science and Innovation and the Ministry of Digital Transformation, two complementary projects have been launched:
Developing a mechanism to attract foreign and returning Slovenian experts, enhancing Slovenia’s competitiveness in global digitalisation trends.Creating an analytical model for evaluating policy measures that support the return of highly educated Slovenes.Looking forward, the SMASH programme is expected to have a long-term impact by:
Increasing Slovenia’s visibility and integration within international research networks.Supporting the next generation of AI-driven research across diverse fields.Enhancing national innovation capacity through talent retention, institutional collaboration, and cross-border knowledge exchange.By combining world-class research infrastructure with targeted policies for talent mobility, SMASH represents a strategic investment in both Slovenia’s scientific future and its role in shaping Europe’s digital transformation.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in the Financial Sector – Interim Report of the Inter-Agency Task Force on the Use of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Israel's Financial Sector
items.original_name: בינה מלאכותית בסקטור הפיננסי - דו"ח ביניים להערות הציבור
items.org: Interagency Task Force encompassing representatives from the Ministry of Justice, Ministry of Finance, Israel Securities Authority, Competition Authority, Capital Market, Insurance and Savings Authority, and the Bank of Israel (Banking Supervision)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: בינה מלאכותית בסקטור הפיננסי - דו"ח ביניים להערות הציבור
items.body:
This initiative aims to improve financial services, reduce costs, and boost innovation. It promotes responsible AI use while addressing risks like bias, data misuse, and lack of transparency. The initiative focuses on flexible, sector-specific regulation. Policymakers and regulators are working together to ensure fair, safe, and effective AI integration that benefits consumers and supports sustainable financial growth.

Israel’s artificial intelligence initiative in the financial sector is a forward-looking effort to harness the potential of AI while ensuring responsible and fair use. The initiative responds to the growing interest in AI applications across banking, insurance, credit, and investment services, where the technology offers opportunities to improve efficiency, reduce operational costs, enhance access to financial services, and promote innovation. At the same time, it addresses significant risks, including algorithmic bias, lack of transparency (the “black box” problem), privacy concerns, cyber threats, and the potential for market concentration or financial instability. These challenges demand a careful and tailored approach to regulation that neither stifles innovation nor compromises consumer protection or market integrity. 
The key objectives of the initiative are to promote safe AI integration in financial services, ensure consumer rights and data privacy, and maintain public trust in digital finance. Led by an inter-agency task force of financial regulators, the initiative encourages a flexible, risk-based regulatory framework that adapts to the level of risk posed by specific AI applications. It emphasizes technological neutrality, proportional regulation, and alignment with global standards while advancing innovation through mechanisms like regulatory sandboxes, innovation hubs, and improved access to anonymized data. Consumer-facing protections—such as explainability of AI decisions, human oversight in critical processes, and clear disclosures about AI use—are prioritized to safeguard fairness and accountability.
The initiative is expected to evolve through continued public consultation, refinement of regulatory principles, and the gradual development of sector-specific rules. While Israel does not currently adopt a single, sweeping AI law, the initiative encourages updates to existing financial regulations and policies to accommodate AI-driven services. Institutionalization will occur through regulator-issued guidelines, inter-agency coordination, and the integration of AI governance and risk management practices across financial institutions. Efforts to monitor systemic risks, such as over-reliance on third-party AI providers or disinformation threats, are also part of the long-term implementation plan. 
The initiative aims to scale through broader adoption of AI tools, supported by clear, consistent oversight and continuous evaluation. Since its inception, the initiative has moved from conceptual discussion to structured planning, producing two key policy documents that assess both current challenges and future needs. These reports reflect the government’s commitment to balancing technological progress with social responsibility. As AI adoption increases, the initiative’s principles and tools will be revisited and updated to ensure a competitive, inclusive, and resilient financial sector.

items.title: Alliance for Language Technologies - European Digital Infrastructure Consortium (ALT-EDIC)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Slovenia is a member of the European Digital Infrastructure Consortium for Language Technologies (ALT-EDIC). This initiative seeks to build shared European infrastructure for language technologies and create large language models for European languages. The goal is to strengthen Europe’s AI capabilities while preserving linguistic diversity.
