Slovenia actively participates in the European Digital Infrastructure Consortium for Language Technologies (ALT-EDIC), a joint initiative addressing the scarcity of high-quality European language data for training artificial intelligence systems. This is a strategic step for both Slovenia and the European Union, as the majority of current AI language models are based on English and non-European data sources.
The objectives of ALT-EDIC include:
Developing shared European infrastructure for language technologies.Creating large language models (LLMs) specifically tailored to European official and regional languages.Promoting linguistic diversity and ensuring smaller languages are represented in AI systems.Advancing Europe’s AI sovereignty by reducing dependence on non-European AI technologies.For Slovenia, participation in ALT-EDIC supports both national and European strategic goals:Strengthening local AI research and development capacity, particularly in natural language processing (NLP).Supporting public services, SMEs, and industries in adopting advanced language technologies.Contributing to the preservation and digitalisation of the Slovene language, ensuring it remains part of cutting-edge AI systems.Looking ahead, ALT-EDIC is expected to become a pan-European hub for language technologies, fostering collaboration among member states, research institutions, and private sector stakeholders. Slovenia’s role in the consortium provides access to infrastructure, shared datasets, and expertise, positioning the country as an active contributor to the development of European multilingual AI ecosystems.

items.title: AI for Science Moonshot
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The national program’s Scientific Advisory Committee, the PBC is happy to launch a new Call for Proposals: AI for Science Moonshot. The term "Moonshot" is used here to describe an ambitious and groundbreaking project aimed at achieving a goal perceived as difficult or nearly impossible, but which has the potential to revolutionize a given domain with far-reaching implications for technological and overall progress.

The current Call for Proposals will provide financial support for a group of top researchers from at least two different public research universities who will focus on solving a central AI challenge or problem. Its aim is to encourage project(s) with the highest potential for discovery, innovation and a significant expansion of existing knowledge in core AI research, thereby positioning Israeli academia at the forefront of scientific and technological development in AI.
The program is open to all Israeli public research universities. Researchers from other higher education institutions may participate and receive funding for research activities within the program. Collaboration between researchers from at least two public research universities is required.

items.title: AI Competence Center
items.org: Ministry of Digital Transformation and Ministry of Higher Education, Science and Innovation
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Slovenia is planning to establish a national Competence Center for Artificial Intelligence, led by the Ministry of Digital Transformation. The center will advance AI research, innovation, and practical applications across industries and public services. It will also act as a one-stop-shop to help SMEs adopt AI solutions.

The Ministry of Digital Transformation of Slovenia is preparing to launch a Competence Center for Artificial Intelligence, designed as a cornerstone of the country’s National Programme for Artificial Intelligence (NpAI). Its purpose is to strengthen Slovenia’s position in AI development, adoption, and integration across both public and private sectors.
The Competence Center will pursue several objectives:
Advance AI research and expertise by supporting collaboration between academia, industry, and government.Foster innovation and encourage the development of AI-based products and services.Support SMEs through training, consulting, and test-before-invest opportunities, acting as a one-stop-shop for AI adoption.Promote economic growth by facilitating the integration of AI into industry, public services, and administration.The Center will be implemented through a consortium model, ensuring broad participation from key stakeholders. A public call was launched in December 2024 to select consortium members, expected to include universities, research institutions, private sector companies, and government actors.
Looking forward, the Competence Center is set to become a national focal point for AI, aligning Slovenia’s research and innovation activities with broader European initiatives. By providing infrastructure, expertise, and support services, it is expected to:Enhance Slovenia’s competitiveness in the global digital economy,Stimulate the development of AI talent and skills,Drive cross-sectoral applications of AI in areas such as healthcare, manufacturing, smart cities, and public administration.

items.title: Slovak Center for Artificial Intelligence Research (AISlovakIA)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Slovak Center for Artificial Intelligence Research (AISlovakIA) was created in 2019 as Slovakia’s national AI platform. It connects researchers, students, businesses, government, and international partners to advance AI research and adoption. Its goal is to build a collaborative environment that fully develops Slovakia’s AI potential.

The Slovak Center for Artificial Intelligence Research (AISlovakIA), originally founded as slovak.AI in 2019, serves as Slovakia’s National Artificial Intelligence Platform. It was established as a platform of excellence in AI research and as a hub bringing together diverse stakeholders—including students, researchers, entrepreneurs, educators, employers, investors, and policymakers—who are engaged in the development and application of AI.
AISlovakIA is overseen by the Center for Artificial Intelligence (CUI), a nonprofit association of legal entities that evolved from the civic association slovak.AI. This governance structure ensures that the platform is collaborative, inclusive, and aligned with both national priorities and European AI initiatives.
The platform’s vision and objectives are to:
Foster collaboration across academia, industry, government, and civil society.Advance excellence in AI research while supporting practical applications.Provide a national forum for knowledge exchange, training, and public awareness about AI.Integrate Slovakia into the European and global AI research landscape.AISlovakIA functions as both a research enabler and a networking platform. It supports cutting-edge research projects, facilitates dialogue between researchers and employers, and strengthens the country’s AI innovation ecosystem. By connecting education, research, and business, it also helps ensure that AI talent is trained, retained, and effectively deployed in the Slovak economy.
Looking forward, AISlovakIA aims to expand its impact by deepening international cooperation, securing resources for national AI initiatives, and fostering the development of innovative AI applications in strategic sectors. Its role as a unifying platform ensures that Slovakia can fully develop the potential of artificial intelligence while aligning with European AI priorities.

items.title: Regional AI Hubs at universities
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
InnovAIte Slovakia brings together regional universities and local industries to advance research and innovation in artificial intelligence. Universities have established dedicated AI research hubs focusing on practical applications. The initiative fosters collaboration and supports the development of AI solutions tailored to Slovakia’s economic and social needs.

InnovAIte Slovakia is a collaborative initiative designed to strengthen Slovakia’s artificial intelligence ecosystem by linking academic research with industry needs. Several regional universities have created dedicated AI research departments and hubs, many of which work closely with local businesses and industrial partners. These hubs focus on advancing both applied and fundamental AI research, while also ensuring that innovations are directly relevant to the country’s economic development.
The main objectives of InnovAIte Slovakia are to:
Promote AI research capacity within Slovak universities.Encourage university–industry collaboration for the development of applied AI solutions.Support regional innovation ecosystems by tailoring AI applications to local needs.Train and upskill researchers and students in high-demand AI fields.Through these hubs, universities are exploring AI applications across multiple areas, such as:
Intelligent manufacturing and industrial automation.Smart cities and mobility.Healthcare and biomedical technologies.Data-driven solutions for public administration and services.By strengthening collaboration between academia and industry, InnovAIte Slovakia helps ensure that research is effectively transferred into practice. This increases the competitiveness of Slovak companies while also contributing to the country’s digital transformation.
Looking ahead, InnovAIte Slovakia aims to scale its activities by expanding university partnerships, integrating into broader European AI networks, and securing additional funding for advanced research and innovation. The initiative is expected to play a key role in positioning Slovakia as an active participant in the European AI landscape.

items.title: European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs)
items.org: Ministry of European Investments and Projects of Romania
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Romania hosts seven European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs), five of which have a strong focus on artificial intelligence. These hubs support SMEs and public organisations in adopting digital and AI technologies. They are co-funded by the European Commission and the Romanian Government to drive digital transformation across the country.

Romania is home to seven European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs) established under the Digital Europe Programme, with five explicitly focused on artificial intelligence (AI): eDIH-DIZ, TDIH, DIH4Society, FIT EDIH, and CiTyInnoHub. These hubs act as regional one-stop shops that help businesses, particularly small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), and public administrations take advantage of digital and AI technologies to improve their products, services, and operations.
The initiative is financed through the Smart Growth, Digitalization and Financial Instruments Programme 2021–2027, co-funded by the European Commission and the Romanian Government (Ministry of European Investments and Projects). By combining European and national resources, the programme ensures that SMEs and other organisations can access high-quality expertise, training, and technological infrastructure.
The main objectives of Romania’s EDIHs are to:
Support digital transformation of SMEs through applied training, testing, and consultancy.Promote AI adoption in diverse sectors of the economy.Offer access to advanced facilities and expertise, such as test-before-invest environments.Facilitate collaboration between academia, businesses, and government institutions.Boost competitiveness by making advanced digital technologies more accessible.Looking forward, the hubs are expected to expand their role in scaling AI adoption nationwide, increasing cross-border cooperation within the European EDIH network, and contributing to a stronger innovation ecosystem in Romania. Their impact will be particularly important in helping SMEs integrate AI into real-world applications, thus enhancing productivity and competitiveness at both national and European levels.

items.title: Aid scheme for the digitalisation of SME
items.org: Ministry of European Investments and Projects of Romania
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Under Romania’s National Recovery and Resilience Plan (NRRP), a dedicated investment supports the digitalisation of SMEs. It provides grants both for developing advanced digital technologies and for helping SMEs adopt them. Eligible areas include AI, cloud computing, blockchain, IoT, cybersecurity, and other key digital tools.

As part of the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (NRRP), Component 9 – Investment 3: Private Sector Aid Schemes was launched to accelerate the digital transformation of Romania’s small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). This initiative recognises that SMEs form the backbone of the economy, but often lack resources to access and implement cutting-edge technologies. By combining financial support with clear eligibility criteria, the programme seeks to foster both technological adoption and innovation-led growth.
The sub-investment is structured around two main instruments:
Grants for the development of advanced digital technologies – targeted at entrepreneurs who are building solutions in fields such as:Artificial intelligence (AI)Data and cloud computingBlockchainHigh-performance and quantum computingInternet of Things (IoT)Cybersecurity2. Grants of up to EUR 100,000 per enterprise for digital adoption – supporting SMEs in integrating new technologies into their operations. Eligible expenses include:
Purchases of ICT hardware and software licences.Robotic Process Automation (RPA) and software automation tools.Blockchain and artificial intelligence systems.Machine learning, augmented reality, and virtual reality applications.Cloud services and IoT solutions.Development of company websites.Staff training in the use of IT equipment.Advisory services and technical assessments for digital readiness.The overall objective is to strengthen the competitiveness of SMEs by enabling them to adopt and create digital solutions that increase efficiency, productivity, and innovation capacity.
Looking ahead, this investment is expected to deliver long-term benefits for the Romanian economy by:
Creating a more digitally skilled workforce.Enhancing SME participation in the digital single market.Supporting the growth of local digital technology providers.Facilitating the integration of Romanian SMEs into European and global value chains.By targeting both the supply side (entrepreneurs developing advanced technologies) and the demand side (SMEs adopting digital tools), the initiative ensures a balanced and sustainable approach to digitalisation.

items.title: Start-up Hub Portal
items.category: National – AI governance bodies or mechanisms
items.body:
The Start-up Hub Portal in Portugal is an online platform that maps the country’s start-up ecosystem. It gathers information on start-ups, incubators, investors, and support programmes, offering a real-time view of the sector. The portal makes it easier for entrepreneurs, investors, and institutions to connect and collaborate.

The Start-up Hub Portal is a comprehensive digital platform designed to provide a clear and up-to-date picture of Portugal’s entrepreneurship landscape. By mapping start-ups, incubators, accelerators, and investment programmes, it responds to the need for a central reference point that both policymakers and entrepreneurs can rely on. Its main function is to bring visibility and structure to a dynamic but sometimes fragmented ecosystem.
The initiative pursues several key objectives:
Identify and geolocate start-ups, incubators, and accelerators across Portugal.Aggregate and benchmark public and private initiatives that support entrepreneurship.Provide real-time information on support measures, funding opportunities, and ecosystem players.Foster collaboration by connecting entrepreneurs, investors, and institutions.Implementation is centred on building a single access point for the entrepreneurship ecosystem. The portal collects, organises, and updates data so that different actors—whether a new entrepreneur seeking an incubator, an investor scouting opportunities, or a policymaker analysing sector growth—can access reliable and comprehensive information.
Over time, the Start-up Hub Portal is expected to evolve into a more interactive and data-driven tool, with expanded features for matchmaking, personalised recommendations, and international visibility. By scaling its reach and improving functionality, the initiative strengthens Portugal’s position as a competitive and transparent environment for entrepreneurship and innovation.

items.title: Romanian AI Innovation Hub for AI (HRIA)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Romanian Hub of Artificial Intelligence (HRIA) is a national project that brings together universities and companies to strengthen Romania’s AI ecosystem. Its goal is to advance research, create new AI products and services, and transfer knowledge to industry and society. Running from 2025 to 2029, the hub aims to position Romania as an active player in the European AI landscape.

The Romanian Hub of Artificial Intelligence (HRIA) is a strategic initiative designed to ensure a broad and long-lasting impact of AI across Romania’s economy and society. Recognised as a national priority, it seeks to accelerate the adoption of AI while building a competitive and collaborative research environment. HRIA is implemented as a consortium of 7 universities and 8 small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), combining academic expertise with industrial innovation capacity.
The general objectives of HRIA are to:
Strengthen the national AI research ecosystem by uniting academic and business efforts.Stimulate original scientific creation and innovation in AI.Transfer research results into industry and society, supporting new products and services.Build a national knowledge base that is integrated into the European Research Area.The project runs from March 1, 2025, to December 31, 2029, during which time it will address multiple research, development, and innovation priorities. These include:
Trustworthy Artificial IntelligenceIntelligent and Autonomous SystemsSmart Human-Computer InterfacesHardware Technologies for AIAI in Medicine and HealthcareAI in Security and SpaceAI for Smart CitiesAI for the EnvironmentDevelopment and Testing of AI Prototypes and SystemsLooking ahead, HRIA is expected to serve as both a national nucleus for AI knowledge and innovation and a bridge to European initiatives. By fostering collaboration between academia and industry, it will enhance Romania’s capacity to develop cutting-edge technologies, generate economic value, and contribute to addressing global challenges through AI.

items.title: Research in areas of strategic interest
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The “Research in Areas of Strategic Interest” programme, part of Romania’s National RDI Plan (2022–2027), supports participation in international scientific initiatives. Its AI subprogramme funds research, development, and innovation projects that apply artificial intelligence across different sectors. The goal is to strengthen Romania’s AI ecosystem and promote the use of advanced technologies in society and the economy.

The “Research in Areas of Strategic Interest” programme is one of ten programmes under Romania’s National Research, Development and Innovation Plan (PNCDI IV) 2022–2027. It aims to boost the participation of Romanian research organisations in international projects while driving progress in fields that are strategically important for the country’s development. Within this framework, Subprogramme 9.8 – Artificial Intelligence is dedicated specifically to advancing AI research and applications.
The AI subprogramme seeks to:
Support cutting-edge AI research, development, and innovation in Romania.Develop cross-applicable AI solutions that can benefit multiple sectors, from healthcare to culture and administration.Encourage the widespread adoption of AI to create added value in economic, social, cultural, and public sectors.Strengthen the national AI ecosystem and align it with international standards and initiatives.To achieve these goals, the subprogramme funds a wide range of projects, including:
Research, development, and innovation (RDI) projects.Advanced research centres in AI.AI-based application development and industrial management solutions.Testing and validation platforms.Participation in global AI initiatives and projects.Public–private RDI partnerships.Data set management and processing platforms.Projects promoting AI in society.Pilot projects and joint research between Romanian diaspora experts and local researchers.Strategic projects for the long-term development of the national AI ecosystem.The Ministry of Research, Innovation and Digitalisation has committed to launching dedicated AI calls under this subprogramme, with research activities coordinated by the newly established National Authority for Research. Through this effort, Romania aims to create an integrated, well-funded AI research environment that both supports domestic innovation and increases the country’s visibility and competitiveness in the global AI landscape.

items.title: Institute for AI Mihai Drăgănescu
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The “Mihai Drăgănescu” Research Institute for Artificial Intelligence in Bucharest carries out advanced research in artificial intelligence and related fields. Its work covers areas such as machine learning, natural language processing, robotics, and intelligent systems. The institute contributes to both fundamental research and practical applications that support technological progress.

The “Mihai Drăgănescu” Research Institute for Artificial Intelligence, based in Bucharest, is a national centre dedicated to advancing knowledge and innovation in AI. Its mission is to combine fundamental and applied research to strengthen Romania’s role in the global AI research landscape. The institute is named after Mihai Drăgănescu, a leading Romanian scientist, and builds on his legacy of connecting science, technology, and society.
Research at the institute spans several domains, including:
Machine learning and data-driven modelsNatural language processing (NLP) and computational linguisticsIntelligent systems and decision-making technologiesRobotics and autonomous systemsComputer network architectures supporting the knowledge societyThe institute works at the intersection of theory and application, producing both academic contributions and real-world innovations. Its researchers develop methodologies, tools, and prototypes that can be applied across industries, while also training the next generation of AI specialists.
Looking forward, the institute aims to deepen international collaboration, strengthen interdisciplinary projects, and expand its role in supporting Romania’s digital transformation. By combining cutting-edge research with practical solutions, the institute positions itself as a key player in shaping how AI contributes to economic and social development.

items.title: ICIINNOLAB
items.org: National Institute for Research and Development in Informatics - ICI Bucharest
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The ICIINNOLAB project at ICI Bucharest created eight innovation laboratories focused on emerging and disruptive technologies, including AI, cybersecurity, and blockchain. These labs provide facilities and resources to support advanced research, talent development, and practical applications. The goal is to strengthen institutional performance and foster innovation in Romania’s digital ecosystem.

The National Institute for Research and Development in Informatics (ICI Bucharest) launched the project “Innovation laboratories for the purpose of increasing institutional performance and developing skills in the field of emerging and disruptive technologies – ICIINNOLAB.” The project established and operationalised eight specialised laboratories that focus on some of the most transformative areas of technology today:
Artificial Intelligence (AI)CybersecurityBlockchainInternet of Things (IoT)High-Performance Computing (HPC)Quantum Computing5G–6G NetworksMetaverseThe primary objective of ICIINNOLAB is to enhance the institute’s capacity for research and innovation while building national expertise in cutting-edge technologies. By creating dedicated spaces equipped with advanced infrastructure, the project supports:
Talent development by training researchers and professionals in next-generation technologies.Advanced research in key emerging fields.Practical solutions that address real-world challenges faced by industry and society.Beyond strengthening institutional performance, the project also seeks to increase Romania’s visibility in the global research community. The labs serve as a platform for interdisciplinary collaboration, where academic researchers, industry partners, and policymakers can work together to design and test innovative solutions.
Looking ahead, ICIINNOLAB is expected to play a central role in shaping Romania’s digital transformation. By combining expertise across multiple technology domains, the initiative will foster innovation, encourage cross-sectoral applications, and provide a foundation for future national and European projects in disruptive technologies.

items.title: AI Research Institute (ICIA)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The AI Research Institute (ICIA) at Cluj-Napoca Technical University was inaugurated in 2024 as part of the Romanian AI Hub. Equipped with high-performance computing systems and advanced research facilities, it focuses on developing innovative AI-driven solutions across multiple sectors. Its work spans areas such as smart cities, robotics, e-health, e-agriculture, and cybersecurity.

The AI Research Institute (ICIA) at Cluj-Napoca Technical University (UTCN) represents a major investment in Romania’s artificial intelligence ecosystem. Officially inaugurated with its first symposium in October 2024, the institute is part of the Romanian AI Hub and was constructed between 2023 and 2024, with additional facilities still under development. Its mission is to provide state-of-the-art infrastructure and expertise to generate innovative AI-based solutions for both industry and society.
ICIA is equipped with cutting-edge research infrastructure, including:
High-performance computing (HPC) systems.Specialised servers for deep learning and Big Data storage.Advanced platforms for modelling, simulation, optimisation, and design.The institute’s research addresses a broad range of domains, such as:
Internet of Things (IoT) and cyber-physical systems.Autonomous and connected mobility and smart city applications.Sensors and integrated circuits for intelligent systems.Advanced multimedia data processing (text, voice, video).Social and service robotics, with AI applied to non-industrial robotics.Cybersecurity and civilian space applications.Smart agriculture (e-agriculture) through robotics and digital technologies.E-administration and e-governance.E-health, including early diagnosis, telemedicine, and software modelling.Human–machine communication technologies, supported by AI and natural language processing.The goal of ICIA is not only to advance scientific knowledge but also to create practical solutions that can be applied across strategic sectors. By combining advanced computing power with interdisciplinary expertise, it fosters innovation and strengthens Romania’s contribution to European and global AI research.
Looking forward, ICIA is expected to become a hub for collaboration between academia, industry, and government, serving as both a training ground for highly skilled AI specialists and a platform for developing technologies with real-world impact.

items.title: AI Innovative Lab
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The AI Innovative Lab focuses on building advanced research and development capacity in artificial intelligence. Its mission is to develop skills and applications in areas such as bioinformatics, computer vision, and natural language processing. The lab also advances research in deep learning and other AI subfields to generate innovative solutions.

The AI Innovative Lab was established to strengthen research and development in artificial intelligence by creating a critical mass of expertise and skills. Its mission is to support high-performance applications across a wide range of AI subfields while fostering both fundamental and applied research.
The lab’s work spans several priority areas:
Bioinformatics and computational biology.Artificial vision and computer vision applications.Text analysis and natural language processing (NLP).Deep learning methods driving recent breakthroughs in AI.In addition, the lab conducts research in key theoretical and applied AI domains, including:
Inductive Logic Programming (ILP).Data mining and large-scale knowledge discovery.Knowledge representation techniques.Constraint logic programming, including constraint handling rules.Automatic reasoning and inference systems.Semantic web technologies.Intelligent information integration.Expert systems and knowledge-based systems.The overarching goal of the AI Innovative Lab is to bridge theoretical advances and practical applications. By cultivating specialised expertise and addressing real-world challenges, it contributes to the development of intelligent systems that can be applied in diverse fields such as healthcare, engineering, and information systems.
Looking forward, the lab aims to expand its research collaborations, strengthen interdisciplinary projects, and position itself as a centre of excellence for AI innovation. Through talent development, cutting-edge projects, and knowledge transfer, it supports both national and international efforts to advance the frontiers of artificial intelligence.

items.title: National Test Beds Network
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The National Test Beds Network in Portugal helps companies and researchers test and apply new AI and digital technologies. It provides access to real environments, equipment, and infrastructure for safe experimentation. The initiative supports collaboration across business, academia, and research to speed up digital transformation in key sectors.

The National Test Beds Network in Portugal complements the country’s Digital Innovation Hubs by creating spaces where new AI and digital solutions can be tested in real-world conditions. It was established to respond to the need for safe, practical environments that allow businesses, especially small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), to experiment with emerging technologies before deploying them more widely.
The initiative has three main objectives:
Accelerate AI and digital adoption through targeted testing and experimentation programmes.Provide infrastructure and technical support so that companies can trial new products, services, and processes in realistic settings.Promote collaboration among companies, universities, and research centres to modernise strategic sectors of the economy.Implementation focuses on bringing together public and private actors, ensuring that companies of different sizes and technological maturity levels have access to cutting-edge resources. By enabling practical experimentation, the network reduces the risks of innovation and increases the chances that AI solutions can be effectively integrated into business operations.
Looking ahead, the initiative is expected to expand in scope, building stronger institutional frameworks and extending access to more regions and industries. By scaling further, the National Test Beds Network could help Portugal establish itself as a leader in AI-driven transformation and enhance the competitiveness of its companies at both the national and European levels.

items.title: TEFs
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Poland is participating in two TEFs for AI:
agrifoodTEF – Test and Experiment Facilities for the Agri-Food Domain: Innovation and co-creation of sustainable agriculture tools. 
The Warsaw University of Technology is a partner in the project TEF Smart Cities & Communities: project “CitCom”.

agrifoodTEF – Test and Experiment Facilities for the Agri-Food Domain: Innovation and co-creation of sustainable agriculture tools: The Polish satellite node harnesses the expertise and resources of high-powered computing to provide services and assistance in robotic and AI-based technologies in sectors such as arable farming and food processing, implemented by the Center for Digital Trans-formation (Centrum Transformacji Cyfrowej) of the Poznan Technology Institut, part of the Instytuty Łukasiewicza, a network of business research centres The Warsaw University of Technology is a partner in the project TEF Smart Cities & Communities: project “CitCom"

items.title: Start in Poland, edition II - Acceleration Programs
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This programme of the Polish Development Fund (PFR) programme aims to create a favourable environment for start-ups, by supporting start-up acceleration programmes. The accelerators in the competition are required to choose min. 25% of startups operating from the following areas: Space Technologies, Fintech, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Smart Plastics, Microelectronics, Industrial Internet of Things/Augmented reality, Smart city, Cybersecurity, Bioeconomy, Pharmaceutical Biotechnology.

Purpose of the financing: Combining the potential of budding creative entrepreneurs with the infrastructure and experience of medium and large enterprises.
At least 400 start-ups are expected to take advantage of the opportunity to bring their innovative products up to a level that will allow them to test their solutions in cooperation with corporate partners. The participants will gain access to an enterprise’s knowledge, physical infrastructure, and sales channels. The programme’s main objective is to increase the survivability of start-ups, while allowing them to bring a product to market and win a crucial contract.

items.title: RNCA Supercomputers and Cloud Access
items.original_name: Fundação para a Ciência e a Tecnologia
items.org: the Portuguese Foundation for Science and Technology
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Fundação para a Ciência e a Tecnologia
items.body:
A call from the Portuguese Foundation for Science and Technology to facilitate access to the National Network for Advanced Computing (RNCA) for AI-related projects. These projects will benefit from RNCA’s HPC and cloud infrastructure, significantly supporting advanced AI research in Portugal. This call started in 2020 and has been renewed every year.

ADVANCED COMPUTING
Today, advanced computing is an essential tool for scientific, technological and economic development. Find out more about this concept and its use.
OPERATIONAL CENTERS
The Operational Centers provide the user community with HPC, HTC, Cloud and other computing services, particularly in terms of technological capacity.
ACCESS AND CALLS
RNCA computer resources are aimed at the research, technology and innovation/industry communities. They can request access public and private institutions from any scientific field.

items.title: Priority 1 of the EU Funds for Smart Economy 2021–2027
items.original_name: Program Funduszy Europejskich na rzecz Inteligentnej Gospodarki
items.org: Ministry of Development Funds and Regional Policy
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Program Funduszy Europejskich na rzecz Inteligentnej Gospodarki
items.body:
Within the programme, Priority 1 aims at directly supporting companies, with special focus on small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). As an incentive to investment in research and development, entrepreneurs have the ability to apply to a flexible combination of modules that include green and digital transition, R&D business infrastructure, internationalisation and support to skills in enterprises.

The project is fully consistent with EU priority objectives. The role of EIB support is to facilitate the financing of the related operational programmes and support their implementation within the shared management policy and legal framework; and ultimately to support the achievement of i.a. the redress of regional imbalances, the implementation of the Pillar of Social Rights, and the strengthening of the economic, social, and territorial cohesion of the Union.
 Poland - outside of Warsaw region - is designated an EIB Cohesion Region. The project therefore supports the strengthening of the EU's economic, social, and territorial cohesion. As for the sectorial public policy goals of the EIB, the multi-sector project is expected to contribute to Innovation, Digital and Human capital (IDHC, 54%), Sustainable Cities and Regions (SCI, 19%), Sustainable Energy and Natural resources (SENR, 19%), and SME development (8%).
 In the area of IDHC, the projects will increase the level of RDI, innovation enabling infrastructure, education and training, and healthcare which will lead to positive spill overs throughout the national economy. Under SCI, the project will support balanced territorial development, including the upgrading, replacement and reorganisation of urban infrastructure and public facilities which will positively impact quality of life for inhabitants. Concerning SENR, the project will further unlock the potential for energy efficiency improvements and renewable energy. 
The project will also protect the environment, biodiversity, and ecosystems, and through climate adaptation and disaster prevention invest in more resilient infrastructure, which reduces the risk of harm to life, property, and public services in the event of disaster. Finally, the project eases financial constraints for SMEs that arise from information asymmetries caused by the lack of track record for such companies and high screening costs for small investments.

items.title: PLLuM
items.org: The Polish Ministry of Digital Affairs
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
A consortium of six institutions, led by the Wrocław University of Science and Technology (PWr), have launched a project to develop the Polish Large Language Universal Model (PLLuM). The model is intended to be open source and free to use, and for it to form the basis of a Polish-speaking intelligent assistant that can help provide public services.

The PLLuM (Polish Large Language Model) project is an initiative aimed at creating an open Polish language model.
Polish language support
An important element of this project is the development of an extensive and diverse data set, reflecting the complexity of the Polish language.
Tools to support innovation
Through the development of tools such as the Intelligent Assistant, we will support innovation in the public and private sectors.
Open collaboration and ease of use
The PLLuM model will be made available under an open license. Models will be available for download via the Huggingface platform. A graphical interface (GUI) in the form of a chat is also available.
Safety and ethics
We make sure that our model is safe, free from harmful and untrue content, which is crucial when using it in public administration.

items.title: PFR Ventures
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This project of the Polish Development Fund (PFR) provides venture capital to VC firms as well as innovative companies, including AI start-ups.

PFR Ventures is the largest fund investor in the CEE region. They support the development of the local Venture Capital and Private Equity market, and more broadly, the innovation ecosystem. Through funds, they finance innovative small and medium enterprises across different growth stages.
The only investor is the Government of Poland, either directly or through the Polish Development Fund or Polish Development Bank (BGK).

items.title: National Digital Innovation Hubs (DIHs) Network
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The national network of European Digital Innovation Hubs (DIHs) in Portugal focuses on the adoption of advanced digital technologies such as AI, HPC, cloud computing, and cybersecurity. These hubs are supported by the National Innovation Agency (ANI) and the Testing Experimental Facility for AI.

The Digital Innovation Hubs (DIH) are structures that aim to centralize a set of services to support the digital transition of companies, under more accessible conditions, focusing this process on 3 disruptive technologies: AI, HPC and Cybersecurity.
The Hubs are essentially intended to help Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs), Start-ups and Public Administration (PA) adopt digital, providing various services for the digital transition.
In addition to the three priority technologies adopted by the European Commission, the Portuguese hubs cover the following areas:
Industry/manufacturingTourismMobilitySea economyConstructionCybersecurityRegional focusDefenceTelcos and ICTAgri-foodUrban sustainabilityHealthcareAI and data science

items.title: INFOSTRATEG
items.org: The National Centre for Research and Development
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This strategic programme of the National Center for Research and Development (NCBR) support on scientific research and development in the area of “Advanced information, telecommunications and mechatronic technologies”. In the first quarter of 2025, the NCBR also plans to announce another, eighth competition in the INFOSTRATEG strategic programme, with the goal to develop the Polish AI potential.

The specific objectives of the program are:
Creation of test data sets and creation of standards for selecting the best solutions;Developing Polish research potential in artificial intelligence;Significant increase in the market activity of Polish IT teams;Application of neural networks in robotics and automation;Creating tools based on blockchain technology to accelerate the development of the digital economy.

items.title: GenAI Team at the CaMiNO
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The University of Lodz has established Poland’s first university team dedicated to generative artificial intelligence at the Centre for Analysis, Modelling and Computational Science (Centrum Analiz, Modelowania i Nauk Obliczeniowych - CaMiNO), which pursues an interdisciplinary research approach in biology, maths, data analysis, finance, economics.

The main tasks of the Team established by the Regulation No. 166 of the Rector of the University of Lodz Rector of 29 September 2023 include:
analysis of trends related to the development of generative artificial intelligence and assessment of their relevance to the education sector and the conduct of research;close cooperation with external experts and institutions working for the responsible and ethical development of generative AI, including in particular the education and research sectors;identification of opportunities and possibilities for the use of generative AI tools at the University of Lodz, as well as potential threats resulting from their development for the scientific and research, teaching and administrative processes carried out at the university;analysis of the needs and expectations related to the development of generative artificial intelligence of all members of the academic community (students, researchers, teaching and administrative staff);promotion of knowledge of generative AI tools and the conditions for their use (legal, ethical, cultural, etc.) in the teaching, research and administrative processes among members of the academic community and recommendation of forms and tools to improve skills and competences within this area;promotion of good national and international practices in terms of using generative AI tools in the teaching, research and administrative processes. The Generative AI Team at the University of Lodz has been operating since 1 October 2023.

items.title: European Digital Innovation Hubs
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
There are 22 Digital Innovation Hubs in Poland, 11 of which are funded under the Digital Europe programme.

The purpose of EDIH HPC4Poland is to increase the competitiveness and innovation of North West Poland (NUTS1) manufacturing companies and public organizations by increasing awareness and availability of advanced digital tools and services based on safe, reliable and efficient High Performance Computing (HPC), including: cloud simulations (PaaS), sensor systems (IoT), AR/VR/MR, collaborative robots, AGV, AMR, additive technologies, AI and Big Data analysis. 
HPC4Poland EDIH is a feedback matrix and a true node of value and service exchange between research teams, suppliers and recipients of advanced concepts, methods and solutions in the target region and collaborating regions/EDIHs of the EU. Based on the resources and domain knowledge of competence centres (research units) and business partners (tool suppliers), the EDIH implements a comprehensive one-stop-shop digital transformation offer, currently unavailable on the Polish market to the 4 target markets: transportation/automotive, medicine/pharmaceutics, wood/furniture, agriculture/processing.

items.title: Centre of Excellence for AI R&D
items.original_name: Centro de Excelência para P&D em IA
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Centro de Excelência para P&D em IA
items.body:
The Centre of Excellence for AI R&D in Portugal is currently under development.

This centre aims to enhance Portugal’s AI innovation ecosystem through dedicated research and development in AI technologies.

items.title: BRIdge VC - TDJ Pitango Ventures fund
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This programme, building on the “Bridge VC” programme of the National Centre for Research and Development (NCBR) to support commercialisation of Polish R&D projects, and the Polish-Israel venture capital fund TDJ Pitango Ventures, helps technology start-ups access financing for R&D, and offers management and consulting assistance. So far, especially AI-focused companies have profited from this programme.

New fund on the market: TDJ Pitango VenturesNew Polish-Israeli TDJ Pitango Ventures fund will invest  in Polish technology companies.

items.title: Attract Digital Innovation Hub
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
As part of the network of EDIH, the Attract Digital Innovation Hub for AI and HPC supports SMEs and public entities in their digital transformation through the full exploitation of the synergetic potential between AI and HPC.

ATTRACT seeks to support the ongoing digital transition in Portugal and Europe, their objectives are:

items.title: Artificial Intelligence & Data Analysis Centre (AIDA)
items.org: Rzeczpospolita Polska | Narodowe Centrum Nauki | ARTIQ
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Artificial Intelligence & Data Analysis Centre (AIDA) is one of our four management centres of the public research centre NASK, focusing on coordinating, initiating and developing projects involving artificial intelligence applications, taking into account the needs of the administration, cybersecurity, education and the media. The goal of AIDA is to become a Central European centre of excellence specialising in artificial intelligence.

Advanced technologies are increasingly used to commit sophisticated criminal activities. Identifying, preventing and fighting modern crimes demands the implementation of ground-breaking technologies and methods. The EU-funded AIDA project is focussing on cybercrime and terrorism by approaching specific issues and challenges related to law enforcement agencies (LEAs) investigation and intelligence using pioneering machine learning and artificial intelligence methods.
The proposed solution aims to deliver a descriptive and predictive data analytics platform and related tools to prevent, detect, analyse, and combat criminal activities.
While cybercrime and terrorism pose distinct problems and may rely on different input datasets, the analysis of this data can benefit from the application of the same fundamental technology base framework, endowed with Artificial Intelligence and Deep Learning techniques applied to big data analytics, and extended and tailored with crime- and task- specific additional analytic capabilities and tools.

The resulting TRL-7 integrated, modular and flexible AIDA framework will include LE-specific effective, efficient and automated data mining and analytics services to deal with intelligence and investigation workflows, extensive content acquisition, information extraction and fusion, knowledge management and enrichment through novel applications of Big Data processing, machine learning, artificial intelligence, predictive and visual analytics. The final solution will reach Technology Readiness Level 7: system prototype demonstration in operational environment.
AIDA system and tools will be made available to LEAs through a secure sandbox environment that aims to raise the technological readiness level of the solutions through their application in operational environment with real data.

items.title: America's AI Action Plan
items.org: White House Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP)
items.category: National – Strategy
items.body:
The Action Plan sets forth policy goals for near-term execution by the Federal government and articulates policy recommendations in line with the President’s vision for US leadership in AI. It is articulated around three main pillars: innovation, infrastructure, and international diplomacy and security.

The Plan identifies over 90 Federal policy actions across three pillars – Accelerating Innovation, Building American AI Infrastructure, and Leading in International Diplomacy and Security – to be implemented by the Trump Administration. Key policies in the AI Action Plan include:
Exporting American AI: The Commerce and State Departments will partner with industry to deliver secure, full-stack AI export packages – including hardware, models, software, applications, and standards – to America’s friends and allies around the world.
 Promoting Rapid Buildout of Data Centers: Expediting and modernizing permits for data centers and semiconductor fabs, as well as creating new national initiatives to increase high-demand occupations like electricians and HVAC technicians.
 Enabling Innovation and Adoption: Removing onerous Federal regulations that hinder AI development and deployment, and seek private sector input on rules to remove.
 Upholding Free Speech in Frontier Models: Updating Federal procurement guidelines to ensure that the government only contracts with frontier large language model developers who ensure that their systems are objective and free from top-down ideological bias.

items.title: mAigov
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
mAigov is an AI-powered digital assistant integrated into Greece's unified public administration portal, gov.gr. Launched in December 2023 by the Ministry of Digital Governance, mAigov aims to streamline citizens' interactions with public services by simplifying access to information and procedures.

mAigov is an AI-powered digital assistant integrated into Greece's unified public administration portal, gov.gr. Launched in December 2023 by the Ministry of Digital Governance, mAigov aims to streamline citizens' interactions with public services by simplifying access to information and procedures.mAIgov initiative seeks to resolve the inefficiencies in public service delivery and leverage the opportunity to enhance digital governance. It aims to make public services more accessible, efficient, and user-friendly through the use of AI technology.Objectives:Improve the quality, speed, and accessibility of public services.Enhance citizen interaction with government services.Promote transparency and accountability in public administration.Key Features of mAigov:Natural Language Processing: Users can engage with mAigov through text or voice inputs in natural language, allowing for intuitive searches of the services they require. The assistant is trained on over 1,600 services available on gov.gr and more than 3,270 administrative procedures from the National Register of Administrative Procedures, "MITOS."Multilingual Support: To accommodate a diverse user base, mAigov supports interactions in 25 languages, including the 24 official languages of the European Union and Albanian. This feature is particularly beneficial for Greeks living abroad and non-Greek-speaking individuals seeking information on Greek public services.User-Friendly Interface: Accessible via mobile devices and computers, mAigov provides a straightforward and friendly interface. Users can submit inquiries and receive guidance on locating the services they need. At the end of each interaction, users have the option to evaluate their experience, contributing to the system's ongoing improvement.Scalability and Performance: In its beta phase, mAigov can handle up to 240 conversations per minute in Greek, with each session limited to five minutes to ensure efficient service. A queuing mechanism manages user traffic, maintaining service quality during peak times.mAIgov goes through continuous updates and integration with more government services.mAIgov platform can scale by expanding its language capabilities and integrating with additional public services. This will allow broader access and improved service delivery for both Greek citizens and international users.Since its launch, mAIgov has evolved by increasing its language support to 25 languages and expanding its service offerings. It has seen significant user engagement and continuous improvements based on user feedback.Results: Over 1.6 million interactions with the bot, since its launch.

items.title: embrAIsme - Improving Conditions and Policies for SMEs to Embrace AI
items.original_name: embrAIsme - Improving Conditions and Policies for SMEs to Embrace AI
items.org: Austrian Promotional Bank (AWS); Federal Chancellery of Austria; Directorate General for Digitalisation and E-Government
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: embrAIsme - Improving Conditions and Policies for SMEs to Embrace AI
items.body:
EmbrAIsme is an Interreg Europe project co-financed by the Austrian Federal Chancellery which aims to encourage uptake of AI by SMEs, in particular by raising awareness of AI and the importance of AI skills, facilitating access to funding and building tools to ease the compliance burden of SMEs.

The Interreg Europe project embrAIsme, led by Austria Wirtschaftsservice (aws), fosters collaboration between partners from Finland, Ireland, Spain, Portugal, Bulgaria, Serbia, and Slovenia to enhance SME support for AI adoption. Running for four years from April 2024, the project is co-financed by the Federal Chancellery of Austria and aims to accelerate AI integration in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) by addressing cultural resistance in SMEs, skill gaps, regulatory challenges, and limited funding access.AI offers vast potential for productivity, innovation, and competitiveness, yet many SMEs struggle with adoption due to internal resistance, lack of expertise, and uncertainty about AI's value. Structural barriers such as funding constraints, regulatory complexity, skill shortages, and insufficient infrastructure further hinder progress. embrAIsme seeks to create an enabling environment for AI adoption by improving policies, providing financial incentives, clarifying regulations, and raising awareness.The project focuses on six core intervention areas: Government Initiatives and Support, Access to Finance, Legal and Ethical Issues, Human Capital & Skills, Infrastructure and Technology Access, and Collaborative Networks and Ecosystems. Through study visits, workshops with AI experts and a strong focus on networking, policy recommendations will be provided to specific policy instruments to improve concepts and frameworks of funding opportunities and regulatory guidance needed for AI integration. By fostering knowledge-sharing, leadership engagement, and hands-on training, the initiative ensures SMEs across diverse regions benefit from AI-driven advancements.As AI adoption grows, the project will play a key role in maintaining SME competitiveness in an increasingly digital economy. Initial findings highlight cultural resistance in SMEs as a major challenge, prompting a stronger focus on leadership engagement, best-practice case studies, and AI-readiness initiatives. By continuously refining its strategies based on stakeholder insights, embrAIsme ensures that European SMEs are well-equipped to leverage AI for sustainable growth and innovation.

items.title: Working Party on AI Governance (AIGO)
items.category: AI Policy Frameworks and Initiatives (intergovernmental or supranational)
items.body:

OECD member governments nominate working party members and are primarily national officials responsible for AI policies in their perspective countries.The working party oversees and gives direction to the DPC work programme on AI policy and governance. This includes: analysis of the design, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national AI policies and action plans; AI impact assessment; approaches for trustworthy and accountable AI; supervising measurement and data efforts as part of the OECD.AI Observatory's pillar on trends & data; and conducting foresight work on AI and on related emerging technologies.AIGO: supports the implementation of OECD standards relating to AI; serves as a forum for exchanging experience and documenting approaches for advancing trustworthy AI that benefits people and planet; develops tools, methods and guidance to advance the responsible stewardship of trustworthy AI, including the OECD.AI Policy Observatory and Globalpolicy.AI platforms; supports the collaboration between governments and other stakeholders on assessing and managing AI risks; conducts outreach to non-OECD Member countries to support the implementation of OECD standards relating to AI.

items.title: White Paper on Artificial Intelligence
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Within the framework of a wide range of digital initiatives taken by the European Commission, the White Paper on AI promotes a coordinated EU approach on the human and ethical implications of AI.

From 19 February to 14 June 2020, citizens and stakeholders shared their opinions on the forthcoming policy and regulatory measures regarding artificial intelligence (AI). The European Commission aimed to encourage the adoption of AI while simultaneously addressing the associated risks by proposing a White Paper outlining policy and regulatory options for creating an "ecosystem for excellence and trust." This document was released on 19 February 2020, alongside an online survey that focused on three key areas:- Specific initiatives to support, develop, and promote AI across the EU economy and public administration.- Potential regulatory frameworks for AI in the future.- Safety and liability considerations related to AI.This report presents a "future regulatory framework" for the EU to navigate the evolving landscape of AI technology. It adopts a comprehensive approach, suggesting methods to make AI accessible to small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and addressing appropriate regulations for high-risk applications and liability in cases of physical or material harm.- The proposed "Ecosystem of Excellence" highlights the necessity of collaboration with member states to invest in AI research and development. Education should enhance AI-related skills and incorporate ethical training. Facilitating access to AI technology for SMEs will accelerate its development and adoption. The private sector should play a role in the research and innovation agenda, particularly through significant public-private partnerships. The White Paper identifies healthcare and transportation as sectors poised to benefit from AI-driven products. Investments should focus on ensuring access to data and computing infrastructure. Additionally, there should be international collaboration among global AI stakeholders to promote EU standards and create a "level playing field."- The "ecosystem of trust" encompasses: (1) human agency and oversight, (2) technical robustness and safety, (3) privacy and data governance, (4) transparency, (5) diversity, non-discrimination, and fairness, (6) societal and environmental well-being, and (7) accountability.- Legislative Updates- Current legislation must be revised to account for AI. The integration of AI technologies into products and services may introduce new safety risks for users. Issues in AI design may arise from the quality and availability of data or other challenges related to machine learning. While some risks are not exclusive to AI-dependent products and services, the use of AI may exacerbate these risks. A lack of clear safety regulations addressing these concerns could lead to legal uncertainty for businesses in the EU that market AI-related products.

items.title: White House Summit on AI in Government

items.org: Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: White House Summit on AI in Government
items.body:
On 9 September 2019, the White House hosted its Summit on AI in Government.

Over the last several years, the private sector has demonstrated that AI can improve the quality of services, create new products, and increase efficiency. The Federal government now has the opportunity to improve its services on behalf of the American people by partnering with the private sector to leverage this knowledge and capability. Some Federal agencies are already leading the way by using AI to process grant applications, check Federal solicitations for regulatory compliance, improve nautical charts, process satellite imagery, perform predictive maintenance, and much more. Still, there is significant room for growth. A number of inter-related challenges must be addressed ” some technical, some requiring process changes, and some involving talent and workforce issues.The initiative has the following objective(s):To find near-term solutions to these challenges to improve government services using AI.

items.title: Voluntary Code of Conduct on the Responsible Development and Management of Advanced Generative AI Systems
items.original_name: Voluntary Code of Conduct on the Responsible Development and Management of Advanced Generative AI Systems
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.document_name: Voluntary Code of Conduct on the Responsible Development and Management of Advanced Generative AI Systems
items.body:
The code identifies measures that should be applied in advance of binding regulation pursuant to the Artificial Intelligence and Data Act by all firms developing or managing the operation of a generative AI system with general-purpose capabilities, as well as additional measures that should be taken by firms developing or managing the operations of these systems that are made widely available for use, and which are therefore subject to a wider range of potentially harmful or inappropriate use.

The initiative has the following objectives:In undertaking this voluntary commitment, developers and managers of advanced generative systems commit to working to achieve the following outcomes: 1. Accountability “ Firms understand their role with regard to the systems they develop or manage, put in place appropriate risk management systems, and share information with other firms as needed to avoid gaps.2. Safety “ Systems are subject to risk assessments, and mitigations needed to ensure safe operation are put in place prior to deployment.3. Fairness and Equity “ Potential impacts with regard to fairness and equity are assessed and addressed at different phases of development and deployment of the systems.4. Transparency “ Sufficient information is published to allow consumers to make informed decisions and for experts to evaluate whether risks have been adequately addressed.5. Human Oversight and Monitoring “ System use is monitored after deployment, and updates are implemented as needed to address any risks that materialize.6. Validity and Robustness “ Systems operate as intended, are secure against cyber attacks, and their behaviour in response to the range of tasks or situations to which they are likely to be exposed is understood.

items.title: Voluntary AI Safety Standard
items.org: Department of Industry, Science, and Resources
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
The Voluntary AI Safety Standard gives practical guidance to all Australian organisations on how to safely and responsibly use and innovate with AI.The standard consists of 10 voluntary guardrails that apply to all organisations throughout the AI supply chain. They include transparency and accountability requirements across the supply chain. They also explain what developers and deployers of AI systems must do.

The 10 guardrails at a glance:1. Establish, implement and publish an accountability process including governance, internal capability and a strategy for regulatory compliance.2. Establish and implement a risk management process to identify and mitigate risks.3. Protect AI systems, and implement data governance measures to manage data quality and provenance.4. Test AI models and systems to evaluate model performance and monitor the system once deployed.5. Enable human control or intervention in an AI system to achieve meaningful human oversight across the life cycle.6. Inform end-users regarding AI-enabled decisions, interactions with AI and AI-generated content.7. Establish processes for people impacted by AI systems to challenge use or outcomes.8. Be transparent with other organisations across the AI supply chain about data, models and systems to help them effectively address risks.9. Keep and maintain records to allow third parties to assess compliance with guardrails.10. Engage your stakeholders and evaluate their needs and circumstances, with a focus on safety, diversity, inclusion and fairness.

items.title: Vision on Generative AI
items.org: Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations (BZK) | Ministry of Economic Affairs and Climate Policy (EZK) | Ministry of Education, Culture and Science (OCW)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
As one of the first EU Member States, the Dutch government has presented a vision on generative AI. In this vision, the government emphasizes the urgent need to take action in light of the opportunities and challenges presented by this disruptive yet promising technology. The vision aligns with a series of investments worth millions of euros already made by research institutions, private enterprises, and the government, all aimed at AI, including generative AI, in the Netherlands.

Specific areas mentioned include:  Safety: Ensuring the safe development and use of generative AI, including mitigating misuse, accidents, and systemic safety risks. Justice: Ensuring lawful development and application that takes into account existing laws and regulations, equal opportunities, and non-discrimination. Well-being and autonomy: Promoting applications of generative AI that serve human well-being and secure human autonomy. Sustainability and prosperity: Encouraging generative AI that contributes to sustainability and increases prosperity. These policy areas imply a wide spectrum of actions, from promoting innovation (e.g. by pilots and promoting an AI-ecosystem) and education to engaging in international collaborations and enforcing and implementing regulation. The goal is to find a balance between leveraging the benefits of generative AI and managing the risks and challenges. The development of the government-wide vision on generative AI was characterized by an open approach with a wide range of involved stakeholders. These stakeholders ranged from experts in various domains to the general public, and their input was collected and assessed in various ways. Key points of this approach include:  Sectoral Sessions: Between June and November 2023, multiple sessions were held in sectors such as public administration, healthcare, employment, and the economy. During these sessions, input for the vision was collected, and it was continually checked that the vision covered the correct aspects. These conversations will continue into 2024. Collaborations: In collaboration with the ECP (Electronic Commerce Platform) and the Dutch AI Coalition (NL-AIC), meetings were organized with stakeholders from the media, higher education, healthcare, and the police to discuss ethical dilemmas surrounding generative AI. Awareness and Impact Analysis: Sessions were organized with Dutch citizens to raise awareness about generative AI and to gain insights into how people perceive the impact of generative AI on their lives and the role of the government in integrating this technology into society. Broad Representation: A working group on generative AI was set up with participants from various ministries, provinces (IPO), and municipalities (VNG) to ensure that the vision reflects a broad perspective on generative AI. Advisory Group: An advisory group with members representing diverse societal perspectives was established to test the vision from various angles. This approach underscores the importance of inclusivity and collaboration with a broad range of stakeholders to arrive at a well-supported and informed vision on generative AI.

items.title: UN Secretary-General's High-level Advisory Body on Artificial Intelligence (HLAB-AI)
items.original_name: UN Secretary-General's High-level Advisory Body on Artificial Intelligence (HLAB-AI)
items.category: AI Governance Bodies and Mechanisms (intergovernmental or supranational)
items.document_name: UN Secretary-General's High-level Advisory Body on Artificial Intelligence (HLAB-AI)
items.body:
HLAB-AI, established in October 2023, comprises 39 preeminent AI leaders from 33 countries across all regions and multiple sectors, serving in their personal capacity. In its final report, the Body presented seven recommendations for global cooperation on AI governance. The recommendations provided inspiration for Member States adopting the Global Digital Compact during the Summit of the Future in September 2024.

The United Nations Secretary-General's High-level Advisory Body on Artificial Intelligence (HLAB-AI) released its final report Governing AI for Humanity in September 2024. It was built on months of extensive global consultations and the publication of an interim report in December 2023. The uniquely diverse Advisory Body was the world's first and most representative expert group capable of reflecting humanity's aspirations for AI.The report was the product of extensive consultations, involving more than 2,000 participants across all regions of the world. The HLAB-AI conducted 18 deep-dive discussions on key issues, reviewed more than 250 written submissions from over 150 organizations and 100 individuals, and held over 50 global engagements. The advisory body also carried out an AI Risk Pulse - the most comprehensive AI horizon scanning exercise to date - and an opportunity scan to assess emerging trends.The report outlined a blueprint for addressing AI-related risks and sharing its transformative potential globally, including by: Urging the UN to lay the foundations of the first globally inclusive and distributed architecture for AI governance based on international cooperation; Proposing seven recommendations to address gaps in current AI governance arrangements; Calling on all governments and stakeholders to work together in governing AI to foster the development and protection of all human rights.The HLAB-AI's report identified key gaps in the current international AI governance landscape, and proposed measures to address these gaps. This included light institutional mechanisms to complement existing efforts and foster global AI governance arrangements that are agile, adaptive and effective to keep pace with AI's evolution.The 7 key recommendations identified are: 1) International Scientific Panel on AI; 2) Policy Dialogue on AI Governance; 3) AI Standards Exchange; 4) Capacity Development Network; 5) Global Fund for AI; 6) Global AI Data Framework and 7) AI Office in the United Nations Secretariat.The Final Report and its recommendations were widely acknowledged and praised internationally. It was covered in major news platforms throughout all the continents, with over 275 news pieces around the launch of the report. 4 Op-Eds written by the Body members were published in global media and the recommendations were also covered in several broadcast hits.During the UN Summit of the Future, several recommendations in the Final Report were taken up in the Global Digital Compact. World leaders on AI also gathered during the Summit to discuss how to secure a better digital future for all. In many segments, the leaders acknowledged the recommendations and emphasised the importance of global cooperation and the role of the UN.The Body concluded in October 2026, but the recommendations and analysis are still widely used in discussions and studies surrounding global AI governance.

items.title: U.S. Patent and Trademark Office Report on Public Views on AI and Intellectual Property Policy
items.original_name: U.S. Patent and Trademark Office Report on Public Views on AI and Intellectual Property Policy
items.org: United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: U.S. Patent and Trademark Office Report on Public Views on AI and Intellectual Property Policy
items.body:
The Report takes a comprehensive look at a wide variety of stakeholder views on the impact of AI across the intellectual property (IP) landscape, including patent, trademark, copyright, and trade secret policy, as well as developing issues about database protection.

Building on the momentum of those discussions, on 27 August 2019, the USPTO issued a request for comments (RFC) on patenting AI inventions.The RFC sought feedback from stakeholders on a variety of patent policy issues, such as AI's impact on inventorship and ownership, eligibility, disclosure, and the level of ordinary skill in the art. The comment period closed in November 2019. The USPTO received 99 comments from a wide range of stakeholders, including individuals, associations, corporations, and foreign IP offices. In October 2019, the USPTO issued a second RFC related to the impact of AI on other IP policy areas, including copyrights, trademarks, database protections, and trade secret law. The comment period for the second RFC closed in January 2020. The USPTO received 98 comments from a wide range of stakeholders. Following the conclusion of the comment periods, a team of experts assembled from across the USPTO examined the responses and generated the Report on Public Views on AI and Intellectual Property Policy.The initiative has the following objective(s):To promote the understanding and reliability of IP rights in relation to AI technology.To ensure that appropriate IP incentives are in place to encourage further innovation in and around this critical area.

items.title: Twelfth Development Plan (2024-2028)
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
The Twelfth Development Plan covers all areas of Turkiye development for the next four years from a holistic perspective and whole-of-government approach. One of the main priorities of the plan is digital technologies including AI.

The Development Plan aims to provide a long-term perspective and unity of purpose for all members of society. The development process has followed a holistic approach based on the principles of human orientation, participation, inclusiveness, accountability, and transparency. The Plan was developed through a participatory approach with contributions from the public sector, private sector, civil society representatives, and academic circles. During the preparatory phase, 60 specialized commissions and 27 working groups were established, and approximately 8,500 people participated in the meetings. Opinions and suggestions on the Plan priorities were received from over 43,000 participants through an online 'citizen survey'. Additionally, the Plan text was informed by over 60 years of planning experience, consultations with non-governmental organizations (NGOs), academics, private sector representatives, and public institutions and organizations, including ministries. The results of these consultations were carefully considered in the preparation of the Plan.The initiative has the following objectives:- The development of fundamental artificial intelligence technologies will be supported and their use will be widespread.- Collaboration between the public, university, and private sectors in the field of artificial intelligence will be enhanced.- International cooperation in the field of artificial intelligence will be increased.- Necessary legal arrangements will be made for the needs arising from artificial intelligence technologies.- The legal and ethical framework for artificial intelligence applications will be established.- A public data space infrastructure will be implemented to enhance institutional capacity through inter-agency advanced data analytics and artificial intelligence projects.

items.title: Trialling Automated Vehicle Technologies in Public
