The National AI Centre will be established to help drive business adoption, development and use of transformative AI technologies across the Australian ecosystem.

The initiative has the following objective(s):Establish a National AI Centre to provide a centralised platform to increase visibility and drive a co-ordinated Australian artificial intelligence ecosystem.Lower barriers to entry and boost capability to adopt, develop and use AI technologies.Co-ordinate Australia's AI ecosystem to engage with international and domestic markets, supporting economic and productivity growth and job creation.Establish deeper connections and relationships between Australian and international AI ecosystems and markets to promote a trusted, secure, and responsible future.2023-24 Budget extends funding to the National AI Centre to support the Responsible AI Network (RAIN) to strengthen AI governance and industry capability.

items.title: National AI Advisory Committee's Subcommittee on Law Enforcement
items.original_name: National AI Advisory Committee's Subcommittee on Law Enforcement
items.org: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), U.S. Department of Commerce
items.category: National – AI governance bodies or mechanisms
items.document_name: National AI Advisory Committee's Subcommittee on Law Enforcement
items.body:
As directed by the National AI Initiative Act of 2020 (DIVISION E, SEC. 5104e), the National AI Advisory Committee will establish a subcommittee that will consider matters related to the use of AI in law enforcement.

The initiative has the following objective(s):To provide advice to the President on topics that include bias, security of data, the adoptability of AI for security or law enforcement, and legal standards that include those that ensure that AI use is consistent with privacy rights, civil rights and civil liberties, and disability rights.

items.title: National AI Advisory Committee
items.category: National – AI governance bodies or mechanisms
items.body:
The NAIAC is tasked with providing an independent assessment of the Initiative and making recommendations to the President and the NAIIO on topics related to AI R&D, ethics, standards, education, technology transfer, commercial application, security, and economic competitiveness.

The National Artificial Intelligence Advisory Committee (NAIAC) was established under the National AI Initiative Act of 2020 as part of the United States' broader strategy to promote the responsible and effective development and deployment of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies. The initiative addresses the growing need for expert, multi-stakeholder guidance on how the federal government should advance AI in alignment with democratic values, national competitiveness, innovation, and public trust. As AI becomes increasingly integral to economic development, public services, national security, and societal well-being, NAIAC's role is to ensure that U.S. AI policy is forward-looking, inclusive, and strategically coordinated.The committee advises the President and the National AI Initiative Office on a wide range of AI-related issues, including research and development priorities, ethical and trustworthy AI principles, workforce impacts, international collaboration, and regulatory frameworks. It brings together experts from academia, industry, civil society, and government to provide balanced and evidence-based recommendations. Its key objectives are to ensure U.S. global leadership in AI innovation while upholding civil liberties, enhancing public-private partnerships, and guiding national investments in AI education and infrastructure.NAIAC is expected to evolve into a permanent fixture of the federal AI governance landscape. It operates through regular meetings, public consultations, and the publication of formal reports and recommendations. Over time, the initiative aims to institutionalize ethical and policy guardrails for AI use across sectors, support the adoption of technical standards, and promote coordinated federal AI actions through transparent and inclusive policymaking. As AI technologies scale, the committee's work is crucial in guiding responsible implementation across critical domains such as healthcare, education, transportation, defense, and justice.Since its formation, NAIAC has already begun shaping national dialogue on trustworthy AI. It has issued public recommendations on AI risk management, equity, algorithmic accountability, and public sector AI adoption. Future efforts may include expanding subcommittees on specialized topics like generative AI, privacy-preserving machine learning, and AI for social good. The committee's adaptive structure and ongoing engagement with stakeholders position it to respond to fast-evolving challenges and opportunities presented by AI innovation.

items.title: NSW AI Assurance Framework
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
The NSW AI Assurance Framework is a set of rules by the New South Wales government to ensure AI systems are safe and fair in public services. It helps government staff use AI responsibly and protects the public from risks. This initiative was created to build trust in AI and make sure it works well for everyone.

The AI Assurance Framework is intended to be used at all major points of an AI project's lifecycle “ from start to finish. Project teams should continually assess their projects against the Framework to ensure their project abides by the ethical principles. As best practice, project leaders and policy makers should review the Framework and consider each of its questions as part of the first steps in any AI project design process, and as part of any review of an existing AI solution.The initiative has the following objective(s):

The initiative has the following objective(s):To help develop NSW's AI Assurance Framework, which will be used to determine the level of risk based on the data that the solution is using and the types of decisions it will generate.

items.title: NSF Program on Fairness in AI
items.original_name: NSF Program on Fairness in AI
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: NSF Program on Fairness in AI
items.body:
NSF and Amazon are partnering to jointly support computational research focused on fairness in AI, with the goal of contributing to trustworthy AI systems that are readily accepted and deployed to tackle grand challenges facing society.

The NSF Program on Fairness in Artificial Intelligence addresses critical challenges related to bias, transparency, accountability, and inclusivity in AI systems. As AI technologies increasingly impact society, concerns over unfair treatment, discrimination, and opaque decision-making processes have grown. This initiative aims to foster research that develops methods and tools to detect, mitigate, and prevent unfairness in AI algorithms, ensuring that AI systems are equitable and trustworthy for all users.The primary objectives of the program include advancing fundamental understanding of fairness in AI, promoting interdisciplinary research combining computer science with social, behavioral, and economic sciences, and supporting the development of frameworks that enable explainability and accountability. By encouraging collaboration among diverse academic fields, the initiative seeks to create AI systems that respect social values and protect against unintended harmful consequences.Looking forward, the program is expected to evolve by integrating emerging research findings into practical applications, influencing policy, and setting standards for ethical AI deployment. Continued funding and collaboration with industry partners like Amazon will help institutionalize these efforts, expand research capacity, and scale innovations broadly across sectors. The program's outputs are anticipated to shape future AI development toward more inclusive and responsible technologies.Since its inception, the initiative has grown to support a wide range of projects and foster a vibrant research community focused on AI fairness. Periodic updates and expanded funding opportunities reflect the evolving landscape of AI challenges and the increasing importance of embedding fairness as a core principle in AI systems worldwide.

items.title: NSF Funding Opportunities with Special Emphasis on AI
items.original_name: NSF Funding Opportunities with Special Emphasis on AI
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects

The U.S. National Science Foundation (NSF) supports a wide range of funding opportunities that emphasize artificial intelligence (AI) research, education, and workforce development. These initiatives aim to advance the frontiers of AI while addressing critical societal challenges, promoting economic growth, and maintaining U.S. leadership in science and technology.A central part of NSF's efforts is the National AI Research Institutes program, which funds multi-disciplinary, multi-institutional centers across priority areas such as trustworthy AI, AI for health, education, climate, and cybersecurity. In addition, NSF provides grants for investigator-led projects through its core programs, enabling both foundational and applied AI research.The initiative also focuses on expanding access to AI research infrastructure, fostering collaborations across academia, industry, and government, and promoting responsible, inclusive innovation. NSF places particular emphasis on training a diverse AI workforce and integrating AI into education systems.Over time, NSF's AI initiatives have evolved in response to national strategies and emerging technologies. Looking forward, NSF plans to scale these efforts by expanding institute networks, deepening partnerships, and aligning investments with long-term national goals for AI development and ethical deployment.

items.title: NITRD Supplement to the President's FY2020 Budget
items.original_name: NITRD Supplement to the President's FY2020 Budget
items.org: Networking and Information Technology Research and Development (NITRD) Program
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: NITRD Supplement to the President's FY2020 Budget
items.body:
The NITRD Supplement to the President's FY2020 Budget outlines federal priorities for research in networking and information technology, including AI. It helps coordinate funding and goals across multiple government agencies. The initiative aims to advance innovation, security, and economic growth through strategic investment in emerging technologies.

The NITRD (Networking and Information Technology Research and Development) Supplement to the President's FY2020 Budget is a strategic document that outlines the federal government's priorities and planned investments in networking, information technology, and artificial intelligence research. The initiative seeks to address the growing need for coordinated research efforts to accelerate technological innovation, improve cybersecurity, and maintain U.S. leadership in critical technology areas. By providing clear guidance on funding priorities and collaboration among agencies, it helps avoid duplication and enhances the impact of federal research programs.The primary objectives of the initiative are to foster innovation in AI and related technologies, support the development of secure and trustworthy computing infrastructure, and stimulate economic growth through technology advancement. It also aims to improve the coordination of research across various federal agencies, ensuring resources are used efficiently and breakthroughs in science and technology are translated into real-world applications. The initiative prioritizes research that can address pressing societal challenges while maintaining U.S. competitiveness in the global technology landscape.Looking ahead, the initiative is expected to evolve by expanding its focus areas in response to emerging technology trends and national priorities. As AI and networking technologies advance rapidly, the program will continue to adapt its strategies to include new research themes such as explainable AI, AI ethics, and advanced computing infrastructure. Institutionalization will involve ongoing collaboration between federal agencies, academia, and industry partners to scale research efforts and accelerate technology transfer. Over time, the NITRD program has grown to include a broader range of agencies and research topics, reflecting the increasing importance of AI and information technology in all sectors of the economy and government.Since its inception, the NITRD initiative has been updated regularly to reflect changing technological landscapes and policy priorities. The FY2020 supplement builds upon previous budget supplements by emphasizing interdisciplinary research and the integration of AI into various domains. This continuous evolution ensures that the initiative remains relevant and effective in supporting the United States' position as a global leader in networking and information technology research and development.

items.title: Methodology to Identify Lessons Learned
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The project seeks to improve the capture of lessons learned in organizations, avoiding the repetition of errors and promoting continuous improvement. Many companies do not document learning due to fear, emotions or lack of time. ChatGPT was trained with a methodology to formulate lessons objectively and quickly, reducing tensions in meetings and improving accuracy. It benefits project teams by generating useful knowledge without friction or long consensus processes.

Many organizations do not document or analyze their lessons learned for fear of criticism, sanctions, or simply because of time pressure on projects. This leads to the repetition of errors and the loss of opportunities for improvement. In addition, the lack of an organizational culture that encourages reflection prevents the generation of useful knowledge for future initiatives.    The objective is to systematize the identification and documentation of lessons learned through artificial intelligence (AI), specifically ChatGPT, to ensure an objective, structured, and efficient process. The aim is for teams to be able to record positive and negative experiences without bias or tension, allowing for continuous improvement in project management.     AI is expected to facilitate the identification of lessons learned in minutes, optimizing decision-making. In addition, the knowledge generated is expected to be reused in new projects, institutionalizing a learning management process that encompasses identification, documentation, dissemination, reuse, and evaluation. In the long term, the impact of using these lessons to improve organizational efficiency and evidence-based decision-making will be measured.    Initially, lessons learned were identified through meetings between participants. However, the lack of a culture of sharing mistakes made consensus difficult. To overcome this barrier, AI was implemented to generate lessons learned objectively and without personal judgment. Today, the process has evolved into a more structured system that includes identification, documentation, dissemination, and evaluation of organizational learning.

items.title: Medical Research Future Fund
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Australian Government provides funding for research through the Medical Research Future Fund (MRFF) and the National Health and Medical Research Council (NHMRC).

The Medical Research Future Fund (MRFF) is a $20 billion long-term investment by the Australian Government designed to transform health and medical research and innovation. It aims to improve the health and wellbeing of Australians by supporting research across the full innovation pipeline”from early-stage discovery to commercialisation and clinical application. Guided by the Australian Medical Research and Innovation Strategy and Priorities, the MRFF is implemented with oversight from the Australian Medical Research Advisory Board (AMRAB), ensuring funding is aligned with national priorities and scientific merit through peer-reviewed, competitive grant processes.One of the MRFF's key challenges is addressing critical funding gaps along the research and development pipeline, particularly the "second valley of death"”the stage where promising medical innovations often fail to advance due to lack of commercialisation support. To counter this, the MRFF has established targeted programs such as the Biomedical Translation Bridge and Biomedical Translation Fund, which help early and late-stage ventures move from research to real-world medical products. These initiatives connect researchers with industry expertise, training, infrastructure, and access to capital.The MRFF also focuses on fostering bold, high-impact "research missions" to tackle pressing national health challenges. These include the Genomics Health Futures Mission (GHFM), which integrates genomics into mainstream healthcare, and initiatives supporting the use of Artificial Intelligence in health. With over $300 million invested in medical research commercialisation alone, the MRFF actively strengthens Australia's biotechnology and medtech industries while creating new jobs and advancing health outcomes.Over time, the MRFF has expanded its scope through the $5 billion, 10-year MRFF Investment Plan and the National Health and Medical Industry Growth Plan. These frameworks institutionalise long-term support for medical innovation by embedding research excellence into national health policy and economic strategy. As it scales, the MRFF is poised to be a cornerstone of Australia's knowledge economy, driving health innovation, commercial growth, and global competitiveness.

items.body:
Mechanisms for attracting foreign and returning domestic experts to strengthen Slovenia's position in global digitisation trends

Identification of solutions that would allow the implementation of appropriately adapted activities in the Republic of Slovenia in a way that would enable their widespread and effective use.- In-depth study and evaluation of programmes based on the example of the State of Israel, with a focus on digital entrepreneurship, industrial and high-tech disciplines (e.g., The Israel Brain Gain Programme, Back to Tech, Israeli Houses, Study in Isreal and other programmes). Emphasis on the study of programmes aimed at attracting foreign professionals to Israel and programmes aimed at supporting the return of Israelis living abroad.- Examine the criteria for the implementation of programmes in Israel and, as a consequence, identify the real needs, opportunities and benefits for the adaptation and transfer of the selected programmes to the Republic of Slovenia.

items.title: Mauritius Artificial Intelligence AI Strategy
items.org: Ministry of Information Technology, Communication and Innovation (ITCI)
items.category: National – Strategy
items.body:
The Mauritius AI Strategy outlines how AI could support key sectors like agriculture, health, FinTech, transport, and manufacturing. It identifies national challenges and opportunities through SWOT analysis. The strategy aimed to guide future development, though it lacked detailed implementation plans and was only partially followed up by the creation of the Mauritius Emerging Technologies Council.

The Mauritius Artificial Intelligence (AI) Strategy was developed to explore the potential application of AI technologies across key national industries. Recognizing AI as a transformative force, the initiative aims to position Mauritius to leverage AI for economic development, increased productivity, and improved public service delivery. The strategy targets six major sectors: agriculture, health, FinTech, transport, manufacturing, and the ocean economy, offering a sector-specific SWOT analysis to outline opportunities, risks, and readiness.The main objective of the strategy was to identify how AI could support national priorities, enhance innovation capacity, and address challenges such as limited digital infrastructure, low AI expertise, and resource constraints. The strategy also responds to global shifts, where countries are racing to integrate AI into their economies, ensuring Mauritius is not left behind. By laying out general recommendations and priority areas, the initiative sought to guide both public and private stakeholders toward coordinated AI development.However, while the strategy was validated by a working group, it lacked a robust implementation plan, dedicated funding, or clearly defined accountability mechanisms. It recommended the creation of a Mauritius Artificial Intelligence Council (MAIC) to oversee governance, consisting of 10 members. This body, however, was never fully institutionalized. In 2022, the Mauritius Emerging Technologies Council (METC) was established as a broader evolution of the MAIC. Despite its creation, the METC has not focused directly on enacting the original strategy's recommendations, due in part to the significant resources and cross-sectoral collaboration required.Looking forward, the future of AI development in Mauritius will likely depend on enhanced coordination, institutional commitment, and the development of a clear action framework. For the initiative to succeed, stronger multi-stakeholder partnerships, investment in digital infrastructure, and AI talent development will be crucial. The initial strategy provides a valuable foundation, but sustained political will and follow-through will determine its real impact on Mauritius's digital and economic transformation.

items.title: Mandatory Guardrails for Safe and Responsible AI
items.original_name: Mandatory Guardrails for Safe and Responsible AI
items.org: Department of Industry, Science, and Resources
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Mandatory Guardrails for Safe and Responsible AI
items.body:
The paper outlines proposed options for mandatory guardrails as preventative measures that would require developers and deployers of high-risk AI to take specific steps across the AI lifecycle.The paper includes:- a proposed definition of high-risk AI- 10 proposed regulatory guardrails to reduce the likelihood of harms occurring from the development and deployment of AI systems- regulatory options to mandate guardrails, building on current work to strengthen and clarify existing laws

The potential for Artificial Intelligence (AI) to improve social and economic well-being is immense. AI development and deployment is accelerating and is already permeating institutions, infrastructure, products and services. This often occurs undetected by those engaging with it.The Australian Government's consultations on safe and responsible AI have shown that our current regulatory system is not fit for purpose to respond to the distinct risks that AI poses. Internationally, governments are reforming existing regulations and introducing new regulations to address the risks of AI, with a focus on creating preventative, risk-based guardrails that apply across the AI supply chain and throughout the AI lifecycle. To unlock innovative uses of AI we need a modern and effective regulatorysystem.In the Australian Government's interim response to the Safe and Responsible AI in Australia discussion paper, a commitment was made to a develop a regulatory environment that builds community trust and promotes AI adoption. The guardrails outlined complement those in the Voluntary AI Safety Standard, and set clear expectations from the Australian Government on how to use AI safely and responsibly. They aim to address risks and harms from AI, build public trust and provide businesses with greater regulatory certainty. Implementing the Voluntary AI Safety Standard now will help businesses start to develop practices required in a future regulatory environment.Consultation on the proposed mandatory guardrails is now closed.Government is now considering the feedback received and next steps.

items.title: MELUXINA Supercomputer
items.org: Ministry of State (METAT; Ministère d'État); Ministry of the Economy (MECO; Ministère de l'Économie); European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC JU)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Luxembourg’s national supercomputer MeluXina launched was launched as part of the EU’s EuroHPC initiative. Operated by LuxProvide, it delivers HPC capabilities to support innovation in sectors such as finance, healthcare, research, and manufacturing. MeluXina is designed to handle large-scale data processing, simulations, and AI applications, playing a key role in Luxembourg’s push to become a leader in digital transformation and data-driven innovation.

The compagny Atos has been selected following the call for tender launched in January 2020 for the acquisition, delivery, installation and maintenance of a Petascale supercomputer located in LuxProvides data center in Bissen, Luxembourg.MeluXina will be a petascale supercomputer, capable of executing more than 10 Petaflops, 10 million billion calculations per second and powered by green energy from a cogeneration plant powered by waste wood. This new supercomputing system is expected to be operational early 2021 and will rank in the worlds top 30 supercomputers. MeluXina is funded via a joint investment of about EUR 30 million from the European Union and Luxembourg.The initiative has the following objectives:To develop top-of-the-range exascale supercomputers for processing big data, based on European technology.

items.title: Lithuanian Artificial Intelligence Strategy: A Vision of the Future
items.original_name: Lietuvos dirbtinio intelekto strategija: Ateities vizija
items.org: Ministry of the Economy and Innovation of the Republic of Lithuania
items.category: National – Strategy
source_urls: Strategija ir veiksmplanas - Lietuvos Respublikos ekonomikos ir inovacijministerija
items.document_name: Lietuvos dirbtinio intelekto strategija: Ateities vizija
items.body:
In 2019, Lithuania launched an AI strategy to become a regional leader and boost its economy by using AI in key areas like healthcare, farming, and energy. The plan helps create good conditions for AI development and ensures it is used ethically. A 2023“2026 action plan supports this by promoting AI innovation and use across all sectors, including government services.

Lithuanian AI strategy and action plan strategy allowed us to develop various AI initiatives that laid down the foundations for creating an environment which is favorable to the development and application of AI technologies. It is important, that share of all Lithuanian companies using AI technologies increased from 4.9% in 2023 to 8.8% in 2024. Moreover, share of large Lithuanian companies using AI technologies increased from 21.3% in 2023 to 31.2% in 2024. In addition, in the Government AI Readiness Index 2024 Lithuania is ranked 33rd among 188 countries. This shows that in Lithuania, both business and the public sector are ready to integrate AI solutions that could deliver benefit to both companies and citizens alike.However, it is obvious that Lithuanian AI strategy and action plan need to be updated because of recent rapid advancements in AI technologies and the adoption of EU AI act which will have a huge impact on the whole AI ecosystem.To update our AI strategy and action plan in 2024 Lithuania organized 5 meetings of the National AI Governance Forum, in which more than 200 stakeholders of AI ecosystem participated, including academia and business sector.

This includes areas such as energy efficiency, resource efficiency, biodiversity conservation, nature protection, species preservation, water management, sustainable consumption, and eco-friendly mobility. The focus is on application-oriented research and development projects.

The program funds solutions that use AI to help solve environmental challenges and promote opportunities to use AI strategically for Environmental and climate protection (for example in the fields of energy efficiency, resource efficiency, protection of biodiversity, nature conservation, species protection, water management, sustainable consumption or eco-friendly mobility). For example, AI can be used to derive recommendations for climate-friendly forest reconstruction, to control industrial processes in a more environmentally friendly way, to combat weeds in fields according to demand and thereby protect biodiversity, or to predict and sustainably reduce nitrate in groundwater.The funding program was published in August 2019. The focus is on research and development projects that are application-oriented. The projects can be funded for a period of three years with a maximum funding amount of 3 million euros. items.title: Legal Opinion: Uses of Copyrighted Materials for Machine Learning

items.body:
A legal opinion addressing the question of "whether ML enterprises can make unauthorized use of copyrighted materials to train Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems"

This Opinion aims to shed light on the most fundamental question in the intersectionbetween machine learning (ML) and copyright law: whether ML enterprises can makeunauthorized use of copyrighted materials to train Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems. ML isthe process that enables computers to autonomously learn from past data. ML thus providesthe foundations for AI systems. The intersection between ML and copyright bears crucialimportance. ML is becoming increasingly central to the global economy and to Israel inparticular, and Israel holds a leading position as a producer of AI systems. Lifting copyrightuncertainties that surround this issue can spur innovation and maximize the competitivenessof Israeli-based enterprises in both ML and content creationThe initiative has the following objectives:This Opinion aims to shed light on the most fundamental question in the intersectionbetween machine learning (ML) and copyright law: whether ML enterprises can makeunauthorized use of copyrighted materials to train Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems

items.title: Leading the Way Into the Age of AI
items.org: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment (MEAE)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
In October 2017, Finland presented the first eight key actions for making Finland one of the leaders in the application of AI. This work was later supplemented with separate analyses and recommendations for measures on the future of work, ethics and security.

Finland's age of AI places a strong emphasis on the applications of AI in the public sector. We will build the world's best public services.Finland's Age of AI (December 2017) and Leading the Way into the Age of AI (June 2019) collectively lay out 11 key actions covering all sectors to help Finland achieve its ambitious goal.1. Enhance business competitiveness through the use of AI.2. Effectively utilise data in all sectors.3. Ensure AI can be adopted more quickly and easily.4. Ensure top-level expertise and attract top experts.5. Make bold decisions and investments.6. Build the world's best public services.7. Establish new models for collaboration.8. Make Finland a frontrunner in the age of AI.9. Prepare for AI to change the nature of work.10. Steer AI development in a trust-based, human-centred direction.11. Prepare for security challenges.

items.title: Lawtech Sandbox
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
The LawTech Sandbox has been created by a government-backed initiative delivered by Tech Nation, the Lawtech Delivery Panel and the Ministry of Justice.

The Sandbox will be launched in collaboration with the Ministry of Justice, the Information Commissioner's Office, the Solicitors Regulatory Authority and the Legal Services Board.The initiative has the following objective(s):To drive more R&D in the digital transformation of legal services.

items.title: Law on the Disclosure of Data Ethics Policy
items.original_name: Law on the Disclosure of Data Ethics Policy
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Law on the Disclosure of Data Ethics Policy
items.body:
The Danish government has adopted law on the disclosure of its Data Ethics Policy. The law affects Denmark's largest companies and how they conduct their annual reporting.

On 26 May 2020, the Danish Parliament passed an amendment to the Danish Financial Statements Act, which means that large companies that have a policy for data ethics must supplement the managements report with an account of the companys policy for data ethics. The statement must contain information about the companys work with and policy on data ethics issues. If the company does not have a policy for data ethics, the managements report must include a statement explaining why they do not. The law enters into force on 1 January 2021, and a guide for businesses on how to include data ethics in their annual reports is in development.The initiative has the following objectives:To foster transparency regarding the companies work with data ethics.

items.title: Law on Road Traffic Safety (Self-Driving Cars)
items.original_name: Lietuvos Respublikos saugaus eismo automobilių keliais įstatymas
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.document_name: Lietuvos Respublikos saugaus eismo automobilių keliais įstatymas
items.body:
Lithuania adopted a law that allows operation of self-driving cars without a driver being present.

The initiative has the following objectives:To encourage autonomous vehicles to come to Lithuania and be tested in Lithuania.

items.title: Law on Protection of Personal Data
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Law on the Protection of Personal Data No. 6698 was published in the Official Gazette on 7 April 2016. The Turkish Data Protection Authority was established under the same Law in Ankara.

The Turkish Data Protection Authority has been established as an independent regulatory authority having organisational and financial autonomy and having a public legal entity to fulfil the duties under the Law. The Authority is comprised by the Personal Data Protection Board and the Presidency. The provisions of the Law shall apply to natural persons whose personal data are processed as well as to natural or legal persons who process such data fully or partially through automatic means or provided that the process is a part of any data registry system, through non-automatic means.The initiative has the following objectives:- To provide the protection of personal data and develop public awareness in line with the fundamental rights related with privacy and freedom stated in the Constitution.- To establish an environment that enhances the ability to compete of public and private organizations in the world of data-driven economy.

items.title: Law on Mobility Orientation
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
The Mobility Orientation Bill commits to a profound transformation of public mobility policies, with one objective in mind: to improve mobility on a daily basis for all French people and in all regions.

The initiative has the following objectives:To reduce territorial inequalities and contribute to the objective of cohesion in metropolitan and ultra-marine territories, by strengthening the accessibility of medium-sized cities and territories that are poorly connected to metropolises, large urban areas or neighboring countries, as well as within urban areas to the priority neighborhoods of the city policy, while taking care to limit the consumption of natural areas and urban sprawl.To strengthen the supply of daily travel options, improve the quality and safety of road, rail and waterway networks, and ensure their sustainability, remedy the saturation of cities and their accesses and improve links between rural or peri-urban areas and urban centers.To accelerate the energy transition, the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions and the fight against pollution and road congestion, by promoting a modal rebalancing in favor of travel by the least polluting individual, collective and goods transport modes, such as rail, river, public transport or active modes, by intensifying the shared use of individual transport modes and by facilitating multimodal travel.To improve the efficiency of freight transport to strengthen the competitiveness of territories and ports, accelerate modal shift, and reduce the environmental impact of freight transport.

items.title: Law n. 4961/2022 Emerging information and communication technologies and societies, enhancing digital governance and other provisions
items.original_name: Νόμος 4961/2022 «Αναδυόμενες τεχνολογίες πληροφορικής και επικοινωνιών, ενίσχυση της ψηφιακής διακυβέρνησης και άλλες διατάξεις.»
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.document_name: Νόμος 4961/2022 «Αναδυόμενες τεχνολογίες πληροφορικής και επικοινωνιών, ενίσχυση της ψηφιακής διακυβέρνησης και άλλες διατάξεις.»
items.body:
Greek Law 4961/2022 regulates emerging technologies like AI, IoT, and 3D printing to ensure their safe, lawful use. It aims to modernize public services, enhance digital governance, and promote Greece's digital transformation. Beneficiaries include public and private entities, as well as citizens who will experience improved services and data protection. The initiative addresses the need for a structured framework to manage the rapid adoption of advanced technologies.

Greek Law 4961/2022 addresses the need for a structured framework to manage the rapid adoption of advanced technologies like AI, IoT, and 3D printing. It aims to modernize public services, enhance digital governance, and promote Greece's digital transformationObjectives:Ensure lawful, safe, and secure use of emerging technologies.Enhance public service efficiency and data protection.Promote innovation and digital transformation.The law will be implemented through sector-specific regulations and horizontal guidelines, ensuring adaptability and scalability. It will be institutionalized by establishing control mechanisms and enforcement bodies. Since its enactment, the law has seen updates to align with the EU's AI Act and other international standards, ensuring continuous improvement and relevance. Specifically on AI, law 4961/2022 defines:Algorithmic Impact Assessment (Article 5) - Requires public bodies to provide technical information and assess the impact of AI systems on rights, freedoms and social groups before implementation.Transparency obligations (Articles 4, 6) - Requires public sector entities to provide information about the operation, characteristics and decisions of AI systems.AI contractor obligations (Article 7) - Contractors developing AI for public entities must disclose technical details and ensure that systems comply with human rights legal frameworks.Registry of AI systems for public entities (Article 8) - Requires public entities to maintain and update a registry of AI systems in use, detailing their purpose, date of commissioning and measures for safe operation.Disclosure of AI use in the workplace (Article 9) - Requires private entities to inform employees and job applicants about the use of AI in decision-making processes affecting employment.Ethical data use policy (Article 10) - Requires large and medium-sized private entities to maintain a policy on the ethical use of data in AI applications, including procedures and measures for ethical compliance.AI Coordination Committee (Article 11) - A committee responsible for the implementation and improvement of the national AI strategy. It ensures the alignment of national efforts with the strategic objectives.National AI Strategy Oversight Committee (Article 13) - Oversees the implementation of the national AI strategy and ensures the alignment of activities of all stakeholders. It focuses on implementation and compliance.AI Observatory (Article 14) - Collects data, monitors AI-related activities and provides key performance indicators for AI initiatives in the country. It identifies opportunities and assesses the impact of AI on fundamental rights.

items.title: Law for the Promotion of AI Technology and Entrepreneurship
items.original_name: ley 2069 - Por medio del cual se impulsa el emprendimiento en Colombia
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: ley 2069 - Por medio del cual se impulsa el emprendimiento en Colombia
items.body:
The purpose of this Law is to establish a regulatory framework that encourages entrepreneurship, as well as the growth, consolidation, and sustainability of companies, to increase social welfare and generate equality. The framework is designed to be implemented through a regionalized approach in accordance with the socioeconomic realities of each region.

Following the National Entrepreneurship Policy CONPES No. 4011 (Pol­tica Nacional De Emprendimiento in Spanish) issued in November of 2020, several entities of the National Government, actors of the entrepreneurship ecosystem and the private sector participated in the creation of this bill. The mentioned framework has been strengthened by its passage through Congress with new initiatives and articles that include benefits for the social, agricultural, sports and women's sectors.The initiative has the following objectives:Incentivize growth with the arrival of more actors to the investment and financial ecosystem.Both National and local governments will organize a decentralized strategy to support entrepreneurship through the promotion of angel investor networks, with an inclusive approach, that allows for the development and practice of entrepreneurship throughout the country.To strengthen iNNpulsa Colombia as a leading entity in the identification, support, and promotion of the entrepreneurial ecosystem, to optimize the management of resources and encourage a comprehensive vision.To lead and advance the public innovation laboratory with a govtech approach, favoring the government collaboration with entrepreneurs who use data intelligence and emerging technologies to promote products and services that solve public problems and accelerate the digital transformation of the State.The creation of income tax incentives as donations given to iNNpulsa as resources to be used to generate new programs or instruments, or to strengthen the existing offer that benefits the country's entrepreneurs. These resources may be used as seed capital (only given to those that have participated in the business consolidation programs offered by iNNpulsa), for the consolidation and promotion of businesses with growth potential.

items.title: Law as Code for Procedures of Public Administration
items.org: Federal Chancellery of Austria, Directorate General for Digitalisation and E-Government
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Law as Code approach aims to represent rules or legal texts in the form of formalized and executable logic-based rules, using methods of symbolic AI. Such a representation ensures transparency, explainability and predictability of the execution of the underlying regulations, and hence is especially suited for procedures of public administration. The Law as Code-initiative aims to create a basis for such an approach in the context of Austrian public administration.

Following the žLaw as Code-approach (or rules as code approach), several international initiatives aim to introduce transparent and explainable methods for the creation and execution of regulations and legal texts in public administration. Examples include initiatives in Canada, social benefit calculators in Barcelona or New Zealand, or a recently established research centre for Computational Law in Singapore. Advantages of this approach are in particular increased transparency and explainability of the computations and evaluations based on these regulations in public administration, as well as the possibility of automatized procedures based on the underlying logic-based formal rules using methods of symbolic Artificial Intelligence.The successfully completed žLaw as Code for procedures of public administration-initiative aimed to provide a basis for such an approach in the context of Austrian public administration. This included both a theoretical analysis of current approaches and their suitability in this context, as well as a proof of concept implementation of an end-to-end workflow. The workflow started with a tool for extracting a logic-based formal rule representation close to the logic programming paradigm from legal texts given in natural language, followed by a tool for viewing these rules, comparing them to the original texts and modifying the extracted formal rules where needed. The resulting rule base could then be used for evaluating business cases using a rule execution engine.When employed on a broader basis, the formulation of legal texts and regulations in a logic-based language as envisioned in this initiative would enable a high degree of automation of processes in public administration with transparent, explainable and predictable results. In addition, it would enable also a more comprehensive analysis of laws and regulations with respect to their mutual relations as well as possible overlaps and conflicts. Ideally, such a formal representation would be developed already in the law-making process itself, to ensure that the intent of the texts is captured exactly.Wherever possible, the initiative employed standardised representations and methods. Standards are a prerequisite for optimal cross-border cooperation between European Member States, companies and developers. The Austrian government therefore endorses and participates in the development of international standards and reference systems for symbolic AI programming languages such as ISO/IEC 13211-1:1995 (Prolog) which are needed to implement AI services reliably, and to ensure digital sovereignty and vendor independence.

items.title: Law No. 9943 Creation of the National Digital Government Agency
items.original_name: Ley N.9943 Creación de la agencia nacional de Gobierno Digital
items.org: Ministry of Science, Innovation, Technology and Telecommunications (MICITT)
items.category: National – AI governance bodies or mechanisms
items.document_name: Ley N.9943 Creación de la agencia nacional de Gobierno Digital
items.body:
Transform and make more efficient and effective the cross-cutting services that public institutions provide to citizens and businesses, through the intensive use of information and communication technologies.

The National Agency for Digital Government was created under the MICITT. For the implementation of strategic and cross-cutting digital government projects and services.The ANGD's functions include:To be the implementer and manager of interoperability at technical level.Generate proposals for the development of cross-cutting or strategic projects and services, based on the public policy issued by the governing body.To provide technical support and advice to public administration institutions in their digital transformation, in the planning and development of their strategic digitalisation plans, which contribute to the fulfilment of their objectives.Drawing up technical guides to the projects and transversal services offered by the ANGD, to facilitate their use and integration in the institutions of the Public Administration.

items.title: Law 5142/2024 Completion of land registration, simplification of procedures, use of artificial intelligence and provisions for the operation of the Hellenic Land Registry Cadastre", other provisions of the Ministry of Digital Governance.
items.original_name: Νόμος 5142/2024 «Ολοκλήρωση της κτηματογράφησης, απλοποίηση διαδικασιών, χρήση τεχνητής νοημοσύνης και διατάξεις για τη λειτουργία του Ν.Π.Δ.Δ. «Ελληνικό Κτηματολόγιο», λοιπές διατάξεις του Υπουργείου Ψηφιακής Διακυβέρνησης.»
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.document_name: Νόμος 5142/2024 «Ολοκλήρωση της κτηματογράφησης, απλοποίηση διαδικασιών, χρήση τεχνητής νοημοσύνης και διατάξεις για τη λειτουργία του Ν.Π.Δ.Δ. «Ελληνικό Κτηματολόγιο», λοιπές διατάξεις του Υπουργείου Ψηφιακής Διακυβέρνησης.»
items.body:
It focuses on completing land registration, simplifying procedures, and integrating AI into the Greek Cadaster. It benefits public and private entities, local governments, and citizens by enhancing legal security and reducing bureaucracy. The law addresses inefficiencies in land registration and leverages AI to improve accuracy and speed. It aims to transition Greece to a fully functional land registry system by 2025, using AI to streamline legal reviews and correct records.

The Hellenic Cadastre, responsible for managing property records, previously encountered delays and inefficiencies due to the manual processing of paper documents for property transactions. This often meant citizens were waiting months or even years to legally own their property. To overcome these challenges, the cadastre developed a system to automate the reading and categorization of property contracts, apply the relevant legal rules, and then generate assessments for approval using AI.Law 5142/2024 addresses inefficiencies in land registration and leverages AI to enhance the accuracy and speed of cadastral processes. It aims to modernize the Greek Cadaster, ensuring legal security and reducing bureaucracy.Objectives:Complete land registration and simplify procedures.Integrate AI to improve cadastral accuracy and speed.Enhance legal security and reduce long-term legal disputes.The new AI tool, which is already in pilot operation, can read the text of the contract in natural language, identify the type of transaction, identify the elements required under legal rules, apply an automatic completeness check of the elements of a contract, such as updates and ENFIA declaration, as well as generate an automatic recommendation to the supervisor to approve or reject elements of the contract. This results in significant time and cost savings for the State, as a process that currently costs 15 euros could cost as low as 30 cents.It is noted that the final decision will continue to be taken by the competent supervisor, but the AI tool will greatly facilitate his/her work by providing a ready-made recommendation that will highlight exactly the points of the contract that need attention.The new tool was created by the Ministry of Digital Government at no cost, is very simple to use and was implemented using Microsoft Azure Open AI technology. The development and hosting of the system was supported by Microsoft, ensuring the high technological quality and reliability of the tool.The framework can scale by expanding its AI capabilities and integrating additional public services, fostering broader digital transformation across Greece.Since its enactment, the law has seen updates to align with the EU's AI Act and other international standards, ensuring continuous improvement and relevance. Regular updates and enhancements have been made to improve the system's efficiency and user experience.

items.title: Law 31814, Law that promotes the use of artificial intelligence in favor of the economic and social development of the country
items.original_name: Ley N. 31814, Ley que promueve el uso de la inteligencia artificial en favor del desarrollo económico y social del paí­s
items.org: Presidency of the Council of Ministers, through the Secretariat of Government and Digital Transformation
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.document_name: Ley N. 31814, Ley que promueve el uso de la inteligencia artificial en favor del desarrollo económico y social del paí­s
items.body:
It is a law to promote the safe, transparent, responsible, and respectful use of human rights of artificial intelligence, which establishes the Presidency of the Council of Ministers, through the Secretariat of Government and Digital Transformation (PCM-SGTD) as the technical-regulatory authority at the national level in charge of directing, evaluating and supervising the use and promotion of the development of AI.

The initiative has the following objectives:It establishes that the SGTD is the competent technical-regulatory national authority on AIIt promotes actions to foster AI useIt promotes actions to train professionalsIt promotes actions to strengthen digital and data infrastructureIt promotes actions to establish ethical guidelinesIt promotes action to build a collaborative ecosystem.

items.title: Launch of the Artificial Intelligence (AI) Institute of South Africa and AI Hubs (University of Johannesburg and Tshwane University of Technology)
items.original_name: Launch of the Artificial Intelligence (AI) Institute of South Africa and AI Hubs (University of Johannesburg and Tshwane University of Technology)
items.org: The Ministry of Communications and Digital Technologies
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Launch of the Artificial Intelligence (AI) Institute of South Africa and AI Hubs (University of Johannesburg and Tshwane University of Technology)
items.body:
South Africa is launching the Artificial Intelligence Institute to support digital innovation and skills. It is a partnership between the government and two universities”UJ and TUT”to help prepare the country for the future. This initiative follows expert recommendations to make South Africa a leader in new technologies.

The initiative has the following objectives:The launch of the AI Institute is realisation of one of the recommendations of the Presidential Commission on the Fourth Industrial Revolution (PC4IR) and aims to place South Africa as a leading country in the world on digital technologies. During the 2022/3 Budget Vote Speech, the Minister made a commitment that the AI Institute will be launched this financial year to mark a new era in the country's digital transformation agenda.

items.title: Latvia's National AI Strategy
items.org: The Ministry of Environmental Protection and Regional Development
items.category: National – Strategy
items.body:
In February 2020, the Latvian government released its National AI Strategy on Developing Artificial Intelligence Solutions.

The initiative has the following objectives:To raise the awareness of and competences in AI across society through education reforms.To promote the adoption and development of AI in the public and private sector.To actively engage in national and international cooperation.To develop an appropriate legal and ethical framework for AI.To unleash the benefits of a well-developed data ecosystem.To invest in a digital and telecommunication infrastructure to support AI developments.

items.title: Language Strategic Project for the Economic Recovery and Transformation
items.original_name: PERTE Nueva economí­a de la Lengua
items.org: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Digital Transformation (MEATD; Ministerio de Transformación Digital)|Ministry of Culture and Sports (Ministerio de Cultura y Deporte)|Ministry of Foreign Affairs, European Union and Cooperation (Ministerio de Asuntos Exter
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: PERTE Nueva economí­a de la Lengua
items.body:
The plan supports AI learning in Spanish and co-official languages and goes beyond AI alone (Presidencia del Gobierno, 2023\[15]). It is partly implemented through the National Plan on Language Technologies, which includes initiatives to advance language technologies and AI in these languages. A key action is the creation of linguistic corpora composed of diverse texts such as novels, plays, film scripts, and press materials, helping train and improve AI language models.

The initiative is based in these key principles: the integrated nature, public-private collaboration, territorial structuring, pan-Hispanic, SMEs and start-ups participation, and inclusive digitalisation based on technological humanism and gender equality.The initiative has the following objectives:Fostering knowledge in Spanish and co-official languagesDeveloping Artificial Intelligence resources in SpanishEstablishing science and research paths that use Spanish language processingFacilitating Spanish learning through digital resourcesFostering cultural services and market

items.title: Labour AI - Centre of Expertise of the Global Partnership on AI
items.org: Foreign Office (MEAE) | Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) | National Research Institute for Digital Sciences (INRIA) | Ministry of Labour
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Labor AI is one of the two centres of expertise of the GPAI. The other one is located in Canada. It aims at studying AI impact on work, employment, and social dialogue.

The GPAI was formerly known as the International Panel on AI (IPAI). In December 2018, at the G7 Multi-stakeholder Conference on AI, Canada's Prime Minister, Minister of Innovation, Science, and Economic Development and France's Secretary of State for the Digital Sector, announced the Mandate for IPAI. In May 2019, they made public the Declaration and organizational structure of IPAI at the end of the informal meeting of G7 Digital Ministers.The initiative has the following objectives:To set up research and innovation co-operation to study and experiment AI technologies' impact on labor, employment, and social dialogue.To develop experimentations and research projects within enterprises and public administrations.To participate in public debate on AI dissemination in the economy and in the society.

items.title: LUMI Supercomputer
items.org: European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC JU)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Finland hosts the EuroHPC supercomputer LUMI, which is located in CSC’s data center in Kajaani. In March 2024, Finland made a funding commitment of up to EUR 250 million in the context of an upcoming call for new top-level EuroHPC supercomputers. As of mid-2021, LUMI (Large Unified Modern Infrastructure) will be a top-of-the-range pre-exascale supercomputer, capable of executing more than 375 petaflops or more than 375 million billion calculations per second.

Objectives: 
To develop top-of-the-range exascale supercomputers for processing big data, based on European technology.

items.title: LT.AI - Fostering AI and the Creation of Lithuanian Language Technological Resources for AI
items.original_name: LT.AI – lietuvių kalbos išteklių dirbtiniam intelektui ir dirbtinio intelekto skatinimas Lietuvoje
items.org: Agency for Science, Innovation and Technology
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: LT.AI – lietuvių kalbos išteklių dirbtiniam intelektui ir dirbtinio intelekto skatinimas Lietuvoje
items.body:
LT.AI is a EUR 17 million financial measure to boost the Lithuanian AI ecosystem.

LT.AI is one of the actions of the recently approved post-COVID-19 Future economy DNA plan, which will help boosting the Lithuanian economy from the crisis. Over the third of the total EUR 6.3 billion investment “ EUR 2.37 billion “ is dedicated to digital economy, innovations and research.The initiative has the following objectives:To create and update the technological resources for Lithuanian language application in AI.To provide early-to-mid stage funding to help over 130 AI startups in developing their ideas and growing into mature companies.To support the industry in performing AI transformations.

items.title: LEAM - Large European AI Models
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
LEAM is an initiative of the German AI Association (KI Bundesverband) and leading representatives from industry and research that promotes the development of large AI models.

In order to realise large AI models made in Europe, the initiative proposes six key steps:1. Collect and create comprehensive training datasets2. Support excellence in AI research3. Provide hyperscale infrastructure4. Develop organisational structures and processes to establish a continuous workflow of model development and improvement5. Integrate the models into the European innovation ecosystem6. Develop methodologies, benchmark datasets and criteria to fulfil ethical requirements and reflect European valuesWe want the models developed under this initiative to be open source and freely available to all market players. All European languages should be fully integrated into the models.

items.title: Korean New Deal
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Korea New Deal aims to boost the economy and create jobs by focusing on digital and contact-free industries. It was developed to respond to the COVID-19 crisis and speed up digital transformation in Korea. This initiative benefits businesses and workers by improving data infrastructure and expanding high-speed internet access.

To increase potential growth by accelerating innovative growth in response to changes in the economic and social structure of the post COVID-19 eraTo establish a virtuous cycle to create sustainable jobs for future generations in the process of promoting innovation projects and activating convergence industries

items.title: Knowledge and Innovation Covenant
items.org: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Climate Policy (EZK)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The covenant describes the cooperation between many stakeholders in the Netherlands on key technologies, including AI.

The KIC 2020-2023 is based on mission-driven top sector and innovation policy. It focuses on four major societal themes, key enabling technologies, and societal earning capacity. The four main themes are energy transition & sustainability, agriculture, water & food, health & care, and safety. The further development of key technologies (such as artificial intelligence), which supports, enables or even drives these themes is of great importance.These themes have been further elaborated into concrete missions in the Knowledge and Innovation Agendas (KIA), drawn up by representatives of the business community and the government. The KIAs contain research and innovation topics that knowledge institutions and companies can address in public-private partnerships. The NWO contribution to the KIC 2020-2023 focuses on scientific and practice-oriented research into questions that contribute to the concrete missions. The KIAs form the starting point for the NWO programming.The initiative has the following objectives:To provide financial assistance to projects that use key technologies to support and drive innovation in the themes of energy transition & sustainability, agriculture, water & food, health & care, and safety.

items.title: Knowledge and Innovation Agenda Ict
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The national agenda for ICT knowledge and innovation (2016-2019) is the framework for PPP-programmes for high end solutions, based on digital technologies 1) big data, 2) artificial intelligence, 3) blockchain, 4) cyber security and 5) Communication technologies (5G).

This program continues the KIA ICT 2015-2017. Public and private funding for this program is estimated at EUR 60 million euros for two years. This program is also part of the broader Knowledge and Innovation Agenda program for Topsectors (energy, health, mobility etc.).The initiative has the following objectives:To connects scientists, corporate businesses and governments in order to develop high end ICT solutions.To use cross-connections and to turn them into opportunities.To stimulate and initiate innovations in ICT for all sorts of (top)sectors.To fully capitalise on the innovations in ICT in the future and to further advance economic growth in The Netherlands.To continue the national human capital programme on ICT.

items.title: Knowledge and Innovation Agenda
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
HTSM has established a thematic framework with five grand societal challenges: climate (including energy and water), sustainability(including circular economy and food), health, security, and mobility.

In this new set-up, the Top Sector will stimulate R&D collaboration in crossovers between key enabling technologies and societal innovation and build bridges between the HTSM community and the mission-driven programming in national and regional public agendas.The initiative has the following objectives:To facilitate interactions on HTSM technologies between key stakeholders inside and outside the Top Sector.

items.title: Knowledge Economy Initiatives
items.original_name: Iniciativas vinculadas a la Promoción de la Economí­a del Conocimiento
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Iniciativas vinculadas a la Promoción de la Economí­a del Conocimiento
items.body:
Implementation of three kinds of policies: tax promotions for companies who adopt 4.0 technologies in their productive processes; funding for 4.0 solutions in companies affected by pandemics and training in 4.0 technologies in local administrations.

The initiative has the following objectives:To promote 4.0 adoption in Argentine companies and local administrations in order to improve competitiveness and to increase the efficiency of administrative processes.

items.title: Knowledge Centre for Data and Society
items.org: Department of Economy, Science and Innovation
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
As part of the Flemish Action Plan AI, the Knowledge Centre Data & Society (Kenniscentrum Data & Maatschappij) was created to focus on the interplay between data, artificial intelligence and society.

The Knowledge Centre combines the expertise of three existing research Centres: imec-SMIT (Vrije Universiteit Brussel), imec-MICT (Ghent University) and the Centre for IT & IP Law (KU Leuven). The Flemish Department on Economy, Science and Innovation funds the initiative.The initiative has the following objectives:To enable Flemish companies, policymakers, regulators and citizens to achieve the greatest social and/or economic benefits of AI. To this end, it will bring together diverse stakeholder representative organisations and facilitate the creation of tools, advice, and recommendations.

items.title: Key Employee Initiative
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Malta's Key Employee Initiative helps skilled workers from outside the EU in AI roles get faster work and residence permits. It supports companies by bringing in talent needed to boost AI innovation and digital growth. This program was created to attract experts who can help Malta stay competitive and aligned with global AI standards.

The start-up residency programme, a joint programme run between Malta Enterprise and the Residency Malta Agency and provides a fast route to settling in Malta.The initiative has the following objectives:It aims to bolster the attractiveness of Malta for non-EU founders, their core employees and immediate family members to relocate to Malta.

items.title: Kenya's Digital Literacy Programme (DigiSchool)
items.org: Ministry of Information, Communications and Technology (MoICT)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The programme introduces primary school children to the use of digital technology and communications. It is targeted at learners in all public primary schools in Kenya.

items.title: Juri Reports on "Making AI European"
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The European Parliament Committee on Legal Affairs (JURI) adopted reports on AI.

In early October 2020, the Legal Affairs Committee of the European Parliament (JURI) approved three reports related to artificial intelligence (AI). These reports address (i) an ethical framework for AI, (ii) civil liability for AI-related damages, and (iii) the safeguarding of intellectual property rights concerning AI.1. The first report proposes an ethical framework for AI, aimed at establishing foundational ethical principles for the development, use, and deployment of AI within the EU. The guiding principles closely align with those outlined in the Ethics Guidelines for Trustworthy AI, emphasizing safety, transparency, accountability, protection against bias and discrimination, the right to redress, social and environmental responsibility, and respect for fundamental rights. The report advocates for the European Commission to create a comprehensive and adaptable legal framework of ethical principles governing AI, robotics, and related technologies including software, algorithms, and data across the Union. It also suggests that the Commission incorporate various guiding principles for high-risk AI and related technologies into upcoming legislation, such as human oversight, transparency, accountability, non-bias, social responsibility, gender equality, environmental sustainability, and privacy considerations. Furthermore, EU law should impose specific requirements on high-risk technologies that could significantly harm individuals or violate EU fundamental rights and safety regulations. The Commission is encouraged to develop common guidance and compile a list of high-risk sectors (e.g., employment, healthcare) and high-risk applications (e.g., recruitment, automated driving, electoral processes) to identify AI technologies that require compliance assessments. The Parliament proposes that national authorities issue a European certificate of ethical compliance for technologies that meet these guiding principles, particularly regarding safety and the right to redress.2. The second report addresses liability for AI-induced damage, focusing on civil liability claims related to AI systems (led by MEP Axel Voss). This report recommends the establishment of a uniform and harmonized legal framework for civil liability claims, which would include a new regulation identifying high-risk AI systems and the critical sectors in which they operate. The Commission, with assistance from the standing Technical Committee for high-risk AI systems, should review and update this list every six months, potentially through a delegated act. The report suggests that operators of high-risk AI systems should be held strictly liable for any harm or damage resulting from activities, devices, or processes driven by those AI systems and should be required to maintain mandatory insurance coverage.

items.title: Israel's Policy on Artificial Intelligece Regulation and Ethics
items.original_name: עקרונות, מדיניות, רגולציה ואתיקה בתחום הבינה המלאכותית 2023
items.org: Ministry for Innovation Science and Technology |Ministry of Justice
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.document_name: עקרונות, מדיניות, רגולציה ואתיקה בתחום הבינה המלאכותית 2023
items.body:
In December 2023, Israel introduced its first policy on AI regulation and ethics. The policy aims to ensure AI is used responsibly, protecting people from risks like bias and privacy issues. Developed by several ministries and experts, it supports innovation while promoting fairness, safety, and transparency for all sectors using AI.

The AI Policy identifies seven main challenges arising from the use of artificial intelligence in the private sector (discrimination, human oversight, explainability, disclosure of AI interactions, safety, accountability and privacy). To address these challenges, and consistent with the approach taken by the OECD AI Recommendations, the AI Policy sets forth common policy principles and a number of practical recommendations.The main recommendation are: Adopting sectoral regulation Promoting consistency with existing regulatory approach of leading countries and international organizations Adopting a risk-based approach Using "soft" regulatory tools intended to allow for an incremental development of the regulatory framework Fostering cooperation between the public and the private sectors.The initiative has the following objectives:The AI Policy provides guidelines and instructions for sectoral regulators when addressing the regulation of AI in the private sector. While some parts of the AI Policy can be natively applied to the public sector as well, a full discussion of the required adaptations and modifications is out of the scope of this Policy. The government's policy on public sector applications of AI is being developed separately.With respect to private sector applications, the AI Policy is premised upon the concept of "Responsible Innovation", which captures the need to support innovation while simultaneously fostering accountability and ethically-aligned design and uses of AI. While private sector innovation and ethics (or regulation) are often perceived as conflicting with one another, responsible innovation views these two goals as synergistic and mutually complementary. The AI Policy applies this concept to the entire lifecycle of AI applications, with a special focus on use and deployment.

items.title: Investments for the Future Programme
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Investments for the Future Programme (PIA) aims to increase the long-term growth potential of the French economy, by strengthening investment in four priority sectors: higher education and research, industries and SMEs, sustainable development and digital economy. The program seeks to accelerate and strengthen a  of the French higher education, research and innovation system.

Since 2010, the National Agency for Research (ANR) is the main operator of the state for the PIAs higher education and research actions.The Investments for the Future Programme was set by a Finance Law of March 9, 2010. The goals of this programme and the amount budgeted are structured in accordance with the 2009 report and recommendations issued by a consultative commission chaired by two previous French Prime ministers, MM. Juppe and Rocard. The ambition of the PIA is to increase the long-term growth potential of the French economy, by strengthening investment in four priority sectors: higher education and research, industries and SMEs, sustainable development and digital economy. Until this day, the PIA consists of three phases: - The first phase (PIA 1) covers the period 2010-2020 with a total budget of USD 40.9 billion PPP (EUR 35 billion) allocated to five priority axes: Higher education and training Research Industrial sectors and SMEs Sustainable development Digital economy - The second phase (PIA 2) covers the period 2013-2025 with a total budget of USD 14.3 billion PPP (EUR 12 billion). Its objective is to improve the growth potential of the French economy by organising technological research activities in global excellence clusters.- The third phase (PIA 3) with a total budget of EUR 10 billion was set by the Finance Law for 2017 of December 26, 2016. Of the EUR 10 billion, EUR 5.9 billion will benefit the teaching, research and development of it. This phase includes, for example, calls for projects to support the development of digital technologies. In particular, a part of the Innovation Contest is allocated to support innovative digital technologies such as artificial intelligence, internet of things, blockchain, big data, etc.The initiative has the following objectives:Encourage the excellences of higher education and research on large campuses with the best international standards in terms of governance and academic level. During the first and the second phases of the Investments for the Future Program, the ambition of the .« Initiatives dexcellence / Initiatives - Science “ Innovation “Territoires “ Economie .» action (IDEX / I-SITE) is to allow best campuses to promote their specific advantages in order to increase their international visibility and attractiveness.In particular, the IDEX / I-SITE action selected :- IDEX in order to create world-leading research universities with leading scientific power and impact in broad areas of knowledge ;- I-SITE so as to help universities with more concentrated, distinctive and internationally recognized thematic scientific assets to emerge. These assets are a point of support for their strategy of development and partnership with the economic world.

items.title: Invest 2035: The Uk's Modern Industrial Strategy
items.original_name: Invest 2035: The Uk's Modern Industrial Strategy
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Invest 2035: The Uk's Modern Industrial Strategy
items.body:
The UK government's new industrial strategy, Invest 2035, is a robust 10-year plan designed to provide the stability and certainty that businesses require to invest in high-growth sectors. Its aim is to attract a larger share of global investment in key areas and encourage domestic companies to increase their investments and expand, which is vital for achieving sustainable, inclusive, and resilient economic growth.

The industrial strategy will be ambitious and targeted. Its primary objective is to drive growth, by taking advantage of the UK's unique strengths and untapped potential, enabling the UK's world-leading sectors to adapt and grow, and seizing opportunities to lead in new sectors, with high-quality, well-paid jobs. It will shape the type of growth being pursued. The government will also seek to support net zero, regional growth, and economic security and resilience. It will be grounded in long-term stability, a renewed commitment to free and fair trade, and a pro-business approach focused on reducing barriers to investment in the UK.The industrial strategy will focus on the sectors which offer the highest growth opportunity for the economy and business. Eight growth-driving sectors have been identified, including digital and technologies.

The initiative has the following objective(s):This guide aims to provide an accessible introduction to both assurance mechanisms and global technical standards, to help industry and regulators better understand how to build and deploy responsible AI systems. The guidance will be updated to reflect feedback from stakeholders, the changing regulatory environment and emerging global best practices. The guidance covers: AI assurance in context: Introduction to the background and conceptual underpinnings of AI Assurance. The AI assurance toolkit: Introduction to key AI assurance concepts and stakeholders. AI assurance in practice: Overview of different AI assurance techniques and how to implement AI assurance within organisations. Key actions for organisations: A brief overview of key actions that organisations looking to embed AI assurance can take.
