items.title: Eleventh Development Plan
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
The Eleventh Development Plan presents a long-term perspective based on the vision of stronger and more prosperous Turkey that produces more value added and shares more fairly. Over the Plan period, through a human centric, participatory, inclusive, accountable, transparent and efficient approach, it will be ensured that the objectives and goals set out in the Plan are bought in by all sections of the society and fundamental steps are taken to achieve the Plan's vision.

The plan includes a number of measures specific to AI and as well as its overarching objectives related to inclusive growth, creating nationwide awareness and coordination on science, technology and innovation and employs a range of policy instruments.The initiative has the following objectives:To encourage technology suppliers to develop applications and services that can be offered on the industrial cloud platform such as artificial intelligence, advanced data analytics, simulation and optimization, product lifecycle and production management systems, and the use of this platform by companies will be encouraged through supports for digital transformation.To prepare road maps for artificial intelligence, internet of things, augmented reality, big data, cybersecurity, energy storage, advanced material, robotics, micro/nano/optoelectronics, biotechnology, quantum, sensor technologies and additive manufacturing technologies in order to achieve National Technology Act, and to establish the necessary infrastructures, to train the qualified human resources in need and to ensure the social orientation to focus on these areas.To develop Agricultural information systems with digitalization, artificial intelligence and data-based business models and will be made available to all segments.To prepare a roadmap for the national-scale studies aimed at the development of domestic technology production capabilities and roll out the efficient use of these technologies across the whole economy, in the field of artificial intelligence technologies.To establish Educational data bank where the databases related to the education system are integrated and the data will be processed by artificial intelligence technologies.To improve processes and technological infrastructure in order to utilize new technologies such as big data, cloud computing, mobile platforms, internet of things, artificial intelligence and blockchain in development of public services.

items.title: Egyptian Charter for Responsible AI
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
The Egyptian Charter for Responsible AI is a guide to help Egypt develop and use AI in a safe and fair way. It adapts global ethical principles to Egypt's needs, ensuring AI benefits people and society. This initiative supports policymakers and organizations in managing AI responsibly while protecting rights and promoting trust.

The initiative has the following objectives:To be a soft launch to empower citizens to expect and demand the best from the use ofAI and for all stakeholders to be aware of ethical considerations related to AI andincorporate those considerations into their AI adoption plans.To signal Egypt's readiness to follow responsible AI practices, something many investorsas well as AI ranking bodies look to measure a country's readiness for AI investment andadoption. It would also help to communicate Egypt's needs and priorities to foreign AIdevelopers looking to develop or market their products in the country.

items.title: Egypt National AI Strategy
items.category: National – Strategy
items.body:
The National AI Strategy is a key priority for helping achieve Egypt's sustainable development goals.

The initiative has the following objectives:To create an AI Industry in Egypt, including the development of skills, technology, ecosystem, infrastructure and governance mechanisms to ensure its sustainability and competitiveness. Egypt's AI Strategy has different pillars:1. AI for Government: The rapid adoption of artificial intelligence technologies through the automation of government processes to increase efficiency and transparency.2. AI for Development: Apply AI in key developmental sectors in Egypt such as agriculture, health Care, environment, infrastructure and manufacturing to help solving the country's challenges in line with the UN Sustainable Development Goals.3. Capacity Building: Prepare the Egyptian population for the age of AI at all levels, from spreading general awareness to guiding formal education and offering vocational training.4. International Relations: Establishing Egypt as a hub for the different AI activities in the region and being an active global player in the different initiatives and AI related discussions.

items.title: Education Information Network
items.category: National – AI governance bodies or mechanisms
items.body:
EBA is a distance education platform prepared by the Ministry of National Education within the scope of the F.A.T.I.H. Project, which has been recently renewed and adapted to distance education during COVID-19.

Through EBA, teachers and students can interact with each other, teachers can send study materials to their students, and they can monitor their students' performances on study materials and general EBA usage. Students can track their progress via reports and portfolios. Parents can also track their children's progress via reports and portfolios.In addition to providing a customized interface and content for each student with personalization, the system recommends content according to the performance of the students - thanks to the smart suggestion system. In EBA, the contents are matched with the relevant curriculum objectives. Other contents that are not matched with the objectives are included in the Library area for free use and supportive course content. When teachers send study material to their students via EBA, the students' work is analyzed in detail by the system and the deficiencies of each student are determined separately based on objectives. Taking this analysis into account, the system determines the content that can help each student to remedy his/her deficiencies and recommends them to the student if the teacher approves. In addition, without teacher intervention, there is also a special content recommendation system that recommends additional content based on questions a student solves while using EBA and the answers he/she provides in the exams.The initiative has the following objectives:- To provide customized interface and content for each student with personalisation.- To recommend content according to the performance of the students through analysing work of each student with AI.

items.title: Easy Export Platform Centre of Excellence of Data Analytics
items.original_name: Kolay Ihracat Platformu Veri Analizi Mœkemmelliyet Merkezi
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Kolay Ihracat Platformu Veri Analizi Mœkemmelliyet Merkezi
items.body:
Users can identify and clean up data, increase data quality, make short-term and long-term forecasts, automate manual operations, use relationship dashboards to data scope, become data scientists, and minimise manpower. This system also helps policymakers to observe the statistics and changes easily.

Studies are carried out to establish the Center of Excellence of Data Analytics within the Ministry of Trade. Turkiye created scenarios related to the field of duty of our Ministry in the Center of Excellence of Data Analytics. Turkiye uses AI and ML technology on the data in these scenarios. Scenarios are made up of subjects that fall under the ministry's field of activity. There are special working teams for these scenarios. The project's key activities are forecasting, technological solutions, text mining in free text fields, early warning/alarm, simulation, data quality studies on various datasets, predictive models (using the methods of ML, AI, etc.), social network analysis, chatbot/assistant, and dashboard design. The Easy Export Platform enables our small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), co-operatives, and entrepreneurs to access all the information that they need via a single platform in the most up-to-date form (including the large-scale data provided with ML algorithms). It makes a significant contribution to our country's export vision.The initiative has the following objectives:- To collect, process, and protect the data of domestic and foreign trade and customs procedures in safe environments.- To support policymakers with tools such as scenario creation, simulation, and forecasting.

items.title: EUROHPC JU Marenostrum5 Supercomputer
items.org: Ministry of Industry and Technology | Scientific and Technological Research Council of Turkey
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC JU) has launched a call for tender for the procurement of a pre-exascale supercomputer. The system, called MareNostrum5, will be hosted by the Barcelona Supercomputing Center (BSC) and will be capable of executing at least 205 Petaflops, or at least 205 million billion calculations per second. Turkey jointly applied to the Precursors to Exascale call and obtained direct access to the supercomputer MareNostrum 5.

In order to equip Europe with a world-leading supercomputing infrastructure, the EuroHPC JU has already procured seven supercomputers, located across Europe. Four petascale supercomputers are now fully operational. Turkiye has participated the EuroHPC in 2019 for high performance computing.The initiative has the following objectives:-To strengthen European medical research through drug research, the development of vaccines, virus spread simulations-To strengthen artificial intelligence and big data processing applications-To support traditional HPC applications, such as climate research, engineering, material science and earth sciences

items.title: EURO HPC Supercomputer
items.org: European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC JU) | Foundation for Science and Technology
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC JU) and the Minho Advanced Computing Centre (MACC) have launched a call for tender for the procurement of a petascale supercomputer, capable of executing more than one Petaflop, or 1 million billion calculations per second.

The procurement will include the acquisition, delivery, installation and maintenance of a EuroHPC petascale supercomputer located in the Minho Advanced Computing Centre (MACC) in Portugal.The initiative has the following objectives:To foster better science and enhance innovation in Europe by providing access to leading edge HPC infrastructures and services to a wide range of users from the research and scientific community as well as the industry and the public sector.To develop top-of-the-range exascale supercomputers for processing big data, based on European technology.

items.title: EU Strategy for Artificial Intelligence
items.category: AI Policy Frameworks and Initiatives (intergovernmental or supranational)

This Coordinated Plan sets out the European Union's strategic objectives and priorities for artificial intelligence. It is a European umbrella strategy for AI, which was developed in cooperation with Member States, and calls on Member States to implement the Coordinated Plan at national level.

The initiative has the following objectives:To increase the EU's technological and industrial capacity and AI uptake by the public and private sectors.To prepare Europeans for the socioeconomic changes brought about by AI.To ensure that an appropriate ethical and legal framework is in place.

On 15 October 2020, The European Commission and the German Presidency of the Council of the European Union welcomed the political will expressed by all 27 Member States on the next generation cloud for Europe.The initiative has the following objectives:To ensure science, business and public services reap benefits of big data revolution.

items.title: EDUC.AR
items.org: Ministry of Science, Technology, and Productive Innovation
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Argentina is taking action to build AI-relevant human capacities from the earliest stages in education, targeting children from ages 6 to 18.

Together with Priority Learning Hubs (NAPs in Spanish) and the National Plan Learning Connected, Argentina is aiming to prepare young generations with future skills, including AI-related capabilities such as statistical thinking, mathematics, logic, computer sciences, programming, computational thinking, and comprehension of AI implications (e.g. relationships between people and technologies, privacy issues, use of data, critical thinking). It also aims to spur development of skills that differentiate people from machines, including advanced cognitive skills and socio-emotional skills (e.g. thinking capacity, reflection, making conclusions, analysis, empathy with others, curiosity, teamwork and creativity). Other initiatives are outlined in Argentina's National Plan for AI (Plan Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial).The initiative has the following objectives:To incentivise digital literacy through Internet connection in schools, the delivery of digital tools, the development of software and virtual training platforms and the creation of spaces of technological innovation.

items.title: EDGE AI Initiative

A set of measures and programmes to place France as a leader in the sector of embedded AI.

This initiative is included in a global trend of rapid growth of Edge AI demand and capacity.The initiative has the following objectives:Maturate and industrialize advanced hardware and paradigms for frugal and embedded AI.Diffuse state-of-the-art embedded AI solutions in all industries as to increase their competitiveness and decrease their costs.Support innovative start-ups on their way to develop and put to market new-generation chips for AI at the edge.Attract to France 15% of the market share in Edge AI by 025.Develop, produce, and commercialise advanced neuromorphic chips by 2025.

items.title: Dubai Future Accelerators

Dubai Future Accelerators (DFA) is an intensive 9-week program pairing the world's most exciting technology companies with leading government organizations to create transformational solutions.

The Dubai Future foundation brings together individuals, organizations and government entities to foresight and co-create the future of Dubai. It also focuses on creating an innovative ecosystem for talent and incubating & prototyping their ideas.The initiative has the following objectives:To imagine, design and co-create the future. items.title: Dsit Portfolio of AI Assurance Techniques
items.original_name: Dsit Portfolio of AI Assurance Techniques
items.org: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Dsit Portfolio of AI Assurance Techniques
items.body:
In June 2023, in collaboration with industry body techUK, the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT) launched the Portfolio of AI Assurance Techniques. The Portfolio features real-world case studies of AI assurance mechanisms being applied by organisations across a range of sectors.The Portfolio is a helpful resource for anyone involved in designing, developing, deploying or procuring AI-enabled systems.

In 2022, DSIT engaged with industry to gauge attitudes towards and engagement with AI assurance techniques and technical standards. The outcome of this engagement was reported in the DSIT Industry Temperature Check, which identified key barriers and enablers to AI assurance and set out clear interventions that government and others can make to overcome these barriers. Following publication of the Industry Temperature Check, DSIT developed the DSIT Portfolio of AI Assurance Techniques to address some of the barriers identified in the report.The initiative has the following objective(s):The Portfolio is designed to support industry, including start-ups and SMEs to identify relevant assurance techniques and standards for their context of use.

items.document_name: Proyecto de Reglamento de la Ley N. 31814, Ley que promueve el uso de la inteligencia artificial en favor del desarrollo económico y social del paí­s
items.body:
Proposed Regulation of Law 31814 that develops measures to promote the safe, ethical, sustainable, transparent, replicable, and responsible use and development of artificial intelligence.

The initiative has the following objectives:It creates an AI governance framework within public entities.It promotes international cooperation and building research networks to foster AI development.It promotes the public provision of computing capabilities for the development of AI.It promotes a pro-innovation policy environment by using regulatory sandboxes for AI.It encourages the use of open data and government data through APIs.It monitors the impact of AI on the labor market.It promotes the development of data science and AI skills in students, university students, and workers.It promotes measures to reduce bias and assure fairness when using AI.It creates ethical guidelines for the use of AI.It promotes public awareness about the ethical use of AI.It requires mandatory disclosure of when and how public entities use AI.It required mandatory disclosure of the person responsible for a product or service that uses AI.It mandates labeling of AI-generated content for public entities.It requires security measures appropriate to the level of risk of AI use.It promotes following international standards for AI when its use includes a high risk for citizens.

items.title: Draft Federal Data Protection Law
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
In September 2021, the United Arab Emirates (UAE) Minister of State for Artificial Intelligence, Digital Economy and Remote Work Applications announced that the UAE would introduce a new federal data protection law, the first federal law of its kind in the UAE.

The initiative has the following objectives:To establish a unified data protection regime in the UAE that would provide an adequate level of protection for the purposes of data transfers from the European Union and other regulated jurisdictions

items.title: Doctoral Graduates' Employment
items.original_name: Concurso De Estímulo ao Emprego Científico
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Concurso De Estímulo ao Emprego Científico
items.body:
FCT runs a career development program to ensure the integration of highly qualified and international competitive scientists into research and academic centers.

Under the Decree 57/2016, amended by Law 57/2017, it funds a mechanism for public and private institutions integrated in the Portuguese Scientific and Technological System to hire doctoral researchers. This mechanism supports the hiring of doctoral researchers in all scientific areas through annual calls (Scientific Employment Stimulus - individual calls) as well as it supports the development of R&D institutional activities through calls directed at institutions to hire doctoral researchers (Scientific Employment Stimulus “ institutional calls).Since the Scientific Employment Stimulus entered into force, five individual calls (CEEC 2017, CEEC 2018, CEEC 2020, CEEC 2021 and CEEC 2022), and two institutional call (CEEC Institution 2018 and CEEC Institution 2021) have been issued.In these five individual calls, twenty-eight AI-oriented doctoral researchers were recommended to be granted a sixty-years contract. Doctoral researchers are funded for a period of three years according to three criteria, - i.e., the number of years holding a Ph.D., adequacy of the curriculum to the scientific area, and proof of scientific independence: junior researcher ( 2.128,34), assistant researcher ( 3.191,82), principal researcher ( 3.601,03), and coordinating researcher ( 4.664,97).The public investment in the AI-oriented doctoral researchers' employment is difficult to estimate in this exercise, due to different variables, namely the modalities of contract (directly or via institution), variable costs, and contractual changes (e.g. three contracts were terminated during the first year). However, it can be indicated the funding for 2019 (  567 365,67) , for 2020 ( 1 163 876,43) and 2021 ( 1 229 025,46).The initiative has the following objectives:- Ensure the integration of highly qualified and international competitive scientists into research and academic centers.

items.title: Discussion Paper on Generative AI - Implications for Trust and Governance
items.original_name: Discussion Paper on Generative AI - Implications for Trust and Governance
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Discussion Paper on Generative AI - Implications for Trust and Governance
items.body:
IMDA and Aicadium have published a discussion paper to share Singapore's approach to building an ecosystem for trusted and responsible adoption of Generative AI, in a way that spurs innovation and tap on its opportunities.

The initiative has the following objectives:The paper seeks to enhance discourse and invite like-minded partners from around the world to work with Singapore to ensure that Generative AI can be trusted and used in a safe and responsible manner.

items.title: Digitising European industry
items.category: AI Policy Frameworks and Initiatives (intergovernmental or supranational)
items.body:
This resolution welcomes the Commission's communication on digitising European industry.

The resolution highlights the need to "establish leadership in digital industrial value chains and key technologies such as 5G, quantum technologies, high-performance computing, artificial intelligence, cloud computing, big data analytics, the Internet of Things (IoT), robotics, automation (including Highly-Automated Driving) and Distributed Ledger Technology".The initiative has the following objectives:- To create conditions for successful industrial digitisation: infrastructure, investment, innovation and skills.- To develop an integrated Industrial Digitalisation Strategy (IDS) for the EU.

items.title: Digital Uzbekistan - 2030
items.org: Ministry of Development of Information Technologies and Communications
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
Digital Uzbekistan - 2030 is a national strategy to use digital technologies to improve government services and daily life for all citizens. It aims to connect more people to fast internet, make online services widely available, and help the country become more modern and competitive. The initiative was created to reduce inequality, increase efficiency, and prepare Uzbekistan for the digital future.

President Mirziyoyev has furthermore instructed the creation of a specialized research institute for development of digital technologies and artificial intelligence, whose main endeavours are envisaged to be, inter alia, the organization of scientific research aimed at the widespread implementation of the Digital Uzbekistan “ 2030 Strategy, the formation of a scientific ecosystem for the development of digital technologies and the development of innovative products for the automation of management and production processes based on artificial intelligence technologies.The initiative has the following objectives:To accelerate development of the digital industry in the republic.To increase competitiveness of national economy.To ensure realisation of the tasks determined in the State program by strategy implementation of actions in five priority directions of development of the Republic of Uzbekistan in 2017 - 2021 in "Year of development of science, education and digital economy."

items.title: Digital Trust Framework, approved by Urgent Decree N. 007-2020
items.original_name: Decreto de Urgencia 007-2020 que aprueba el marco de confianza digital y dispone medidas para su fortalecimiento
items.org: Presidency of the Council of Ministers, through the Secretariat of Government and Digital Transformation
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.document_name: Decreto de Urgencia 007-2020 que aprueba el marco de confianza digital y dispone medidas para su fortalecimiento
items.body:
Article 12.2 provides that public entities and private sector organizations ensure the ethical use of artificial intelligence.

The Digital Trust Framework is a comprehensive approach to deal with the risks and threats on the digital environment. It is composed of digital security, personal data protection and consumer protection measures. As an essential component of the Digital Trust Framework, It has the National Registry of Cyber Incidents, which in charge of the Government and Digital Transformation Secretariat.The initiative has the following objectives:Ensure the ethical use of AI

items.title: Digital Transformation and Telecommunications Agency
items.original_name: Agencia de Transformación Digital y Telecomunicaciones
items.category: National – AI governance bodies or mechanisms
items.document_name: Agencia de Transformación Digital y Telecomunicaciones
items.body:
The Agency for Digital Transformation and Telecommunications is a new entity created by the government of Mexico, Its main objective is to digitize government procedures that are currently carried out in person. This seeks to simplify the lives of citizens, reduce corruption and improve administrative efficiency, among its specific objectives is to unify the technological capabilities of the government, generate technological autonomy. reduce budget costs and facilitate access to digital service

Mexico's Digital Transformation and Telecommunications Agency is considering the use of artificial intelligence in several of its projects. One of the main objectives is to improve the efficiency of the public administration through the digitization of procedures and processes, which is why it could be understood that it is linked to all aspects of technology, for which one of its functions also includes participating in international forums, regarding the matters of its competence,  with the appropriate intervention of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and to propose to it the conclusion of international conventions and treaties in such matters and to participate in the conclusion and monitoring of the implementation of international agreements in the areas of information technologies, communications, telecommunications and broadcasting.

items.title: Digital Transformation Strategy: The Bicentennial of Costa Rica
items.original_name: Estrategia de Transformación Digital hacia la Costa Rica del Bicentenario 4.0 2018-2022
items.org: Ministry of Science, Technology and Telecommunications
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Estrategia de Transformación Digital hacia la Costa Rica del Bicentenario 4.0 2018-2022
items.body:
This Strategy helps Costa Rica to build on and benefit from two major developments shaping productive processes and the quality of life of persons: the fourth industrial revolution and knowledge societies.

In order to foster the conditions for the development of the Digital Transformation Strategy: The Bicentennial of Costa Rica, the Government issued Executive Decree N.41248. This Decree establishes the creation of a High Level Commission of the Digital Government of the Bicentennial that will act as an advisory body for the development of the national strategy aimed at the implementation of the digital government public policy. In addition, the Government issued Directive N.019, which sets out guidelines for institutions of the public sector for the development of the Digital Government of the Bicentennial. In addition to the instruments promoting progress in areas such as government digitalization, the National Science and Technology Plan raises the need to include a Digital Agenda that identifies a strategy to use ICTs to develop tools that promote a rapprochement between public institutions and their respective users, thereby facilitating communication and interactions, as well as the processing of services. This Digital Transformation Strategy: The Bicentennial of Costa Rica is a response to the demands of the National Science and Technology Plan, the National Development of Telecommunications Plan, and defines the actions to achieve the provisions and objectives of the National Development Plan.The initiative has the following objectives:To guarantee the development and well-being of the population through the opportunities brought by Industry 4.0 and the knowledge society are two of the main objectives of the Government of the Bicentennial.

items.title: Digital Transformation Strategy for Africa
items.category: AI Policy Frameworks and Initiatives (intergovernmental or supranational)
items.body:
Recognizing the efforts of the continent's leadership to prioritize and accelerate digital transformation, and building on the vision of many African leaders, African countries are ready for a comprehensive digital transformation strategy to guide a common, coordinated response to reap the benefits of the fourth industrial revolution

The Digital Transformation Strategy for Africa will build on the existing initiatives and frameworks such as the Policy and Regulatory Initiative for Digital Africa (PRIDA), the Programme for Infrastructure Development in Africa (PIDA), the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), the African Union Financial Institutions (AUFIs), the Single African Air Transport Market (SAATM); and the Free Movement of Persons (FMP) to support the development of a Digital Single Market (DSM) for Africa, as part of the integration priorities of the African Union. The Smart Africa Initiative has set the creation of a Digital Single Market in Africa as its strategic vision.The initiative has the following objectives:To harness digital technologies and innovation to transform African societies and economies to promote Africa's integration, generate inclusive economic growth, stimulate job creation, break the digital divide, and eradicate poverty for the continent's socio-economic development and ensure Africa's ownershipof modern tools of digital management.

items.title: Digital Transformation Strategy Of Costa Rica
items.org: Ministry of Science, Innovation, Technology and Telecommunications
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
This Strategy promotes public policy actions to improve people's quality of life through the implementation of secure and resilient digital solutions at the service of citizens and all sectors of society with a perspective of co-creation and collaboration.

To foster the conditions for the development of the digital transformation strategy, there is a broad regulatory framework, but it is worth highlighting the Executive Decree N.41248, which establishes the High Level Commission of Digital Government, which will act as a consultative body for the development of the national strategy for the implementation of the public policy of digital government, and Law N.9943, which establishes the National Agency of Digital Government, as the executing body for interoperability and strategic projects in this area.There is a strategic framework within the institution that focuses on the development of the Costa Rican society and economy, which is the National Policy for the Knowledge-Based Society and Economy (PNSEBC); the plans of each vice ministry with a sectoral vision focused on their areas of work, such as the National Plan for Science, Technology and Innovation (PNCTI), the National Telecommunications Development Plan (PNDT), the National Cybersecurity Strategy and the Bioeconomy Strategy.In this way, the Digital Transformation Strategy seeks to be transversal to these planning instruments, developing digital government and governance components through its strategic axes.

items.title: Digital Transformation Guidelines
items.org: Ministry of Environmental Protection and Regional Development of the Republic of Latvia (VARAM)
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
Digital transformation of society, including private and public sectors

The Digital Transformation Guidelines 2021“2027 is Latvia's national policy framework guiding digital development across society, the economy, and public administration. The initiative was designed to address key challenges and opportunities in digitalisation, including the low level of digital technology adoption among businesses, lack of ICT specialists, and the need for more efficient, user-friendly public services. It builds upon Latvia's National Development Plan (NDP 2027) and aligns with EU strategies, including the Digital Europe Programme and Sustainable Growth Strategy, to support a digitally empowered and inclusive society.The Guidelines set five main development priorities: digital skills and education; digital security and trust; access to telecommunications and computing; digital transformation of the economy and public administration; and innovation, ICT industry, and science. Objectives include expanding broadband access, increasing public use of e-governance services, improving digital literacy, supporting SMEs with digital tools, and encouraging greater collaboration between the public and private sectors. Particular emphasis is placed on ensuring that all citizens can participate in and benefit from digital technologies throughout their lives.The initiative is being implemented through coordinated efforts between ministries, municipalities, the private sector, and NGOs. Funding comes from a mix of EU funds, state budget allocations, and private investment, with annual budget reviews to prioritise digital initiatives. One notable success has been the communication and training campaign My Latvia. Do it Digitally!, which helped over 6,000 professionals guide citizens in using e-services. However, gaps remain in SME digital adoption and ICT workforce capacity, both of which are key focus areas moving forward.Over time, the Guidelines are expected to evolve based on progress reviews and funding opportunities. Implementation is supported by strategic governance mechanisms, including cross-sectoral working groups and performance indicators. As digital technologies continue to advance, Latvia plans to strengthen its digital ecosystem, promote innovation, and increase competitiveness, while ensuring no one is left behind in the digital transition. These efforts aim to build a resilient, open, and future-ready society by 2027 and beyond.

items.title: Digital Tech Fund
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Digital Tech Fund, part of the Digital Luxembourg initiative, is a seed fund designed to support ICT start-ups and strengthen the country's tech ecosystem. It operates as a joint public-private partnership, with contributions from the government, Société Nationale de Crédit et d'Investissement (SNCI), the University of Luxembourg, and other key stakeholders. The fund focuses on investing in areas such as cybersecurity, fintech, big data, digital health, media, or next-generation comms.

This fund is part of the strategy Digital Ltzebuerg in which the state seeks to strengthen and consolidate the eminent position of the country in the field of ICT. As a consequence, the state participates in the fund with a budget of EUR 5 million. The financial contribution of other investors amounts to a total of EUR 15.33 million, of which EUR 3 million are from the National Credit and Investment Company (SNCI) and one million euros from the University of Luxembourg. The fund will take stakes in promising innovative enterprises created less than 7 years ago, and who develop products that already exist, preferably in the form of functional prototypes. The fund will focus primarily, but not exclusively, on venture capital investments in areas such as cybersecurity, FinTech, Big Data, Digital Health, media and the next-generation communication networks, digital learning, the Internet of Things or satellite telecommunications and services.The initiative has the following objectives:To support the financing and development of innovative start-ups in the field of information and communication technologies (ICTs).

items.title: Digital Task Force for AI
items.original_name: Digital Taskforce for kunstig intelligens i den offentlige sektor
items.org: Ministry of Digital Affairs and Ministry of Finance
items.category: National – AI governance bodies or mechanisms
items.document_name: Digital Taskforce for kunstig intelligens i den offentlige sektor
items.body:
To accelerate the roll-out of AI in the public sector, the government, together with Local Government Denmark and Danish Regions, have established a Digital Taskforce for Artificial Intelligence.
The Task force shall promote a structured and coordinated initiative to to identify and address barriers to the use of AI and promote large-scale deployment of AI solutions across the public sector.

The Digital Task Force for AI in Denmark was established to address the challenges and opportunities presented by the rapid development of artificial intelligence technologies. The initiative seeks to ensure that Denmark remains at the forefront of AI innovation while promoting ethical, responsible, and inclusive AI adoption across public and private sectors. It aims to tackle issues such as data privacy, AI governance, transparency, and the impact of AI on society and the labour market.The primary objectives of the Task Force include developing national strategies and guidelines that support trustworthy AI, fostering collaboration among government agencies, academia, and industry, and promoting public awareness and education about AI technologies. By coordinating efforts across sectors, the initiative works to create an AI ecosystem that balances innovation with ethical considerations, ensuring AI benefits all citizens and respects fundamental rights.Looking forward, the Digital Task Force for AI is expected to evolve into a permanent body that continuously monitors AI developments and advises policymakers on emerging risks and opportunities. It will institutionalize AI governance frameworks and encourage the integration of AI in public services while maintaining transparency and accountability. The initiative also plans to expand its outreach, facilitating international cooperation and knowledge exchange to strengthen Denmark's position in the global AI landscape.Since its inception, the initiative has grown from a coordinating task force to a more structured and collaborative platform involving diverse stakeholders. It has contributed to national AI policies, supported pilot projects, and enhanced dialogue on AI ethics and regulation. Ongoing updates reflect the fast-paced AI environment, ensuring that Denmark's approach remains adaptive and proactive in addressing new technological and societal challenges.

items.title: Digital Talent
items.org: National Training and Employment Service (SENCE) | OTIC SOFOFA (OTIC SOFOFA)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
This initiative integrates companies, training institutions, and the government to develop new capacities in people, in tune with the demands of the digital economy, generating more opportunities to access quality jobs. It aims to connect the demand for talent, the supply of training and job placement.

It is the only country initiative that integrates companies, training institutions, and the government to develop new capacities in people, in tune with the demands of the digital economy, generating more opportunities to access quality jobs. We work collaboratively to be a bridge that connects the demand for talents, the supply of training and job placement.Inspired by the successful international model New York Tech Talent Pipeline, we add efforts and capacities to articulate and implement the necessary mechanisms to identify the demand for talent, manage job training processes, evaluate the results of training, and generate employment opportunities. The initiative has the following objectives:We are determined to accelerate Chile's transition to the digital economy and urgently address the demands of a new market, expanding opportunities for both individuals and companies to reach their full potential.In our country there are severe gaps in IT professionals. For this reason, we have proposed to have 16,000 people trained between 2019 and 2022 who, through short and effective trainings, can apply for new job opportunities and change their life trajectory as entrepreneurs or within organizations or companies of any field.

items.title: Digital Switzerland Strategy
items.org: The Federal Chancellery's Digital Transformation and ICT Steering Division (DTI)
items.category: National – Strategy
items.body:
The "Digital Switzerland" Strategy provides the guidelines for government action and indicates where and how authorities, academia, the private sector, civil society and politics must work together in order to shape the transformation process for the benefit of everyone in Switzerland.

The initiative has the following objectives:To foster innovation, growth and prosperity in the digital world.To ensure equal opportunities and the participation of all.To promote transparency and security.To contribute to sustainable development.

items.title: Digital Society Initiative
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Initiative housed at the University of Zurich to help shape the digital transformation of society and science through research, education, and public outreach.

The initiative has the following objectives:- To research and inform the discourse on society's digital transformation- Engage with the public on digital transformation- Promote national and international cooperation across scientific disciplines

items.title: Digital Skills Initiative
items.org: Federal Chancellery of Austria (Bundeskanzleramt), Directorate General for Digitalisation and E-Government
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Austria has established a “Digital Skills Initiative” (Digitale Kompetenzoffensive) as an intersectional cooperation between five federal ministries (BKA, BMKOES, BMAW, BMF and BMBWF). The initiative focuses on the development and coordination of measures for digital literacy and skills. Under the umbrella of the initiative, the Digital Competencies and Skills strategy outlines how Austria is going to achieve increased digital competencies among the citizens.

Austria has established a Digital Competencies Initiative (Digitale Kompetenzoffensive) as an intersectional cooperation between 4 federal ministries. The initiative focuses on the development and coordination of measures for digital literacy and skills. Under the umbrella of the initiative, the Digital Competencies and Skills strategy outlines how Austria is going to achieve more digital competencies among the citizens. Measures around AI are a major priority in the strategy.

Accordingly, a specific strategy for AI literacy and skills is currently in development and has successfully kicked off with an expert event in the beginning of July 2024. Following the explicit goals and principles of the general national digital literacy and skills strategy and the national AI strategy, the AI literacy and skills strategy will focus on the inclusion of population groups with low levels of digital literacy, like the elderly and rural population, and gender diversity for AI skills, with the aim to broaden the national IT expert's pool.

A number of AI workshops are already offered for free across the country as part of the general “Digital Everywhere”. AI will also be a major focus for the building-up programme “Digital Everywhere PLUS” with modular workshops, online learning, train-the-trainer concepts and other innovative teaching methods.

Currently, an AI competences consultation with experts from the AI Board, the national interest groups, scientific experts in education, adult education experts and other important stakeholder groups is in progress. The results will inform the further development of the programme and flow into a white paper on AI competences as a backbone of the programme. In parallel, a scientific working group for the definition of a basic curriculum on AI has kicked off to make sure that AI courses are meeting the criteria of critical AI literacy of the population.

items.title: Digital Services Act Package
items.category: AI Policy Frameworks and Initiatives (intergovernmental or supranational)
items.body:
The Digital Services Act and Digital Markets Act aim to create a safer digital space where the fundamental rights of users are protected and to establish a level playing field for businesses.

The Digital Services Act (DSA) and the Digital Market Act (DMA) form a single set of rules (Digital Services Act package) that entered into force in November 2022. They have two main goals. First, to create a safer digital space in which the fundamental rights of all users of digital services are protected. Second, to establish a level playing field to foster innovation, growth, and competitiveness, both in the European Single Market and globally.

items.title: Digital Rights Charter
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
This charter presents a set of digital rights to be followed by institutions using digital technologies in their work.

This text is based on the significant progress already made in Spain in the recognition of digital rights, including Title X of Organic Law 3/2018 of 5 December on the Protection of Personal Data and the guarantee of digital rights and the recently approved Royal Decree-Law 28/2020 of 22 September on distance work.The initiative has the following objectives:The objective of the Charter is descriptive, prospective and assertive. Descriptive of the digital contexts and scenarios that determine conflicts, sometimes unexpected, between rights, values and goods that have always existed, but which require new consideration; this mere description helps to visualise and become aware of the impact and consequences of digital environments and spaces. Prospective in anticipating future scenarios that can already be predicted. Assertive in the sense of revalidating and legitimising the principles, techniques and policies that, from the very culture of fundamental rights, should be applied in present and future digital environments and spaces.

items.title: Digital Republic Bill
items.org: Ministry of Economy, Industry and Digital
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
The Digital Republic Bill is the result of large-scale direct consultations with the community and has three components: (1) data and knowledge flow; (2) protection of citizens in the digital society; and (3) access to digital for all.

The initiative has the following objectives:To disseminate wider data and knowledge.To ensure equal rights for Internet users.To promote fraternity through an inclusive digital society.

items.title: Digital Platform SPROGTEKNOLOGI.DK
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
A joint public sector collaboration was initiated to develop a Common Danish language resource.

In June 2020, the Danish government in collaboration with municipalities and regions launched the website sprogteknologi.dk where metadata about existing language resources are gathered and displayed. Future actions include the development of further Danish language resources, e.g. a central word register and the development of a Danish speech recognition resource.Furhter open-source text data should ensure easy and efficient access to data, thereby accelerating innovation in, for example, small and medium-sized Danish enterprises. With open-source text data, all actors”Danish and international”will be able to use the data to create competitive Danish-language artificial intelligence. The available data should be accessible open-source on sprogteknologi.dk, where it will be presented alongside additional Danish language data.

items.title: Digital Pathology and Radiology Programme
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The UK (BEIS and DHSC) has funded up to 50 million for five new centres of excellence in England for digital pathology and imaging, including radiology, using AI medical advances. As of 2019, this has received an additional 50m to expand the programme within the existing centres.

The initiative has the following objective(s):A programme to revolutionise Digital Pathology and Radiology using AI, ensuring routine cases take a fraction of the time to assess, whilst allowing clinicians to concentrate on complex cases. This programme has recently been awarded an additional £50m investment from the Department of Health and Social Care to scale up the work of the Centres of Excellence. The work of the Centres, supported by this new funding, will ultimately lead to more intelligent analysis of medical imaging and pathology data, and the development of new innovative ways of using AI to: speed up diagnosis of diseases, improve outcomes for patients, and free up more NHS staff time for direct patient care.

items.title: Digital Luxembourg
items.org: Ministry of State (METAT) | Ministry of Finance (MFIN) | Ministry of the Economy (MECO)
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
Consolidating Luxembourgs position in the ICT fields in the longer term.

Over the past ten years, Luxembourg's digital economy has experienced unprecedented growth. The aim was clear: starting with infrastructure, to create the most propitious environment for the growth of companies in the information and communication technologies (ICT) sector. Successive Luxembourg governments have made this their leading priority and have acted accordingly.But outstanding infrastructure is not enough. The digital transformation affects all aspects of public and private life. Companies and citizens want, and the country must progress further along this path. To that end, it needs leaders who understand the challenges facing companies and citizens on a daily basis, and needs to introduce legislation designed to back their development while providing public services that are adapted to their requirements.After laying down the foundations and in order to ensure the long-term viability of the changes being made, the government of Luxembourg sought to provide a common umbrella for the numerous public and private initiatives that make up the country's digital economy and society. Thus, in autumn 2014, the Digital Luxembourg initiative was launched.The initiative has the following objectives:To provide a common umbrella for public and private initiatives that make up the country's digital economy and society.

items.title: Digital Innovation Cooperation Platform
items.org: Ministry of Industry and Technology|Presidency Of The Republic Of Turkiye Digital Transformation Office
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The cooperation platform serves as a dynamic nexus, uniting public institutions, organizations, industrial entities, and R&D infrastructures engaged in the research, development, application, and dissemination of Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Robotics, and related technologies. Its overarching mission is to expedite the implementation of multidisciplinary projects, leveraging national resources and opportunities to drive the creation of economic, technological, and social value.

The platform is set to enter its next phase, aiming to include representatives from the private sector and relevant NGOs after establishing cooperation with public institutions. This expansion seeks to form effective consortia within the platform, enabling the dissemination of advanced digital technology solutions developed within the country to a broader ecosystem.The initiative has the following objectives:- Highly effective coordination of the development of domestic technology solutions for public needs- Supporting short/long term trainings for the development of advanced digital skills- Establishing a consortium and supporting project development for the Digital Europe Program calls and other Union Programs- Supporting strategy and policy studies in order to benefit from the opportunities that the digital economy will create in the future with the highest efficiency- Expanding the scope of service with international collaborations- Supporting the formation of consortia of European Digital Innovation Hubs

items.title: Digital Hub Initiative
items.org: Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy (BMWi)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Germany's federal structure with broad regional start-up communities includes cross-sectoral innovation hubs such as Berlin, Hamburg and Munich as well as specific sectoral innovation hubs like Frankfurt.

In order to foster this start-up ecosystem as a whole, Germany has set up the Digital Hub Initiative with two main elements: First, the regional hubs are linked and coordinated through a Hub Agency on federal level. The Agency provides support, organizes events and promotes the Initiative nationally. Second, Germany Trade and Invest is in charge of international cooperation and promotion.Germany's federal structure with broad regional start-up communities includes cross-sectoral innovation hubs such as Berlin, Hamburg and Munich as well as specific sectoral innovation hubs like Frankfurt. In order to foster this start-up ecosystem as a whole, Germany has set up the Digital Hub Initiative with two main elements: First, the regional hubs are linked and coordinated through a Hub Agency on federal level. The Agency provides support, organizes events and promotes the Initiative nationally. Second, Germany Trade and Invest is in charge of international cooperation and promotion.Objectives:To foster co-operations within each digital hub, by strengthening the networking between start-ups and scientific institutes, SMEs and large corporations.To foster co-operations between the digital hubs, by encouraging cross-sectoral interactions for innovation, in order to strengthen the network and drive forward the digital transformation.To create and spread the de:hub brand with the aim of increasing the visibility of digital hubs and attracting international start-ups, investors and talents.

items.title: Digital Hub Denmark
items.original_name: Digital Hub Denmark - partnerskab for digital vækst
items.org: Ministry for Industry, Business and Financial Affairs
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Digital Hub Denmark - partnerskab for digital vækst
items.body:
A platform aiming at developing public-private collaboration models. It helps bringing together private businesses, researchers, tech-entrepreneurs, and students to foster the development of new digital products.

Digital Hub Denmark was established in May 2018 and in November 2018, the 2019 Agreement on Allocation of the Research Reserve was unilaterally passed by Parliament and DKK 100 millIions (EUR 13.4 million) were allocated to activities in a National Centre for Research in Digital Technologies.The initiative has the following objectives:A public/private partnership with the ambition to:1) support access to competences and collaborations between established universities, companies and other stakeholders;2) to strengthen companies' access to knowledge and experts within commercial use of digital technologies;3) to market Denmark as a digital frontrunner with a view to attracting investments and digital competences to Denmark;4) to establish a centre with the purpose of solving the capacity issue by building the necessary research capacity in Denmark via excellent research of the highest international class.

items.title: Digital Government Strategy 2023-2030
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Digital Government Strategy (2023-2030) defines the Kingdom's aspirations, vision, objectives, initiatives, and roadmap. Most strategic initiatives are geared towards achieving the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the Saudi Vision 2030. The Strategy is also guided and aligned with the Saudi Vision 2030 goals and strategic objectives.

To be determined

items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
The Digital Government Regulatory Framework categorized as an organizational tool based on international best practices. With this framework, the main components of designing and strategically executing the digital government policy are created, and it works on unifying the concept of policies, standards, and guidelines of digital government.

To be determined

items.title: Digital Education Action Plan
items.category: AI Policy Frameworks and Initiatives (intergovernmental or supranational)
items.body:
The Digital Education Action Plan (2021-2027) outlines the European Commission's vision for high quality, inclusive and accessible digital education in Europe.

The Digital Education Action Plan (2021-2027) outlines the European Commission's vision for high quality, inclusive and accessible digital education in Europe.The initiative has the following objectives: 'To foster the development a high-performing digital education ecosystem.  This requires: infrastructure, connectivity and digital equipment. effective digital capacity planning and development, including up-to-date organisational capabilities. digitally competent and confident teachers and education and training staff. high-quality learning content, user-friendly tools and secure platforms which respect privacy and ethical standards.To enhance digital skills and competences for the digital transformation.  This requires: basic digital skills and competences from an early age (i.e. digital literacy, including fighting disinformation; computing education; good knowledge and understanding of data-intensive technologies, such as artificial intelligence). advanced digital skills which produce more digital specialists and also ensure that girls and young women are equally represented in digital studies and careers.

items.title: Digital Economy Partnership Agreement (New Zealand, Singapore, Chile, and South Korea)
items.original_name: Digital Economy Partnership Agreement (New Zealand, Singapore, Chile, and South Korea)
items.org: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade New Zealand|Ministry of Trade & Industry Singapore (MTI)|Ministry of Foreign Affairs Chile | Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy, Republic of Korea
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.document_name: Digital Economy Partnership Agreement (New Zealand, Singapore, Chile, and South Korea)
items.body:
The Digital Economy Partnership Agreement (DEPA) between New Zealand, Singapore, Chile and South Korea will help establish new rules and practices for digital trade, and promote ongoing discussion on issues like digital inclusion, inclusive trade and support for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in the digital economy.

The Digital Economy Partnership Agreement (DEPA) between New Zealand, Singapore and Chile is an agreement that establishes new approaches and collaborations in digital trade issues, promotes interoperability between different regimes and addresses the new issues brought about by digitalisation. The Republic of Korea joined the DEPA on 3 May 2024. The agreement covers broad areas, from e-invoicing to artificial intelligence, and will continue to evolve as new digital opportunities and issues emerge.The initiative has the following objectives:DEPAs commitments include: Cooperation - Implement the agreement and explore how to further enhance our digital economy partnership. Trade facilitation - Facilitate paperless trading, e-invoicing, e-payments and streamlined customs procedures for parcels. SMEs and the digital economy - Share information that SMEs need to operate in the digital economy and develop a Digital SME Dialogue. Consumer trust - Promote online consumer protection to ensure consumers have the information to trade with confidence and access to appropriate redress if things go wrong. Digital products “ Promote a level playing field for digital products through provisions regarding the non-discrimination of digital products and ICT products that use cryptography. Data issues - Protect personal information and ensure generally free cross-border data flows and freedom regarding the location of computer facilities. Innovation - Enhance and encourage innovation in the digital economy, such as through open government data.Digital identities - Start discussing digital identities, and share best practice on digital identity policies and regulations. Emerging technologies - Explore new issues, including competition in the digital economy. Promote financial technology and develop frameworks to support the safe and responsible use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies. Digital inclusion - Establish a framework for future cooperation between partners on matters of digital inclusion and inclusive trade, including new people-to-people connections among Indigenous Peoples.

Emerging technologies - Explore new issues, including competition in the digital economy. Promote financial technology and develop frameworks to support the safe and responsible use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies. Digital inclusion - Establish a framework for future cooperation between partners on matters of digital inclusion and inclusive trade, including new people-to-people connections among Indigenous Peoples.

items.title: Digital Czech Republic
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Digital Czech Republic is a national strategy that supports the country's transition to the digital age. It focuses on digital public services, education, the economy, and cooperation within the EU. The initiative aims to improve digital skills, modernize public administration, and boost economic growth through digital technologies.

The digitalisation strategy of the Czech Republic covers three different levels: (i) Czech Republics approach towards the EU digital agenda, (ii) further development of e-Government, and (iii) the digitalisation of the economy and society and (iv) digital skills development and training of experts in the area of ICT (in relation to the priorities on European level)..It is a set of concepts that create the conditions for the long-term prosperity of the Czech Republic. Its content can be defined as follows: Strategy of Coordinated and Comprehensive Digitalisation of the Czech Republic 2018+.Under the 2020 update of the strategy a specific goal focusing on AI was added "Profiling of the Czech Republic as a country supporting the development of artificial intelligence". The revised implementation plans for 2020-2021 can be found (in CZ) here: https://www.mvcr.cz/clanek/rada-vlady-pro-informacni-spolecnost.aspx?q=Y2hudW09Ng%3D%3DThe IP contain specific action steps, projects and estimated budget needed for their implementation. The timeline is in the range of 1-10 years, depends on the specific project. Activities concerning Digital Czechia Strategy and its implementation are shared among many platforms: - Website for the umbrella Innovation Strategy https://www.countryforfuture.com/en/pilir/digitalization/- twitter account (@digiczech, @country4future)- newsletter "Czech Republic in the Digital Europe"- conferences, seminars and other events. The Government Council for Information Society has regular plenary sessions involving experts from the government bodies, stakeholders from civil society and businesses (Confederation of Industry and Transport, Chamber of Commerce, Association of Regions, etc.). The European Digital Innovation Hubs is a concept launched within the Digital Europe Program. The goal of the centers will be to help transfer new technologies from the research to the market use. Each MS will have several eDIHs, CZ will have 6-8 that will be cofinanced from the EU funds.

items.title: Digital Catapult
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Digital Catapult Centre in the UK is an advanced technology innovation centre established by Innovate UK. It supports early adoption of advanced digital technologies which can then be emulated by UK industry more widely to drive innovation and economic growth, with a focus on the creative and manufacturing sectors.

Digital Catapult focuses on three priority technologies: AI, Future Networks (e.g. 5G and Internet of Things) and Immersive technologies (e.g. virtual and augmented reality).It focuses on two industries: manufacturing and creative sectors.The initiative has the following objective(s):Providing technical and innovation expertise to deliver interventions, facilities and programmes that overcome key barriers to the growth of digital technology companies.Acting as an independent and transnational interface between the UK's digital sector and the wider UK economy.Working with key industries to shape national strategies around the adoption and innovation of emerging digital technologies.Representing the needs of start-ups and scale-ups and informing government and industries to design policy intervention or industry initiatives that overcome common barriers and accelerate growth.

items.title: Development of the Legal and Conceptual Framework for the Establishment and Operation of a National Regulatory Sandbox for Artificial Intelligence
items.original_name: Priprava pravnega in vsebinskega okvira vzpostavitve in delovanja nacionalnega regulativnega peskovnika za umetno inteligenco
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.document_name: Priprava pravnega in vsebinskega okvira vzpostavitve in delovanja nacionalnega regulativnega peskovnika za umetno inteligenco
items.body:
This initiative establishes a national regulatory sandbox for AI in Slovenia,   The main objective is to create a legal and governance framework that allows for safe and compliant testing of AI solutions while addressing legal challenges. At the same time, the initiative ensures that AI development respects human rights, environmental protection, and market competitiveness.

The objectives of the initiative are: Establishing the legal and conceptual framework for the operation of a national regulatory sandbox for artificial intelligence in Slovenia, in accordance with EU legislation, particularly Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 on harmonized AI rules (AI Act), Enabling safe, efficient, and legally compliant testing of AI solutions while fostering innovation in this field. Establishing a regulatory sandbox for AI with a legal and governance framework, Developing a legal basis through comparative analyses and the creation of standards for participation in the sandbox, Focusing on ethical and legal issues such as data protection, human rights, and security, Disseminating results and increasing public awareness through analysis, articles, and events.

items.title: Development of Scikit-learn Ecosystem
items.org: National Institute for Research in Digital Science and Technology (Inria)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:

The initiative has the following objectives:Consolidate Scikit-Learn's leading position in data science.Extend Scikit-Learn toolbox to tackle new trends and use cases, especially in industrial sectors and with issues relative to trustworthy AI.Enhance Scikit-Learn's position in the Big Data segment by speeding up the library, allowing better parallelisation and GPUs use tools, but also by working on a better integration with Deep Learning libraries such as Tensorflow and Pytorch.Enhance Scikit-Learn along with the whole open-source Data Science ecosystem with a self-contained, interoperable Data Wrangling package.Position France in the global effort for the Web 4.0 by developing locally pieces of the futures W3C standards (especially RDF 2.0).

items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Développement d'un écosystème de Deep Learning embarqué à partir de la plateforme N2D2 du CEA
items.body:
Sovereign framework for deep learning at the edge.

In the 2010s decade there had been a growing tendency on Deep Learning, and in the meantime on intensive cloud computing. From Deep Learning Framework (Tensorflow, Pytorch) to computing hardware (AMD, Nvidia, Intel) the market had been dominated by a few numbers of actors, mostly American and Europe was roughly left aside.In the recent years there have been a shift of attention toward Edge AI and embedded application.Europe not only have a role to play in those new techologies yet to emerge, but those have a special importance for the continent, whose industries are historically very oriented on sectors like automotive or aeronautic which would be very relying on Edge AI.The initiative has the following objectives:Develop and maintain a sovereign and trustworthy platform for embedded AI in critical and strategic applications, especially for defence and critical systems (power grid, transportation network, etc.).

items.original_name: Opredelitev modela kazalnikov za spremljanje potenciala uvajanja UI v Sloveniji
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.document_name: Opredelitev modela kazalnikov za spremljanje potenciala uvajanja UI v Sloveniji
items.body:
Definition of an indicator model and methodology for assessing and monitoring the uptake of AI in the private and public sectors in Slovenia, with an overview of the situation in Slovenia (including an overview of stakeholders in Slovenia - public and private sector) and an analysis of the factors influencing the pace of AI uptake.

The initiative has the following objectives:- Definition of a model of indicators and a methodology for assessing the uptake of AI in Slovenia (in the private and public sectors). The methodology should relate to methodologies and analyses already defined at EU level.- review and assess the state of play of the deployment of AI in Slovenia according to a prepared methodology (by sector, by size of organisation, etc.) in the private and public sectors, based on a representative sample of stakeholders in Slovenia (public and private organisations) that use or intend to deploy AI in their business (to improve and optimise their own operations and business processes, or to create new innovative services and products for their users, suppliers or customers);- Analysis of factors influencing the ability and interest to accelerate the deployment of AI, including internal factors within organisations (e.g. human resources, financial resources, computerisation of internal operations, computerisation of operations with external partners in the value chain, availability and accessibility of data, changes in work processes, employee readiness for change, etc.), market factors and other factors (e.g. regulatory compliance, ethical compliance).

items.original_name: Opredelitev okvira za zagotavljanje zaupanja javnosti v rešitve UI na podlagi različnih socialno tehnoloških dejavnikov

items.document_name: Opredelitev okvira za zagotavljanje zaupanja javnosti v rešitve UI na podlagi različnih socialno tehnoloških dejavnikov

Defining a framework for ensuring public trust in AI solutions based on socio-technological factors, based on the interaction between the technological characteristics of AI technologies, methodologies for developing and deploying AI solutions, standardisation, the use of different licensing modalities (open source, proprietary software), on the one hand, and ethical and legal principles, cultural and social characteristics and social status, on the other hand.

Initiative relates to implementation of 7th strategic goal of links to National AI programme ensuring Increasing public trust in the AI.The initiative has the following objectives:- Determine and analyse the impact of various characteristics of the AI system such as technological characteristics (e.g. robustness, explainability, transparency, models used), development methodologies used (e.g. classical, agile, incremental), existence of and compliance with relevant standards, type of licensing (e.g. open source, proprietary software) that are relevant to individual trust in AI;- Identification and analysis of the impact of different ethical principles and fundamental rights on individual trust in AI;- Identify and analyse the impact of cultural and societal characteristics such as economic stability, social vulnerability, access to education, risk perception, appropriate legislation to ensure legal certainty and predictability, etc. on individual trust in AI;

items.title: Declaration of U.S.-UK Co-operation in AI R&D
items.original_name: Declaration of U.S.-UK Co-operation in AI R&D
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Declaration of U.S.-UK Co-operation in AI R&D
items.body:
Building on the U.S.-UK Science and Technology Agreement signed in September 2017, this Declaration communicates the U.S. and the UK's intention to advance their shared vision and work towards an AI R&D ecosystem.

This Declaration is an outcome of the U.S.-UK Special Relationship Economic Working Group, which was established following a meeting between President Donald J. Trump and Prime Minister Boris Johnson in 2019.The initiative has the following objective(s):To take stock of and utilise existing bilateral and multilateral science and technology co-operation frameworks.To recommend priorities for future co-operation, particularly in R&D areas where each partner shares strong common interest and brings complementary challenges, regulatory or cultural considerations, or expertise to the partnerships.To co-ordinate as appropriate the planning and programming of relevant activities in these areas, including promoting researcher and student collaboration that could potentially involve national partners, the private sector, academia, and the scientific community.To promote AI R&D, focus on challenging technical issues, and protect against efforts to adopt and apply these technologies in the service of authoritarianism and repression.

items.title: Declaration of Montevideo
items.category: AI Policy Frameworks and Initiatives (intergovernmental or supranational)
items.body:
Ministers and High-Level Authorities representing the countries gathered at the Second Ministerial and High-Level Authorities Summit on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence in Latin America and the Caribbean, on October 3rd and 4th, 2024.  Countries include Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Cuba, Curacao, Ecuador, El Salvador, Honduras, Jamaica, Mexico, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, Dominican Republic and Uruguay.

This initiative will seek to promote the regional cooperation in AI that contributes to the economic and social development of the countries of the region with an ethical approach.

items.title: Declaration of Cooperation on AI
items.category: AI Policy Frameworks and Initiatives (intergovernmental or supranational)
items.body:
Addressing this emerging trend, on 10 April 25 European countries signed a Declaration of cooperation on AI.

Artificial intelligence (AI) endows systems with the capability to analyse their environment and take decisions with some degree of autonomy to achieve goals. Machine learning denotes the ability of a software/computer to learn from its environment or from a very large set of representative data, enabling systems to adapt their behaviour to changing circumstances or to perform tasks for which they have not been explicitly programmed. To build robust models at the core of AI-based systems, high-quality data is a key factor to improve performances. The Commission adopted legislation to improve data sharing and open up more data for re-use. It includes public sector data as well as research and health data.The initiative has the following objectives:Whereas a number of Member States had already announced national initiatives on Artificial Intelligence, they now declared a strong will to join forces and engage in a European approach to deal therewith. By teaming up, the opportunities of AI for Europe can be fully ensured, while the challenges can be dealt with collectively.To make the most of it for the citizens and the economy, the European Commission will engage in a dialogue with all actors on the future of AI in Europe, to allow for an open discussion of all relevant developments and their impact on the economy and society.

items.title: Decision about Plan for AI R&D
items.original_name: Quyết định của Bộ trưởng Bộ Khoa học và Công nghệ về Kế hoạch triển khai "Nghiên cứu và Phát triển trí tuệ nhân tạo đến năm 2025"

Measures and initatives are described in this Decision with the aim to supporting Viet Nam to take best use of AI in economic growth for the period of 2018-2025.

At the National Forum in AI, it was the highlight activity to implement this Plan. It drew more than 2,000 participants with event on AI start-ups. Ho Chi Minh City used AI technology to develop a smart city model, particularly in the transportation and health services.The initiative has the following objectives:To research and monitor AI technology to develop AI products made in Viet Nam, creating leverage for national economic growth.To develop a skillful labour force in the technical sector generally, and in the AI industry in particular.
