items.title: AI Use Cases in the Portuguese Public Sector
items.original_name: AI Use Cases in the Portuguese Public Sector
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: AI Use Cases in the Portuguese Public Sector
items.body:
AI use cases in the public sector in Portugal.

Within the scope of the DSAIPA (Data Science and Artificial Intelligence in the Public Administration) initiative, which aimed to increase and reinforce the digital skills of the Portuguese population, projects were financed that focused on promoting knowledge combined with innovation and the modernization of public services and the development of scientific research, in favor of the execution of public policies for the benefit of people. Of the 71 projects, 28 were financed by the Foundation for Science and Technology (FCT) and 43 by the Agency for Administrative Modernization (AMA). The total amount of funding amounted to more than 18 million euros.In 2022, INCoDe.2030, launched the second questionnaire with the entities indicated as responsible for the development of the project. In response to the questionnaire, it was possible to collect 52 responses from the 71 initially requested. 46 projects responded indicating concrete results of the state of maturation of their projects; 3 projects were extinguished and did not get started and 3 projects were at such an early stage that they did not have enough data to respond to the questionnaire. This questionnaire aimed to identify the state of maturity and development of financed projects. In summary, the result of the questionnaire allowed us to conclude that: Most do not have information available online (other than information regarding the project when it was launched) There are theses and scientific articles that focus on some projects (but only on specific parts and done before their completion) With four exceptions, there are no websites/pages about the projects, so it is unknown whether most of them are completed or not The best practice identified is MOVEPREVIS (project 3) because it has a dedicated website with all the information (still in progress) In some projects (few) the objectives and contacts of the researchers are not even found (probably they will no longer be assigned to the entities No completion report (of any project) was found available for consultationIn November 2022, a workshop was held, where 18 of the funded projects presented their projects to the Secretary of State for Digitization and Administrative Modernization and took stock of the added value of the projects and the difficulties experienced.The initiative has the following objectives:To promote AI usage in the public sector.

items.title: AI Upskilling Fund
items.org: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The AI Upskilling Fund will support small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) by match-funding AI skills training for their employees.

The UK government announced a £7.4 million pilot scheme to subsidise the cost of AI skills training for SMEs in the Professional Business Services sector. Of this, £6.4 million of grant funding is available. This pilot is funded through the £37.5 million Labour Market Evaluations and Pilots fund (LMEP), announced by the Chancellor at Spring Budget 2023.Eligible businesses can apply for up to 50% of the cost of AI skills training. This training should support employees to develop their technical skills and/or understanding of AI, helping them develop, deploy, or use AI in their role.Evidence shows that a lack of AI skills in businesses is hindering AI adoption, in part due to low investment in AI upskilling by UK businesses. This is particularly true in smaller companies. The pilot aims to increase AI adoption and productivity by incentivising greater employer-led investment in skills and training. Eligible businesses could apply for funding for up to 50% of the cost of AI skills training and other AI upskilling activities. The training should support employees to develop their technical skills and/or understanding of AI, helping them develop, deploy, or use AI in their role.Specifically, the objectives of the pilot are to:(1) Stimulate employer investment in AI training.(2) Address AI skills gaps in the UK workforce that are limiting AI adoption.(3) Measure the impact of AI upskilling on business productivity and outcomes.

items.title: AI Training for the Acquisition Workforce Act (Bill S-2551)
items.original_name: AI Training for the Acquisition Workforce Act (Bill S-2551)
items.org: The White House |Office of Management and Budget (OMB)|General Services Administration
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.document_name: AI Training for the Acquisition Workforce Act (Bill S-2551)
items.body:
This Bill requires the Director of the Office of Management and Budget to establish or otherwise provide an AI training program for the acquisition workforce and for other purposes.

The AI training program shall include information relating to: (A) the science underlying AI, including how AI works; (B) introductory concepts relating to the technological features of AI systems; (C) the ways in which AI can benefit the Federal government; (D) the risks posed by AI, including discrimination and risks to privacy; (E) ways to mitigate the risks described in subparagraph (D), including efforts to create and identify AI that is reliable, safe, and trustworthy; and (F) future trends in AI, including trends for homeland and national security and innovation.The initiative has the following objective(s):To ensure that the workforce has knowledge of the capabilities and risks associated with AI.

This Roadmap was released in November 2019 at Australia's national AI summit "Techtonic: Australia's AI Future", which hosted over 100 AI experts from across the nation.The initiative has the following objective(s):To provide an initial evidence base to guide government policy on AI.

items.title: AI Task Force
items.original_name: Oficina y Observatorio de Inteligencia Artificial
items.org: Presidency of the Republic of Colombia
items.category: National – AI governance bodies or mechanisms
items.document_name: Oficina y Observatorio de Inteligencia Artificial
items.body:
The Presidency of the Republic of Colombia, with the support of the Development Bank of Latin America (CAF), is working towards the design and implementation of a task force for AI in Colombia. This Task Force will be in charge of fostering the implementation of AI Policy. It will also promote and facilitate the use of AI in the public sector. The Presidency of the Republic is launching a website presenting the AI Project and its work.

The Administrative Department of the Presidency of the Republic (DAPRE), in response to the technical assistance provided by the Multilateral Bank, has decided to work towards a greater dynamization of AI governance in the country. The Government of Colombia has positioned itself as a regional and global leader in the construction of a public policy on Artificial Intelligence. Thus, the need has arisen to achieve an adequate implementation of the initiatives that have been developed and that meet these expectations. To this end, and with the objective of reinforcing the commitment assumed in the framework of the technical assistance provided on the subject, the technical design of a Project exclusively dedicated to this purpose has been proposed. This is part of an effort to institutionalize the artificial intelligence policy and give it a long-term scope, within the framework of the functions of the Administrative Department of the Presidency of the Republic, aimed at providing guidelines for the evaluation, formulation and implementation of public policies, AI being one of the strategic sectors to be promoted by the government.The initiative has the following objectives:To define mechanisms and tools to accelerate the implementation of Colombia's AI strategy or policy and ethical framework.To monitor projects in public entities that are using AI systems to provide a more efficient and effective service to the public.To increase international cooperation and coordination with governments and international entities on AI-related topics to achieve the goals of Colombias AI strategy.To develop mechanisms to foster the access and use of data for the design and development of AI systems.To increase collaboration with the private sector and the entrepreneurship ecosystem in AI-related topics.

Providing support to agencies that develop new AI solutions was one of the focuses of the National AI Strategy 2022-2023 to ensure the development safe and ethical AI solutions. The interest has been high and private sector experts are eager to collaborate.The initiative has the following objectives:To support organisations that are developing products and services that use data in innovative and safe ways;To encourage a data-driven decision-making process;To increase the capacity of institutions to initiate and execute projects involving the use of AI

items.title: AI Strategy of Japan
items.org: Integrated Innovation Strategy Promotion Council (Cabinet Office)
items.category: National – Strategy
items.body:
This Strategy describes measures that Japan should immediately take to overcome issues Japan faces by leveraging Japan's strengths and to open up opportunities for the future.

Since formulating the Strategy in 2019 in the form of four strategic objectives, the government has been actively promoting various measures to realize these strategic objectives. In addition, the government has reviewed and revised these measures on an annual basis.The initiative has the following objectives:To specify the environment and measures conducive to effective future utilization of AI, including generative AI, for the purposes of contributing to the solution of global issues through realization of Society 5.0 and overcoming the issues facing Japanese society.

items.title: AI Strategy for the Digital Government
items.original_name: Estrategia de Inteligencia Artificial para el Gobierno Digital
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Estrategia de Inteligencia Artificial para el Gobierno Digital
items.body:
This AI Strategy for the Digital Government presents the first actions to be carried out, through an open construction process, and shares what has been elaborated with different stakeholders to obtain their vision and contributions, both nationally and internationally.

AI policy is now part of a broader initiative that encompasses data management in public administration. This data policy and strategy for Digital Transformation establish the fundamental principles of government data as well as the organisational ecosystem to carry out a national data strategy that promotes and develops specific projects.The initiative has the following objectives:To promote and strengthen the responsible use of AI in Public Administration. Within that framework, four pillars that make up this strategy have been identified, each with specific objectives and lines of action. They are as follows:To advance AI governance in Public Administration.To advance capacity development for AI.To advance use and application of AI.To advance digital citizenship and AI.

A cross-governmental team was set up to devise recommendations for a policy plan to promote AI R&I activities in Israel.

On February 16, 2020, the chairman of the Telem Forum (the Hebrew acronym translates as 'The Israeli National Forum for R&D infrastructure') appointed an inspection committee to examine the need for government intervention in order to accelerate the development of the field of artificial intelligence and data science. This paper describes the work of the committee and its recommendationsThe initiative has the following objectives:To design a cross-agency and cross-sector policy plan to promote AI in Israel.

items.title: AI Strategic Program
items.org: Minister of technological innovation and digital transition (MITD)
items.category: National – Strategy
items.body:
Strengthening skills and attracting talents to develop an Artificial Intelligence ecosystem in Italy; increasing funding for advanced research in Artificial Intelligence; and incentivizing the adoption of Artificial Intelligence and its applications both in public administrations and in the private sector.

In 2019, a group of expert was set out by the Ministry of Economic Development in order to develop suggestions and proposals for a national strategy on artificial intelligence. The group concluded its activity presenting a document of proposals to build a draft strategy. The public consultation ended and the Ministry of Economic Development is wrapping up the final amendments and integrations. On 2 July 2020, the Ministry published the final document containing the Guidelines prepared by AI experts.The initiative has the following objectives:To strengthening frontier research in AI.To reduce the fragmentation of AI research.To develop and adopt human-centric and trustworthy AI.To increase AI-based innovation and AI technology development.To develop AI-based policies and services in the public sector.To create, retain and attract AI researchers in Italy.

This initiative collects the available instruments of public policy in Colombia that accelerate the development of the AI market and the promotion of entrepreneurship in this area. items.title: AI Standardisation Committee
items.org: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution | Ministry of Communications
items.category: National – AI governance bodies or mechanisms
items.body:
To tackle standardization challenges, the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) established an AI standardization committee aimed at creating various interface standards and developing India's AI stack. This stack will be organized across all sectors, focusing on data protection, data federation, data minimization, an open algorithm framework, defined data structures, interfaces and protocols, as well as proper monitoring, auditing, logging, and data privacy, among other aspects.

The Committee includes key stakeholders from ABB, BOSCH, NASSCOM, TCS, IIT Delhi, DSF, IIT Kanpur, NITI Aayog, Mahindra, IIT Patna and Intel.In September 2020, the Committee published an AI Stack paper highlighting five major horizontal pillars and one main vertical pillar, covering crucial aspects in AI deployment such as security, data storage, privacy, customer experience and computing. Objectives: To address certification methodologies, trustworthiness and AI standards.

items.title: AI Stakeholder Forum
items.org: Federal Chancellery of Austria and Federal Ministry for Climate Action, Environment, Energy, Mobility, Innovation and Technology (BMK)
items.category: National – AI governance bodies or mechanisms
items.body:
The AI Stakeholder Forum, founded March 2024, consists of various associations and interest groups and is intended to strengthen a lively and active exchange between the federal government and Austria's various stakeholders in the field of artificial intelligence. Part of the AI Stakeholder Forum are amongst others representatives of employers and labour in Austria, AI and IT associations, as well as associations for youth and for disabilities.

The AI Stakeholder Forum, founded March 2024, consists of 30 diverse associations and interest groups: The broad range of associations covers amongst others organisations from the AI ecosystem, representatives of employers and labour, as well as organisations representing the interests of people with disabilities, youth and senior citizens. The newly created forum is intended to promote and strengthen the exchange between the federal government, represented by Austria's Federal Chancellery (BKA) and Federal Ministry for Climate Action, Environment, Energy, Mobility, Innovation and Technology (BMK), and Austria's various stakeholders in the field of artificial intelligence.The AI Stakeholder Forums main objectives are: Exchange: The AI Stakeholder Forum aims to promote a lively and active exchange on various aspects of artificial intelligence, both between the federal government and stakeholders, as well as between the nominated members. Information: The AI Stakeholder Forum is also intended to distribute the latest news from the European Union, the Federal Government and the AI Advisory Board more quickly in order to be able to react more dynamically to upcoming changes resulting from the AI Act coming into force. Synergies: By bringing together the diverse and broad-based associations and interest groups in the AI Stakeholder Forum, new synergies can be found and new perspectives can be added to existing collaborations.

items.title: AI Source List
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The Government of Canada has created an AI Source List with 73 pre-approved suppliers to provide Canada with responsible and effective AI services, solutions and products. The framework allows government agencies to expedite procurement from firms that have demonstrated that they are capable of providing quality AI goods and services.

The initiative has the following objectives:Procurement vehicle to establish a pre-qualified list of suppliers (Source List) - who meet all of the mandatory criteria - to provide Canada with responsible and effective AI services, solutions and products.Qualified suppliers must demonstrate competence in AI ethics, as well as implementation and access to talent. Firms that responded to the Invitation to Qualify had to prove to an inter-disciplinary panel that they satisfied these requirements.The process of establishing and maintaining a list of AI service providers is an important way for the Government of Canada to engage with private companies in longer-term relationships. This dialogue facilitates the development of shared expectations and mutual understanding of the challenges faced by private companies which are relevant to public sector organisations.The framework has three bands with escalating requirements. The lowest band has less stringent requirements, making it easier for small start-ups to qualify, thereby driving innovation and creating a deeper market.

items.title: AI Skills for Business Competency Framework
items.original_name: AI Skills for Business Competency Framework
items.org: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: AI Skills for Business Competency Framework
items.body:
To address the skills barriers limiting AI adoption in businesses, the AI Skills for Business Competency Framework presents guidance, including the high-level skills and competencies employees need to support AI adoption. This is the first of a series of products designed to enable businesses to understand their AI upskilling needs and training providers to develop relevant training solutions.

The framework outlines the essential knowledge, skills, personal attributes, and behaviors necessary to effectively address practical challenges and demonstrate competence in both personal and professional contexts. It is designed for the following groups:1) **AI Citizens**: Individuals in the public who may engage with organizations utilizing artificial intelligence. The framework clarifies the understanding of AI, focusing on its capabilities, opportunities, and risks, thereby equipping AI Citizens with a realistic perspective on AI usage.2) **AI Workers**: Employees whose roles are not primarily centered on data but may still be influenced by these technologies. The framework aids AI workers in recognizing the efficiency and productivity enhancements that AI can offer in their jobs.3) **AI Professionals**: Individuals whose main responsibilities involve data and AI, such as data analysts, machine learning engineers, and data ethicists. The framework delineates the essential cross-disciplinary competencies needed to collaborate effectively within teams and across their organizations.4) **AI Leaders**: Senior personnel responsible for the acquisition and governance of AI solutions. The framework assists them in anticipating the implications of emerging technologies, including their effects on the workforce, and in overseeing the responsible and safe implementation of AI in complex organizational environments.The framework consists of five dimensions, each representing a set of competencies and behaviors across five key areas.**Dimension A: Privacy & Stewardship**. This dimension focuses on data security and protection, encompassing the design, creation, storage, distribution, and associated risks.**Dimension B: Specification, acquisition, engineering, architecture, storage, and curation**. This area addresses the collection, secure storage, manipulation, and curation of data, along with competencies related to data management and analytical techniques, including handling issues arising from the (mis)use of sensitive data.**Dimension C: Problem definition & communication**. This dimension emphasizes the ability to identify and articulate a problem clearly, understand how artificial intelligence can contribute to potential solutions, and effectively communicate this knowledge to diverse audiences.**Dimension D: Problem solving, analysis, modeling, visualization**. This area involves the knowledge and application of various mathematical, statistical, and computing tools and methods to define and analyze problems and present solutions.**Dimension E: Evaluation and Reflection**. It is crucial for all professionals in data science and AI to have a solid grasp of the ethical principles guiding their work and to take responsibility for the integrity of the models they develop.

The initiative has the following objectives:To catalyse AI innovation in the industry through projects and talents pipeline.To create significant economic and social impacts through solving national challenges.To invent next generation AI techniques and algorithms.The initiative has the following objectives:To catalyse AI innovation in the industry through projects and talents pipeline.To create significant economic and social impacts through solving national challenges.To invent next generation AI techniques and algorithms.

items.title: AI Service Desk
items.org: Federal Chancellery of Austria, Federal Ministry of Finance, Austrian Regulatory Authority for Broadcasting and Telecommunications (RTR-GmbH)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The AI Service Desk is set up at Austrian Regulatory Authority for Broadcasting andTelecommunications (RTR-GmbH) and serves as a point of contact and information hub for the general public on the topic of AI from a regulatory perspective. It also supports the implementation of the European AI Act by providing information on the regulatory framework for the use of artificial intelligence as well as aspects relating to cybersecurity, data economy and its use in the media sector.

Compliance with the AI Act is a key issue for a broad range of stakeholders who often face uncertainty and a lack of clarity on how the AI Act should be implemented. The Austrian AI Service Desk aims to help organisations achieve compliance with the AI Act and thus facilitate a smooth transition to a new regulatory framework for potential providers and deployers of AI systems. The AI Service Desk provides information on the AI Act, including through infographics, and responds to questions about its implementation, which are as a rule published after anonymisation as FAQs. Inaddition, it tenders studies on particular sectors or topics and organises events on key issues. Set up asof March 2024, the AI Service Desk has become a central contact point for regulatory questions relatedto the AI Act

items.title: AI Seoul Summit
items.org: Ministry of Science and ICT, Ministry of Foreign Affairs
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Following the AI Safety Summit held by the UK in 2023, the AI Seoul Summit contributed to making the AI Summit a leader-level platform for comprehensive discussion on global AI governance.The Seoul Declaration suggests a balanced global AI governance that promotes AI safety while also supporting AI innovation and inclusivity, and received endorsement from global AI leaders, including the G7.

The Seoul Declaration lays out three concrete priorities of safety, innovation, and inclusivity as the direction of global AI governance, and contributed to achieving a consensus among leaders, digital ministers, and CEOs from home and abroad.The Seoul Declaration, elevated from the 2023 ministerial-level Bletchley Declaration to a leader's level, was adopted by the leaders participating in the Summit to give a momentum to the international community's efforts to establish a governance and norms for AI, while also securing Korea's AI leadership.The Seoul Ministerial Statement was adopted by 28 digital ministers to take concrete steps to advance the vision of the Seoul Declaration through cooperation between developed and developing nations.In response to the Seoul Declaration, 14 Korean and global tech companies signed the Seoul Business Pledge, a voluntary commitment for ensuring responsible development and management of AI and sharing the benefits of AI.

items.title: AI Sector Deal
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The government and the AI sector have reached an agreement on a £1 billion support package aimed at enhancing the UK's position as a leader in AI technology development. This initiative will promote the goals of the Industrial Strategy's AI and Data Grand Challenge, ensuring the UK remains the top choice for AI innovation and investment. This deal is set to establish the UK as the premier destination for AI advancements and funding. The Industrial Strategy is founded on...

In 2021, the government released its new National AI Strategy as a follow-up to the 2018 AI Sector Deal. The Sector Deal builds on the review by Professor Dame Wendy Hall and Jer´me Pesenti, Growing the artificial intelligence industry in the UK', which involved an extensive range of business leaders, academics and research councils. UK's broad priorities in AI were first outlined in the Industrial Strategy White Paper which builds upon a previous independent report released titled, Growing AI Industry in the UK." Some of the main action areas highlighted in the strategy include: Find ways to use data and AI for prevention, early diagnosis and treatment of chronic diseases by the year 2030,especially for cancer diagnosis. Lead the world in safe and ethical use of data and AI and offer citizens and businesses more confidence and clarity inthe subject. Use automation to do extreme jobs which endanger human life. Help people develop the skills needed for the future jobsThe initiative has the following objective(s):Ideas - the world's most innovative economyPeople - good jobs and greater earning power for allInfrastructure - a major upgrade to the UK's infrastructureBusiness environment - the best place to start and grow a businessPlaces - prosperous communities across the UK

items.title: AI Sandbox Program of the National Data Protection Authority
items.original_name: Bac à sable de données personnelles de la CNIL
items.org: National Commission on Informatics and Liberty (CNIL)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: Bac à sable de données personnelles de la CNIL
items.body:
The CNIL, Commission Nationale Informatique & Libertes, is the French Data Protection Agency. As part of its support strategy, the CNIL has launched a first "personal data sandbox" session, in the form of a call for projects in the field of health.

Created in 1978, the CNIL is an independent administrative body that operates in accordance with the data protection legislation of the 6th January 1978 as amended on the 6th August 2004. The independence of the CNIL is guaranteed on account of its composition and organisation. The CNIL is responsible for ensuring that information technology remains at the service of citizens. Ten projects will benefit from CNIL support in 2021, four of which will receive enhanced support in order to come up with a solution that respects the privacy of individuals. CNIL has published several documents on artificial intelligence, such as their paper on algorithmic discrimination (2020) and "How can humans keep the upper hand? Report on the ethical matters raised by algorithms and artificial intelligence" (2017).The initiative has the following objectives:To ensure that data privacy law is applied to the collection, storage, and use of personal data.To foster data-driven innovation such as AI applications.To support the development of GDPR-compliant solutions (especially in the field of health for the 2021/2022 session, and edtech for 2022/2023).

items.title: AI Research Investments
items.org: Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Funding for AI research is allocated through several MBIE-administered mechanisms. E.g., AI is one of six priorities in the Catalyst Fund, and Data Science is one of ten platforms funded in the Strategic Science Investment Fund.

As at August 2024, since 2007 MBIE (and predecessors) has invested NZD $62.9 million directed towards AI or Machine Learning research across 103 projects.Of these, 44 projects have completed, leaving MBIE's total current investment in AI or Machine learning at $51.6 million across 59 active projects.For the majority (88) of the 103 projects, AI or Machine Learning was not the main focus of the research but contributed to other research aims.For 24 projects, 11 complete ($4.89 million) and 13 active ($11.5 million), AI or machine learning was the primary focus (more than 50%) of the research.Note that, in these figure, the total investment in the projects is mostly greater that the sums quoted, eg. the total investment in the headline 103 projects is $211 million. The dollar figures quoted are the value of the portion of the contracted specifically directed towards AI/Machine Learning research as opposed to other research aims.

items.title: AI Regulatory Sandbox Mexico
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
In Mexico, ANIA organizes working groups on AI to democratize knowledge and contribute to public policies and best practices. The need for an AI "sandbox" as a flexible mechanism to address technical, legal, and ethical implications was highlighted. In collaboration with the UK Embassy and AMCID, an analysis was initiated to promote technical exchange between the two countries and update the AI landscape in Mexico.

The collaboration between the British Embassy in Mexico, the Mexican Academy of Cybersecurity and Digital Law and ANIA is a significant step towards the consolidation of the AI ecosystem in Mexico. This project seeks to identify, together with regulators and experts, alternatives and tools to establish ethical standards and uses in the implementation of AI. Through the participation of specialists from various sectors, the aim is to answer crucial questions about the regulation, design and governance of  regulatory sandboxes,  paving the way for a more trustworthy, responsible and ethical digital future in Mexico.

The AI Sandbox will be implemented by two focus groups and they will work on the publication of initial guidelines. The initiative will include a quality label.

The AI Regulatory Sandbox, developed in collaboration with the European Commission, is a digital space that seeks to connect competent authorities with AI development companies to jointly define best practices when implementing future European AI regulation, and ensure its application.The AI Sandbox will be implemented by two focus groups and they will work on the publication of initial guidelines. items.title: AI Regulation White Paper
items.org: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT)
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Establishing clear, innovation-friendly, and flexible approaches to regulating AI will be core to achieving the UK's ambition to unleash growth and innovation while safeguarding fundamental values and keeping people safe and secure.

The initiative has the following objective(s):To be context-specific and acknowledge that AI is a dynamic, general purpose technology and that the risks arising from it depend principally on the context of its application.To be pro-innovation and risk-based, asking regulators to focus on applications of AI that result in real, identifiable, unacceptable levels of risk, rather than seeking to impose controls on uses of AI that pose low or hypothetical risk to avoid stifling innovation.To be coherent and ensure the system is simple, clear, predictable and stable.To be proportionate and adaptable, asking that regulators consider lighter touch options, such as guidance or voluntary measures, in the first instance.

items.title: AI Register
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects

Through the register, you can get acquainted with the quick overviews of the city's artificial intelligence systems or examine their more detailed information based on your own interests. You can also give feedback and thus participate in building human-centred AI in Helsinki.

Objectives:To ensure that the AI used in public services operates on the same principles of responsibility, transparency, and security as other local government activities.To improve both the availability of services and the experiences of customers.

This Guideline was prepared in 2017 as a basis for international discussions at G7 and OECD regarding matters expected to be considered in R&D activities for promoting the benefits and reducing the risks of AI.The initiative has the following objectives:These Guidelines aim at protecting the interests of users and deterring the spread of risks, thus achieving a human-centered Wisdom Network Society by way of increasing the benefits and mitigating the risks of AI systems through the sound progress of AI networks. items.title: AI Principles and Ethics for the Emirate of Dubai
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Dubai's AI Principles and Guidelines aim to help AI developers, government and society develop AI in a safe, responsible, and ethical way.

Launched in January 2019, the AI Principles and Guidelines for the Emirate of Dubai demonstrate Dubai's broader approach to ethical AI. Accompanying the Principles and Guidelines is an Ethical AI Self-Assessment Tool built to enable AI developer or operator organisations to evaluate the ethics level of an AI system. It gives an assessment (from proof of concept to production) of the potential ethical issues that may arise throughout the development process and how specific AI applications could be improved to ensure fairness, transparency, accountability and explainability. The tool also aims to ensure careful adoption of AI in which innovation potential is optimised and where economic and social value is captured. Dubai established a governing AI ethics board, comprising government policy, academic, legal and industry experts to oversee and guide the strategic development of the tool and guidance. The Executive Council of Dubai has directed government entities to use the principles and guidelines when considering AI development, and entities including the Road and Transport Authority and the Dubai Police have formally acknowledged their adoption of the self-assessment tool when developing AI.The initiative has the following objectives:To provide commissioners, developers, and users of AI with an understanding of how AI should be developed and monitored in a way that is fair, transparent, accountable, and explainable.To ensure that the innovation potential is optimised whilst societal risks are minimised.To capture economic and social value generated through AI and boost its use in pursuit of sustainability goals.To grow AI as a segment within Dubai's broader economy.

items.title: AI Portugal 2030 – National Strategy for AI
items.original_name: AI Portugal 2030 - Estratégia Nacional para Inteligência Artificial
items.category: National – Strategy
items.document_name: AI Portugal 2030 - Estratégia Nacional para Inteligência Artificial
items.body:
The AI Portugal 2030 strategy aims to foster a collective process mobilizing citizens at large and key stakeholders in particular, towards building-up a knowledge intensive labour-market with a strong community of forefront companies producing and exporting AI technologies supported by research and innovation communities involved in excellent high level research.

This strategy is fully in line with the EU's Coordinated Action plan and is part of INCoDe.2030, Portugal's initiative aimed at enhancing digital skills. AI Portugal 2030 is spearheaded by the INCoDe.2030 Coordination Structure, in collaboration with the Portuguese Science and Technology Foundation (FCT), the Portuguese Innovation Agency (ANI), Cincia Viva, and the Portuguese Agency for Administrative Modernisation (AMA). The initiative was launched in February 2019 by the Minister of Science, Technology and Higher Education, following six public discussion meetings that began in October 2018. Additionally, it follows the launch of the Mobilizing Program to Foster AI in Public Administration by FCT on March 1, 2018, which has already conducted two project calls in March 2018 and March 2019. In December 2018, FCT also initiated three Collaborative Laboratories (CoLABs) that engage industry and R&D units from higher education institutions in AI-related activities, specifically: the Digital Transformation in Industry CoLAB, the Smart Farm CoLAB, and the CoLAB focused on Cyber-physical Systems and Cyber Security.The objectives of AI Portugal 2030 are built upon seven foundational pillars:1. Enhancing societal well-being through sustainability, resource management, and job creation;2. Promoting AI skills and fostering "digital minds" for everyone through education, lifelong learning, and talent attraction;3. Creating new job opportunities and developing an AI service economy;4. Establishing Portugal as a living laboratory for testing new innovations in areas such as urban transformation, sustainable energy, biodiversity, autonomous driving, cybersecurity, and quantum materials for AI;5. Securing niche markets in Portugal with specialized services in natural language processing, real-time AI applications, software development, and edge computing;6. Contributing to advancements in knowledge and innovation through AI research;7. Enhancing public services for citizens and businesses by leveraging available data for evidence-based decision-making.The Action Plan outlines seven key action lines:1. Inclusion and Education: spreading general knowledge about AI;2. Qualification and specialization;3. Research and innovation in specific thematic areas within European and international networks;4. Modernizing public administration;5. Specific areas of focus.

items.title: AI Policy Forum
items.org: Federal Chancellery of Austria and Federal Ministry for Climate Action, Environment, Energy, Mobility, Innovation and Technology (BMK)
items.category: National – AI governance bodies or mechanisms
items.body:
The ministries responsible for Austria's AI strategy jointly lead the inter-ministerial working group AI Policy Forum, which consists of representatives of all twelve ministries. The AI Policy Forum was set up 2021 to support the inter-ministerial implementation of the national AI strategy. Its main tasks include the ongoing monitoring of AI strategy measures and the coordination of AI activities in the specialist ministries.

In order to support the cross-departmental implementation of the national AI strategy an inter-ministerial working group, the AI Policy Forum, was set up at the end of 2021, chaired by the Federal Chancellery (BKA) and the Federal Ministry for Climate Action, Environment, Energy, Mobility, Innovation and Technology (BMK). With members from all federal ministries, the AI Policy Forum contributes to a broad coordination of the federal government in the field of artificial intelligence. Its tasks include, among other things, coordinating AI implementation measures in the ministries, connecting experts in their specialist areas and the exchange of information on developments in the field of AI. The AI Policy Forum also contributes to shaping the content of the AI strategy and implementation plans and provides support with the implementation and ongoing and the ongoing monitoring of the AI measures contained therein. The AI Policy Forum Network Meeting is an annual series of events to which administration, academia, the business community and the interested public are invited to discuss developments in the field of AI and exchange information on current projects and topics.

items.title: AI Pilot Schools: Learning and Teaching with AI Tools
items.original_name: KI-Pilotschulen: Lernen und Lehren mit KI-Tools
items.org: Federal Ministry of Education, Science and Research
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: KI-Pilotschulen: Lernen und Lehren mit KI-Tools
items.body:
The initiative žAI Pilot Schools explores the integration of AI tools in Austrian classrooms through empirical research. It includes three phases: an initial survey on AI use, a second survey documenting practical experiences, and ongoing documentation by teachers. The initiative aims to provide insights into AI-supported teaching and learning.

The initiative žAI Pilot Schools, spearheaded by the Austrian Federal Ministry of Education, Science, and Research, examines the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in schools. The project involves three empirical phases: Baseline Survey (2023/24): A comprehensive questionnaire was distributed to assess the status quo of AI usage in Austrian schools. This survey combined rating scales and open questions to gather insights into the existing knowledge and tools available. Focus Survey (2024): Building on the initial results, a second quantitative survey titled žAI Pilot Schools in Focus documented teachers' experiences with AI technologies in their classrooms. Ongoing Documentation (2024): Teachers were provided with a structured template to record their qualitative experiences with AI-based learning tools throughout 2024.The surveys and documentation are conducted online, ensuring direct communication with the participating pilot schools. Data from the surveys have been analyzed using SPSS, while the qualitative documentation is being evaluated with MAXQDA software. These insights aim to support evidence-based recommendations for AI integration in education, enhancing teaching practices and student learning outcomes in the digital age.

items.title: AI National Policy
items.org: Ministry of Science, Technology, Knowledge and Innovation (Minscience)
items.category: National – Strategy
items.body:
The Chilean AI Policy 2021-2030 covers three pillars: (1) enabling factors, (2) development and adoption of AI (3) ethics, regulatory aspects and socio-economic impacts.

The Policy was originally due to launch in April 2020, but due to the social riots in Chile and COVID-19, it has been postponed to early 2021. However, this extension made a broad participation process possible.The Ministry of Science, Technology, Knowledge and Innovation is leading a working plan to launch a national AI policy and action plan in early 2021.The Chilean AI Policy will contain the strategic alignments that the country has to follow to achieve the following objective: empower the Chilean population in the usage and development of AI tools and participate actively in the legal, ethical, social and economic consequences of AI.The initiative has the following objectives:To empower citizens in the development and application of AI tools, and encourage their participation in the debate on their legal, ethical, social and economic consequences.To develop AI-enabling factors which encompass development of human capital, technological infrastructure, and data availability.To foster the use and development of AI which encompasses research, development, innovation, and entrepeneurship based on AI systems. It also foster adoption both in the private and the public sector.To discuss and reach consensus about ethics, standards, cybersecurity and regulation between the private and public sectors for a human-centered development and use of AI. This includes topics such as privacy, transparency, responsibility, environmental issues, gender-gap, automation impacts, among others.

items.title: AI National Plan
items.category: National – Strategy
items.body:
The strategy will establish policies to promote AI development in alignment with ethical and legal principles, contributing to national development goals and the SDGs. It aims to create, develop, and implement AI technologies that enhance human capacities and provide innovative solutions to drive Argentina's development.

It is currently being reviewed by new National Administration and it will include new initiatives planned and deployed in this field according to updated objectives.It is currently being reviewed by new National Administration and it will include new initiatives planned and deployed in this field according to updated objectives.The initiative has the following objectives:To foster Argentina's economic potential by generating favorable conditions for AI development and adoption in different sectors of the Argentinian industry and on various government levels, and by encouraging the consolidation of the knowledge-based economic sector concerned with AI development.To promote the development of inclusive and sustainable AI for a better quality of life for people.To minimise the potential risks of AI development and implementation for society, by protecting personal data and individual privacy through guidelines for the design of AI systems consistent with ethical and legal principles; and by analyzing the potential impact in the production scheme, resulting effects on labor forces and prevent automated systems from reproducing or reinforcing discriminatory or exclusionary stereotypes.To encourage the development of AI-oriented talent and of AI technical and scientific capabilities, and promote research, development and innovation (R&D&I) initiatives for basic and applied science in AI in the public and the private sector.To promote federal coordination and linkage of AI between government organizations, research bodies, scientists, professionals, local and foreign companies for the development of the domestic ecosystem.To position Argentina as a regional leader in this paradigm shift that will have an impact on the scientific-technological, socio-economic and political environments and the productive structure.

items.title: AI Monitor
items.org: Federal Chancellery of Austria, Directorate General for Digitalisation and E-Government
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The AI Monitor aims to provide information about usage of AI as well as opportunities and challenges related to AI. Updated annually, it will comprise a dashboard with a broad range of quantitative data, alongside short introductions to lighthouse projects and initiatives within the Austrian AI ecosystem and contributions by the Austrian AI Advisory Board and the AI Stakeholder Forum.

Despite a wealth of data available on developments related to AI, this information is often not accessible in a centralised manner, thus hindering evidence-based discussion about developments related to AI. The AI Monitor seeks to address this issue by collecting and presenting quantitative data from a variety of sources, mainly publiclyavailable, and by supplementing this dashboard with information about existing initiatives which provide some form of support for actors in the Austrian AI ecosystem. In addition, qualitative assessments of the Austrian AI Advisory Board and the AI Stakeholder Forum on the opportunities and challenges related to AI will help tomonitor these developments from multiple perspectives.The Austrian AI Monitor will be hosted on digitalaustria.gv.at and will be published in 2025 with annual updates.The AI Monitor will be able to integrate further initiatives and data points, allowing for a gradual expansion of itsscope.

items.title: AI Mission Austria 2030
items.original_name: Strategie der Bundesregierung für Künstliche Intelligenz Artificial Intelligence Mission Austria 2030 (AIM AT 2030)
items.org: Federal Ministry for Climate Action, Environment, Energy, Mobility, Innovation and Technology (BMK); Federal Chancellery of Austria (BKA)
items.category: National – Strategy
items.document_name: Strategie der Bundesregierung für Künstliche Intelligenz Artificial Intelligence Mission Austria 2030 (AIM AT 2030)
items.body:
The three agencies Austria Wirtschaftsservice GmbH (aws), the Austrian Research Promotion Agency (FFG) and the Austrian Science Fund (FWF) offer funding for basic research, applied research and its entrepreneurial implementation under the title ‘AI Mission Austria’ (AIM AT). The funding initiative was implemented for 2022 and 2023 with funds from the Fonds Zukunft Österreich (FZÖ) (FFG, 2024[16]).

In order to realise the opportunities of AI for Austria and at the same time minimise potential risks, the AI strategy of the Austrian federal government Artificial Intelligence Mission Austria 2030 (AIM AT 2030) was published in 2021 and developed in a participatory process together with experts and other stakeholders.The Austrian AI Strategy aims:To promote a responsible and broad use of AI in the public interest based on European fundamental values (inviolability of human dignity, respect for privacy and the principle of equality) in Austria and thus to contribute to the preservation of the greatest possible sovereignty of the country with regard to the use and application of AI, and thus to the reduction of dependence on global monopolies and market leaders.To develop measures to recognise, mitigate or prevent possible dangers and undesirable developments that may result from AI for people and society and make AI applications verifiable. To raise awareness and organise social dialogues on how to deal with AI and its specific regulation in various fields of application with the participation of civil society to promote social participation, freedom of action, and self-determination for citizens.To raise research, technology and innovation for AI in key areas or niches to a worldwide top level, thereby pushing forward the massive strengthening of fundamental scientific research.To position Austria as a leading research and innovation location for AI worldwide and thus use the opportunities that AI offers for the competitiveness of the industrial location. To establish the public administration as a lead user and provider of AI-supported public services for citizens and thus to push ahead the modernisation of the administration.To promote the transfer of AI applications into Austrian SMEs, to generate new added value from the application of AI and to improve framework conditions for the establishment of start-ups in order to set economic and employment policy impulses.To create a legal framework that ensures the safety of the use of AI for people and society and meets the requirements of EU legislation.

items.body:
The AI MOOC is an online course accessible to all Austrian teachers, offering self-paced, flexible learning. Participants can explore AI fundamentals, ethical considerations, and practical tools tailored to their teaching context. The course aims to empower educators with knowledge and skills for integrating AI into education.

The AI MOOC, developed by the Austrian Federal Ministry of Education, Science, and Research, provides a comprehensive and flexible digital training course for educators. Accessible online, this course allows participants to learn independently at their own pace, anytime and anywhere. The course is designed to support individualized learning with tailored content suitable for different school types and teaching contexts.Key content areas include: AI Fundamentals: Introduction to artificial intelligence concepts. AI in Education: Exploration of applications and tools for teaching and learning. Ethics and Data Protection: Ethical implications and privacy considerations for AI use. Practical Tools and Platforms: Hands-on training with AI-supported tools and platforms for educational purposes.The MOOC combines theoretical knowledge with practical applications, ensuring participants are equipped to implement AI in their classrooms effectively. The course is hosted on the Virtual PH platform.

items.title: AI Labeling
items.org: Federal Chancellery of Austria, Directorate General for Digitalisation and E-Government
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
In order to ensure transparency and trust in AI, Austria intends to introduce a labelling for AI systems used in the Austrian federal administration. The primary goal is to ensure that users of modern technologies are immediately informed when they interact with artificial intelligence.

The labelling of AI systems in the public administration is understood as a code of conduct on a voluntary basis, which is based on the intentions of the transparency regulations for certain AI systems in Article 50 of the AI Act and can therefore be extended in the future.The aim is not to label AI-generated content, but only AI systems that interact with citizens. A concept with an evaluation methodology is being developed, which assesses the autonomy and impact of AI systems. This results in an overall category that provides additional information about the AI system.

Twice a week during the school year, seventh grade students study the role and importance of artificial intelligence through these subjects, but also gain knowledge about its application in everyday life and the impact of artificial intelligence on humans.In the eighth grade, students continue to expand their knowledge of artificial intelligence through the compulsory subject of Engineering and Technology. items.title: AI Hub Tetouan
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
A groundbreaking 386MW data center and AI hub is planned in Tetouan, Morocco. Named Eureka Park, this hub aims to become a premier global technology center, focusing on advanced AI computation and data storage. It will feature the Iozera AI Data Center, GenV Data Management Services for AI training and data handling, Ryse Research for startup incubation and workforce training, and an AI Expo to showcase global advancements in AI technology.

In a significant stride toward transforming the artificial intelligence industry, US-based tech startup Iozera, in partnership with the Moroccan government, announced plans to establish a groundbreaking 386MW data center and AI hub in Tetouan, Morocco. Named Eureka Park, this hub aims to become a premier global technology center, focusing on advanced AI computation and data storage.The expansive Eureka Park will feature the Iozera AI Data Center, GenV Data Management Services for AI training and data handling, Ryse Research for startup incubation and workforce training, and an AI Expo to showcase global advancements in AI technology.The project will harness renewable energy sources including the Noor Solar Power Complex and the Koudia Al Baida Wind Farm, highlighting its commitment to green and innovative technology. With construction scheduled to begin in late 2024, the facility is expected to be operational by mid-2026 and ready to serve global clients by the 2030 World Cup hosted in Morocco.

items.body:
Practical AI governance guideline for organization executives to consider when implementing AI application within their organizations.

Important milestone of the initiatives:2021: Thailand AI Ethics Guideline received approval from the cabinet.2022: Establishment of the National AI Committee, chaired by the Prime Minister2022: Thailand National AI Strategy and action Plan 2022-2027 received approval from the cabinet.2022: Establishment of the AI Governance Clinic (AIGC) under the Electronic Transactions Development Agency to lead AI governance promotion effort.2023: Publication of the AI Governance Guideline for Executives which helps facilitate understanding and practical implementation of the AI Ethics Guideline.2023-present: AIGC publicizes and offers training programs related to the AI Governance Guideline for Executives to the public. BackgroundAI technology has increasingly played a significant role in the daily lives of humans, leading to global concerns regarding its potential impact on ethics, morality, privacy, and security. These concerns further extend to questions of accountability when AI is utilized to assist in or make decisions on behalf of humans. Consequently, the governance of AI applications, known as AI governance, or the principles governing the responsible use of AI, has emerged as a critical issue that organizations must address within their specific contexts. Although Thailand AI Ethics Guideline has been available since 2021, its widespread implementation remains limited. The AI Governance Guideline for Executives was developed to offer a more practical and easily understandable guide on AI governance for organizational leaders to voluntarily follow.The initiative has the following objectives:AI Governance Guideline for Executives aims to provide a practical and comprehensive framework for implementing AI technology in a responsible and ethical manner while maintaining business objectives.

items.title: AI Governance Center
items.original_name: ศูนย์ธรรมาภิบาลปัญญาประดิษฐ์
items.category: National – AI governance bodies or mechanisms
items.document_name: ศูนย์ธรรมาภิบาลปัญญาประดิษฐ์
items.body:
The AI Governance Center (AIGC) ensures responsible AI adoption in Thailand through policies, testing frameworks, and global collaborations.Founded under the National AI Strategy and action Plan (2022 - 2027), AIGC tackles AI risks, promotes ethical use, and aligns Thailand with global AI governance standards to ensure safe and sustainable AI development.Policymakers, businesses, and researchers benefit from its guidelines, AI testing tools, and advisory services.

The AI Governance Center (AIGC) was established to address the growing risks and ethical challenges associated with AI adoption in Thailand while positioning the country as a leader in AI governance. With AI becoming integral to various sectors, issues such as bias, privacy risks, and transparency gaps require robust governance. AIGC leverages this opportunity by developing comprehensive guidelines, risk assessment tools, and policy frameworks to ensure responsible and sustainable AI deployment. Additionally, it strengthens Thailand's alignment with global AI governance standards, facilitating international cooperation and investment.The initiative's key objectives include developing AI governance guidelines and toolkits, fostering AI ethics awareness, and enhancing testing frameworks to mitigate AI-related risks. By engaging policymakers, businesses, and researchers, AIGC ensures practical implementation of responsible AI principles. It has also introduced AI ethics education through training programs such as the AI Executive Program (AIX), AI Change Agent Program (AICA) and knowledge sharing, reaching over 20,000 participants in 2024. International collaboration is another priority, with Thailand serving as a key contributor to OECD AI governance initiatives and ASEAN AI ethics frameworks, reinforcing its regional and global leadership.Looking ahead, AIGC will continue to expand its impact by institutionalizing AI governance across sectors. It is set to co-host the UNESCO Global Forum on the Ethics of AI 2025, further elevating Thailand's presence in AI policy discussions. The AI Sandbox, which currently focuses on LLM testing, may evolve to encompass broader AI applications, enhancing regulatory preparedness. Scaling AI governance efforts across industries through partnerships with both public and private organizations will be crucial. Institutionalizing AI governance frameworks through regulatory integration and industry-specific adaptation will ensure long-term sustainability.Since its inception, AIGC has progressed from research and policy development to implementation and global advocacy. Early efforts focused on establishing AI governance principles, while recent initiatives emphasize practical application, such as the AI Readiness Scan (AIRS) and AI Risk Assessment tools. AIGC's expanding network of domestic and international stakeholders enables ongoing refinement of governance models, ensuring they remain relevant amid rapid AI advancements. As AI continues to evolve, AIGC's role in shaping responsible AI adoption will strengthen, ensuring Thailand remains at the forefront of ethical and sustainable AI governance.

items.title: AI Expertise Center
items.category: National – AI governance bodies or mechanisms
items.body:
The AI Expertise Center supports and guides the use of artificial intelligence within the Flemish government and local authorities to improve the efficiency, effectiveness and innovation of their (digital) services. The AI Expertise Center takes on the role within the Flanders Digital agency of providing the framework, supporting the knowledge sharing and stimulating the innovative application of AI in government.

The AI Expertise Center supports and guides the use of artificial intelligence within the Flemish government and local authorities to improve the efficiency, effectiveness and innovation of their (digital) services. The activities of the AI Expertise Center focus on five pillars: (1) defining a long-term AI vision and strategy, (2) stimulating AI-driven innovation, (3) creating AI building blocks, (4) increasing the reliability of AI and (5) preparing people and organisations. The AI Expertise Center is now in a start-up phase, but will expand to become the center of excellence for the trustworthy use of AI in government. One of the expertise centers is the Flanders Digital Agency's AI Expertise Centre identifies civil servants’ needs for AI upskilling and reskilling. It supports public sector innovation by equipping civil servants to use AI for improved policymaking, operational efficiency, and service delivery (Digital Vlaanderen, 2024[78]).

The Mission is necessary as a mechanism to establish a prospective roadmap to achieve the implementation of an AI Policy based on the technical and integral vision of the experts to complement and guide the path that Colombia is advancing in this regard.

The Artificial Intelligence Expert Mission consists of a group of experts who will meet periodically to evaluate the different dimensions of AI and produce concrete recommendations in the short, medium and long term. The Mission is necessary as a mechanism to establish a prospective roadmap to achieve the implementation of an AI Policy based on the technical and integral vision of the experts to complement and guide the path that Colombia is advancing in this regard. Colombia's AI Expert Mission is one of the first of its kind in the region, and one of the first to focus on developing measures for the development of citizen empowerment and future of work policies for the fourth industrial revolution.Colombia recognizes the international leadership of certain countries and institutions in the development of AI. Therefore, it is necessary to exchange knowledge with leading international entities and generate strategies to build relationships with other organizations on AI-related topics, mitigating information asymmetries through continual interaction with the international community, especially in the LAC region.Colombia held a public consultation on the proposal for the creation of this council, with comments due on March 30th 2021.https://dapre.presidencia.gov.co/AtencionCiudadana/convocatorias-consultas/consejo-internacional-de-inteligencia-artificial-para-colombiaThe initiative has the following objectives:Generate recommendations in the areas of future of work, gender and citizen empowerment that respond to the challenges originated by artificial intelligence, among which the knowledge and gender gaps stand out.Promote the development of technological tools to mitigate the effects of climate change, environmental protection and promote the sustainable development of the country. Recommendations are expected on the implementation of AI solutions oriented to this purpose, as well as the generation of the necessary talent and skills to achieve it.

items.title: AI Covid-19 Response
items.original_name: IA y Ciencia de Datos para la detección temprana de potenciales brotes epidémicos y pandémicos post-COVID-19: Implementación de una estrategia escalable de historias cl­ínicas electrónicas, género-inclusiva y socialmente responsable en Argentina
items.org: Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (Mincyt) | Ministry of Health (MinSal) | Center for Interdisciplinary Studies in Science, Technology and Innovation (CIECTI) | Sadosky Foundation
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: IA y Ciencia de Datos para la detección temprana de potenciales brotes epidémicos y pandémicos post-COVID-19: Implementación de una estrategia escalable de historias cl­ínicas electrónicas, género-inclusiva y socialmente responsable en Argentina
items.body:
The project will help develop a central objective for the national sanitary policy: promoting quality and equitable access to public health services despite gender, age, economic or geographic conditions.

This initiative is part of a national strategy in health, science, technology, and innovation, explicitly supported by two key national ministries responsible for these areas. The National Government, which oversees the federal health system, is responsible for implementing measures to build a more efficient, balanced, and equitable system across all Argentine provinces.The project was designed in response to the emergency crisis caused by COVID-19. Its goal is to equip the National Health System with new technological capabilities to better manage health crises.In Argentina, the first COVID-19 case was registered on March 3, 2020. By early July, there were 1,490 deaths and over 75,000 infections. The infection rate grew rapidly in poor neighborhoods where overcrowding and fragile living conditions made it difficult to maintain hygiene and social distancing. The pandemic also had a differential impact on men and women's ability to exercise their right to health, increasing vulnerability for women due to factors such as rising domestic violence, a higher proportion of female health workers exposed to infection, and socially assigned caregiving roles predominantly shouldered by women.Besides COVID-19, Argentina faces other epidemic outbreaks. Since early 2019, there has been the most extensive measles outbreak since the virus was eliminated in 2000, with nearly 200 cases. Dengue fever also put the National Health Surveillance System on alert, with over 51,000 local cases and 1,000 imported cases between 2019 and 2020”marking the largest outbreak in the country's history. Dengue mainly affects the most vulnerable and disadvantaged provinces, including Jujuy, Salta, Misiones, and Tucum¡n. In Buenos Aires, over half of the cases occurred in vulnerable neighborhoods. These social, environmental, and health determinants directly influence the effectiveness of epidemiological surveillance.Early detection of outbreaks is a major health policy challenge. It is essential because:Preventive actions help avoid the spread of infectious diseases.Early detection allows health systems to prepare and respond effectively.Alerts can be issued to other provinces and the wider Latin American region.Early diagnosis leads to better treatment outcomes.New technologies, particularly artificial intelligence (AI) and the analysis of large, high-quality datasets, have proven highly effective in predicting potential epidemic outbreaks globally and in the region.The initiative aims to develop a national system that uses AI and electronic medical records to detect pandemics and epidemic outbreaks at an early stage, enabling faster and more effective responses.

items.body:
Colombia promotes the development of solutions for problems caused by the COVID-19 pandemic and other acute respiratory infections (ARIs) with a great impact on public health, through the selection and funding of AI projects that promote scientific and technological results in the diagnosis, treatment, mitigation and monitoring of the corresponding diseases.

The Ministry of Health and Social Protection declared a national emergency in Resolution 285 of 2020 to face the present pandemic caused SARS-Cov-2 pandemic. In this context, the National Government established a national priority the funding of science, technology and innovation (STI) projects, especially AI projects, aimed to develop rapid diagnostic techniques, devices and/or tools to care for medical personnel and patients.The initiative has the following objectives:To support prototype technologies based on the incorporation of scientific and technological knowledge, to face the COVID-19 pandemic.To promote access to results in Science, Technology and Innovation in order to generate strategies and instruments that counteract the effects of the propagation of the COVID-19 virus and other viruses that have the potential to impact public health.To promote and strengthen the countrys scientific and technological capabilities through the articulation and formation of partnerships between Science, Technology and Innovation systems and international actors that promote interdisciplinarity contributions to main challenges faced by the pandemic of COVID-19.To increase the transfer and access to results, valuable data and scientific evidence amongst Colombian governmental entities.

items.title: AI Center

items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The AI Center (Argentina) is a technical cooperation project between the Argentine government and the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB). Its main goal is to strengthen the country's institutional capacity in artificial intelligence by establishing an AI center that follows global best practices. The initiative supports the national strategy to promote AI research, development, and adoption across public and private sectors.

The AI Center (Argentina) is a collaborative project led by the Argentine Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation in partnership with the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB). Launched in 2021, the initiative aims to build national capacity in artificial intelligence by creating a dedicated AI center aligned with international standards and best practices. This center will support AI research, innovation, and policy development to foster the adoption of AI technologies across public administration and industry.By strengthening institutional frameworks and promoting knowledge sharing, the initiative seeks to position Argentina as a regional leader in AI. It focuses on enhancing AI skills, encouraging responsible and ethical AI use, and supporting sustainable economic and social development through advanced technologies. The project is funded through non-reimbursable technical cooperation and is a key component of Argentina's broader AI strategy.

items.title: AI COVID-19 Response
items.org: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
Estonia implemented an AI powered chatbot SUVE which helped people to acquire information regarding the state of play.

Suve is an automated chatbot, whose main task was to make sure that everyone living in or visiting Estonia got their questions answered from official sources. Suve was integrated into several public websites. During the emergency situation related to COVID-19, she helped to provide accurate and trustworthy information in English, Estonian and Russian. After the end of the pandemic, the chatbot is not actively used anymore.The initiative has the following objectives:To provide official information during emergency situations.To keep emergency phone lines open.To avoid fake news.

items.title: AI Business Program
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
AI Business program was launched as part of AI Programme. In 2018, with public funding amounting to EUR 34 million and a total of 115 projects, the AI Business program, focusing on AI and the platform economy, was Business Finland's biggest programme. The programme, launched at the beginning of 2018, has been reserved an authorisation to allocate EUR 100 million over a four-year period, as well as an authorisation to grant EUR 60 million of capital loan for the first two years to be all

Demand for the AI campaign was significant, and it was expanded into a program in 2018. By 2021, the AI Business program (2018“2021) funded 347 projects by Finnish companies and research institutes or projects involving innovative public procurement with a total of EUR 235 million. Nine of the companies also received funding for young innovative companies. The combined exports of the SMEs involved in the program increased by more than 2.5 times, to a value of around EUR 280 million over four years, and the companies' staff doubled. - The export of digital B2B services is becoming a strong pillar for Finland. For example, more than half of the exports to the United States are service exports. So far, games have been the most important segment of service exports, but B2B exports are growing and, as digitalization progresses, the growth accelerates. Traditional industrial companies are also exporting digital services more and more.

The initiative has the following objective(s):Drawing on the expertise of over 120 expert panellists from industry, academia, civil society and government, it identifies the most pressing opportunities, risks, and governance challenges associated with AI and data use, initially across five key UK sectors (including Criminal Justice, Financial Services, Health & Social Care, Digital & Social Media and Energy & Utilities).

items.title: AI Badge for eEducation Schools
items.org: Federal Ministry of Education, Science and Research
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The AI Badge for eEducation Schools is a new accreditation within the network eEducation Austria. It fosters ongoing commitment with AI topics in schools by integrating AI activities into school development. Completion of at least one AI Badge is mandatory for all schools by the end of the 2024/25 school year.

The network eEducation Austria, comprising over 4,100 schools (including 1,400 Expert or Expert+ schools), introduces the AI Badge to enhance digital and AI literacy in schools. This initiative builds upon the network's existing badge system, which tracks digital activities and supports schools' progression from Member to Expert and Expert+ status.The AI Badge emphasizes: School Development: By integrating AI-related activities into the autonomous school development process, the initiative ensures that AI becomes a strategic focus at the local school level. Sustainable Engagement: Schools are required to engage with AI topics and complete at least one AI Badge by the end of the 2024/25 school year. Involvement of leadership: The initiative encourages school leadership to prioritize and sustain AI-focused initiatives, fostering awareness and readiness among educators and students alike.By implementing the AI Badge, eEducation Austria aims to ensure that attention is directed toward AI at the school level, where its impact is most critical. The initiative strengthens the role of AI as a key component of school development and prepares students for the demands of a digital future.

items.title: AI Apprenticeship Programme
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
The AIAP is a full time 9-month programme where we train and groom local Singaporean AI talent. This is in line with the nation's focus in deepening national capabilities in AI, not only in terms of technology, but also skillsets and talents. The AIAP is a deep skilling programme and successful applicants to the AIAP are expected to have prior knowledge in AI and Machine Learning. During the duration of the programme the apprentice is paid a stipend of between SGD$3500 - $5500 per month.

The initiative has the following objectives:AIAP aims to foster local AI talent by enhancing their technical careers as well as skills.

items.category: National – AI governance bodies or mechanisms
items.body:
The Austrian AI Advisory Board consists of eleven members from academia, civil society, industry and public administration. Its tasks include advising the Austrian government and the AI service desk on developments related to AI, including technical, ethical and societal aspects and prioritising topics in the field of AI, as well as strategic planning and advice in relation to the Austrian AI strategy.

The Advisory Board for Artificial Intelligence (AI Advisory Board “ KI-Beirat) was constituted on February 28th 2024. The eleven members of the AI Advisory Board are proven experts in the field of AI and have excellent knowledge in the areas of ethics, research, economics, law and technology. The AI Advisory Board will advise the Federal Government on issues relating to AI and pool knowledge on AI as a whole. An administrative support office for the AI Advisory Board is located at the Austrian Regulatory Authority for Broadcasting and Telecommunications (RTR-GmbH), which is also home to Austria's AI Service Desk.The AI Advisory Board's tasks include:- Advising and informing the Federal Government on technical, social and ethical issues relating to artificial intelligence- Observing the technological development of AI and assessing the associated opportunities and risks for Austria- Supporting the federal government in prioritizing and focusing on AI topics and measures- Strategic advice to the federal government in the context of development and implementation of Austria's AI strategy AIM AT 2020 and the associated implementation plans
