items.title: AI 4.0
items.category: National – Strategy
items.body:
The programme and its networks have taken Finland towards the age of artificial intelligence through 11 key actions.

The programme and its networks have taken Finland towards the age of artificial intelligence through the following 11 key actions:Enhance business competitiveness through the use of AIEffectively utilise data in all sectorsEnsure that AI can be adopted more quickly and easilyEnsure top-level expertise and attract top expertsMake bold decisions and investmentsBuild the world's best public servicesEstablish new models for collaborationMake Finland a frontrunner in the age of AIPrepare for artificial intelligence to change the nature of workSteer AI development into a trust-based, human-centric directionPrepare for security challengesDuring Autumn 2021, the programme's thematic sub-groups have, together with stakeholders, specified the objectives and defined the key results as well as the measures and indicators required by them. This interim report compiles the results of the work of the sub-groups and four proposals for achieving the vision of Finland as a winner in the dual transition in 2030.The program is based on the results of the previous AI initiative and aims to promote the implementation of Artificial Intelligence as part of the Fourth Industrial Revolution, while also endorsing the new skills demanded during this digital transition. The aim is to respond to the specific challenges regarding digitalisation in Finland, such as the relatively low levels of investments in digital, the moderate re-generation of value creation in small or medium sized enterprises as well as the need for strategic leadership in the fourth industrial revolution. The program bases on the results of the AI Finland “program and aims to promote the implementation of Artificial Intelligence as part of the Fourth Industrial Revolution, while also endorsing the new skills demanded during this digital transition.In the Artificial Intelligence 4.0 program, AI technology is combined with a wide range of other digital technologies such as IoT (Internet of things), 3D-printing, robotics, quantum computing as well as the virtual and augmented reality. Together, these digital technologies enable change in the general functioning and practice of businesses, regenerate value creation, enable the detection of societal challenges and encourage sustainable growth.

items.title: AI 4 Belgium
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
Experts have written AI guidelines for Belgian policy makers.

The initiative has the following objectives:In March 2019, Belgium launched its national AI strategy, AI 4 Belgium. The strategy includes seven objectives for action:1. items.original_name: 지능정보화 구현을 위한 제6차 국가정보화 기본계획

items.body:
Korea's 6th National Informatization Master Plan aims to accelerate digital transformation and improve public services using intelligent technologies. It was developed to address fragmented e-government systems and limited use of data and smart technologies. The plan benefits citizens, businesses, and government by promoting innovation, building trust, and creating a human-centered digital society.

A fragmented e-government system by institution and by function and insufficient utilization of intelligent information technology systems have resulted in inefficient operations of information budget and limited customized intelligent service.Korea has been lacking data, multi-purpose technologies, convergence of intelligent information technology across industries, and SMEs technological capabilities. This has delayed the nations digital transformation and productivity growth. The plan has the following four components: i) acceleration of national digital transformation with intelligence, ii) finding growth engines with digital innovation, iii) creation of human-centered intelligent information society, and iv) establishment of intelligent infrastructure based on trust.Objectives:To achieve prosperity through information-based intelligence for Korea.

items.title: 2023 Industry and Technology Strategy
items.category: Regulations, guidelines and standards
items.body:
The Ministry of Industry and Technology published the 2023 Industry and Technology Strategy, which aims to carry out a program that covers the fields of industry and technology with a holistic approach and designed specifically according to the dynamics of the country, provides wide participation and mobilizes the society. The Strategy consists of five main pillars: High Technology and Innovation, Digital Transformation and Industry Move, Entrepreneurship, Human Capital and Infrastructure.

Policies that increase Turkey's global competitiveness, ensure its economic and technological independence and result in breakthroughs in critical technologies are structured in "The National Technology Initiative." The first successful example can be seen in the technology development projects implemented in the defence industry. Defence industry projects have increased the ability of domestic suppliers to produce technology, reduce costs, and demonstrate product development capacity for advanced technologies such as unmanned aerial vehicles, missiles, radar systems, and satellites. The gains from defence industry technology development projects and self-developing domestic suppliers set an example for other industries. Strong national planning and coordination play a significant role in the domestic production of critical technologies in the defence industry and the increase in domestic product utilisation from 20% to 68%. In ivil sectors, national governance mechanisms will be developed and the private sector will lead process design. Industrial road maps that consider the need for cost-effective and competitive solutions will be prepared.The initiative has the following objectives:- The share of medium-high and high technology products in manufacturing industry exports was36.4% and 3.2%, respectively in 2018. We aim to increase these ratios to 44.2% and 5.8% by 2023respectively.- R&D human resources in Turkey consisted of 153 thousand full-time employees (FTE) and 112thousand researchers in 2017. We aim to increase these numbers to 300 thousand and 200 thousand respectively by 2023.- According to the European Union's R&D Leadership Scoreboard, there are 4 Turkish companies among the 2,500 companies with the highest R&D expenditures in 2018. We aim to gradually increase this figure by 2023 to 23.- In Turkey, the estimated number of Professional software developers in 2018 was around 140thousand. We aim to increase the software development capacity required for digital transformation to exceed 500 thousand people by 2023 in Turkey.- In 2018, In Turkey, the total of venture investments and angel investments investment was US$ 60million. By 2023, we aim to increase the size of annual investments in technology-based businesses in Turkey to TL 5 billion.- We aim to make sure that Turkey will create at least 23 smart products with leading global market share and brand value in at least one of these disruptive technologies.

items.title: "AI in Everyday Consumer Life" - Teaching Materials on Artificial Intelligence for Secondary School
items.original_name: "KI im Konsumalltag" - Unterrichtsmaterialien zur kunstlichen Intelligenz fur 8. und 9. Schulstufe
items.org: Federal Ministry for Social Affairs, Health, Care and Consumer Protection
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.document_name: "KI im Konsumalltag" - Unterrichtsmaterialien zur kunstlichen Intelligenz fur 8. und 9. Schulstufe
items.body:
Thes teaching materials are intended to support teachers in addressing the topic of AI in the classroom. The materials encourage a conscious examination of the opportunities and risks associated with artificial intelligence in the context of consumer education. They inspire students to critically reflect on how AI influences their everyday lives, such as in purchasing decisions, personalized advertising, or digital voice assistants.

This initiative aims to close the gap between the rapid pace of technological advancements and the more traditional structure of educational curricula. The material provides a comprehensive guide to teaching artificial intelligence in consumer contexts for students of Secondary School. It includes structured methods, lesson plans, and materials that help students explore AI's impact on everyday consumer life. Designed for Secondary school, the teaching materials aim to introduce students to the concept of AI and its applications in a way that is practical and age-appropriate. Students will begin by gathering associations about AI and learning what the term truly means. They will explore generative chatbots as tools and practice using them effectively. The materials also highlight the impact of AI on consumer behavior, including potential risks and drawbacks. Students will examine devices and applications that utilize AI, gaining an understanding of its specific functions and the societal contexts in which it is developed and applied. Finally, the materials encourage students to think critically about the future of AI, reflect on its development, and form their own perspectives on its potential impact.The main goals of the initiative are to enhance students' understanding of AI, develop practical skills such as interacting with generative chatbots, and explore the societal and ethical dimensions of AI's influence. It addresses potential challenges posed by AI, such as privacy concerns, job displacement, and algorithmic bias, by raising awareness and fostering ethical reflection. At the same time, it supports teachers by offering free, high-quality teaching materials and tools that allow them to effectively integrate AI topics into their lessons. These resources are freely available for download at www.konsumentenfragen.at, and accompanying workshops are provided to guide teachers in using the materials.Looking ahead, the initiative is set to expand. Starting in the summer semester of 2026, digital education will become a mandatory subject in schools. Materials like these will play a critical role in helping educators meet this requirement and ensure that students are equipped with essential digital competencies.

items.title: "AI Next" Campaign
items.category: AI policy initiatives, programmes and projects
items.body:
In September 2018, DARPA announced a multi-year investment of more than $2 billion on AI R&D in a portfolio of some 50 new and existing programs collectively called the AI Next campaign.

Broad Agency Announcements (BAAs) are preceded by consultations with industry, research organizations and universities. DARPA comprises approximately 220 government employees in six technical offices, including nearly 100 program managers, who together oversee about 250 R&D programs. DARPA invests in AI R&D, though budget figures are not publicly available.The initiative has the following objective(s):To automate critical DoD business processes, such as security-clearance vetting or accrediting software systems for operational deployment.To improve the robustness and reliability of AI systems.To enhance the security and resiliency of machine learning and AI technologies.To reduce power, data, and performance inefficiencies.To pioneer the next generation of AI algorithms and applications.
